### DANIEL Chapter VII. Verses 13. 14.

> *I saw in visions of the night, and behold, one like the SON OF MAN was coming with the clouds of the heavens: And to Him was given Dominion, and Glory, and a Kingdom, and all peoples, nations, and languages shall worship Him: His Dominion is an everlasting dominion <note>original: "dominium sæculi," literally "dominion of the age" or "eternal dominion"</note>, which shall not pass away, and His Kingdom that which shall not perish.*
<note>In Swedenborg’s theology, the "Son of Man" represents the Lord in respect to the Word (the scriptures), and "coming in the clouds" signifies the opening of the Word's internal, spiritual meaning.</note>

### REVELATION <note>original: "Apocalypsis"</note> Chapter XXI: 1. 2. 5. 9. 10.

> *I, John, saw a New Heaven and a New Earth: and I saw the holy City, New Jerusalem, descending from God out of Heaven, prepared as a Bride adorned for her Husband. And the Angel spoke with me, saying, "Come, I will show you THE BRIDE, THE LAMB’S WIFE"; and he carried me away in the spirit onto a great and high mountain, and showed me the great holy City, Jerusalem, descending out of Heaven from God.*
> *He who sat upon the Throne said, "Behold, I MAKE ALL THINGS NEW"; and he said to me, "Write, because these words are true and faithful."*
<note>Swedenborg interprets the "New Jerusalem" not as a literal city, but as a "New Church" or a new state of spiritual life and doctrine among mankind.</note>

## THE FAITH OF THE NEW HEAVEN AND THE NEW CHURCH.

<margin>1.</margin>
<image-desc>A decorative woodcut drop cap 'F' featuring intricate floral and foliage patterns.</image-desc>
The **F**aith in its universal and particular <note>original: "singulari," referring to the specific or individual applications of the doctrine.</note> form is presented first, so that it may be like a Face before the Work that follows; and like a Gate, through which entry into the Temple is made; and as a Summary, in which the individual things that follow are contained in their own way. It is called the Faith of the New Heaven and the New Church, because the Heaven where the Angels are, and the Church in which Men are, act as one, just like the Internal and External <note>Swedenborg frequently uses the analogy of the "Internal" (the soul/mind) and the "External" (the body/action) to describe how spiritual and earthly realms interact.</note> in a person; for this reason, the person of the Church—who is in the good of love from the truths of faith, and in the truths of faith from the good of love—is, regarding the interior parts of their mind, an Angel of heaven. Therefore, they also come into Heaven after death and there enjoy happiness according to the state of the union of those two. It must be known that in the New Heaven, which is being established by the Lord today, this Faith is its face, gate, and summary.

<margin>2.</margin>
**THE FAITH OF THE NEW HEAVEN AND THE NEW CHURCH IN ITS UNIVERSAL FORM** is this: That the Lord from eternity, Who is **JEHOVAH**, came into the World to subjugate the Hells <note>original: "Inferna." Swedenborg views "Hell" as a plural collective of various spiritual regions of evil.</note> and to glorify His Human; and that without Him no mortal could have been saved; and that those who believe in Him are saved.

It is called a "Universal form" because this is the **Universal of faith** <term>Universal of faith: a core principle that must be present in every single specific detail of a belief system</term>, and a **Universal of faith** is that which must be present in each and every part. It is a **Universal of faith** that God is One in Essence and Person, in Whom is the Divine Trinity, and that the Lord God the Savior Jesus Christ is He. It is a **Universal of faith** that no mortal could have been saved unless the Lord had come into the World. It is a **Universal of faith** that He came into the World to remove Hell from

<summary>This page introduces the foundational summary of Swedenborg's theology, presenting the "Faith of the New Church" as a gateway to the rest of the work. It defines the core "Universal" of this faith: that God is one in the person of Jesus Christ, who came to earth to overcome evil and save humanity.</summary>

<keywords>True Christian Religion, New Heaven, New Church, Jehovah, Jesus Christ, Divine Trinity, Universal of faith, Salvation, Glorification, Subjugation of Hell</keywords>

from man, and that he removed it through battles against it, and through victories over it; thus he subjugated it, and brought it back into order, and under his obedience. The universal <note>In this context, "universal" refers to a general principle or a foundational truth that applies to everything else.</note> of faith is, that He came into the World to glorify His Humanity <note>original: "Humanum suum." Swedenborg uses "the Human" or "Humanity" as a noun to describe the human nature the Lord assumed on earth, which became Divine through His life.</note> which he took on in the World—that is, to unite it with the Divine from which [He came]; thus He holds Hell in order and under His obedience forever. Since this could not have been done except through Temptations admitted into His Humanity, even to the Last of them—and the last of them was the Passion of the cross—therefore He underwent that [passion]. These are the Universals of faith concerning the Lord.

The universal of faith on the part of man is that he should believe in the Lord; for through believing in Him, a conjunction <note>A "joining together" or spiritual connection between the individual and the Divine.</note> is made with Him, through which comes Salvation. To believe in Him is to have confidence that He saves; and because no one can have confidence except one who lives well, therefore this [living well] is also understood by "believing in Him." This the Lord also says in John:
> “*This is the will of the Father, that everyone who believes in the Son may have eternal life*” (6:40). 
And elsewhere: 
> “*He who believes in the Son has eternal life; but he who does not believe the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God remains upon him*” (3:36).

3. **THE FAITH OF THE NEW HEAVEN AND THE NEW CHURCH IN ITS PARTICULAR FORM** <note>original: "singulari forma," referring to the specific or detailed explanation as opposed to the general summary.</note> is this: That Jehovah God is Love itself and Wisdom itself, or that He is Good itself and Truth itself; and that He, as to Divine Truth (which is the Word, and which was God with God), descended and assumed Humanity for the purpose of restoring to order all things that were in Heaven, all things in Hell, and all things in the Church; because at that time the power of Hell prevailed over the power of Heaven, and on Earth the power of evil over the power of good, and as a result, total damnation stood before the doors and was imminent. This impending Damnation Jehovah God removed by means of His Humanity, which was Divine Truth, and thus He redeemed Angels and Men. Afterward, in His Humanity, He united Divine Truth to Divine Good, or Divine Wisdom to Divine Love, and thus He returned into His Divine (in which He was from eternity) together with and in His glorified Humanity. These things are understood by this in John: 
> “*The Word was with God, and the Word was God: and the Word was made Flesh*” (Chapter 1:1, 14); 
and in the same: 
> “*I came forth from the Father, and have come into the World; again [I leave the world and go to the Father]*” <note>original: "Exivi a Patre, & veni in Mundum; iterum [relinquam mundum, & vadam ad Patrem]." This refers to John 16:28.</note>

<summary>This page defines faith as a two-way connection involving the Lord's victory over hell and the individual's choice to believe and live well. It introduces the core doctrine that God descended as Divine Truth to prevent human destruction and united His earthly humanity with His eternal divinity.</summary>

*“I leave the World, and go to the Father,” Chapter 16:28. And further through this: “We know that the Son of God has come, and has given us understanding, that we might know the True One, and we are in the True One in His Son Jesus Christ: This is the true God and eternal Life,” 1 John Chapter 5:20, 21.* From these passages it is clear that without the Lord’s coming into the World, no one could have been saved. It is the same today; therefore, unless the Lord comes again into the World in <term>Divine Truth</term><note>In this context, Divine Truth refers to the internal spiritual meaning of the Bible, which Swedenborg believed he was revealing.</note>, which is the Word, no one can be saved.

The particulars of faith on the part of man are: 1. That God is One, in whom is the Divine Trinity, and that He is the Lord God the Savior Jesus Christ. 2. That saving Faith is to believe in Him. 3. That evils must not be done, because they are of the devil and from the devil. 4. That good deeds must be done, because they are of God and from God. 5. And that these must be done by man as if by himself; yet it must be believed that they are from the Lord, acting in him and through him. The first two belong to Faith, the next two to charity; and the fifth concerns the conjunction <note>A "joining together" or spiritual union.</note> of charity and faith, and thus of the Lord and man.

# CHAPTER ONE

### CONCERNING

## GOD THE CREATOR.

4. **T**he Christian Church, from the time of the Lord, had passed through its ages from Infancy to extreme Old Age; its Infancy was during the time when the Apostles lived and preached Repentance and Faith in the Lord God the Savior throughout the whole World. That they preached those two is evident from these words in the Acts of the Apostles: “*Paul testified both to Jews and Greeks Repentance toward God, and Faith in our Lord Jesus Christ,*” Chapter 20:21. It is a memorable thing that a few months ago, the Lord called together his twelve Disciples, now Angels, and sent them out into the whole Spiritual World with the command to preach the Gospel there anew <note>Swedenborg is referring to a spiritual event he claims occurred on June 19, 1770, where the deceased apostles were commissioned to teach the new doctrines of the New Church in the afterlife.</note>, since the Church established by the Lord through them has today reached such a point of <term>consummation</term><note>original: "consummata est." This term refers to the final end of a spiritual era or "dispensation" when genuine faith and love have been lost.</note> that scarcely any remnants of it remain. This happened because they divided the Divine Trinity into three Persons, each of whom is God and Lord; from this, something like a frenzy has flowed into the whole of Theology, and thus into the Church, which—

<summary>This page concludes the foundational principles of faith, emphasizing that the Lord must return as "Divine Truth" to save humanity. It then begins Chapter One, describing the historical decline of the Christian Church from the apostolic age to its present state of spiritual exhaustion.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the introduction to the nature of God, specifically critiquing the current state of Christian thought and beginning a systematic proof of the Unity of God. It follows the previous page's discussion on the necessity of the Lord's coming and the basic components of faith.</meta>

<page-num>6</page-num>
<header>UNIVERSAL THEOLOGY</header>

is called Christian from the name of the Lord; it is called <term>madness</term><note>The original Latin is *phrenesis*, referring to a delirium or mental derangement.</note>, because human minds have been driven into such a delirium by it that they do not know whether God is one, or whether there are three. He is one in the speech of the mouth, but three in the thought of the mind, which is why the mind disagrees with its own mouth, or the thought with its own speech. From this disagreement, the result is the conclusion that there is no God. The <term>Naturalism</term><note>The philosophical belief that everything arises from natural properties and causes, and supernatural or spiritual explanations are excluded or discounted.</note> prevailing today stems from nowhere else. Consider, if you please, while the mouth speaks of one and the mind thinks of three, whether they do not inwardly, along the way, cancel each other out in turn? Thus, a man hardly thinks of God otherwise—if he thinks at all—than from the mere word "God," without any sense that involves a knowledge of Him. Since the idea of God, along with every notion of Him, has been so torn apart, I wish to treat in order concerning God the Creator, the Lord the Redeemer, and the Holy Spirit the Operator, and finally the Divine Trinity, for the purpose of repairing what has been torn apart. This occurs when human Reason is convinced by the Word and the light therefrom that there is a Divine Trinity, and that this Trinity is in the Lord God the Savior Jesus Christ, just as the Soul, Body, and Proceeding <note>The "Proceeding" refers to the outward activity or influence of a person, comparable to the Holy Spirit's role in the Trinity.</note> are in man. Thus, what is said in the <term>Athanasian Creed</term><note>A classic statement of Christian belief focused on the Trinity and the nature of Christ.</note> remains valid: <note>original: "Quod in Christo Deus & Homo, seu Divinum & Humanum, non sint duo, sed in una Persona; & quod sicut Anima rationalis & Caro unus est homo, ita Deus & Homo unus sit Christus."</note> *That in Christ, God and Man, or the Divine and the Human, are not two, but in one Person; and that just as the rational soul and flesh are one man, so God and Man are one Christ.*

## ON THE UNITY OF GOD.

5. Since the acknowledgment of God from the knowledge of Him is the very essence and soul of everything in Universal Theology, it is necessary to begin with the UNITY OF GOD, which will be demonstrated in order through the following Articles: I. *That the whole Sacred Scripture, and consequently the Doctrine of the Churches in the Christian World, teach that God is one.* II. *That there is a universal influx into the souls of men, teaching that God exists and that He is one.* III. *Hence it is that in the whole world there is no nation possessing religion and sound reason that does not acknowledge a God, and that God is one.* IV. *That as to what that one God is, nations and peoples have differed and continue to differ for several reasons.* V. *That human Reason can perceive or conclude from many things in the world, if it wishes, that God exists and that He is one.* VI. *That unless God were one, the Universe could not have been created and preserved.* VII. *That the man who does not acknowledge God is excommunicated from the Church and condemned.* VIII. *That with a man who does not acknowledge one God, but several, nothing of the Church holds together.* But these points will be unfolded individually.

6. I. THAT THE WHOLE SACRED SCRIPTURE, AND CONSEQUENTLY ALL THE DOCTRINES OF THE CHURCHES IN THE CHRISTIAN WORLD, TEACH THAT GOD EXISTS, AND THAT HE IS ONE. The reason the whole Sacred Scripture teaches that God exists is that in its innermost parts there is nothing else but God—that is, the Divine which proceeds from God. For it was dictated by God, and nothing can proceed from God except what He is Himself, which is called the Divine; this is in its innermost parts. In the derivatives, however, which are below and come from there, that Holy Scripture is accommodated to the perception of Angels and Men; in these, there is likewise the Divine, but in another form, and in this form it is called the Divine Celestial, Spiritual, and Natural, which are nothing other than the coverings of God. For God Himself, as He is in the innermost parts of the Word, cannot be seen by any created being; for He said to Moses, when he prayed to see the glory of <term>Jehovah</term><note>The personal name of God in the Hebrew Bible.</note>, that no one can see God and live. It is the same with the innermost parts of the Word, where God is in His own Being and His own Essence; yet the Divine, which is innermost and is covered by such things as are accommodated to the perceptions of Angels and Men, shines through like Light through crystalline forms, though differently according to the state of mind which the man has formed for himself from God or from himself. To everyone who has formed the state of his mind from God, the Sacred Scripture is like a Mirror in which he sees God, but each in his own way. Truths, which...

He outlines eight points to prove the unity of God, starting with the testimony of Sacred Scripture.</summary>

<header>OF THE NEW HEAVEN AND THE NEW CHURCH.</header>

# OF THE NEW HEAVEN AND THE NEW CHURCH.

<note>original: NOVI CÆLI ET NOVÆ ECCLESIÆ. This title refers to Swedenborg’s belief that a new spiritual era was beginning, necessitating a fresh understanding of God.</note>

...learned from the **Word**, and imbibed through a life according to its truths, compose that **Mirror**. From these things it is first established that the Sacred Scripture is the fullness of God. That it not only teaches that God is, but also that God is one, can be established from the Truths which, as has been said, form that Mirror; for they cohere in a single connection, and ensure that a man cannot think of God except as one. Hence it is that everyone whose reason has been imbued with some holiness from the Word knows, as if of himself, that God is one, and perceives it as a kind of madness to say that there are many. The angels cannot even open their mouths to speak of "gods," for the heavenly atmosphere in which they live resists it. That God is one, the Sacred Scripture teaches not only universally in the manner just described, but also specifically in many places, such as these:

> *Hear, O Israel, Jehovah our God, Jehovah is one*, Deut. 6:4; likewise Mark 12:29. *Surely God is in thee, and there is no God besides Me*, Isaiah 45:14, 15. *Am I not Jehovah, and there is no God else beside Me?*, Isaiah 45:21, 22. *I am Jehovah thy God, and thou shalt acknowledge no God beside Me*, Hosea 13:4. Thus said *Jehovah the King of Israel, I am the First and the Last, and besides Me there is no God*, Isaiah 44:6. *In that day Jehovah shall be King over all the earth; in that day Jehovah shall be one, and His Name one*, Zech. 14:9.

7. It is well known that the doctrines of the churches in the Christian world teach that God is one; they teach this because all their doctrines are derived from the Word, and they remain coherent so long as they acknowledge one God not only with the mouth, but also with the heart. Those who acknowledge one God only with the mouth, but three with the heart—as is the case with many in Christianity today—for them, God is nothing more than a mere spoken word. All <term>Theology</term><note>Literally "the study of God." Swedenborg argues that without a true idea of God’s unity, the study becomes hollow.</note> is to them like an idol of gold locked in a cabinet, the key to which is held only by the priests. When they read the Word, they do not perceive any light there or from it; they do not even perceive that God is one. The Word to them is as if covered with ink-blots, hiding the unity of God. These are the ones described by the Lord in Matthew: "By hearing you shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing you shall see, and shall not perceive... they have closed their eyes, lest they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them," Chapter 13:14, 15. All such people are like those who flee the light and enter rooms without windows, where they grope along the walls seeking food and money; at last they acquire a sight like that of owls and see in the dark. They are like a woman who has many husbands, who is not a wife but a lustful prostitute; or like a virgin who accepts rings from many suitors, and after her wedding, spends her nights with one, and then also with the rest.

8. II. **THAT THERE IS A UNIVERSAL INFLUX FROM GOD INTO THE SOULS OF MEN, THAT GOD IS, AND THAT HE IS ONE.**
That there is an <term>influx</term><note>From the Latin *influxus*, meaning "a flowing in." Swedenborg uses this to describe how life and spirit flow from the Divine into the human mind, like light into an eye.</note> from God into man is evident from the confession of all: that every good thing which is good in itself—which is in man and done by him—is from God. Similarly, everything of charity and everything of faith is from Him; for we read, *A man can receive nothing, except it be given him from heaven*, John 3:27; and Jesus said, *Without Me you can do nothing*, John 15:5; that is, nothing of charity or of faith. This influx is into the souls of men because the soul is the innermost and highest part of man, and the influx from God enters there, and from there descends into the things below, vivifying them according to how they are received. It is true that the truths of faith enter through hearing and are thus implanted in the mind—below the soul—but man is only prepared by these truths to receive the influx from God through the soul. As the preparation is, such is the reception, and such is the transformation of natural faith into spiritual faith. That there is an influx from God into the souls of men teaching that God is one, is because everything Divine, whether taken universally or individually, is God; and because everything Divine coheres as one, it cannot help but inspire in man the idea of one God. This idea is strengthened daily as man is raised by God into the light of heaven; for the angels, in their light, cannot even force themselves to ut-

Although this influx—that God is one—flows into the souls of all men, the reason why many think His Divinity is divided into several beings of the same essence is that when that Influx descends, it falls into forms that do not correspond to it. It is the same God who gives life to every beast and to every man, but the receiving form causes the beast to be a beast and the man to be a man. A similar thing happens with a man when he introduces the form of a beast into his own mind. There is a similar influx from the Sun into every tree, but it is varied according to the form of each; it is the same for the vine as it is for the thorn, but if a thorn is grafted onto a vine, the influx is inverted and proceeds according to the form of the thorn. The same happens in the subjects of the mineral kingdom: the light flowing into limestone and into a diamond is the same, but it shines through the latter and is darkened in the former. As for human minds, they vary according to their forms, which are inwardly spiritual according to their faith in God and a life led from God. Those forms become transparent and angelic through faith in one God; but conversely, they become dark and bestial through a faith in many gods, which differs little from a faith in no God.

### 9. III. FOR THIS REASON, THERE IS NO NATION IN THE WHOLE WORLD POSSESSING RELIGION AND SOUND REASON THAT DOES NOT ACKNOWLEDGE A GOD, AND THAT GOD IS ONE.

From the Divine Influx into the souls of men, mentioned just above, it follows that there is an internal dictate in every person that there is a God, and that He is one. That there are still those who deny God, who acknowledge Nature in place of God, or who worship many gods or even idols as gods, is because they have obstructed the interiors of their reason or understanding with worldly and bodily concerns. By these means, they have obliterated the primary idea of God from their infancy and have simultaneously cast Religion from their breast to their back. That Christians acknowledge one God—but in what manner—is evident from their <term>Creed<note>original: Symbolica Confessione. This refers to the formal statements of faith, specifically the Athanasian Creed discussed below.</note></term>, which is as follows: 

> *The Catholic Faith is this: that we worship one God in Trinity, and Trinity in Unity; there are three Divine Persons, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, and yet they are not three gods, but one God. And there is one Person of the Father, another of the Son, and another of the Holy Spirit, and they have one Divinity, equal Glory, and co-eternal Majesty; thus the Father is God, the Son is God, and the Holy Spirit is God. But because we are compelled by Christian truth to acknowledge each Person individually as God and Lord, so we are forbidden by the Catholic Religion to say there are three Gods and three Lords.* 

Such is the Christian faith concerning the Unity of God; but how the Trinity of God and the Unity of God disagree with each other in that confession will be seen in the chapter on the **Divine Trinity**. The remaining nations in the world who possess religion and sound reason agree that God is one: all the Muslims in their empires; the Africans in many kingdoms of their continent; and also the Asians in many of theirs; and furthermore, the Jews today. The most ancient people in the Golden Age, those who possessed religion, worshipped one God whom they named **Jehovah**. Similarly, the Ancient people in the following age—before monarchical empires were established, when worldly and finally bodily loves began to close the higher parts of the understanding (which were previously open and then functioned like Temples and <term>Sanctuaries<note>original: Adyta. The innermost, holiest part of a temple.</note></term> for the worship of one God). But so that the Lord God might reopen those parts and thus restore the worship of one God, He established a Church among the descendants of Jacob and placed this at the head of all their religious precepts: *There shall be no other God before my face, Exodus 20:3.* The name **Jehovah**, which He named Himself anew before them, signifies the supreme and unique Being from whom is everything that is and exists in the universe. The ancient Gentiles acknowledged **Jupiter** as the supreme God (perhaps so named from "Jehovah"), and they also granted divinity to many others who made up his court; but the wise men in the following age, such as Plato and Aristotle, confessed that these were not Gods, but so many properties, qualities, and at-

10. Every sound mind, even if not religious, can see that anything divided will fall apart of itself unless it depends on a single point of unity. For example, a Human being is woven together from so many members, viscera, and sensory and motor organs, yet would collapse without a single soul; and the Body itself would fail without a single heart. Similarly, a Kingdom cannot stand without one King; a Household without one master; and every function, which is manifold in any Kingdom, must trace back to one presiding officer. What value would an Army have against enemies without a General who holds supreme power, with subordinate officers under him, each having their own right of command over the soldiers? It would be the same with the Church if it did not acknowledge one God, and also with the angelic Heaven, which is like the head of the Church on earth, and in which the Lord is the Soul itself. This is why Heaven and the Church are called His Body; if they did not acknowledge one God, both would be like a lifeless corpse which, being useless for anything, would be cast out and buried.

## 11. IV. THAT NATIONS AND PEOPLES HAVE WANDERED, AND STILL WANDER, INTO DIFFERENT CONCEPTIONS OF THE NATURE OF THE ONE GOD FOR SEVERAL REASONS.

The first reason is that knowledge about God, and the resulting acknowledgment of God, is not possible without Revelation. Furthermore, knowledge of the Lord—and the acknowledgment that in Him dwells all the fullness of the Divinity bodily—is only possible from <term>the Word<note>In this context, "The Word" refers to Sacred Scripture, which the author views as the ultimate communication from the Divine.</note></term>, which is the Crown of Revelations. For through the Revelation provided, a person can approach God and receive <term>influx<note>The spiritual process by which life and thought flow from God into the human mind.</note></term>, and thus be changed from a "natural" person into a "spiritual" one. A primary Revelation once spread throughout the entire world, but the "natural man" perverted it in many ways; this gave rise to the divisions, disagreements, heresies, and religious schisms we see. 

The second reason is that the <term>Natural man<note>The "natural man" refers to a person who focuses only on the physical world and the five senses, as opposed to the "spiritual man" who perceives deeper truths.</note></term> cannot perceive anything of God, but only of the World, and applies this only to himself. For this reason, it is a canon of the Christian Church that the Natural man is opposed to the Spiritual man, and that they fight against each other. From this it follows that those who have learned that God exists—whether from the Word or from some other Revelation—have diverged and continue to diverge regarding the *Quality* of God and His *Unity*. Consequently, those whose mental vision depended on the physical senses, yet who still wished to "see" God, fashioned for themselves Idols of gold, silver, stone, and wood, so that they might worship God under those forms as objects of sight. Others, who rejected idols for religious reasons, fashioned images of God for themselves out of the Sun, Moon, Stars, and various things on earth. Yet others, who believed themselves to be wiser than the common people but remained "natural," acknowledged Nature as God—some seeing Him in its innermost workings and others in its outermost effects—because of God's immensity and omnipresence in creating the World. Some, in an attempt to separate God from nature, devised a most universal abstraction which they called the <term>Being of the universe<note>original: "Ens universi" — a philosophical term for a vague, impersonal "Universal Being" or "Entity of the Universe."</note></term>; and because they know nothing more about God, this "Being" is for them merely a "being of reason," which signifies nothing at all. 

Who cannot understand that knowledge of God is like a mirror of God? Those who know nothing of God do not see Him in a mirror placed before their eyes, but in a mirror turned the wrong way, or from the back, where the mercury or "black glue" covers it; it does not reflect the image, but smothers it. Faith in God enters a person through the <term>Prior Way<note>The "inner path" or "internal way."</note></term>, which is from the soul into the higher parts of the intellect; but knowledge of God enters through the <term>Posterior Way<note>The "outer path" or "external way," meaning knowledge gained through the senses and reading.</note></term>, because it is drawn from the revealed Word by the Intellect through the physical senses. In the "middle" of the Intellect, these two flows of influence meet. There, "natural faith" (which is merely a matter of being persuaded) becomes "spiritual faith," which is true acknowledgment. Therefore, the human Intellect is like a marketplace or exchange, in which this transformation takes place.

## 12. V. THAT HUMAN REASON CAN PERCEIVE OR CONCLUDE FROM MANY THINGS IN THE WORLD, IF IT IS WILLING, THAT GOD EXISTS AND THAT HE IS ONE.

This truth can be confirmed by countless things in the visible World; for the Universe is like a Theater, upon which testimonies that God exists and that He is one are continually exhibited. But to illustrate this, I will bring forward this **MEMORABLE OCCURRENCE** from the Spiritual World. Once, while I was speaking with Angels, some Newcomers from the natural world were present. Seeing them, I wished them a happy arrival and told them many unknown things about the Spiritual World. After this talk, I asked them what learning they had brought from the world regarding God...

...and regarding Nature and the World, they carried the idea with them that Nature performs everything that happens in the Created Universe, and that God, after Creation, instilled and impressed that faculty and power into it, and that God only sustains and preserves those things so they do not perish. For this reason, all things that exist, are born, and are reborn upon the Earth are today ascribed to Nature. But I replied that Nature does nothing from itself, but God works through nature. Because they demanded a demonstration, I said: those who believe in Divine operation in every detail of nature can, from the many things they see in the world, confirm their belief in God much more than in Nature. For those who confirm their belief in Divine Operation in every detail of nature pay attention to the wonders seen in the productions of both plants and animals.

In the **PRODUCTION OF PLANTS**, from a tiny seed cast into the earth, a root comes forth, then through the root a stem, and successively branches, shoots, leaves, flowers, and fruits, even unto new seeds, exactly as if the Seed knew the order of succession or the process by which it was to renew itself. What rational person can think that the Sun, which is pure fire, knows this, or that it can instill into its heat and light the power to effect such things or to intend these uses? A person whose rational mind is elevated, while seeing and rightly weighing these things, cannot think otherwise than that they are from Him who has infinite Wisdom—that is, from God. Those who recognize Divine Operation in every detail of nature also confirm their belief when they see these things. 

On the other hand, those who do not recognize it do not see such things with the "eyes of reason in the forehead," but rather in the back of the head <note>original: "in occipitio." This suggests a backward or inverted way of thinking that looks only at effects, not causes.</note>. These are people who draw all the ideas of their thought from the senses of the body and confirm their fallacies, saying: "Do you not see the Sun performing all these things through its heat and light? What is there that you do not see? Is there anything else?" 

Those who confirm their belief in the Divine pay attention to the **WONDERS** they see in the **PRODUCTION OF ANIMALS**. To mention first what occurs in Eggs: within them, the chick lies hidden in its seed with every requirement for its formation, and also with the entire progression it will follow after hatching until it becomes a bird in the form of its parent. Furthermore, if one pays attention to flying creatures in general, things are presented to a mind that thinks deeply which create amazement. For instance, in the smallest of them as in the largest, in the invisible as in the visible—that is, in tiny insects as in large birds and beasts—there are organs of sense (sight, smell, taste, and touch) as well as organs of motion (muscles, for they fly and walk). There are also internal organs attached to the heart and lungs, which are activated by brains. 

Those who ascribe everything to Nature certainly see such things, but they think only that they "are," and say that Nature produces them. They say this because they have turned their minds away from thinking about the Divine. Those who have turned away from the Divine, while seeing the wonders in Nature, cannot think about them rationally—much less spiritually—but think sensually and materially. In such a state, they think *in* nature *from* nature, and not *above* it. Their only difference from beasts is that they possess rationality <term>rationality: the capacity to understand truths if they choose to use it</term>; that is, they are able to understand if they wish.

Those who have turned away from thinking about the Divine, and have thereby become sensual and corporeal, do not consider that the sight of the eye is so coarse and material that it views many tiny insects as a single dark speck. And yet, every single one of them is organized to feel and to move itself, and is thus endowed with fibers and vessels, as well as little hearts, pulmonary tubes, tiny organs, and brains. These are woven from the purest elements in nature, and these textures correspond to life in its lowest degree, by which the smallest parts of them are distinctly moved. Since the sight of the eye is so coarse that many things—with innumerable parts in each—appear to it as a small dark speck, and yet those who are sensual think and judge based on that sight, it is clear how thickened their Minds are, and consequently in what darkness they reside regarding spiritual things.

Anyone can confirm their belief in the Divine from the visible things in Nature if they wish; and anyone who thinks about God and His Omnipotence in creating the Universe, and His Omnipresence in preserving it, does so confirm it. For instance, when one sees the flying creatures of the sky...

They can smell from a distance the flowers and herbs from which they collect wax for the house and honey for food; and, laden with these, they fly back according to the direction of their hive. Thus, they provide food for the coming winter as if they foresaw it. They even set over themselves a mistress like a Queen, from whom posterity may be propagated; and for her, they build a sort of palace above themselves with guards around it. From these things, it can be established that because of the **Use** they provide to the human race, they have a form of government through Divine influx via the Spiritual World, just like the government among men on earth, or even among the angels in the Heavens. Who, with their reason intact, does not see that such things in them are not from the Natural world? What does the Sun, from which Nature comes, have in common with a government that rivals and mimics the government of heaven?

From these and similar examples among the brute animals, the confessor and worshiper of Nature confirms their belief in Nature, while the confessor and worshiper of God confirms from the same things their belief in God. For the **Spiritual man** sees spiritual things in them, and the **Natural man** sees natural things in them—each according to their own quality. As for me, such things have been testimonies to me of the Influx of the Spiritual World into the Natural from God. # 13. VI. THAT UNLESS THERE WERE ONE GOD, THE UNIVERSE COULD NOT HAVE BEEN CREATED AND PRESERVED.

That the Unity of God can be concluded from the creation of the Universe is because the Universe is a coherent Work—like a single entity from first things to last—and it depends on one God just as a body depends on its soul. The Universe was created in such a way that God can be **omnipresent**, holding each and every part of it under His guidance, and containing it as one forever, which is what it means to preserve it. It is also for this reason that Jehovah God says that He is the *First and the Last, the Beginning and the End, the Alpha and the Omega* (Isaiah 44:6; Revelation 1:8, 17); and elsewhere, *that He makes all things, spreads out the heavens, and extends the Earth* by Himself (Isaiah 44:24). This great System called the Universe is a coherent Work like a single entity from firsts to lasts because God, in creating it, intended one **End** <note>In this context, 'End' refers to the ultimate purpose or goal.</note>: an Angelic Heaven from the Human Race. The means to that end are all the things that make up the world; for whoever wills the end also wills the means.

Therefore, whoever contemplates the World as a Work containing the means to that end can contemplate the created Universe as a coherent Work. Such a person can see that the World is a complex of **uses** in successive order for the Human Race, from which the Angelic Heaven comes. **Divine Love** cannot intend any other end than the eternal happiness of humans from His own Divine nature, and His **Divine Wisdom** cannot produce anything other than the uses that serve as means to that end. From an inspection of the World with this universal idea, every wise person can understand that the Creator of the universe is one, and that His Essence is Love and Wisdom. Therefore, there is nothing so small in the world that a use does not lie hidden within it, near or far, for the sake of man—for his food from the fruits of the earth and animals, and his clothing from the same. It is among the wonders that those lowly worms called **Silkworms** clothe and magnificently adorn both women and men, from Queens and Kings to maidservants and menservants; and that the lowly worms which are **Bees** supply wax for lights, which fill Temples and Halls with splendor. Those who look at specific things in the world individually, and not at all things universally in a series (in which there are ends, mediating causes, and effects), and those who do not derive Creation from Divine Love through Divine Wisdom, cannot see that the Universe is...

The <term>Handiwork</term><note>original: "Opificium." This refers to God as a craftsman or master builder who designs the universe with specific purposes.</note> of the one God exists in every single **use** because He dwells within the **end**; for whoever is in the end is also in the means, since the end is intimately within all the means, acting through them and guiding them. Those who do not contemplate the Universe as the Handiwork of God, and as the Dwelling-place of His **Love** and **Wisdom**, but rather as the handiwork of nature and a dwelling-place for the sun's heat and light, close off the higher reaches of their minds to God. Instead, they open the lower parts of their minds to the devil. In doing so, they cast off what is **Human** and put on what is bestial. They not only believe themselves to be like beasts, but they actually become so: they become foxes in their cunning, wolves in their ferocity, leopards in their deceit, tigers in their cruelty, and crocodiles, serpents, or owls according to their specific natures. Those who are like this even appear from a distance in the **Spiritual World** as these very beasts; for their love of evil takes on that outward shape.

## 14. VII. THAT THE PERSON WHO DOES NOT ACKNOWLEDGE GOD IS EXCOMMUNICATED FROM THE CHURCH, AND DAMNED.

The reason a person who does not acknowledge God is excommunicated from the **Church** is that God is the "all" of the Church; the Divine things called "theology" are what constitute the Church. Therefore, the denial of God is the denial of everything belonging to the Church. This denial itself excommunicates the person—thus the person excommunicates themselves; it is not God who does it. Such a person is damned because, by being excommunicated from the Church, they are also excommunicated from **Heaven**. For the Church on earth and the angelic Heaven act as one, just like the **Internal and External**, or the **Spiritual and Natural** in a human being. 

God created humans so that their **Internal** self would be in the **Spiritual World** and their **External** self in the **Natural World**. Thus, a person is created as a citizen of both worlds for a specific reason: so that the spiritual (which belongs to Heaven) may be implanted in the natural (which belongs to the world), much like a seed is planted in the soil, so that the person may become stable and endure forever. 

A person who has excommunicated themselves from the Church (and thus from Heaven) by denying God has closed off their **Internal Man** in regard to the **will**, and thus in regard to their innate love. For the human will is the receptacle of one's love and becomes its dwelling place. However, they cannot close off their Internal Man in regard to the **Understanding**; if they could and did do this, a human would no longer be human. Instead, the love of the person's will infatuates the higher parts of the Understanding with falsehoods. Consequently, the Understanding becomes, as it were, closed to the truths of **faith** and the goods of **charity**, becoming more and more opposed to God and the spiritual things of the Church. 

In this way, the person is excluded from communion with the **Angels of Heaven**. Once excluded, they cast themselves into communion with the **Satans** <note>In Swedenborg’s theology, "Satans" refers specifically to inhabitants of hell who are characterized by false thinking and intellectual pride, as opposed to "Devils," who are characterized by evil desires.</note> of Hell and think as one with them. All Satans deny God and think foolishly about God and the spiritual things of the Church. A person joined to them does the same. When such a person is in their own **Spirit**—which happens when they are left alone at home and allow their thoughts to be led by the delights of the evil and the false which they have conceived and brought forth—they think of God as non-existent. They think of "God" merely as a voice echoing from pulpits to keep the common people bound to obedience to the laws of justice that govern **Society**. 

They also think that the **Word** <note>The Holy Scripture.</note>, from which ministers preach about God, is something visionary and a collection of stories given a sacred status by authority. Furthermore, they think that the **Decalogue** (the Ten Commandments) or the **Catechism** is just a little book that, once worn out by the hands of children, should be tossed aside—for it commands that parents be honored, that one should not kill, commit adultery, steal, or bear false witness, and who does not already know these same things from civil law? 

Regarding the Church, they think it is merely a congregation of simple, gullible, and faint-hearted people who claim to see what they do not see. They think of other humans, and of themselves as humans, in the same way they think of beasts; and they think of life after death in the same way as the life of a beast after it dies. This is how the **Internal Man** thinks, no matter how differently the **External Man** speaks. For as has been said, every person has an Internal and an External, and it is the Internal that makes the person—this is called the **Spirit**, and it lives after death. The External, by which one acts the hypocrite through outward morality, is buried; and then, because of the denial of God, the person is damned. Every person, as to their Spirit, is associated with their own kind in the Spiritual World and is as one with them. It has often been granted to me to see the spirits of men...

From this it became clear that whoever denies God is already among the damned, and that after death they are gathered to their own kind.

## 15. VIII. THAT AMONG PEOPLE WHO DO NOT ACKNOWLEDGE ONE GOD, BUT SEVERAL, NO PART OF THE CHURCH HOLDS TOGETHER.

Anyone who acknowledges one God in faith and worships Him with the heart is in the <term>communion of Saints</term><note>A traditional term for the spiritual union of all believers, both living and deceased.</note> on earth, and in the communion of Angels in the heavens. These are called "communions," and they truly are, because they are in one God and one God is in them. These people are also in conjunction with the entire Angelic Heaven, and I would dare say, with each and every person there; for they are all like children and descendants from one Father, whose souls, characters, and faces are similar, by which they recognize each other. The Angelic Heaven is organized into Societies according to all the varieties of the love of good; these varieties aim toward one most universal Love, which is toward God. From this Love all have been propagated who acknowledge God as the one Creator of the universe, and at the same time Redeemer and Regenerator, in faith and heart. 

But it is entirely different for those who approach and adore not one, but several Gods—whether this happens by saying "one" with the mouth and "three" in thought (as those in the church today do, who distinguish God into three Persons and declare each Person to be God by Himself, attributing to each separate qualities or properties that do not belong to the other). From this, it happens that not only is the unity of God actually divided, but even Theology itself, and also the human Mind in which it should reside, is similarly divided. What results from this but something tangled and incoherent in matters of the Church? (The state of the current Church will be demonstrated in the Appendix after this work). This is the truth: that the division of God, or of the Divine Essence, into three Persons, each of whom is God by Himself or individually, leads to the denial of God. 

It is like someone entering a Temple to worship and seeing on a painting above the Altar one God depicted like the **Ancient of Days**<note>original: "Antiquum dierum." A reference to God the Father as described in the Book of Daniel.</note>, another like a **High Priest**, and a third like a flying **Aeolus**<note>original: "Æolum." The Greek god of the winds, here likely referring to the Holy Spirit depicted as a rushing wind or winged figure.</note>, with the caption: *These three are One God.* Or perhaps like seeing Unity and Trinity painted there like a man with three Heads on one body, or with three bodies under one Head—which is a monstrous form. If anyone entered Heaven with such an idea, they would certainly be cast down headlong, even if they said that the Head or Heads signified the Essence, and the Body or Bodies signified distinct Properties.

These are first-hand accounts Swedenborg included to illustrate spiritual truths through his experiences in the afterlife.</note>: I saw some newcomers from the natural World in the Spiritual World talking among themselves about Three Divine Persons from eternity. They were Canons <note>Clergy members belonging to a cathedral or collegiate church.</note>, and one of them was a Bishop. They approached me, and after some conversation about the Spiritual World (about which they had previously known nothing), I said: "I heard you talking about three Divine Persons from eternity; and I ask you to open up this great Mystery according to your ideas which you brought from the natural World, where you recently were." 

Then the Primate <note>A title for a high-ranking bishop.</note>, looking at me, said: "I see that you are a Layman, therefore I will open and teach the ideas of my thought regarding this great Mystery. My ideas were, and still are, that God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Spirit sit in the Midst of Heaven upon magnificent and high thrones. God the Father sits upon a throne of pure gold <note>original: "obryzo auro," meaning gold that has been tested or refined.</note> with a Scepter in hand; God the Son at His right hand upon a throne of purest silver with a Crown upon his head; and God the Holy Spirit near them upon a throne of shining Crystal, holding a Dove in his hand; and that all around them, hanging in a triple row, lamps..."

The walls flashed with precious stones; and from afar, countless Angels stood around this Circle, all worshipping and glorifying. Furthermore, God the Father speaks continually with His Son about those who are to be Justified <term>Justification: the process by which a person is made righteous in the eyes of God</term>, and they decide and decree between themselves who on earth are worthy to be received among the Angels and crowned with eternal life. And God the Holy Spirit, having heard those names, immediately runs throughout the world to them, carrying the gifts of justice as many reinforcements of salvation for those to be justified. As soon as He arrives and breathes upon them, He dissipates sins—just as a winnower blows smoke from a furnace—and whitens the soul. He also removes the hardness of stone from their hearts and inserts the softness of flesh, and simultaneously renews their spirits or minds, generating them anew, and giving them the faces of infants. Finally, He seals their foreheads with the sign of the cross and calls them the elect and sons of God. 

When this speech ended, that Primate <note>original: "Primas" — a title for a high-ranking bishop</note> said to me, "Thus have I unraveled that great mystery in the world; and because most of our Order there applauded these words of mine, I am persuaded that you, who are a layman, will also join in believing them." 

After the Primate said these things, I looked at him and the canons <note>original: "canonicos" — members of a cathedral chapter or specific clergy</note> with him, and noticed that they all favored this with full assent. Therefore, I began to respond and said: "I have weighed the pronouncements of your faith, and from them I have gathered that you have captured and cherish an entirely natural and sensual—even material—idea regarding the Triune God, from which the idea of three Gods inevitably flows. Is it not thinking sensually about God the Father to imagine Him sitting upon a Throne with a Scepter in hand? And about the Son, that He sits on His Throne with a Crown upon His head? And the Holy Spirit, that He sits on His with a Dove in hand, and that according to what He has overheard, He runs across the world? 

Because such an idea results from this, I cannot give faith to your words; for from my infancy I have been unable to admit any other idea into my mind than that of **ONE GOD**, and since I have admitted and retained only this, everything you have said falls away for me. I then saw that by the Throne upon which Jehovah is said to sit according to Scripture, **Kingdom** is understood; by the Scepter and Crown, **Rule and Dominion**; by 'sitting at the right hand,' the **Omnipotence of God through His Human**; and by those things related concerning the Holy Spirit, the **Operations of Divine Omnipresence**. Take up, sir, if you please, the idea of **ONE GOD**, and revolve it properly in your Reasoning, and eventually you will clearly perceive that it is so. 

Indeed, you even say that God is one, because you make the Essence one and also the individual of those three Persons; and yet you do not permit anyone to say that this one God is one Person, but that there are still three. You do this lest the idea of three gods, such as yours is, should perish. You also assign to each a property separate from the others; do you not thus divide your Divine Essence? When this is the case, how can you speak and simultaneously think that there is One God? I would forgive you if you said there is one 'Divine' <note>In this context, referring to a singular divine nature or substance rather than a person.</note>. How can anyone, while hearing that the Father is God, the Son is God, and the Holy Spirit is God, and that each Person is individually God, think that there is one God? Is it not a contradiction to which faith can never be joined? 

That He cannot be called one God, but only a 'similar Divine,' can be illustrated by this: regarding several men who together form one Senate, Council, or Assembly, it cannot be said that they are 'one man'; but when there is one opinion among all and each of them, it can be said they are of one mind. Nor can it be said of three diamonds of the same substance that they are 'one Diamond,' but that they are one as to substance, and also each diamond differs from the others in price according to its own weight; but this is not so if it were one, and not three. 

But I perceive that you call three Divine Persons—each of whom by Himself or individually is God—one God, and have enjoined everyone in the Church so to speak, for this reason: because enlightened and sound Reason throughout the whole world acknowledges that there is **One God**, and therefore you would be covered in shame if you did not also speak similarly. But yet, while you pronounce 'one God,' even though you think 'three,' that shame does not pull those two words into the mouth, but you spe—

...follow me. Having said and heard these things, the Bishop departed with his Canons; and as he was leaving, he turned around and wanted to exclaim, "There is one God," but he could not, because his thought pulled back his tongue, and then with an open mouth he breathed out "three Gods." Those standing by, having seen this portent, laughed with a loud guffaw and went away.

17. Afterward I asked where I might find those among the Learned who possess the sharpest intellect and who stand for a Divine Trinity divided into three Persons. Three such men were present, to whom I said: "How can you divide the Divine Trinity into three Persons and assert that each Person, by Himself or individually, is God and Lord? Does not the confession of the mouth—that God is one—stand as far apart from your thought as the south is from the north?" To this they replied: "It does not differ a bit, because the three Persons have one Essence, and the Divine Essence is God. In the world, we were the Guardians of the Trinity of Persons; the Ward <note>original: "Pupillus" — an orphan or minor under the care of a legal guardian</note> whose guardianship we carried out was our faith, in which each Divine Person obtained His own part: God the Father that part which He imputes and grants, God the Son that part which He intercedes and mediates, and God the Holy Spirit that part which brings about the application <term>Operation: the actual work or effect produced by divine grace</term> of imputation and mediation."

But I asked, "What do you understand by the 'Divine Essence'?" They said, "We understand Omnipotence, Omniscience, Omnipresence, Immensity, Eternity, and Equality of Majesty." To which I said, "If that Essence makes one God out of several, you could add even more—for example, a fourth who is mentioned in Moses, Ezekiel, and Job, and is called God Shaddai <note>original: "Deus Schaddai" — an ancient Hebrew name for God, often translated as "God Almighty"</note>. The Ancients in Greece and Italy did similarly; they assigned equal attributes and thus a similar essence to their gods, such as Saturn, Jupiter, Neptune, Pluto, Apollo, Juno, Diana, Minerva, and even Mercury and Venus; yet they still could not say that all of them were one God. And you also, who are three and, as I perceive, of similar learning and thus a similar essence in that regard, still cannot combine yourselves into one single learned man." At this they laughed, saying, "You are joking! It is different with the Divine Essence: it is one and not tripartite; it is individual and thus not divided; partitioning and division do not apply to it."

Hearing this, I replied, "Let us descend into this arena and do battle." I asked, "What do you understand by 'Person,' and what does it signify?" They said, "The name 'Person' signifies not a part or a quality in another, but that which properly subsists <term>Subsistence: a philosophical term meaning to exist independently and in one's own right</term>; this is how all the Leaders of the Church define 'Person,' and we with them." I said, "Is this the definition of Person?" and they replied, "It is." To which I countered, "Then there is no part of the Father in the Son, nor any part of both in the Holy Spirit. From this it follows that each is of His own judgment, right, and power; and thus there is nothing that joins them except the will, which is proper to each, and thus shared only by good pleasure. Are not, then, three Persons actually three distinct Gods? 

Listen further: you also defined 'Person' as that which properly subsists; consequently, there are three substances into which you divide the Divine Essence—and yet this Essence, as you also say, is indivisible because it is one and individual. Moreover, to each substance (that is, to each Person) you attribute properties that are not in the other and cannot be shared with the other, namely Imputation, Mediation, and Operation. What else results from this than that the three Persons are three gods?" At these words they withdrew, saying, "We will scrutinize <note>original: "ventilabimus" — literally 'to winnow' or 'fan'; here meaning to debate or examine a question thoroughly</note> these things, and after our examination we will respond." 

A certain Wise Man was standing by; having heard these things, he said, "I do not wish to look upon this supreme matter through such subtle lattices <note>original: "tranſennas" — screens or grilled windows; a metaphor for overly complex or restrictive logical arguments</note>, but outside those subtleties, I see in clear light that in the ideas of your thought there are three Gods. But because it is a matter of shame to proclaim them before the whole world—for if you did, you would be called insane and foolish—it is therefore useful for avoiding disgrace to confess one God with your mouth." But to this, the three, clinging to their opinion, paid no attention. As they were leaving, they were muttering some terms borrowed from the Metaphysical Art, from which I noticed that this was their tripod <note>original: "tripos" — the three-legged stool of the Oracle at Delphi; the author implies they rely on abstract philosophy as their source of divine authority</note> from which they wished to give answers.

# ON THE DIVINE BEING, WHICH IS JEHOVAH.

18. This first section deals with the Divine **Being** <term>Being: translated from the Latin "Esse," meaning the very core of existence or "to be-ness"</term>, and afterwards with the Divine **Essence**. It appears as if those two are one and the same, but yet **Being** is more universal than **Essence**, for **Essence** presupposes **Being**, and from **Being** comes **Essence**. The **Being** of God, or the Divine **Being**, cannot be described, because it is above every idea of human thought; into human thought nothing falls except what is created and finite, but not the Uncreated and Infinite, and thus not the Divine **Being**. The Divine **Being** is Being itself, from which all things are, and which must be in all things so that they may exist. A further notion of the Divine **Being** can flow from the following Articles:

*I. That the one God is called Jehovah from His **Being**, thus because He alone **Is, Was, and Will Be**, and because He is the **First and Last, the Beginning and the End, the Alpha and the Omega**.*

*II. That the one God is **Substance itself and Form itself**, and that Angels and Men are substances and forms from Him, and that insofar as they are in Him, and He in them, so far are they images and likenesses of Him.*

*III. That the Divine **Being** is Being in itself, and at the same time **Existing** in itself.* <note>In this context, "Existing" refers to the outward manifestation or becoming of the inner "Being."</note>

*IV. That the Divine **Being and Existing** in itself cannot produce another Divine being that is Being and Existing in itself; consequently, another God of the same Essence is not possible.*

*V. That a plurality of gods in ancient times, and also in the present day, has existed from no other cause than the Divine **Being** not being understood.* 

But these points must be elucidated one by one.

19. I. THAT THE ONE GOD IS CALLED JEHOVAH FROM **BEING**, THUS BECAUSE HE ALONE IS, AND WILL BE, AND BECAUSE HE IS THE FIRST AND LAST, THE BEGINNING AND THE END, THE ALPHA AND THE OMEGA. That "Jehovah" signifies **I Am** and **To Be** is well known; and that God has been so called from the most ancient times is evident from the Book of Creation, or Genesis, where in the first chapter He is named "God," but in the second and following chapters, "Jehovah God." Afterward, when the sons of Abraham through Jacob had forgotten the name of God during their stay in Egypt, it was recalled to their memory, concerning which it is written: 
,, *Moses said to God, "What is your name?" God said, I AM WHO I AM; thus shall you say to the children of Israel, I AM has sent me to you; and you shall say, JEHOVAH THE GOD of your fathers has sent me to you: this is my Name forever, and this is my Memorial from generation to generation"* <note>Exodus 3:14–15</note>. 
Since God alone is **I Am** and **Being**, or Jehovah, therefore there is nothing in the created Universe that does not derive its being from Him; but how this is so will be seen below. This same thing is also understood by these words: *I am the First and the Last, the Beginning and the End, the Alpha and the Omega* <note>original: "Alphah et Omegah"</note>, Isaiah 44:6, and Revelation 1:8, 11; 22:13; by which is signified: He who is the Self-Existing and Only One from firsts to lasts, from whom all things come. 

The reason God is called Alpha and Omega, the Beginning and the End, is because Alpha is the first and Omega is the last letter in the Greek alphabet, and they therefore signify all things in the aggregate. The reason for this is that every alphabetical letter in the spiritual world signifies a certain thing, and a vowel, because it serves for sound, signifies something of affection or love. From this origin comes spiritual or angelic speech, and also the writing there. But this is a secret <term>Arcanum: a hidden or profound mystery known only through revelation</term> unknown until now; for there is a Universal Language in which all Angels and Spirits are, and this has nothing in common with any language of men in the world. Every person comes into this language after death, for it is implanted in every person by creation; therefore everyone can understand another in the entire spiritual world. It has been granted to me many times to hear 그 language, and I have compared it with languages in the world, and I have found that it does not, even in the smallest detail, make one with any natural language on earth. It differs from these...

## 20. II. THAT THE ONE GOD IS SUBSTANCE ITSELF AND FORM ITSELF, AND THAT ANGELS AND MEN ARE SUBSTANCES AND FORMS FROM HIM; AND AS MUCH AS THEY ARE IN HIM, AND HE IN THEM, SO MUCH ARE THEY IMAGES AND LIKENESSES OF HIM.

Since God is Being <term>Being: "Esse," the fundamental state of existing</term>, He is also Substance, for Being, unless it is a substance, is a mere creature of reason <term>creature of reason: "ens rationis," a philosophical term for something that exists only as a thought and not in reality</term>; for substance is a subsisting entity. And He who is substance is also form, for substance, unless it is form, is a creature of reason. Therefore, both can be predicated of God, but in such a way that He is the unique, the very, and the first Substance and Form. That this Form is the truly Human Form—that is, that God is Very Man, in whom all things are Infinite—has been demonstrated in **ANGELIC WISDOM CONCERNING THE DIVINE LOVE AND THE DIVINE WISDOM**, published in Amsterdam in the year 1763. Similarly, it is demonstrated that Angels and Men are created and organized substances and forms for receiving the Divine things flowing into them through Heaven. Therefore, in the Book of Creation <note>The book of Genesis</note>, they are called "Images and Likenesses of God" (Chapter 1:26, 27), and elsewhere they are called His sons and born of Him. But how much a man lives under Divine auspices—that is, allows himself to be led by God—so much he becomes His image more and more interiorly, will be demonstrated in many places in the series of this Work. Unless an idea is formed of God as the first Substance and Form, and of His Form as the truly Human Form, human minds would easily adopt fantasies like ghosts regarding God Himself, the origin of men, and the Creation of the World. They would take no other notion of God than as the Nature of the universe in its first principles, or as its Expanse, or as a void or nothingness. Regarding the origin of men, they would see it as a chance confluence of elements into such a form; and regarding the Creation of the World, they would think the origin of its substances and forms was from geometric points and lines, which, because they have no properties, are in themselves nothing. Among such people, everything regarding the Church is like the Styx <note>A river in the underworld of Greek mythology</note> or the gloom of Tartarus <note>The deepest abyss of the underworld</note>.

## 21. III. THAT THE DIVINE BEING IS BEING IN ITSELF, AND AT THE SAME TIME EXISTING IN ITSELF.

That Jehovah God is Being <term>Being: "Esse"</term> in Himself is because He is the "I Am," the Itself, the Unique and the First, from eternity to eternity, from whom is everything that is, so that it may be something. Thus, and not otherwise, is He the Beginning and the End, the First and the Last, and the Alpha and the Omega. It cannot be said that His Being is from Himself, because **THIS "FROM HIMSELF"** <note>original: "HOC EX SE"</note> posits a "before" and thus time, which does not apply to the Infinite (which is called **FROM ETERNITY**). It would also posit another God who is God in Himself—thus a God from a God—or suggest that God formed Himself, and thus He would not be Uncreated nor Infinite, because He would have limited Himself either by Himself or by another. From the fact that God is Being in Himself, it follows that He is Love in Himself, Wisdom in Himself, and Life in Himself, and that He is the Itself from Whom all things are, and to which all things relate, so that they may be something. That God is Life in Himself, and thus God, is evident from the Lord's words in John, Chapter 5:26. And in Isaiah: "I am Jehovah, making all things, stretching out the Heavens alone, and spreading out the Earth by Myself" (Chapter 44:24). And that He is the only God, and besides Him there is no God (Isaiah 45:14, 15, 20, 21; Hosea 13:4). That God is not only Being <term>Esse</term> in Himself, but also Existing <term>Existing: "Existere," the manifestation or "standing forth" of Being</term> in Himself, is because Being, unless it Exists, is not anything; likewise, Existing is nothing unless it is from Being. Therefore, where one is given, the other will be given. Similarly, unless a substance is also a form, nothing can be predicated of that Substance; and this is because it has no quality, and is in itself nothing. The reason "Being" and "Existing" are used here, rather than "Essence" and "Existence," is because a distinction must be made between Being and Essence, and between Existing and Existence, as between a prior and a posterior. That which is prior is more universal than that which is posterior. Infinity and Eternity apply themselves to the Divine Being, but to the Divine Essence and Existence they apply—

22. That God is the Itself, the Unique, and the First, which is called Being <term>Being: "Esse," the inner essence of life</term> and Existing <term>Existing: "Existere," the manifestation or outward form of that essence</term> in Himself, from Whom are all things that are and exist, the **Natural man** <note>In this context, the "Natural man" refers to someone who thinks only from their physical senses and worldly logic, without spiritual insight.</note> can by no means discover by his own reason; for the natural man from his own reason can take nothing else than what belongs to nature, for this fits with his essence, because into that nothing else has entered from infancy and childhood. But since man was created to also be **Spiritual**, because he is to live after death, and then among spiritual beings in their World, God therefore provided **the Word** <note>original: "Verbum," referring to the Sacred Scriptures</note>, in which He has not only revealed Himself, but also that there is a Heaven and a Hell, and that in one or the other of these every man is to live forever, each according to his life and simultaneously his faith. He has also revealed in the Word that He is the *I Am* or Being, and the Itself and the Unique which is in Himself, and thus the First or the Beginning, from which are all things. 

It is from this Revelation that the Natural man is able to elevate himself above nature, and thus above himself, and to see such things as belong to God; but even then, it is as if from a great distance, although God is near to every man, for He is in him with His Essence. Because this is so, He is near to those who love Him; and those love Him who live according to His precepts and believe in Him; these, as it were, see Him. For what is faith but a spiritual sight of Him? And what is a life according to His precepts but an actual acknowledgment that salvation and eternal life are from Him? 

But truly, those who do not have spiritual faith, but only natural faith—which is merely knowledge <note>original: "scientia," meaning academic or external information rather than lived belief</note>—and a life according to it, they indeed see God, but from a great distance, and this only when they speak of Him. The difference between these and the former is like that between those who stand in clear light and see men near them and touch them, and those who stand in a dense fog and from it cannot see whether they are men, or whether they are trees or rocks. Or it is like those who stand upon a high Mountain where there is a City, and walk here and there and speak with fellow Citizens; and like those who look down from that Mountain and do not know whether the things they see are men, or beasts, or statues. Indeed, it is like the difference between those who stand on some planetary Globe and see their own people there, and those who are on another planetary globe with telescopes in their hands, looking there and saying they see men, when yet they see nothing but the land in general, like moonlight, and watery spots. Such is the difference between seeing God and the Divine things that proceed from Him in one’s mind among those who are in faith and at the same time in a life of charity, and among those who are merely in knowledge about them; and thus between Natural and Spiritual men. But those who deny the Divine Holiness of the Word, and yet carry those things which belong to Religion as if in a sack upon their backs, they do not see God at all, but merely make the sound "God," with very little difference from parrots.

23. IV. THAT THE DIVINE BEING [ESSE] AND EXISTING [EXISTERE] IN HIMSELF CANNOT PRODUCE ANOTHER DIVINE WHICH IS BEING AND EXISTING IN HIMSELF; CONSEQUENTLY, ANOTHER GOD OF THE SAME ESSENCE IS NOT POSSIBLE. That the one God, who is the Creator of the Universe, is Being and Existing in Himself, thus God in Himself, has been shown thus far; from this it follows that a "God from God" <note>The author is challenging the traditional Nicene Creed's phrasing of "God from God, Light from Light."</note> is not possible, because the very Essential Divine, which is Being and Existing in Himself, is not possible in such a being. It is the same whether one says "born of God" or "proceeding" from Him; it is still "produced by God," and this differs little from being created. Therefore, to introduce into the Church the faith that there are three Divine Persons, each of whom individually is God and of the same Essence, and one born from eternity, and a third proceeding from eternity, is to utterly abolish the idea of the Unity of God, and with it every notion of Divinity, and thus to cause all the spirituality of reason to be driven into exile. Then man is no longer man, but entirely Natural, differing no more from a beast than by the fact that he can speak; and he is against all the spiritual things of the Church, for these the natural man calls "delusions." From this, and from nowhere else, have such enormous heresies concerning God gushed forth. Therefore, a Divine Trinity divided into Persons has brought in not on...

### 24. V. THAT THE PLURALITY OF GODS IN ANCIENT AGES, AND ALSO TODAY, HAS ARISEN FROM NO OTHER SOURCE THAN THE DIVINE BEING <term>Being: "Esse," the underlying core of existence</term> NOT BEING UNDERSTOOD.

That the **Unity of God** is intimately inscribed on the mind of every man—since it is at the center of all things that flow into the soul of man from God—was shown above in number 8. But the reason it has not always descended into the human **Understanding** is that there was a lack of *knowledges* <note>original: "cognitiones," specific facts or spiritual insights</note> through which a man must ascend to meet God. For everyone must "prepare the way for God," that is, prepare himself for reception, and this is done through knowledges. 

The knowledges that were lacking—without which the Understanding could not penetrate far enough to see that God is one, and that no Divine Being is possible except the Unique One, and that all things of Nature are from Him—are the following:

1.  Because until now no one knew anything about the **Spiritual World**, where Spirits and Angels are, and into which every man comes after death.
2.  Likewise, it was unknown that in 그 World there is a **Sun**, which is pure Love from **Jehovah God**, who is in its midst.
3.  That from that Sun proceeds **Heat**, which in its essence is Love, and **Light**, which in its essence is Wisdom.
4.  That consequently all things in that World are **Spiritual**, and affect the Internal man, forming his Will and Understanding.
5.  That Jehovah God, from His Sun, produced not only the Spiritual World and all its spiritual things (which are innumerable and **substantial**), but also produced the natural world and all its natural things (which are also innumerable, but **material**).
6.  That until now no one has known the distinction between the **Spiritual** and the **Natural**, nor even what the Spiritual is in its essence.
7.  Nor that there are **three Degrees** of Love and Wisdom, according to which the angelic Heavens are ordered.
8.  And that the **human Mind** is distinguished into the same number of degrees, so that it can be elevated into one of the three Heavens after death, which happens according to his life and faith together.
9.  And finally, that not even a single point of all these things could exist except from the **Divine Being**, who is the "Itself" in Himself, and thus the First and the Beginning from which all things come.

These knowledges have been lacking until now, yet they are the means by which man ascends and comes to know the Divine Being. It is said that man "ascends," but it is understood that he is **elevated by God**; for man has **Free Will** <term>Free Will: "Liberum arbitrium," the capacity to choose and act freely</term> in acquiring knowledges for himself, and as he acquires them from the **Word** by means of his Understanding, he clears the way by which God may descend and elevate him. The knowledges by which the human Understanding ascends—with God holding him by the hand and leading him—can be compared to the steps of the **Ladder seen by Jacob**, which was set up on the earth, whose top reached into Heaven, and by which the Angels...
