25. To these things I will add this **MEMORABLE RELATION**: Once, having awakened from sleep, I fell into deep meditation about God; and when I looked up, I saw above me in Heaven a most white Light in an oval form. As I fixed my gaze upon that Light, the Light receded to the sides and entered into the peripheries, and then, behold, Heaven was opened to me, and I saw magnificent things, and Angels standing in a circular formation <note>original: "forma Circi," referring to the circular arrangement of an arena</note> at the southern side of the opening, and they were speaking among themselves. Because I was burning with a desire to hear what they were saying, it was first granted to me to hear the Sound, which was full of heavenly love, and afterwards their Speech, which was full of wisdom from that love.

They were speaking among themselves about the **ONE GOD**, and about **CONJUNCTION WITH HIM**, and from that, **SALVATION**. They spoke ineffable things, most of which cannot fall into the words of any natural language; but because I had been in the company of Angels in Heaven itself many times, and was then in a similar speech with them (being in a similar state), I was now able to understand them and select from their discourse certain things that can be expressed rationally in the words of natural language. 

They said that the **DIVINE BEING IS ONE, THE SAME, THE VERY REALITY, AND INDIVISIBLE.** They illustrated these things through spiritual ideas, saying that the Divine Being cannot fall upon several individuals, each of whom would possess the Divine Being, and yet that Being still be One, the Same, the Very Reality, and Indivisible. For if each were to think from his own Being by himself, and individually for himself—even if they then thought unanimously from the others and through the others—there would be several unanimous Gods, and not one God. For unanimity, because it is the agreement of several (and simultaneously of each one from himself and for himself), does not agree with the unity of God, but with plurality. They did not say "a plurality of Gods," because they could not; the Light of Heaven, from which their thought comes, and the aura in which their speech proceeded, resisted it. 

They also said that when they wished to utter the word "Gods," and to mean each Person by Himself, the effort to speak fell instantly into the word "One," indeed, into the "Only God." To this they added that the Divine Being is **DIVINE BEING IN ITSELF**, not "from itself"; for "from itself" implies a Being in itself from another prior source, thus it posits a "God from God," which is not possible. What is *from* God is not called God, but is called "the Divine." For what is a "God from God"? Thus, what is a "God from God born from eternity," and what is a "God from God proceeding through a God born from eternity," except words in which there is no light from Heaven? <note>This is a critique of the traditional Nicene Creed, which uses the phrase "God of God... begotten, not made."</note>

Furthermore, they said that the Divine Being, which in itself is God, is **THE SAME**—not a simple sameness, but infinite; that is, the Same from eternity to eternity. It is the Same everywhere, and the Same with every person and in every person; but all variety and changeability is in the recipient; the state of the recipient causes this. 

That the Divine Being, which is God in Himself, is **THE VERY REALITY** <note>original: "Ipsum," meaning the thing itself or the essential substance</note>, they illustrated thus: God is the Very Reality because He is Love itself and Wisdom itself, or because He is Good itself and Truth itself, and therefore Life itself. Unless these were the Very Reality in God, they would not be anything in Heaven or the world, because there would not be anything in them relative to the Very Reality. Every quality derives its quality from the fact that there is a "Very Reality" from which it exists, and to which it refers itself so that it may be such as it is. This **Very Reality**, which is the Divine **Being**...

26. Having heard these things, the Angels perceived in my thought the common ideas of the Christian Church concerning a Trinity of Persons in the Unity, and their Unity in the Trinity of God; as well as concerning the Birth of the Son of God from eternity. They then said, "What are you thinking? Are you thinking those things from natural Light, with which our spiritual Light does not agree? And they did so, and they saw that by three Persons I understand Three proceeding Divine Attributes, which are **CREATION**, **REDEMPTION**, and **REGENERATION**, and that those Attributes belong to One God. I explained that by the Birth of the Son of God from eternity, I understand His Birth foreseen from eternity and provided for in time. I argued that it is not only above nature and reason, but contrary to nature and reason, to think that any Son was born of God from eternity; but it is quite different to believe that the Son born of God through the Virgin Mary in time is the Unique and Only-begotten Son of God; and that to believe otherwise is a monstrous error. I then recounted that my natural thought concerning the Trinity and Unity of Persons, and the Birth of the Son of God from eternity, had come to me from the Doctrine of faith of the Church, which takes its name from <note>Athanasius (c. 296–373 AD) was a bishop whose name is attached to the Athanasian Creed, which defines the Trinity as three distinct persons.</note> Athanasius. Then the Angels said, "Well," and they asked that I say from their own mouths that if anyone does not approach the God of Heaven and Earth Himself, they cannot come into Heaven, because Heaven is Heaven from that One God; and **THAT THIS GOD IS JESUS CHRIST, WHO IS JEHOVAH THE LORD, FROM ETERNITY THE CREATOR, IN TIME THE REDEEMER, AND INTO ETERNITY THE REGENERATOR**, thus He who is simultaneously Father, Son, and Holy Spirit; and that this is the Gospel that must be preached. After this, the heavenly Light previously seen over the opening returned, and gradually lowered itself from there, filling the interiors of my mind and illustrating my ideas concerning the Trinity and Unity of God. I then saw the ideas I had initially held about them—which had been merely natural—separated, just as chaff is separated from wheat by a winnowing fan, and carried away as if by a wind into the North of Heaven, and they vanished.

# CONCERNING THE INFINITY OF GOD, OR HIS IMMENSITY AND ETERNITY.

27. There are two properties of the natural world that cause all things within it to be finite; one is SPACE, and the other is TIME. Because that world was created by God, and Spaces and Times were created along with that world and give it its limits, we must therefore treat of their two origins, which are *Immensity* and *Eternity*. For the Immensity of God relates to Spaces, and His Eternity to Times, and **Infinity** encompasses both Immensity and Eternity. But because Infinity transcends what is finite, and the knowledge of it transcends a finite Mind, it must be dealt with in this series so that it may be perceived in some way: I. *That God, because He is and Exists in Himself, and all things in the Universe are and exist from Him, is Infinite.* II. *That God, because He was before the World, and thus before Spaces and Times arose, is Infinite.* III. *That God, since the World was made, is in Space without Space, and in Time without Time.* IV. *That Infinity in relation to Spaces is called Immensity, and in relation to Times is called Eternity; and that although these relations exist, there is nevertheless nothing of Space in His Immensity, and nothing of Time in His Eternity.* V. *That Reason, when enlightened by the many things in the world, can see the Infinity of God the Creator.* VI. *That every created thing is finite, and that the Infinite is in finite things as in its receptors, and in men as in its images.* These points will be explained one by one.

28. I. **THAT GOD, BECAUSE HE IS AND EXISTS IN HIMSELF, AND ALL THINGS IN THE UNIVERSE ARE AND EXIST FROM HIM, IS INFINITE.** It has been shown so far that God is one, and that He is the "Itself," and that He is the primary <term>Being (Latin: *Esse*, the inner essence of God)</term> of all things, and that all things which are in the Universe, exist, and subsist, are from Him; from this it follows that He is Infinite. That human Reason can see this from the many things in the created Universe will be demonstrated in what follows. But although the human Mind can acknowledge from these things that the first Entity or first Being is infinite, it still cannot know *what kind* of thing that is; therefore, it cannot define it except as the "Infinite All," and as that which subsists in itself, and thus that it is the very and only Substance—and because nothing can be predicated of a substance unless it is a form, that it is the very and only Form. Yet even so, it does not appear what the Infinite is; for the human Mind itself, even when highly analytical and elevated, is finite, and the "finite" in it cannot be removed. For this reason, it is not at all capable of seeing the Infinity of God as it is in itself—that is, God Himself—but it can see God "in a shadow from behind," as was said to Moses when he prayed to see God: that he was placed in a cleft of the rock and saw His back parts (Exodus 33:20 to 23). <note>By "back parts" (Latin: *posteriora*), the author means the visible effects of God in the world and the perceivable truths in the Word, rather than God’s direct, infinite essence.</note> From these things it is clear that it is vain to wish to know what God is in His own Being or in His own Substance; but that it is enough to acknowledge Him from finite things—that is, created things—in which He is infinitely. A man who busies himself beyond this can be compared to a fish pulled out into the air, or to a bird placed in a vacuum pump, which gasps for breath as the air is pumped out and finally expires. He can also be compared to a ship which, when overcome by a storm and failing to obey the rudder, is carried onto rocks and quicksands; so it happens to those who wish to know the Infinity of God from within, not content that they can acknowledge it from without through manifest signs. We read of a certain Philosopher among the Ancients who, because he could not see or comprehend the Eternity of the World in the light of his own mind, threw himself into the sea; what might he have done if he had wished to comprehend the Infinity of God?

## 29. II. THAT GOD, SINCE HE EXISTED BEFORE THE WORLD, AND THUS BEFORE SPACES AND TIMES AROSE, IS INFINITE.

In the natural world, there are Times and Spaces, but in the Spiritual World <note>In this context, the "Spiritual World" refers to the realm inhabited by souls after death, which the author describes as a tangible but non-physical reality.</note> they do not exist so actually, but only apparently. The reason Times and Spaces were introduced into the Worlds was so that one thing might be distinguished from another: the great from the small, the many from the few—that is, quantity from quantity, and quality from quality—and so that the senses of the body might distinguish their objects and the senses of the mind theirs, and thus be affected, think, and choose. Times were introduced into the natural world by the Earth rotating on its axis, and by those rotations proceeding from station to station along the zodiac; these changes appear to be caused by the Sun, from which the entire terrestrial globe receives its heat and light. From this come the times of the Day—morning, noon, evening, and night—and the times of the Year—spring, summer, autumn, and winter. The times of the Days are for light and darkness, and the times of the Years are for heat and cold. Spaces, however, were introduced into the natural world by the Earth being massed into a sphere and filled with matter, the parts of which are distinct from one another and extended at the same time.

In the spiritual world, however, there are no material Spaces and the Times that correspond to them, yet there are still appearances of them. These appearances depend on the differences of the **states** <note>A "state" refers to the internal condition of a person's mind, specifically their feelings and thoughts.</note> in which the Minds of the spirits and angels there exist. Therefore, Times and Spaces there conform to the affections of their will and the resulting thoughts of their intellect. But these appearances are real, because they are constant according to those states. 

The common opinion regarding the State of Souls after death—and therefore also of Angels and Spirits—is that they are not in any "Extension" <note>Physical space or volume.</note> and consequently not in Space and Time. From this idea, it is said of souls after death that they are in a "Somewhere" or "Where" <note>original: "Pu seu Ubi"; philosophical terms for an undefined or non-spatial location.</note> and that Spirits and Angels are "Spirits" <note>original: "Pneumata"; Greek for breaths or spirits.</note> of which nothing is thought except as if they were like ether, air, breath, or wind. Yet they are actually **substantial humans** and live together just like people of the natural world, upon Spaces and in Times, which (as has been said) are determined according to the states of their minds. If it were otherwise—that is, without these dimensions—that whole Universe into which Souls flow and where Angels and Spirits dwell could be passed through the eye of a needle or concentrated on the tip of a single hair. This would be possible if there were no substantial Extension there; but since it does exist, Angels live among one another as discretely and distinctly as humans do who have material Extension. 

However, times there are not divided into Days, Weeks, Months, and Years, because the Sun there does not appear to rise and set, nor to revolve; instead, it remains stationary in the East at a middle degree between the Zenith and the Horizon. They also have Spaces because all things in that World are substantial, just as in the natural world they are material (more will be said on this in the section <note>original: "Lemmate"; a heading or specific part of a chapter.</note> of this Chapter concerning Creation). From what has been said, it can be understood that Spaces and Times limit each and every thing in both Worlds, and therefore humans are finite, not only in their bodies but also in their souls; the same applies to Angels and Spirits.

From all this, it can be concluded that God is Infinite—that is, not finite—because He Himself, as the Creator, Former, and Maker of the Universe, gave limits to all things. He limited them through His Sun, in the center of which He resides, and which consists of the Divine Essence that goes forth from Him like a sphere. There and from there is the beginning of limitation, but its progression continues to the very furthest reaches of the nature of the World. It follows that He is Infinite in Himself because He is uncreated. To a human, however, the infinite appears like "nothing," for the reason that a human is finite and thinks from finite things. Therefore, if the finite quality that clings to his thought were taken away, it would seem to him as if the remainder were nothing. Yet the truth is that God is infinitely **everything**, and that man, by comparison, is nothing of himself.

## 30. III. THAT GOD, AFTER THE WORLD WAS MADE, IS IN SPACE WITHOUT SPACE, AND IN TIME WITHOUT TIME.

That God, and the Divine which proceeds immediately from Him, is not in Space, even though He is Omnipresent and with

# OF THE NEW HEAVEN AND THE NEW CHURCH.

...in every human being in the World, and in every Angel in Heaven, and in every Spirit under heaven, cannot be understood through a purely natural idea, but can be understood to some extent through a spiritual idea. The reason it cannot be understood through a purely natural idea is that such an idea contains Space; for it is formed from the things that exist in the World, and in each and every thing seen by the eyes, there is Space. Everything large and small there belongs to Space; everything long, wide, and high there belongs to Space; in a word, every measurement, figure, and form there belongs to Space. Yet, a person can still understand this to some extent through natural thought, provided they admit some spiritual light into it. But first, something must be said about the idea of spiritual thought: this does not derive anything from Space, but derives its everything from <term>State</term> <note>In this theological context, "State" refers to the internal condition of a person’s mind or soul—their love, wisdom, and feelings—rather than their physical location.</note>. State is spoken of in relation to love, life, wisdom, affections, and joys—in general, regarding what is good and true. A truly Spiritual idea of these things has nothing in common with Space; it is superior, and looks down upon ideas of Space beneath it, just as heaven looks down upon the earth.

The reason God is present in Space without space, and in Time without time, is that God is always the same, from eternity to eternity; thus, He is the same after the world was created as He was before it. Before creation, spaces and times did not exist in God or before God, but only after it. Therefore, because He is the Same, He is in Space without being limited by space, and in Time without being limited by time. From this it follows that nature is separate from Him, and yet He is omnipresent within it; much like how life is present in every substantial and material part of a human being, even though it does not mix itself with them. To use a comparison, He is like light in the eyes, sound in the ears, taste on the tongue, or like the <term>ether</term> <note>The "ether" was historically believed to be a subtle fluid filling all space and transmitting light and heat.</note> in the land and waters, by which the terrestrial globe is held together and rotated. If these active forces were taken away, those substantial and material things would collapse or fall apart in an instant. Indeed, the human Mind, if God were not present in it everywhere and at all times, would dissipate like a bubble in the air; and both halves of the Brain, in which the mind acts from its first principles, would turn to foam. Thus, everything human would become the dust of the earth, or a fleeting odor in the atmosphere.

Because God is in all time without time, He speaks in His Word of the past and the future in the present tense, as in Isaiah: <note>original Latin: "Puer natus est nobis, Filius datus est, cujus nomen est, Heros, Princeps pacis"</note> *“A child is born to us, a Son is given, whose name is Hero, Prince of Peace,”* Chapter IX: 5. And in David: <note>original Latin: "Annuntiabo de statuto, Jehovath dixit ad me, Filius meus Tu, Hodie genui te"</note> *“I will announce the decree, Jehovah said to me, You are my Son, today I have begotten you,”* Psalm II: 7. These refer to the Lord who was to come. For this reason, it is also said in the same place: <note>original Latin: "Mille anni in oculis tuis sicut dies hesternus"</note> *“A thousand years in your eyes are like yesterday,”* Psalm XC: 4. That He is present everywhere in the Universal World, and yet nothing of the World's own nature is in Him—that is, nothing belonging to space and time—can be clearly seen from many other places in the Word by those who are observant and watchful, such as this in Jeremiah: <note>original Latin: "Numne Deus in propinquo Ego, & non Deus e longinquo; num occultabitur vir in latibulis ut Ego non videam, omne Cœlum & omnem Terram Ego impleo"</note> *“Am I a God at hand, and not a God from afar? Can a man hide himself in secret places so that I shall not see him? Do I not fill all Heaven and all Earth?”* Chapter XXIII: 23, 24.

## 31. IV. THAT THE INFINITY OF GOD IN RELATION TO SPACES IS CALLED IMMENSITY, AND IN RELATION TO TIMES IS CALLED ETERNITY; AND THAT ALTHOUGH THESE RELATIONSHIPS EXIST, YET THERE IS NOTHING OF SPACE IN HIS IMMENSITY, AND NOTHING OF TIME IN HIS ETERNITY.

The reason the Infinity of God in relation to spaces is called Immensity is that "Immense" is predicated of what is Great and Ample, and also of what is Extended, and therein of what is Spacious. However, the reason the Infinity of God in relation to times is called Eternity is that "Eternal" is predicated of progressive things that are measured by times, without end. For example: of the terrestrial globe viewed in itself, those things belonging to space are predicated; and of its rotation and progression, those things belonging to time are predicated. These latter make times, and the former make spaces, and they are presented thus through the senses in the perception of reflecting minds. But in God there is nothing of space and time, as was shown above, and yet the beginnings of these are from God. It follows from this that His Infinity in relation to spaces is understood as Immensity, and His Infinity in relation to times is understood as...

...Eternity. But in Heaven, the Divinity is perceived by the Angels through the **Immensity** of God in regard to <term>Being</term> <note>original: "Esse"; the essential substance or "is-ness" of God</note>, and through **Eternity** the Divinity in regard to <term>Existing</term> <note>original: "Existere"; the manifestation or "going forth" of God's Being</note>; also, through Immensity the Divinity in regard to **Love**, and through Eternity the Divinity in regard to **Wisdom**. The reason for this is that Angels abstract space and time from the Divinity, and then those spiritual notions result.

But because a human being cannot think except from ideas captured from such things as belong to space and time, they cannot perceive anything of God's Immensity before spaces, and of His Eternity before times; indeed, when they wish to perceive them, it is as if their mind falls into a swoon, almost like someone who has fallen into the water and is in a state of shipwreck, or like someone sinking into the earth in a state of being swallowed up. Indeed, if they persist in trying to penetrate those mysteries, they can easily fall into a delirium, and from this be led into a denial of God. 

I myself was once in a similar state, thinking about what God did from eternity—what He did before the World was created; whether He deliberated about Creation and thought out the order according to which it should be done; and whether deliberative thought could exist in a pure vacuum, among other useless ideas. But lest I be carried away into delusions by such things, I was raised by the Lord into the sphere and light in which the interior angels are. After the idea of space and time, in which my thought had previously been, was slightly removed there, it was granted to me to understand that the **Eternity of God** is not an eternity of time; and that because time did not exist before the World, it would be utterly vain to think such things about God. Furthermore, because the Divine from eternity—and thus abstracted from all time—does not involve days, years, and centuries, but because all these things are to God an **Instant**, I concluded that the World was created by God not *in* time, but that times were introduced by God *with* the creation.

To this I will add this **Memorable Relation**: two Statues appear in a monstrous human form with gaping mouths and widened jaws at one extremity of the Spiritual World; those who think vain and insane things about God from eternity seem to themselves to be swallowed up by these statues. But these are fantasies into which those cast themselves who think absurd and improper things about God before the World was created.

### 32. V. THAT ENLIGHTENED REASON CAN SEE THE INFINITY OF GOD FROM VERY MANY THINGS IN THE WORLD.

A few things will be listed from which human Reason can see the Infinity of God:

**I.** That in the Created Universe, no two things are given that are the same. Human learning has seen and confirmed from reason that such <term>Identity</term> <note>Absolute sameness or being identical</note> does not exist in things occurring simultaneously, and yet the substantial and material parts of the universe, viewed individually, are infinite in number. That there is no Identity between two effects in successive things in the World can be concluded from the rotation of the Earth; the eccentricity of its poles ensures that no same position ever returns. That this is so is clearly evident from human faces: in the Universal World, there is not one face exactly like or the same as another, nor can there be for eternity. This infinite variety could by no means exist except from the Infinity of God the Creator.

**II.** That no one's Mind <note>original: "Animus"; often referring to the lower or natural mind</note> is exactly like another's, which is why it is said, **"as many heads, so many minds"** <note>original: "quot capita tot animi"</note>; hence, no one's Mind <note>original: "Mens"; the higher or intellectual mind</note>—that is, the will and understanding—is exactly like or the same as another's. Consequently, no one's speech, in regard to its sound and the thought from which it comes, nor anyone's action in regard to gesture and the affection behind it, are perfectly equal to another's. From this infinite variety, as in a mirror, the Infinity of God the Creator can be seen.

**III.** That in every seed, whether of animals or vegetables, there is implanted a certain immensity and eternity: **immensity**, in that it can be multiplied to infinity; and **eternity**, in that such multiplication has persisted without interruption from the creation of the World until now, and will persist forever. Take the fish of the sea from the animal kingdom; if they were multiplied according to the abundance of their seeds, within 20 or 50 years they would fill the Ocean until it consisted of nothing but fish, and then its water would flood the entire Earth and thus destroy it. But lest this happen, it has been provided by God that fish should serve as food for other fish. It would be the same with the seeds of vegetables; if as many as arise from one seed every year were planted, within 20 or 30 years they would fill the surface not only of one earth,

of the earth, but also of many earths; for there are shrubs, each one of whose seeds produces hundreds and thousands of others; test this by calculation, by multiplying the production of one continuously by 20 or 30, and you will see; from these examples the Divine **Immensity** and **Eternity** can be seen, from which it is impossible that a similar production should not be brought forth in a certain general aspect. 

IV. The Infinity of God, illustrated before **Reason**, can also appear from the infinity into which every science can grow, and likewise any intelligence and wisdom; both of these can grow like a tree from seeds, and like forests and gardens from trees, for there is no end to them. The memory of man is their soil, the intellect is where they germinate, and the will is where they bear fruit; and these two faculties, the intellect and the will, are such that they can be cultivated and perfected in the World until the end of life, and afterwards into eternity. 

V. The Infinity of God the Creator can also be seen from the infinite number of Stars, which are so many Suns, and therefore so many Worlds; that in the starry Heaven there are also Earths <note>The author is referring to his work "Earths in the Universe," where he describes visions of life on other planets.</note> upon which are men, beasts, birds, and plants, has been shown in a certain small Work described from things seen. 

VI. The Infinity of God became even more evident to me from the Angelic Heaven, and also from Hell, because those two are ordered and coordinated into innumerable Societies or Congregations according to all the varieties of the love of good and evil, and everyone is assigned a place according to their own love. For everyone there is from the Human Race, collected since the Creation of the World, and to be collected for ages of ages; and although everyone has their own place or their own seat, nevertheless all there are so joined together that the whole Angelic Heaven represents one <term>Divine Man</term> <note>The "Grand Man" (Maximus Homo), a concept where the entire community of heaven functions as a single human organism.</note>, and the whole Hell represents one monstrous Devil; from these two, and from the infinite wonders within them, the **Immensity** together with the **Omnipotence** of God is clearly presented to be seen. 

VII. Who also cannot understand, if they elevate the reasoning of their mind even a little, that life into eternity—which belongs to every person after death—could not be given except by an Eternal God? 

VIII. Besides those things, there is a certain Infinity in many things that fall into the <term>natural light</term> <note>Lumen naturale: the light of human reason and sensory experience</note> and into the <term>spiritual light</term> <note>Lumen spirituale: divine truth that illuminates the soul</note> within man. In natural light: that there are various Series in Geometry which go into infinity; that between the three <term>degrees of altitude</term> <note>A technical term for "discrete degrees" (End, Cause, Effect) which are distinct levels of reality, like soul and body, rather than just variations in shade or size.</note> there is a progression into infinity, namely, that the first Degree, which is called natural, cannot be perfected and raised to the perfection of the second degree, which is called spiritual, nor this to the perfection of the third, which is called celestial. The same is true between the end, the cause, and the effect, such that the effect cannot be perfected to become like its cause, nor the cause to become like its end. This can be illustrated by the <term>atmospheres</term> <note>The invisible spiritual and natural layers of the universe.</note>, of which there are three degrees: there is the highest <term>aura</term>, the ether below that, and the air below this; and any quality of the air cannot be raised to any quality of the ether, nor that of the ether to any quality of the aura; and yet an elevation of perfections into infinity is given in each one. In spiritual light: that natural love, which belongs to a beast, cannot be raised into spiritual love, which was implanted in man from creation; it is the same with the natural intelligence of a beast relative to the spiritual intelligence of a man. But because these things are still unknown, they will be explained elsewhere. From these things it can be established that the universals of the World are perpetual types of the Infinity of God the Creator: how, however, particulars emulate universals and represent the Infinity of God, is an Abyss, and is an Ocean in which the human Mind can, as it were, sail, but it must beware of the storm arising from the natural man, which will submerge the ship, with masts and sails, from the stern where the self-confident natural man stands.

### 33. VI. THAT EVERYTHING CREATED IS FINITE, AND THAT THE INFINITE IS IN FINITE THINGS AS IN RECEPTACLES, AND IN HUMANS AS IN HIS IMAGES.

That everything created is finite is because all things are from Jehovah God through the Sun of the spiritual world, which most closely encompasses Him; and that Sun is from the substance which went out from Him, the essence of which is love; from that Sun, through its heat and light, the Universe was created from its firsts to its lasts; but to set forth the progress of creation in order...

### UNIVERSAL THEOLOGY

This is not the place for it, but a certain outline of it will be given in what follows. Here it is only of interest to know that one thing is formed from another, and that <term>degrees</term> <note>Swedenborg uses the term "degrees" to describe distinct levels of reality, like the difference between a thought and the action that follows it.</note> were made from this—three in the spiritual world, three corresponding to them in the natural world, and just as many in the inert substances out of which the terraqueous globe consists. But where those degrees come from, and what they are like, has been fully explained in *ANGELIC WISDOM CONCERNING DIVINE LOVE AND DIVINE WISDOM*, published in Amsterdam in the year 1763 <note>original: "SAPIENTIA ANGELICA de DIVINO AMORE ET DIVINA SAPIENTIA"</note>; and in the short work *ON THE INTERCOURSE BETWEEN SOUL AND BODY*, published in London in the year 1769 <note>original: "COMMERCIO ANIMÆ ET CORPORIS"</note>. Through these degrees, it has come to pass that all later things are receptacles of prior ones, and these again of things even more prior, and so in order they are receptacles of the first things of which the Sun of the Angelic Heaven consists; thus, finites are receptacles of the Infinite. This also coincides with the wisdom of the Ancients, from which comes the idea that each and every thing is divisible into infinity. The common idea is that, because the finite is not capable of containing the infinite, finite things cannot be receptacles of the infinite; but from those things handed down in *MY WORKS on Creation*, it is clear that God first "finitized" His Infinity through substances sent out from Himself, from which His nearest surrounding area, which makes the Sun of the spiritual world, came into being; and that thereafter, through that Sun, He perfected the remaining surrounding layers down to the last one, which consists of inert matter; and that thus He finitized the world more and more through degrees. These things are cited for the purpose of satisfying human reason, which does not rest unless it sees a cause.

34. That the Divine Infinite is in humans as in His images is evident from the *Word* <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note>, where we read: "Finally God said, let us make man in our Image, according to our likeness; and so God created man into His own Image, into the image of God he created him," Genesis 1: 26, 27. From these words it follows that man is a receiving organ of God, and that he is an organ according to the quality of his reception. The human mind—from which and according to which a man is a man—is formed into three regions according to three degrees. In the first degree is the "celestial" region, in which the angels of the highest heaven also dwell; in the second degree is the "spiritual" region, in which the angels of the middle heaven dwell; and in the third degree is the "natural" region, in which the angels of the lowest heaven dwell. The human mind, organized according to those three degrees, is a receptacle of Divine <term>influx</term> <note>Influx is the spiritual concept of life or energy "flowing in" from God to the soul.</note>; but the Divine does not flow in any further than the person clears the way or opens the door. If he does this all the way to the highest or celestial degree, then the man becomes truly an image of God, and after death becomes an angel of the highest heaven; but if he clears the way or opens the door only to the middle or spiritual degree, then the man indeed becomes an image of God, but not in that same perfection, and after death becomes an angel of the middle heaven. However, if he only clears the way or opens the door to the lowest or natural degree, then the man—if he acknowledges God and worships Him with actual piety—becomes an image of God in the lowest degree, and after death becomes an angel of the lowest heaven.

But if he does not acknowledge God and does not worship Him with actual piety, he strips off the image of God and becomes like a certain animal, except for the fact that he enjoys the faculty of understanding and, from that, the ability to speak. If he then shuts the highest natural degree (which corresponds to the highest celestial), he becomes, regarding his love, like a beast of the earth; if he shuts the middle natural degree (which corresponds to the middle spiritual), he becomes like a fox in his love, and like an owl <note>original: "avis vesperæ," literally "bird of the evening."</note> in the sight of his intellect; but if he also shuts the lowest natural degree in regard to its spiritual part, he becomes like a wild beast in his love, and like a fish in his understanding of truth. Divine Life, which actuates man through influx from the Sun of the Angelic Heaven, can be compared with light from the Sun of the world and its influx into a transparent object. The reception of life in the highest degree is like the influx of light into a diamond; the reception of life in the second degree is like the influx of light into a crystal; and the reception of life in the last degree is like the influx of light into glass or a transparent membrane. But if this degree were entirely shut off in regard to its spiritual part—which happens when God is denied and Satan is worshiped—the reception of life from God can be compared with the influx of light into the opaque things of the earth, such as rotten wood, or the turf of a swamp, or dung, and so on; for the man then becomes a spiritual corpse.

35. To these things I will add this **MEMORABLE RELATION**. Once, I was in a state of wonder at the vast multitude of people who credit Creation to Nature, and consequently all things under the Sun and all things above the Sun. These people say from the acknowledgment of their heart, when they see anything, "Is this not from Nature?" And when they are asked why they say those things are from Nature and not from God—when yet they occasionally say, in agreement with the Common Faith, that God created Nature and therefore could just as easily say that what they see is of God as of Nature—they respond with an internal tone that is almost silent, "What is God but Nature?" 

All those who are convinced that the Universe was created by Nature appear—from that insanity which they take for wisdom—so glorious in their own eyes that they look down on all who acknowledge the Creation of the Universe from God. They view them like ants crawling on the ground and treading a worn path, and some like butterflies flying in the air, calling their doctrines dreams because they see what they do not see, saying, "Who has seen God? and who does not see Nature?" 

While I was in wonder at the multitude of such people, an Angel stood at my side and said to me, "What are you meditating upon?" I answered, "About the multitude of such people who believe that Nature exists of itself, and is thus the creator of the Universe." The Angel said to me, "All of Hell consists of such people. They are called Satans and Devils there—Satans <note>In Swedenborg's theology, "Satans" are those who have confirmed themselves in false intellectual ideas, while "Devils" are those who are in the evils of the will or lifestyle.</note> are those who have confirmed themselves in favor of Nature and therefore denied God; Devils are those who have lived wickedly and thus rejected all acknowledgment of God from their hearts. But I will lead you to the <term>Gymnasia</term> <note>In the spiritual world, these are centers of learning or debate where those recently deceased explore their philosophical convictions.</note> which are in the south-western quarter, where such people are found before they are sent to Hell." 

He took me by the hand and led me; and I saw small houses, in which were the schools, and in the middle of them one that was like the headquarters for the rest. This was built of pitch-black stones, which were covered with thin plates like glass, shimmering with gold and silver, such as those called <term>selenites</term> <note>A transparent variety of gypsum, also known as moonstone or mirror-stone, used in the past for windows.</note> or specular stones; and here and there shining seashells were interspersed. 

We approached and knocked, and soon someone opened the door and said, "Welcome." He ran to a table and brought four books, saying, "These books are the Wisdom which a multitude of kingdoms applaud today: many in France <note>original: "Gallia"</note> applaud this book or wisdom, many in Germany <note>original: "Germania"</note> this one, some in Holland <note>original: "Batavia"</note> this one, and some in Britain <note>original: "Britannia"</note> this one." He further said, "If you wish to see, I will make these four books shine before your eyes." Then he poured out and spread around the glory of his own reputation, and the books soon shone as if from light; but this light vanished instantly before our eyes. 

Then we asked what he was writing now, and he replied that he was now bringing forth and expressing from his treasures things of the most inward wisdom, which in summary are these: 
I. *Whether Nature is of Life, or whether Life is of Nature.* 
II. *Whether the Center is of the Expanse, or whether the Expanse is of the Center.* 
III. *Concerning the Center of the Expanse and of Life.* 

Having said this, he sat back down on a throne at the table, while we walked about in his school, which was spacious. He had a candle on the table because there was no sunlight there, but rather a nocturnal lunar light. And, to my surprise, the candle seemed to be carried around and give light; but because it was not trimmed, it gave little light. And while he wrote, we saw images in various forms flying from the table to the walls, which in that nocturnal moonlight appeared like beautiful Indian birds; but when we opened the door, behold, in the daily sunlight they appeared like evening birds <note>Likely bats or owls, symbolizing thoughts that cannot bear the light of truth.</note> with net-like wings. For they were "similarities" <note>Appearances that seem like truth but are actually based on false premises.</note> which had been made into fallacies through confirmations, which he had ingeniously connected into series. 

After we saw these things, we approached the table and asked him what he was writing now. He said, concerning that first point, **WHETHER NATURE IS OF LIFE, OR WHETHER LIFE IS OF NATURE**. Regarding this, he said he could confirm both and make either be true; but because something hidden lies within which he fears, he dared not confirm anything except that Nature is of Life—that is, from Life—but not that Life is of Nature—that is, from...

The scene highlights how false intellectualism can appear beautiful in the dim light of self-intelligence but is revealed as monstrous when exposed to Divine light.</summary>

## ON THE ESSENCE OF GOD, WHICH IS DIVINE LOVE AND DIVINE WISDOM.

36. We have distinguished between the <term>Being</term> <note>original: "Esse"</note> of God and the <term>Essence</term> <note>original: "Essentia"</note> of God, because we distinguish between the Infinity of God and the Love of God. Infinity is applied to the Being of God, and Love to the Essence of God. For, as said before, Being is more universal than Essence, just as Infinity is more universal than Love. Therefore, "Infinite" is an adjective for God's essentials and attributes, all of which are called infinite—as we say of Divine Love that it is infinite, of Divine Wisdom that it is infinite, and similarly of Divine Power. This is not because God's Being exists prior to His Essence, but because it enters the Essence as a cohesive addition, determining, forming, and at the same time elevating it. This section of the chapter, like the previous ones, will be divided into the following articles: *I. That God is Love itself and Wisdom itself, and that these two constitute His Essence. II. That God is Good itself and Truth itself, because Good belongs to love, and Truth to wisdom. III. That Love itself and Wisdom itself are Life itself, which is Life in itself. IV. That Love and Wisdom make one in God. V. That the essence of love is to love others outside of oneself, to want to be one with them, and to make them happy from oneself. VI. That these aspects of divine love were the cause of the creation of the Universe, and that they are the cause of its preservation.* But we shall speak of these individually.

### 37. I. THAT GOD IS LOVE ITSELF AND WISDOM ITSELF, AND THAT THESE TWO CONSTITUTE HIS ESSENCE.

The truth that Love and Wisdom are the two essentials to which all the infinite things in God and proceeding from God refer was seen by the earliest people <note>original: "prima Antiquitus" - likely referring to what the author calls the "Most Ancient Church" or prehistoric spiritual wisdom</note>. But succeeding ages gradually lost sight of this as they drew their minds away from Heaven and immersed them in worldly and bodily things. They began to not know what Love is in its essence, and consequently what Wisdom is in its essence, not knowing that Love, when abstracted from form, cannot exist, and that it works in and through form. Now, because God is the self-same and only—and thus the first—Substance and Form, whose Essence is Love and Wisdom, and because all things that were made were made from Him, it follows that He created the Universe with each and every part of it from Love through Wisdom. Consequently, Divine Love together with Divine Wisdom is in each and every created thing. Love is also not only the essence that forms all things, but also the essence that unites and joins them, thus keeping the formed things in connection. 

These things can be illustrated by countless examples in the world: such as by **HEAT** and **LIGHT** from the Sun, which are the two essentials and universals through which each and every thing on Earth exists and subsists. These exist there because they correspond to Divine Love and Divine Wisdom; for the Heat that proceeds from the Sun of the spiritual world is, in its essence, Love, and the Light from it is, in its essence, Wisdom. These can also be illustrated by the two essentials and universals by which human minds exist and subsists, which are the **WILL** and the **UNDERSTANDING**. Every person's mind consists of these two, and those two are and operate in each and every part of it; the reason is that the Will is the receptacle and dwelling-place of love, and the Understanding is similarly the dwelling-place of wisdom. Therefore, those two correspond to the Divine Love and Divine Wisdom from which they originate. 

Furthermore, these same things can be illustrated by the two essentials and universals by which human bodies exist and subsist, which are the **HEART** and the **LUNGS**, or the <term>systole and diastole</term> <note>The rhythmic contraction and expansion</note> of the heart and the respiration of the lungs. It is well known that these two operate in each and every part of the body; the reason is that the Heart corresponds to love, and the Lungs to wisdom. This correspondence has been fully demonstrated in *Angelic Wisdom concerning Divine Love and Divine Wisdom*, published in Amsterdam <note>Referring to the author's 1763 work *Sapientia Angelica de Divino Amore et de Divina Sapientia*</note>. That Love, like a bridegroom and husband...

### 38. II. THAT GOD IS GOOD ITSELF AND TRUTH ITSELF, BECAUSE GOOD BELONGS TO LOVE, AND TRUTH TO WISDOM.

It is universally known that all things relate to good and truth—an indication that all things exist from Love and Wisdom. For everything that proceeds from love is called good, as it is felt; and the delight through which love manifests itself is good to everyone. However, everything that proceeds from Wisdom is called truth, for wisdom consists of nothing but truths, and it affects its objects with the pleasantness of light; and this pleasantness, when perceived, is truth derived from good. Therefore, Love is the complex of all goodness, and Wisdom is the complex of all truths. But both of these are from God, who is Love itself and therefore Good itself, and Wisdom itself and therefore Truth itself. 

Because of this, there are two essentials in the Church called <term>Charity</term> and <term>Faith</term>, which consist of each and every part of the church and must be within them all. The reason is that all the goods of the Church belong to charity and are called Charity, and all its truths belong to faith and are called Faith. The delights of love, which are also the delights of charity, cause those delights to be called "goods"; and the pleasantnesses of wisdom, which are also the pleasantnesses of faith, cause truths to be called "truths." For delights and pleasantness constitute their life; without life from these, goods and truths are like inanimate things and are also sterile. 

But the delights of love are of two kinds, as are the pleasantnesses that appear to belong to wisdom: namely, the delights of a good Love and the delights of an evil love; and consequently, the pleasantnesses of a faith in truth and the pleasantnesses of a faith in what is false. Both of those delights of Love, in the subjects where they exist, are called "goods" based on how they are felt; and both those pleasantnesses of faith, from their perception, are also called "goods," but because they are in the intellect, they are actually nothing other than truths. This remains true even though they are opposites: the "good" of one love is truly good, while the "good" of the other love is evil; likewise, the "truth" of one faith is truth, while the "truth" of the other faith is false. 

But the Love whose delight is essentially good is like the heat of the Sun—fructifying, life-giving, and working upon fertile soil, upon trees of use, and upon crops. Where it works, it becomes like a paradise, a <term>garden of Jehovah</term>, and like the land of Canaan. The pleasantness of its truth is like light from the Sun in springtime, or like light flowing into a crystal vessel containing beautiful flowers, which, when opened, breathes out a sweet scent. 

But the delight of an evil love is like the parching heat of the Sun—killing and working upon sterile soil, upon harmful trees like thorns and briars. Where it works, it becomes like an Arabian desert where there are <term>hydra-serpents</term> and <term>burning snakes</term> <note>original: "presteres," referring to a type of venomous snake mentioned in classical literature whose bite causes intense thirst or burning inflammation</note>. The pleasantness of its falsity is like light from the Sun in wintertime, or like light flowing into a leather bottle in which worms swim in vinegar and stinking reptiles crawl. 

It should be known that every good forms itself through truths and also clothes itself through them, thus distinguishing itself from other goods. Furthermore, the goods of one lineage bind themselves into bundles and clothe these together, thus distinguishing themselves from others. That such formations occur is evident from each and every part of the human Body; and that something similar occurs...

**39. III. THAT GOD, BECAUSE HE IS LOVE ITSELF AND WISDOM ITSELF, IS LIFE ITSELF, WHICH IS LIFE IN ITSELF.** It is said in John: "*The Word was with God, and the Word was God... In Him was Life, and the Life was the Light of men*" (Chapter 1:1, 4). By "God" there is meant Divine Love, and by "the Word," Divine Wisdom. Strictly speaking, Divine Wisdom is Life, and Life is the Light that proceeds from the Sun of the spiritual world, in the center of which is <term>Jehovah God</term>. Divine Love forms Life just as fire forms light. In fire there are two properties: burning heat and brightness. From its burning heat comes warmth, and from its brightness comes light. Similarly, in Love there are two properties: one to which the burning heat of fire corresponds, which is something that deeply affects the human will; and another to which the brightness of fire corresponds, which is something that deeply affects the human understanding. From this, a human being has love and intelligence. For, as has been said several times before, from the Sun of the spiritual world proceeds Heat, which in its essence is love, and Light, which in its essence is wisdom. These two flow into each and every part of the Universe and affect them most deeply—and in humans, they flow into their will and understanding. These two were created as receptacles for this <term>Influx</term> <note>The spiritual "flow" of life from God into the soul, similar to how light flows into a room.</note>: the will is the receptacle of love, and the understanding is the receptacle of wisdom. Thus it is clear that a person's life resides in the Understanding, and that it is of such a quality as his wisdom is, and that the love of the will modifies it.

40. We also read in John: *As the Father has life in Himself, so has He given also to the Son to have life in Himself* (Chapter 5:26). Life in itself is the very and only Life, from which all angels and humans live. Human reason can see this from the Light that proceeds from the Sun of the natural world: this light is not "creatable," but the forms that receive it are created. For example, the eyes are its <term>recipient forms</term>, and the light flowing from the Sun allows them to see. It is the same with Life, which (as was said) is the Light proceeding from the Sun of the spiritual world. It is not creatable, but it flows in continuously, and just as it illuminates, it also gives life to the human Understanding. Consequently, because Light, Life, and Wisdom are one, Wisdom is not creatable; similarly, neither is faith, nor truth, nor love, nor charity, nor good. Rather, the forms that receive them are created. Human and angelic minds are those forms.

Therefore, let everyone be careful not to persuade themselves that they live from themselves, or that they are wise, believe, love, perceive truth, or will and do good from themselves. ## 41. IV. THAT LOVE AND WISDOM MAKE ONE IN GOD.

Every wise person in the Church knows that every good of love and charity is from God, and similarly every truth of wisdom and faith. Human Reason can also see that this is so, provided it knows that the origin of love and wisdom is from the Sun of the spiritual world, in the center of which is <term>Jehovah God</term> <note>The name for God emphasizing His self-existent being and the source of all life.</note>, or—what is the same thing—that it is from Jehovah God through the Sun that surrounds Him. For the Heat proceeding from that Sun is, in its essence, love; and the Light proceeding from it is, in its essence, wisdom. Hence, it is as clear as day that love and wisdom are one in that origin, and consequently in God, from whom that Sun originates.

This can also be illustrated by the sun of the natural world, which is pure Fire: from its fiery nature proceeds heat, and from the radiance of its fire proceeds light; thus, both are one in their origin. However, that they are divided in the process of proceeding is evident from the objects that receive them, some of which receive more heat and some more light. This happens especially with human beings. In them, the Light of life (which is intelligence) and the Heat of life (which is love) are divided. This happens because a person must be <term>reformed and regenerated</term> <note>The process of spiritual rebirth and the reshaping of one's character.</note>, and this cannot happen unless the Light of life, which is Intelligence, teaches what ought to be willed and loved. 

It should be known, however, that God continually works to bring about the union of love and wisdom in man, but unless a person looks to God and believes in Him, that person continually works to divide them. Therefore, to the extent that these two—the good of love or charity and the truth of wisdom or faith—are joined together in a person, that person becomes an <term>image of God</term> and is raised toward Heaven and into Heaven where the angels are. Conversely, to the extent that those two are divided by a person, that person becomes an image of Lucifer and the Dragon <note>Symbolic figures representing prideful self-intelligence and the separation of faith from good deeds.</note>, and is cast down from Heaven to the earth, and then beneath the earth into Hell. 

From the conjunction of these two, a person's state becomes like that of a tree in springtime, when heat joins equally with light, resulting in its budding, flowering, and fruiting. But conversely, from the division of these two, a person's state becomes like that of a tree in wintertime, when heat withdraws from the light, resulting in it being stripped bare of every leaf and branch. When spiritual heat (which is love) separates itself from spiritual light (which is wisdom)—or what is the same, charity from faith—a person becomes like souring or rotting soil in which worms are born; and if it produces shrubs, their leaves are filled with lice and are consumed. For the allurements of evil love, which are in themselves lusts, break out; the Intelligence does not tame or restrain them, but instead loves, educates, and nourishes them. In a word, to divide love and wisdom, or charity and faith (two things which God continually strives to join), is comparatively like robbing a face of its healthy redness, leaving the paleness of the dead, or taking the whiteness away from the red, leaving the face like a flaming torch. It is also like dissolving the marriage bond between two people, making the wife a harlot and the husband an adulterer; for love or charity is like a husband, and wisdom or faith is like a wife, and when those two are separated, there occurs spiritual whoredom and adultery, which are the falsification of truth and the adulteration of good.

## 42.

Beyond these things, it should be known that there are three levels of love and wisdom, and consequently three levels of life, and that the human Mind is formed into regions according to these levels. Life in the highest region is at the highest level; in the second region, it is at a lower level; and in the final region, it is at the lowest level. These regions are opened successively in human beings. The lowest region, where life is at the lowest level, is opened from infancy to childhood, and this happens through the sciences <note>original Latin: "scientias," referring to basic acquired knowledge or facts.</note>. The second region, where life is at a higher level, is opened from childhood to adolescence, and this happens through thoughts derived from those sciences. And the highest region, where life is at the highest level, is opened from adolescence to youth and beyond, and this happens through the perceptions of truths, both moral and spiritual. Furthermore, it should be known that the perfection of life does not consist in thought, but in the perception of truth from the light of truth. The differences of life among men can be concluded <note>The Latin text cuts off here with the catchword "clu-", which would complete the word "concludi" (be concluded/inferred) on the next page.</note>...

There are others who do not perceive the truth immediately but conclude it through confirmations based on appearances; these are represented by songbirds. There are those who believe something to be true simply because it was dictated by a man of authority; these are represented by magpies. Furthermore, there are those who are unwilling, as well as those who are unable, to perceive truth, but only what is false. The reason for this is that they are in a "fatuitous light" <note>A deceptive or foolish light that mimics true intelligence but leads to error.</note>, in which what is false appears as true, while the truth appears either like something hidden in a thick cloud above the head, like a fleeting meteor, or even like a falsehood. The thoughts of these people are represented by owls, and their speech by screech-owls. Those among them who have confirmed their own falsehoods cannot bear to hear truths; as soon as any truth knocks at the door of their ears, they repel it with aversion, much like a nauseated, bilious stomach rejects food.

## 43. V. THAT THE ESSENCE OF LOVE IS TO LOVE OTHERS OUTSIDE ONESELF, TO DESIRE TO BE ONE WITH THEM, AND TO MAKE THEM HAPPY FROM ONESELF.

There are two things that constitute the essence of God: Love and Wisdom. However, there are three things that constitute the essence of His Love: to love others outside Himself, to desire to be one with them, and to make them happy from Himself. These same three also constitute the essence of His Wisdom, because Love and Wisdom make one in God (as shown above), but Love wills these things, and Wisdom produces them.

**THE FIRST ESSENTIAL**, which is to love others outside oneself, is recognized in God's love for the entire human race; and for the sake of humanity, God loves everything He has created, because they are the means to an end. For whoever loves an end also loves the means. All things in the universe are "outside" God because they are finite, and God is Infinite. The love of God reaches and extends itself not only to good people and good things, but also to evil people and evil things; consequently, not only to those in Heaven, but also to those in Hell—thus, not only to Michael and Gabriel <note>Traditional names for high-ranking angels, representing the celestial and spiritual heavens.</note>, but also to the devil and satan <note>In this context, Swedenborg often uses "devil" to refer to the love of self and "satan" to the love of the world or false thinking.</note>. For God is everywhere and is the same from eternity to eternity. He also says, *that He makes His sun rise on the good and the evil, and sends rain on the just and the unjust* (Matthew 5:45). But the reason that the evil remain evil and evil things remain evil lies in the subjects and objects themselves—they do not receive the love of God as it is in its inner essence, but only as they themselves are. This is similar to how a thorn or a nettle reacts to the heat of the sun and the rain from the sky.

**THE SECOND ESSENTIAL OF DIVINE LOVE**, which is to desire to be one with them, is recognized from His conjunction with the angelic Heaven, with the Church on earth, and with everyone there, as well as with every good and truth that enters into and forms a person and the Church. Love, viewed in itself, is nothing other than an endeavor toward conjunction. Therefore, so that this essential of love might be achieved, God created man in His own image and likeness, with whom conjunction is possible. That Divine Love continually intends conjunction is clear from the Lord's words: *that He wills they may be one, He in them and they in Him, and that the love of God may be in them* (John 17:21, 22, 23, 26).

**THE THIRD ESSENTIAL OF DIVINE LOVE**, which is to make them happy <note>original: "beaficare," likely a typo for "beatificare"</note> from Himself, is recognized from eternal life, which is a state of blessedness, prosperity, and happiness without end, which God gives to those who receive His love in themselves. For just as God is Love itself, He is also Blessedness itself; every love exhales a delight from itself, and Divine Love exhales absolute bliss, prosperity, and happiness to eternity. Thus, God makes angels and humans happy after death from Himself, which occurs through conjunction with them.

44. That Divine Love is of such a nature is known from its Sphere, which pervades the Universe and affects everyone according to their state. It especially affects parents, which is why they tenderly love their children who are "outside" themselves, why they wish to be one with them, and why they want to make them happy from themselves. This Sphere of Divine Love affects not only the good but also the evil, and not only humans but even beasts and birds of every kind. What else does a mother think of when she has given birth to her offspring than to unite herself to it and provide for its good? What else does a bird think of, when she has hatched her young from their eggs, than to cherish them under her wings and, through kisses, place food into their throats?

that even dragons and vipers love their offspring is well known. That universal sphere <note>In this context, a "sphere" refers to a spiritual atmosphere or influence that radiates from God and affects all of creation.</note> specifically affects those who receive that Love of God within themselves; these are the people who believe in God and love their neighbor. Among them, charity is the image of that love. Even friendship among those who are not good mimics this love; for a friend at his table gives the better portions to his friend, kisses him, strokes him, joins hands with him, and promises helpful services. Sympathetic attractions and the striving of like or similar things toward a union <note>A reference to "homogenecorum," the natural tendency for similar substances or people to be drawn together.</note> have no other origin. This same Divine Sphere also works in inanimate things, such as trees and plants, but it does so through the sun of the natural world and its heat and light. This heat enters them from without, joins with them, and causes them to bud, flower, and bear fruit—which serves as a substitute for the happiness found in living beings. This heat does this because it corresponds to spiritual heat, which is love. Representations of the operation of this love are also found in various subjects of the mineral kingdom; its typical forms are seen in their refinement into useful and therefore precious things.

45. From the description of the Essence of Divine Love, one can see the nature of the essence of diabolical love; this can be seen by looking at its opposite. Diabolical love is self-love; while it is called "love," when viewed in itself, it is actually hatred. For such a person does not love anyone outside himself, nor does he wish to be joined to others to do them good, but only to benefit himself. From his innermost being, he continually strives to rule over everyone and also to possess the goods of all, and ultimately to be worshiped as a god. This is the reason why those in Hell do not acknowledge God, but instead acknowledge as gods those who excel in power over others—thus there are lower and higher, or lesser and greater gods, according to the extent of their power. And because everyone there carries this in their heart, they also burn with hatred against their own "god," and the leader against those under his rule, regarding them as vile slaves. While he may speak smoothly to them as long as they worship him, he rages as if with fire against others, and even inwardly—in his heart—against his own followers. Indeed, self-love is the same as the love among robbers, who kiss each other while they are engaged in robberies but afterwards burn with the desire to kill one another so they can steal their companions' plunder. This love is the reason why its lusts in Hell (where it reigns) appear from a distance like various species of wild beasts: some like foxes and leopards, some like wolves and tigers, and some like crocodiles and venomous snakes. It is also why the deserts where they live consist of nothing but heaps of stones or bare gravel, interspersed with marshes where frogs croak; and why mournful birds fly and shriek over their huts. The *ochim, tziim, and jiim* <note>original: "ochim, tziim, & jiim". These are transliterated Hebrew terms from the Bible (Isaiah 13:21) referring to various doleful creatures, wild cats, and jackals that inhabit ruins.</note> mentioned in the prophetic parts of the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scripture or the Bible.</note>—where the subject is the love of ruling from self-love—are nothing else. *Isaiah 13:21; Jeremiah 50:39; Psalm 74:14.*

## 46. VI. THAT THESE ESSENTIALS OF DIVINE LOVE WERE THE CAUSE OF THE CREATION OF THE UNIVERSE, AND THAT THEY ARE THE CAUSE OF ITS PRESERVATION.

That those three Essentials of Divine Love were the cause of Creation can be seen through a scrutiny and examination of them. That this **FIRST** essential—which is to love others outside oneself—was a cause, is evident from the Universe, which exists outside of God, just as the world exists outside of the sun. It is a realm into which He can extend His love and in which He can exercise it, and thus find rest. We also read that after God had created the Heaven and the Earth, He rested, and that the Sabbath day was made from this. *Genesis 2:2, 3.* That the **SECOND** essential—which is to desire to be one with them—was a cause, is evident from the creation of man in the image and likeness of God. By these terms, it is understood that man was made a form capable of receiving love and wisdom from God, and thus a being with whom God can unite Himself—and for man's sake, with each and every thing in the Universe, which are nothing other than means. For a union with the final cause is also a union with the intermediate causes. That all things were created for the sake of Man is also clear from the *Book of Creation or Genesis, Chapter 1:28, 29, 30.* That the **THIRD** essential—which is to make them happy from Himself—is a cause, is evident from the Angelic Heaven, which is provided for every person who receives the love of God, where the happiness of all is from God alone. That these three essentials of the love of God are also the cause of preservation...

That the Universe consists of perpetual Uses produced by Wisdom and initiated by Love, every wise person can contemplate as if in a mirror, while they form for themselves a general idea of the Creation of the universe, and in that idea observe the particulars; for particulars adapt themselves to their general whole, and the general whole disposes them into a form so that they may agree; how this happens will be illustrated by more examples in the following pages.

48. To these things shall be added this **MEMORABLE RELATION**. Once I spoke with two Angels, one was from the eastern Heaven, the other from the southern Heaven; who, when they perceived that I was meditating on the Secrets of wisdom concerning Love, said, "Do you know anything about the Games of Wisdom in our World?" I replied, "Not yet"; and they said, "There are many; and those who love truths from a spiritual affection, or truths because they are truths, and because wisdom comes through them, convene at a given signal and debate and conclude upon those things which belong to a deeper understanding." They then took me by the hand, saying, "Follow us, and you shall see and hear; the signal for the meeting has been given today." I was led across a plain to a hill, and behold, at the foot of the hill was a portico of palms, continuing all the way to its summit; we entered it and ascended; and on the head or top of the hill a Grove was seen, among whose trees the raised ground formed as it were a Theater, within which was a level space paved with stones of various colors: around it, placed in a square form, were Seats, upon which sat the lovers of wisdom; and in the middle of the Theater was a Table, upon which was placed a Paper sealed with a seal. Those sitting upon the Seats invited us to the seats still empty, and I replied, "I have been led here by two Angels to see and listen, and not to sit." And then those two Angels went into the middle of the level space to the table, and broke the seal of the paper, and read before those sitting there the secrets of wisdom written on the Paper, which they were now to debate and unfold; they had been written by the Angels of the third Heaven <note>In this cosmology, the third heaven is the highest and most celestial realm.</note>, and sent down upon the table. There were three Secrets:

**FIRST**, *what is the Image of God, and what is the Likeness of God, into which man was created.*

**SECOND**, *why man is not born into the knowledge of any love, when yet Beasts and Birds, both noble and ignoble, are born into the knowledges of all their loves.*

**THIRD**, *what the Tree of Life signifies, and what the Tree of the Knowledge of good and evil, and what the Eating from them signifies.*

Beneath these was written: "Join those three into one sentence, and write this upon a new Paper, and place it back upon this Table, and we shall see; if the sentence appears balanced and just upon the scale, to each of you shall be given a prize of wisdom." Having read these, the two Angels withdrew and were taken up into their Heavens. And then those sitting upon the Seats began to debate and unfold the Secrets proposed to them; and they spoke in order: first those who sat at the North, then those at the West, after that those at the South, and lastly those at the East. And they took up the First subject of debate, which was: **WHAT IS THE IMAGE OF GOD, AND WHAT IS THE LIKENESS OF GOD, INTO WHICH MAN WAS CREATED;** and then first from the Book of Creation <note>The Book of Genesis</note> these words were read before everyone: "God said, let us make man **IN OUR IMAGE**, according to **OUR LIKENESS**: and God created man..."

*God made man in* HIS OWN IMAGE, *in the* LIKENESS OF GOD *he made him*, Genesis I: *In the day that God created man, in the* LIKENESS OF GOD *he made him.* Genesis V: 1.

Those who sat at the NORTH spoke first, saying that the Image of God and the Likeness of God are the two Lives inspired into man by God, which are the Life of the will and the Life of the intellect; for it is read, *Jehovah God breathed into the nostrils of Adam the breath* <note>original: "animam"; literally 'soul' or 'breath'</note> OF LIVES, *and man was made into a living Soul*, Genesis II: 7; by which it seems to be understood that there was inspired into him the Will of good and the Perception of truth, and thus the Soul of lives; and because life was inspired into him by God, the Image and Likeness signify integrity <note>In this context, "integrity" refers to a state of spiritual wholeness and perfection before the "fall."</note> arising from love and wisdom, and from justice and judgment in him. To these things, those who sat at the WEST gave their favor, adding however this: that the state of integrity inspired into him by God is continually inspired into every man after him; but that it is in man as in a receptacle, and man, insofar as he is a receptacle, is the image and likeness of God. Afterward the third in order, who were those sitting at the SOUTH, said: The Image of God and the Likeness of God are two distinct things, but united in man from creation; and we see, as if from a certain interior light, that the image of God can be destroyed in man, but not the likeness of God. This appears as if through a lattice <note>i.e., a glimpse of the truth</note> from the fact that Adam retained the likeness of God after he had lost the image of God; for it is read after the curse, "Behold, the man is like one of us, knowing good and evil," Genesis III: 22. And afterward he is called the likeness of God, and not the image of God, Genesis V: 1. But let us leave it to our associates who sit at the East, and are therefore in superior light, to say what the image of God is properly, and what the likeness of God is properly. And then, after a silence was made, those sitting at the East rose from their leaves <note>The participants in these spiritual "Games of Wisdom" are often described as sitting on benches made of laurel or other symbolic leaves.</note> and looked up to the Lord, and afterward settled themselves back upon the leaves and said: The Image of God is a receptacle of God, and because God is Love itself and Wisdom itself, the Image of God is the reception of love and wisdom from God within him. But the Likeness of God is the perfect likeness and full appearance as if love and wisdom were in man [as his own], and therefore entirely as if they were his; for man does not feel otherwise than that he loves from himself and is wise from himself, or that he wills good and understands truth from himself; when nevertheless, he does so not a whit from himself, but from God. God alone loves from Himself and is wise from Himself, because God is Love itself and Wisdom itself. This likeness or appearance—that love and wisdom, or good and truth, are in man as if his own—causes man to be man, and enables him to be conjoined to God, and thus to live forever. From this it flows that man is man because he can will good and understand truth entirely as if from himself, and yet know and believe that it is from God; for as he knows and believes this, God places His image in man; it would be otherwise if he believed it was from himself and not from God. When these things were said, there came upon them a zeal from the love of truth, from which they spoke these things: How can man receive anything of love and wisdom, and retain it, and reproduce it, unless he feels it as his own? And how can conjunction with God be given through love and wisdom unless there is given to man some reciprocal part of conjunction? For without a reciprocal, no conjunction is possible; and the reciprocal of conjunction is that man should love God, and do those things which are of God, as if from himself, and yet believe that they are from God. Furthermore, how can man live forever unless he is conjoined to the eternal God? Consequently, how can man be man without that likeness in him? When these things were said, all favored them and said: let a Conclusion be made from these things; and this was done: Man is a receptacle of God, and a Receptacle of God is the Image of God; and because God is Love itself and Wisdom itself, man is a Receptacle of these; and a Receptacle is an image of God according to how it receives. And man is the likeness of God from the fact that he feels in himself that those things which are from God are in him as his own; but yet, he is only so much an Image of God from that likeness as he acknowledges that love and wisdom, or good and truth, are not his in him, and thus not from him, but only in God, and thus from God.

After this, they took up another object for debate: **WHY IS MAN NOT BORN—**
