First, they confirmed the truth of this proposition by various facts, such as that man is born into no knowledge, not even into the knowledge of *conjugial love* <note>original: "amor conjugialis"; this is Swedenborg’s specific term for a spiritual, eternal marriage love between souls.</note>; they investigated and heard from researchers that an infant does not even know its mother's breast from innate knowledge, but learns this from its mother or nurse through reminders; it only knows how to suck, and it has drawn this from continuous suction in the mother's womb. Later, it does not know how to walk, nor how to articulate sound into any human word, nor even how to sound out the affections of love as beasts do. Furthermore, it does not know what food is suitable for it, as beasts do, but seizes whatever is in its path, whether clean or unclean, and puts it in its mouth. The researchers said that without instruction, man knows absolutely nothing about the ways of loving the opposite sex, and that not even young men or maidens know these things without being taught by others. In a word, man is born corporeal like a worm; and remains corporeal unless he learns to know, to understand, and to be wise from others.

After this, they confirmed that Beasts, both noble and ignoble—such as the animals of the earth, the birds of the heaven, reptiles, fish, and the tiny worms called insects—are born into all the knowledges of the loves of their lives. They are born into everything concerning nutrition, everything concerning their dwellings, everything concerning sexual love and procreation, and everything concerning the education of their offspring. They confirmed these things by the wonders they recalled from what they had seen, heard, and read in the natural world, where they lived previously, and where real (not just representative) beasts exist. After the truth of the proposition was thus proven, they turned their minds to investigating and discovering the causes by which they might unfold and reveal this Secret <note>original: "Arcanum"; a term Swedenborg uses for hidden spiritual truths.</note>. They all said that these things could only exist from Divine Wisdom, so that man might be man and beast might be beast; and thus, that the imperfection of man's birth is actually his perfection, and the perfection of the beast's birth is its imperfection.

Then the **NORTHERNERS** first began to open their minds, saying that man is born without knowledges so that he can receive them all; but if he were born into knowledges, he could not receive any except those he was born into, and then he could not make any his own. They illustrated this with this comparison: man is first born like ground in which no seeds have been planted, but which is nonetheless able to receive all seeds and to produce and bear fruit from them. But a beast is like ground already sown and filled with grasses and herbs, which receives no other seeds than those already planted; if others were sown, it would choke them. This is why a man grows up over many years, during which he can be cultivated like the ground and produce every kind of grain, flower, and tree; but a beast grows up in a few years, during which it cannot be cultivated into anything other than what was innate.

Next, the **WESTERNERS** spoke and said that man is not born with knowledge like a beast, but is born a *Faculty* and an *Inclination*—a Faculty for knowing and an Inclination for loving. He is born with a Faculty not only for loving those things which belong to himself and the world, but also those which belong to God and Heaven. Consequently, man is born as an Organ which hardly lives by the external senses (except obscurely) and not at all by internal senses, for the reason that he may live successively and become a man: first natural, then rational, and finally spiritual. This would not happen if he were born into knowledges and loves like the beasts; for innate knowledges and affections of love limit that progression, whereas only innate faculties and inclinations limit nothing. Therefore, man can be perfected in knowledge, intelligence, and wisdom forever.

The **SOUTHERNERS** took up the discussion and delivered their judgment, saying that it is impossible for man to take any knowledge from himself, but he must take it from others, since no knowledge is innate to him. And because he cannot take any knowledge from himself, neither can he take any love; for where there is no knowledge, there is no love. Knowledge and love are inseparable companions; they can no more be separated than the will and [the intellect...]

For this reason, **Man** <note>original: "Homo"</note> is named from the Ground <note>original: "Humus"</note>, and **Adam** from **Adama**, which is the Ground <note>In Hebrew, 'Adama' refers to red earth or soil, from which the name Adam is derived.</note>. To this we add that **Beasts** are born into natural loves, and thus into the knowledges corresponding to them; yet they do not truly know, think, understand, or possess wisdom regarding any of those knowledges. Instead, they are carried toward them by their loves, almost like blind men led through the streets by dogs—for as far as the intellect is concerned, they are blind; or rather, they are like sleepwalkers who, out of blind knowledge while the intellect is asleep, do what they do. Lastly, the **Easterners** spoke and said: "We agree with what our brothers have spoken, that man knows nothing of himself, but from others and through others, so that he may know and acknowledge that all things which he knows, understands, and is wise in, are from God. Furthermore, a person could not otherwise be born and generated by God, and become His image and likeness. For the image of God is formed by this: that he acknowledges and believes that every good of love and charity, and every truth of wisdom and faith, he has received and continues to receive from God, and not a bit from himself. And the likeness of God is this: that he feels those things in himself as if they were from himself. He feels this because he is not born into knowledges but receives them; and because he receives them, it appears to him as if they are from himself. This feeling is also granted to man by God so that he may be a man and not a beast; since it is through the fact that he wills, thinks, loves, knows, understands, and is wise as if from himself, that he receives knowledges and exalts them into intelligence, and through their use, into wisdom. In this way, God joins man to Himself, and man joins himself to God. This could not have happened unless God had provided that man be born in total ignorance." After this statement, they all wished for a **Conclusion** to be made from the points discussed, and it was made as follows: "That man is born into no knowledge, so that he may come into all, and progress into intelligence, and through this into wisdom; and that he is born into no love, so that he may come into all, through the application of knowledges from the intellect, and into love toward God through love toward the neighbor, and thus be joined to God, and through that become a human being, and live forever."

After this, they took up a paper and read the third object of discussion, which was: <term>WHAT IS SIGNIFIED BY THE TREE OF LIFE, THE TREE OF THE KNOWLEDGE OF GOOD AND EVIL, AND THE EATING FROM THEM?</term> Everyone requested that those from the East should unfold this secret <note>original: "Arcanum"; a term Swedenborg uses for deep, hidden spiritual truths within the Bible.</note>, because it is of a more profound understanding, and because those from the East are in a flaming light—that is, in the wisdom of love. This wisdom is understood by the Garden of Eden, in which those two trees were placed. They responded: "We will speak, but because man takes nothing from himself, but from God, we will speak from Him, yet still from us as if from ourselves." And then they said: "A tree signifies man, and its fruit signifies the good of life. Hence, by the Tree of Life is signified a man living from God. And because love and wisdom, and charity and faith, or good and truth, make the life of God in man, by the Tree of Life is signified the man in whom these things are from God, and thus eternal life is in him. Similar things are signified by the Tree of Life from which it will be given to eat in **Revelation 2:7 and 22:2, 14.** By the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil is signified a man believing that he lives from himself and not from God—thus, that love and wisdom, charity and faith, that is, good and truth, are in the man as his own and not God's. He believes this because he thinks and wills, and speaks and acts, in every..."

For this reason, he then fell from his state of integrity—a state which he possessed as long as he believed that he was wise and did good from God, and nothing from himself. This is what is meant by "Eating from the <term>Tree of Life</term>." The Lord alone, when He was in the world, was wise from Himself and did good from Himself, because the Divine Itself was in Him and was His from birth; therefore, by His own power, He became the Redeemer and Savior. From these points, they reached this conclusion: that by the <term>Tree of Life</term>, and by the <term>Tree of the knowledge of good and evil</term>, and by <term>Eating</term> from them, it is understood that for man, Life is God within him, which brings Heaven and eternal life; and that Death for man is the persuasion and belief that life is not God in him, but himself—from which comes Hell and eternal death, which is damnation.

After this, they looked at the Paper <note>original: "Chartam"</note> left by the angels on the table, and they saw written at the bottom: JOIN THOSE THREE INTO ONE SENTENCE. They then gathered them together and saw that those three points hung together in a single series, and that the series or sentence was this: "That Man was created so that he might receive love and wisdom from God, yet in all likeness as if from himself, and this for the sake of reception and conjunction; and that therefore man is not born into any love, nor into any knowledge, nor even into any power of loving and being wise from himself. Wherefore, if he attributes every good of love and every truth of wisdom to God, he becomes a living Man; but if he attributes them to himself, he becomes a dead man." They wrote these things on a new Paper and placed it upon the Table; and behold, suddenly angels were present in a bright white cloud and carried the Paper away into Heaven. After it was read there, those sitting upon the leaves heard voices from above saying, "Well done, well done, well done." And immediately one appeared from there as if flying, with what looked like two wings around his feet and two around his temples, carrying rewards, which were <term>Gowns</term>, <term>Caps</term>, and <term>Laurels</term>. He descended and gave <term>Gowns</term> <note>original: "Togæ"</note> of an opaline color to those who sat at the North; to those at the West, <term>Gowns</term> of a scarlet color; to those at the South, <term>Caps</term> <note>original: "Pileos"</note> whose brims were adorned with bands of gold and pearls, and on the raised portions of the left side were diamonds cut in the shape of flowers; to those at the East, however, he gave <term>Laurels</term> <note>original: "Laureas", traditional wreaths of honor</note> set with rubies and sapphires. And all of them, decorated with these rewards, departed for home with joy from the <term>School of Wisdom</term> <note>original: "Ludo sapientiæ", literally "the play" or "exercise of wisdom"</note>.

# ON THE OMNIPOTENCE, OMNISCIENCE, AND OMNIPRESENCE OF GOD.

49. Having discussed <term>DIVINE LOVE</term> and <term>DIVINE WISDOM</term>, and having shown that these two constitute the <term>DIVINE ESSENCE</term> <note>original: "DIVINA ESSENTIA"</note>, we now follow with God’s <term>OMNIPOTENCE</term>, <term>OMNISCIENCE</term>, and <term>OMNIPRESENCE</term>. These <term>Three</term> proceed from Divine Love and Divine Wisdom in much the same way as the power and presence of the Sun in this world, and in every part of it, proceed through heat and light. Indeed, the Heat from the Sun of the spiritual world—at the center of which is <term>Jehovah God</term>—is in its essence <term>Divine Love</term>, and the Light from there is in its essence <term>Divine Wisdom</term>. From this it is clear that just as Infinity, Immensity, and Eternity belong to the <term>DIVINE BEING</term> <note>original: "DIVINUM ESSE," referring to God's underlying existence</note>, so Omnipotence, Omniscience, and Omnipresence belong to the <term>DIVINE ESSENCE</term>. However, because these three universal <term>Attributes of the Divine Essence</term> have not been understood until now—since their progression along their own paths (which are the laws of Order) was unknown—it is necessary to shed light on them through distinct Articles:

*I. That Omnipotence, Omniscience, and Omnipresence belong to Divine Wisdom derived from Divine Love. II. That God’s Omnipotence, Omniscience, and Omnipresence cannot be known unless one knows what Order is, and specifically that God is Order, and that at Creation He introduced Order into the Universe and every part of it. III. That God’s Omnipotence in the Universe and all its parts proceeds and operates according to the laws of His own Order. IV. That God is Omniscient; that is, He perceives, sees, and knows everything down to the smallest detail that happens according to Order, and from those things also perceives what happens against Order. V. That God is Omnipresent from the first to the last things of His Order. VI. That Man was created as a form of Divine Order. VII. That a man has power against evil and falsity from Divine Omnipotence, wisdom regarding what is good and true from Divine Omniscience, and is in God through Divine Omnipresence, only to the extent that he lives according to Divine Order.* But these must be explained one by one.

## 50. I. THAT OMNIPOTENCE, OMNISCIENCE, AND OMNIPRESENCE BELONG TO DIVINE WISDOM DERIVED FROM DIVINE LOVE.

That <term>Omnipotence</term>, <term>Omniscience</term>, and <term>Omnipresence</term> belong to <term>Divine Wisdom from Divine Love</term>, and not to <term>Divine Love through Divine Wisdom</term>, is a Secret from Heaven <note>original: "Arcanum e Cælo"</note> that has not yet dawned on anyone’s understanding. This is because no one has yet known what Love is in its essence, nor what Wisdom is from it, and even less about the flow of one into the other. This flow consists of Love, with every detail of itself, flowing into Wisdom and residing there like a King in his Kingdom, or a master in his house. Love leaves the entire governance of justice to its own judgment; and because justice belongs to love and judgment belongs to wisdom, love leaves all governance to its wisdom. This Secret will provide light in what follows, but for now, let this serve as a rule. That God is Omnipotent, Omniscient, and Omnipresent through the Wisdom of His love is also understood by these words in <term>John</term>:

> "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God... all things were made by Him, and without Him was nothing made that was made. In Him was life, and the Life was the Light of men... and the World was made by Him... and the Word was made Flesh." Chapter 1: 1, 3, 4, 10, 14.

By "the Word" <note>original: "Verbum," or the Greek "Logos"</note> there is understood Divine Truth, or what amounts to the same thing, Divine Wisdom. This is why it is also called Life and Light, for Life and Light are nothing other than Wisdom.

52. II. THAT GOD’S OMNIPOTENCE, OMNISCIENCE, AND OMNIPRESENCE CANNOT BE KNOWN UNLESS ONE KNOWS WHAT **ORDER** IS, AND UNLESS THESE TWO FACTS ARE KNOWN: THAT **GOD IS ORDER**, AND THAT AT **CREATION HE INTRODUCED ORDER** INTO BOTH THE UNIVERSE AND EVERY SINGLE PART OF IT. How many and what kind of absurdities have crept into human minds—and from there, through the heads of the founders, into the Church—because they did not understand the <term>Order</term> in which God created the Universe and everything in it, will be clear from the mere listing of them in the following pages. But here we will first open the subject of Order with a general definition: *Order is the quality of the arrangement, determination, and activity of the parts, substances, or beings which make up a form; from this arises a state, whose perfection is produced by wisdom from its love, or whose imperfection is forged by the insanity of reason from its lust.* In this definition, we mention <term>Substance</term>, <term>Form</term>, and <term>State</term>. By Substance we simultaneously mean form, because every substance is a form; and the quality of a form is its state, the perfection or imperfection of which results from order. But because these are <term>metaphysical</term> <note>the philosophical study of the nature of reality, including concepts like being, substance, and cause</note> matters, they cannot help but be in darkness until this obscurity is cleared away in the following sections through applications to examples which will provide illustration.

53. The reason God is <term>Order</term> is that He is <term>Substance</term> itself and <term>Form</term> itself. He is Substance because all things that subsist have come forth and do exist from Him; He is Form because every quality of substances has arisen and continues to arise from Him, for quality is given from no other source than from form. Now, because God is the very first, only, and primary Substance and Form, and at the same time is Love itself and Wisdom itself, and because wisdom from love produces form—and the state and quality of this form is according to the order within it—it follows that God is Order itself. Consequently, God introduced Order from Himself into both the Universe and into each and every part of it; and He introduced a most perfect Order, because everything He created was good, as is read in the Book of Creation. How evils, along with Hell, came into existence after creation will be demonstrated in its proper place. But let us move to things that enter the understanding more closely, illustrate more clearly, and affect the mind more gently.

54. The nature of the <term>Order</term> into which the Universe was created can only be explained through many pages; a certain <term>outline</term> <note>original: "schiagraphia," meaning a brief sketch or preliminary draft</note> of it will be presented in the following section on Creation. It must be held that each and every thing in the Universe was created into its own orders so that they might subsist by themselves, and that from the beginning they were so created that they might join themselves with the order of the universe. This was done so that individual orders might subsist within the Universal Order, and thus make a one. To give some examples: Man was created into his own order, and likewise every part of him into its own, such as the Head

into its own; its body into its own; the heart, lungs, liver, pancreas, and stomach into theirs; every organ of motion called a muscle into its own; and every organ of sense, such as the eye, ear, and tongue, into its own. Indeed, there is not a tiny artery or fiber there that is not in its own order; and yet these innumerable parts join themselves with the common whole, and insert themselves into it so that they together form a unity. It is the same with other things, the mere listing of which is enough for illustration: every beast of the earth, every bird of the sky, every fish of the sea, every reptile, and even every worm down to the cockroach, is created into its own order. Likewise, every tree, every shrub, plant, and legume is in its own; and furthermore, every stone and every mineral, down to every grain of dust of the earth, is in its own.

55. Who does not see that no empire, kingdom, dukedom, republic, city, or house can be established except through laws which create <term>Order</term> <note>Order here refers to the structural arrangement that allows a system to function</note>, and thus the form of its government? In each of these, laws of justice are in the highest place, political laws in the second, and <term>economic laws</term> <note>original: "Leges Œconomicæ" — in this context, laws governing household management and social conduct</note> in the third. If these are compared to a human being, the laws of justice form the head, political laws the body, and economic laws the clothing; which is why, like clothing, these latter laws can be changed. But as concerns the Order into which the Church has been established by God, it is this: that God should be in each and every part of it, and the neighbor is the one toward whom Order must be exercised. The laws of that order are as many as the Truths in the <term>Word</term> <note>The Word refers to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible</note>; the laws that regard God form its head, the laws that regard the neighbor form its body, and ceremonies form the clothing. For unless ceremonies held the others in their Order, it would be as if the body were stripped and exposed to the heat in summer and the cold in winter; or as if the walls and ceilings were removed from a temple, and thus the <term>sanctuary</term> <note>original: "Adytum" — the innermost, most sacred part of a temple</note>, the altar, and the pulpit would stand exposed to various acts of violence under the open sky.

56. III. *THAT GOD’S OMNIPOTENCE, BOTH IN THE UNIVERSE AND IN EACH AND EVERY PART OF IT, PROCEEDS AND OPERATES ACCORDING TO THE LAWS OF HIS OWN ORDER.* God is Omnipotent because He can do all things from Himself, and all others have power from Him. His "To be able" and "To will" are one; and because He wills nothing but what is Good, He therefore can do nothing but what is Good. In the spiritual world, no one can do anything against their own will; they derive this from God, in whom power and will are one. God is also Good itself; therefore, while He does Good, He is in Himself, and He cannot go out of Himself. From this it is clear that His Omnipotence proceeds and operates within the sphere of the extension of Good, which is infinite. For this sphere fills the universe from its inmost, and each and every thing there; and from the inmost He governs those things which are on the outside, to the extent that they join themselves according to their own orders. And even if they do not join themselves, He still sustains them, and with every effort He labors to bring them back into an order harmonious with the universal one, in which God Himself is in His Omnipotence, and according to which He acts. If this cannot be done, they are cast outside of Him, where He nevertheless sustains them from the inmost. From these things it can be established that Divine Omnipotence can by no means go out from itself to the contact of any evil, nor promote it from itself, for evil turns itself away; hence it happens that evil is entirely separate from Him and cast into Hell, between which and Heaven, where He is, there is a vast gulf. From these few points it can be seen how much they wander in delusion who think—and more who believe, and even more who teach—that God can damn anyone, curse anyone, cast anyone into Hell, predestine anyone's soul to eternal death, avenge injuries, be angry, or punish. Indeed, He cannot even turn Himself away from a human being and look upon them with a harsh face; these and similar things are against His Essence, and to be against this is to be against Himself.

57. The opinion prevailing today is that the Omnipotence of God is like the absolute power of a king in the world, who can at his pleasure do whatever he wants: absolve and condemn whom he wills, make the guilty innocent, declare the unfaithful faithful, and exalt the unworthy and undeserving above the worthy and deserving—indeed, that he can under...

# UNIVERSAL THEOLOGY

on whatever pretext to snatch away the property of their subjects, and then to sentence them to death, besides other similar things. From this fatuous opinion regarding the faith and doctrine of Divine Omnipotence, as many falsehoods, fallacies, and <term>chimeras</term> <note>In mythology, a chimera is a creature made of mismatched parts; here it refers to impossible or absurd theological ideas.</note> have flowed into the Church as there are moments, expressions, and generations of faith there. More may yet flow in, as many as the jugs that can be filled with water from a large lake, or as many as the serpents that can crawl out of their caves and bask in the open sun in the desert of Arabia. What is needed but two words, **OMNIPOTENCE & FAITH**, and then to scatter before the common people as many conjectures, fables, and trifles as can fall upon the bodily senses? For from both of these, reason is cast out. But what is human thought worth once reason is ejected, compared to the "reason" of a bird flying over one's head? Or what then is the <term>Spiritual</term> <note>The higher, God-oriented part of the human mind.</note> quality, which distinguishes man from the beasts, except like the stench in a menagerie, which suits the wild beasts there, but does not suit a man unless he has become like them? If the extension of Divine Omnipotence were equally for doing evil as for doing good, what distinction would there be between God and the devil? Would it be any different than the distinction between two monarchs, one of whom is a King and a tyrant at the same time, and the other a Tyrant whose power is bound, and who therefore cannot be called a King? Or between a Shepherd who is permitted to act like a sheep and also like a leopard, and a shepherd who is not permitted this? Anyone can know that Good and Evil are opposites, and if God, out of His Omnipotence, were able to will both and act from that willing, He could do absolutely nothing at all. Thus He would have no power, much less Omnipotence. This would be like two wheels turning in opposite directions acting against each other, from which reaction both wheels would stop and remain entirely still; or like a Ship in a torrent acting against its path, which, unless it rested upon an anchor, would be swept away and perish; or like a man who has two wills disagreeing with each other, so that while one acts, the other must necessarily be still, but if both were to act at once, madness or vertigo would invade his mind.

58. If the Omnipotence of God were absolute according to the faith of today, for doing both good and evil, would it not be possible, indeed easy, for God to raise all of Hell into Heaven, and to convert devils and satans into Angels, and on earth to purify every wicked person from sins in a moment, to renew, sanctify, and regenerate them, and to make a child of wrath into a child of grace—that is, to <term>justify</term> <note>Theological term for being made righteous in the sight of God.</note> them—which would be done solely through the application and <term>imputation</term> <note>The doctrine that Christ's righteousness is "credited" to a person's account regardless of their actual character.</note> of the righteousness of His Son? But God, out of His Omnipotence, cannot do this, because it is against the laws of His <term>Order</term> in the Universe, and at the same time against the laws of Order commanded for every man, which are that they should join themselves together from both sides <note>This refers to the idea that both God and man must act for a spiritual connection to occur; God does not force salvation.</note>. That this is so will be seen in the following parts of this Work. From that fatuous opinion and faith regarding God's Omnipotence, it would follow that God could convert every "goat" of a man into a "sheep" of a man, and at His pleasure move him from His left side to His right; or that He could, at His pleasure, transmute the spirits of the "dragon" into the Angels of Michael; or that He could gift a man whose intellect is like a mole's with the sight of an eagle—in a word, make a dove out of an owl-like man. These things God cannot do, because they are against the laws of His own Order, even though He continually wills and strives for this. If He had been able to do such things, He would not have permitted Adam to listen to the serpent and take the fruit from the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil and bring it to his mouth; if He had been able, He would not have permitted Cain to kill his brother; or David to number the people; or Solomon to build shrines for idols; or the Kings of Judah and Israel to profane the Temple, which they did so many times. Indeed, if He could have done so, He would have saved the entire human race without exception through the Redemption of His Son, and would have uprooted all of Hell. The ancient Gentiles ascribed such Omnipotence to their gods and goddesses, from which arose their fables, such as that of Deucalion and Pyrrha, where stones thrown behind their backs became human beings; or of Apollo, who turned Daphne into a laurel tree; or of Diana, who turned a hunter into a doe; and that another of their gods turned the virgins of Parnassus into magpies. Similar faiths concerning...

# OF THE NEW HEAVEN AND THE NEW CHURCH.

The modern view of Divine Omnipotence is the reason why so many fanatical and consequently heretical ideas have been introduced into the world in every region where there is religion.

59. IV. **GOD IS OMNISCIENT; THAT IS, HE PERCEIVES, SEES, AND KNOWS ALL THINGS AND EVERY SINGLE THING DOWN TO THE SMALLEST DETAILS WHICH HAPPEN ACCORDING TO ORDER, AND FROM THESE HE ALSO PERCEIVES THOSE WHICH HAPPEN CONTRARY TO ORDER.** That God is Omniscient—meaning He perceives, sees, and knows all things—is because He is Wisdom itself and Light itself. Wisdom itself perceives all things, and Light itself sees all things. It was shown above that God is Wisdom itself; that He is Light itself is because He is the Sun of the Angelic Heaven, which enlightens the understanding of all angels and all men alike. For just as the eye is illuminated by the light of the natural sun, so is the understanding illuminated by the light of the <term>Spiritual Sun</term> <note>In this theology, the Spiritual Sun is the first proceeding of the Divine Love and Wisdom, appearing as a sun to the angels and providing the "light" of truth to the human mind.</note>. Nor is it only illuminated, but it is also filled with intelligence according to the love of receiving it, since this Light in its essence is Wisdom. Therefore, it is said in David <note>original: "apud Davidem"</note>, **THAT GOD DWELLS IN INACCESSIBLE LIGHT**; and in the Book of Revelation, *That in the New Jerusalem they have no need of a lamp, because the Lord God enlightens them;* and in John, *That the Word, which was with God, and was God, is the Light which enlightens every man coming into the world.* By "the Word" is meant Divine Wisdom. This is why angels are in such brilliance of light as they are in wisdom; and it is also why in the Word, where light is named, wisdom is meant.

60. That God perceives, sees, and knows all things down to the smallest details which happen according to order, is because <term>Order</term> <note>Divine Order is the structural law of the universe, originating from God's nature.</note> is a Universal made up of the most singular details; for the singulars taken together are called the Universal, just as particulars taken together are called the General. The Universal, along with its most singular parts, is a work cohering as one, so much so that one part cannot be touched or affected without some sense of it flowing back to the rest. It is from this quality of order in the universe that something similar occurs in all created things in the world. But this will be illustrated by comparisons taken from visible things. In the whole man there are general and particular parts, and the general parts involve the particular ones there, arranging themselves through such a connection that one belongs to the other. This happens because a general envelope surrounds every member there, and this insinuates itself into every single part within, so that they act as one in every office and use. For example, the envelope <note>The fascia or connective tissue.</note> of any muscle enters into the individual motor fibers and clothes them from itself. Similarly, the envelope of the liver, pancreas, and spleen enters into the individual parts that are within them. Likewise, the envelope of the lung, which is called the <term>pleura</term>, enters into its interior parts; and likewise the <term>pericardium</term> into each and every part of the heart; and generally the <term>peritoneum</term> connects through <term>anastomoses</term> <note>The connection or opening between vessels or parts.</note> with the envelopes of all the viscera. Likewise, the <term>Meninges</term> of the Brain <note>The membranes covering the brain and spinal cord.</note> enter into all the underlying glands through threads drawn from themselves, and through these into all the fibers, and through these into everything in the body. From this it is that the Head, by means of the Brains, rules each and every thing subject to it. These examples are brought forward only so that from visible things some idea may be formed of how God perceives, sees, and knows all things down to the smallest details which happen according to order.

61. That God perceives, knows, and sees each and every thing down to the smallest details that happen **against** Order, is because God does not hold man in evil, but detains him from evil; thus He does not lead him, but struggles with him. From that perpetual reluctance, resistance, opposition, repugnance, and reaction of evil and falsity against His Good and Truth (and thus against Himself), He perceives both how much and what kind they are. This follows from the Omnipresence of God in each and every thing of His Order, and simultaneously from the Omniscience of each and every thing there. By comparison, one whose ear is attuned to harmony and consonance notices exactly how much and in what way a disharmony or dissonance deviates when it enters. Likewise, one whose senses are in a pleasant state notices when something unpleasant interrupts. In the same way, one whose sight is on what is beautiful sees it exactly when something deformed is at its side; for this reason, it is common for painters to place a deformed face next to a beautiful one. It is the same with good and tr—

...but when evil and falsity struggle against those things, they are perceived distinctly; for everyone who is in good can perceive evil, and he who is in truth can see falsity. The reason is that good is in the heat of heaven and truth is in its light, while evil is in the cold of hell and falsity is in its darkness. This can be illustrated by the fact that the Angels of heaven can see whatever is done in hell and what kind of monsters are there; but on the other hand, the spirits of Hell cannot see the slightest bit of what is done in Heaven. They cannot even see the Angels, any more than a blind man can, or any more than an eye looking into empty air or the pure ether. Those whose understanding is in light from wisdom are like those who stand on a mountain at noon and see everything below clearly. Those who are in even higher light are, by comparison, like those who see surrounding and lower things through <term>optical tubes</term> <note>original: "tubos opticos." In the 18th century, these were telescopes or early magnifying instruments.</note> as if they were right in front of them. But those who are in the deceptive light of Hell from the confirmation of falsities are like those who stand on that same mountain at night with lanterns in their hands, seeing nothing but what is closest to them, and even then seeing indistinct shapes and confused colors. A man who is in some light of truth and yet in an evil life, while he is in the delight of his evil love, sees truths at first like a bat sees laundry hanging in a garden, toward which it flies as its sanctuary; afterward he becomes like a screech-owl, and finally like a horned owl. Then he becomes like a chimney-sweep clinging to the dark interior of a chimney, who, when he looks up, sees heaven through the smoke, but when he looks down, sees the hearth from which that smoke comes.

62. It must be held that the perception of <term>opposites</term> is different from the perception of <term>relatives</term> <note>Swedenborg uses "relatives" here to mean things that relate to one another within a harmonious system, like different colors in a single painting.</note>. Opposites are things that are outside and against those which are within. An opposite arises when one thing entirely ceases to be anything, and another then rises up with an effort to act against the first, like one wheel acting against another, or one river against another. Relatives, however, concern the arrangement of many and various things into an order so that they agree and harmonize, like precious stones of different colors in the sash on a Queen's breast, or like flowers of different colors in a garland to provide a pleasant sight. There are therefore relatives in both opposites—both in good and in evil, and in truth and in falsity—thus both in heaven and in Hell. But all relatives in hell are opposite to the relatives in heaven. Now, because God perceives and sees, and from there knows all the relatives in Heaven from the Order in which He Himself is, and from there perceives, sees, and knows all the opposite relatives in Hell (as follows from what was said above), it is clear that God is omniscient in Hell just as He is in heaven, and likewise with men in the world. Thus He perceives, sees, and knows their evils and falsities from the good and truth in which He is, and which in their essence are Himself. For He says: *If I ascend into the Heavens, Thou art there; if I make my bed in Hell, behold, Thou art there* <note>original: Psalm CXXXIX: 8</note>. And elsewhere: *If they dig into Hell, thence shall my hand take them* <note>original: Amos IX: 2. 3</note>.

### 63. V. THAT GOD IS OMNIPRESENT FROM THE FIRSTS TO THE LASTS OF HIS ORDER.

God is omnipresent from the firsts to the lasts of His Order through the Heat and Light from the Sun of the Spiritual World, in the midst of which He is. Through this Sun, Order was made, and from it He sends out heat and light which pervade the Universe from its firsts to its lasts, and produce the life which is in man and in every animal, and also the vegetative soul which is in every bud upon the Earth. These two flow into each and every thing, and cause every single subject to live and grow according to the Order implanted in them from creation. And because God is <term>not extended</term> <note>original: "non est extensus." In theological terms, this means God is not made of physical matter and does not take up space in a way that limits Him; He is beyond spatial dimensions.</note> and yet fills all the extensions of the Universe, He is omnipresent. That God is in all space without space, and in all time without time, and that consequently the Universe, as to its essence and order, is the fullness of God, has been shown elsewhere. Because this is so, through His omnipresence He perceives all things, through His omniscience He provides all things, and through His omnipotence He operates all things. From this it is clear that Omnipresence, Omniscience, and Omnipotence make one—or that one implies the others, and thus they cannot be separated.

64. **Divine Omnipresence** can be illustrated by the wonderful presence of Angels and Spirits in the **Spiritual World**. In that World, because there is no space, but only the appearance of space, an angel or spirit can be presented to another in a moment, provided they come into a similar affection of love and a resulting thought, for these two things create the appearance of space. That such a presence of all people exists there was made clear to me by the fact that I was able to see Africans and Indians close at hand, although they are thousands of miles apart on Earth. Indeed, I was even able to be presented to those who are on the **Planets of this World**, and also to those on Planets in other Worlds outside this solar system. Because of this presence—not of location but of the appearance of location—I have spoken with the **Apostles**, and with deceased **Popes, Emperors, and Kings**, with the restorers of the church today—**Luther, Calvin, and Melanchthon**—and with others from distant lands. If such presence exists for Angels and Spirits, what then of the **Divine Presence** in the universe, which is infinite? The reason why Angels and spirits have such presence is that every affection of love, and the resulting thought of the intellect, is in space without space, and in time without time. For anyone can think of a brother, a relation, or a friend who is in the East Indies, and then have him as if present with him; in the same way, one can be moved by love for them through memory. 

Through these things, because they are known to man, **Divine Omnipresence** can in some way be illustrated; and also through human thoughts, in that when someone recalls to memory what they saw in various places during a journey, they are in those places as if present. Indeed, the sight of the body emulates that same presence; the eye does not notice distance except through intermediate objects, which act as measurements. The Sun itself would seem near the eye, indeed as if it were in the eye, unless intermediate things revealed how distant it is. <note>Swedenborg is referencing the contemporary understanding of optics and perspective.</note> Optical writers in their books have also observed that this is so. Such presence belongs to both the intellectual and bodily sight of man, because his spirit sees through his eyes; but it is not similar for any beast, because they lack spiritual sight. From these things it can be established that God is **Omnipresent** from the **Firsts to the Lasts** <note>original: "a Primis ad Ultima." A philosophical phrase meaning from the highest spiritual beginnings to the lowest physical ends.</note> of His Order; and that He is also Omnipresent in Hell, as was shown in the preceding article.

### 65. VI. THAT MAN WAS CREATED AS A FORM OF DIVINE ORDER.

The reason man was created as a form of **Divine Order** is that he was created as the **image and likeness of God**, and since God is Order itself, man was created as an image and likeness of order. There are two things from which Order exists, and through which it subsists: **Divine Love** and **Divine Wisdom**. Man was created as a receptacle for them; therefore, he was also created into the order according to which those two act in the Universe, and principally according to which they act in the **Angelic Heaven**. Thus, that whole Heaven is, in its greatest image, the form of Divine Order, and that Heaven in the sight of God is like **one Man**. <note>Swedenborg calls this the "Grand Man" (Maximus Homo), a core concept where the entire heaven functions as a single human organism.</note> There is also a full <term>correspondence</term> <note>Correspondence is the relationship between spiritual causes and natural effects.</note> between that Heaven and man; for there is no Society in Heaven that does not correspond to some member, internal organ, or sensory organ in man. Therefore, it is said in Heaven that this Society is either in the province of the **Liver**, or the **Pancreas**, or the **Spleen**, or the **Stomach**, or the **Eye**, or the **Ear**, or the **Tongue**, and so on. The Angels themselves even know in which region of some Part of man they dwell. That this is so has been given to me to know through living experience; I have seen a Society consisting of several thousand Angels appearing as **one man**, from which it was clear that Heaven in its entirety is the image of God, and the image of God is the form of Divine Order.

66. It should be known that all things proceeding from the **Sun of the spiritual world**, in the midst of which is **Jehovah God**, relate to man; and that consequently, whatever things exist in that World conspire toward the human form, and present that form in their innermost parts. Thus, all objects presented to the eyes there are representatives of man: Animals of every kind appear there, and these are **Likenesses** of the affections of love and the resulting thoughts of the angels; similarly, groves, flower-beds, and green... <note>The text cuts off here at the end of the page.</note>

67. Before Creation, God was **Love itself** and **Wisdom itself**, and these two existed in a <term>striving</term><note>original: "conatus"; a technical term for an internal inclination or force that tends toward an outward action.</note> to perform <term>uses</term><note>original: "usus"; in this theology, "use" refers to the practical application of love and wisdom through service or beneficial activity.</note>. For Love and Wisdom without use are merely fleeting things of the reason; they fly away unless they commit themselves to use. These first two are also separated from the third (use) like birds flying over a great Ocean, which at length grow weary from flight, fall down, and are submerged. From this it is clear that the Universe was created by God so that uses might exist; therefore, the Universe can also be called a **Theater of Uses**. Since man is the principal goal of creation, it follows that each and every thing was created for the sake of man, and consequently that all the particulars of order were gathered into him and concentrated in him, so that God might perform primary uses through him. 

Love and Wisdom without their third—which is Use—can be compared to the heat and light of the sun. Unless these operated upon men, animals, and vegetables, they would be empty things; but they become real through their flow into and operation within them. There are also three things that follow in a sequence: **End, Cause, and Effect**. It is well known in the learned world that an "end" (a goal) is nothing unless it looks toward an "efficient cause," and that the end and cause are nothing unless an "effect" is produced. An end and a cause can indeed be turned over abstractly in the Mind, but only for the sake of some effect which the end intends and the cause procures. It is the same with love, wisdom, and use: use is what love intends and produces through the cause. When the use is produced, love and wisdom truly exist; they make a home and a seat for themselves within that use, resting there as if in their own house. It is the same with man: the love and wisdom of God are within him while he performs uses. To enable him to perform God's uses, he was created as an "image and likeness"—that is, a form of **Divine Order**.

## 68. VII. THAT MAN POSSESSES POWER AGAINST EVIL AND FALSITY FROM DIVINE OMNIPOTENCE, POSSESSES WISDOM REGARDING GOOD AND TRUTH FROM DIVINE OMNISCIENCE, AND IS IN GOD FROM DIVINE OMNIPRESENCE, ONLY TO THE DEGREE THAT HE LIVES ACCORDING TO DIVINE ORDER.

The reason man has power against evils and falsities from **Divine Omnipotence** <note>Omnipotence: God's all-encompassing power.</note> only to the degree that he lives according to **Divine Order**, is because no one can resist evils and the resulting falsities except God Alone. All evils and their falsities are from Hell, and in Hell they stick together as one, just as all goods and their truths do in Heaven. As was said above, the whole of Heaven appears before God like "one Man," and conversely, Hell appears like "one Giant" who is a Monster. Therefore, to act against a single evil and its resulting falsity is to act against that monstrous Giant or Hell itself. No one can do this except God, because He is Omnipotent. 

From this it is clear that unless a person approaches God the Omnipotent, they have no more power against evil and falsity from themselves than a fish has against the Ocean, a flea against a whale, or a grain of dust against a falling mountain—and much less than a locust against an elephant, or a fly against a camel. Furthermore, man has even less power against evil and falsity because he is born into evil, and evil cannot act against itself. It follows from this that man must live according to Order; that is, he must acknowledge God and His Omnipotence, and the protection from Hell that comes from it. Then, the man must also do his part and fight against the evil in himself, for this [work], together with Him, is...

69. That a person becomes wise in goodness and truth from Divine <term>Omniscience</term><note>The attribute of God knowing all things.</note> only in proportion as they live according to Divine order, is because all love of goodness and all wisdom of truth—or every good of love and every truth of wisdom—is from God. This is even according to the confession of all the Churches in the Christian World; from which it follows that a person cannot be inwardly in any truth of wisdom except from God, because God has <term>Omniscience</term>, which is infinite wisdom. The human mind is divided into three degrees <note>Swedenborg taught that the mind has levels: natural, spiritual, and celestial, corresponding to the levels of heaven.</note>, just like the <term>Angelic Heaven</term>, and therefore it can be raised to a higher and higher degree, and can also be lowered to a lower and lower degree. However, in proportion as it is raised to the higher degrees, it is raised into wisdom, because it is raised into the light of Heaven, and this can only be done by God; and as much as it is raised there, so much is the person truly a "man." But as much as it is lowered to the lower degrees, so much is it in the deceptive light of hell, and so much is it not a man, but a beast. For this reason, a man stands upright on his feet and looks with his face toward heaven, and can raise it to the zenith <note>the point directly overhead</note>; but a beast stands on its feet in a position parallel with the earth, and looks there with its whole face, nor can it without difficulty lift its gaze to heaven.

A person who raises their mind to God and acknowledges that all truth of wisdom is from Him, and at the same time lives according to order, is like one who stands on a high tower and sees a populous city below him, and at the same time everything that is happening in the streets. But a person who confirms in themselves that all truth of wisdom is from the natural light within themselves—and thus from themselves—is like one who lives in a cavern under that tower, and looks through holes there at the same city; they see nothing but the wall of a single house in that city, and how the bricks there are joined together. Furthermore, a person who draws wisdom from God is like a bird flying on high, which looks around at everything in the gardens, woods, and villages, and flies toward those things that are for its use; but a person who draws things pertaining to wisdom from themselves, without faith that they are still from God, is like a hornet <note>original: "crabro"</note> that flies near the ground, and where it sees a dung-hill, it flies in and delights in its stench. Every person, as long as they live in the World, walks in the middle between Heaven and Hell, and is therefore in equilibrium, and thus in the free choice to look upward toward God or downward toward hell. If they look upward toward God, they acknowledge that all wisdom is from God, and as to their spirit, they are actually with the Angels in Heaven; but whoever looks downward—which everyone does who is in falsehoods from evil—is as to their spirit actually with the devils in Hell.

70. That a person is in God from Divine <term>Omnipresence</term><note>The attribute of God being present everywhere at once.</note> only in proportion as they live according to order, is because God is <term>Omnipresent</term>; and because where He is in His own Divine order, there He is as if in Himself, because He Himself is <term>Order</term>, as was shown above. Now, because man was created as a form of Divine Order, God is in him; truly, so much as the person lives fully according to Divine Order. But if they do not live according to Divine Order, God is still in them, but in their highest parts, and grants them the ability to understand truth and to will good—that is, He gives them the faculty for understanding and the inclination for loving. But as much as a person lives against order, so much they close the lower parts of their mind or spirit, and thus prevent God from descending and filling their lower parts with His presence; hence God is in them, but they are not in God. It is a common law in Heaven that God is in every person, both evil and good, but that the person is not in God unless they live according to order; for the Lord says that He wills that man be in Him, and He in man (John 15:4). That a person is in God through a life according to order is because God is omnipresent in the Universe and in each and every part of it, in their innermost parts—for these are in order. But in those things that are against order—which are only those things that are outside the innermost parts—God is <term>Omnipresent</term> through a continual struggle with them, and through a continual

The absence of God from man is no more possible than the absence of the Sun, through its heat and light, from the earth; but the objects of the earth are not within the sun's power except in proportion as they receive those two things proceeding from that Sun, which happens in the time of spring and summer. These things can be applied to God's <term>Omnipresence</term><note>The quality of being present everywhere at the same time.</note> in this way: that a man is only in spiritual heat and at the same time in spiritual light—that is, in the good of love and in the truths of wisdom—insofar as he is in order. 

However, spiritual heat and light are not like natural heat and light, for natural heat recedes from the Earth and its objects during winter, and light recedes during the night; and this happens because the Earth, through its rotations and revolutions, creates those seasons. But spiritual heat and spiritual light do not act this way, for God, through His Sun, is present with both [heat and light] and does not go through cycles like the sun of the world apparently does. Man himself turns away, just as the Earth turns from its Sun; and when he turns away from the truths of wisdom, it is like the earth turning from its sun at night; and when a man turns away from the goods of love, it is like the earth turning from its sun in winter. Such is the <term>correspondence</term><note>A central concept in Swedenborg's thought where natural things reflect spiritual realities.</note> between the effects and uses from the Sun of the spiritual World, and the effects and uses from the Sun of the natural World.

71. To these things shall be added three **MEMORABLE RELATIONS**, the **FIRST** being this: Once I heard below me something like the roaring of the sea, and I asked what it was. Someone told me that it was a tumult among those gathered in the lower Earth, which is located directly above Hell. Soon the ground, which formed a roof over them, gaped open, and behold, out of the opening flew crowds of birds of the night, which spread themselves to the left; and immediately after them, locusts surged up, leaping upon the grass of the ground and creating a desert everywhere. After a little while, I heard alternating wails from those birds of the night, and to the side, a confused shouting as if from ghosts in the woods. 

After this, I saw beautiful birds from Heaven, which spread themselves to the right; those birds were distinguished by wings like gold, interspersed with streaks and spots like silver, and upon the heads of some were crests in the form of crowns. While I looked and wondered at these things, suddenly from the lower Earth where that tumult was, a spirit raised himself up who was able to transform himself into an <term>Angel of light</term><note>A spirit who disguises their true nature to appear heavenly.</note>, and he cried out: "Where is the one who speaks and writes about the **Order** to which the Almighty God has bound Himself regarding man? We have heard these things through the roof below." 

While he was above that Earth, he ran along a paved way and finally came to me, and immediately faked being an Angel of Heaven; speaking in a tone that was not his own, he said: "Are you the one who thinks and speaks about Order? Tell me in brief what Order is, and some things that belong to Order." 

And I replied: "I will tell you the summaries, but not the particulars, because you cannot grasp those." And I said:

I. That God is Order itself.
II. That He created Man out of Order, in Order, and for Order.
III. That He created man’s rational mind according to the Order of the entire spiritual World, and his Body according to the Order of the entire natural World; for which reason Man was called by the Ancients a <term>Micro-Uranos</term><note>Greek for "Little Heaven."</note> and a <term>Microcosm</term><note>Greek for "Little World."</note>.
IV. That it is a Law of order that man, from his Micro-Uranos or little spiritual world, is to rule his Microcosm or little natural world; just as God, from His <term>Macro-Uranos</term><note>"Great Heaven."</note> or spiritual World, rules the <term>Macrocosm</term><note>"Great World" or the universe.</note> or natural World in all its individual parts.
V. That the Law of order following from this is that it is necessary for man to introduce himself into faith through truths from the Word, and into charity through good works, and thus reform and regenerate himself.
VI. That it is a Law of order that man should purify himself from sins by his own work and power, and not stand in a faith of helplessness and wait for God to immediately wipe away his sins.
VII. It is also a Law of Order that Man should love God with all his soul and with all his heart, and his neighbor as...

### OF THE NEW HEAVEN AND THE NEW CHURCH.

[...one must prepare] himself, and not delay and wait for both that love to be brought directly from God into his mind and heart, like bread from a baker into a mouth; along with many similar things. Having heard these things, that <term>Satan</term><note>In this context, the author uses "Satan" to refer to a specific spirit representing a false or deceptive viewpoint.</note> responded with a smooth voice, within which there was a hidden heat: "What is this you are saying? That a man, by his own power, is to bring himself into order by performing those laws of his? Do you not know that man is not under the law, but under grace? That all things are given freely, and that a man can take nothing for himself unless it is given to him from Heaven? And that in spiritual matters, he can no more act of himself than <term>Lot’s wife</term><note>A reference to the biblical figure who turned into a pillar of salt (Genesis 19:26), used here to represent total spiritual paralysis.</note> as a statue, or no more than <term>Dagon</term><note>An ancient Philistine deity whose idol fell and broke before the Ark of the Covenant.</note>, the idol of the Philistines in Ekron? And therefore, that it is impossible for a man to justify himself, which is done through Faith and Charity."

But to these things I replied only this: "The law of order is also that a man, by his own work and power, is to acquire faith for himself through truths from the Word; and yet he will believe that not a grain of faith is from himself, but from God. Furthermore, a man, by his own work and power, is to justify himself, but yet he will believe that not even a point of justification is from himself, but from God. Is it not commanded that a man is to believe in God, and to love God with all his strength, and his neighbor as himself? Think and say how these things could have been commanded by God if man had no power to obey and act."

Hearing this, that Satan’s face was transformed; from white it first became pale, and then black. Speaking from his mouth, he said: "You have spoken paradoxes against paradoxes!" And immediately he sank down to his companions and vanished. Then the birds on the left, together with the specters, let out unusual sounds and threw themselves into the sea, which is there called the <term>Sea of Suph</term><note>The Hebrew name for the Red Sea.</note>, and locusts followed them in leaps. The air was cleared, the earth was cleansed of those wild creatures, the tumult below ceased, and it became tranquil and serene.

72. **THE SECOND MEMORABLE RELATION**, Once I heard an unusual murmur from a distance, and in spirit I followed the path of the sound. I approached, and when I came to its source, behold, there was a group of spirits reasoning about **IMPUTATION AND PREDESTINATION**. They were Dutch and British, with some from other kingdoms mixed in. At the end of each argument, they cried out, "*We wonder, we wonder!*" The dispute was why God does not impute the merit and righteousness of His Son to everyone and each person created by Him and later redeemed. "Is He not Omnipotent?" they asked. "Can He not, if He wills, make <term>Lucifer</term><note>The fallen angel, representing extreme evil.</note>, the Dragon, and all the <term>Goats</term><note>A biblical reference to those who are condemned, as opposed to the "sheep."</note> into Archangels? Is He not Omnipotent? Why does He permit the injustice and impiety of the devil to triumph over the righteousness of His Son and the piety of God's worshipers? What is easier for God than to deem everyone worthy of faith and thus salvation? What is needed for this but a small word? And if He does not do so, does He not act against His own words, which say that He wills the salvation of all and the death of none? Tell us, therefore, from whom and in what is the cause of the damnation of those who perish?"

Then a certain <term>Supralapsarian</term><note>A technical term for a strict Calvinist view that God decided who would be saved or damned before the Fall of Man occurred.</note> from among the Dutch said: "Is this not according to the good pleasure of the Omnipotent? Shall the clay rebuke the potter because he makes it into a vessel of dishonor?" And another said: "The salvation of anyone is in His hand like a scale in the hand of a weigher."

There stood at the sides some who were simple in faith and upright in heart—some with eyes inflamed, some as if stunned, some as if intoxicated, and some as if suffocated—muttering among themselves: "What have we to do with those delusions? Their faith has made them foolish, which claims that God the Father imputes the righteousness of His Son to whom He wills and when He wills, and sends the Holy Spirit to work out the rewards of that righteousness; and lest man should claim a grain for himself in the ministry of his own salvation, he is to be entirely like a stone in the business of justification, and like a log in spiritual matters." 

Then one of them thrust himself into the group and, speaking loudly, said: "O insane ones! Your reasoning is about <term>goat’s wool</term><note>original: "lana caprina." A classical idiom meaning to argue about something of no importance or complete nonsense.</note>. You clearly do not know that God Omnipotent is Order itself, and that the laws of Order are myriads—as many as there are Truths in the Word—and that He cannot act against them. Because to act against them would be to act against Himself, and thus not only against His Justice but also against His Omnipotence." And he saw from a distance on the right something like a sheep, a lamb, and a flying dove, and on the left something like a goat, a wolf, and a vulture, and he said: "Do you believe that..."

# UNIVERSAL THEOLOGY

Could God, out of His Omnipotence, convert that goat into a sheep, or that wolf into a lamb, or that vulture into a dove, or vice versa? Not at all; for it is contrary to the laws of His own Order, from which not even a tittle <note>original: *apex*, referring to the smallest stroke of a pen in a letter, used here in the sense of the smallest detail of a law; cf. Matthew 5:18</note> can fall to the earth, according to His own words. How then can He apply the justice of His Son's redemption to someone who is rebellious against the laws of His justice? How can Justice itself perform an injustice, and predestine someone to hell, casting them into the fire where the devil stands with torches in hand and fans the flames? O you madmen, empty of spirit! Your faith has seduced you; is it not in your hands like a snare for catching pigeons? Having heard these things, a certain Magician <note>In the author's visionary style, a "Magus" often represents one who manipulates spiritual appearances or false doctrines.</note> made a snare out of that faith and hung it in a tree, saying, "You will see that I am going to catch that pigeon." But soon a hawk flew by, stuck its neck into the snare, and hung there; and the pigeon, seeing the hawk, flew past. The bystanders were amazed and cried out, "This game is a proof <note>original: *auctoramentum*, a guarantee or confirmation</note> of justice."

73. The following day, some of the Company <note>original: *Cohorte*, likely referring to a specific group of spirits or thinkers encountered in the author's vision</note> came to me, who were in the faith of predestination and imputation, and they said: "We are like drunken men—not from wine, but from the discourse that man gave yesterday. He spoke of Omnipotence and simultaneously of Order, and concluded that just as Omnipotence is Divine, so too is Order Divine; indeed, that God Himself is Order. He said that there are as many laws of Order as there are truths in the Word, which are not only thousands, but myriads of myriads, and that God is bound to His laws there, just as man is to his. What then is Divine Omnipotence if it is tied to laws? For in this way, every absolute thing recedes from Omnipotence. Does God then have less power than a King of the World who is a Monarch? Such a king can turn the laws of justice as easily as the palms of his hands, and act absolutely like Octavius Augustus <note>The first Roman Emperor, known for establishing absolute rule.</note>, or just as absolutely as Nero. After we thought about Omnipotence being bound to laws, we became as if intoxicated and prone to fainting, unless a remedy is quickly brought. For out of our faith we have prayed that God the Father might have mercy on us for the sake of His Son, and we believed that He could have mercy on whomever He pleased, and remit sins to whom it pleases Him, and save whom He wills; and we did not dare to subtract even the smallest thing from His Omnipotence. Therefore, to see God bound by the chains of some of His own laws we regard as a wickedness, because it seems contradictory to His Omnipotence." 

Having said these things, they looked at me, and I at them; and seeing them astonished, I said: "I will pray to the Lord, and I will bring a remedy from Him by illustrating this matter, but for now only through examples." And I said: "Almighty God created the World from the Order within Himself, and thus into the Order in which it exists and according to which He rules it. He implanted into the Universe, and into all its parts, its own order: to man his own, to the beast its own, to the bird and fish their own, to the worm its own, to every tree, and even to the grass, its own. But so that examples may illustrate this, I will briefly bring forward the following: the laws of Order commanded for man are that man should acquire truths for himself from the Word, and think upon them naturally and, as far as he is able, rationally, and thus provide himself with a natural faith. The laws of Order then on God's part are that He approaches, fills the truths with His Divine light, and thus fills man's natural faith—which was previously only knowledge and persuasion—with the Divine essence. In this way, and no other, does faith become saving faith. The case is similar with charity; but we shall briefly review a few points. God cannot, according to His laws, remit sins to any man, except insofar as the man, according to his own laws, desists from them. God cannot spiritually regenerate a man, except insofar as the man, according to his own laws, regenerates himself naturally. God is in a perpetual effort of regenerating and thus saving man, but He cannot effect this except as man prepares himself as a receptacle, and thus levels the way for God and opens the door. A bridegroom cannot enter the chamber of a virgin who is not betrothed; she shuts the door and keeps the key with her inside; but after the virgin has become a bride, she gives the key to the bridegroom. God could not, out of His Omnipotence, redeem men unless He became Man; nor could He make His Human Divine unless His Human was first like the human of an infant, and afterwards like the human of a child, and..."

<summary>This page argues that God's Omnipotence is not an "absolute" power to act against logic or His own nature, but is synonymous with Divine Order. Using the analogy of a bridegroom and a monarch, the author explains that salvation requires a reciprocal response from man, as God operates according to established spiritual laws.</summary>

...unless the <term>Human [nature]</term> <note>original: *Humanum*; Swedenborg refers here to the humanity assumed by Jesus, which had to be "glorified" or made divine through a process.</note> afterwards formed itself into a receptacle and dwelling-place into which His Father might enter. But these are only a few points brought forward for the sake of illustration, so that you may see that Divine Omnipotence exists within order. His government, which is called <term>Providence</term>, acts according to Order; He acts continually and eternally according to the laws of His own Order and cannot act against them, nor change them in the slightest detail <note>original: *quoad apicem*, literally "to the point of a pen," meaning the smallest stroke or tittle.</note>, because Order itself, with all its laws, is God Himself. 

After these things were said, a splendor of light in a golden color flowed through the roof and formed flying cherubs in the air. The reddish light from this illuminated the temples of some of the bystanders from the back of the head, but not yet from the forehead, for they were muttering: "We still do not know what Omnipotence is." And I said, "It will be revealed once the things said thus far have shed some light among you."

74. ***THE THIRD MEMORABLE***. I saw from a distance many people gathered with caps on their heads; some wore caps bound with silk, representing those of the **Ecclesiastical Order**, and some wore caps whose edges were adorned with golden bands, representing those of the **Civil Order**. All of these were learned and erudite men. Furthermore, I saw some wearing turbans, who were unlearned. I approached and heard them talking among themselves about unlimited Divine Power. They argued that if Divine Power proceeded according to certain established laws of order, it would not be unlimited but limited, and thus merely power and not **Omnipotence**. For who does not see that no necessity of law can force Omnipotence to act in one way and not another? Surely, when we think of Omnipotence and simultaneously of the laws of Order according to which it is obliged to proceed, our preconceived ideas of Omnipotence fall like a hand when its walking-staff is broken. 

When they saw me near them, some ran up and said with a certain vehemence: "Are you the one who has bound God with laws as if with chains? How insolent this is! In doing so, you have also torn apart our faith, upon which our salvation is founded. In the center of that faith we place the justice of the **Redeemer**; above that, the Omnipotence of God the Father; and we add the operation of the **Holy Spirit** as an appendix, noting its efficacy in man's absolute helplessness in spiritual things. For such a man, it is enough to speak of the fullness of **justification**, which is present in that faith by the Omnipotence of God. But we have heard that you see only emptiness in this faith, because you find nothing of Divine order required from the side of man within it."

Hearing these things, I opened my mouth and, speaking with a loud voice, said: "Learn the laws of Divine Order, and then open up that faith, and you will see a vast wilderness. In it, you will find a twisting and long <term>Leviathan</term> <note>A biblical sea monster; in Swedenborg’s symbolic language, it often represents natural sciences or reasonings that have become disconnected from spiritual truth.</note>, and all around it, nets wound about like knots that cannot be untied. But do as we read of ***Alexander***, when he saw the ***Gordian Knot*** <note>original: *Nodum Gorgium*; refers to the legend where Alexander the Great cut an impossibly complex knot with his sword rather than untying it.</note>: he drew his sword, cut it in two, and thus unraveled its tangles, threw it to the ground, and crushed its threads with his heel." 

At these words, those gathered bit their tongues, wanting to sharpen them for insults, but they did not dare, because they saw Heaven open above me and heard a voice from there: "Listen first with moderation to what Order is, according to whose laws the All-creating God acts. God created the Universe from Himself as Order, in order, and toward order. Likewise, He created man, in whom He established the laws of His order, by which man was made into the **image and likeness of God**. These laws, in summary, are: that he believe in God and love his neighbor. To the degree that a person does those two things using their natural power, they make themselves a receptacle of Divine Omnipotence, and to that degree God joins Himself to them and them to Himself. From this, their faith becomes living and saving, and their actions become **charity**, also living and saving. 

But it must be known that God is perpetually present, and continually strives and acts in man, and also touches his **free will**, but never violates it. For if He were to violate man's free will, man's ability to dwell in God would perish, and the dwelling would be God's alone in man. This dwelling-place is in everyone—both those on earth and those in heaven, and even those in hell—for from this comes their ability to have power, will, and understanding. However, there is no reciprocal dwelling of man in God except among those who live according to the laws of order laid down in the **Word**. These people become His images and likenesses, and to them is given paradise in possession..."

...sitting, and the fruits of the tree of life for food; but the rest gather themselves around the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, and converse with the Serpent there, and eat, but afterwards they are expelled from Paradise; yet God does not leave them, but they leave God. These things those in caps <note>original: *pileis*; in Swedenborg’s visions, simple caps often represent genuine intelligence, while ornate headwear can represent pride in false wisdom.</note> understood and approved, but those in tiaras denied them and said, "Is not Omnipotence thus limited? and a limited Omnipotence is a contradiction."

But I responded, "It is not a contradiction to act omnipotently according to the laws of justice with judgment, or according to the laws inscribed upon Love by Wisdom; but it is a contradiction that God should be able to act against the laws of His own Justice and Love, for this would be from a lack of judgment and wisdom. Your faith involves such a contradiction, which is that God can justify the unjust out of mere grace, and bestow upon them all the gifts of salvation and rewards of life."

"But I will say in few words what the Omnipotence of God is: God from His Omnipotence created the Universe, and at the same time introduced <term>Order</term> <note>original: *Ordo*; a central concept in this work, referring to the structural laws of reality that originate in God.</note> into each and every part of it. God also from His Omnipotence preserves the Universe, and keeps the Order there with its laws forever, and when anything falls out of order, He brings it back and restores it. Furthermore, God from His Omnipotence established the Church, and revealed the laws of its Order in the <term>Word</term> <note>The Bible or Sacred Scripture.</note>; and when it fell out of order, He restored it; and when it had totally fallen away, He Himself descended into the world, and through the <term>Human [nature]</term> <note>original: *Humanum*; the humanity assumed by Jesus Christ.</note> he assumed, He put on Omnipotence and restored it."

"God, from His Omnipotence and also His Omniscience, explores everyone after death, and prepares the righteous (or the sheep) for their places in Heaven, and from these He builds Heaven; and He prepares the unrighteous (or the goats) for their places in Hell, and from these He builds Hell. He arranges both into Societies and congregations according to all the varieties of their love—which in Heaven are as many as the stars in the firmament of the world—and He joins the Societies in Heaven into one, so that they may be like <term>one Man</term> <note>original: *unus Homo*; the "Grand Man," a concept where all of heaven collectively reflects the human form.</note> before Him. Similarly, He organizes the congregations in Hell so that they may be like one Devil; and He separates these from those by a chasm, lest Hell should bring violence upon Heaven, and lest Heaven should bring torment upon Hell; for those who are in Hell are tormented in proportion to the degree that Heaven flows in. Unless God, by His Omnipotence, did these things every instant, a wildness would enter into men, until they could no longer be restrained by the laws of any Order, and thus the human race would perish. These and similar things would happen, unless God were Order itself, and Omnipotent within Order."

Having heard these things, those who were covered with caps went away with their caps under their arms, praising God; for in that world the intelligent are covered with caps. But those covered with tiaras were not so, because they are bald, and baldness signifies <term>dullness</term> <note>original: *obefitatem*, likely a typo for *hebetudinem* (dullness/insensibility), which in Swedenborg's system is signified by baldness (a lack of the "hairs" of literal truth).</note>; and these went away to the left, while the others went to the right.
