## ON THE CREATION OF THE UNIVERSE.

75. Since in this first chapter the subject is God the Creator, the Creation of the Universe by Him must also be treated, just as in the following chapter on the Lord the Redeemer, Redemption will also be treated. But no one can acquire a just idea of the Creation of the Universe for himself, unless some universal knowledges are first presented to bring the understanding into a state of perception; these are as follows:

**I.** That there are two worlds: a **Spiritual World**, in which there are Angels and Spirits, and a **Natural World**, in which there are men.

**II.** That in both worlds there is a **Sun**, and that the Sun of the spiritual world is pure **Love** from Jehovah God, who is in the midst of it; and that from that sun proceed heat and light; and that the heat proceeding from there is in its essence love, and that the light proceeding from there is in its essence wisdom; and that these two affect the will and the understanding of man—its heat the will, and its light the understanding. But the Sun of the natural world is pure Fire, and therefore the heat from it is dead...

Next, that the two things which proceed from the Sun of the spiritual world—and consequently all things that exist there through them—are *substantial* and are called *spiritual*; while the similar two things which proceed from the Sun of the natural world—and consequently all things that exist here through them—are *material* and are called *natural*. IV. That in both Worlds there are three Degrees, which are called <term>degrees of altitude</term> <note>original: *gradus altitudinis*; these refer to discrete levels of reality, like the difference between a thought and a spoken word, rather than a continuous scale of "more" or "less."</note>, and consequently three Regions, according to which the three angelic Heavens are organized, and according to which human Minds are organized, which thus correspond to those three angelic Heavens; and that other things here and there are similarly arranged. V. That there is a <term>Correspondence</term> <note>original: *Correspondentia*; the concept that every natural effect has a spiritual cause, and that the two "answer" to one another.</note> between those things which are in the spiritual World and those which are in the natural World. VI. That there is an <term>Order</term> <note>original: *Ordo*</note> into which each and every thing of both Worlds was created. VII. That a clear idea of these things must first be acquired; for if it is not, the human mind—out of mere ignorance of them—easily falls into the idea that the Universe was created by Nature, and says only on the basis of Church Authority that Nature was created by God. But because the mind does not know *how*, if it searches into that matter more deeply, it slides headlong into <term>Naturalism</term> <note>original: *Naturalismum*; the belief that only the physical world exists and that God is unnecessary.</note> which denies God. However, because to explain and demonstrate these points individually as they deserve would be a work of a massive Volume, and also does not properly enter into a Theological System as its primary theme or argument (which is the purpose of this Book), I wish only to bring forward some **MEMORABLE RELATIONS**, from which an idea of the Creation of the Universe by God can be conceived, and from that conception, some offspring representing that idea may be born.

## 76. THE FIRST MEMORABLE RELATION.

One day I was in meditation concerning the Creation of the Universe; and because the Angels above me on the right side perceived this—where those were who had occasionally meditated and reasoned on the same subject—one of them descended and invited me. I was "in the spirit" <note>original: *in spiritu*; a state of visionary awareness or out-of-body experience common in Swedenborg’s writings.</note> and accompanied him; and after I entered, I was led to the Prince, in whose Court I saw about a hundred people gathered, with the Prince in their midst. 

Then one of them said, "We perceived here that you were meditating on the Creation of the Universe, and we have been in similar meditation several times, but we could not reach a conclusion. This was because our thoughts were stuck on the idea of Chaos—that it was like a great Egg from which each and every thing of the Universe was hatched in its Order; yet now we perceive that such a vast Universe could not have been hatched in that way. Furthermore, another idea stuck in our minds: that all things were created by God <term>out of nothing</term> <note>original: *ex nihilo*; the traditional theological view that God created the world without pre-existing matter.</note>, and yet we now perceive that from nothing, nothing comes. From these two ideas, our Minds have not yet been able to untangle themselves to see the Creation in any light as to how it was done. Therefore, we called you from the place where you were, so that you might set forth your meditation on this subject."

Having heard these things, I replied, "I will set it forth." And I said, "I meditated on this for a long time, but in vain. But later, when I was admitted by the Lord into your World, I perceived that it was useless to conclude anything about the Creation of the Universe unless it is first known that there are two Worlds: one in which Angels are, and another in which men are, and that men pass through death from their own world into the other. And then I also saw that there were two Suns: one from which all Spiritual things flow, and another from which all Natural things flow. The Sun from which all spiritual things flow is pure Love from Jehovah God, Who is in its midst; and the Sun from which all natural things flow is pure Fire. Knowing these things, once when I was in a state of enlightenment, it was granted to me to perceive that the Universe was created by Jehovah God through the Sun in whose midst He is. And because Love cannot exist except together with Wisdom, the Universe was created by Jehovah God from His Love through His Wisdom. That this is so is proven by each and every thing I have seen in the World where you are, and which I have seen in the World where I..."

I am there in the body. How the progression of Creation took place from its beginning is too long to explain; but while I was in a state of enlightenment, I perceived that through the means of Light and Heat from the Sun of your World, spiritual atmospheres were created—which are <term>substantial</term> <note>original: *substantiales*; in this context, it refers to spiritual reality which is more "real" and enduring than physical matter</note> in themselves—one from another. Because there are three of these, and consequently three degrees of them, three Heavens were made: one for the Angels who are in the highest degree of love and wisdom, a second for the Angels who are in the second degree, and a third for the Angels who are in the lowest degree.

But because this spiritual Universe cannot exist without a natural Universe, in which it might carry out its effects and uses, the Sun from which all natural things proceed was created at the same time. Through this sun, similarly, by means of light and heat, three atmospheres were created surrounding those former ones, just as shells surround kernels, or bark surrounds the wood of a tree. Finally, through these, the terraqueous globe was formed, where humans, beasts, fishes, as well as trees, shrubs, and herbs exist, made from the lands which consist of soil, stones, and minerals.

But this is only a very general sketch of Creation and its progression; the particulars and specifics cannot be explained except in volumes of books. Truly, all things lead to this conclusion: that God did not create the Universe out of nothing, because, as you have said, <note>original: *ex nihilo nihil fit*</note> "nothing comes from nothing," but rather through the Sun of the angelic heaven, which is from His very <term>Being</term> <note>original: *Esse*; the core, essential existence of God</note>, and is therefore pure Love combined with Wisdom. That the Universe—by which is understood both Worlds, the Spiritual and the Natural—was created from Divine Love through Divine Wisdom, is testified and proven by each and every part of it. If you weigh these things in their proper order and connection, you can see this clearly from the light in which the perceptions of your intellect reside. However, it must be kept in mind that the Love and Wisdom which make one in God are not Love and Wisdom in an abstract sense, but are in Him as a Substance; for God is the very, unique, and therefore the first Substance and Essence, which in itself *Is* and *Subsists*. That each and every thing was created from Divine Love and Divine Wisdom is understood by these words in John:

> "The Word was with God, and the Word was God. All things were made by Him, and the world was made by Him." <note>John 1:1, 3, 10</note>

"God" there signifies <term>Divine Love</term>, and "the Word" signifies <term>Divine Truth</term>, or <term>Divine Wisdom</term>; for this reason the Word is there called "Light," and by "Light," when speaking of God, is meant Divine Wisdom. When these things were finished and I was saying goodbye, sparks of light from the Sun there glided down through the angelic Heavens into their eyes, and through these into the dwellings of their minds; and thus enlightened by what I had said, they gave their approval. Afterward, they followed me into the atrium, and my former companion went with me to the house where I was staying, and from there ascended back to his own Society.

## 77. THE SECOND MEMORABLE RELATION.

One morning, having woken from sleep, I was meditating in the serene morning light before being fully awake, when I saw something like a flashing lightning bolt through the window, and soon heard something like a crack of thunder. While I wondered where this came from, I heard from Heaven that there were some people not far from me who were arguing sharply about **GOD AND NATURE**, and that the vibration of light like lightning and the cracking of the air like thunder were <term>correspondences</term> <note>original: *correspondentiæ*; outward natural appearances that reflect internal spiritual states</note> and thus the appearances of the battle and collision of arguments—on one side for God, and on the other for Nature.

The beginning of this spiritual battle was this: there were some <term>Satans</term> <note>original: *Satanæ*; in this theology, Satans are inhabitants of hell who represent false reasoning based on the senses</note> in Hell who said to one another: "If only we were allowed to speak with the Angels of Heaven, we would demonstrate thoroughly and fully that Nature is what they call 'God,' from whom all things come, so that 'God' is merely a word, unless Nature is meant." And because those Satans believed this with all their heart and soul, and desired to speak with the angels of heaven, it was granted to them to ascend out of the mud and darkness of Hell, and to speak with two Angels then descending from Heaven. They were in the <term>World of Spirits</term> <note>original: *Mundus spirituum*; an intermediate realm between Heaven and Hell where spirits first go after death</note>, which is in the middle between Heaven and Hell. When the Satans saw the Angels there, they ran swiftly toward them and cried out in a furious voice: "Are you the Angels of Heaven with whom we may join in debate concerning God and Nature? You are called wise because you acknowledge a God, but oh, how simple you are! Who has seen God? Who understands what God is? Who grasps how God could rule the Universe, and each and every part of it? Who but the common people and the rabble acknowledges what he does not see and understand? What...

nothing is more prominent than that **Nature** is all in all. Who has seen anything with the eye but nature? Who has heard anything with the ear but nature? Who has smelled anything with the nostril but nature? Who has tasted anything with the tongue but nature? Who, by any touch of the hand or body, has felt anything but nature? Are not the senses of our body the witnesses of truths? Who cannot swear by them that it is so? Is not the breath by which our body lives a witness? What do we breathe but nature? Are not our heads and yours in nature? From where does the influence into the thoughts of our heads come, if not from her? If she is taken away, can you think anything at all? <note>This argument represents the "sensualist" philosophy, which claims that only what can be seen and touched is real.</note> Along with many other things of the same ilk. 

Having heard these things, the **Angels** responded: You speak this way because you are merely sensual. All those in **Hell** have the ideas of their thoughts immersed in the senses of the body, and they cannot lift their minds above them. Therefore, we forgive you. A life of evil, and the resulting faith in what is false, has closed the interiors of your minds so that an elevation above sensual things is not possible for you, except in a state far removed from the evils of life and the falsities of faith. For a **Satan** <note>In this context, a "Satan" refers to a spirit in hell who focuses on false reasoning, whereas a "Devil" typically refers to one driven by evil desires.</note> can understand the truth just as well as an **Angel** when he hears it, but he does not retain it, because evil wipes out the truth and brings in the false. 

But we perceive that you are now in such a state of removal, and thus you can understand the truth we are speaking. Therefore, pay attention to what we shall say. And they said: You were in the **Natural World**, and you died there, and now you are in the **Spiritual World**. Did you know anything about life after death before now? Did you not previously deny it and make yourselves equal to the beasts? Did you previously know anything about **Heaven and Hell**, or anything about the light and heat of this world? Or that you are no longer within **Nature**, but above it? For this world and all its things are spiritual, and spiritual things are above natural things, so much so that not even the smallest bit of the nature in which you once were can flow into this world. 

But because you believed **Nature** to be **God** or a **Goddess**, you also believe the **Light and Heat** of this world to be the light and heat of the natural world, when in fact there is not even a tiny bit of it here. For **natural light** is **darkness** here, and **natural heat** is **cold** here. Did you know anything about the **Sun** of this world, from which our **Light and Heat** proceed? Did you know that this **Sun** is pure **Love**, and that the **Sun** of the natural world is pure **Fire**? And that the Sun of the [natural] world, which is pure fire, is that from which **Nature** existed and subsists, but the **Sun** of heaven, which is pure **Love**, is that from which **Life** itself—which is love combined with wisdom—exists and subsists? And thus, that **Nature**, which you make into a **God** or **Goddess**, is completely dead. 

If protection is granted to you, you can ascend with us into **Heaven**, and if protection is granted, we can descend with you into **Hell**. You will see magnificent and splendid things in **Heaven**, but foul and filthy things in **Hell**. These differences exist because everyone in **Heaven** worships **God**, and everyone in **Hell** worships **Nature**. Those magnificent and splendid things in the **Heavens** are the <term>correspondences</term> <note>original: *correspondentiæ*; a key concept in this theology meaning that outward appearances in the spiritual world perfectly mirror the inner state of the inhabitants' hearts and minds.</note> of the affections of the love of good and truth, while the foul and filthy things in the **Hells** are the correspondences of the affections of the love of evil and the false. From these things, conclude now whether **God** or **Nature** is all in all. 

To this, the **Satans** responded: In the state in which we are now, we can conclude from what we have heard that **God** exists; but when the delight of evil occupies our minds, we see nothing but **Nature**. 

Those two **Angels** and the **Satans** were standing not far from me, so I saw and heard them. And behold, I saw many around them who had been celebrated for their learning in the **Natural World**. I wondered that these **Learned Men** <note>original: *Eruditi*</note> stood now near the **Angels**, now near the **Satans**, and that they favored those they were standing next to. It was told to me that the changes in their positions were changes in the state of their minds, favoring now one side and now the other; for regarding faith, they were like <term>shifters</term> <note>original: *vertumni*; referring to Vertumnus, the Roman god of seasons and change, describing people who constantly change their opinions.</note>. 

And we will tell you a mystery: we looked down toward the **Earth** at those celebrated for their learning, and we found six hundred out of a thousand to be in favor of **Nature**, and the rest for **God**. And those who were for **God** were so not from the intellect, but only from having heard frequently that **Nature is from God**; and frequent speaking from memory and recollection, even if not at the same time from thought and intelligence, brings about an appearance of faith. After this, protection was given to the **Satans**, and they ascended with the two **Angels** into **Heaven**.

78. **THIRD MEMORABLE RELATION.** The next day an **Angel** came to me from another Society of Heaven, and said, "We have heard there that because of your meditation on the **Creation of the Universe** you were admitted into a society near ours, and that there you told such things about Creation which they then favored and afterwards rejoiced in; I will now show you how Animals and Vegetables of every kind were produced by God." 

And he led me into a broad green Field, and said, "Look around." And I looked around, and saw Birds most beautifully colored, some flying, some sitting on trees, and some on the field plucking small leaves from roses; among the birds there were also Doves and Swans. After these vanished from my sight, I saw not far from me Flocks of sheep with lambs, of kids and goats, and all around those flocks I saw Herds of Oxen and Calves, then of Camels and Mules, and in a certain grove Hinds with high horns, and also Unicorns. <note>In the author's spiritual visions, "Unicorns" often symbolize the power of truth in the natural world.</note> 

After seeing these, he said, "Turn your face to the East." And I saw a Garden, in which were fruit Trees: Oranges, Citrons, Olives, Vines, Figs, Pomegranates, and also shrubs which bore berries. Afterwards he said, "Look now to the South," and I saw Harvests of various kinds of grain: wheat, millet, barley, and beans, and around those Flower-beds of roses beautifully variegating their colors. Toward the North, however, were Groves full of chestnuts, palms, lindens, plane trees, and other leafy trees. 

When these were seen he said, "All those things which you have seen are **Correspondences** <note>term: Correspondences (The theological concept that every natural object is a physical manifestation of a specific spiritual affection or thought).</note> of the affections of the love of the Angels who are nearby." "We perceive from these things what each one is like in terms of love and wisdom; those things which are in our houses and serve for uses remain there constantly, but before those who wander from society to society, such things change according to their companions. These things were shown to you so that you may see **Universal Creation** in a particular **Model**; <note>original: "Typo"</note> for God is Love itself and Wisdom itself, and of His Love there are infinite affections, and of His Wisdom there are infinite perceptions, and the **Correspondences** of these are each and every thing that appears on the Earth; hence birds and beasts, hence trees and shrubs, hence crops and harvests, and hence herbs and grasses. Because He is Omnipresent, such **Correspondences** of the affections of His Love and Wisdom are in the whole natural World; but in our World, which is called the **Spiritual World**, there are similar correspondences among those who receive affections and perceptions from God. 

The difference is, that such things in our World are created by God in a moment according to the affections of the Angels, but in your World they were similarly created in the beginning, but it was provided that they should be perpetually renewed through generations, one from another, and thus Creation should be continued. 79. **FOURTH MEMORABLE RELATION.** Once, while I was reflecting on the **Creation of the Universe**, some individuals from the Christian World approached. In their own time, they had been among the most famous Philosophers and were considered wiser than others. They said, "We perceive that you are thinking about Creation; tell us your mind on the matter." But I replied, "First, tell me yours." 

And one said, "My view is that Creation is from **Nature**, and thus that **Nature** created itself, and that it has existed from eternity. For there is no such thing as a vacuum, nor can there be. And what else do we see with our eyes, catch with our ears, smell with our noses, and breathe with our chests but **Nature**? And because it is outside of us, it is also within us." 

Another, hearing this, said, "You name **Nature** and make her the creator of the universe, but you do not know how **Nature** worked the Universe into being; so I will tell you. It rolled itself into vortices, which collided with each other like clouds, or like houses collapsing in an earthquake. From that collision, the thicker parts gathered together into one, forming the Earth; the more fluid parts separated from these and gathered together to form the Seas; and from these the lighter parts also separated, forming the ether and air, and from the very lightest of these, the Sun. Have you not seen that when Oil, Water, and Earth-dust are mixed together, they divide spontaneously and arrange themselves in order, one above the other?" 

Then another, listening in, said, "You speak from fantasy. Who does not know that the first origin of all things was **chaos**, which filled a fourth part of the Universe in size? In its center was Fire, around it ether, and around that, matter. That **Chaos** developed cracks, and Fire erupted through them, as from Etna and Vesuvius, creating the Sun. After this, the Ether unfolded and spread around it, creating the Atmosphere; and finally, the remaining matter gathered into a sphere, creating the Earth. As for the Stars, they are merely lights in the Expanse of the Universe, arisen from the Sun and its fire and light. For the Sun was at first like a fiery Ocean which, so it would not burn the Earth, cast out from itself small shining flames which, finding their place in the surroundings, completed the Universe—thus its Firmament." 

But one stood among them who said, "You are wrong. You seem wise to yourselves, and I seem simple to you, but in my simplicity, I have believed and still believe that the Universe was [created] by God..."

Upon hearing this, the first man went back to his associates, asking that they join him in untying this knotty question. They concluded that the <term>human Soul</term> is nothing other than ether, and that thought is nothing other than the modification of that ether by the light of the sun, and since ether belongs to nature, so does the soul. They said, "Who does not know that we speak by means of air? And what is thought but speech in a purer air, which is called ether? This is why thought and speech make one. Who cannot observe this in a person during infancy? He first learns to speak, and gradually learns to speak with himself, and this is thinking. What then is thought but a modification of ether? And what is the sound of speech but its melody? From this we conclude that the <term>Soul</term>, which thinks, belongs to nature."

However, some among them did not exactly disagree but clarified the state of the question, saying that <term>Souls</term> arose when the ether emerged from that great <term>Chaos</term>, and that in the highest region, it divided itself into innumerable individual forms, which infuse themselves into humans when they begin to think from the purer air; these are then called <term>Souls</term>.

Hearing this, another said, "I concede that innumerable individual forms were shaped by the ether in the higher region, but still, the number of humans born since the creation of the <term>World</term> has exceeded that number. How then could those ethereal forms have been sufficient? Therefore, I have thought to myself that <term>Souls</term> departing from the mouths of men when they die return to them after several thousand years and enter into and live a life similar to the previous one. It is well known that many of the wise believe in such similarities and in *<term>Metempsychosis</term>* <note>The Greek term for the transmigration of souls, or reincarnation.</note>."

Besides these, other conjectures were scattered by the rest, which I pass over because they were insane. After a short hour, the <term>Priest</term> returned, and then the one who had first spoken about the Creation of the Universe from God told him of their decisions regarding the <term>Soul</term>. Having heard these things, the <term>Priest</term> said to them, "You have spoken exactly as you thought in the World, not knowing that you are not in that World, but in another, which is called the <term>Spiritual World</term>. All those who have become sensually-minded and bodily-focused through their arguments in favor of Nature do not know otherwise than that they are in the same World in which they were born and raised. The reason is that there they were in a material body, but here they are in a substantial body; and the substantial man sees himself and his companions around him exactly as the material man sees himself and his companions. For the substantial is the primitive essence of the material. And because you think, see, smell, taste, and speak just as you did in the <term>natural World</term>, you believe that the same Nature is here. Yet the nature of this World differs and is as distant from the nature of that World as the substantial is from the material, or the spiritual from the natural, or the prior from the posterior. And because the Nature of the World in which you previously lived is, by comparison, dead, you—through your arguments in its favor—have become as if dead toward those things which belong to God, Heaven, and the Church, and also regarding that matter which concerns your <term>Souls</term>. But nevertheless, every man, both...

At such a time, he can see that God exists, that there is life after death, and that the **Soul** of man is not "ethereal"—and thus not derived from the nature of this World—but is spiritual, and therefore destined to live forever. The understanding can remain in that angelic light as long as the <term>natural loves</term><note>Selfish or worldly desires focused on the physical body and social status.</note>, which are from the World and for it, and from the body and for its own sake, are removed. These loves are removed by the Lord in that moment; and it was granted to these spirits to speak with Angels. From the conversation of the angels in that state, they perceived that God exists, and that they would live in another World after death. At this, they were overwhelmed with shame and cried out, "We have been insane! We have been insane!" 

But because this state was not their own <term>internal nature</term>, it became tedious and unpleasant to them after a few minutes. They turned away from the **Priest** and refused to hear his speech any longer. Thus, they returned to their former loves—which were purely natural, worldly, and corporeal—and went away to the left, from society to society. Finally, they came to a path where the delights of their own loves breathed upon them, and they said, "Let us go this way." They went, descended, and finally came to those who shared in the delights of similar loves, and even worse. Because their delight was the "delight of doing evil," and they had done evil to many even on the way, they were imprisoned and became <term>demons</term>. Then their delight was turned into unpleasantness, because through punishments and the fear of them, they were coerced and restrained from their prior delight, which had formed their very nature. They asked those who were in the same prison whether they were to live this way forever. Some there replied, "We have been here for several ages, and we are to remain for ages of ages; for the nature which we contracted in the World cannot be changed, nor can it be expelled by punishments. Even when it seems expelled by them, it returns after a short lapse of time."

## 80. THE FIFTH MEMORABLE RELATION
<note>A "Memorable Relation" (Memorabile) is a firsthand account of an experience in the spiritual world.</note>

Once, a certain <term>Satan</term><note>In this context, a "Satan" refers to a spirit who is centered in false intellectual principles, rather than "the" singular Devil.</note> ascended from Hell by permission, along with a woman, and approached the house where I was. When I saw them, I closed the window, yet I spoke with them through it. I asked the Satan where he came from; he said from the company of his own kind. I asked where the woman came from; he said the same, that she was from a troop of <term>Sirens</term><note>Spirits who excel at deceiving the senses through illusions.</note>. These Sirens are skilled at using <term>fantasies</term><note>original: "phantaſia." Deceptive appearances created when the higher mind is closed and only the senses are active.</note> to take on every habit and form of beauty and adornment. Sometimes they take the beauty of **Venus**, sometimes the grace of a Muse's face as if she were from **Parnassus**, or they deck themselves out like **Queens** with crowns and robes, walking magnificently while leaning on a silver staff. In the **World of Spirits**, such women are harlots and devote themselves to fantasies. Fantasy is created by sensual thought when ideas from any interior thought are closed off. 

I asked the Satan if she was his Wife. He replied, "What wife? I do not know the word, nor does my society; she is my harlot." Then she inspired the man with lust, which Sirens are very clever at doing. When he received it, he kissed her and said, "Ah, my **Adonis**." 

But to turn to serious matters: I asked the Satan what his function was. He said, "My function is **Learning**. Do you see the laurel upon my head?" This, his "Adonis" had fashioned by her art and placed on him from behind. I said, "Since you come from a society where there are masteries of learning, tell me what you and your associates believe about **God**." 

He replied, "**God** to us is the **Universe**, which we also call **Nature**. The simple among us call it the **Atmosphere**, which to them is the air; but the wise call it the Atmosphere which is also the **Ether**. God, Heaven, Angels, and the like—about which many people tell many stories in this world—are empty words and fictions caught from **Meteors**<note>In the 18th century, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomena, like lightning or rainbows, often used as metaphors for fleeting illusions.</note> which play before the eyes of many here. Are not all things which appear upon the Earth created by the **Sun**? Does not every arrival of the Sun in springtime give birth to winged and wingless worms? And by its heat, do not the birds love one another and procreate? Does not the Earth, warmed by its heat, bring forth seeds into shoots, and finally into fruits as offspring? Is not the **Universe** thus God, and **Nature** the Goddess? And she, as the spouse of the Universe, conceives, gives birth to, educates, and nourishes them." 

Furthermore, I asked what his society believed concerning **Religion**. He replied, "For us who are learned above the common folk, religion is nothing..."

It also details an encounter with a "Satan" and a "Siren" who argue for a materialistic worldview, claiming that Nature and the Universe are the only true God.</summary>

...[nothing] <note>original: "nisi"</note> but a delusion of the common people, which surrounds the sensitive and imaginary parts of their minds like a breeze, in which ideas of piety fly like butterflies in the air. Their faith, which connects those ideas together like a chain, is like a silkworm in its cocoon, from which it flies out like a king of butterflies. For the **unlearned Communion** <note>original: "Communio inerudita"; referring to the body of believers who do not think deeply or spiritually.</note> loves images more than the physical senses and the thoughts derived from them. Because of their desire to fly, they make wings for themselves so that they might lift themselves up like eagles and boast before the inhabitants of the earth, saying, "Look at me!" 

But as for us, we believe what we see, and we love what we touch. (And at that moment he touched his **Harlot** <note>In this theological context, a "Harlot" often symbolizes the affection for false doctrines or a life led by worldly lusts rather than spiritual truth.</note> and said): I believe this, because I see and touch it. Truly, we throw such mockeries out through our windows and drive them away with a gust of laughter.

Afterward, I asked what he and his companions believe concerning **Heaven and Hell**. He replied with a loud laugh: "What is **Heaven** but the ethereal firmament in its height? And what are the **Angels** there but wandering spots moving around the Sun? And **Archangels** but comets with long tails, upon which their crowd lives? And what is **Hell** but marshes, where frogs and crocodiles are the **devils** in their imagination? Beyond these ideas of heaven and hell, the rest are trifles, introduced by some **Primate** <note>A high-ranking church leader or authority figure.</note> to seize glory from an ignorant people."

But he spoke all these things exactly as he had thought about them while in the World, not knowing that he was living after death, and having forgotten all that he had heard when he first entered the **World of Spirits** <note>original: "Mundum Spirituum"; in Swedenborgian theology, this is the intermediate state between Heaven and Hell where spirits first arrive after death.</note>. Therefore, when questioned about life after death, he replied that it was an imaginary thing, and that perhaps some "effluvium" <note>A vapor or invisible emanation.</note> rising from a corpse in a tomb in the shape of a man—or something called a **specter** <note>original: "spectrum"</note> which some people tell stories about—had introduced such a thing into human fantasies.

Hearing these things, I could no longer hold back my laughter, and it broke out. I said: "**Satan**, you are raving in your madness! What are you now? Are you not in human form? Do you not speak, see, hear, and walk? Remember that you lived in another World which you have forgotten, and that you now live after death, and that you have spoken exactly as you did before."

Then **remembrance** <note>original: "reminiscentia"</note> was granted to him, and he recalled it. At this he was ashamed and cried out: "I am insane! I saw heaven above, and I heard angels there speaking unspeakable things—but that was when I first arrived here. But now I will hold onto this to tell my companions from whom I have departed, and perhaps then they will be ashamed likewise." 

He kept it in his mouth to call them insane; but as he descended, forgetfulness drove out the remembrance. When he arrived there, he raved in the same way, and called those things he had heard from me "insanities." Such is the state of thought and speech of **Satans** after death. Those are called **Satans** who have confirmed falsities in themselves until they believe them; and those are called **Devils** who have confirmed evils in themselves by the way they have lived.

# CHAPTER TWO
## CONCERNING THE LORD THE REDEEMER.

81. **I**n the previous chapter we dealt with God the Creator and, at the same time, with Creation. In this chapter, we must deal with the Lord the Redeemer and, at the same time, with Redemption; and in the following chapter, with the Holy Spirit and Divine Operation. By the "Lord the Redeemer," we mean Jehovah in the Human <note>original: "Jehovah in Humano"; Swedenborg uses the term "the Human" as a noun to describe the physical and mental nature assumed by God on earth.</note>. The fact that Jehovah Himself descended and took on the Human for the purpose of accomplishing Redemption will be demonstrated in what follows. The reason He is called "the Lord" and not "Jehovah" is because Jehovah in the Old Testament is called the Lord in the New, as can be seen from these examples. It is said in Moses:
> "Hear, O Israel, JEHOVAH your God, JEHOVAH is one: you shall love JEHOVAH GOD with all your heart, and with all your soul." Deuteronomy 6:4, 5.

But in Mark:
> "The LORD your God is one Lord: you shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, and with all your soul." Chapter 12:29, 30.

Likewise, in Isaiah:
> "Prepare the way of JEHOVAH, make straight in the desert a path for our God." Chapter 40:3.

But in Luke:
> "You shall go before the face of the LORD, to prepare the way for Him." Chapter 1:76.

This is found elsewhere as well. Furthermore, the Lord commanded His disciples to call Him "Lord," and therefore He was called so by the Apostles in their Epistles, and afterward by the Apostolic Church, as is evident from its creed, which is called the <term>Apostles' Creed</term> <note>original: "Symbolum Apostolicum"; the basic statement of Christian belief used since the early centuries of the Church.</note>. The reason for this was that the Jews did not dare to speak the name "Jehovah" because of its holiness; also, by "Jehovah" is understood the <term>Divine Being</term> <note>original: "Divinum Esse"; the fundamental, underlying reality of God's existence.</note> which existed from eternity, whereas the Human that He assumed in time was not that same "Being." What the Divine Being or Jehovah is was shown in the previous chapter (nos. 18 to 26, and 27 to 35). For this reason, here and in the following pages, by "the Lord" we mean Jehovah in His Human. Now, because knowledge concerning the Lord exceeds in excellence all other knowledge available in the Church—and indeed in Heaven—the following points will be arranged in order so that this knowledge may come into the light:

*I. That Jehovah, the Creator of the Universe, descended and took on the Human so that He might redeem and save mankind. II. That He descended as Divine Truth, which is the Word, and yet He did not separate the Divine Good from it. III. That He took on the Human according to His own Divine order. IV. That the Human through which He sent Himself into the world is what is called the <term>Son of God</term>. V. That the Lord made Himself righteousness through the acts of redemption. VI. That through these same acts He united Himself to the Father, and the Father united Himself to Him, also according to Divine order. VII. That thus God became Man, and Man became God, in One Person. VIII. That the progression toward union was His state of emptying <note>original: "exinanitionis"; a theological term for Christ's "self-emptying" or state of humiliation while on earth.</note>, and the Union itself is His state of <term>glorification</term>. IX. That hereafter, no Christian can enter Heaven unless they believe in the Lord God the Savior and approach Him alone.*

But these points will be explained one by one.

82. I. THAT JEHOVAH GOD DESCENDED AND TOOK ON THE HUMAN SO THAT HE MIGHT REDEEM AND SAVE MANKIND. In the Christian churches today, it is believed that God the Creator of the Universe begat a Son from eternity, and that this Son descended and took on the Human to redeem and save men. But this is an error, and it falls apart on its own as soon as one considers that God is one, and that it is more than a fable to the rational mind to think that one God begat another Son from eternity—and also that God the Father, together with the Son and the Holy Spirit (each of whom is individually God), is one God. This fable is completely dispelled, like a falling star in the air, when it is demonstrated from the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note> that Jehovah God Himself descended and became Man, and also the <term>Redeemer</term>. Regarding the first point—that Jehovah God Himself descended and became Man—this is clear from the following:

Besides those places where the coming of the Lord is called the **DAY OF JEHOVAH**, as in Isaiah 13:6, 9, 13, 22; Ezekiel 31:15; Joel 1:15; Chapter 2:1, 2, 11; Chapter 3:2, 4; Chapter 4:14, 18; Amos 5:13, 18, 20; Zephaniah 1:7 to 18; Zechariah 14:1, 4 to 21, and elsewhere. To whom the Angel responded, **THE HOLY SPIRIT SHALL COME UPON THEE, AND THE POWER OF THE MOST HIGH SHALL OVERSHADOW THEE, WHEREFORE THAT HOLY THING WHICH IS BORN OF THEE SHALL BE CALLED THE SON OF GOD**," Chapter 1:34, 35. That by the Holy Spirit is meant the Divine which proceeds from Jehovah God will be seen in the third chapter of this work. Who does not know that the Soul and Life of an offspring are from the father, and that the Body is from the soul? What, therefore, is more clearly stated than that the Lord had His Soul and Life from Jehovah God? And because the Divine cannot be divided, the very Divine of the Father was His Soul and Life. This is why the Lord so often called Jehovah God His Father, and Jehovah God called Him His Son. What, then, can be heard that is more ridiculous than that the Soul of our Lord was from His mother Mary, as both Roman Catholics and the Reformed dream today, not yet having been awakened by the Word?

83. That any Son born from eternity descended and assumed the Human falls away and is dissipated as completely erroneous by those places in the Word in which Jehovah Himself says that He Himself is the Savior and Redeemer, which are the following: "AM I NOT **JEHOVAH**, and there is no God besides Me? A just **GOD** and a **SAVIOR**, there is none besides Me," Isaiah 45:21, 22. "I AM **JEHOVAH**, AND BESIDES ME THERE IS NO **SAVIOR**," Isaiah 43:11. # OF THE NEW HEAVEN AND THE NEW CHURCH.
<note>The header refers to the "New Church" or "New Jerusalem" which Swedenborg believed he was announcing.</note>

*Your Redeemer is Jehovah*, Isaiah 54:8. *You have redeemed me, Jehovah of Truth*, Psalm 31:6. *Let Israel hope in* JEHOVAH, *for with* JEHOVAH *there is Mercy, and with Him is plenteous* REDEMPTION; *He shall redeem Israel from all his iniquities*, Psalm 130:7, 8. JEHOVAH GOD, AND YOUR REDEEMER, *the Holy One of Israel, shall be called the God of the whole earth*, Isaiah 54:5. From these passages and many others, every man who has eyes and whose mind is opened through those eyes can see that God, who is one, descended and became Man for the purpose of carrying out Redemption. Who cannot see this as clearly as morning light when he attends to those very Divine utterances that have been brought forward? But truly, those who are in the shadow of night—because they have confirmed the birth of another God from eternity and his descent and Redemption—close their eyelids to those Divine utterances and think below them about how they might apply them to their own false views and pervert them.

84. There are many reasons why God could not have redeemed men—that is, pulled them out from damnation and Hell—except through an assumed Human <note>original: "Humanum." Swedenborg uses this term technically to refer to the physical and mental nature God took on in Jesus Christ.</note>; these will be revealed in order in what follows. For Redemption was the subjugation of the Hells and the ordering of the Heavens, and after these, the restoration of the Church. God, out of His Omnipotence, could not effect these things except through the Human; just as no one can work unless he has an arm (His Human is also called the "Arm of Jehovah" in the Word, Isaiah 40:10; Chapter 53:1); and just as no one can attack a fortified city and destroy the shrines of idols within it except through intermediate powers. That God had Omnipotence in this Divine work through His Human is also evident from the Word. For God, who is in the inmost and thus the purest things, could not possibly pass through to the outmost things <note>The "ultimates" or most external, physical levels of existence.</note> where the Hells are, and where the people of that time were, in any other way—comparable to how the soul cannot do anything without a body. Or, it is like someone who cannot conquer enemies who do not come into his sight, or whom he cannot approach and get near to with some kind of weapons, such as spears, shields, or guns. To carry out Redemption without the Human was as impossible for God as it is for a man to subjugate the Indies without transporting soldiers there by ships; or like making trees grow only by heat and light unless the air is created through which they pass, and the earth is created from which they are produced. Indeed, it is as impossible as casting nets into the air to catch fish there, rather than in the waters. For Jehovah, as He is in Himself, cannot by His Omnipotence touch any devil in Hell nor any devil on earth and restrain him and his fury, or tame his violence, unless He is in the outmost things just as He is in the first things. He is in His Human in the outmost things; wherefore in the Word He is called the First and the Last, Alpha and Omega, the Beginning and the End.

85. II. **THAT JEHOVAH GOD DESCENDED AS DIVINE TRUTH, WHICH IS THE WORD, AND YET THAT HE DID NOT SEPARATE DIVINE GOOD.** There are two things that make up the Essence of God: Divine Love and Divine Wisdom, or what is the same, Divine Good and Divine Truth. That the Essence of God consists of those two was demonstrated above in numbers 36 to 48. Those two are also understood in the Word by JEHOVAH GOD: by "Jehovah" is meant Divine Love or Divine Good, and by "God" is meant Divine Wisdom or Divine Truth. Hence it is that they are distinguished in various ways in the Word; sometimes only "Jehovah" is named, sometimes only "God"—for where the subject is Divine Good, there it says "Jehovah," and where it is Divine Truth, there "God," and where it is both, there "Jehovah God." That Jehovah God descended as Divine Truth, which is the Word, is evident in John, where it says: "*In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God... all things were made through Him, and without Him nothing was made that was made... And the Word was made Flesh, and dwelt among us*," Chapter 1:1, 3, 14. The reason Divine Truth is meant there by "the Word" is because the Word, which is in the Church, is Divine Truth itself; for it was dictated by Jehovah Himself, and what is dictated by Jehovah is purely Divine Truth, nor...

it cannot be anything else; but because that <note>The Word or Divine Truth</note> passed through the Heavens even into the World, it was made adapted to the Angels in Heaven and also to humans in the World. For this reason, there is a spiritual sense within the Word in which Divine Truth is in light, and a natural sense in which Divine Truth is in shadow. Therefore, Divine Truth in this Word is what is meant in John: this is further evident from the fact that the Lord came into the World to fulfill all things of the Word, which is why we so often read that this or that was done by Him so that the Scripture might be fulfilled. Neither is anything else understood by the Messiah or Christ, nor by the Son of Man, nor by the <term>Paraclete</term> <note>original: "Paracletum." A Greek-derived term meaning the Advocate, Helper, or Comforter, referring here to the Holy Spirit.</note> or Holy Spirit, whom the Lord sent after His departure. It will be seen in the chapter on <term>Sacred Scripture</term> <note>original: "Scriptura Sacra." Swedenborg's technical term for the Bible as a divinely inspired, multi-layered text.</note> that He represented Himself as that Word in His Transfiguration before the three Disciples on the mountain (Matthew 17, Mark 9, and Luke 9), and also before John in Revelation (Chapter 1:12 to 16). That the Lord in the World was Divine Truth is clear from His own words: *I am the Way, the Truth, and the Life* (John 14:6); and from these: *We know that the Son of God has come, and has given us Understanding, that we may know the Truth, and we are in the Truth, in His Son Jesus Christ: This is the true God, and eternal life* (1 John 5:20, 21). And furthermore, He is called the *Light*, as in these places: *The true Light was that which enlightens every man coming into the World* (John 1:4, 9). *Jesus said, for a little while longer the Light is with you; walk while you have the Light, lest darkness seize you: as long as you have the Light, believe in the Light, that you may be children of Light* (John 12:35, 36, 46). *I am the Light of the World* (John 9:5). Simeon said, *my eyes have seen your Salvation, a Light for revelation to the nations* (Luke 2:30, 31, 32). *This is the judgment, that Light has come into the World* (John 3:19, 21). In these and other places, Divine Truth is meant by "Light."

86. The reason Jehovah God descended into the World as Divine Truth was to perform Redemption; and Redemption was the subjugation of the Hells, the ordering of the Heavens, and after these, the restoration of the Church. To accomplish these things, <term>Divine Good</term> <note>In Swedenborg’s theology, "Good" relates to the will and love, while "Truth" relates to the intellect and wisdom.</note> is not sufficient, but Divine Truth from Divine Good is. Divine Good, viewed in itself, is like the round pommel of a sword, or like a blunt piece of wood, or like a bare bow; but Divine Truth from Divine Good is like a sharp sword, like a spear, and like a bow with arrows, which are effective against enemies. By swords, spears, and bows in the spiritual sense of the Word, fighting truths are also meant—see *Revelation Revealed*, numbers 52, 299, 436, where this is demonstrated. In no other way could the falsities and evils in which the entire Hell was, and perpetually is, be attacked, conquered, and subjugated except through Divine Truth from the Word. Nor could the New Heaven (which was also created at that time) be established, formed, and ordered by any other means; nor could the New Church on earth be restored by any other means. Furthermore, all the strength, all the virtue, and all the power of God belongs to Divine Truth from Divine Good. This was the reason that Jehovah God descended as Divine Truth, which is the Word. Therefore it is said in David: *Gird your sword upon your thigh, O Mighty One, and in your glory ascend; ride upon the Word of truth; your right hand shall teach You wonders; your arrows are sharp, your enemies shall fall under You* (Psalm 45:3, 4, 5). This refers to the Lord, to His battles with the Hells, and to His victories over them.

87. What Good is without Truth, and what Truth is from Good, appears clearly from the human being. All of a person's good resides in the Will, and all of their truth in the Intellect. The Will, from its good, cannot act even a tiny bit except through the Intellect; it cannot work, it cannot speak, nor can it feel. All its virtue and power is through the intellect, and consequently through truth, for the intellect is the receptacle and dwelling place of truth. The situation is similar to the operation of the Heart and the Lungs in the Body. The Heart, without the respiration of the Lungs, produces no motion and no sensation; rather, the respiration of the lungs performs these two things from the heart. This is evident in the fainting spells of those being suffocated or those who have fallen into water, in whom respiration ceases,

Therefore it is said in John: *That through the Word all things were made, and without It nothing was made that was made* (Chapter 1:3, 10); and in David: *By the Word of Jehovah the Heavens were made, and by the Spirit of His mouth all their host* (Psalm 33:6).

88. Although God descended as Divine Truth, He nevertheless did not separate the Divine Good. This is evident from the Conception, of which we read that the power of the Most High overshadowed Mary (Luke 1:35), and by the "power of the Most High" is meant the <term>Divine Good</term> <note>original: "Divinum Bonum." The essential being or "heat" of God, whereas Divine Truth is the "light" or manifestation.</note>. The same is evident from the passages where He Himself says that the Father is in Him, and He is in the Father; that all things of the Father are His; and that the Father and He are one, besides many other things. By "the Father" is meant the Divine Good.

### 89. III. THAT GOD ASSUMED THE HUMAN ACCORDING TO HIS DIVINE ORDER.

In the Paragraph on Divine <term>Omnipotence</term> and <term>Omniscience</term>, it was shown that God, together with Creation, introduced Order both into the Universe and into each and every part of it; and that therefore God’s Omnipotence in the Universe and in its parts proceeds and operates according to the laws of His own Order, which were discussed in the series from numbers 49 to 74 above. Now, because God descended, and because He is Order Himself (as was also demonstrated there), He could not actually become a man in any other way than being conceived, carried in the womb, born, educated, and successively learning sciences, and through them being introduced into intelligence and wisdom. Therefore, as to the <term>Human</term> <note>original: "Humanum." Swedenborg uses this as a noun to refer to the human nature or vessel that God took on in the world.</note>, He was an infant like an infant, a boy like a boy, and so on; with the only difference being that He completed that progression sooner, more fully, and more perfectly than others. That this progress occurred according to Order is clear from these words in Luke: *The child Jesus grew and was strengthened in spirit, and increased in wisdom, age, and grace before God and men* (Chapter 2:40, 52). That He did so sooner, more fully, and more perfectly than others is clear from what is said of Him by the same Evangelist: that when He was a *Boy of twelve years, He sat in the Temple in the midst of the Doctors and taught, and that all who heard Him were astonished at His Intelligence and His Answers* (Chapter 2:46, 47; and later Chapter 4:16 to 22, 32). This was done because Divine Order requires that a person prepare himself for the reception of God; and as one prepares oneself, so God enters into him as into His own dwelling and home. That preparation is made through cognitions about God and about the spiritual things belonging to the Church, and thus through intelligence and wisdom. For it is a Law of Order that as much as a person approaches and draws near to God (which he must do exactly as if by his own effort), so much God approaches and draws near to the person, and joins Himself with him in his midst. That the Lord progressed according to this Order even to Union with His Father will be further demonstrated in what follows.

92. ## IV. THAT THE HUMAN, THROUGH WHICH GOD SENT HIMSELF INTO THE WORLD, IS THE SON OF GOD.

The Lord frequently said that the Father sent Him, and that He was sent by the Father, as in Matthew 10:40, Chapter 15:24; John 3:17, 34; Chapter 5:23, 24, 36, 37, 38; Chapter 6:29, 39, 40, 44, 57; Chapter 7:16, 18, 28, 29; Chapter 8:16, 18, 29, 42; Chapter 9:4; and very often elsewhere. He says this because by "being sent into the World," is understood to descend and come among men; and this was done through the Human, which He assumed through the virgin Mary. The Human is also actually the Son of God, because it was conceived from <term>Jehovah God</term> <note>Swedenborg identifies Jehovah as the one God of the Old Testament who became incarnate as Jesus Christ.</note> as Father, according to Luke 1:32, 35. He is called the "Son of God," the "Son of Man," and the "Son of Mary." By the **Son of God** is understood Jehovah God in His Human; by the **Son of Man**, the Lord regarding the <term>Word</term> <note>original: "Verbum." Here referring to the Divine Truth or Scripture.</note>; and by the **Son of Mary**, specifically the Human that He assumed. That those two things are understood by "Son of God" and "Son of Man" will be demonstrated in what follows. That by the "Son of Mary" is understood the merely human [part] is clearly evident from the generation of men: that the soul is from the father and the body is from the mother. For the soul is in the seed of the father, and this is clothed with a body in the mother; or what is the same, everything spiritual that a man has is from the father, and everything material is from the mother. Regarding the Lord, the Divine that He had was from the Father, Jehovah, and the Human was from the mother; these two united are the Son of God. That this is so is clearly evident from the birth of the Lord, concerning which it says in Luke: *“The Angel Gabriel said to Mary, The Holy Spirit shall come upon thee, and the power of the Most High shall overshadow thee, therefore that Holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God,”* Chapter 1:35. The Lord called Himself "Sent by the Father" also for this reason: because "Sent" signifies the same thing as "Angel." [...to view the Lord as] the Son of Mary and not the Son of God results in the idea of His Divinity perishing from the mind. With it, everything said in the Word about Him as the Son of God is lost. Furthermore, this opens the door to Judaism, Arianism, Socinianism, and Calvinism (as it existed in its early stages), and eventually to Naturalism and Fanaticism. This stems from the belief that the Son of Mary was the offspring of Joseph and that His soul was from His mother; thus, He is called the Son of God but is not truly so. Let everyone, whether clergy or laity, examine themselves to see if they have conceived or fostered any other idea of the Lord as the Son of Mary than that of a mere man. 

Because such an idea began to prevail among Christians as early as the third century when the Arians arose, the Council of Nicaea <note>The first ecumenical council in 325 AD, which addressed the Arian controversy regarding the nature of Christ.</note> invented the "Son of God born from eternity" to defend the Lord’s Divinity. By this fiction, the Human of the Lord was indeed elevated to the Divine then—and is still elevated today among many—but not among those who understand the hypostatic union <term>hypostatic union: a technical theological term for the union of Christ’s divine and human natures in one person</term> as a union between two separate beings, where one is above and the other is below. 

What else results from this but the destruction of the entire Christian Church, which is founded solely upon the worship of Jehovah in the Human—and thus upon the God-Man? The Lord declares in many places that no one can see the Father, nor know Him, nor come to Him, nor believe in Him, except through His Human. If this is not maintained, every noble seed of the Church is turned into an ignoble one: the seed of the olive becomes the seed of the pine; the seeds of the orange, lemon, apple, and pear become the seeds of the willow, elm, linden, or oak; the vine becomes a marsh reed; and wheat and barley become mere chaff. Indeed, all spiritual food becomes like the dust upon which serpents feed. For in such a person, spiritual light becomes natural and finally sensual-corporeal, which, when viewed in itself, is a deceptive light <note>original: "lux fatua," often referring to a "will-o'-the-wisp" or misleading glow</note>. Indeed, the person then becomes like a bird that falls to the ground with clipped wings while flying high; as it walks, it sees no further than what lies at its feet. Such a person thinks of the spiritual matters of the Church, which are for eternal life, no differently than a fortune-teller <note>original: "hariolus," a soothsayer or diviner</note>. These things happen whenever a person regards the Lord God the Redeemer and Savior as the mere Son of Mary—that is, as a mere man.

95. **V. THAT THE LORD MADE HIMSELF RIGHTEOUSNESS THROUGH ACTS OF REDEMPTION.** It is said and believed in Christian churches today that merit and righteousness belong to the Lord alone through the obedience He rendered to God the Father in the world, and especially through the passion of the cross. However, it has been mistakenly assumed that the passion of the cross was the actual act of redemption, when in fact it was not the act of redemption, but the act of the glorification of His Human (this topic is discussed in the following section on REDEMPTION). 

The acts of Redemption, by which the Lord made Himself righteousness, consisted in His performing the Last Judgment (which took place in the spiritual world). At that time, He separated the evil from the good and the goats from the sheep, expelled from Heaven those who were at one with the "beasts of the dragon," and formed a New Heaven from the worthy and Hell from the unworthy. He successively restored all things to order in both realms and, moreover, established a New Church. These were the acts of Redemption by which the Lord made Himself righteousness; for righteousness is to do all things according to Divine Order, and to restore to order those things which have fallen out of it—for Divine Order itself is Righteousness. 

These concepts are understood by these words of the Lord: *“It is fitting for Me to fulfill* ALL THE RIGHTEOUSNESS OF GOD,” *Matthew 3:15*; and by these passages in the Old Testament: *“Behold, the days are coming when I will raise up to David* A RIGHTEOUS BRANCH, *who shall reign as King, and shall do* RIGHTEOUSNESS IN THE EARTH, *and this is His name: JEHOVAH OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS,” Jeremiah 23:5-6; 33:15-16. “I speak in* RIGHTEOUSNESS, *mighty to save,” Isaiah 63:1. “He shall sit upon the throne of David to establish it in* JUDGMENT *and* RIGHTEOUSNESS,” *Isaiah 9:7 <note>The source text cites IX:6, which corresponds to verse 7 in English Bibles.</note>. “Zion shall be redeemed in* RIGHTEOUSNESS,” *Isaiah 1:27.*

96. Our own leaders, who hold the highest positions in the Church, describe the Lord's righteousness in a completely different way; they make their saving faith consist in the "imputation" <note>The theological concept that Christ's righteousness is legally credited to a believer's account.</note> of this righteousness to man. Yet the truth is that the Lord's righteousness—because of its nature and origin, being in itself purely Divine—cannot be joined to any human being, and thus cannot produce any salvation, any more than Divine Life (which is Divine Love and Divine Wisdom) [could be joined directly].

# OF THE NEW HEAVEN AND THE NEW CHURCH.

The Lord enters into every person with these <note>Referring to the principles of life and salvation mentioned previously.</note>, but unless a person lives according to order, that Life is indeed present within, but it contributes nothing at all to salvation; it merely provides the faculty for understanding truth and doing good. To live according to Order is to live according to the commandments of God; and when a person lives and acts in this way, they then acquire for themselves **righteousness** <term>righteousness: the Latin "justitia" carries the weight of both moral uprightness and divine justice</term>—not the righteousness of the Lord’s redemption, but the Lord Himself as **Righteousness**. These are the ones who are understood by these words: *"Unless your RIGHTEOUSNESS exceeds that of the Scribes and Pharisees, you shall not enter the Kingdom of the heavens" (Matthew 5:20)* <note>The Latin text cites verse 19, but this corresponds to verse 20 in modern Bibles.</note>, and *"Blessed are those who suffer persecution for the sake of RIGHTEOUSNESS, for theirs is the Kingdom of the Heavens" (Matthew 5:10)*. At the consummation of the age, the Angels will go out and separate the wicked from the midst of the RIGHTEOUS *(Matthew 13:49)*, among other places. By the "Righteous" in the Word are meant those who have lived according to Divine order, because Divine order is Righteousness itself. 

This Righteousness itself, which the Lord became through the acts of redemption, cannot be assigned, inscribed, adapted, or joined to a person in any way other than how light is joined to the eye, sound to the ear, the will to the muscles of one acting, thought to the lips of one speaking, air to the lung when breathing, or heat to the blood; everyone perceives for themselves that these things flow in and attach themselves, rather than being inherently joined. But righteousness is acquired in proportion to how much a person practices righteousness; and one practices righteousness in proportion to how much they act with their neighbor out of a love for what is just and true. In the good itself, or in the very use that one performs, righteousness dwells. For the Lord says that every tree is known by its fruit. Who does not know another person by their works, if they pay attention to the end and purpose of the will, and the intention and cause for which they are done? To these things all the Angels attend, as do all the wise in our World. In general, every growth and sprout from the earth is known by its flower and seed, and by its use; every metal by its goodness; every stone by its quality; every field, every food, and every animal of the earth and bird of the Heaven by its own quality. Why not also man? But regarding the quality of a man's works—and where that quality comes from—this will be revealed in the chapter on FAITH.

## 97. VI. THAT THE LORD UNITED HIMSELF TO THE FATHER AND THE FATHER UNITED HIMSELF TO THE LORD BY THE SAME ACTS.

The reason the union was effected through the acts of redemption is that the Lord performed them from His Human; and as He performed them, the Divine (which is understood by "the Father") drew nearer, helped, and cooperated, until finally they joined themselves so that they were not two, but one. This Union is **Glorification**, which will be discussed in the following sections.

98. That the Father and the Son—that is, the Divine and the Human—are united in the Lord like Soul and Body, is indeed part of the faith of the Church today, and also comes from the Word; yet scarcely five in a hundred, or fifty in a thousand, actually know this. The cause is the Doctrine of justification by faith alone. Most of the Clergy, who pursue a reputation for learning for the sake of honors and profit, devote themselves to this doctrine with all their zeal, until today that doctrine carries and occupies every point of their minds. Because these thoughts have intoxicated them like the spirit of wine called **alcohol**, they—like drunkards—have failed to see this most essential point of the Church: that Jehovah God descended and assumed the Human. Yet, it is only through this Union that a conjunction of man with God is possible, and through that conjunction, salvation. That salvation depends on the knowledge and acknowledgment of God can be clear to anyone who considers that God is the "all in all" of Heaven, and therefore the "all in all" of the Church, and consequently the "all in all" of Theology. 

But first, it will be demonstrated here that the Union of the Father and the Son, or the Divine and the Human in the Lord, is like the union of soul and body; and afterwards, that this Union is reciprocal. The Union like that of soul and body is established in the **Athanasian Creed** <note>A statement of Christian doctrine from the 5th or 6th century, traditionally attributed to St. Athanasius.</note>, which is accepted throughout the Christian World as the Doctrine concerning God. ...because God is one and not three, while that Union is understood to be with the one God from eternity, that Doctrine agrees with the Word; in the Word these things are read: "*That he was conceived by Jehovah the Father*," Luke 1:34, 35; hence His soul and life, wherefore He says, that *He and the Father are one*, John 10:30. *That he who sees and knows Him, sees and knows the Father*, John 14:9. *If you knew Me, you would also know my Father*, John 8:19. *He who receives Me, receives Him who sent Me*, John 13:20. *That He is in the bosom of the Father*, John 1:18. *That all things whatsoever the Father has, are His*, John 16:15. *That He is called the Father of eternity*, Isaiah 9:5 <note>In many English Bibles, this is Isaiah 9:6.</note>. *That hence He has power over all flesh*, John 17:2 <note>The OCR says XVIII, but the quote refers to John 17:2.</note>. *And all power in Heaven and on Earth*, Matthew 28:18. From these and many more places in the Word it can be clearly seen, that the Union of the Father and Himself is like that of Soul and Body; wherefore also in the Old Testament He is very often named Jehovah, Jehovah of Hosts <note>original: "Jehovah Zebaoth"</note>, and Jehovah the Redeemer, see above no. 83.

99. That this Union is reciprocal, is clearly evident from these places in the Word: "*Philip, do you not believe, that I am in the Father, and the Father is in Me? Believe Me, that I am in the Father, and the Father is in Me*," John 14:10, 11 <note>The OCR says verse 6, but it is 10-11.</note>. "*That you may know and believe, that the Father is in Me, and I in the Father*," John 10:38. "*That they all may be one, as You, Father, are in Me, and I in You*," John 17:21. "*Father, all Mine are Yours, and all Yours are Mine*," John 17:10. The reason that the Union is reciprocal <term>reciprocal union: a two-way connection where both parties actively approach and dwell within each other</term>, is because no Union or conjunction is possible between two, unless one approaches the other in turn; every Conjunction in the universal Heaven, and in the universal World, and in the whole person, comes from no other source than from the reciprocal approach of one to the other, and then that one wills one with the other; from this comes what is homogenous and sympathetic, as well as unanimous and concordant, in every single part of both. Such a reciprocal conjunction exists between the soul and body in every person; such is the conjunction of the human spirit with the sensory and motor organs of its body; such is the conjunction of the heart and lungs; such is the conjunction of the will and the understanding; such is the conjunction of all the members and viscera within and among themselves, in a person; such a conjunction of minds exists among all who love each other interiorly, for that is inscribed upon all love and friendship, for love wants to love and wants to be loved. There is a reciprocal conjunction of all things in the World that are soundly joined together; a similar conjunction is that of the sun’s heat with the heat of wood and stone, of vital heat with the heat of all the fibers in living creatures, similar is that of the tree with the root, through the root with the tree, and through the tree with the fruit; such is that of a magnet with iron, and so forth. Unless conjunction happens by the approach of one to the other reciprocally and in turn, there is only an external conjunction and not an internal one, and this, over time, slips away from each other, sometimes to the point that they no longer recognize each other.

100. Now because no conjunction is possible which is truly conjunction unless it happens reciprocally and in turn, therefore the conjunction of the Lord and man is no different, as is clearly evident from these places: "*He who eats my flesh, and drinks my blood, ABIDES IN ME, AND I IN HIM*," John 6:56. "*ABIDE IN ME, AND I IN YOU; HE WHO ABIDES IN ME AND I IN HIM, he brings forth much fruit*," John 15:4, 5. "*He who opens the door, I will enter in to him, and WILL DINE WITH HIM, AND HE WITH ME*," Revelation 3:20, besides elsewhere; this Conjunction happens because man approaches the Lord, and the Lord approaches him; for it is a certain and immutable Law, that as much as man approaches the Lord, so much the Lord approaches man; but more on this will be seen in the Chapter on CHARITY and FAITH.

### 101. VII. THAT THUS GOD BECAME MAN, AND MAN BECAME GOD, IN ONE PERSON.

That Jehovah God became Man and Man became God in one Person follows as a conclusion from all the preceding Articles of this Chapter, especially from these two: "That Jehovah the Creator of the universe descended and assumed the Human, so that He might redeem and save mankind," concerning which see above no. 82, 83, 84; and "That the Lord through the acts of Redemption united Himself to the Father, and the Father Himself to Him, thus reciprocally and in turn," concerning which see above no. 97 to 100; from that reciprocal Union it is evidently clear, that God became...

...becomes Man, and Man God in one Person: the same also follows from the Union of both, that it is like that of the Soul and Body. That this is according to the faith of the contemporary Church from the Athanasian Creed <note>original: "Symbolo Athanaasii"; this is a 5th-century statement of Christian belief focusing on the Trinity and Christology</note>, see above, no. 89; as well as according to the faith of the Protestants <note>original: "Evangelicorum"; in Swedenborg’s time, this specifically referred to the Lutheran Church</note> in the chief book of their Orthodoxy, which is called the **FORMULA OF CONCORD**, where it is firmly established—both from Sacred Scripture and from the Church Fathers, and also through reason—that the Human Nature of Christ was exalted to Divine Majesty, Omnipotence, and Omnipresence. It also establishes that in Christ, Man is God and God is Man; on this see that book, pages 607 and 765. Furthermore, in this Chapter it is proved that Jehovah God, with respect to His Human, is called in the Word Jehovah, Jehovah God, Jehovah of Hosts <note>original: "Jehovah Zebaoth"</note>, and also the God of Israel. Wherefore Paul says, *That in Jesus Christ all the fullness of the Divinity dwells bodily*, Colossians 2:9; and John says, *That Jesus Christ the Son of God is the true God and eternal Life*, 1 Epistle 5:20, 21. That by "the Son of God" His Human nature is properly understood, see above no. 92 and following. And furthermore, Jehovah God calls both Himself and Him "Lord"; for it is read, *The LORD said to my Lord, sit at my right hand*, Psalm 110:1; and in Isaiah, *A child is born to us, a Son is given to us, whose name is* GOD, ETERNAL FATHER, Chapter 9:5, 6. By "Son" is also understood the Lord regarding His Human in David: *I will announce the decree, Jehovah said, YOU ARE MY SON, TODAY I have begotten You, kiss the* SON, *lest He be angry, and you perish in the way*, Psalm 2:7, 12. Here it does not mean the Son from eternity, but the Son born in the world, for it is a prophecy of the Lord to come; this is why it is called a "Decree" about which Jehovah announced to David. In that same Psalm it is stated earlier, *I have anointed my King over Zion*, verse 6, and follows, *I will give Him the nations as an inheritance*, verse 8; therefore "TODAY" in that context does not mean from eternity, but in time, for with Jehovah the future is as the present.

102. It is believed that the Lord, regarding His Human, not only was, but also remains the Son of Mary; but in this the Christian world is mistaken. That He was the Son of Mary is true, but that He still is, is not true; for through the acts of Redemption He cast off <note>original: "exuit"; literally to strip off or undress</note> the human nature from the Mother and put on <note>original: "induit"; to clothe or put on</note> a Human nature from the Father. From this, the Lord's Human is Divine, and in Him God is Man and Man is God. That He cast off the human from the mother and put on a Human from the Father—which is the Divine Human—can be seen from the fact that He Himself never called Mary His mother, as can be established from these passages: *The Mother of Jesus said to Him, they have no wine, Jesus said to her, what is there to Me and to you, WOMAN, my hour has not yet come*, John 2:4. And elsewhere, *Jesus from the cross sees His Mother, and the Disciple standing by whom He loved, He says to His Mother, WOMAN behold your son, then He says to the Disciple, behold your mother*, John 19:26, 27. And once He did not even acknowledge her: *It was announced to Jesus by those saying, Your mother and your brothers stand outside, and want to see You. Jesus responding said, My mother and my brothers are these, who hear the Word of God and do it*, Luke 8:20, 21; Matthew 12:46 to 49; Mark 3:31 to 35. Thus the Lord did not call her "Mother" but "Woman," and gave her to John to be his mother. In other places she is called His Mother, but never by His own mouth. This is also confirmed by the fact that He did not acknowledge Himself to be the Son of David; for it is read in the Gospels, *Jesus asked the Pharisees, saying, what do you think of the Christ, whose Son is He? They say to Him, David's. He said to them, how then does David in spirit call Him his Lord, saying, THE LORD said TO MY LORD, sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool; if therefore David calls Him Lord, how is He his son? and no one could answer Him a word*, Matthew 22:39 to 44; Mark 12:35, 36, 37; Luke 20:41 to 44; Psalm 110:1.

To these things I will add this new account: once it was granted to me to speak with Mary the Mother. She passed by once, and was seen in Heaven above my head in white clothing as if of silk. Then, lingering a little, she said that she had been the Mother of the Lord because He was born of her, but that having become God, He cast off all the human nature he had from her, and that therefore she worships Him as her God, and that she does not want anyone [to...]

...acknowledge Him as His Son, because in Him is everything Divine." From these things it now becomes clear this truth: that Jehovah is Man in such a way that He is in the first things and also in the last things, according to these words: *I am the Alpha and the Omega, the Beginning and the End; He who Is, and who Was, and who is to Come, the Almighty,* Revelation 1:8, 11. When John saw the Son of Man in the midst of the seven lampstands, he fell at His feet as if dead; but He laid His right hand upon him, saying, *I am the First and the Last,* Revelation 1:13, 17; Chapter 21:6. *Behold, I come quickly, to give to every man according to his work, I am the Alpha and the Omega, the Beginning and the End, the First and the Last,* Revelation 22:12, 13.
