103. To these things I will add this Secret <note>original: "Arcanum"; a term Swedenborg uses for hidden spiritual truths revealed through his writings</note>: that the Soul, which is from the Father, is the man himself, and that the Body, which is from the mother, is not the man in himself, but is from the soul; the body is merely the soul's clothing, woven from such things as are in the natural world, while the Soul is from such things as are in the spiritual world. After death, every man lays aside the natural part which he took from his mother, and retains the spiritual part which is from his father, together with a certain fringe <note>original: "limbo"; referring to a thin "border" or "envelope" of the finest natural substances</note> from the purest elements of nature surrounding it. But in those who come into Heaven, this fringe is below and the spiritual part above, whereas in those who come into Hell, that fringe is above and the spiritual part below. This is why an angelic man speaks from Heaven, and thus speaks what is good and true; but a devilish man speaks from hell when he speaks from his heart, even if he speaks as if from Heaven when he speaks only from his mouth; he does the latter when in public, but the former when at home. Since the Soul of a man is the man himself, and is spiritual by its origin, it is clear why the mind, the disposition, the character, the inclination, and the affection of the Father’s love dwells in the offspring one after another, and returns and presents itself visibly from generation to generation. This is why many families, and indeed even nations, are recognized by their first Father; there is a common image in the faces of each generation that manifests itself. This image is only changed through the spiritual matters of the Church. The reason why the common image of Jacob and Judah still remains in their descendants, and why they are distinguished by it from others, is because they have firmly adhered to their Religious system even until now. For in the seed of everyone from which he is conceived, there is a <term>tradux</term> <note>original: "tradux"; a biological/theological term meaning a sprout or a branch, used here to describe the transmission of the soul from the father</note> or propagation of the Soul of the father in its fullness within a certain covering of natural elements; through these the body is formed in the womb of the mother. This body can be made either in the likeness of the father or the likeness of the mother, yet the image of the father remains within it, which constantly labors to bring itself out; therefore, if it cannot do so in the first child, it achieves it in the following ones. The reason the father's image is in its fullness in the seed is because, as stated, the Soul is spiritual by its origin, and the spiritual has nothing in common with space; therefore, it is like itself in a small volume just as in a large one. As for the Lord, while He was in the world, He put off all the Human from the Mother through acts of redemption, and put on a Human from the Father, which is the Divine Human; hence it is that in Him, Man is God and God is Man.

### VIII. THAT THE PROGRESSION TOWARD UNION WAS HIS STATE OF EMPTYING, AND THAT THE UNION ITSELF IS HIS STATE OF GLORIFICATION.

104. It is known in the Church that the Lord, when He was in the world, had two states, which are called the states of <term>Emptying</term> <note>original: "Exinanitionis"; a theological term based on Philippians 2:7, referring to Christ "emptying" Himself of His divine glory to take on human form</note> and of <term>Glorification</term>. The former state, which was that of Emptying, is described in many places in the Word, especially in the Psalms of David, and also in the Prophets, and particularly in Isaiah Chapter 53, where it is said that *He emptied His soul even unto death,* verse 12. This same state was His state of humiliation before the Father, for in it He prayed to the Father, and says that He does His will, and ascribes everything He worked and spoke to the Father. That He prayed to the Father is evident from these places: Matthew 26:39, 44; Mark 1:35; Chapter 6:46; Chapter 14:32 to 39; Luke 5:16; Chapter 6:12; Chapter 22:41 to 44; John 17:9, 15, 20. That He did the will of the Father: John 4:34; Chapter 5:30. That He ascribed everything He worked and spoke to the Father: John 8:26, 27, 28; Chapter 12:49, 50.

[John] 14:10; indeed, on the cross He cried out, *My God, my God, why have You forsaken Me?* (Matthew 27:47, Mark 15:34); and besides, without this state He could not have been crucified. The State of <term>Glorification: the process by which Jesus made His human nature divine</term> is also the State of Union; He was in this state when He was Transfigured before His three disciples, and also when He performed Miracles, and as often as He said that the Father and He are one, that the Father is in Him and He is in the Father, and that all things of the Father are His. And after the full Union, He said that He had power over all flesh (John 17:2) and all power in Heaven and on Earth (Matthew 28:18), among many other things.

105. The reason why the Lord experienced those two states, of <term>Emptying: also called Exinanition; the state in which Jesus felt separate from His Divine soul and underwent temptations</term> and of Glorification, was because no other progression toward Union is possible, since it is according to the Divine Order, which is unchangeable. Divine Order requires that a person dispose themselves for the reception of God, and prepare themselves as a receptacle and dwelling place into which God may enter and inhabit as if in His own Temple. A person must do this as if by themselves, yet they must still acknowledge that it is done by God. They must acknowledge this because they do not feel the presence and operation of God, even though God is most present, bringing about every good of love and every truth of faith within them. Every person proceeds, and must proceed, according to this Order so that from being natural <note>living only by the senses and worldly logic</note> they may become spiritual. The Lord proceeded in the same way to make His Natural Humanity Divine. This is why He prayed to the Father, why He did the Father's Will, why He attributed everything He did and said to Him, and why He said on the cross, *My God, my God, why have You forsaken Me?*—for in this state, God appears to be absent. But after this state comes another, which is the state of Conjunction with God. In this state, a person acts similarly, but they act from God; they no longer need to consciously attribute to God every good they will and do, and every truth they think and speak (as they did before), because this is now inscribed on their heart, and is thus within every action and word. In a similar way, the Lord united Himself to His Father, and the Father to Himself. In short, the Lord glorified His Humanity—that is, He made it Divine—just as the Lord regenerates a person—that is, makes them spiritual.

That every person who becomes spiritual from being natural undergoes two states, and that they enter the second through the first, and thus pass from the World to Heaven, will be fully demonstrated in the chapters on FREE WILL, on CHARITY AND FAITH, and on REFORMATION AND REGENERATION. Here it is only noted that in the first state, which is called <term>Reformation</term>, a person is in full liberty to act according to the rationality of their understanding. In the second state, which is <term>Regeneration</term>, they are also in a similar liberty, but they then will and act, and think and speak, from a new love and a new intelligence which are from the Lord. For in the first state, the Understanding plays the primary part and the Will the secondary; in the second, the Will plays the primary part and the Understanding the secondary—yet the Understanding still acts from the Will, not the Will through the Understanding. The conjunction of good and truth, of charity and faith, and of the internal and external man, happens in no other way.

106. These two States are represented by various things in the Universe; the reason is that they are according to Divine order, and Divine Order fills each and every thing, even the smallest details, in the Universe. The first state is represented in every person by their state of infancy and childhood until their puberty, adolescence, and youth—which is a state of humiliation before parents, of obedience, and of receiving information from teachers and ministers. The other state is represented by the state of that same person when they become their own master <note>original: "sui juris"; legally independent</note> and act of their own choice—that is, from their own will and understanding—at which time they have power in their own house. The first state is also represented by the state of a Prince, or the son of a King or Duke, before he becomes King or Duke; similarly by the state of any citizen before he becomes a magistrate; of any subject before they hold some office; also of any student <note>original: "gymnasistæ"; a student in higher education</note> who is initiated into the ministry before he becomes a priest, then of a priest before he becomes a pastor, and then of a pastor before he becomes a Primate <note>a high-ranking bishop</note>; also of any maiden before she becomes a wife, and of any servant-girl [before she becomes a mistress].

The first of these is a state of servitude, and the other is a state of one's own will and the resulting understanding. These two states are also represented by various things in the **Animal Kingdom**: the first by beasts and birds as long as they are with their mothers and fathers, whom they then follow constantly, and by whom they are nourished and led; and the second state is when they leave them and look out for themselves. 107. IX. THAT HEREAFTER NO ONE FROM THE CHRISTIAN WORLD ENTERS HEAVEN, UNLESS HE BELIEVES IN THE LORD GOD THE SAVIOR, AND APPROACHES HIM ALONE. We read in Isaiah: "*Behold, I create a new Heaven and a new Earth, and the former things shall not be remembered, nor shall they come upon the heart; and behold, I am about to create Jerusalem an exultation, and her people a joy*" (Chapter 65:17). And in the Revelation: "*I saw a new Heaven and a new Earth, and I saw the Holy Jerusalem descending from God out of Heaven, prepared as a Bride for her Husband: and He who sat upon the throne said, Behold, I make all things new*" (Chapter 21:1, 2, 5). It is stated many times that no others shall enter Heaven than those who are written in the **Lamb's Book of Life** (Revelation 13:8; Chapter 17:8; Chapter 20:12, 15; Chapter 21:26). By "Heaven" there is not meant the heaven visible before our eyes, but the Angelic Heaven; by "Jerusalem," not some city from the sky, but the Church which will descend from that Heaven from the Lord; and by the "Lamb's Book of Life" is not meant some book written in Heaven that will be opened, but the Word, which is from the Lord and about Him. That Jehovah God, who is called the Creator and Father, descended and assumed <term>the Human: the physical and mental nature of a human being</term> for this very reason—that He might be approached and joined [to humanity]—has been confirmed, proved, and established in the preceding parts of this chapter. For who, when approaching a man, approaches his soul? And who can even do this? Rather, one approaches the man himself, whom he sees face to face, and with whom he speaks mouth to mouth. It is the same with God the Father and the Son, for God the Father is in the Son, just as the soul is in its body. That one must believe in the Lord God the Savior is evident from these passages in the Word: "*For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son, that whoever believes in Him should not perish but have eternal life*" (John 3:15, 16). Paul testified to both Jews and Greeks regarding repentance toward God, and **FAITH IN OUR LORD JESUS CHRIST**, Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 20:21. *I am the Way, the Truth, and the Life; no one comes to the Father except through Me*, John 14:6. That whoever believes in the Son believes in the Father (since, as stated above, the Father is in Him just as the Soul is in the Body) is evident from these passages: *If you knew Me, you would know my Father also*, John 8:19; Chapter 14:7. *He who sees Me, sees Him who sent Me*, John 12:45. *He who receives Me, receives Him who sent Me*, John 13:20. The reason for this is that *no one can see the Father and live*, Exodus 33:20; wherefore the Lord says, *No one has ever seen God; the only-begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, He has made Him known*, John 1:18. *No one has seen the Father except He who is from the Father; He has seen the Father*, John 6:46. *You have never heard the Father’s voice, nor seen His form*, John 5:37. However, those who know nothing of the Lord—such as the majority of people in two parts of the world, Asia and Africa, and also in the Indies—if they believe in one God and live according to the precepts of their own religion, are saved through their faith and life. For <term>imputation: the spiritual "counting" of merit or guilt</term> applies to those who know, and not to those who are ignorant, just as blind people are not blamed when they stumble; for the Lord says: *If you were blind, you would have no sin; but now that you say 'We see,' your sin remains*, John 9:41.

108. To confirm this further, I will relate what I know, because I have seen it and can therefore testify to it. These things are: that today a New Angelic Heaven is being established by the Lord, and it is being established from those who believe in the Lord God the Savior and approach Him directly, while the rest are rejected. Therefore, if hereafter anyone from the Christian world comes into the <term>Spiritual World: the realm humans enter immediately after death</term> (which happens to every person after death) and does not believe in the Lord and approach Him alone—and if they cannot then receive this faith because they lived evilly or confirmed themselves in falsehoods—they are repelled at the first step toward Heaven. Their face is turned away and directed toward the <term>Lower Earth: a region in the spiritual world between heaven and hell</term>, where they go and join those who are understood in the Book of Revelation by the "Dragon" and the "False Prophet." Furthermore, every person in Christian lands who does not believe in the Lord is henceforth not heard; their prayers in Heaven are like foul smells or like breaths from diseased lungs. Even if they think their prayer is like the burning of incense, it still does not ascend to the angelic heaven except as smoke from a fire, which is driven back into their eyes by a downward-rushing storm, or like incense from a censer hidden under a monk's cloak. This is how it will be from this time forward with all piety directed toward a "discrete" Trinity <note>A 'discrete' Trinity refers to the belief that the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are three separate persons or beings, rather than being unified in the person of Jesus Christ.</note> and not toward a conjoined one. That the Divine Trinity is conjoined in the Lord is the principal object of this work. Here I will add this new information: that a few months ago, the twelve Apostles were called together by the Lord and sent out into the entire Spiritual World, just as they previously were into the natural world, with the command to preach this Gospel; and then to each Apostle his own region was assigned. They are fulfilling this command with all zeal and effort. But regarding these things, they will be dealt with specifically in the last chapter of this book, where the **CONSUMMATION OF THE AGE**, the **COMING OF THE LORD**, and the **NEW CHURCH** will be discussed.

He claims a new spiritual era has begun, marked by the Apostles being sent out in the spirit world to preach this unified view of God.</summary>

## COROLLARY.

109. All the Churches that existed before the Advent of the Lord were **Representative Churches**, which could see Divine Truths only as if in a **Shadow**; but after the Lord’s advent into the world, a Church was established by Him which saw, or rather, was able to see Divine Truths in the **Light**. The difference is like that between **Evening and Morning**. The state of the Church before the Advent of the Lord is also called "Evening" in the Word, and the state of the Church after His advent is called "Morning." Before His advent into the world, the Lord was indeed present with the people of the Church, but mediately through **Angels** who represented Him; yet after His advent, He is present with the people of the Church immediately, for in the world He also took on the <term>Divine Natural</term> <note>The physical and external dimension of humanity which the Lord made Divine during His life on Earth.</note>, in which He is present with mankind. The **Glorification of the Lord** is the glorification of His **Humanity**, which He assumed in the world, and the glorified Humanity of the Lord is the Divine Natural. That this is so is evident from the fact that the Lord rose from the sepulcher with His whole Body that He had in the world, and left nothing behind in it; consequently, He took that very **Natural Humanity** with Him from its first to its last parts. Therefore He said to the disciples, who after the resurrection believed they were seeing a spirit: *Videte Manus meas & Pedes meos, quod Ipse Ego sim, palpate Me & videte, nam Spiritus carnem & ossa non habet, sicut Me videtis habere* <note>original: "See my hands and my feet, that it is I myself; touch Me and see, for a spirit does not have flesh and bones as you see Me have"</note>, Luke 24:37, 39. From these words it is clear that His **Natural Body** was made Divine through Glorification; wherefore Paul says, *Quod in Christo habitet omnis plenitudo Divinitatis corporaliter* <note>original: "That in Christ dwells all the fullness of the Divinity bodily"</note>, Colossians 2:9, and John says, *Quod Filius Dei Jesus Christus sit Verus Deus* <note>original: "That the Son of God, Jesus Christ, is the True God"</note>, 1st Epistle 5:20, 21. From these things the Angels know that the Lord alone in the whole **Spiritual World** is a **Full Man**.

It is known in the Church that all worship among the **Israelite and Jewish nation** was merely **External**, and that it foreshadowed the **Internal Worship** which the Lord opened; and thus worship before the advent of the Lord consisted in <term>types and figures</term> <note>Symbolic rituals or historical precursors that point toward a future spiritual reality.</note>, which represented true worship in its proper form. The Lord Himself was indeed seen by the Ancients, for He said to the Jews: *Abraham Pater vester exultavit ut videret diem meum, & vidit, & gavisus est: dico vobis, priusquam Abraham fuit, Ego fui* <note>original: "Abraham your father rejoiced to see my day, and he saw it, and was glad: I say to you, before Abraham was, I am"</note>, John 8:56, 58. But because the Lord was then only **represented** (which was done through Angels), all things of the Church among them became representatives; but after He came into the world, those representations vanished. The interior cause of this was that the Lord in the world also took on the **Divine Natural**, and from this He enlightens not only the internal spiritual man, but also the external natural man. Unless these two are enlightened together, a person is as if in a shadow; but when both are enlightened together, it is like being in the day. For when only the internal man is enlightened and not the external at the same time, or only the external and not the internal, it is like someone who sleeps and dreams, and soon after waking, recalls the dream and draws various conclusions from it which are nevertheless imaginary; it is also like a sleepwalker who thinks the objects he sees are being seen in the light of day. The difference between the state of the Church before the Lord's advent and after His advent is also like someone reading scripture at night by the light of the **Moon and Stars**, compared to someone reading in the **light of the sun**. It is clear that the eye errs in the former light (which is merely white) and does not err in the latter (which is also fiery). Therefore, it is written of the Lord: *Dixit Deus Israelis, mihi loquuta est Petra Israelis, ille sicut Lux matuta, dum oritur Sol, matuta sine nubibus* <note>original: "The God of Israel said, the Rock of Israel spoke to me: He is like the morning light when the sun rises, a morning without clouds"</note>, 2 Samuel 23:3, 4. The **God of Israel** and the **Rock of Israel** is the Lord. And elsewhere: *Erit lux Lunæ sicut lux Solis, & lux Solis erit septupla, sicut Lux septem dierum, in die quo obligabit Jehovah fracturam populi sui* <note>original: "The light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days, in the day that Jehovah binds up the breach of His people"</note>, Isaiah 30:

## OF THE NEW HEAVEN AND THE NEW CHURCH.

[Isaiah] 30: 25, 26: these things are spoken concerning the state of the Church after the Lord’s advent. In a word, the state of the Church before the Lord’s advent can be compared to an **old woman** <note>original: "Vetulæ"</note> whose face was painted, and who appeared beautiful to herself because of the redness of the makeup; but the state of the Church after the Lord’s advent can be compared to a **virgin** who is beautiful from her own natural glow. Furthermore, the state of the Church before the Lord’s advent can be compared to the rind of some fruit—such as an orange, an apple, a pear, or a grape—and to its flavor; but the state of the Church after His advent can be compared to the **interiors** of those fruits and their flavor. These comparisons are made for this reason: because the Lord, after He also put on the <term>Divine Natural</term> <note>The dimension of the Divine that reaches into the physical world.</note>, illustrates the **internal** spiritual man and the **external** natural man at the same time. For when only the **internal** man is illuminated and not the **external** at the same time, it results in shadow; similarly, when only the **external** is illuminated and not the **internal** at the same time.

110. Here, the following <term>Memorable Relation</term> <note>original: "MEMORABILIA." Swedenborg used this term for accounts of his visions in the spiritual world.</note> is added. **First.** Once in the **Spiritual World**, I saw a **Will-o'-the-wisp** <note>original: "Ignem fatuum," a phosphorescent light seen at night.</note> falling from the air to the earth, with a bright glow around it; it was a meteor that the common people call a **"Dragon."** I noted the place where it fell, but it vanished in the dawn as the sun rose, as happens with every Will-o'-the-wisp. After morning arrived, I went to the place where I saw it fall in the night, and behold, there the ground was a mixture of sulfur, iron filings, and muddy clay. Suddenly, two **tents** were seen, one directly over the spot and the other to the side toward the south. I looked up and saw a certain **spirit** falling from heaven like lightning, and he was cast into the tent that stood directly over the spot where the meteor fell. I was in the other tent which was nearby toward the south, standing in its doorway; I saw the spirit in the other tent also standing in the doorway of his own tent.

I then asked him why he fell so from **heaven**. To this he replied that he was cast out as an **angel of the dragon** by the **angels of Michael**, because he had spoken about certain things regarding his **faith**, in which he had confirmed himself while in the **world**. Among these things was this: that **God the Father and God the Son** are two, and not one. For everyone in the **heavens** today believes that they are **one, just as soul and body are one**; and every word spoken against that is like a sting in their nostrils, or like an awl piercing their ears, causing them disturbance and pain. Therefore, anyone who contradicts this is ordered to leave, and if he hesitates, he is cast down.

Having heard this, I said to him, "Why did you not believe as they do?" He replied that after departing from the **world**, no one can believe anything other than what they had impressed upon themselves through confirmation; this remains fixed and cannot be torn away, especially that which someone has confirmed in themselves concerning **God**. This is because in the **heavens**, everyone has a place according to their idea of **God**.

Furthermore, I asked by what means he had confirmed that the **Father and Son** were two. He said: by these things in the **Word** <note>The Bible.</note>: that the **Son** prayed to the **Father**, not only before the **passion of the cross**, but even during it; and also that He humbled Himself before His **Father**. How, then, can they be one, as the soul and body are one in a man? Who prays to another as if to someone else, and humbles himself as if before another, while he is that very person? No one does so, least of all the **Son of God**. Moreover, the entire Christian Church in my time divided the Divinity into **persons**, and each **person** is one by itself, and is defined as that which properly subsists.

After hearing these things from him, I replied: "I perceive from your speech that you know absolutely nothing about how **God the Father and the Son** are one. And because you do not know how, you have confirmed yourself in the falsehoods in which the **Church** still remains concerning **God**. Do you not know that the **Lord**, when He was in the **world**, had a soul just like every other man? From where did He have this, if not from God the Father? That this is so is abundantly clear from the **Word of the Evangelists**. What then is that which is called the **Son** but the **Human**, which was conceived from the Divine of the Father and born of the **Virgin Mary**? A mother cannot conceive a **soul**; this is totally contrary to the **Order** according to which every man is born. Nor can God the Father implant a **soul**...

Hence it is that the Lord says that the Father and He are one, and that the Father is in Him and He is in the Father, along with many similar statements. Even the framers of the *Athanasian Creed* <note>A foundational Christian statement of faith defining the Trinity and the nature of Christ as both God and Man.</note> saw this from a distance; therefore, after they divided God into three Persons, they still say that in Christ, God and Man—that is, the Divine and the Human—are not two, but one, just as the soul and body are one in man. That the Lord in the world prayed to the Father as if to another, and that He humbled Himself before the Father as if before another, was according to the Order established from Creation. This order is immutable, and according to it, everyone must progress toward conjunction with God. That order is this: just as a man, by living according to the laws of order (which are the commandments of God), joins himself to God, so God joins Himself to the man and makes him spiritual instead of natural. In the same way, the Lord united Himself to His Father, and God the Father united Himself to Him. Was the Lord not like an infant while an infant, and like a boy while a boy? Do we not read that He progressed in wisdom and favor, and afterward, that He asked the Father to glorify His Name—that is, His Human? To glorify means to make Divine through Union with Himself. From this it is clear that the Lord, in His *state of exinanition* <note>original: "statu exinanitionis." A theological term for the Lord's state of humiliation or "emptying" during His earthly life, when He felt separate from the Divine.</note>—which was the state of His progression toward Union—prayed to the Father. 

That same Order from Creation is inscribed upon every human being: namely, just as a person prepares their understanding through truths from the Word, they adapt it to receive faith from God; and just as they prepare their will through works of charity, they accommodate it to receive love from God. For just as a craftsman cuts a diamond, so he prepares it to receive and emit the brightness of light; and so it goes. To prepare oneself for the reception of God and conjunction with Him is to live according to Divine Order, and the laws of order are all the commandments of God. These the Lord fulfilled to the very last detail, and thus made Himself a receptacle of the Divinity in all its fullness; which is why Paul says that in Jesus Christ all the fullness of the Divinity dwells bodily, and the Lord Himself says that all things belonging to the Father are His. Furthermore, it must be held that the Lord alone is active within a person, and the person of themselves is merely passive; yet, through the influx of life from the Lord, the person also becomes active. Because of this perpetual influx from the Lord, it appears to the person as if they are active of themselves; and because it is so, <term>free will</term> is given to them. This is given so that they may prepare themselves to receive the Lord, and thus for conjunction—which is not possible unless it is reciprocal. It becomes reciprocal when a person acts from their own freedom, and yet, from faith, attributes all activity to the Lord.

After this, I asked whether he, like his companions, confessed that God is one. He replied that he did. Then I said, "But I fear that the confession of your heart is that there is no God. Does not every speech of the mouth proceed from the thought of the mind? Therefore, it cannot be otherwise than that the mouth's confession of one God should expel the thought of three from the mind, or conversely, that the mind's thought should expel the confession of one from the mouth. What else results from this but that there is no God? Is not the entire space between the thought and the mouth, and back again, thus emptied? What then does the mind conclude about God, other than that *Nature* is God, and about the Lord, that His *Soul* was either from His Mother or from *Joseph*?" From these two ideas, as from things horizontal and abominable, all the Angels of heaven turn away. After these things were said, that Spirit was sent away into the *Abyss* <note>A region in the spiritual world described in Swedenborg's writings as a place for those who have confirmed themselves in false doctrines.</note>, which is described in the *Apocalypse Chapter 9, verse 2 and following*, where the *Angels of the Dragon* <note>In Swedenborg's symbolic interpretation, these are spirits who believe in salvation through faith alone without regard for one's life.</note> argue the mysteries of their Faith. The next day, when I looked toward the same place, I saw in place of the Tents two Statues in the likeness of men, made from the dust of the earth, which was a mixture of sulfur, iron, and clay. ### 111. THE SECOND MEMORABLE RELATION.

In the natural world, man possesses a twofold speech because he possesses twofold thought, both External and Internal. For a man can speak from internal thought and at the same time from external thought; and he can speak from external thought while not speaking from the internal—even speaking against the internal. This is the source of pretenses, flattery, and hypocrisy. But in the <term>Spiritual World</term> <note>The intermediate realm where souls go immediately after death before heaven or hell.</note>, man does not have twofold speech, but simple speech: there, he speaks just as he thinks. Otherwise, the sound of his voice grates and hurts the ears. Yet, he is still able to remain silent and thus not reveal the thoughts of his mind. Therefore, when a hypocrite comes among the wise, he either leaves, or rushes away to a corner of the room, makes himself inconspicuous, and sits mute.

Once, many were gathered in the World of Spirits talking among themselves about this matter, saying that it was hard for those in the company of the good who had not thought rightly about God and the Lord to be unable to speak except as they thought. In the middle of those gathered were <term>Reformers</term> <note>Protestants from the tradition of Luther or Calvin.</note> and many of the Clergy, and near them were <term>Papists</term> <note>Followers of the Roman Catholic Church.</note> with monks. At first, both groups said this was not hard: "What need is there to speak otherwise than as one thinks? And if one happens not to think rightly, can he not compress his lips and keep silence?" And the Clergy said, "Who does not think rightly about God and the Lord?"

But some of the assembly said, "Let us test them." And they told those who had confirmed themselves in a <term>Trinity of Persons</term> <note>The traditional view of God as three distinct persons: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.</note> regarding God to say "One God" from their thought. But they could not. They twisted and folded their lips into many shapes, but they could not articulate the sound into any words other than those consistent with the ideas of their thought—which were of three Persons, and therefore of three Gods.

Furthermore, those who had confirmed <term>Faith Separate</term> <note>The doctrine that salvation comes through belief alone, regardless of one's actions or "charity."</note> from charity were told to name **JESUS**, but they could not. Yet all were able to say "Christ," and also "God the Father." They wondered at this and looked for the cause, and they found it to be this: they had prayed to God the Father for the sake of the Son, but they had not prayed to the Savior Himself; and **JESUS** signifies Savior.

Furthermore, they were told to say **DIVINE HUMAN** from their thought concerning the Lord’s Human property. But none of the Clergy present there were able to, though some of the Laity could. Therefore, this was brought under serious examination. Then, the following passages from the <term>Evangelists</term> <note>The writers of the four Gospels: Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John.</note> were read before them:

> *The Father has given all things into the hand of the Son.* John 3:35.
> *The Father has given the Son power over all flesh.* John 17:2.
> *All things have been delivered to Me by the Father.* Matthew 11:27. <note>OCR lists verse 7, but the text cited is verse 27.</note>
> *All power is given to Me in Heaven and on Earth.* Matthew 28:18.

And they were told: "Hold it in your thought from these verses that Christ, both as to His Divine and as to His Human, is the God of Heaven and Earth, and thus utter **DIVINE HUMAN**." But they still could not. They said that they might hold some thought from the understanding about it, but not any acknowledgment, and for that reason they were unable.

They were asked to hold this in their thought, and also that the Only Begotten Son of God born in the world cannot but be God, just as the Father is God, and then to speak the words **DIVINE HUMAN**. But they said, "We cannot, because our spiritual thought, which is interior, does not admit any ideas into the thought nearest to speech other than...

...how similar they were, and what they perceived from this: that it is not permitted there to divide one's thoughts, as it is in the natural world. **III:** Next, the words of the Lord to Philip were read in their presence, namely: *Philip said, Lord, show us the Father; and the Lord said, he who sees Me sees the Father; do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in Me?* <note>Original Latin: "Dixit Philippus, Domine, monstra nobis Patrem, & dixit Dominus, qui videt Me videt Patrem, nonne credis, quod Ego in Patre & Pater in Me."</note> John 14:8–11; and also other passages stating that the Father and He are one, as in John 10:30. They were told to hold this in their thought and so say **DIVINE HUMAN** <note>original: "DIVINUM HUMANUM"</note>; but because that thought was not rooted in an acknowledgment that the Lord was God even in His Human nature, they twisted their lips into folds even to the point of indignation. They tried to force their mouths to speak it, but they were unable. The cause was that the ideas of thought, which flow from acknowledgment, make a one with the sounds of the tongue among those who are in the <term>Spiritual World</term> <note>In Swedenborg’s theology, the "Spiritual World" is the realm of the afterlife where internal character and external appearance must eventually align.</note>; and where those ideas do not exist, no words are given, for ideas become words in speech. **IV.** Furthermore, these words were read to them from the Doctrine received throughout the Christian world: *That the Divine and Human in the Lord are not two, but one—indeed, one Person, united just as the soul and body are in man.* <note>This is a reference to the Athanasian Creed, a fundamental statement of Christian faith.</note> This is from the <term>Athanasian Creed</term> and acknowledged by the Councils. It was said to them: "From this you can surely have an idea based on acknowledgment that the Lord’s Human is Divine, because His Soul is Divine—for this is from the doctrine of your Church, which you acknowledged in the world. Moreover, the soul is the very essence of a man, and the body is its form; essence and form make a one, just as 'to be' and 'to exist' do, or like an efficient cause and the effect itself." They held onto that idea and wanted to pronounce **DIVINE HUMAN** based on it, but they could not; for their interior idea concerning the Lord's Human drove out and erased this new, "acquired" idea (as they called it). **V.** Still more was read to them from John: *The Word was with God, and the Word was God... and the Word was made Flesh,* <note>original: "Verbum erat apud Deum, & Deus erat Verbum, & Verbum Caro factum est"</note> John 1:1, 14; and also this: *Jesus Christ is the true God and Eternal Life,* <note>original: "Jesus Christus est verus Deus & Vita æterna"</note> 1 John 5:21; and from Paul: *In Christ Jesus dwells all the fullness of the Divinity bodily,* <note>original: "In Christo Jesu habitat omnis plenitudo Divinitatis corporaliter"</note> Colossians 2:9. They were told to think in the same way: namely, that the God who was the Word was made Man; that He was the true God; and that all the fullness of the Divinity dwelt in Him bodily. They did so, but only in their external thought. Therefore, because of the resistance of their internal thought, they could not speak the words **DIVINE HUMAN**. They said openly that they could not have the idea of a "Divine Human," because "God is God, and man is man, and God is a Spirit, and we have never thought of spirit as anything other than wind or ether." **VI.** Finally, it was said to them: "You know that the Lord said, *Abide in Me, and I in you; he who abides in Me and I in him, he bears much fruit, because without Me you can do nothing,*" <note>original: "Manete in Me, & Ego in vobis, qui manet in Me & Ego in illo, hic fert fructum multum, quia sine Me non potestis facere quicquam"</note> John 15:4–5. And because some of the English Clergy were present, a passage was read to them from one of their Prayers at Holy Communion: *For, when we spiritually eat the flesh of Christ and drink the blood, then we dwell in Christ, and Christ in us.* <note>This quote appears in English in the original Latin manuscript.</note> "If you now consider that this cannot be possible unless the Lord's Human is Divine, then pronounce **DIVINE HUMAN** from an acknowledgment in your thought." But still they could not. For the idea was so deeply impressed upon them that the Divine could not be Human, and the Human could not be Divine, and that His Divine was from the "Son from eternity," and His Human was like the human of any other man. But it was said to them: "How can you think thus? Can a rational mind ever conceive of a Son being born from God from eternity?" **VII.** Afterward they turned to the <term>Evangelicals</term> <note>Here referring specifically to the Lutheran Church.</note>, saying that the <term>Augsburg Confession</term> <note>The primary confession of faith of the Lutheran Church, written in 1530.</note> and Luther taught that the Son of God and the Son of Man in Christ are one Person; and that He, even as to His Human Nature, is Omnipotent and Omnipresent; and that as to that nature He sits at the right hand of God the Father, governs all things in the Heavens and on Earth, fills all things, is with us, and dwells and works in us; and that there is no difference in adoration, because through the Nature that is seen, the Divinity that is not seen is adored; and that in Christ, God is Man and Man is God. But then some of the Catholics pulled him back and said, "Shame on you." ### 112. THE THIRD MEMORABLE RELATION.

Once, having awakened after dawn, I went out into the garden before the house, and I saw the rising Sun in his radiance, and around him a belt, at first thin and afterwards more prominent, shining like gold; and under its border a cloud was rising, which, like a **pyrope** <note>A deep red gemstone, likely used here to describe a fiery, glowing cloud</note>, sparkled from the flame of the sun. And then I fell into meditation based on the fables of the ancients, that they imagined **Aurora** <note>The Roman goddess of the dawn</note> as winged with silver feathers, carrying gold in her mouth. While my mind was delighting in these things, I was in the spirit, and I heard some people speaking among themselves, saying, "If only it were granted to speak with the **Innovator** who has thrown the **apple of discord** <note>original: "pomum Eridis." A reference to the Greek myth where Eris (Strife) throws a golden apple into a wedding, sparking the Trojan War; here used to mean a bone of contention</note> among the leaders of the Church, to which many of the Laity have run, and having taken it up, have offered it to our eyes." By that "apple" they understood a small book entitled, *SUMMARY EXPOSITION OF THE DOCTRINE OF THE NEW CHURCH*. And they said, "It is certainly schismatic, something thought of by no one until now." And I then heard one of them shouting, "What do you mean schismatic? It is **Heretical**!" But some at his side retorted, "Quiet! Hold your tongue! It is not heretical; it quotes an abundance of declarations from the **Word** <term>The Bible</term>, to which our strangers (by whom we mean the laity) pay attention and give their support." When I heard these things, because I was in the spirit, I approached and said, "I am here; what is the matter?" And immediately one of them (who, as I heard later, was a German, a native of **Saxony**) spoke in a tone of authority and said, "Where do you get the audacity to overturn the Worship established in the Christian World for so many centuries? This worship has been that God the Father as Creator of the Universe, and His Son as Mediator, and the Holy Spirit as Operator, should be invoked. Yet you separate the First and the Last God from our Personality, even though the Lord Himself says, 'When you pray, pray thus:

->**OUR FATHER, WHO ART IN THE HEAVENS, HALLOWED BE THY NAME, THY KINGDOM COME,**<-

Is it not commanded thus, that we should invoke God the Father?" After these things were said, silence fell, and all who favored him stood like brave soldiers upon warships when they see an enemy fleet, about to shout, "Let us fight now, victory is certain!" And then I began to speak, and said, "Who among you does not know that God descended from Heaven and was made man? For it is read, *The Word was with*...

What do those words mean other than that the Father is in the Son and the Son in the Father, and that they are one just as the Soul and Body are in man, and thus that they are one Person? This will also be part of your faith if you believe the **Athanasian Creed** <note>A foundational Christian statement of faith that defines the Trinity and the "two natures" of Christ.</note>, where similar things are said. But take from what has been cited only this saying of the Lord, *Father, all Mine are Yours and all Yours are Mine*; what is this but that the Divine of the Father belongs to the Human of the Son, and the Human of the Son belongs to the Divine of the Father, and consequently that in Christ, God is Man and Man is God, and thus they are one as the soul and body are one? Every man can say the same of his own soul and his own body: namely, all yours are mine and all mine are yours, you are in me and I in you, he who sees me sees you, we are one as to person and as to life. The reason is that the soul is in the whole and in every part of man, for the life of the soul is the life of the body, and there is a mutual connection between them. From these things it is clear that the Divine of the Father is the soul of the Son, and the Human of the Son is the body of the Father. From where does the soul of a son come if not from his father, and from where his body if not from his mother? 'The Divine of the Father' is mentioned, and by it the Father Himself is understood, since He and His Divine are the same; this is also one and indivisible. That it is so is also evident from these words of the Angel Gabriel to Mary: *The power of the Most High shall overshadow thee, and the Holy Spirit shall come upon thee, and the holy thing that shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God*, and shortly before He is called the *Son of the Most High*; and elsewhere, the *Only-begotten Son*. But you, who only call Him the 'Son of Mary,' lose the idea of His Divinity; but this is not lost by any except the Learned among the clergy and the Erudite among the laity, who, while they lift their thoughts above the senses of their body, look toward the glory of their own reputation, which not only overshadows but even extinguishes the light through which the glory of God enters. But let us return to the **Lord's Prayer** <note>original: "Orationem Dominicam"</note>, where it is said:

> Our Father who art in the Heavens, hallowed be Thy Name, Thy Kingdom come;

113. **THE FOURTH MEMORABLE RELATION.** I looked out into the World of Spirits <note>In Swedenborg’s theology, the "World of Spirits" is an intermediate realm between Heaven and Hell where people arrive immediately after death.</note>, and I saw an Army on red and black horses. They were shaking the reins with both hands, and thus pulling their Horses back from the battle; and this they did continually. Then two Angels descended from Heaven and came to me, asking, "What do you see?" I told them that I saw this ridiculous Cavalry, and I asked what it was and who they were. The Angels replied: "They are from the place called Armageddon, *Revelation Chapter 16:16* <note>original: "Apoc. Cap. XVI: 16"</note>, in which several thousands have been gathered to fight against those who belong to the Lord's New Church, which is called the New Jerusalem. In that place they spoke about the Church and Religion, and yet among them there was nothing of the Church, because there was no spiritual truth; nor was there anything of Religion, because there was no spiritual good. They spoke there with mouth and lips about various religious matters, but only for the purpose of using them to gain dominion."

"In their youth they learned to confirm **Faith Alone** <note>term: *Sola Fides*—the doctrine that salvation is achieved through faith alone, without the necessity of good works</note>, and something about God; but when they were promoted to higher Offices in the Church, they retained those things for a while. Yet, because they then began to think no more about God and Heaven, but about Self and the World—and thus not about eternal blessedness and happiness, but about temporal eminence and wealth—they cast down the doctrines they had acquired in youth from the interiors of the rational Mind (which communicate with Heaven and are thus in the light of Heaven) into the exteriors of the rational Mind (which communicate with the World and are thus in the luminescence of the World). Finally, they thrust them down into the sensual natural level. Thus the doctrines of the Church became, for them, a matter of the mouth only, and no longer of thought from reason, and even less of affection from love. And because they have made themselves such, they do not admit any Divine truth belonging to the Church, nor any genuine good belonging to Religion."

"By comparison, the Interiors of their minds have become like Wine-skins <note>original: "Utres"</note> filled with iron filings mixed with sulfur powder; if water is poured into these, there is first a heating and then a flame, by which those skins are burst. Similarly, when they hear anything about the living water, which is the genuine truth of the Word, and this enters through their ears, they are violently enraged and inflamed, and they reject it as something that would burst their heads. These are the ones who appeared to you like Monkeys riding with bodies reversed upon red and black Horses with reins around their necks. This is because those who do not love the truth and good of the Church from the Word do not wish to look at the front of any Horse, but at its rear. For a Horse signifies the understanding of the Word <note>Swedenborg frequently uses the horse as a symbol for human intellect, specifically how one understands the Bible.</note>; a red Horse signifies the understanding of the Word destroyed as to good, and a black Horse signifies the understanding of the Word destroyed as to truth. That they shouted for battle against those riding on white horses is because a white Horse signifies the understanding of the Word as to truth and good. That they were seen to pull back their Horses by the neck was because they feared the battle, lest the truth of the Word might reach many, and so come into the light. This is the interpretation."

The Angels further said: "We are from the Society of Heaven called Michael, and we have been commanded by the Lord to descend into the place called Armageddon, from where that Cavalry you saw erupted. By Armageddon, among us in Heaven, is signified a state and a mind-set of fighting from falsified truths, arising from the love of dominating and excelling over everyone. And because we perceive in you a desire to know about that Battle, we will tell you something of it." After descending from Heaven, we approached that place called Armageddon, and saw several thousands gathered there. However, we did not enter into that assembly, but there were some Houses on the southern side of that place, where there were Boys with their Teachers; we entered there, and they received us kindly. IX. 5" — Isaiah 9:6 in English bibles</note>. LXIII: 16" — Isaiah 63:16</note>." Did He not say to Philip, who wanted to see the Father, "Philip, have you not known Me? He who sees Me sees the Father," John 14:9; Chapter 12:45. Who then is the Father other than the one whom Philip saw with his own eyes? 

To these we add this: it is said throughout the Christian World that those who belong to the Church make up the Body of Christ and are in His Body; how then can a person of the Church approach God the Father except through Him in whose body he is? He would have to go entirely out of the Body to approach Him. 

Lastly, we informed them that today a <term>NEW CHURCH</term> <note>original: "NOVA ECCLESIA"</note> is being established by the Lord, which is understood by the <term>NEW JERUSALEM</term> <note>original: "NOVAM HIEROSOLYMAM"</note> in the Book of Revelation, in which the worship of the Lord alone will exist, just as it is in Heaven; and thus everything will be fulfilled that is contained in the <term>Lord's Prayer</term> <note>original: "Oratione Dominica"</note> from beginning to end. We confirmed all things from the Word in the Gospels, and in the Prophets, and from the Book of Revelation, in which that Church is the subject from beginning to end, in such abundance that they grew weary of listening.

Having heard these things with indignation, those at <term>Armageddon</term> <note>The assembly of opponents introduced on the previous page</note> wanted to interrupt our discourse here and there; and finally they broke it off and cried out: "You have spoken against the Doctrine of our Church, which is that God the Father must be approached directly—"

# ON REDEMPTION.

114. It is known in the Church that there are two offices in the Lord: the **PRIESTLY** and the **ROYAL**. However, few know in what the one consists and in what the other consists, and therefore this shall be explained. From His Priestly Office, the Lord is called **JESUS**, and from His Royal Office, He is called **CHRIST**. Also, from His Priestly Office in the Word, He is called **JEHOVAH** and **LORD**, and from His Royal Office, He is called **GOD**, the **HOLY ONE OF ISRAEL**, and **KING**. These two are distinguished from each other just as Love and Wisdom are, or what is the same, as Good and Truth are distinguished. For this reason, whatever the Lord did and performed from Divine Love or Divine Good, He did and performed from His Priestly Office; but whatever He did from Divine Wisdom or Divine Truth, He did from His Royal Office. In the Word, "Priest" and "Priesthood" signify Divine Good, while "King" and "Royalty" signify Divine Truth; these two roles were represented by the priests and kings in the Israelite Church. As far as Redemption is concerned, it pertains to both offices; but what part of it belongs to the one and what to the other will be revealed in the following pages. To ensure that each point is perceived distinctly, the explanation of Redemption will be divided into canons or articles:

I. *That Redemption itself was the subjugation of the hells, the ordering of the heavens, and through these, a preparation for a new spiritual Church.*
II. *That without this Redemption, no human could have been saved, nor could the Angels have remained in a state of integrity.*
III. *That the Lord thus redeemed not only humans, but also Angels.*
IV. *That Redemption was a purely Divine work.*
V. *That this Redemption itself could not have been accomplished except by God Incarnate.*
VI. *That the passion of the cross was the final temptation which He sustained as the greatest Prophet, and that it was the means of the Glorification of His Human (that is, of union with the Divine of His Father), and not Redemption itself.*
VII. *That the belief that the passion of the cross was Redemption itself is a fundamental error of the Church; and that this error, together with the error concerning three Divine Persons from eternity, has perverted the entire Church to such an extent that nothing spiritual remains within it.*
These points must now be unfolded one by one.

115. **I. THAT REDEMPTION ITSELF WAS THE SUBJUGATION OF THE HELLS, THE ORDERING OF THE HEAVENS, AND THROUGH THESE, A PREPARATION FOR A NEW SPIRITUAL CHURCH.**
That these three things constitute Redemption, I can state with all certainty, since the Lord is performing a Redemption even today, which began in the year 1757 along with the <term>LAST JUDGMENT</term> <note>Swedenborg claimed to have witnessed the Last Judgment taking place in the spiritual world in 1757, marking the beginning of a new spiritual era.</note> that occurred then. From that time, this Redemption has continued until now. The reason is that today is the **SECOND COMING OF THE LORD**, and a New Church is to be established, which cannot be established unless the subjugation of the hells and the ordering of the heavens precedes it. Since it has been granted to me to see all these things, I could describe how the hells were subjugated and how the New Heaven was founded and ordered, but this would fill an entire work. However, how the Last Judgment was accomplished, I have revealed in a small book published in London in 1758. The reason that the subjugation of the hells, the ordering of the heavens, and the establishment of a New Church were Redemption is that without these, no human could be saved. They also follow in order: for first, the hells must be subjugated before a new Angelic Heaven can be formed...

## 116.
That the Lord, while He was in the world, fought against the Hells, and conquered and subjugated them, and so brought them under His obedience, is evident from many places in the Word <note>The Bible</note>, from which I will draw these few; in Isaiah:
> *Who is this that comes from Edom, with garments splattered from Bozrah, this one honorable in his clothing, marching in the multitude of his strength? I who speak in justice, great to save. Why is your clothing red, and your garment like that of one treading in the winepress? I have trodden the winepress alone, and of the people not a man was with Me; therefore I have trodden them in my anger, and trampled them in my heat; hence their victory is sprinkled upon my garments; for the day of vengeance is in my heart, and the year of my Redeemed has come. My own arm provided salvation for Me; I have made their victory go down to the earth. He said, Behold, they are my people, children; therefore He became a Savior to them; because of His love and because of His mercy He redeemed them. (Isaiah 63: 1 to 9)*

These things concern the Lord’s battle against the Hells. By the "garment" in which He is honorable and which is "red," is understood the Word, to which violence was done by the Jewish people. The battle itself against the Hells, and the victory over them, is described by His "treading them in His anger" and "trampling them in His heat." That He fought alone and from His own power is described by these words: *not a man from the people was with Me, my own arm provided salvation for Me, I have made their victory go down to the earth.* That He saved and redeemed through this is shown by: *therefore He became a Savior to them, because of His love and because of His mercy He redeemed them.* That this was the reason for His coming is understood by: *the day of vengeance is in my heart, and the year of my Redeemed has come.* Again in Isaiah:
> *He saw that there was no one, and was astonished that there was no intercessor; therefore His arm provided salvation for Him, and Justice stirred Him up; hence He put on Justice like a breastplate, and a helmet of salvation upon His head, and He put on garments of vengeance, and covered Himself with zeal as with a cloak; then the Redeemer came to Zion. (Isaiah 59: 16, 17, 20)*

In Jeremiah:
> *They are dismayed, their strong ones are beaten down; they have fled in flight, and have not looked back; that day is for the Lord Jehovih Zebaoth a day of vengeance, that He may take vengeance on His enemies, the sword shall devour and be satisfied. (Jeremiah 46: 5, 10)*

These and other passages speak of the Lord’s battle against the Hells and of the victory over them. In David:
> *Gird your sword upon your thigh, O Mighty One; your arrows are sharp, the people shall fall under You, the enemies of the King from the heart. Your Throne is for an age and forever; you have loved Justice, therefore God has anointed You. (Psalm 45: 4 to 7)*

Besides these, it is found in very many other places. Since the Lord alone conquered the Hells without any help from any Angel, He is therefore called <term>HERO</term> <note>original: "Heros"; a mighty champion</note> and <term>MAN OF WARS</term> (*Isaiah 42:13; Chapter 9:5*), <term>KING OF GLORY</term>, <term>JEHOVAH THE MIGHTY</term>, <term>HERO OF WAR</term> (*Psalm 24:8, 10*), <term>THE MIGHTY ONE OF JACOB</term> (*Psalm 132:2*), and in many places <term>Jehovah Zebaoth</term> <note>original: "Jehovah Zebaoth"; a Hebrew title meaning Jehovah of Hosts or Armies</note>, that is, Jehovah of Armies. His Coming is also called the Day of Jehovah—terrible, cruel, of indignation, of heat, of anger, of vengeance, of destruction, of war, of the trumpet, of shouting, of tumult, and so forth. By the "world," the "Prince of the world," "Satan," and the "Devil," Hell is meant. Besides these, in the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation</note>, from beginning to end, it is described what the Christian Church is like today, and also that the Lord is to come again, and will subjugate the Hells, and will make a New Angelic Heaven, and then establish a New Church on earth. All these things were predicted there, but not revealed until today. 117. The subjugation of the Hells, the ordering of the Heavens, and the subsequent establishment of the Church can be illustrated by various comparisons. They can be compared to an army of robbers or rebels who invade a Kingdom or a City, where they burn houses, plunder the goods of the inhabitants, and divide the loot among themselves, rejoicing and glorying in it. Redemption itself can be illustrated by the comparison of a just King who attacks them with his army, puts part of them to the sword, locks part of them in prison, takes away their loot to restore it to the subjects, and afterward puts the Kingdom in order and makes it safe from similar attacks. It can also be illustrated by comparing it to wild beasts gathered together and breaking out of a forest, invading flocks and herds and even people, so that no one dares to go outside the walls of their city to till the ground; consequently, the fields are deserted and the city-dwellers are about to perish from hunger. Redemption can then be seen as the slaughter and driving away of those wild beasts, and the protection of the fields and plains from further invasion. It can also be illustrated by locusts consuming every green thing on the ground, and by the means used to stop them from advancing further; or likewise by caterpillars in early summer that strip the trees of leaves and thus also of fruit, so that they stand naked as if in mid-winter, and by the shaking off of those pests, which restores the garden to its state of blooming and fruit-bearing. The same would happen with the Church, had the Lord not separated the good from the evil through Redemption, casting the latter into Hell and raising the former to Heaven. What would become of an Empire or Kingdom where there was no justice or judgment to remove the evil from the midst of the good and protect the good from violations, so that everyone might live in security in his own house and—as it says in the Word—"sit in tranquility under his own vine and fig tree"? <note>A reference to Micah 4:4, symbolizing peace and spiritual security.</note>

## 118. II. THAT WITHOUT THAT REDEMPTION NO HUMAN COULD HAVE BEEN SAVED, NOR COULD THE ANGELS HAVE REMAINED IN A STATE OF INTEGRITY.

First, it will be stated what Redemption is. To "Redeem" means to liberate from damnation, to rescue from eternal death, to snatch from Hell, and to take captives and prisoners out of the hand of the devil. This was done by the Lord by His subjugating the Hells and founding a new Heaven. The reason a human could not otherwise have been saved is that the Spiritual World has such a connection with the natural world that they cannot be separated—especially regarding the interiors of people, which are called their Souls and Minds. The souls and minds of the good are joined with the souls and minds of angels, and those of the evil with the souls and minds of infernal spirits. They have such a union that if these spirits were removed from a human, the human would fall dead like a log. Similarly, neither can Angels nor Spirits continue to exist if humans were taken away from them. From this, it is clear why Redemption was performed in the spiritual world, and why Heaven and Hell had to be ordered first before the Church could be established on earth. That this is so is clearly seen in the Apocalypse, where it says that after the New Heaven was made, the New Jerusalem (which is the New Church) descended from that Heaven (Chapter 21:1, 2).

## THE NEW HEAVEN AND THE NEW CHURCH.

119. The reason why the Angels could not have remained in a state of integrity unless Redemption had been performed by the Lord, is that the entire Angelic Heaven, together with the Church on earth, is like a single Person <note>Swedenborg often refers to this as the "Grand Man" or *Maximum Homo*, the idea that the collective of all those in heaven forms a single human shape in God's sight</note> before the Lord. The Angelic Heaven constitutes the Internal, and the Church constitutes the External; or more specifically, the Highest Heaven constitutes the Head, the Second and Last Heavens constitute the Breast and the Middle Region of the body, and the Church on earth constitutes the Loins and the Feet. The Lord Himself is the Soul and Life of this entire Person. Therefore, unless the Lord had performed Redemption, this "Person" would have been destroyed: the Feet and Loins would have perished when the Church on earth fell away; the gastric region when the Last Heaven fell; the Thorax when the Second Heaven fell; and then the Head, having no connection or correspondence with the Body, would fall into a faint. 

But this can be illustrated through comparisons. It is well known that when necrotic flesh <note>original: "Caro morticina"</note> attacks the feet, the decay progressively climbs upward; it first infects the loins, then the abdominal organs, and finally reaches the neighborhood of the Heart, at which point the person dies. It can also be illustrated by comparison with diseases of the organs below the Diaphragm: when these become diseased, the Heart begins to palpitate and the Lungs to gasp for breath, until finally they cease to function altogether. It can also be illustrated by the relationship between the Internal and External man: the Internal man remains healthy as long as the External man obediently performs its functions; but if the External does not obey, but resists, or worse, attacks the Internal, the Internal is eventually weakened and eventually deprived of its joys by the pleasures of the External, until it finally gives in and agrees with it. 

It can also be illustrated by the likeness of a man standing on a Mountain who sees the lands below him flooded. As the waters steadily rise toward the height where he stands, he too will be flooded unless he can find safety in some little boat tossed by the waves. Similarly, if someone on a mountain sees a thick cloud rising higher and higher from the earth, hiding the fields, villages, and cities, once that cloud reaches him, he can see nothing, not even where he himself is. It is the same with the Angels when the Church on earth perishes: at that time, the lower Heavens also pass away. The reason is that the Heavens consist of people from the earth; and when there is no longer any good of the heart or truth of the Word remaining on earth, the Heavens are flooded by the evils rising up, and they are suffocated by them as if by the waters of the Styx <note>In Greek mythology, the river of the underworld; here used to represent hellish influences</note>. Yet, these souls are hidden away somewhere by the Lord and reserved for the day of the Last Judgment, and then they are raised up into a New Heaven. These are the ones understood in the *Apocalypse* <note>The Book of Revelation</note> by these words:

> *I saw under the Altar the souls of those slain for the Word of God, and for the Testimony which they held; and they cried with a loud voice, saying, How long, O Lord, Holy and True, dost Thou not judge and avenge our blood on those who dwell upon the Earth; and white robes were given to each; and it was said to them, that they should rest yet a little while, until their fellow-servants and their brothers, who were to be killed as they were, should be fulfilled,* Chapter VI: 9, 10, 11. <note>original: "Vidi sub Altari animas occisorum..."</note>

120. There are many reasons why, without Redemption by the Lord, iniquity and malice would have spread through the entire Christian world in both the Natural and Spiritual Worlds. With deceased parents, brothers, relatives, and friends, every husband first seeks his wife, and every wife her husband. By these connections, they are introduced into various circles of people who outwardly appear like sheep, but inwardly are like wolves; and even those who studied piety are led astray by them. Because of this, and because of wicked arts unknown in the natural world, that World is as filled with malicious people as a pond turning green with frog-spawn. That associating with the wicked produces this effect can be seen from common experience: it is like someone staying with robbers or pirates until they eventually become like them; or like someone living with adulterers and harlots until they eventually think nothing of adultery; or like someone who mixes with rebels until...

### 121. III. THAT THE LORD IN THIS WAY REDEEMED NOT ONLY HUMANS, BUT ALSO ANGELS.

This follows from what was said in the preceding Article: that without Redemption by the Lord, not even the Angels could have remained in their state. To the causes mentioned above, these are added:

<margin>a</margin>
1. At the time of the Lord's First Advent, the Hells <note>In Swedenborg's theology, "Hells" refers to the collective spiritual societies of those who have rejected the Divine</note> had grown up so high that they filled the entire World of Spirits <note>The "World of Spirits" is the intermediate realm between Heaven and Hell where souls first arrive after death</note>, which is the middle region between Heaven and Hell. In doing so, they not only threw the "lowest heaven" into confusion, but even attacked the "middle heaven," which they infested in a thousand ways. Unless the Lord had sustained it, that heaven would have been destroyed. Such an assault by the Hells is meant by the Tower built in the land of Shinar, whose top reached even to heaven, and whose efforts were stopped by the "confusion of tongues," after which the people were scattered and the city was called Babel (Genesis 11:1–9). What is meant there by the Tower and the confusion of tongues is explained in *Heavenly Secrets* <note>original: "ARCANIS CÆLESTIBUS," Swedenborg's multi-volume commentary on Genesis and Exodus</note> published in London. The reason the Hells grew to such a height was that at the time the Lord came into the world, the entire globe had completely alienated itself from God through idolatries and magic; and the Church—which had existed among the children of Israel and finally among the Jews—had been utterly destroyed by the falsification and adulteration of the Word. All these people flowed into the World of Spirits after death, where they eventually increased and multiplied so much that they could not be expelled from there except by the descent of God Himself, and then by the strength of His Divine arm. How this was done is described in the small work *The Last Judgment* <note>original: "ULTIMO JUDICIO"</note> published in London in 1758. This was accomplished by the Lord while He was in the world. A similar thing has been done by the Lord today, since, as stated above, today is His Second Advent, which is predicted everywhere in the Revelation, and in Matthew 24:3, 30; in Mark 13:26; in Luke 21:27; in the Acts of the Apostles 1:11; and elsewhere. The difference is that in His First Advent, the Hells had increased from idolaters, sorcerers, and falsifiers of the Word; but in this Second Advent, they have increased from so-called Christians—both those who have soaked up naturalism <note>the belief that nature is all there is, denying the supernatural</note> and those who have falsified the Word by confirming their "fabulous faith" concerning three Divine Persons from eternity, and concerning the Passion of the Lord as being Redemption itself. For these are the ones meant by the Dragon and his two Beasts in Revelation 12 and 13.

<margin>b</margin>
2. The second cause why the Lord also redeemed the Angels is that not only every human, but also every Angel, is kept back from evil and held in good by the Lord. For no one, whether Angel or human, is in good from themselves; all good is from the Lord. Therefore, when the "footstool" <note>an image of the World of Spirits acting as the foundation upon which the heavens rest</note> of the Angels, which is for them in the World of Spirits, was snatched away, it happened to them just as it happens to someone sitting on a throne when its supports are removed. That the Angels are not pure before God is evident from the prophetic parts of the Word, and also from Job; and also from the fact that there is no Angel who was not first a human. > „ and brought it back under His own obedience. Furthermore, [it is shown] through these things, that Jehovah
> „ God descended and took on the Human <note>original: "Humanum" - Swedenborg’s term for the human nature and body the Lord assumed on earth</note>, for the purpose of bringing back into order
> „ all things which are in Heaven, and all things which shall be in the Church; because at that time the
> „ power of the Devil, that is, of Hell, prevailed over the power of Heaven, and on earth the
> „ power of evil over the power of good, and therefore total damnation stood at the doors and
> „ was imminent; this future damnation Jehovah God took away through His Human,
> „ and thus redeemed men and angels: from which it is clear, that without the
> „ coming of the Lord no one could have been saved. It is similar today; wherefore unless the Lord
> „ comes again into the World, no one can be saved” see above n. 2, 3.

122. That the Lord has vindicated the Spiritual World, and through it will vindicate the Church from universal damnation, can be illustrated by comparison with a King, who frees his sons (the princes) from an enemy who has captured them, shut them in prisons, and bound them in chains; by victories over that enemy, he sets them free and leads them back to his own Court. It can also be compared to a Shepherd, who—like Samson and David—snatches his sheep from the jaws of a lion or a bear, or drives out those wild beasts when they break out from the woods into the meadows, pursuing them to the very borders, and finally driving them into marshes or deserts; afterwards he returns to the sheep, feeds them in safety, and gives them drink from springs of clear water. It can also be illustrated by someone who sees a serpent coiled in a spiral, lying in the path and intending to strike the heel of a traveler; he seizes its head, and even though it twists itself around his hand, he carries it all the way home, and there cuts off its head and throws the rest into the fire. It can also be illustrated by a groom or a husband who, seeing an adulterer attempting to offer violence to his bride or wife, attacks him; he either wounds the man's hand with a sword, or strikes his legs and loins with blows, or has his servants throw him out into the streets to be chased with clubs all the way to his own house; having thus freed her, he leads her back into his bedchamber. By the **Bride** and **Wife** in the Word <note>original: "Verbum" - refers to the Sacred Scripture</note>, the Lord's Church is understood; and by **adulterers** are meant those who violate it, namely those who adulterate His Word; because the Jews did this, they were called an adulterous generation by the Lord.

### 123. IV. THAT REDEMPTION WAS A PURELY DIVINE WORK.

Anyone who knows what Hell is like, and how great its height and its flooding over the entire World of Spirits <note>the intermediate spiritual realm where souls go immediately after death</note> was at the time of the Lord’s coming—as well as the power by which the Lord cast down and scattered Hell, and afterwards brought it and Heaven back into order—cannot help but be struck with amazement and exclaim that all these things were a purely Divine Work. First, *What Hell is like*: it consists of myriads upon myriads of people, since it includes all those who from the creation of the world have alienated themselves from God through evils of life and falsities of faith. Second, *The height and flooding of hell over the entire World of Spirits at the time of the Lord's coming*: this was explained to some extent in the preceding Articles. What it was like at the time of His first Advent has not been made known to anyone, because it was not revealed in the literal sense of the Word; but what it was like at the time of His second Advent was granted to me to see with my own eyes. From this, the former state can be inferred. This is described in the short work *ON THE LAST JUDGMENT* <note>original: "Ultimo Judicio"</note> published in London in the year 1758; likewise the power by which the Lord cast down and scattered that hell is described there. But it would be a pointless task to transfer here those things which were described from eye-witness testimony in that booklet, because it exists, and copies are still kept in abundance at the printer's in London. Anyone who reads it can clearly see that this was the work of an Almighty God. Fourth, how the Lord afterwards brought all things both in Heaven and in Hell back into order has not yet been described by me, since the organizing of the heavens and the hells has continued from the day of the Last Judgment until the present time, and still continues; but after this book is published, if it is desired, it will be given to the public.

Swedenborg also asserts that Redemption is a purely Divine task, referencing his own eye-witness account of the Last Judgment in 1758.</summary>
