...concerns me, regarding this matter, I have seen and I see every day the Divine Omnipotence of the Lord as if face to face; but this latter belongs properly to Redemption, while the former belongs properly to the Last Judgment. Those who look at these two things distinctly are able to see many things that are hidden under figures in the prophetic parts of the Word <note>The "Word" is Swedenborg’s term for the Sacred Scriptures, or the Bible.</note>, and yet described there, when they are brought into the light of the understanding through the explanation of correspondences <term>correspondences — the spiritual science of how the natural world reflects the spiritual world</term>. This and that Divine work cannot be illustrated otherwise than by comparisons, yet even then only slightly. It can be illustrated by comparison with a battle against the Armies of all the Nations in the entire World, equipped with spears, shields, swords, muskets, and cannons, having clever and cunning leaders and officers; this is said because most in Hell are skilled in arts unknown in our world, in which they train one another in how they might attack, set ambushes, besiege, and assault those who are from Heaven.

The Lord's battle with Hell can also be compared—though only slightly—to a battle with the wild beasts of the whole world, and with their slaughter and taming, until none of them dare to creep out and make an assault on any person who is in the Lord. Hence, if one of them shows a threatening face, he suddenly draws back as if he felt a vulture in his breast attempting to pierce him to the heart; indeed, in the Word, infernal spirits are described as wild beasts; these are also meant by the wild beasts with whom the Lord was for forty days, in Mark 1:13. It can also be compared to resistance against the entire Ocean, with its waves breaking into regions and cities when the dikes are ruptured; the subjugation of Hell by the Lord is also understood by His calming the Sea when He said, *peace, be still* <note>original: "sile, obmutesce"</note>, Mark 4:38-39; Matthew 8:26; Luke 8:23-24; for by the "Sea" there, as in many other places, Hell is signified. 

By similar Divine power, the Lord today fights against Hell in every person who is being regenerated <term>regenerated — the spiritual process of being "born again" or reformed by God</term>; for Hell attacks all such people with a diabolical fury, and unless the Lord resisted and tamed it, man could not help but succumb. For Hell is like one monstrous man, or like an immense Lion—with which it is also compared in the Word—wherefore, unless the Lord held that Lion or that Monster bound in handcuffs and foot-shackles, it could not be otherwise than that a man, while being rescued from one evil, would fall of his own accord into another, and then into many more.

### 124. V. THAT THIS REDEMPTION ITSELF COULD NOT HAVE BEEN ACCOMPLISHED EXCEPT BY GOD INCARNATE.

In the preceding Article it was shown that Redemption was a purely Divine Work, consequently that it could not have been performed except by God Almighty. That it could only be done by Him becoming incarnate—that is, being made Man—is because Jehovah God, as He is in His infinite essence, cannot approach Hell, much less enter into it; for He is in the purest and first things. Therefore, Jehovah God, being such in Himself, if He were only to breathe upon those who are in Hell, He would kill them in a moment; for He said to Moses, who wished to see Him, *You cannot see my face, for no man shall see Me and live* (Exodus 33:20). Since, therefore, Moses could not, even less could those who are in Hell, where everyone is in the lowest and thickest <note>Likely referring to the density of spiritual atmosphere or state</note> things, and thus in the most remote; for they are the lowest natural beings. 

For this reason, unless Jehovah God had assumed the Human <note>original: "Humanum" — the human nature/body assumed by God</note>, and thus clothed Himself with a body that is in the lowest things, He would have entered into any Redemption in vain. For who can attack an enemy unless he approaches him and is equipped with arms for the battle? Or who can drive away and destroy dragons, hydras, and basilisks in some desert, unless he surrounds his body with a breastplate and his head with a helmet, and with a spear in his hand? Or who can catch whales in the sea without a ship and the tools adapted for the catch? By these and similar things the battle of the Almighty God with the Hells cannot be perfectly compared, but it can be illustrated—a battle He could not enter unless He had first put on the Human. But it must be known that the Lord's battle with the Hells was not a battle of words, as between those reasoning and quarreling—such a battle accomplishes absolutely nothing there—but it was a spiritual battle, which...

All these were done by the Lord alone through the power of Divine Truth from Divine Good.

125. That Jehovah God could not set such things into act and accomplish them except through His Human nature can be illustrated by various comparisons. For instance, an invisible person cannot join hands or speak with another unless he becomes visible; not even an angel or spirit can communicate with a human, even if he were standing next to the person's body and before his face. Nor can anyone's soul speak and act with anyone except through its own body. The Sun, with its light and heat, cannot enter into any human, beast, or tree, unless it first enters the air and acts through it; similarly, it cannot act upon fish except through the waters; for it must act through the element in which the subject exists. No one can even scale a fish with a knife, or pluck a crow, without fingers; nor can one descend into the depths of a lake without a <term>diving bell — original: "campana urinatoria," an early device used for underwater exploration</term>. In a word, each thing must be adapted to the other before communication and operation against or with it can take place.

## 126. VI: THAT THE PASSION OF THE CROSS WAS THE LAST TEMPTATION WHICH THE LORD SUSTAINED AS THE GREATEST PROPHET; AND THAT IT WAS THE MEANS OF THE GLORIFICATION OF HIS HUMAN—THAT IS, OF THE UNION WITH THE DIVINE OF HIS FATHER—AND NOT REDEMPTION.

There are two things for which the Lord came into the World, and by which He will save humans and Angels: namely, Redemption and the **Glorification** of His Human. These two are distinct from each other, yet they act as one for the sake of salvation. What **REDEMPTION** is has been shown in the preceding Articles: namely, that it was a Battle with the Hells, their subjugation, and afterward the ordering of the Heavens. **GLORIFICATION**, however, is the Uniting of the Lord’s Human with the Divine of His Father; this was done successively, and fully completed through the Passion of the cross. For every person must, for their part, draw near to God; and as much as a person draws near, so much does God, for His part, enter in. This is similar to a Temple: it must first be built, which is done by the hands of men, and afterward it must be dedicated, and finally prayed over, so that God may be present and unite Himself with the Church there. The reason that the Union itself was fully accomplished through the Passion of the cross is because that was the last Temptation which the Lord underwent in the World, and conjunction is achieved through Temptations. In these, a person is apparently left to themselves alone, even though they are not actually left; for God is then most present in their innermost parts and supports them. Therefore, when someone conquers in temptation, they are intimately joined to God; and so the Lord was then intimately united to God His Father. That the Lord was left to Himself in the Passion of the cross is clear from His exclamation upon the cross: "*My God, why hast Thou forsaken Me?*" and also from these words of the Lord: "*No one takes my soul from Me, but I lay it down of Myself; I have the power to lay it down, and I have the power to take it up again; this commandment I have received from my Father*" John 10:18. From these things it can now be established that the Lord did not suffer as to His Divine, but as to His Human,

127. These two things, Redemption and the Passion of the cross, must be perceived distinctly; otherwise, the human mind—like a ship hitting sandbanks or rocks—is lost along with the pilot, the captain, and the sailors. That is, the mind errs in everything regarding salvation from the Lord. For a man without a distinct idea of these two things is as if in a dream, seeing empty things and prophesying from what he believes to be real, when they are actually illusions; or he is like one walking in the night, who, while grasping the leaves of some tree, believes them to be a man’s hair, and coming closer, entangles his own hair with them. But although Redemption and the Passion of the cross are two distinct things, they make one for the purpose of salvation, since the Lord, through the Union with His Father—which was fully accomplished through the Passion of the cross—was made the Redeemer forever.

128. **On GLORIFICATION**, by which is understood the uniting of the Lord’s <term>Divine Human</term><note>A central concept in this theology: the idea that Jesus’s human nature was itself made Divine through His life on earth.</note> with the Divine Father, which was fully accomplished through the Passion of the cross. The Lord Himself speaks in this way in the Gospels: *After Judas went out, Jesus said, "Now the Son of Man is glorified, and God is glorified in Him; if God is glorified in Him, God will also glorify Him in Himself, and will immediately glorify Him,"* John 13:31-32. Here glorification is spoken of regarding both God the Father and the Son, for it is said, "God is glorified in Him," and "He will glorify Him in Himself." It is clear that this means to be united. *Father, the hour has come; glorify your Son, that your Son also may glorify You,* John 17:1, 5; it is said this way because the uniting was reciprocal, and as it is said, the Father was in Him and He in the Father. *Now my soul is troubled, and He said, "Father, glorify your Name," and a voice came from Heaven, "I have both glorified it, and will glorify it again,"* John 12:27-28. This was said because the Uniting was accomplished successively. *Ought not Christ to have suffered these things and to enter into his glory?* Luke 24:26. "Glory" in the <term>Word</term><note>In this context, "The Word" refers to the Holy Scriptures.</note>, where it refers to the Lord, signifies Divine Truth united to Divine Good. From these things it is clearly evident that the Lord’s Human is Divine.

129. The reason why the Lord willed to be tempted even to the Passion of the cross was because He was the <term>Prophet</term><note>The author uses "Prophet" here to mean one who represents the Word of God or the state of the Church.</note> itself. In ancient times, prophets signified the doctrine of the Church from the Word, and thus represented the state of the Church as it was, through various things—even through unjust, hard, and wicked things which were enjoined upon them by God. Because the Lord was the Word itself, through the Passion of the cross as the Prophet He represented the Jewish Church: how it had profaned the Word itself. To this cause is added the fact that He might thus be acknowledged in the Heavens as the Savior of both Worlds; for all things of His Passion signified things pertaining to the profanation of the Word, and the Angels understand those things spiritually while the men of the Church understand them naturally. That the Lord was the Prophet itself is established from these passages: *The Lord said, "A PROPHET is not without honor, except in his own country and in his own house,"* Matthew 13:57, Mark 6:4, Luke 4:24. *Jesus said, "It is not fitting for a PROPHET to perish outside of Jerusalem,"* Luke 13:33. *Fear took hold of them all, praising God and saying, "that a GREAT PROPHET has been raised up among them,"* Luke 7:16. They said of Jesus, *"THAT PROPHET from Nazareth,"* Matthew 21:26, John 7:40-41. *That a PROPHET would be raised up from among their brothers, whose words they should obey,* Deuteronomy 18:15 to 19.

130. It was commanded to the prophet Ezekiel that he should represent the state of the Church by making *vessels of migration <note>original: "vasa migrationis" — likely referring to the baggage of an exile or captive.</note>, and migrate to another place in the eyes of the children of Israel, and carry out the vessels by day, and go out in the evening through a hole dug in the wall, and cover his face so that he might not*

Then he was to take wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet, and spelt, and make bread from them; and also a barley cake made with human dung; and because he prayed against this, he was permitted to make it with cow dung. It was said to him: "Lie upon your left side, and lay the **INIQUITY OF THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL** upon it; for the number of days that you lie upon it, **YOU SHALL BEAR THEIR INIQUITY**; for I will give to you the years of their iniquity according to the number of days, 390 days, **THAT YOU MAY BEAR THE INIQUITY OF THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL**: and when you have completed these, you shall lie on your right side a second time, that **YOU MAY BEAR THE INIQUITY OF THE HOUSE OF JUDAH**" (Ezekiel 4:1–15). That the prophet, through these acts, "bore" the iniquities of the House of Israel and the House of Judah, and did not *remove* them and thus "atone" for them, but merely represented and showed them, is evident from what follows there: "Thus," says Jehovah, "shall the children of Israel eat their unclean bread: behold, I am breaking the staff of bread, so that they shall lack bread and water, and be desolated one with another, and rot away because of their iniquity" (Verses 13, 16, 17 in the same chapter). 

A similar meaning is therefore understood concerning the Lord where it is said: "He took our diseases, He **BORE** our sorrows; Jehovah made the iniquities of us all to fall upon Him; by His knowledge He justified many, because **HE HIMSELF BORE THEIR INIQUITIES**" (Isaiah 53 <note>original: Esaj. LIII: 1. The text cites verse 1 but refers to the contents of the whole chapter.</note>), where the whole chapter treats the Passion of the Lord. That the Lord, as the Prophet <note>Swedenborg often refers to the Lord as "The Prophet" because He is the "Word" itself made flesh.</note> Himself, represented the state of the Jewish Church regarding <term>the Word</term> <note>In this context, "the Word" refers to the Sacred Scripture as the container of Divine Truth.</note>, is clear from the individual details of His passion: Such as that He was betrayed by Judas; that He was seized and condemned by the Chief Priests and the Elders; that they struck Him with their fists; that they struck His head with a reed; that they placed a crown of thorns upon Him; that they divided His garments and cast lots for His tunic; that they crucified Him; that they gave Him vinegar to drink; that they pierced His side; that He was buried, and that He rose again on the third day. 

That He was betrayed by Judas signified that He was betrayed by the Jewish nation, with whom the Word then resided, for Judas represented that nation. That He was seized and condemned by the Chief Priests and Elders signified that this was done by that entire Church. That they struck Him, spat in His face, scourged Him, and beat His head with a reed signified that they did similarly with the Word in regard to its Divine truths. That they placed a crown of thorns upon Him signified that they falsified and adulterated those truths. That they divided His garments and cast lots for His tunic signified that they dispersed all the truths of the Word, but not its spiritual sense (the Lord’s tunic signified this spiritual sense). That they crucified Him signified that they destroyed and profaned the whole Word. That they offered Him vinegar to drink signified that they offered only things that were falsified, which is why He did not drink it. That they pierced His side signified that they fully extinguished every truth of the Word and every good thereof. That He was buried signified the rejection of what remained from the mother <note>The "residue from the mother" refers to the human nature inherited from Mary, which was set aside during the process of becoming Divine.</note>. That He rose again on the third day signified His Glorification or the Union of His Human with the Divine of the Father. From these things it is now clear that "to bear iniquities" <note>original: "Portare iniquitates"</note> does not mean to take them away, but to represent the profanation of the truths of the Word.

### 132. VII: THAT THE PASSION OF THE CROSS IS BELIEVED TO HAVE BEEN REDEMPTION ITSELF IS A FUNDAMENTAL ERROR OF THE CHURCH; AND THAT THIS ERROR, TOGETHER WITH THE ERROR CONCERNING THREE DIVINE PERSONS FROM ETERNITY, HAS PERVERTED THE ENTIRE CHURCH TO SUCH AN EXTENT THAT NOT A SINGLE SPIRITUAL REMNANT REMAINS WITHIN IT. 

What fills and stuffs the books of the Orthodox more today, and what is more ardently taught and inspired in the academies <note>original: "Gymnasiis"</note>, and more frequently preached and shouted from the pulpits, than that God the Father, in His anger against the human race, not only removed it from Himself but also shut it up under universal damnation, and consequently excommunicated it? But because He is gracious, it is said that He persuaded or raised up His Son to descend and take that specific damnation upon Himself, and thus appease <note>original: "expiaret"</note> the anger of His Father; and that only in this way, and no other, could the Father look upon man with any favor. Furthermore, it is taught that this was accomplished by the Son taking the damnation of the human race upon Himself, suffering Himself to be scourged by the Jews, spat upon in the face, and then—like a curse—to be **CRUCIFIED** (Deuteronomy 21:23). They say that after this act, the Father was appeased <note>original: "propitiatus"</note> and, out of love for the Son, withdrew the damnation, but only from those for whom the Son might intercede, and that he thus became a Mediator before His Father forever. These and similar ideas resound in the temples today, echoing off the walls like an echo from the woods, filling the ears of everyone there. 

But who—provided their reason has been enlightened and made healthy by the Word—cannot see that God, who is Mercy and Clemency itself, because He is Love itself and Good itself, and that these are His very Essence? Consequently, it is a contradiction to say that Mercy itself or Good itself could look upon man with anger and decree his damnation, and yet remain His own Divine Essence. Such traits hardly belong to an upright man, but rather to a wicked one; nor to an Angel of Heaven, but to a spirit of Hell. Therefore, it is unspeakable to attribute such things to God. If one searches for the Cause, it is this: they have taken the Passion of the cross for Redemption itself. From this, errors have flowed just as one falsehood follows another in a continuous series—like nothing but vinegar comes from a jar of vinegar, or nothing but insanity from an insane mind. For from one conclusion follow theorems of the same lineage; they lie hidden within the conclusion and come forth from it successively. From that idea that the Passion of the cross is Redemption, many more scandalous and shameful things against God can come forth and be dragged out, until it becomes as Isaiah says: 
> "The Priest and the Prophet err through strong drink <note>original: "siceram"; an intoxicating fermented beverage</note>, they stagger in judgment; all tables are full of filthy vomit" (Chapter 28:7, 8).

### 133. 
From this idea of God and of Redemption, the whole of Theology has been turned from spiritual into the lowest form of natural. This happens because merely natural properties have been attributed to God. Yet upon the idea of God and the idea of Redemption (which makes one with Salvation) hangs everything of the Church. For that idea is like the Head from which all things of the body proceed; therefore, while the head is spiritual, all things of the Church become spiritual, and while it is natural, all things of the Church become natural. Because the idea of God and of Redemption has become merely natural—that is, sensual and corporeal—therefore all things are merely natural which the leading figures <note>original: "Capita"</note> and members of the Church have handed down and continue to hand down in their dogmas. That nothing but falsehoods can be hatched from this is because...

# NEW HEAVENS AND THE NEW CHURCH.

The <term>natural man</term> <note>In Swedenborg's vocabulary, the "natural man" refers to someone focused only on the physical world and self-interest, whereas the "spiritual man" is focused on heaven and the neighbor.</note> constantly acts against the spiritual man, and consequently views spiritual things as though they were ghosts and phantoms in the air. Therefore, it can be said that because of that sensual idea concerning Redemption and thus concerning God, the ways to Heaven—which lead to the Lord God the Savior—are blocked by <term>thieves and robbers</term>, <term>John 10:1, 8, 9.</term> It is as if the doors in the Temples have been torn down, allowing dragons, screech owls, <note>original: "tziim and jiim"—these are Hebrew terms from the book of Isaiah referring to wild desert creatures or doleful spirits.</note> desert-dwellers, and wild beasts to enter and shriek in discordant chorus. It is well known that this idea of Redemption and of God has been forced into the faith of today: that people should pray to God the Father to forgive their sins for the sake of the cross and blood of His Son; to God the Son to pray and intercede for them; and to God the Holy Spirit to justify and sanctify them. What else is this but to pray to three Gods in their specific order? How then can the thought of Divine Government be anything other than the thought of an Aristocratic or Hierarchical government? Or like a Triumvirate, such as once existed in Rome? But instead of a Triumvirate, it could be called a <term>Trium-personate</term>. <note>original: "Triumperſonatus"—a play on the Roman "triumvirate" (a group of three men holding power), suggesting instead a government of three "persons."</note> What is then easier for the Devil than to "divide and conquer"—that is, to tear minds apart and stir up rebellious movements, now against one God, now against another, as has been done from the time of <term>Arius</term> <note>Arius (c. 250–336 AD) was a priest whose teachings led to the Arian controversy, questioning the nature of the Trinity and the divinity of Christ.</note> until now? In this way, they cast the Lord God the Savior—to whom belongs all power in Heaven and Earth (<term>Matthew 28:18</term>)—down from His Throne, and set up some client of theirs in His place, devoting worship to him, or by worshipping him, taking away the worship that belongs to the Lord Himself.

134. To these things shall be added these **MEMORABLE RELATIONS: FIRST**; Once I entered a Temple in the spirit world where many people were gathered. Before the Sermon, they were arguing among themselves about **REDEMPTION**. The Temple was square, and there were no windows in the walls, but rather a large opening at the top in the middle of the roof, through which light from Heaven entered; this illuminated the space more than if there had been windows on the sides. And suddenly, while they were in the middle of their conversation about Redemption, a black cloud floating in from the north covered the opening, causing such darkness that they could not see one another, and barely anyone could see his own palm. While they stood there stunned by this, behold, that black cloud was split in the middle, and through the crack angels were seen sent down from Heaven. They dispersed the cloud on both sides, so that the Temple became bright again. Then the Angels sent one of their number down into the Temple, who, on their behalf, asked the congregation what they were arguing about that caused such a dark cloud to come over and take away the light, bringing in darkness. They replied that it was about Redemption: that it was accomplished by the Son of God through the <term>Passion of the cross</term>, and that through this He made atonement and liberated the human race from damnation and eternal death. But to this, the angel who had been sent down said: "What do you mean 'through the Passion of the cross'? Explain why through that." Then a Priest came forward and said: "I will explain in order what we know and believe, which is: that God the Father, being angry against the human race, damned it, excluded it from His mercy, and declared everyone devoted to destruction and cursed, sentencing them to Hell. He willed that His Son should take that damnation upon Himself; the Son agreed, and for that reason descended, took on the Human form, and allowed Himself to be crucified, so that the damnation of the human race might be transferred to Him. For it is written, *Cursed is everyone who hangs on the wood of the cross.* <note>original: "Maledictus omnis suspensus super ligno crucis"; a reference to Galatians 3:13.</note> Thus the Son appeased the Father by interceding and mediating. Then the Father—moved by love for His Son and by the misery He saw in Him upon the wood of the cross—decreed: 'I will forgive, but only those to whom I impute your <term>Justice</term>. I will make these from children of wrath and a curse into children of grace and blessing, and I will justify and save them. The rest shall remain, as previously decreed, children of wrath.' This is our faith, and these things are the justice which God the Father applies to our <term>Faith</term>, which alone justifies and saves." The Angel [listened] to these things...

## UNIVERSAL THEOLOGY

After hearing these things, he was silent for a long time, for he stood in a state of shock. Finally, he broke the silence and spoke these words: "Can the Christian world <note>original: "Orbis Christianus"</note> be so insane, and turn away from sound reason into such delusions, and from those paradoxes conclude a fundamental dogma of salvation? Who cannot see that those things are diametrically opposed to the Divine Essence itself—that is, against His Divine Love and His Divine Wisdom, and at the same time against His Omnipotence and Omnipresence? No good master <note>original: "herus probus"</note> could act this way toward his servants and maids; no, not even a wild beast against its own cubs and chicks. It is unspeakable! 

Is it not against His Divine Essence to annihilate the Calling which was made to each and every person of the human race? Is it not against the Divine Essence to change the <term>Order</term> <note>In Swedenborg’s philosophy, "Order" refers to the spiritual laws established by God at creation, which dictate how life and salvation function.</note> established from eternity—which is that everyone is judged according to their life? Is it not against the Divine Essence to withdraw love and mercy from any person, much less from the entire human race? Is it not against the Divine Essence to be 'brought back' to mercy by seeing the misery in the Son? For since mercy is the very Essence of God, He is brought back into His own Essence; it is a wicked thing to think that He ever departed from it, for He is Mercy itself from eternity to eternity. 

Is it not also impossible to force into any being a thing like your faith—the 'Justice of redemption' which in itself belongs to Divine Omnipotence—and to <term>impute</term> <note>To "impute" here means to legally credit the merits of Christ to a person's account as if those merits were their own.</note> and assign it to a person, and to declare them just, pure, and holy without any other means? Is it not impossible to forgive someone's sins, and to renew, regenerate, and save someone through mere imputation alone, and thus turn injustice into justice and a curse into a blessing? Can one thus turn Hell into Heaven, and Heaven into Hell, or the <term>Dragon</term> <note>A reference to the "Dragon" in the Book of Revelation, representing those who separate faith from charity.</note> into <term>Michael</term>, and Michael into the Dragon, and so cut short the battle between them? What is needed except to take away the imputation of your faith from one and give it to the other? If so, we who are in Heaven would tremble forever. It is neither justice nor judgment that one person should take upon himself the wickedness of another, making the wicked man innocent and thus washing away the crime. Is this not against both Divine and human Justice?"

The Christian world is still ignorant of what Order is, and even more, what that Order is which God introduced at the same time He created the world—and that God cannot act against it, because he would then be acting against Himself; for God is Order itself.

The Priest understood those things said by the Angel, because the Angels who were above infused light from Heaven. Then he groaned and said, "What is to be done? Today, everyone preaches, prays, and believes this way. It is on everyone's lips: 'Good Father, have mercy on us and forgive us our sins for the sake of the blood of Your Son, which He shed for us on the cross.' And to Christ: 'Lord, intercede for us.' And we Priests add to these: 'Send us the Holy Spirit.'"

Then the Angel said, "I have noticed that the Priests prepare <term>eye-salves</term> <note>original: "collyria"—referencing Revelation 3:18, these are medicinal ointments used here as a metaphor for false interpretations that blind the faithful.</note> from the Word when it is not understood inwardly. They smear these over eyes blinded by their faith, or they make a 'plaster' out of them which they place over the wounds inflicted by their dogmas; yet they do not heal them, because the wounds are deep-seated. Therefore, go to that man standing there"—and he pointed to me with his finger—"he will teach you from the Lord that the <term>Passion of the cross</term> was not Redemption, but the unification of the Lord's Human with the Divine of the Father. But Redemption was the subjugation of the hells and the ordering of the Heavens; and without these things having been performed by the Lord while He was in the world, there would have been no salvation for anyone on Earth, nor for anyone in the Heavens. He will teach you further about the Order established from creation, according to which people must live to be saved, and that those who live according to it are numbered among the Redeemed and are called the Elect."

After these things were said, windows were made in the sides of the Temple, through which light from the four quarters of the world flowed in, and <term>Cherubim</term> <note>Angelic beings often associated with the protection of Divine mysteries and the presence of God.</note> appeared flying in the brilliance of the light. Then the Angel was taken up to his own people above the opening; and we departed joyfully.

...[light] is in that Sun; this falls in an articulate way through the middle Heavens to the Lowest, and from there into the World of spirits <note>In Swedenborg’s theology, the "World of Spirits" is an intermediate realm where everyone first arrives after death before being prepared for Heaven or Hell.</note>, where I was; and I perceived that the idea of one God held by the Angels was, according to its descent through the degrees, turned into an idea of three Gods. When I observed this, I went in to speak with those who were thinking of three Gods, saying, "Oh, what an enormity! From where did you get that?" And they replied, "We think of three from our perceptive idea of a Triune God <note>original: "Deo Triuno"</note>, but this still does not fall from our mouths; when we speak, we always say with a full mouth that God is one. If there is another idea in our minds, it happens as long as it does not flow down and split the unity of God in our speech. Yet from time to time it does flow down because it is within us, and if we were to speak then, we would say there are 'three Gods'; but we are careful of this, so that we are not exposed to the laughter of those listening." 

And then they spoke openly from their thought, saying, "Are there not three Gods, since there are three Divine Persons, each of whom is God? Nor can we think otherwise, since the leaders of our Church, from the chest of their holy dogmas, ascribe Creation to one, Redemption to another, and Sanctification to the third. Furthermore, they attribute properties to each—which they assert are incommunicable <note>In traditional scholastic theology, "incommunicable" properties are those unique to one person of the Trinity that cannot be shared with the others.</note>—which are not only Creation, Redemption, and Sanctification, but also Imputation, Mediation, and Operation. Is there not, then, one who created us, and he also imputes; another who redeemed us, and he also mediates; and a third who performs the mediated imputation, and he also sanctifies? Who does not know that the Son of God was sent into the World by God the Father to redeem the human Race, and so became the Expiator, Mediator, Propitiator, and Intercessor? And because this one is one with the Son of God from eternity, are they not two Persons distinct from each other? And because these two are in Heaven, one sitting at the right hand of the other, must there not be a third Person who carries out in the World the decrees made in Heaven?"

Hearing these things, I was silent, but thought to myself, "Oh, what foolishness! They do not know anything of what is understood by 'Mediation' in the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scripture.</note>." And then, at the Lord’s command, three Angels descended from Heaven and joined me, for the purpose that I might speak from an interior perception with those who held the idea of three Gods—specifically regarding **Mediation, Intercession, Propitiation, and Expiation**, which they attribute to the Second Person, or the Son, but not until after He became Man; and He became Man many centuries after Creation, when those four means of salvation did not yet exist, and thus [according to that logic] God the Father was not propitiated, the human Race was not expiated, and no one was sent from Heaven to intercede and mediate. 

Then, by an infused inspiration, I spoke with them, saying, "Come as many as can, and hear what is understood in the Word by Mediation, Intercession, Expiation, and Propitiation. These four are the Preachings of the grace of the one God in His Human <note>Swedenborg uses the term "The Human" (Latin: *Humanum*) as a noun to describe the body and soul Christ took on to interact with the physical world.</note>. God the Father can never be approached, nor can He Himself approach any person, because He is Infinite and in His Being <note>original: "Esse"</note>, which is Jehovah; if He approached a person from that Being, He would dissolve them as fire dissolves wood and reduces it to ashes. This is clear from the fact that He said to Moses, who wanted to see Him, that no one can see Him and live (Exod. 33:20); and the Lord says, 'No one has ever seen God, except the Son who is in the bosom of the Father' (John 1:18, Matt. 11:27); also, 'No one has heard the Father’s voice, nor seen His form' (John 5:37). It is read, indeed, that Moses saw Jehovah face to face and spoke with Him mouth to mouth, but this was done through an Angel; similarly with Abraham and Gideon."

"Now, because God the Father is such in Himself, it pleased Him to assume the Human, and in this to admit people, and so to hear them and speak with them. And this Human is what is called the Son of God; and this is what mediates, intercedes, propitiates, and expiates. I will tell you, therefore, what those four Predicates of the Human of God the Father signify: **MEDIATION** signifies that it is the intermediate through which a person can approach God the Father, and God the Father can approach a person, and so teach and lead them so that they may be saved; therefore the Son of God, by whom is understood the Human of God the Father, is called the Savior, and in the World, Jesus—that is, Salvation. **INTERCESSION** signifies perpetual Me—"

[He performs] mediation, for Love itself—which is Mercy, clemency, and grace—perpetually intercedes, that is, mediates, for those who keep His commandments, whom He loves. **EXPIATIO** <note>original: "Expiatio," meaning "Expiation" or "Atonement."</note> signifies the removal of sins, into which a person would rush headlong if they were to approach the "naked" or unshielded Jehovah. **PROPITIATIO** <note>original: "Propitiatio," meaning "Propitiation" or "Appeasement."</note> signifies the operation of clemency and grace, lest a person bring themselves into damnation through sins; it also signifies protection, so that they do not profane holiness. This was what the Mercy Seat <note>original: "Propitiatorium," the lid of the Ark of the Covenant.</note> atop the Ark in the Tabernacle signified. 

It is well known that God has spoken in the Word through appearances; for example, that He is angry, that He takes vengeance, that He tempts, punishes, casts into hell, and damns—even that He does evil. Yet, in truth, He is angry with no one; He does not avenge, tempt, punish, cast into hell, or damn. These things are as far removed from God as Hell is from Heaven, and infinitely more so. Therefore, these are expressions of appearance. Expressions of appearance—in another sense—are also Expiation, Propitiation, Intercession, and Mediation. By these terms are meant the proclamations of access to God, and of grace from God, through His Humanity. 

Because these things have not been understood, people have divided God into Three, and upon these Three they have founded the entire doctrine of the Church, and thus falsified the Word. From this comes the **ABOMINATION OF DESOLATION** <note>A biblical term from Daniel and Matthew referring to a state of spiritual ruin where the true understanding of God is lost.</note> predicted by the Lord in Daniel, and later in Matthew chapter 24. After these things were said, the troop of spirits departed from around me, and I noticed that those who actually thought of three Gods looked toward Hell, while those who thought of one God—in whom is the Divine Trinity, and that this Trinity is in the Lord God the Savior—looked toward Heaven. To these latter people, the Sun of Heaven appeared, in which Jehovah is present in His Humanity.

136. **THIRD MEMORABLE RELATION.** <note>Swedenborg's "Memorable Relations" are accounts of his purported visions and interactions in the spiritual world.</note> I saw from a distance five Gymnasia <note>term: "Gymnasia" (plural of Gymnasium). In the spiritual world, these are schools or halls of assembly where the learned gather to discuss spiritual mysteries.</note>. A light from Heaven surrounded each one. A purple light surrounded the first Gymnasium, like the light in the clouds on earth before sunrise in the morning. A yellowish light surrounded the second Gymnasium, like the dawn after sunrise. A bright white light surrounded the third Gymnasium, like the light of the world at noon. A middle-light surrounded the fourth Gymnasium, like that when the evening shadow begins to mix in. The fifth Gymnasium stood in the very shadow of evening. 

In the world of spirits, Gymnasia are halls where the learned meet and debate various secrets that serve their science, intelligence, and wisdom. Having seen them, a desire came over me to go to one of them, and I went in spirit to the one surrounded by the middle-light. I entered and saw a gathering of learned men who were debating among themselves the meaning of what is said about the Lord: that having been taken up into Heaven, He "sits at the right hand of God" (Mark 16:19). 

Most of the assembly said that this must be understood strictly according to the words: that the Son sits next to the Father in this manner. But when asked why it should be so, some said that the Son was placed at the right hand by the Father because of the Redemption He performed; some said He sits there out of love; others that it is so He might be the Father’s Counselor, and because of this, He receives honor from the Angels; and some said it is because it was given to Him by the Father to reign in His stead, for we read that "all power is given to Him in Heaven and on Earth." However, a large part said He sits at the right hand so that He may hear those for whom He intercedes. For everyone in the Church today approaches God the Father and prays that He may have mercy for the sake of the Son; this causes the Father to turn toward the Son to receive His mediation. 

Yet some said that only the Son of God from eternity sits at the right hand of the Father, so that He may communicate His Divinity to the Son of man born in the world. Hearing these things, I marveled greatly that the learned, although they had stayed for some time in the spiritual world, were still so ignorant of heavenly things. But I perceived the cause: that out of trust in their own intelligence, they did not allow themselves to be instructed by the wise. 

Truly, lest they remain any longer in ignorance about the Son sitting at the right hand of the Father, I raised my hand, asking them to lend their ears to a few things I wished to say on the subject. Since they nodded their assent, I said: "Do you not know from the Word that the Father and the Son are one, and that the Father is in the Son and the Son in the Father? The Lord says this openly in John 10:30 and chapter 14:10-11. If you do not believe these things, [you...]"

you divide God into two, and by doing so, you cannot think of God in any way other than naturally, sensually, or even materially. This is exactly what has happened in the world since the time of the **COUNCIL OF NICEA** <note>The Council of Nicaea (325 AD) established the Nicene Creed, which defined the relationship of the Father and the Son.</note>, which introduced "Three Divine Persons from eternity," and thereby turned the Church into a theater. In this theater, it hung painted backdrops, behind which masked actors represented new scenes. Who does not know and acknowledge that *God is One*? If you acknowledge this in your heart and spirit, all the things you have spoken are dissipated of themselves and bounce away into the air like trifles from the ear of a wise man. 

At these words, many in the group were inflamed with anger and burned with the desire to pull at my ears and command me to be silent. But the presiding official of the congregation said in indignation, "This is not a discussion about the unity or plurality of God, for we believe in both; rather, the question is: what does it mean that the Son sits at the right hand of His Father? If you know anything about this, speak." 

I responded, "I will speak, but I ask you, restrain the noise." I then said: "By 'sitting at the right hand,' one should not understand literally sitting at the right hand. Rather, it signifies the **Omnipotence** of God through the **Humanity** <note>original: "Humanum." In this theology, this refers to the Divine Human nature that God took on in the world.</note> which He assumed in the world. Through this Humanity, He is in the 'last things' just as He is in the 'first things.' Through this, He entered, destroyed, and subjugated the Hells; through this, He ordered the Heavens. Thus, through this, He redeemed both men and angels, and continues to redeem them forever. If you consult the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures.</note>, and if you are capable of being enlightened, you will perceive that by the 'Right Hand' there, Omnipotence is understood. As it says in David: *MY HAND FOUNDED the Earth, and MY RIGHT HAND measured the Heavens* (**Psalm 48:13**). *God swore by HIS RIGHT HAND, and by the Arm of His strength* (**Psalm 62:8**). *THY RIGHT HAND sustains me* (**Psalm 18:36**). *Look upon the Son whom You have strengthened for Yourself; let YOUR HAND BE UPON THE MAN OF THE RIGHT HAND, upon the Son of man whom You have strengthened for Yourself* (**Psalm 80:16-17**) <note>The original text cites Psalm 120, but the passage is from Psalm 80.</note>. 

From this it is clear how this is to be understood: *Jehovah said to my Lord, sit at MY RIGHT HAND, until I make your enemies your footstool; Jehovah shall send the scepter of your strength out of Zion; rule in the midst of your enemies* (**Psalm 110:1-2**). That entire Psalm treats the Lord's battle with the Hells and their subjugation. Since the 'Right Hand of God' signifies Omnipotence, the Lord therefore says that He is to sit **AT THE RIGHT HAND OF POWER** (**Matthew 26:63-64**) and **AT THE RIGHT HAND OF THE VIRTUE OF GOD** (**Luke 22:69**)."

At this, the assembly made an uproar. But I said: "Watch yourselves; perhaps a Hand might appear from Heaven." When that Hand appears—as it has appeared to me—it strikes an incredible terror of power into the soul. This served as a confirmation to me that the 'Right Hand of God' signifies Omnipotence. Hardly had this been said when a Hand was seen stretched out under Heaven. At the sight of it, such great terror seized them that they rushed in crowds toward the doors, and some toward the windows to throw themselves out, while others, losing their breath, sank down. But I remained, not terrified, and after them I slowly walked away. From a distance, I turned back and saw that hall covered by a dark cloud. I was told from Heaven that this happened because they spoke from a faith in three gods, and that the former light would return around that place when more sensible people were gathered there.

## 137. FOURTH MEMORABLE RELATION.

I heard that a Council <note>original: "Synedrium."</note> was called of men famous for their writings and learning regarding the Faith of today and the justification of the elect through it. This took place in the world of spirits. It was granted to me to be present in spirit, and I saw those gathered from the Clergy, both those in agreement and those in dissent. On the right side stood those who in the world were called the **Apostolic Fathers** <note>Early Christian theologians who lived in the generations immediately following the Apostles.</note>, who lived in the centuries before the Council of Nicaea. On the left side stood men famous from the centuries after that, known for their printed works or manuscripts copied by students. Many of these latter men had shaved chins and wore wigs made of curled women's hair; some wore ruffled collars, and others wore collars like wings. The former group, however, had bearded chins and wore their natural hair. 

In front of both groups stood a man—a Judge and Arbiter of the writings of this century—with a staff in his hand. He struck the ground and called for silence. # CHAPTER THREE

## DIVINE OPERATION.

138. All those of the Holy Order <note>This refers to the clergy or those ordained into the ministry.</note> who have fostered any just idea regarding the Lord our Savior, when they enter the spiritual world—which for the most part happens on the third day after death—are first instructed concerning the Divine Trinity, and specifically concerning the Holy Spirit: that it is not a God unto itself, but that by it in the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures.</note> is understood the Divine Operation proceeding from the One and Omnipresent God. The reason they are specifically instructed about the Holy Spirit is that many Enthusiasts <term>Enthusiasts: In this historical context, "Enthusiasts" refers to those who claimed to receive direct, private, and often fanatical revelations from God, bypasssing the established Word.</term> after death fall into the insane fantasy that they themselves are the Holy Spirit; and many from the Church who believed in the world that the Holy Spirit spoke through them, terrify others with the words of the Lord in Matthew: that to speak against those things which the Holy Spirit has inspired in them is the unforgivable sin (Chapter 12:31, 32). Those who, after instruction, withdraw from the faith that the Holy Spirit is a God unto itself, are afterward informed about the Unity of God: that it is not divided into three Persons, each of whom is individually God and Lord according to the **Athanasian Creed** <note>The Athanasian Creed is a 5th-century statement of faith widely used in Western Christianity that defines the Trinity as three distinct persons.</note>, but that the Divine Trinity is in the Lord the Savior, just as the Soul, Body, and proceeding Virtue <note>meaning: active power or influence</note> are in any man. These people are then prepared to receive the faith of the New Heaven; and for these, after they have been prepared, a way is opened to a Society in Heaven where a similar faith exists, and a dwelling place is given to them with their fellow brothers, with whom they will live in blessedness forever. Now, because the subjects of God the Creator and the Lord the Redeemer have been dealt with, it is necessary that the Holy Spirit also be dealt with; which Treatise, like the rest, is to be divided into its own Articles, which are the following:

*I. That the Holy Spirit is the Divine Virtue and Operation proceeding from the One God, in whom the Divine Trinity is, thus from the Lord God the Savior.*
*II. That the Divine Virtue and Operation, which is understood by the Holy Spirit, are in general Reformation and Regeneration; and according to these, Renewal, Quickening, Sanctification, and Justification; and according to these, Purification from evils and the Remission of sins, and finally Salvation.*
*III. That the Divine virtue and operation, which is understood by the sending of the Holy Spirit, is among the Clergy specifically Enlightenment and Instruction.*
*IV. That the Lord works these Virtues in those who believe in Him.*
*V. That the Lord works from Himself from the Father, and not the other way around.*
*VI. That the spirit of a man is his Mind, and whatever proceeds from it.*

139. I. THAT THE HOLY SPIRIT IS DIVINE TRUTH, AND ALSO DIVINE VIRTUE AND OPERATION PROCEEDING FROM THE ONE GOD, IN WHOM IS THE DIVINE TRINITY, THUS FROM THE LORD GOD THE SAVIOR. By the "Holy Spirit" is properly signified Divine Truth, and thus also the Word; and in this sense, the Lord Himself is also the Holy Spirit; but because in the Church today the Divine Operation is described by the Holy Spirit...

reasoning, which is actual Justification <note>In this context, "Justification" refers to the process by which a person is made just or righteous through the activity of God.</note>, is therefore taken here for the Holy Spirit, and this is the primary subject of discussion, especially because Divine Operation is performed through Divine Truth, which proceeds from the Lord. That which proceeds is of one and the same essence with Him from whom it proceeds, just as these three—**Soul, Body, and Proceeding** <note>The "Proceeding" refers to the active influence or operation that a person exerts on the world around them.</note>—together make up one Essence: in man, a purely human essence; but in the Lord, a Divine and at the same time Human Essence. 141. That the Divine Trinity is in the Lord has been demonstrated above, and will be demonstrated more fully in the following pages where it is to be treated as a primary subject; here, only some absurdities <note>original: *absona*</note> following from a Trinity divided into Persons will be brought forward. This would be as if a Minister of the Church should teach from the pulpit what is to be believed and what is to be done, while next to him stands another Minister whispering in his ear, "You say this rightly, and add this besides"; and a third says, standing on a ladder, "Go down into the Temple, open their ears, and pour those things into their hearts, and at the same time make them to be pledges of purity, holiness, and justice." A Divine Trinity divided into Persons, each of whom is individually God and Lord, is also like three Suns in one World, one next to the other in the height, and a third below, which surrounds angels and men, and brings the heat and light of the two others with all power into their minds, hearts, and bodies, and as a fire in a retort, sharpens, clarifies, and sublimes the materials; who does not see that if it were so, man would be burnt to ashes? The government of three Divine Persons in Heaven would also be similar to the government of three Kings in one Kingdom; or the government of three Generals of equal power over one Army; or rather the Roman Government before the times of the Caesars, when there were the Consul, the Senate, and the Tribune of the people, among whom the power was indeed divided, but yet the supreme power was with all of them together. Who does not see the absurdity, the mockery, and the madness of introducing such a Government into Heaven? Yet it is introduced when a power like that of a supreme Consul is assigned to God the Father, a power like that of the Senate to the Son, and a power like that of a Tribune of the people to the Holy Spirit—which is what happens when a specific function is attributed to each, and even more so if it is added that those properties are not communicable <note>meaning these roles cannot be shared or transferred between the three</note>.

142. II. THAT DIVINE POWER AND OPERATION, WHICH IS UNDERSTOOD BY THE HOLY SPIRIT, ARE IN GENERAL **REFORMATION AND REGENERATION**; AND ACCORDING TO THESE, **RENEWAL, VIVIFICATION, SANCTIFICATION, AND JUSTIFICATION**; AND ACCORDING TO THESE, **PURIFICATION FROM EVILS, REMISSION OF SINS, AND FINALLY SALVATION**. These are, in their order, the Powers which the Lord operates in those who believe in Him, and who accommodate and dispose themselves for His reception and habitation; and this is done through Divine Truth, and among Christians through the Word, for this is the only medium through which man approaches the Lord, and into which the Lord enters; for as was said above, the Lord is Divine Truth itself, and whatever proceeds from Him is that. But it must be understood as Divine Truth from Good <term>Good: In this theology, "Good" refers to the intent of the will and the quality of love, while "Truth" refers to the structure of the intellect and faith.</term>, which is the same as Faith from Charity; for faith is nothing else than truth, and charity is nothing else than goodness. Through Divine Truth from Good, that is, through Faith from Charity, man is reformed and regenerated, then renewed, vivified <note>given spiritual life</note>, sanctified, justified, and according to the progression and increase of these, he is purified from evils—and purification from these is the remission of sins. But all these Operations of the Lord cannot be explained individually here, because each one requires its own analysis confirmed from the Word and illustrated by reason, and this is not the place for it; wherefore the reader is referred to those things which follow in order in this Work, which are concerning Charity, Faith, Free Will, Repentance, and concerning Reformation and Regeneration. It must be known that the Lord continually operates these salvations in every man, for they are the steps to Heaven; for the Lord wills the salvation of all, wherefore the salvation of all is His end, and he who wills the end, wills the means. For the sake of the salvation of men was His Coming, Redemption, and the Passion of His cross (Matthew 18:11, Luke 19:10); and because the salvation of men was and is His end to eternity, it follows that the above-mentioned operations are the intermediate ends, and salvation is the ultimate end.

In those passages, by a "new Heart" <note>original: *Cor novum*</note> is meant the will of what is good, and by a "new Spirit" <note>original: *Spiritum novum*</note> is meant the understanding of what is true. That the Lord works these things in those who do good and believe truth—that is, in those who are in the faith of charity—is clearly evident from the fact that God gives a soul to those walking in it, and from its being called a "willing spirit." That man must also work on his own part is clear from the words: *Make for yourselves a new heart and a new spirit; why will you die, O house of Israel?*

144. We read that when Jesus was baptized, the Heavens were opened, and John saw the Holy Spirit descending like a Dove (Matthew 3:16; Mark 1:10; Luke 3:22; John 1:32, 33). This happened because Baptism signifies Regeneration <note>The process of spiritual rebirth</note> and purification, and the Dove signifies the same. Who cannot perceive that the Dove was not actually the Holy Spirit, nor was the Holy Spirit in the dove? In Heaven, doves frequently appear, and whenever they appear, the Angels know that they are "correspondences" <note>In this context, a "correspondence" is a physical representation of a spiritual reality or thought.</note> of the affections and the resulting thoughts concerning regeneration and purification among people standing nearby. Therefore, as soon as the angels approach them and speak about something other than what was in their thoughts when the appearance occurred, the doves immediately vanish. This is similar to many things seen by the Prophets, such as when John saw a Lamb upon Mount Zion (Revelation 14:1). Who does not know that the Lord was not that Lamb, nor was He in the Lamb, but that the Lamb was a representation of His innocence? From this, the error is revealed of those who deduce three Persons of the Trinity from the Dove seen over the Lord when He was baptized, and from the voice heard from Heaven at that time saying, *This is my beloved Son.* That the Lord regenerates man through faith and charity <note>In this theology, "charity" refers to active neighborly love and "faith" to the truth one believes.</note> is meant by what John the Baptist said: *I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance, but He who is coming after me... shall baptize you with the HOLY SPIRIT and with fire* (Matthew 3:11; Mark 1:8; Luke 3:16). To baptize with the Holy Spirit and with fire is to regenerate through Divine Truth (which belongs to faith) and through Divine Good (which belongs to charity). The same is signified by these words of the Lord: *Unless a man be born of water and the spirit, he cannot enter into the Kingdom of God* (John 3:5). By "water" here, as elsewhere in the Word, is signified truth in the natural or external man, and by "spirit" is signified truth from good in the spiritual or internal man.

145. Now, because the Lord is Divine Truth itself from Divine Good, and this is His very Essence, and everyone acts from their own Essence, it follows that the Lord continually wills—and cannot will otherwise—to implant truth and good, or faith and charity, into every person. This can be illustrated by many things in the world: every person wills and thinks, and as far as they are allowed, speaks and acts according to their essence. For example, a faithful man thinks and intends faithful things; an honest, upright, pious, and religious man thinks and intends honest, upright, pious, and religious things. Conversely, a proud, cunning, deceitful, or greedy man does those things which make one with his essence. A fortune-teller <note>original: *hariolus*</note> wants nothing but to tell fortunes, and a fool wants nothing but to babble against the things of wisdom. In short, an Angel ponders and strives for nothing but heavenly things, and a devil for nothing but infernal things. It is the same with every subject of a lower sort in the Animal Kingdom, such as a bird, a beast, a fish, or a winged or wingless insect: each one is known by its essence or nature...

### 146. III. **THAT THE DIVINE VIRTUE AND OPERATION, WHICH IS UNDERSTOOD BY THE SENDING OF THE HOLY SPIRIT, IS SPECIFICALLY ENLIGHTENMENT AND INSTRUCTION AMONG THE CLERGY.**

The operations of the Lord, reviewed in the preceding Article—which are reformation, regeneration, renewal, quickening, sanctification, justification, purification, the forgiveness of sins, and finally salvation—flow from the Lord into both the Clergy and the Laity. These are received by those who are in the Lord and in whom the Lord is, as in John 6:56; 14:20; 15:4, 5. However, the reasons why <term>Enlightenment</term> <note>original: *Illustratio*—a spiritual light given to the understanding</note> and Instruction are specific to the clergy are because these belong to their particular office; inauguration into the ministry carries these along with it. They also believe that while they preach from zeal, they are inspired, just like the disciples of the Lord upon whom the Lord breathed, saying, *Receive the Holy Spirit* (John 20:22; see also Mark 13:11). Some even testify that they have felt the influx. But let them be well on their guard not to persuade themselves that the zeal by which many are seized while preaching is the Divine operation in their hearts. For a similar and even more burning zeal is found among <term>Enthusiasts</term> <note>In the 18th century, "Enthusiasts" referred to religious fanatics who claimed direct, personal revelation from God apart from the Word.</note>, and also among those who are in extreme falsities of doctrine—even among those who think nothing of the Word and worship nature instead of God, casting faith and charity into a bag behind their backs. While preaching and teaching, they hang these in front of them like a kind of ruminating stomach from which they draw out and disgorge such things as they know will serve as food for the listeners. For zeal, viewed in itself, is the heat of the natural man. If the love of truth is within it, then it is like the holy fire which flowed into the Apostles, of which it is said in the Acts: *There appeared to them divided tongues like fire, and it sat upon each one of them, wherefore they were all filled with the Holy Spirit* (Chapter 2:3, 4). But if the love of falsity lies hidden within that zeal or heat, it is like fire imprisoned in wood, which breaks out and sets the house on fire. You, who deny the Holiness of the Word and the Divinity of the Lord, take your bag from your back, I pray, and open it—as you do freely at home—and you will see. I know that those who are understood by "Lucifer" in Isaiah—who are those from <term>Babylon</term> <note>Swedenborg uses "Babylon" to describe those who use religion as a means to gain power over others.</note>—when they enter a Temple, and even more when they climb the pulpit (especially those who call themselves the Society of Jesus <note>The Jesuits</note>), are carried away by a zeal which for many is from infernal love. From this, they shout more vehemently and draw deeper sighs from the chest than those who are in zeal from heavenly love. That there are two other spiritual operations among the clergy may be seen below in number 155.

### 147.

The Church is still almost unaware that in every act of will, thought, and resulting action and speech of man, there is an <term>Internal</term> and an <term>External</term>. From infancy, man is taught to speak from the External, however much the Internal disagrees; from this come simulations, flatteries, and hypocrisies. Consequently, man becomes "double," and only he is "simple" <note>Meaning "whole" or "undivided"</note> whose External thinks, speaks, wills, and acts from the Internal. These are also meant by the "simple" in the Word (as in Luke 8:15; 11:34, and elsewhere), although they are wiser than the "double." That there is a doubling and tripling in every created thing is evident from the human body: every nerve consists of fibers, and a fiber of fibrils; every muscle of bundles of fibers, and these of motor fibers; every artery of coats in a triple series. It is the same in the human Mind, whose spiritual organism is of such a nature. This is because, as stated above, the human Mind is divided into three regions: the highest (which is also the innermost) is called **celestial**, the middle is **spiritual**, and the lowest is **natural**. The minds of all people who deny the holiness of the Word and the Divinity of the Lord think in the lowest region; but because they have learned from infancy even the spiritual things belonging to the Church and have received them, yet...

That such are those who in their hearts disparage the holiness of the Word and the Divinity of the Lord, has been given to me to know through years of experience in the Spiritual World; for there, all are first held in their external states, but afterwards, these being taken away, they are let into their internals, and then their comedy becomes a tragedy.*

149. IV. THAT THE LORD WORKS THOSE VIRTUES IN THOSE WHO BELIEVE IN HIM. *That the Lord works those virtues, which are understood by the sending of the Holy Spirit, in those who believe in Him—that is, that He reforms, regenerates, renews, quickens, sanctifies, justifies, purifies them from evils, and finally saves them—is evident from all those places in the Word which confirm that salvation and eternal life belong to those who believe in the Lord, which may be seen cited above in number 108. Furthermore, it is evident from this: "Jesus said, whoever BELIEVES IN ME, as the Scripture says, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water; this He said of the SPIRIT, which those BELIEVING IN JESUS were to receive" (John 7:38, 39). Also from this: "THE TESTIMONY OF JESUS IS THE SPIRIT OF PROPHECY" (Revelation 19:10 <note>The source text lists "Apoc. LIX: 10," which is a typo for 19:10</note>); by the <term>spirit of prophecy</term> <note>prophetic spirit</note> is understood the Truth of doctrine from the Word—prophecy signifies nothing else than doctrine, and to prophesy is to teach it—and by the testimony of Jesus is understood a confession from faith in Him. A similar meaning is intended by His Testimony in this passage: "The angels of Michael conquered the dragon through the blood of the Lamb, and through the Word of THEIR TESTIMONY: and the Dragon went away to make war with the rest of her offspring, who kept the commandments of God and have the Testimony of Jesus Christ" (Revelation 12:11, 17).*

150. That those believing in the Lord Jesus Christ are to receive those spiritual virtues is because He Himself is Salvation and Eternal Life. He is Salvation because He is the Savior—this is also His name, Jesus—and He is Eternal Life because eternal life is in those in whom He is and who are in Him. For this reason, He is also called Eternal Life by John in his First Epistle (5:20) <note>The source text cites V:21</note>. Now, because He is Salvation and Eternal Life, it follows that He is also everything through which salvation and eternal life are obtained; consequently, He is everything pertaining to reformation, regeneration, renewal, quickening, sanctification, justification, purification from evils, and finally Salvation. The Lord works these things in every individual—that is, He strives to introduce them—and when a person adapts and disposes themselves for reception, He introduces them. The very activity of adaptation and disposition is also from the Lord; but if a person does not receive them with a willing spirit, then despite the effort which constantly persists, He cannot introduce them.

151. To believe in the Lord is not only to acknowledge Him, but also to do His commandments. For simply acknowledging Him is merely an act of thought from a certain level of understanding; but doing His commandments is also an act of acknowledgment from the will. The human mind consists of the **Understanding** and the **Will**; the role of the Understanding is to think, and the role of the Will is to do. Therefore, while a person only acknowledges from the thought of the understanding, they approach the Lord with only half a mind; but when they do His commandments, they approach with the whole mind, and this is truly "believing." Otherwise, a person can divide their heart, forcing its surface to lift itself upward while their flesh turns itself downward. Thus, such a person flies like an eagle between Heaven and Hell. Yet, the person does not actually follow the direction of their sight, but the direction of their flesh; and because the flesh is in Hell, they fly down there. After they have offered sacrifices to their pleasures there and poured out new wine to demons, they put on a face of pleasantries and a look of fiery sparks, pretending to be an angel of light. Such people become "satans" after death—those who acknowledge the Lord but do not do His commandments.

152. In the previous article, it was shown that the salvation and eternal life of men are the Lord's first and last goal. Since the first and last goals contain all the intermediate goals within them, it follows that the aforementioned spiritual virtues are simultaneously in the Lord, and also from the Lord in man, though they still come forth in succession. For the human mind grows just like the body: the body grows in stature, but the mind grows in wisdom. Thus, the mind is also raised from region to region—namely, from the **natural** to the **spiritual**, and from that to the **celestial**. In the celestial region, a person is "wise"; in the spiritual, they are "intelligent"; and in the lowest (natural) region, they are "knowledgeable." <note>Swedenborg categorizes the mind into three levels: the Natural (facts/science), the Spiritual (understanding/truth), and the Celestial (love/wisdom).</note> But this elevation of the mind only happens over time, and it occurs as the person acquires truths for themselves and joins them to "good" (right action). This is similar to someone building a house: first, they gather the materials for it, such as bricks, tiles, beams, and boards; then they lay the foundation, build the walls, divide it into rooms, add doors, put windows in the walls, and build stairs from floor to floor. All these things are simultaneously present in the goal—which is a comfortable and honorable dwelling—which the builder foresees and provides for. It is the same with a Temple; when it is being built, all the stages of its construction are contained in the goal, which is the worship of God. It is the same with all other things, such as gardens and fields, and also with offices and businesses, for which the goal itself prepares the necessary means.

### 153. V. THAT THE LORD OPERATES FROM HIMSELF FROM THE FATHER, AND NOT VICE VERSA.

By "operating" here, the same thing is meant as by "sending the Holy Spirit." This is because the spiritual operations mentioned above—which are, generally speaking, **Reformation**, **Regeneration**, **Innovation** (renewal), **Vivification** (giving life), **Sanctification**, **Justification** (cleansing) from evils, and the **Remission of sins**—are actually the operations of the Lord, though today they are attributed to the Holy Spirit as a God unto Himself. That these are from the Lord from the Father, and not the other way around, will first be confirmed from the Word <note>The Word refers to the Sacred Scriptures/Bible.</note> and afterwards will be illustrated by many points of reason. From the Word, we see these passages:

"When the Comforter <term>Paracletus: A Greek title for the Holy Spirit, meaning 'Advocate' or 'Helper'</term> comes, WHOM I WILL SEND TO YOU FROM THE FATHER, the Spirit of truth who goes out from the Father, He will testify of Me" (John 15:26).

"If I do not go away, the Comforter will not come to you; but if I go, I WILL SEND HIM TO YOU" (John 16:7).

"The Comforter, the Spirit of truth, will not speak from Himself, but HE WILL RECEIVE FROM MINE and announce it to you; all things whatever the Father has ARE MINE; for this reason I said, that He will receive FROM MINE and announce it to you" (John 16:13-15).

"The Holy Spirit was not yet, because Jesus was not yet glorified" (John 7:39).

"Jesus breathed on the Disciples and said, receive the Holy Spirit" (John 20:22).

"Whatever you shall ask in My Name, THIS I WILL DO, that the Father may be glorified in the Son; if you ask anything in My Name, I WILL DO IT" (John 14:13-14).

From these passages, it is clearly evident that the Lord sends the Holy Spirit—that is, He performs those operations which are today ascribed to the Holy Spirit as a God unto Himself. For He said that He would send Him from the Father, that He would send Him to you, that the Holy Spirit was not yet because Jesus was not yet glorified, and that after His glorification He breathed on the Disciples and said, "Receive the Holy Spirit"; also that He said, "Whatever you ask in My Name, I [will do]."

I shall do so, as also [to show] that the Advocate <note>original: "Paracletus," often translated as Comforter or Helper</note> is to receive from Mine what he will announce; that the Advocate is the same as the Holy Spirit, see John 14:26. *That God the Father does not work those virtues from Himself through the Son, but that the Son [works them] from Himself from the Father,* is evident from these words: *No one has ever seen God; the Only-begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, He has made Him known,* John 1:18. And elsewhere: *You have never heard the Father's voice, nor seen His form,* John 5:37. From these it follows, then, that God the Father works in the Son and into the Son, but not through the Son; but rather that the Lord works from Himself from His Father, for He says: *All things of the Father are mine,* John 16:14. *That the Father has given all things into the hand of the Son,* John 3:35. *Also, that just as the Father has life in Himself, so He has given to the Son to have life in Himself,* John 5:26. That the Lord says the Spirit of truth goes out from the Father, John 15:26, is because it goes out from God the Father into the Son, and out of the Son from the Father; wherefore He also says: *In that day you shall know that the Father is in Me, and I in the Father, and you in Me and I in you,* John 14:11, 20. From these clear statements of the Lord, the error in the Christian World is plainly evident—which is that God the Father sends the Holy Spirit to man—as well as the error of the Greek Church, that God the Father sends Him directly. This truth, that the Lord sends Him from Himself from God the Father, is new and is from Heaven; the Angels call it a hidden secret <note>original: "Arcanum," a term for a deep spiritual mystery</note> because it has not yet been uncovered in the world.

154. These things can be illustrated by many points of reason; such as these: it is well known that the Apostles, after they were gifted with the Holy Spirit from the Lord, preached the Gospel through much of the world, and that they proclaimed this by mouth and in writings; and they did this from themselves from the Lord. For Peter taught and wrote in one way, James in another, John in another, and Paul in another, each according to his own intelligence. The Lord filled them all with His spirit, but each took a portion from it according to the quality of his own perception, and they carried it out according to the quality of their own power. All the Angels in the heavens are filled by the Lord, for they are in the Lord and the Lord is in them, but still each one speaks and acts according to the state of his own mind—some simply, some wisely, thus with infinite variety—and yet every single one speaks from himself from the Lord. It is similar with every Minister of the Church, both the one who is in truths and the one who is in falsehoods; each has his own mouth and his own intelligence, and each speaks from his own mind, that is, from his own spirit which he possesses. All Protestants, whether they are called Evangelicals or Reformed <note>Refers to Lutherans and Calvinists</note>, after they have been instructed in the dogmas handed down by Luther, Melanchthon, or Calvin—these men or their dogmas do not speak through them, but they speak from themselves from those teachers. Every single dogma can also be explained in a thousand ways, for every dogma is like a horn of plenty <note>original: "cornucopia"</note>, from which each person draws what favors and suits his own genius, and explains it according to his own gift. This can be illustrated by the action of the heart in the lungs and into the lungs, and by the reaction of the lungs from themselves from the heart; these are two distinct things, yet reciprocally united. The lung breathes from itself from the heart, but the heart does not breathe through the lung; if that happened, both would stop. It is also similar with the action of the heart in and into the internal organs of the whole body; the heart sends out blood everywhere, but the organs draw from it, each its own requirement according to the type of use it performs, and it also acts according to this, thus in diverse ways. This same thing can be illustrated by this: evil from parents, which is called hereditary <note>original: "haereditarium"</note>, acts in man and into man; similarly good from the Lord, the latter from above or within, the former from below or without. If evil acted *through* man, man would not be capable of being reformed, nor would he be blameworthy; similarly, if good from the Lord acted *through* man, he would not be capable of being reformed. But because both depend on the free choice <note>original: "libera electio"</note> of man, he becomes guilty when he acts from himself from evil, and innocent when from himself from good. Now, because evil is the devil and good is the Lord, he becomes guilty if he acts from the devil, and innocent if from the Lord; it is from that free choice, which is in every man, that man is able to be reformed. It is the same with every Internal and External in man—

<summary>Swedenborg argues that the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Lord Jesus Christ, who acts from the Father, rather than directly from the Father. He illustrates this through the individuality of the Apostles and the physiological relationship between the heart and lungs, emphasizing that human free will is maintained because God acts into man, but man acts "as if of himself."</summary>
