In man, these are two distinct things, yet they are still reciprocally united; the Internal acts into the External and toward it, but it does not act through the External. For the Internal revolves thousands of things, from which the External only takes what is adapted for use. In the Internal of man—by which is meant his voluntary and perceptive <term>Mind</term><note>The "voluntary" refers to the will (voluntas), and "perceptive" refers to the understanding (intellectus).</note>—there are masses of ideas in a volume; if these were to flow out through a man's mouth, it would be like wind from a bellows. Because the Internal revolves universals, it can be compared to an Ocean, or a Flowerbed, or a Garden, from which the External draws as much as is sufficient for use. The Word of the Lord is like an Ocean, a Flowerbed, and a Garden; when the Word is in some fullness in the Internal of a man, then the man speaks and acts from himself from the Word, and not the Word through him. It is the same with the Lord, because He is the Word—that is, the Divine Truth and Divine Good there. The Lord acts from Himself or from the Word into man and toward him, but not through him, because man acts and speaks freely from the Lord while he acts from the Word. But this can be more closely illustrated by the mutual commerce of the soul and the body, which are two distinct things but reciprocally united. The Soul acts into the body and toward the body, but not through the body, so that the body acts from itself from the soul. That the soul does not act through the body is because they do not consult and deliberate with each other, nor does the soul command or ask the body to do this or that, or to speak from its mouth; nor does the body request or petition the soul to give or supply something—for everything of the soul belongs to the body, mutually and in turn. It is the same with the Divine and the Human of the Lord, for the Divine of the Father is the Soul of His Human, and the Human is His Body; and the Human does not ask from His Divine what it shall speak or work. Therefore the Lord says: *In that day you shall ask in my Name, and I do not say to you that I will ask the Father for you; for the Father Himself loves you, because you have loved Me,* John 16:26, 27. "In that day" means after the glorification—that is, after the perfect and absolute union with the Father. This <term>Secret</term><note>original: "Arcanum," a term Swedenborg uses for deep spiritual truths or "mysteries" of faith revealed for the New Church.</note> is from the Lord Himself for those who will be of His new Church.

155. Above in Article Three it was shown that the Divine Virtue, which is understood by the operation of the Holy Spirit among the Clergy, specifically becomes <term>Enlightenment</term> and <term>Instruction</term>; but to these two are added two intermediate ones, which are <term>Perception</term> and <term>Disposition</term>. Therefore, there are four which follow in order among the Clergy: Enlightenment, Perception, Disposition, and Instruction. **ENLIGHTENMENT** is from the Lord. **PERCEPTION** exists in the man according to the state of his mind formed by doctrines; if these are true, the perception becomes clear from the light that enlightens; but if they are false, the perception becomes obscure, which can nonetheless appear as if clear from confirmations—but this is from a <term>fatuous light</term><note>original: "luce fatua," literally a foolish or deceptive light, like a 'will-o'-the-wisp,' which makes falsehoods look like truths.</note> which, before purely natural sight, is of similar clarity. **DISPOSITION**, however, is from the affection of the love of the will; the delight of this love arranges it. If this is a love of evil and thence of falsity, it excites a zeal which is outwardly harsh, bristling, burning, and fire-breathing, while inwardly it is anger, madness, and unmercifulness. But if it is of good and thence of truth, it is outwardly smooth, polished, thundering and glowing, while inwardly it is charity, grace, and mercy. **INSTRUCTION** then follows as an effect from those as causes. Thus Enlightenment, which is from the Lord, is turned into various lights and various heats in everyone according to the state of his mind.

### 156. VI. THAT THE SPIRIT OF MAN IS HIS MIND, AND WHATEVER PROCEEDS FROM IT.

By the spirit of man in the concrete, nothing else is meant than his Mind; for this is what lives after death, and is then called a spirit—if good, an angelic Spirit and later an angel; if evil, a satanic Spirit and later a satan. The Mind of any man is his Internal man, which is actually the man, and is within the External man which makes up his body; therefore, when the body is cast off (which happens through death), he is in a full human form. They err, therefore, who believe that the Mind of man is only in the Head; it is there only in its principles <note>Meaning its starting points or primary centers.</note>, from which everything that a man thinks from the intellect and acts from the will first goes forth; but in the body it is in the derivatives <note>original: "principiatis," things originating from the principles.</note>, formed for sensing and acting. And because it adheres inwardly to the body—

Now, because the spirit of man thinks from the <term>understanding</term><note>Latin: intellectus</note> and acts from the <term>will</term><note>Latin: voluntas</note>, and the body does not act from itself but from the spirit, it follows that by the "spirit of man" is meant his intelligence and his affection of love, and whatever proceeds and operates from them. That the "spirit" of man signifies such things as belong to the mind is evident from many places in the <term>Word</term><note>Swedenborg uses "The Word" to refer to the Sacred Scriptures/Bible.</note>; when these are brought forward, anyone can see that they mean nothing else. Out of many, these few examples are cited: *Bezalel was filled with the spirit of wisdom, understanding, and knowledge*, Exodus 31:3. *Nebuchadnezzar said of Daniel that an excellent spirit, knowledge, understanding, and wisdom were in him*, Daniel 4:5. *Joshua was filled with the spirit of wisdom*, Deuteronomy 34:9. *Make for yourselves a new heart and a new spirit*, Ezekiel 18:31. *Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven*, Matthew 5:3. *I dwell in a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble*, Isaiah 57:15. *The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit*, Psalm 51:19. *I will give the garment of praise instead of a heavy spirit*, Isaiah 61:3. Besides these and others, it is also clear that "spirit" signifies things belonging to a perverse and wicked mind: *Woe to the foolish prophets who follow their own spirit*, Ezekiel 13:3. *Conceive chaff, bring forth stubble; as for your spirit, fire shall consume you*, Isaiah 33:11. *A man wandering in spirit and uttering lies*, Micah 2:11. *A generation whose spirit was not faithful to God*, Psalm 78:8. *The spirit of whoredoms*, Hosea 5:4; Zechariah 4:12. *That every heart may melt and every spirit grow faint*, Ezekiel 21:12. *That which comes into your spirit shall never happen*, Ezekiel 11:5. *In whose spirit there is no deceit*, Psalm 32:2. *Pharaoh's spirit was troubled*, Genesis 41:8; similarly Nebuchadnezzar’s, Daniel 2:3. From these and many other passages, it is manifest that "spirit" signifies the mind of man and the things belonging to the mind.

157. Since by the spirit of man his mind is understood, therefore by **BEING IN THE SPIRIT**—a phrase used several times in the Word—is meant a state of the mind separated from the body. Because in that state the Prophets saw things that exist in the <term>Spiritual World</term><note>The realm inhabited by spirits and angels, distinct from the natural world.</note>, it is called the **Vision of God**. Their state then was the same as that of spirits and angels in that world. In that state, the spirit of man—that is, his mind regarding its sight—can be transferred from place to place while the body remains in its own. This is the state in which I have now been for twenty-six years <note>Swedenborg dates his spiritual call to the mid-1740s; this text (True Christian Religion) was published in 1771.</note>, with the difference that I am in the spirit and in the body at the same time, and only occasionally outside the body. That Ezekiel, Zechariah, Daniel, and John when he wrote the Apocalypse, were in this state is evident from the following; EZEKIEL says, "*The Spirit lifted me up and brought me back to Chaldea to the captivity in a* **VISION OF GOD, IN THE SPIRIT OF GOD**; *so the* **VISION** *that I had seen went up from me*," Chapter 11:1, 24. He also says *that the Spirit lifted him up and he heard a rumbling behind him*, Chapter 3:12, 14. Also *that the Spirit lifted him up between earth and heaven and brought him to Jerusalem, where he saw abominations*, Chapter 8:3 and following. He saw *four living creatures which were Cherubim, and various things with them*, Chapter 1 and Chapter 10; as well as *a new Earth and a new Temple, and an Angel measuring them*, Chapters 40 to 48, noting that he was then in Vision and in the Spirit, Chapter 40:2; Chapter 43:15. The same happened with ZECHARIAH, in whom an Angel was present at the time, when he saw *a man riding among the myrtle trees*, Chapter 1:8 and following; *four horns, and a man with a measuring line in his hand*, Chapter 2:1, 5 and following; *Joshua the High Priest*, Chapter 5:1, 6 <note>original: "Joschuam Sacerdotem magnum"; this refers to Zechariah 3:1</note>; *four chariots coming out from between two mountains, and horses*, Chapter 6:1 and following. DANIEL was in a similar state when he saw *four beasts rising from the sea, and many things concerning them*, Chapter 7:1 and following; and when he saw *the battles of the ram and the goat*, Chapter 8:1 and following. He states *that he saw these in Vision*, Chapter 7:1, 2, 7, 13; Chapter 8:2; Chapter 10:1, 7, 8; and *that the Angel Gabriel was seen by him in Vision and spoke with him*. The same occurred with JOHN when he wrote the Apocalypse; he says he was in the Spirit on the Lord’s day, Revelation 1:10; and that he was *carried away into the wilderness in the Spirit*, Chapter 17:3; and *to a high mountain in the Spirit*, Chapter 21:10.

# COROLLARY.

158. Since this chapter has treated the **HOLY SPIRIT** <note>Latin: "Spiritu Sancto".</note>, it is altogether worth mentioning that in the Word of the Old Testament, the "Holy Spirit" is nowhere named, but only the "spirit of holiness" in three places: once in David (Psalm 51:11 <note>Original text cites Psalm 51:13 following a different numbering system.</note>) and twice in Isaiah (Chapter 63:10, 11). But in the Word of the New Testament, it is mentioned frequently—among the Evangelists, in the Acts of the Apostles, and in their Epistles. The reason is that the Holy Spirit existed for the first time when the Lord came into the world, for the Spirit proceeds from Him from the Father; for **THE LORD ALONE IS HOLY** (Revelation 15:4); wherefore it was also said by the Angel Gabriel to Mary the Mother, "**THE HOLY THING** *which shall be born of thee*" (Luke 1:35). As for the statement, "*The Holy Spirit was not yet, because Jesus was not yet glorified*" (John 7:39), and yet it is said earlier that the Holy Spirit filled Elizabeth (Luke 1:41), as well as Zacharias (Luke 1:67) and Simeon (Luke 2:25), the reason was that the Spirit of Jehovah the Father filled them; this was called the "Holy Spirit" because of the Lord, who was already in the world. This is the reason why in the Word of the Old Testament it is nowhere said that the Prophets spoke from the Holy Spirit, but from Jehovah; for everywhere it is said, **JEHOVAH SPOKE TO ME**, **THE WORD FROM JEHOVAH WAS MADE TO ME**, **JEHOVAH SAID**, **THE SAYING OF JEHOVAH**. So that no one may doubt that this is so, I wish to cite from **JEREMIAH** alone, where these things are said:

159. To these things I will add these <term>MEMORABLE OCCURRENCES</term><note>Latin: "Memorabilia." These are narrative accounts of Swedenborg’s visions and interactions in the spiritual world, which he used to illustrate his theological points.</note>. FIRST: Once when I was in the company of <term>Angels</term> in <term>Heaven</term>, I saw at a distance below a great Smoke, and from it fire breaking out at intervals; and then, as the Angels were conversing with me, I said that few here know that the smoke seen in the <term>Heels</term><note>Latin: "Infernis," referring to the lower regions or hells.</note> arises from falsities confirmed by reasonings, and that the fire is wrath burning against those who contradict them. To this I added that this is as unknown in this World as it is in my own—where I live in the body—that flame is nothing other than ignited smoke. I have often experienced that this is so: for in the fireplace I have seen smoke ascending from the wood, and when I applied fire to it with a brand, I saw that smoke turn into flames, taking a similar shape to the smoke; for the individual particles of smoke become tiny sparks which burn together, just as happens with ignited gunpowder. It is the same with this Smoke which we see below; it consists of just as many falsities, and the fire breaking out there like a flame is the heat of zeal for those falsities.

Then the Angels said to me, "Let us pray to the Lord that we may be allowed to descend and approach, so that we may perceive what kinds of falsities they are that smoke and burn in this way among those people." And it was granted; and behold, a column of light appeared around us, continuing down to that place. And then we saw four companies of spirits who were strenuously maintaining that **God the Father**, because He is invisible, ought to be approached and worshipped, and not **His Son** born in the World, because He is a man and visible. 

When I looked to the sides, on the left were seen the Learned from the <term>Clergy</term>, and behind them the unlearned; and on the right were the Scholarly from the <term>Laity</term>, and behind them the unrefined. But between us and them was a gaping chasm which could not be crossed. But we turned our eyes and ears to the left, where the Learned from the Clergy were, with the unlearned behind them, and we heard them reasoning about God in this way: 

"We know from the Doctrine of our Church, which is the same concerning God throughout the **European World**, that God the Father, because He is invisible, must be approached, and at the same time God the Son and God the Holy Spirit, who are also invisible because they are co-eternal with the Father. And because God the Father is the Creator of the universe, and is therefore present in the Universe wherever we turn our eyes, He graciously hears us when we pray to Him; and after receiving Mediation from the Son, He sends the holy spirit, who brings the glory of His Son's righteousness into our hearts and blesses us. We, having been made <term>Doctors of the Church</term>, have felt the holy operation of that mission in our breasts while we preached, and we have breathed out devotion from His presence in our minds. We are affected in this way because we direct all our senses to the invisible God, who works not specifically in the sight of our intellect, but universally in the whole system of our mind and body through His emissary spirit. The worship of a visible God—that is, a God appearing before the mind as a man—would not produce such effects."

When these things had been said, the unlearned among the Clergy, who stood behind them, applauded and added this: "From where does Holiness come if not from the Divine that is inconspicuous and imperceptible? At this [thought], as soon as it touches the threshold of our hearing, we expand the expressions of our faces and are gladdened as if by the soothing of a fragrant breeze, and we also beat our breasts; otherwise, toward that which is clear and perceptible..." <note>The text cuts off here, continuing on the next page.</note>

When this enters the ear, it becomes merely natural, and not Divine. For a similar reason, the Roman Catholics cry out their Masses in the Latin tongue, and bring forth and show the hosts—about which they produce Divine mysteries—from the inner sanctuaries of the altars; at these things, as if they were the most secret of mysteries, the people fall upon their knees and breathe in a sense of holiness. After this, we turned to the right, where the Learned stood, and after them the unlearned from the Laity. From the Learned I heard these things: "We know that the wisest of the Ancients worshipped an invisible God, whom they called Jehovah <note>original: "Jehovam"</note>. But after these, in the age that followed, people made for themselves gods from deceased Monarchs, among whom were Saturn, Jupiter, Neptune, Pluto, Apollo, as well as Minerva, Diana, Venus, and Themis. They built temples for them and assigned them Divine worship. From this worship, as it descended through time, idolatry arose, from which the whole world finally went insane. We, therefore, unanimously agree with our priesthood and presbytery: that there have been and are three Divine Persons from eternity, each of whom is God. It is enough for us that they are invisible." To these the unlearned behind them added, "We agree! Is not God God, and man man? But we know that if someone proposes a 'Man-God,' the common people—who have a purely sensual idea of God—would flock to him."

After these things were said, their eyes were opened, and they saw us near them. They then became silent out of indignation that we had heard them; but the Angels, by the power given to them, closed the exterior or lower levels of their thoughts (from which they had been speaking) and opened the interior or higher levels. From these higher levels, the Angels compelled them to speak their true thoughts about God. Then, they spoke and said, "What is God? We have not seen His appearance, nor heard His voice. What then is God but Nature in its firsts and its lasts? We see Nature because it shines in our eyes, and we hear it because it sounds in our ears."

Hearing this, we said to them: "Have you ever seen <term>Socinus</term> <note>Lelio or Fausto Sozzini, 16th-century theologians who denied the full divinity of Christ</note>, who acknowledged only God the Father, or <term>Arius</term> <note>A 4th-century priest whose teachings, known as Arianism, held that Jesus was a created being and not co-eternal with God</note>, who denied the Divinity of the Lord the Savior, or any of their followers?" To this they replied, "We have not seen them." We said, "They are in the deep below you." Soon after, some from that deep were summoned; when questioned about God, they spoke just as the others had, and even added: "What is God? We can make as many gods as we want." 

Then we said, "It is in vain to speak with you about the Son of God born in the World; but we will still say this: lest faith in God—which must be in Him and from Him—should perish because no one has seen Him, it pleased Jehovah God to descend and assume the Human. Without this, faith would be like a water bubble in the air, beautifully colored in the first and second age, but in the third and following it would dissipate into nothing. He did this to bring Himself into view and to prove that God is not a mere 'being of reason' <note>Latin: "Ens rationis," a conceptual abstraction existing only in the mind</note>, but is the very One who Was, Is, and Will Be from eternity to eternity. God is not a word of three syllables <note>original: "vox trium syllabarum." Likely referring to the Latin "Je-ho-vah" or perhaps an abstract term like "Nu-me-en"</note>, but is the everything of all things from the <term>Alpha</term> to the <term>Omega</term>. Consequently, He is the Life and Salvation of all who believe in Him as visible, and not of those who say they believe in an invisible God; for to believe, to see, and to know make one. Wherefore the Lord said to Philip: *He who sees and knows Me, sees and knows the Father*; and elsewhere: *it is the will of the Father that they believe in the Son, and he who believes in the Son has eternal life, but he who does not believe the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God remains upon him.* He says these things in John Chapter 3:15, 16, 36 and Chapter 14:6 to 15."

Hearing this, many from the four groups grew so angry that smoke and fire seemed to come out of their nostrils. We then departed, and the Angels, after they accompanied me home, ascended into their Heaven.

I conversed with them about many things, including this: that in the World where I am in the body, during the night, innumerable Stars, greater and smaller, appear, and that those are so many suns, which only transmit light into the World of our sun. # UNIVERSAL THEOLOGY

Regarding the stars, I remarked that there might be as many of them as there are in the world where I am. The angels, delighted by this conversation, said that perhaps there are indeed just as many, since every <term>Heavenly Society<note>In this context, a "society" refers to a distinct community of angels organized by their specific type of love and goodness.</note></term>, in the sight of those below the heavens, sometimes shines like a star. These societies of heaven are innumerable, all organized according to the varieties of the affections of the love of good, which are infinite in God and thus innumerable from Him. Because these were foreseen before creation, I consider that a corresponding number of stars were provided—that is, created—in the world where men live, who will exist in natural, material bodies. 

As we were conversing in this way, I saw in the north a paved way, so crowded with spirits that there was scarcely room for a footprint between any two of them. I told the angels that I had seen this road before, with spirits like ranks of an army upon it, and I had heard that this is the path traveled by all who depart from the natural world. The reason that road is covered with such a multitude of spirits is that several tens of thousands of people die every week, and all of them migrate into this world after death. To this, the angels added that the road ends in the middle of this world, right where we are now. The reason it ends in the center is that to the side toward the East are the Societies that dwell in love toward God and the neighbor; to the left, toward the West, are the Societies of those who are opposed to those loves; and ahead toward the South are the Societies of those who are more intelligent than the rest. This is why those recently arrived from the natural world first flow to this spot. When they are here, they remain in their "externals"—the outward personality they had in the former world—and afterwards they are gradually let into their "internals" to be explored for what they truly are. After this exploration, the good are carried to their places in Heaven, and the evil to their places in Hell.

We stationed ourselves in the center where this influx of spirits ended and said, "Let us stay here a little while and speak with some of the new arrivals." We chose twelve from those flowing in; and because they were all fresh from the natural world, they did not realize they were anywhere else but still in that world. We asked them what they thought about **HEAVEN** and **HELL**, and about **LIFE AFTER DEATH**. 

To this, one of them replied, "Our <term>Holy Order<note>Referring to the priesthood or clergy.</note></term> impressed upon me the faith that we are to live after death, and that there are a Heaven and a Hell. Therefore, I believed that all who live morally go to Heaven, and because everyone lives morally, no one goes to Hell; thus, Hell is a fable made up by the Clergy to deter people from living badly. What does it matter if I think about God one way or another? Thought is merely like chaff or a bubble on the water, which dissolves and passes away."

A **SECOND** person near him said, "My faith is that Heaven and Hell exist, and that God rules Heaven and the Devil rules Hell. Because they are enemies and opposed to each other, one calls 'evil' what the other calls 'good.' A moral man is a simulator <note>meaning a hypocrite or actor</note> who can make evil appear as good and good as evil; he stands on the side of both. What does it matter then whether I am with one Lord or the other, as long as he favors me? Evil delights men just as much as good does."

A **THIRD** at his side said, "What does it matter to me if I believe Heaven and Hell exist? For who has come from there and told us? If every man lived after death, why has not one person out of such a great multitude returned and announced it?"

A **FOURTH** next to him said, "I will inform you why no one has returned to tell us. The cause is that when a man breathes out his soul and dies, he either becomes a ghost and is dissipated, or he is like the breath of the mouth, which is merely wind. How can such a thing return and speak with anyone?"

A **FIFTH** took up the conversation and said, "Friends, wait until the day of the **Last Judgment**, for everyone will then return into their bodies, and you will see them and speak with them, and each will then tell his fate to the other."

A **SIXTH**, standing directly opposite and laughing, said, "How can a spirit, which is wind, return into a body eaten by worms, or into a skeleton dried by the sun and fallen into dust? And how can some Egyptian who has been made into a **mummy** <note>original: "Mumi"</note>, and mixed by an apothecary into extracts or emulsions to be drunk or eaten, return and tell anything? Therefore, wait for that last day if you have faith, but you will wait forever and ever in vain."

It is the same with you today; therefore you have spoken just as you thought in the former world." Then the angels shook off their ignorance, and they saw themselves in another world and among those they did not know; then they exclaimed, "Oh, where are we?" Then we said to them: "Do not delay, or else you will be cast out." They hurried downward and went away.

On the way home, we spoke about the reason why the <term>Occipitia</term> of those who find delight in doing evil are hollowed out in this world. I gave this reason: that man has two brains, one in the back of the head, which is called the <term>Cerebellum</term>, and the other in the front, which is called the <term>Cerebrum</term>; and that in the <term>Cerebellum</term> dwells the love of the will, and in the <term>Cerebrum</term> the thought of the understanding. When the thought of the understanding does not lead the love of the man's will, the innermost parts of the <term>Cerebellum</term>, which in themselves are celestial, collapse; hence the hollow.

Wherefore, I opened my mind, saying: "Is it not against reason to think that God the Father fell out of grace with the human race and rejected and excommunicated it? Is not Divine Grace an attribute of the Divine Essence? Therefore, to 'fall out of grace' would be to fall out of His own Divine Essence, and to fall out of His Divine Essence would be to no longer be God. Can God be alienated from Himself? Believe me, Grace on God's part, just as it is infinite, is also eternal. The grace of God on man's part can be lost if he does not receive it; but if grace were to recede from God, it would be the end for the entire Heaven and the entire human race. Therefore, grace remains on God's part forever—not only toward Angels and Men, but even toward the devils in Hell. Since this is according to reason, why do you say that the only access to God the Father is through faith in the merit of the Son, when it is actually perpetual through grace?"

"But why do you speak of access to God the Father *on account of* the Son, and not *through* the Son? Is not the Son the Mediator and Savior? Why do you not approach the Mediator and Savior Himself? Is He not God and Man? Who on earth approaches a Caesar, King, or Prince directly? Is there not a spokesperson or someone to introduce them? Do you not know that the Lord came into the world so that He Himself might introduce us to the Father, and that access is given only through Him? This access is perpetual when you approach the Lord Himself directly, because He is in the Father and the Father is in Him. Search the Scripture now, and you will see that this is according to it, and that your way to the Father is against it, just as it is against reason. I tell you also, it is an act of impudence <note>original: "protervitas," meaning boldness or insolence</note> to climb up to God the Father and not go through Him who is in the bosom of the Father and alone is with Him. Have you not read John 14:6?" <note>"Jesus said to him, 'I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.'"</note>

Hearing these things, the old man became so incensed that he leaped from his seat and shouted to his scribes to throw me out. And when I had left by my own cleverness, he threw the book which his hand happened to grab after me out the door—and that book was **The Word**.

## ON THE DIVINE TRINITY

163. Having treated **God the Creator** and at the same time **Creation**, and afterward the **Lord the Redeemer** and at the same time **Redemption**, and finally the **Holy Spirit** and at the same time **Divine Operation**, and because the **Triune God** has thus been treated, it is necessary that the **Divine Trinity** also be addressed—which is known in the Christian World, and yet unknown. For by this alone is a just idea of God obtained, and a just idea of God is in the Church like the inner sanctuary and the altar in a Temple; and like a Crown upon the head and a scepter in the hand of a King sitting upon his Throne. From this hangs, like a chain from its head, the entire body of Theology; and if you are willing to believe it, everyone's place in the Heavens is assigned according to their idea of God. For that idea is like a <term>touchstone</term> <note>original: "Lapis lydius," a stone used to test the purity of gold and silver</note> by which gold and silver are tested—that is, the nature of the good and truth in a person. For no saving good is given in a person except from God, nor any truth that does not draw its specific quality from the heart of that good. But so that the **Divine Trinity** may be seen with both eyes, its explanation must be divided into the following points: 

*I. That there is a Divine Trinity, which is Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. II. That these three—Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—are the three Essentials of one God, which make one, just as Soul, Body, and Operation do in man. III. That before the World was Created this Trinity did not exist, but that after the World was created, when God became incarnate, it was provided and made; and then in the Lord God the Redeemer and Savior Jesus Christ.*

### 164. I. **THAT THERE IS A DIVINE TRINITARY, WHICH IS FATHER, SON, AND HOLY SPIRIT.**

That there is a Divine Trinity—Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—is clearly evident from the <term>Word</term> <note>The Holy Scriptures or Bible.</note>, and from these passages therein: "The Angel Gabriel said to Mary, the <term>HOLY SPIRIT</term> <note>original: "Spiritus Sanctus"</note> shall come upon you, and the <term>POWER OF THE MOST HIGH</term> <note>original: "Virtus Altissimi"</note> shall overshadow you; therefore that Holy thing which is born of you shall be called the <term>SON OF GOD</term> <note>original: "Filius Dei"</note>," Luke 1:35; here three—the Most High (who is God the Father), the Holy Spirit, and the Son of God—are named. When *Jesus* was baptized, behold, the Heavens were opened, and John saw the <term>HOLY SPIRIT</term> descending like a Dove, coming upon Him, and a voice from Heaven saying, "This is my beloved <term>SON</term>, in whom I am well pleased," Matthew 3:16, 17; Mark 1:10, 11; John 1:32. It is even more clear from these words of the Lord to the Disciples: "Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the <term>FATHER</term>, and of the <term>SON</term>, and of the <term>HOLY SPIRIT</term>," Matthew 28:19; and furthermore from these in John: "There are three who bear witness in Heaven, the <term>FATHER, THE WORD, AND THE HOLY SPIRIT</term>," 1st Epistle, Chapter 5:7. And besides these, there is the fact that the Lord prayed to His Father, and that He spoke of Him and with Him, and that He said He would send the Holy Spirit, and also that He did send it. Moreover, the Apostles in their Epistles frequently named the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit. From these things it is plain that there is a Divine Trinity, which is Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

### 165.

But how these things are to be understood—whether it means there are three Gods who are one God in essence and therefore in name, or whether they are three objects of one subject, such that they are merely qualities or attributes of one God which are named in this way, or otherwise—Reason, if left to itself, can in no way see. But what path to take? There is no other way than for a person to approach the Lord God the Savior, and under His guidance read the Word, for He is the God of the Word; then he will be enlightened and will see Truths which Reason will also recognize. However, if you do not approach the Lord, even if you read the Word a thousand times and see the Divine Trinity and also the Unity there, you will understand nothing other than that there are three Divine Persons, each of whom individually is God, and thus three Gods. But because this is repugnant to the common perception of all people in the entire World, to avoid insults, they have devised the idea that although there are three in truth, nevertheless faith demands that they not be called three Gods, but One. And furthermore, lest they be overwhelmed with criticism, the understanding must be especially imprisoned in this matter and kept bound under "the obedience of faith"; and this shall henceforth be considered a holy thing of the Christian Order in the Christian Church. Such a paralyzed offspring <note>original: "foetus paralyticus"</note> was born because they did not read the Word under the Lord’s guidance; and everyone who does not read the Word under His guidance reads it under the guidance of his own intelligence. 166. II. **THAT THESE THREE, FATHER, SON, AND HOLY SPIRIT, ARE THE THREE ESSENTIALS OF THE ONE GOD, WHICH MAKE ONE, JUST AS SOUL, BODY, AND OPERATION DO IN MAN.**
There are general *Essentials* of a single thing, and also particular ones, and these together constitute one *Essence*. The general *Essentials* of a single human being are his *soul, body, and operation* <note>meaning the person's activity or way of acting in the world</note>. That these make one *Essence* can be seen from the fact that one is from the other, and for the sake of the other, in a continuous series. For a human being begins from the *soul*, which is the very essence of the seed; this not only initiates, but also produces in its own order those things which belong to the body, and afterward, those things which proceed from the two of them—the *soul and body*—together, which are called *operations*. Therefore, from the production of one from the other, and the resulting insertion and conjunction, it is evident that these three are of one essence, and for that reason they are called the three essentials.

167. That in the *Lord God the Savior* those three *Essentials*—namely *Soul, Body, and Operation*—were and are, everyone acknowledges. That *His Soul* was from *Jehovah the Father* cannot be denied except by an *Antichrist*, for in the *Word* of both *Testaments* He is called the *Son of Jehovah*, the *Son of the Most High God*, and the *Only-begotten*. Therefore, the *Divine of the Father*, like the *Soul* in man, is *His* first *Essential*. That the *Son*, whom *Mary* brought forth, is the *Body* of that *Divine Soul*, follows from this; for nothing else than a *Body*, conceived and derived from the soul, is prepared in the mother's womb; this, therefore, is the second *Essential*. That *Operations* make the third *Essential* is because they proceed from the soul and body together; and those things which proceed are of the same essence as those that produce them. That the three *Essentials*, which are *Father, Son, and Holy Spirit*, are one in the *Lord*, just as *soul, body, and operation* are in man, is clearly evident from the *Lord’s* words: that the *Father and He* are one, and that the *Father is in Him and He in the Father*. Similarly, that *He and the Holy Spirit* are one, since the *Holy Spirit* is the *Divine* proceeding from the *Lord* from the *Father*, as was fully demonstrated above from the *Word* in numbers 153 and 154. Therefore, to demonstrate this again would be like adding superfluous light, or like loading a table with food after everyone is full.

But when it is understood that the *Divine of the Father*, which constitutes the *Soul*, and the *Divine of the Son*, which constitutes the *Body*, and the *Divine of the Holy Spirit*, or the *Divine* pro-

Yet the Essence is actually one and indivisible; thus, in that view, not one of the three is God in His fullness, but each exists only in a three-fold diminished power, which a sound intellect cannot help but reject.

Therefore, the Trinity in the Lord is Divine, but in man it is human. Who does not see that in this mystery—the claim that there are three Divine Persons and yet one God, and that this God, although He is one, is still not one Person—Reason has no part? Instead, Reason is lulled to sleep, forcing the mouth to speak like a parrot. When Reason is asleep, what is the speech of the mouth but something lifeless? While the mouth speaks words from which Reason turns away and with which it disagrees, what is that speech but foolishness? Today, human Reason is bound regarding the Divine Trinity like a prisoner in handcuffs and leg-irons, and can be compared to a Vestal virgin buried in the earth <note>In ancient Rome, a Vestal Virgin who broke her vows or allowed the sacred fire to go out was punished by being buried alive.</note> because she extinguished the sacred fire; yet the Divine Trinity ought to shine like a lamp in the minds of the people of the Church, since God in His Trinity and in His unity is everything in all the holy things of Heaven and the Church. For what would it be to make one God out of the Soul, another out of the Body, and a third out of the Operation, other than taking the three Essentials of one man and making them into three distinct parts? What is this but to mutilate and kill him?

### 170. III. THAT BEFORE THE WORLD WAS CREATED THIS TRINITY DID NOT EXIST, BUT THAT AFTER THE WORLD WAS CREATED, WHEN GOD BECAME INCARNATE, IT WAS PROVIDED AND MADE, AND THEN IN THE LORD GOD THE REDEEMER AND SAVIOR JESUS CHRIST.

In the Christian Church today, a Divine Trinity is acknowledged as existing before the world was created; this is the idea that Jehovah God from eternity begat a Son, and that from both of them the Holy Spirit then proceeded, and that each of those Three is God by Himself or individually, because each is a Person subsisting by Himself. But because this does not fit into any rational thinking, it is called a "mystery," which can only be entered into by the idea that those Three share one Divine Essence, by which is understood Eternity, Immensity, and Omnipotence, and therefore equal Divinity, Glory, and Majesty. However, it will be demonstrated in the following sections that this Trinity is actually a trinity of three Gods, and thus not a truly Divine Trinity. On the other hand, the Trinity which is indeed of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—but which was provided and made after God became incarnate, and thus after the world was created—is a Divine Trinity because it belongs to the one God. This is evident from all that has been stated previously. That this Divine Trinity is in the Lord God the Redeemer and Savior Jesus Christ is because the three Essentials of one God, which make one Essence, are in Him. That all the fullness of the Divinity is in Him, according to Paul, is also clear from the Lord's own words: that all things of the Father are His, and that the Holy Spirit does not speak from Himself but from Him. Furthermore, when He rose from the tomb, He took up His whole Human Body, both as to the Flesh and the Bones (Matthew 28:1–8; Mark 16:5, 6; Luke 24:1, 2, 3; John 20:11–15), unlike any other man. He even testified to this vividly to the Disciples, saying, "*See my hands and my feet, that it is I Myself; touch Me and see, for a spirit does not have flesh and bones, as you see Me have*" (Luke 24:39). From this, every person can be convinced, if they wish, that the Lord’s Human is Divine, and consequently that in Him, God became Man and Man became God.

## 172. IV. THAT A TRINITY OF DIVINE PERSONS FROM ETERNITY, OR BEFORE THE WORLD WAS CREATED, IS A TRINITY OF GODS IN THE IDEAS OF THOUGHT; AND THAT THIS CANNOT BE ABOLISHED BY AN ORAL CONFESSION OF ONE GOD.

That a Trinity of Divine Persons from eternity is a Trinity of Gods is clearly evident from these words in the **Athanasian Creed** <note>The Athanasian Creed is a foundational statement of Christian belief, focusing on the nature of the Trinity and the Incarnation</note>: *“There is one Person of the Father, another of the Son, and another of the Holy Spirit. The Father is God and Lord, the Son is God and Lord, and the Holy Spirit is God and Lord; yet there are not three Gods and Lords, but one God and Lord. For just as we are compelled by Christian truth to acknowledge each Person individually as God and Lord, so we are forbidden by the Catholic Religion to say there are three Gods or three Lords.”* 

This Creed has been received as ecumenical or universal by the entire Christian Church, and everything known and acknowledged concerning God today comes from it. Anyone who reads it with open eyes can see that the members of the **Council of Nicaea** <note>The council held in 325 AD that first formalized the relationship between the Father and the Son</note>—from whom this Creed emerged as a posthumous offspring—understood the Trinity only as a Trinity of Gods. It follows that not only was a Trinity of Gods understood by them, but that no other Trinity is understood in the Christian world today, because all knowledge of God is derived from that source, and everyone remains in the faith of the words written there. 

I appeal to anyone, whether layperson or cleric, whether titled masters and doctors, or consecrated bishops and archbishops, or even the purple-robed cardinals and the Roman Pontiff himself: let each person consult themselves, and then speak from the ideas of their own mind. From the words of this universally accepted doctrine concerning God, it is as manifest and transparent as water in a crystal goblet <gloss>Original Latin: Chrystallinum Schyphum</gloss> that there are three Persons, and each one of them is God and Lord. It also shows that according to "Christian Truth," they must acknowledge each Person individually as God and Lord, but that their "Religion" or "Catholic Faith" forbids them to speak of or name three Gods and Lords. Thus, Truth and Religion—or faith and confession—are not one thing, but two conflicting things. 

The reason why the phrase was added stating "there are not three Gods and Lords, but one God and Lord," was so that they might not be exposed to the ridicule of the whole world; for who would not guffaw at the mention of three Gods? Yet who cannot see the contradiction in that addition? If, however, they had said...

173. The reason the idea of three Gods cannot be abolished by a mere spoken confession of one God is that the idea has been planted in the memory from childhood, and every man thinks from the things stored there. In humans, the **Memory** is like the **rumen** <term>Ventriculus ruminatorius: The first stomach of a ruminant animal, like a cow, where food is stored before being chewed again</term> in birds and beasts. These animals pack food into that stomach to be nourished by it later; they bring it up at intervals and send it down into the actual stomach, where the food is digested and distributed for all the body’s needs. The human **Understanding** is like this second stomach, while the Memory is the first. 

Anyone can see that the idea of three Divine Persons from eternity—which is the same as the idea of three Gods—cannot be wiped out by speaking a confession of one God, simply because it has not yet been abolished, and because there are famous men who do not *want* it to be abolished. They insist that three Divine Persons are one God, but stubbornly deny that because God is one, He is also one Person. But what wise man does not think to himself that the word "Person" here does not actually mean a person, but rather the description of some quality? Yet, what that quality is, no one knows. Because it is unknown, it remains planted in the memory from childhood like the root of a tree in the earth; even if the tree is cut down, a shoot still grows from it. 

But my friend, do not just cut down that tree; pull up its root as well, and then plant trees of good fruit in your garden. Take care, therefore, that the idea of three Gods does not sit in your mind while your mouth—having no actual idea behind it—sounds out the words "one God." If the Understanding above the memory thinks of three Gods, while the Understanding below the memory makes the mouth speak of one God, what is the result? The mind becomes like a fortuneteller on a stage who plays two parts, running from one side to the other, saying one thing on one side and contradicting it on the other, calling himself wise here and insane there. What else results from this but that, while he stands in the middle looking both ways, he thinks that neither one nor the other is actually anything? Thus, perhaps, he concludes there is no one God, nor three, but none at all. The **naturalism** <note>A philosophical view that everything arises from natural properties and causes, and supernatural or spiritual explanations are excluded</note> reigning today has no other origin than this. 

In Heaven, no one can say a "Trinity of Persons" where each one is individually God. The very heavenly atmosphere—in which their thoughts fly and wave like sounds do in our air—resists it. Only a hypocrite can do it there, but the sound of his speech in that heavenly air grates like teeth grinding together, or croaks like a crow trying to sing like a songbird. I have also heard from Heaven that trying to abolish a faith in a Trinity of gods (which has been confirmed in the mind) through a spoken confession of one God is as impossible as trying to move a tree by its seed, or pulling a man’s chin by a single hair of his beard.

I am the Door; if anyone enters through Me, he shall be saved <note>original: "sum Janua, per Me si quis introiverit, salvabitur" — John 10:9</note>. This crime was committed by Arius <note>Arius (c. 256–336) was a priest in Alexandria who taught that Jesus was a created being, distinct from and subordinate to God the Father</note> and his followers. Because of this, a Council was called by Constantine the Great in the city of Nicaea in Bithynia <note>An ancient region in what is now northwest Turkey</note>. Those gathered there, in order to cast out the damaging heresy of Arius, devised, concluded, and decreed that there were three Divine Persons from eternity—the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit—to each of whom belonged personality, existence, and subsistence in and of Himself. Furthermore, they decreed that the Second Person, or the Son, descended and took on a Human nature and performed Redemption, and that His Human nature possessed Divinity through the <term>Hypostatic Union</term> <note>The theological doctrine that the human and divine natures of Christ are united in one individual person</note>, and that through this union He had a close affinity with God the Father. 

From that time, heaps of abominable heresies concerning God and the Person of Christ began to unfurl from the earth, and the Antichrist began to lift his head and divide God into three, and the Lord Savior into two. Thus, they destroyed the Temple built by the Lord through the Apostles, until not one stone was left upon another that was not thrown down, according to His own words in Matthew 24:2. In that passage, the "Temple" refers not only to the Temple of Jerusalem, but also to the Church, whose "consummation" or end is discussed in that entire chapter. 

But what else could be expected from that Council, and from those that followed, which similarly divided the Divinity into three parts, and placed the incarnate God beneath those three upon their footstool? For they removed the Head of the Church from its Body by "climbing up another way" <note>A reference to John 10:1</note>; that is, they bypassed Him and climbed past Him to God the Father as to another God, with only the phrase "the Merit of Christ" in their mouths, praying that He might have mercy for the sake of that merit. They believed that <term>Justification</term> <note>The process by which a person is made or declared righteous in the eyes of God</note> would thus flow in directly, along with its entire company—namely the remission of sins, renewal, sanctification, regeneration, and salvation—and all this without any intermediate effort from the human being.

175. That the Apostolic Church knew not a single shred about a "Trinity of Persons," or about three Persons from eternity, is clearly evident from the Creed of that Church, which is called the **APOSTLES' CREED**. There it is written: *I believe in God the Father Almighty, Creator of Heaven and Earth: and in Jesus Christ His only Son our Lord, who was conceived by the Holy Spirit, born of the Virgin Mary: and in the Holy Spirit.* No mention is made there of any "Son from eternity," but only of the Son conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of the Virgin Mary. They knew from the Apostles that Jesus Christ was the true God <note>1 John 5:21</note>; that in Him all the fullness of the Divinity dwelt bodily <note>Colossians 2:9</note>; that the Apostles preached faith in Him <note>Acts 20:21</note>; and that all power was given to Him in Heaven and on Earth <note>Matthew 28:18</note>.

176. What trust is to be placed in Councils when they do not go directly to the God of the Church? Is not the Church the Body of the Lord, and He its Head? What is a body without a head? And what kind of body is it upon which three heads have been placed, under whose guidance they take counsel and make decrees? When that happens, does not enlightenment—which is spiritual and comes only from the Lord (who is the God of Heaven and the Church, and also the God of the Word)—become more and more natural and eventually sensual? Then, no genuine theological truth in its internal form is even "scented," but is immediately cast out of the thought of the rational intellect, scattered like chaff in the wind by a winnowing fan. 

In such a state, fallacies take the place of truths, and darkness takes the place of rays of light. People then stand as if in a cavern with spectacles on their noses and a candle in their hand, closing their eyelids to spiritual truths that are in the light of Heaven, but opening them to sensual things that are in the deceptive light <note>original: "luce fatua" — literally 'fatuous' or 'foolish' light</note> of the body's senses. Similarly, later on, when the Word is read, the mind falls asleep to truths and wakes up to falsehoods, becoming like the description of the **Beast from the Sea**: with a mouth like a lion, a body like a leopard, and feet like a bear <note>Revelation 13:2</note>. 

It is said in Heaven that when the Council of Nicaea was finished, those things occurred which the Lord predicted to His disciples: *The sun shall be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken* <note>Matthew 24:29</note>. In reality, the Apostolic Church was like a new star appearing in the starry sky; but the Church after the two Councils of Nicaea became like that same star when it has since grown dim and darkened.

## 177. VI. THAT FROM THE NICENE AND THE ATHANASIAN TRINITY AT THE SAME TIME AROSE THE FAITH WHICH HAD PERVERTED THE ENTIRE CHRISTIAN CHURCH.

That the Nicene Trinity and the Athanasian Trinity <note>The Athanasian Creed, likely written in the 5th century, further defined the Trinity as three co-equal persons, which the author argues leads to the mental image of three separate Gods</note> together constitute a Trinity of Gods can be seen shown above in number 172 from their own Creeds. From this has arisen the modern Faith of the Church, which is directed toward God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Spirit: toward God the Father, that He might <term>impute</term> <note>To "impute" in this context means to legally credit the righteousness of Christ to a person’s account</note> the justice of His Savior Son and assign it to man; toward God the Son, that He might intercede and mediate; and toward the Holy Spirit, that He might actually write upon the person the imputed justice of the Son, sealing and establishing it by justifying, sanctifying, and regenerating the man. This is the modern Faith, which alone can testify that it is a Trinity of Gods which is acknowledged and worshiped. 

From the Faith of any Church flows not only all its worship, but also every one of its dogmas; therefore, it can be said that as the faith is, so the doctrine becomes. It follows that because this Faith is a faith in three Gods, it has perverted everything belonging to the Church. For Faith is the first principle, and the various doctrines are the derivatives; and the derivatives draw their essence from the principle. If anyone examines individual doctrines—such as those concerning God, the Person of Christ, Charity, Repentance, Regeneration, Free Will, Election, and the use of the Sacraments of Baptism and the Holy Supper—he will clearly see that a Trinity of Gods is present in each one. Even if it does not actually appear to be in them, it nevertheless flows from that Trinity as if from its own fountain. But because such an examination cannot be carried out here, and yet it is worth the effort to open one's eyes to it, an Appendix will be added to this work in which this will be demonstrated. 

The Faith of the Church concerning God is like the Soul of the body, and the doctrines are like its limbs. Furthermore, Faith in God is like a Queen, and the dogmas are like the officers of her court; and just as these depend on the word of the Queen, so the dogmas depend on the decree of faith. From that faith alone can it be seen how the Word is understood in its Church; for faith applies to itself and draws toward itself, as if by ropes, whatever it can. If the faith is false, it plays the harlot with every truth there, dragging it toward what is wrong, falsifying it, and making a person act with spiritual insanity. If, however, the Faith is true, then the whole Word supports it, and the God of the Word—who is the Lord God the Savior—pours in light, breathes His Divine approval upon it, and makes the person wise. 

That the modern Faith—which in its internal form is a faith in three Gods, but in its external form is in one God—has extinguished the light in the Word and removed the Lord from the Church, and thus cast its morning into night, will also be seen in the Appendix. This was done by heretics before the Council of Nicaea, and afterward by heretics stemming from it and following it. But what trust should be placed in Councils that do not enter through the "Door into the Sheepfold," but "CLIMB UP SOME OTHER WAY," according to the Lord’s words in John 10:1, 9? Their deliberation is not unlike the walking of a blind man in the day, or a man with eyes in the night, neither of whom sees the pit until they have fallen into it. 

What trust, for example, is to be placed in Councils that established the <term>Vicariate of the Pope</term> <note>The claim that the Pope acts as the representative or "vicar" of Christ on Earth</note>, the <term>Apotheosis</term> <note>The elevation of a human to the status of a god or saint to be prayed to</note> of the dead and the invocation of them as minor deities, the veneration of their images, the authority of indulgences, and the division of the Eucharist <note>Referring to the practice of withholding the wine from the laity</note>, among many other things? Or what trust is to be placed in the Council that established that horrific Predestination <note>Likely referring to the Synod of Dort (1618-1619) which solidified the Calvinist doctrine of absolute predestination</note>, and hung it like the <term>Palladium</term> <note>In Greek mythology, the Palladium was a statue that supposedly protected a city; here it refers to a central doctrine used as a defensive shield for a religion</note> of their religion before the temples of their Church? 

But, my friend! Go to the God of the Word, and thus to the Word itself; enter through the Door into the Sheepfold—that is, into the Church—and you will be enlightened. Then you yourself, by your own sight—

...you will see as if from a mountain, not only the steps of many others, but also your own prior steps and errors in the dark forest beneath the mountain.

178. The Faith of any Church is like a seed from which all its dogmas spring. It can be compared to the seed of a tree, from which everything—right down to the fruit—grows; it is also like a man's seed, from which offspring and families are produced in a successive lineage. Therefore, when the primary Faith is known (which, due to its dominance, is called the "saving faith"), the quality of that Church is understood. This can be illustrated by the following example: suppose a Faith holds that *Nature is the creator of the Universe*. From this, these consequences follow: that the Universe is what is called "God"; that Nature is His essence; that the <term>ether</term> <note>original: "Æther" — historically, the rarefied air of the upper heavens</note> is the supreme God, whom the ancients called Jupiter; that the Air is the Goddess whom the ancients called Juno and made Jupiter’s wife; that the Ocean is a God below them, who with the ancients can be called Neptune; and because the Divinity of Nature reaches even to the center of the earth, that there is also a God there, who with the ancients can be called Pluto. In this view, the Sun is the court of all the gods, where they meet when Jupiter calls a council; moreover, fire is life from God; and thus birds fly "in God," beasts walk "in God," and fish swim "in God." Furthermore, it follows that thoughts are merely modifications of the ether, just as speech is the modulation of the air; and that the affections of love are occasional changes of state caused by the influx of the sun’s rays. Among these views is the idea that life after death, along with Heaven and Hell, is a fable invented by the Clergy to hunt for honors and profit—but that even though it is a fable, it is still useful and should not be openly mocked because it serves the Public by keeping the minds of the simple in the bond of obedience to Magistrates. Finally, it follows that those who are lured into religion are "abstracted" men, their thoughts are fantasies, their actions are ridiculous, and they are the <term>drudges</term> <note>original: "mediastini" — low-level servants or workers</note> of priests who believe what they do not see, and see things that exceed the sphere of their own minds. These consequences, and many others like them, are contained in that Faith—that Nature is the creator of the universe—and they proceed from it when it is opened up.

These things have been brought forward so that it may be known that in the Faith of the modern Church (which in its **internal** form is in Three Gods, but in its **external** form in one), there are falsehoods in swarms. From that faith, as many errors can be pulled out as there are small spiders in a ball of web from a single mother-spider. Anyone whose mind has been made truly rational by light from the Lord sees this; but how can anyone else see it while the door to that faith and its offspring is barred shut by the decree that it is unlawful for reason to look into its mysteries?

## 179. VII. THAT FROM THIS ARISES THAT ABOMINATION OF DESOLATION, AND THE AFFLICTION SUCH AS HAS NOT BEEN AND SHALL NOT BE, WHICH THE LORD HAD FORETOLD IN DANIEL, THE EVANGELISTS, AND THE APOCALYPSE.

In **DANIEL** we read the following: *At last, upon the wing of abominations shall come desolation, even until the consummation and the decree; it shall drop upon the devastation,* Chapter IX: 27 <note>original: "Cap. IX: 2." The author likely refers to verse 27</note>. In the **EVANGELIST MATTHEW**, the Lord says these things: *Then many false prophets shall arise and shall lead many astray; when therefore you see the Abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the Prophet, standing in the holy place (let him who reads note it well),* Chapter XXIV: 11, 15; and later in the same chapter: *For then there shall be great Affliction, such as has not been from the beginning of the world until now, nor shall be,* Verse 21. 

This affliction and that abomination are treated in seven chapters of the **APOCALYPSE**; they are what are meant by the *black horse* and the *pale horse* coming out of the Book whose seals the Lamb opened, Apocalypse Chapter VI: 5 to 8. Also by the *beast ascending from the abyss, which made war with the two witnesses and killed them,* Chapter XI: 7 and following. As also by the *dragon, which stood before the woman about to give birth, that he might devour her offspring, and pursued her into the wilderness, and there cast out water from his mouth like a river to swallow her up,* Chapter XII. And also by the *beasts of the dragon, one from the sea and the other from the earth,* Chapter XIII. Furthermore, by the *three spirits like frogs, which went out from the mouth of the dragon, from the mouth of the beast, and from the mouth of the false prophet,* Chapter XVI: 13. And additionally by this: that after the seven Angels poured out the bowls of the wrath of God, in which were the seven last plagues...

*...onto the earth, into the sea, into the springs and rivers, into the sun, into the throne of the beast, into the Euphrates, and finally into the air, there occurred a great earthquake, such as had not been since men were made, Chapter 16:* an earthquake signifies the inversion <note>or "overturning"</note> of the Church, which occurs through falsehoods and the falsification of truth; this is similar to what is signified by the "great affliction, such as has not been since the beginning of the world," in *Matthew 24:21.* Similar things are understood by these words: *The Angel swung his sickle, and gathered the vintage of the vineyard of the earth, and cast it into the great winepress of the wrath of God, and the winepress was trodden, and blood came out even to the horses' bridles for a distance of one thousand six hundred stadia, Chapter 14: 19, 20.* Blood signifies truth that has been falsified; this is in addition to many other things found in those seven chapters.

180. In the Evangelists—*Matthew 24, Mark 13, and Luke 21*—the successive declines and corruptions of the Christian Church are described. There, by the "great affliction, such as has not been from the beginning of the world, nor shall be," is meant (as *elsewhere throughout the Word*) the infestation of truth by falsehoods, until no truth remains that has not been falsified and <term>consummated</term> <note>original: "consummatum" — here meaning "brought to an end" or "exhausted of its spiritual life"</note>. This is also what is meant there by the "abomination of desolation," and it is also meant by the "desolation upon the wing of abominations," and by the "consummation and decree" in Daniel. This same state is described in the Revelation by the passages just cited above. This has been brought about because the Church did not acknowledge the Unity of God in a Trinity, and His Trinity in Unity, in one Person, but in Three. From this, they founded the Church in the Mind upon the idea of three Gods, while in the Mouth they founded it upon the confession of one God. In this way, they separated themselves from the Lord, eventually to the point where they had no remaining idea of Divinity in His Human Nature—even though He is God the Father Himself in the Human. For this reason, He is also called the "Father of eternity" in *Isaiah 9:5*, and says to Philip, *He who sees Me, sees the Father, John 14:7, 9.*

181. But one might ask: where is the very vein of the fountain <note>the source</note> from which such an "abomination of desolation" (as described in *Daniel 9:27*) and such an "affliction as has not been, nor shall be" (*Matthew 24:21*) has flowed? The answer is: from the "universal faith" currently held in the Christian world, and from its influence, operation, and imputation, according to traditions. It is a marvel that the doctrine of justification by that faith alone—although it is not faith, but a <term>chimera</term> <note>a mythical monster; here used to describe an illogical and impossible theological invention</note>—carries every point in the Christian churches. That is to say, it reigns there almost as the sole theological point in the Sacred Order. This is what all the newcomers to the clergy in the universities eagerly learn, drink in, and absorb; and afterward, as if inspired by heavenly wisdom, they teach it in the Temples and publish it in books. Through it, they seek and profit from the name, fame, and glory of superior erudition; and for its sake, degrees, licenses, and rewards are granted. And these things happen even though, through that "faith alone," the Sun has been darkened today, the Moon has been deprived of its light, the Stars of the heavens have fallen, and the Powers of the heavens have been shaken, according to the words of the Lord’s prediction in *Matthew 24:29*. That the doctrine of this faith has so blinded minds today that people are unwilling—and thus seemingly unable—to see any Divine Truth within the light of the sun or the light of the moon, but only outwardly on a certain rough surface in the light of a fire at night, has been made manifest to me. Therefore, I can prophesy that if Divine Truths concerning the genuine conjunction of charity and faith, concerning Heaven and Hell, concerning the Lord, concerning Life after death, and concerning eternal Happiness, were sent down from Heaven written in letters of silver, they would not be judged worth reading by those who justify and sanctify through "faith alone." But it would be quite different if a paper on "Justification by faith alone" were sent up from the underworld; they would seize upon it, kiss it, and carry it home in their bosoms.

We read in Matthew: *There shall then be great affliction, such as has not been from the beginning of the world until now, nor shall be; indeed, unless those days were shortened, no flesh would be saved, Chapter 24: 21, 22.* That chapter deals with the "Consummation of the Age," by which is meant the end of the Church today—

By the "Dragon" are meant those who are in the faith of the modern church.

I have several times spoken in the spiritual world with those who justify men by "faith alone," and I said that their doctrine is erroneous and actually absurd; that it induces security, blindness, sleep, and darkness in spiritual matters, and leads to the death of the soul. I exhorted them to desist from it. But I received the answer: "Why desist? Does not the superior learning of the Clergy over the Laity depend on this alone?" But I replied that they do not look to the salvation of souls as their goal, but rather the excellence of their own reputation; and because they have applied the truths of the Word to their own false principles and thus corrupted them, they are "Angels of the Abyss," called <term>Abaddons</term> and <term>Apollyons</term> <note>Revelation 9:11; names meaning "Destroyer"</note>, which signifies those who destroy the Church by a total falsification of the Word. But they responded: "What is this? By our knowledge of the mysteries of that faith, we are Oracles, and from it, as if from an inner shrine, we give answers; therefore we are not Apollyons, but <term>Apollos</term> <note>A play on words; Apollo was the Greek god of oracles and wisdom</note>." Indignant at this, I said: "If you are Apollos, you are also <term>Leviathans</term> <note>monstrous sea creatures representing pride and complex false reasoning</note>—the first among you are 'crooked Leviathans' and the second 'long Leviathans,' whom God will visit with His hard and great sword" (*Isaiah 27:1*). But at this, they laughed.

### 183. IX. THAT FROM THE TRINITY OF PERSONS, EACH OF WHOM INDIVIDUALLY IS GOD, ACCORDING TO THE ATHANASIAN CREED, SEVERAL ABSURD AND INCOMPATIBLE IDEAS ABOUT GOD HAVE ARISEN, WHICH ARE PHANTASIES AND ABORTIONS.

From the doctrine of three Divine Persons from eternity—which is the head of all doctrines in the Christian churches—there have arisen many unseemly ideas about God, unworthy of the Christian world. This world ought to be, and could be, a light to all peoples and nations in the four quarters of the earth concerning God and His Unity. All who live outside the Christian Church, whether <term>Mahometans</term> <note>Muslims</note> or Jews, as well as the Gentiles of every worship, are repelled by Christianity solely because of the belief in three Gods there. Those who propagate Christianity know this; therefore, they are extremely careful not to spread the "Trinity of Persons" as it is found in the <term>Nicene</term> and <term>Athanasian Creeds</term> <note>foundational statements of Christian belief from the 4th and 5th centuries</note>, for if they did, people would flee and mock them. 

The absurd, laughable, and frivolous ideas that have arisen from the doctrine of three Divine Persons from eternity—and which arise in anyone who remains in the faith of the words of that doctrine, rising from the ears and eyes into the sight of thought—are these: That God the Father sits on high above the head, and the Son at His right hand, and the Holy Spirit before them, listening, and immediately running throughout the whole world, and according to their decision, dispenses the gifts of justification, inscribes them, and makes those who were "children of wrath" into children of...

of grace, and the elect from the damned; I appeal to the learned among the Clergy and to the educated among the Laity, whether they harbor any other view in their minds than this ideal one—for it flows in of its own accord from the Doctrine itself; see the <term>MEMORABLE RELATION</term> <note>original: "MEMORABILE" — a narrative of a spiritual vision</note> above at number 16. And yet, in Christian Churches, these very things are held as Holy, to be kissed with the lips but not examined with any sight of the mind because they are "above reason." If such things are raised from the memory into the understanding, a person becomes insane; yet this does not remove the idea of three Gods, but instead induces a mindless faith, from which a person thinks about God like one sleeping in a dream, walking in the darkness of night, or like one blind from birth in the light of day.

184. That a *Trinity of Gods* takes up residence in the Minds of Christians, even though they deny it out of shame, is clearly evident from the ingenuity of many in demonstrating that three are one and one is three, through various examples in Geometry, <term>Solid Geometry</term> <note>original: "Stereometricis"</note>, Arithmetic, and Physics, and also through the folding of clothes and papers; thus they play with the Divine Trinity like <term>soothsayers</term> <note>original: "harioli" — diviners or fortune-tellers</note> among themselves. Their soothsaying about it can be compared to the eyesight of those in a fever, who see one object—be it a person, a table, or a candle—as three, or three as one. It can also be compared to the mockery of those who turn soft wax between their fingers and mold it into various shapes: now into a triangle to show the Trinity, now into a sphere to show unity, saying, "Is it not still one and the same substance?" Yet the Divine Trinity is like a pearl of the greatest price; but when divided into Persons, it is like a pearl divided into three parts, whereby it utterly and clearly perishes.

***

185. To these things shall be added these <term>MEMORABLE RELATIONS</term>. FIRST: In the *Spiritual World*, there are Climates and Zones just as in the *Natural World*; there is nothing in the latter that is not also in the former, though they differ in origin. In the *Natural World*, the varieties of Climates are according to the distances of the Sun from the Equator; in the *Spiritual World*, they are according to the distances of the affections of the will, and the resulting thoughts of the intellect, from true love and true faith. All things there are correspondences of these. In the cold Zones of the *Spiritual World*, things appear similar to those in the cold Zones of the *Natural World*; there appear Lands bound by frost, as well as waters, and also snow upon them. Those people come there and dwell there who, in the World, lulled their intellect to sleep through an inertia in thinking about spiritual things, and who were consequently in an inertia in performing any useful works. They are called *Northern Spirits*. Once, a desire came over me to see some *Region in the cold Zone* where those northern spirits were; and therefore in spirit I was led into the *North*, even to a tract where the whole land appeared covered with snow and all the water bound with ice. It was the *Sabbath* day, and I saw men—that is, spirits—of a similar stature to men in the World; but on account of the cold, their heads were clothed in lion skins, the mouths of which were fitted over their own mouths; as for their bodies, they were covered from front and back down to their loins with leopard skins, and their feet with bear skins. I also saw many carried in chariots, and some in chariots carved in the form of a dragon, whose horns stretched out forward. Those chariots were pulled by small horses whose tails had been cut off; they ran like terrible wild beasts...
