<note>original: "NOVI CÆLI ET NOVÆ ECCLESIÆ"</note>

...and the driver, holding the reins in his palms, continually urged them on and pressed them into a gallop. Finally, I saw crowds flocking toward a Temple, which had not been visible because it was covered in snow; but the keepers of the Temple were softening the snow and, by digging it away, were preparing an entrance for the arriving worshippers, who descended and entered. I was also granted to see the Temple from the inside; it was illuminated with an abundance of lamps and lanterns. There stood an Altar made of hewn stone, behind which a Tablet was hung, and upon it was written: **THE DIVINE TRINITY: FATHER, SON, AND HOLY SPIRIT, WHO ARE ESSENTIALLY ONE GOD, BUT PERSONALLY THREE.** 

At length, the Priest standing at the Altar, after he had bowed his knees to the Altar-Tablet, ascended the pulpit with a Book in his hand and began a sermon on the Divine Trinity. He cried out: "O, how great a Mystery! That God in the Highest begot a Son from eternity, and through Him brought forth the Holy Spirit; these Three joined themselves through Essence, but separated themselves by their properties, which are <term>Imputation</term> <note>The theological idea that Christ's righteousness is credited to a person's account</note>, <term>Redemption</term>, and Operation. But if we look upon these things with reason, our vision grows dark, and a spot appears before it, just as it does before the eye of one who fixes his gaze upon the naked Sun. Therefore, my listeners, regarding this matter, let us henceforth keep our understanding under the <term>obedience of faith</term>." <note>A phrase meaning that one should accept doctrines blindly, even if they contradict logic</note>

After this, he cried out again, saying: "O, how great a Mystery is our Holy Faith! Which is this: that God the Father imputes the righteousness of the Son and sends the Holy Spirit, who, from that imputed righteousness, works the pledges of <term>Justification</term> <note>The process by which a sinner is declared righteous before God</note>—which in short are the remission of sins, innovation, regeneration, and salvation. Regarding the influx or act of this faith, a human being knows no more than the pillar of salt into which Lot’s wife was turned; and regarding its indwelling or state, he knows no more than a fish in the sea. But my friends, a treasure lies hidden in it, so hedged about and concealed that not a crumb of it is visible. Therefore, regarding this also, let us captivate our understanding under the obedience of faith."

After some sighs, he cried out yet again, saying: "O, how great a mystery is <term>Election</term>! <note>The doctrine that God chooses specific individuals for salvation regardless of their actions</note> He is 'Elect' to whom God imputes that faith, which out of His free pleasure and pure grace He pours into whomsoever He wills and whenever He wills. Man is like a tree stump when it is being poured in, but becomes like a tree once it has been infused. Truly, the fruits—which are good works—do indeed hang from that tree (which in a symbolic sense is our faith), but they do not actually cling to it; for this reason, the value of that tree is not from its fruit. But because this sounds like a <term>heterodox</term> <note>An opinion or doctrine at variance with established religious beliefs</note> view, and yet is a mystical truth, my brothers, let us captivate our understanding under the obedience of this faith."

And then, after some interval, standing as if he were still extracting something from his memory, he continued, saying: "From the heap of Mysteries I will draw forth yet one more, which is: that in spiritual matters, man does not possess even a grain of <term>Free Will</term>. For the leaders and bishops of our order say in their theological canons that in those things which pertain to faith and salvation (which are specifically called 'spiritual'), man cannot will, think, or understand anything—nor even adapt and apply himself to receiving them. Therefore, I say of myself, that concerning these things, a man cannot by his own power think from reason or chatter from thought any differently than a parrot, a magpie, or a raven. Thus, in spiritual things, man is truly a donkey, and only in natural things is he a man. But my associates, lest this should disturb your reason, let us—in this as in the rest—captivate our understanding under the obedience of faith. For our Theology is a bottomless abyss into which, if you plunge the sight of your understanding, you will be submerged and perish as if shipwrecked. Yet listen: there is nonetheless smoke in the very light of the Gospel, which shines high above our heads; but alas, the hair on our heads and the bones of our skulls prevent and ward it off, so that it cannot penetrate into the chamber of our understanding."

Having said these things, he descended. After he had offered up prayers at the Altar and the worship was finished, I approached some people who were talking among themselves, where the Priest also was. Those standing around him said, "We give you immortal thanks for such a magnificent and rich sermon of wisdom!" 

But then I said to them, "Did you understand anything?" 

And they replied, "We took it all in with full ears; but why do you ask if we understood? Does the understanding not go numb in such matters?" 

And to these words, the Priest added: "Because you have heard and not understood, you are blessed, for from that comes your salvation."

Afterward, I spoke with the Priest and asked whether he held a laurel wreath <note>A symbol of a high academic degree, such as a Doctorate or Mastership</note>. He replied, "I am a laureated Master." Then I said, "Master, I heard you preaching about Mysteries. If you know those mysteries but do not know anything of what they contain, you know nothing at all. For right now, they are like chests locked with three seals. Unless you open them and look inside—which must be done through the understanding—you do not know if they contain precious things, or worthless trifests, or even harmful things. They could be vipers' eggs and spiders' webs, according to the description in **Isaiah Chapter 59:5**." After I said this, the Priest looked at me with a grim expression. The worshippers withdrew and climbed into their carriages, intoxicated by paradoxes, made foolish by vanities, and surrounded by a thick darkness in all matters of faith and the means of salvation.

### 186. SECOND MEMORABLE RELATION.
Once, I was turning over in my thought the question of which region of the human mind theological matters reside in. Because these matters are spiritual and heavenly, I originally believed they resided in the highest region. For the human mind is divided into three regions, just as a house has three stories, or the dwellings of the Angels are divided into three Heavens. 

Then an Angel stood by me and said: "For those who love Truth because it is true, theological matters rise up even into the highest region, because that is where their Heaven is, and they are in the same light as the Angels. Moral principles, when examined theoretically and as precepts, place themselves below these in the second region, because they communicate with spiritual things. Political matters sit below these in the first region. As for the <term>Scientifics</term> <note>The Latin 'scientificas' refers to factual knowledge, data, and the natural sciences</note>, which are manifold and can be classified into types and species, these form the door to those higher levels. 

"In those people where spiritual, moral, political, and scientific matters are so subordinated, whatever they think or do is done from justice and judgment. The reason for this is that the Light of Truth, which is also the Light of Heaven, illuminates everything that follows from the highest region—much like the light of the Sun, passing through the upper ethers, progressively illuminates the air and the sight of men, beasts, and fish. 

"However, it is quite different for theological matters in those who do not love truth because it is true, but only for the sake of their own reputation and glory. In these people, theological matters reside in the lowest region alongside the 'scientifics.' In some people, these mix together, while in others they cannot mix. Below these, in the same region, are political matters, and below those are moral ones. This is because, for such people, the two higher regions are not open on the right side <note>In Swedenborg's symbolism, the 'right side' represents the will or the love of good</note>. Therefore, they possess no interior reason of judgment nor any affection for justice, but only a certain cleverness. From this cleverness, they can speak about any subject as if from intelligence, and confirm whatever comes their way as if from reason. But the objects of reason that they primarily love are falsehoods, because these cling to the fallacies of the senses. This is why there are so many in the world who can see the truths of Doctrine from the Word no better than those born blind; when they hear such truths, they pinch their nostrils lest the odor offend them and cause nausea. Yet, toward falsehoods, they open all their senses and swallow them down like whales swallowing water."

### 187. THIRD MEMORABLE RELATION.
Once, while I was meditating on the Dragon, the Beast, and the False Prophet mentioned in the Apocalypse <note>The biblical Book of Revelation</note>, an Angelic Spirit appeared to me and asked, "What are you meditating on?" I replied, "On the False Prophet." 

Then he said, "I will lead you to the place where those meant by the 'False Prophet' are found." He added that these are the same people who, in Chapter 13 of the Apocalypse, are understood as the Beast arising from the earth, which had two horns like a Lamb and spoke like a Dragon. I followed him, and behold, I saw a crowd in the midst of which were the <term>Prelates</term> <note>High-ranking church officials or 'Antistites'</note> of the Church. They taught that nothing saves a human being except Faith in the merit of Christ, and that Works are good, but not for the sake of salvation. They insisted that Works must still be taught from the Word so that the laity, especially the simple-minded, might be kept more strictly in the bonds of obedience to the government, and be compelled—as if by religion, and thus from within—to practice moral charity.

Then one of them, seeing me, said: "Would you like to see our Temple <note>original: 'Fanum', often implying a shrine or sanctuary</note>, in which there is an image representing our Faith?" I approached and saw it; behold, it was magnificent. In the center was the image of a Woman clothed in a scarlet robe, holding a gold coin in her right hand and a chain of pearls in her left. But both the image and the Temple were brought about through <term>phantasy</term> <note>In this context, 'phantasy' refers to a spiritual hallucination or a deceptive appearance created by the state of one's own mind</note>; for infernal spirits are able, through phantasies, to represent...

When I looked inside, I saw the foundation stone under which the Word was stored, surrounded by precious stones; from these, a light like lightning flashed onto the walls, which were adorned with forms of cherubs, variegating them beautifully with colors. 

While I marveled at this, the Angels said, "You shall see something even more wonderful." It was then granted to them to open the Third Heaven, where the celestial Angels dwell, who are in love. From the flaming Light flowing from there, that entire Temple vanished, and in its place the Lord Alone was seen, standing upon the foundation stone—which was the Word—in the same appearance in which He was seen by John in **Revelation Chapter 1**. But because a holiness then filled the interiors of the Angels' minds, causing them to fall upon their faces, the way of Light from the third Heaven was suddenly closed by the Lord, and the way of Light from the second Heaven was opened. This caused the earlier appearance of the Temple to return, and also the Tabernacle, though the Tabernacle was now in the center of the Temple. 

By these events, it was illustrated what is meant in **Revelation Chapter 21**:

THE SECOND DISCUSSION <note>original: "Ventilatio"; a formal term for the analytical "airing out" or examination of a theological point</note> CONCERNING THE LORD WAS: Are not the Father and He one, just as the Soul and Body are one? They said that this follows, because the Soul is from the Father. Then one of those who sat on the leaves <note>Swedenborg describes celestial seating arrangements as appearing like leaves or benches in rows</note> in the third row, read from the Symbolic Faith <term>Symbolic Faith: refers to the official Creeds of the church</term>, which is called the Athanasian, these words:

The Reader said that this Creed, where these words are found, is accepted throughout the entire Christian world, even by the Roman Catholics. And they said, what more is needed? The Father God and He are one, just as Soul and Body are one. And they said, because this is so, we see that the Lord's Humanity <term>Humanum: the human nature or manifestation of God</term> is Divine, because it is the Humanity of Jehovah; and also that the Lord is to be approached in His Divine Humanity, and that in this way—and no other—can the Divine, which is called the Father, be approached. This conclusion of theirs was confirmed by the Angel through many passages from the Word <note>The Holy Scriptures</note>, among which were these:

> *A child is born to us, a son is given to us, whose name is Wonderful, Counselor, GOD, Hero, THE ETERNAL FATHER, Prince of Peace* (Isaiah 9:5) <note>In English Bibles, this is Isaiah 9:6</note>.

Do you not believe that I AM IN THE FATHER AND THE FATHER is in Me? Believe me, THAT I AM IN THE FATHER AND THE FATHER IS IN ME* (John 14:8, 9). *Jesus said, I AND THE FATHER ARE ONE* (John 10:30). *Then, all things that the Father has are mine, and all mine are the Father's* (John 16:15; Chapter 17:10). Finally, *Jesus said, I am the Way, the Truth, and the Life; no one comes to the Father except through Me* (John 14:6).

To these, the Reader added that similar things said by the Lord here concerning Himself and His Father could also be said by a man concerning himself and his own soul. Hearing these things, they all said with one voice and heart that the Lord's Humanity is Divine, and that this must be approached in order to approach the Father; since Jehovah God sent Himself into the world through it, and made Himself visible to the eyes of men, and thus accessible. Likewise, He made Himself visible, and thus accessible, in Human Form to the Ancients, but then through an Angel; but because this form was representative of the Lord who was to come, therefore all things of the Church among the Ancients were representative.

After this followed the Deliberation CONCERNING THE HOLY SPIRIT. First, the idea held by many concerning GOD THE FATHER, THE SON, AND THE HOLY SPIRIT was uncovered, which was: that God the Father sits on high, and the Son at His right hand, and from themselves they send out the Holy Spirit to enlighten, teach, justify, and sanctify men. But then a voice was heard from Heaven, saying, "We cannot endure that idea of thought! Who does not know that Jehovah God is Omnipresent? Whoever knows and acknowledges this will also acknowledge that He Himself enlightens, teaches, justifies, and sanctifies, and that there is no mediating God distinct from Him—much less from two—as one person from another person. Therefore, let the former idea, which is vain, be removed, and let this one, which is just, be received, and you will see this clearly." But then a voice was heard from the Roman Catholics, who were standing near the Altar of the Temple, saying, "What then is THE HOLY SPIRIT, who is named in the Word in the Gospels and in Paul, by whom so many learned men from the Clergy—especially from our own—say they are led? Who today in the Christian world denies the Holy Spirit and its operations?" To this, one of those sitting on the leaves of the second row turned and said, "You say that the Holy Spirit is a Person by Himself, and God by Himself. But what is a Person going out and proceeding from a Person, except an Operation going out and

...proceeding, one person cannot go out and proceed from another, but an operation can; or what is God going out and proceeding from God, unless it is the Divine going out and proceeding? One God cannot go out and proceed from another through another, but the Divine can go out from the One God. Hearing this, those sitting upon the thrones unanimously concluded that the Holy Spirit is not a Person by Himself, and thus not a God by Himself, but that it is the Holy Divine <note>original: "Sanctum Divinum"; referring to the active power or influence of God</note> going out and proceeding from the Unique, Omnipresent God, who is the Lord. To this, the Angels standing at the golden Table, upon which was the Word <note>The Word refers to the Sacred Scriptures/Bible</note>, said: WELL DONE. It is nowhere read in the Old Testament that the Prophets spoke the word from the Holy Spirit, but from Jehovah; and where "Holy Spirit" is mentioned in the New Testament, it is understood as the Divine proceeding, which is the Divine illuminating, teaching, vivifying, reforming, and regenerating. 

After this, there followed another discussion <note>original: "Ventilatio"; a formal term for the analytical "airing out" or examination of a theological point</note> concerning the Holy Spirit: from Whom does the Divine—which is understood by the Holy Spirit—proceed? Does it proceed from the Father or from the Lord? While they were examining this, a light shone from Heaven, by which they saw that the Holy Divine, which is meant by the Holy Spirit, does not proceed from the Father through the Lord, but from the Lord from the Father; by comparison, in a human being, his activity does not proceed from the soul through the body, but from the body from the soul. The Angel standing at the Table confirmed this through these passages from the Word: 

*He whom the Father has sent speaks the words of God; He has not given the Spirit by measure to Him; the Father loves the Son, and has given all things into His hand*, John 3:34–35. *A Rod shall come forth from the stem of Jesse, the Spirit of Jehovah shall rest upon Him, the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might*, Isaiah 11:1–2. *That the Spirit of Jehovah was given upon Him, and was in Him*, Isaiah 42:1; Chapter 59:19–20; Chapter 61:1; Luke 4:18. *When the Holy Spirit comes, WHOM I WILL SEND TO YOU FROM THE FATHER*, John 15:26. *He will glorify Me, BECAUSE HE WILL RECEIVE OF MINE, and will announce it to you; ALL THINGS WHATSOEVER THE FATHER HAS ARE MINE, FOR THIS REASON I SAID THAT HE WILL RECEIVE OF MINE, AND ANNOUNCE IT TO YOU*, John 16:14–15. *If I go away, I WILL SEND THE COMFORTER <term>Paracletus: The Counselor or Advocate mentioned in the Gospel of John</term> TO YOU*, John 16:7. *That the Comforter is the HOLY SPIRIT*, John 14:26. THE HOLY SPIRIT WAS NOT YET, BECAUSE JESUS WAS NOT YET GLORIFIED <note>In Swedenborg’s theology, "Glorification" is the process by which Jesus made His human nature Divine</note>, John 7:39. But after the Glorification, JESUS BREATHED ON THEM AND SAID TO THE DISCIPLES, RECEIVE THE HOLY SPIRIT, John 20:22. And in the Revelation: *WHO SHALL NOT GLORIFY THY NAME, O LORD, FOR THOU ALONE ART HOLY*, Chapter 15:4. 

Since the Divine Operation of the Lord from His Divine Omnipresence is understood by the Holy Spirit, therefore when He spoke to the Disciples about the Holy Spirit, whom He was to send from the Father, He also said: *I will not leave you orphans, I GO AWAY AND I COME TO YOU; and in that day you will know that I AM IN MY FATHER, AND YOU IN ME, AND I IN YOU*, John 14:18, 20, 28. And shortly before He departed from the world, He said: *Behold, I am with you always, even to the Consummation of the age*, Matthew 28:20. After these things were read in their presence, the Angel said: from these and many other passages from the Word, it is clear that the Divine, which is called the Holy Spirit, proceeds from the Lord from the Father. To this, those sitting upon the thrones said: THIS IS DIVINE TRUTH.

Finally, this decree was made: That from the deliberations in this Council, we have clearly seen, and therefore acknowledge as Holy Truth, that in the Lord God the Savior Jesus Christ, there is a Divine Trinity, which is: the Divine from Whom (which is called the Father), the Divine Human (which is called the Son), and the Divine proceeding (which is called the Holy Spirit); they cried out together: THAT IN CHRIST ALL THE FULLNESS OF THE GODHEAD DWELLS BODILY, Colossians 2:9. Thus there is one God in the Church.

After these matters were concluded in that magnificent Council, they rose; and the guardian Angel came from the treasury <note>original: "Cimeliarchio"; a place where valuables or precious garments are kept</note> and brought to each of those who sat upon the Thrones splendid garments, interwoven here and there with golden threads, and said: receive the WEDDING GARMENTS. And they were led in glory into the New Christian Heaven, with which the Lord's Church on Earth, which is the New Jerusalem, will be joined.

# CHAPTER FOUR
->CONCERNING<-
# SACRED SCRIPTURE
->OR THE<-
# WORD OF THE LORD.

---

<image-desc>Decorative floral typographical divider.</image-desc>

->**I.**<-

->*That Sacred Scripture or the Word is*<-
->*Divine Truth itself.*<-

189. It is on everyone's lips that the Word is from God, Divinely inspired, and therefore Holy; but up until now it has not been known where in the Word the Divine actually resides. For in its literal sense, the Word appears like common writing, composed in a strange style—neither sublime nor brilliant in appearance, as the secular writings of this age are. Because of this, a person who worships Nature instead of God (or above God) and who thinks from himself and his own <term>proprium: a technical term for the human ego or the "self" that feels independent from God</term>, rather than from Heaven from the Lord, can easily fall into error concerning the Word. Such a person might hold it in contempt and say to himself while reading, "What is this? What is that? Can this be Divine? Can God, who possesses infinite Wisdom, speak in such a way? Where and from whence does its Holiness come, if not from religious sentiment and the resulting persuasion?"

190. But whoever thinks this way does not consider that Jehovah the Lord, who is the God of Heaven and Earth, spoke the Word through Moses and the Prophets, and that it therefore cannot be anything other than Divine Truth; for what Jehovah the Lord Himself speaks, that is what it is. Nor does such a person consider that the Lord the Savior, who is one and the same as Jehovah, spoke the Word through the Evangelists—much of it from His own mouth, and the rest from the Spirit of His mouth, which is the Holy Spirit, through His twelve Apostles. Hence it is, as He Himself says, that in His Words there are Spirit and Life, and that He Himself is the Light that enlightens, and that He is the Truth. This is evident from the following passages: *Jesus said, "the words that I speak to you are Spirit and are Life,"* John 6:63. *Jesus said to the woman at Jacob's well: "If you knew the gift of God, and who it is that says to you, Give me to drink, you would ask of Him, and He would give you living Water... whoever drinks of the Water that I shall give shall not thirst forever, but the Water that I shall give shall become in him a fountain of Water springing up into eternal life,"* John 4:10–11. By "Jacob's Well" <note>original: "Fontem Jacobi"</note> is signified the Word, as also in Deuteronomy 33:28; for this reason the Lord, because He is the Word, sat there and spoke with the woman; and by "living water" is signified the truth of the Word. *Jesus said, "If anyone thirsts, let him come to Me and drink; whoever believes in Me, as the Scripture says, [out of his belly shall] flow...*

## UNIVERSAL THEOLOGY

"rivers of living water shall flow from his belly," John 7:37, 38. <note>original: *Aquæ viventis*</note>. Peter said to Jesus, "You have the words of eternal life," John 6:63. Jesus said, "Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away," Mark 13:31. The reason the Lord's words are Truth and Life is that He Himself is the Truth and the Life, as He teaches in John: "I am the Way, the Truth, and the Life," Chapter 14:6. And in the same Gospel: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and God was the Word; in Him was life, and the life was the light of men," John 1:1, 2, 3. By "the Word" is meant the Lord with respect to <term>Divine Truth: the reality of God as expressed through wisdom and revelation</term>, in which alone there is Life and Light. For this reason, the Word—which is from the Lord and which *is* the Lord—is called a "fountain of living waters," Jeremiah 2:13, Chapter 17:13, Chapter 31:9; a "fountain of salvation," Isaiah 12:3 <note>The Latin text cites XI: 1. 3, likely a slight manuscript or printing error for Isaiah 12:3</note>; a "fountain," Zechariah 13:1; and a "river of the water of life," Revelation 22:1. It is also said that "the Lamb who is in the midst of the throne shall lead them to living fountains of waters," Revelation 7:17. This is besides other places where the Word is also called a "Sanctuary" and a "Tabernacle" in which the Lord dwells with man.

191. But the natural man <note>In this context, the "natural man" refers to someone who thinks only from their physical senses and worldly logic, without spiritual insight</note> still cannot be convinced by these things that the Word is <term>Divine Truth</term> itself, containing <term>Divine Wisdom</term> and <term>Divine Life</term>; for he looks at it based on its style, in which he does not see those things. Yet the style of the Word is the <term>Divine Style</term> itself, with which no other style—no matter how sublime and excellent it may appear—can be compared. The style of the Word is such that there is a holiness in every sense, and in every word—indeed, in some places in the very letters themselves. Because of this, the Word joins man to the Lord and opens Heaven. Two things proceed from the Lord: <term>Divine Love</term> and <term>Divine Wisdom</term> (or what is the same, <term>Divine Good</term> and <term>Divine Truth</term>). The Word in its essence is both of these; and because it joins man to the Lord and opens Heaven, as was said, the Word fills man with the goods of love and the truths of wisdom—his Will with the goods of love, and his Understanding with the truths of wisdom. Thus, man has life through the Word. But it must be clearly understood that life from the Word belongs only to those who read it for the purpose of drawing Divine Truths from it as from their own Fountain, and who simultaneously apply the truths drawn from it to their lives. The opposite happens to those who read the Word merely for the purpose of hunting for honors and gaining the world.

192. Every person who does not know that a certain <term>Spiritual Sense</term> is within the Word, just as the "soul is in the body," can only judge the Word from the sense of its letter. Yet the literal sense is like a <term>case containing precious things</term> <note>original: *Theca continens pretiosa*</note>, which are its spiritual sense. Therefore, when this internal sense is unknown, the Divine Holiness of the Word can only be judged as one might judge a precious stone still in its matrix (the rough rock that surrounds it), which sometimes looks like an ordinary stone. Or it is like a chest made of jasper, lapis lazuli, amianthus <note>a type of fine, silky asbestos mineral</note>, specular stone <note>mica or transparent gypsum</note>, or agate, in which diamonds, rubies, sardonyxes, and oriental topazes lie arranged in their order. While this is unknown, it is no wonder if that chest is valued no more than the price of the material that is visible to the eye. It is the same with the Word regarding the sense of its letter. Therefore, so that man might not be in doubt as to whether the Word is Divine and most Holy, its <term>internal sense</term> has been revealed to me by the Lord. This sense is spiritual in its essence and lives within the external, natural sense just as the soul lives in the body. That sense is the spirit that gives life to the letter; therefore, that sense can testify to the Divinity and Holiness of the Word, and can convince even the natural man, if he is willing to be convinced.

# II.

## *That in the Word there is a Spiritual Sense, Hitherto Unknown.*

193. Who does not acknowledge and agree when it is said that the Word, because it is Divine, is spiritual in its inner heart? But who until now has known what "Spiritual" means, or where that spiritual nature is hidden within the Word? What is "Spiritual" will be made clear in the <term>MEMORABLE RELATION: a descriptive account of a spiritual vision or experience</term> after this chapter; and where it lies hidden in the Word will be shown in what now follows. The Word is spiritual in its heart because it descended from Jehovah the Lord and passed through the Angelic Heavens. The Divine itself, which in itself is inexpressible and beyond perception, was made suitable for the perception of Angels during its descent, and finally for the perception of men. From this comes the Spiritual Sense, which is inside the Natural sense, just as the soul is in a human being, as the thought of the understanding is in speech, and as the affection of the will is in action. And if we may compare it with things that appear before our eyes in the natural world: the spiritual sense is in the natural sense just as the entire brain is within its <term>meninges: the protective membranes or "mothers" of the brain</term>; or as the living shoots of a tree are within its outer and inner barks; or indeed as all the parts of a developing chick are within the eggshell, and so on. But that there is such a spiritual sense of the Word within its natural sense has been guessed by no one until now. Therefore, it is necessary that this Secret—which in itself stands above all secrets revealed until now—should be opened to the understanding. This will be done as it is explained in the following order:

I. *What the spiritual sense is.*
II. *That this sense is in each and every part of the Word.*
III. *That it is because of this sense that the Word is Divinely inspired and holy in every word.*
IV. *That this sense has been unknown until now.*
V. *That from now on it will not be given to anyone except those who are in genuine truths from the Lord.*
VI. *Wonderful things about the Word from its spiritual sense.*

These points will now be unfolded one by one.

194. I. WHAT THE SPIRITUAL SENSE IS. The spiritual sense is not that sense which shines out from the literal sense of the Word when someone searches and explains the Word to confirm some <term>dogma: an established church doctrine</term> of the Church; this may be called the literal and ecclesiastical sense of the Word. Rather, the Spiritual Sense does not appear in the sense of the letter; it is within it, as the soul is in the body, as the thought of the understanding is in the eyes, and as the affection of love is in the face. It is primarily this sense that makes the Word spiritual, not only for men but also for angels; therefore, through that sense, the Word communicates with the Heavens. Since the Word is inwardly spiritual, it was written entirely through <term>Correspondences: the systematic relationship between natural things and spiritual realities</term>. Because it was written through Correspondences, it was written in the ultimate sense in such a style as is found in the Prophets, the Evangelists, and the Revelation. Although this style appears common, it nevertheless hides within itself Divine Wisdom and all Angelic Wisdom. What "Correspondence" is can be seen in the work *On HEAVEN AND HELL*, published in London in 1753, where the *Correspondence of all things of Heaven with all things of man* (numbers 87 to 102) and the *Correspondence of all things of Heaven with all things of the Earth* (numbers 103 to 115) are discussed; more will be seen from examples from the Word to be brought forward below.

195. From the Lord proceed the DIVINE CELESTIAL, the DIVINE SPIRITUAL, and the DIVINE NATURAL, one after the other. Whatever proceeds from His Divine Love is called the DIVINE CELESTIAL, and all of that is Good. Whatever proceeds from His Divine Wisdom is called the DIVINE SPIRITUAL, and all of that is Truth. The DIVINE NATURAL is from both; it is their complex or container in the ultimate <note>In this context, the "ultimate" refers to the lowest or most external level of reality.</note> degree. The Angels of the Celestial Kingdom, who make up the Third or Highest Heaven, are in the Divine that proceeds from the Lord which is called "Celestial," for they are in the Good of love from the Lord. The Angels of the Lord’s Spiritual Kingdom, who make up the Second or Middle Heaven, are in the Divine that proceeds from the Lord which is called "Spiritual," for they are in the Divine...

The Angels of the Lord's Natural Kingdom, who make up the First or lowest Heaven, are in the Divine that proceeds from the Lord which is called the "Divine Natural," and they are in the faith of charity from the Lord. The people of the Church, however, are in one of these Kingdoms according to their own love, wisdom, and faith; and into whichever one they are in, they also enter after death. As the Heaven is, so also is the Word of the Lord: in its last <note>or "outermost"</note> sense it is Natural, in its interior it is Spiritual, and in its innermost it is Celestial, and in each part it is Divine; for this reason, it is adapted for the Angels of the Three Heavens, and also for human beings.

### 196. II. THAT THE SPIRITUAL SENSE IS IN EACH AND EVERY PART OF THE WORD can be seen no better than from examples, such as the following. John says in the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation</note>: *I saw Heaven opened, and behold, a White Horse, and He who sat upon him was called Faithful and True, who in justice judges and fights. And His eyes were a flame of fire; and upon His head were many diadems, having a Name written, which no one knows but Himself. And He was clothed in a garment dipped in blood; and His name is called* THE WORD OF GOD. *His armies in Heaven followed Him upon white horses, clothed in fine linen, white and clean. He has upon His garment and upon His thigh a Name written:* KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS. *I further saw an Angel standing in the Sun, who cried out with a loud voice, "Come and gather yourselves together to the great supper, that you may eat the flesh of kings, and the flesh of captains <note>original: "chiliarchorum" – commanders of a thousand soldiers</note>, and the flesh of the mighty, and the flesh of horses and of those sitting upon them, and the flesh of all, free and slave, and small and great,"* Chapter XIX: 11 to 18. No one can see what these things signify except from the Spiritual Sense of the Word, and no one can know the Spiritual Sense except from the <term>science of correspondences: the understanding of how physical objects in the Word represent specific spiritual or mental realities</term>; for all the words are correspondences, and not one word is empty. The science of correspondences teaches what the "White Horse" signifies, what "He who sat upon it," what the "Eyes like a flame of fire," what the "Diadems upon the head," what the "Garment dipped in blood," what the "White fine linen" with which those of His army in heaven were clothed, what the "Angel standing in the Sun," what the "Great supper" to which they should come and be gathered, as well as the "Flesh of kings and captains" and many others, which they were to eat. However, what each of these means in the Spiritual Sense has been explained in *THE APOCALYPSE REVEALED* from numbers 820 to 838, and also in the small work *ON THE WHITE HORSE*; therefore, a further explanation of them here will be bypassed. It is shown there that the Lord is described there in respect to the Word, and that by His "Eyes like a flame of fire" is meant the Divine Wisdom of His Divine Love; and by the "Diadems upon the head," and by the "Name which no one knows but Himself," are meant the Divine Truths of the Word from Him; and that no one sees what the Word is like in the spiritual sense except the Lord, and those to whom He reveals it; also, that by the "Garment dipped in blood" is meant the natural sense of the Word, which is the sense of its letter, to which violence has been done <note>original: "violentia illata est" – meaning the literal meaning has been misinterpreted or corrupted by those who lack spiritual insight</note>. That it is the Word which is described in this way is clearly evident, for it is said, "HIS NAME IS CALLED THE WORD OF GOD"; that it is the Lord who is meant is also clearly evident, for it is said that the Name of the one sitting upon the White Horse was "KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS," just as in Apocalypse XVII: 14, where it is said, *And the Lamb shall overcome them, because He is LORD OF LORDS AND KING OF KINGS.* That the spiritual sense of the Word is to be opened at the end of the Church is signified not only by what is said of the White Horse and the one sitting upon it, but also by the "Great supper," to which all are invited by the Angel standing in the Sun to come and eat the flesh of kings and captains, etc., by which is signified the appropriation <note>the taking into oneself</note> of all goods from the Lord. All the expressions there would be empty words, without life and spirit, unless the Spiritual Sense were within them, just as the soul is in the body.

197. In the Apocalypse, Chapter XXI, the New Jerusalem is described in this way: *That in it there was a luminary like a most precious stone, like a jasper stone, shining like crystal. That it had a Wall great and high, having twelve Gates, and...*

Since Jerusalem there signifies the Church, it follows that everything said of it as a City—its Gates, its Wall, the Foundations of the wall, as well as their measurements—contains a spiritual sense, because the things belonging to the Church are spiritual. It is enough to know from this that a spiritual sense is within every detail of its description, like the Soul is within the body. Without that sense, nothing of the Church would be understood in what is written there: such as that the City was made of pure gold, its gates of pearls, the wall of jasper, the foundations of the wall of precious stones; that the wall was 144 cubits (the measure of a man, that is, of an Angel); and that the City's length, breadth, and height were 12,000 furlongs, and so on. However, one who knows the spiritual sense through the <term>Science of Correspondences</term> <note>The study of how natural objects and descriptions represent specific spiritual concepts</note> understands these things; for instance, that the Wall and its Foundations signify the doctrinal teachings of that Church from the literal sense of the Word <note>The Bible</note>, and that the Numbers 12, 144, and 12,000 signify all its parts, or its truths and goods, in one comprehensive whole.

198. Where the Lord speaks before His Disciples concerning the "Consummation of the Age" <note>original: Consummatione sæculi; often translated as the "End of the World," but here referring to the end of a specific religious era</note>, which is the final time of the Church, He says at the end of the predictions regarding the successive changes in its state: *Immediately after the affliction of those days, the Sun shall be darkened, the Moon shall not give her light, and the Stars shall fall from Heaven, and the Powers of the heavens shall be shaken. And then shall appear the Sign of the Son of Man in Heaven, and then shall all the Tribes of the earth wail, and they shall see the Son of Man coming in the clouds of Heaven with power and great glory; and He shall send His Angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together His elect from the four winds, from one end of the Heavens to the other*, Matthew 24:29, 30, 31. In the spiritual sense, these words do not mean that the Sun and Moon would literally be darkened, that the Stars would fall from the sky, that a physical sign of the Lord would appear in the heavens, or that people would see Him in the physical clouds along with Angels blowing trumpets. Rather, through each individual word, spiritual things belonging to the Church are meant, concerning its state at its end. For in the spiritual sense:
* By the **Sun** which shall be darkened, love for the Lord is meant;
* By the **Moon** which shall not give her light, faith in Him is meant;
* By the **Stars** which shall fall from Heaven, the knowledge of what is true and good is meant;
* By the **Sign of the Son of Man in Heaven**, the appearance of Divine Truth in the Word from Him is meant;
* By the **Tribes of the earth** who shall wail, the lack of all truth which belongs to faith, and all good which belongs to love, is meant;
* By the **Coming of the Son of Man in the clouds of Heaven with power and glory**, the Lord's presence in the Word and revelation is meant—the **clouds of heaven** signify the literal sense of the Word, and **glory** signifies the spiritual sense of the Word;
* By the **Angels with a great sound of a trumpet**, Heaven is meant, from which comes Divine Truth;
* By **gathering the elect from the four winds from one end of the Heavens to the other**, a new Heaven and a new Church are meant, made of those who have faith in the Lord and live according to His commandments.

That the darkening of the sun and moon and the falling of stars to the earth are not meant literally is clearly evident from the Prophets, in whose writings similar things are said about the state of the Church when the Lord was about to come into the World. For example, in Isaiah: *Behold, the day of Jehovah comes, cruel, and with the heat of anger; the Stars of the heavens and their Constellations shall not give their light; the Sun shall be darkened in its rising, and the Moon shall not shine*—

...shall cause his light to shine; I will punish the world for its evil <note>Isaiah 13:10-11. The OCR "XXIV" appears to be a misprint in the original text or transcription for Chapter 13</note>. In Joel:

By the "Day of Jehovah" is understood the coming of the Lord, which occurred when there was no longer any remaining good of love or truth of faith in the Church, nor any knowledge of the Lord; therefore it is called a "Day of darkness and gloom."

199. That the Lord, while He was in the world, spoke through <term>Correspondences</term> <note>the systematic relationship between natural things in this world and spiritual realities in the next</note>—thus speaking spiritually even while using natural terms—can be established from His parables. In every single word of these parables, there is an indwelling spiritual sense. Let the Parable of the Ten Virgins serve as an example; He said:
> "The Kingdom of Heaven is like ten virgins, who, taking their lamps, went out to meet the Bridegroom. Five of them were wise, and five were foolish. Those who were foolish, taking their lamps, took no oil; but the wise took oil in their lamps. While the bridegroom delayed, they all grew drowsy and slept. But at midnight a cry was made: 'Behold, the bridegroom comes; go out to meet him!' Then all those virgins awoke and trimmed their lamps. But the foolish said to the wise, 'Give us some of your oil, for our lamps are going out.' But the wise answered, saying, 'No, lest there be not enough for us and you; go rather to those who sell, and buy for yourselves.' But while they went to buy, the bridegroom came, and those who were ready entered with him to the wedding; and the door was shut. At last the remaining virgins also came, saying, 'Lord, Lord, open to us!' But he answering said, 'Truly I say to you, I do not know you,'" Matthew 25:1 to 12.
No one sees that there is a spiritual sense—and thus a Divine Holiness—in every detail of this story unless they know that such a sense exists and what its nature is. In the spiritual sense, the "Kingdom of Heaven" means Heaven and the Church; the "Bridegroom" means the Lord; the "Wedding" means the marriage of the Lord with people through the good of love and the truth of faith; "Virgins" mean those who belong to the Church; "Ten" means all; "Five" means some part; "Lamps" mean the things belonging to faith; "Oil" means the things belonging to the good of love; "Sleeping and Waking" mean a person's life in the world (which is natural) and their life after death (which is spiritual); "Buying" means to acquire for oneself; "Going to those who sell and buying oil" means to try to acquire the good of love from others after death. Because this can no longer be acquired at that time, even though they came to the door where the wedding was with their lamps and the oil they had bought, the Bridegroom still said to them, "I do not know you." The reason is that a person remains after their life in the world exactly as they had lived in the world. From this it is clear that the Lord spoke through pure correspondences, and did so because He spoke from the Divinity that was within Him and was His own. Because "Virgins" signify those who are of the Church, the "Virgin and Daughter of Zion, of Jerusalem, of Judah, and of Israel" is mentioned so often in the Prophetic Word. And because "Oil" signifies the good of love, all the holy things of the Church were anointed with oil. It is the same in the rest of the parables and in all the words the Lord spoke; this is why the Lord says that His words "are spirit and are life," John 6:63.

### 200. III. THAT IT IS FROM THE SPIRITUAL SENSE THAT THE WORD IS DIVINELY INSPIRED, AND HOLY IN EVERY EXPRESSION.

It is said in the Church that the Word is Holy, and this is because Jehovah the Lord spoke it. However, because its holiness is not apparent in the literal sense alone, anyone who once begins to doubt its holiness for that reason will later, when reading the Word, find many things there to confirm their doubt. For such a person says to themselves, "Is this holy? Is this divine?" Therefore, lest such a thought should flow into many minds and later grow strong—leading to the Word being rejected as a worthless piece of writing, and thereby destroying the connection between the Lord and that person—it has pleased the Lord to now reveal its spiritual sense. This is done so that it may be known exactly where the Divine Holiness lies hidden within it. Let examples illustrate this: in the Word, the text deals now with Egypt, now with Assyria <note>original: Aschure</note>, now with Edom, Moab, the sons of Ammon, the Philistines, Tyre, and Sidon...

Similarly, when he sees in the Word that gardens, groves, and forests are named so often, along with their trees, such as the olive, vine, cedar, poplar, and oak; and that so often the lamb, sheep, goat, calf, and ox are mentioned; and also mountains, hills, and valleys, and therein springs, rivers, waters, and many similar things; he who knows nothing of the spiritual sense of the Word cannot believe otherwise than that only those literal things are meant. For he does not know that by a garden, grove, and forest are understood wisdom, intelligence, and knowledge; that by the olive, vine, cedar, poplar, and oak are understood the good and truth of the church—celestial, spiritual, rational, natural, and sensual; that by the lamb, sheep, goat, calf, and ox are understood innocence, charity, and natural affection; that by mountains, hills, and valleys are understood the higher, lower, and lowest things of the church. Likewise, that by Egypt is signified the scientific <term>scientificum</term> <note>refers to the storehouse of factual knowledge in the natural memory</note>, by Assyria <note>original: "Afchurem"</note> the rational, by Edom the natural, by Moab the adulteration of good, by the children of Ammon the adulteration of truth, by the Philistines faith without charity, by Tyre and Sidon the knowledges of good and truth, and by Gog external worship without internal. In general, by JACOB in the Word is understood the natural Church, by ISRAEL the spiritual Church, and by JUDAH the celestial Church. When a person knows these things, then he can reflect that the Word deals only with heavenly things, and that those worldly things are merely the subjects in which they reside. But let an example from the Word also illustrate this; it is read in Isaiah:

> "*In that day there shall be a path from Egypt to Assyria, that Assyria may come into Egypt, and Egypt into Assyria, and the Egyptians shall serve with Assyria: in that day Israel shall be a third to Egypt and Assyria, a blessing in the midst of the land: whom Jehovah of Hosts shall bless, saying, blessed be my people Egypt, and the work of my hands Assyria; and my blessing Israel*," Chapter XIX: 23, 24, 25.

By these things in the spiritual sense it is understood that at the time of the Lord’s Advent, the Scientific, the Rational, and the Spiritual will make one, and that then the Scientific will serve the Rational, and both will serve the Spiritual; for, as was said, by Egypt is signified the scientific, by Assyria the rational, and by Israel the spiritual: by the "day" named twice is understood the First and Second advent of the Lord.

## 201. IV. THAT THE SPIRITUAL SENSE OF THE WORD HAS HITHERTO BEEN UNKNOWN.

That each and every thing in Nature corresponds to spiritual things, and likewise each and every thing in the human body, has been shown in the work *ON HEAVEN AND HELL*, numbers 87 to 105. But what <term>CORRESPONDENCE</term> <note>the systematic relationship between natural effects and spiritual causes</note> is, has hitherto been unknown; yet in the most ancient times it was very well known. For to those who lived then, the Science of Correspondences was the "science of sciences," and so universal that all their scrolls and books were written through correspondences. The Book of Job, which is a book of the Ancient Church, is full of correspondences. The hieroglyphics of the Egyptians, and also the fables of the most ancient people, were nothing else. All the Ancient Churches were representative churches of spiritual things; their rites, and also the statutes according to which their worship was established, consisted of pure correspondences. Likewise all things of the church among the children of Israel; the burnt offerings, sacrifices, grain offerings, and drink offerings were correspondences in every detail; likewise the Tabernacle with everything in it; then also their feasts, such as the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Tabernacles, and the Feast of First-fruits; also the priesthood of Aaron and the Levites, as well as their garments of holiness. But what the spiritual things were to which these various things corresponded has been shown in the *HEAVENLY SECRETS* <note>original: "Arcanis Coelestibus"</note> published in London; besides these, also all the statutes and judgments that concerned their worship and life were correspondences. ...therefore the Word was written through mere Correspondences <term>Correspondentia</term> <note>Swedenborg’s central concept that every natural object reflects a specific spiritual reality</note>; for this reason the Lord, because He spoke from the Divine, spoke through Correspondences; for that which is from the Divine, when it falls into Nature, falls into such things as correspond to Divine things, and which then hide in their bosom those Divine things called *Celestial and Spiritual*.

202. I have been instructed that the men of the Most Ancient Church <note>original: *Antiquissimæ Ecclesiæ*; Swedenborg refers here to the era of humanity before the biblical Flood</note>, which existed before the Flood, were of such a celestial character that they spoke with the Angels of Heaven, and that they were able to speak with them through Correspondences; from this, the state of their wisdom became such that whatever they saw on Earth, they thought about not only naturally, but also simultaneously spiritually, thus in conjunction with the Angels of Heaven. Furthermore, I have been instructed that Enoch <note>original: *CANOCH*</note>, who is mentioned in *Genesis Chapter V: 21 to 24*, with his companions, collected Correspondences from the lips of those people and propagated the Science <term>Scientia</term> <note>Here meaning a structured system of knowledge</note> of them to posterity; from this it came about that the Science of Correspondences was not only known but also cultivated in many Kingdoms of Asia, especially in the Land of *Canaan, Egypt, Assyria, Chaldea, Syria, Arabia, in Tyre, Sidon, and Nineveh*, and that from there it was translated into *Greece*, but there it was turned into *Fables* <note>original: *Fabulosa*; referring to Greek mythology</note>, as can be established from the writings of the *Most Ancient* authors there.

203. So that it may be seen that the Science of *Correspondences* was long preserved among the Nations in Asia (though among those who were called *Diviners and Wise Men*, and by some, *Magi*), I wish to bring forward One Example from *1 Samuel Chapters V & VI*. There it is recorded that the *Ark*, in which were the two Tables upon which the *Decalogue* <note>The Ten Commandments</note> was inscribed, was captured by the *Philistines* and placed in the Temple of *Dagon* in *Ashdod*, and that *Dagon* fell to the ground before it, and afterward his head with the palms of his hands lay severed from the body upon the threshold of the Temple; and that the people of *Ashdod and Ekron* were smitten with *hemorrhoids* <note>original: *hæmorrhoidibus*; likely referring to tumors or sores</note> by the thousands because of the *Ark*, and that their land was devastated by *mice*. Because of this, the *Philistines* called together their *Lords and Diviners*, and to prevent their destruction, they concluded that they should make five *Hemorrhoids* and five *Mice* out of gold, and a new *Cart*, and place the *Ark* upon it, and beside it the *hemorrhoids* and *mice* of gold. Then, by means of two *Cows* which lowed on the way before the *Cart*, they would send the *Ark* back to the *Children of Israel*, by whom the *Cows and the Cart* were sacrificed, and thus the *God of Israel* was propitiated. That all these things devised by the *Diviners of the Philistines* were *Correspondences* is evident from their significance, which is this: the *Philistines* themselves signified those who are in faith separated from charity; *Dagon* represented that religious system; the *Hemorrhoids* with which they were smitten signified natural loves, which are unclean when separated from spiritual love; and the *Mice* signified the devastation of the Church through the falsification of truth; the new *Cart* signified natural *Doctrine of the Church* (for a *Chariot* in the Word signifies doctrine from spiritual truths); the *Cows* signified good natural Affections; the *hemorrhoids* made of gold signified natural loves purified and made good; the *Mice* of gold signified the devastation of the Church removed through good (for *Gold* in the Word signifies good); the lowing of the *Cows* on the way signified the difficult conversion of the lusts of the natural man's evil into good affections; and that the *Cows with the Cart* were offered as a burnt offering signified that thus the *God of Israel* was propitiated. All these things, which the *Philistines* did at the persuasion of their Diviners, were *Correspondences*; from which it is clear that this Science was long preserved among the nations.

204. Since the *Representative Rites of the Church*, which were *Correspondences*, began in the course of time to be turned into *Idolatrous* and also into *Magical* things, then that Science, by the Divine Providence of the Lord, was gradually lost, and among the *Israelite and Jewish* Nation it was completely obliterated. The worship of this Nation did indeed consist of mere Correspondences, and was therefore representative of Celestial things, but even so they did not know what anything signified; for they were entirely *Natural* men, and therefore they neither wished to know nor were able to know anything about Spiritual and Celestial things.

...consequently, they knew nothing about Correspondences <term>Correspondentia</term> <note>The relationship between a natural object and its spiritual cause</note>, for Correspondences are Representations of Spiritual and Celestial things in Natural things.

205. The fact that the Idolatries of the Nations in ancient times drew their origin from the science of Correspondences was because all things that appear on Earth correspond; thus, not only Trees, but also Beasts and Birds of every kind, as well as Fish and all other things. The Ancients, who possessed the science of Correspondences, made for themselves Images which corresponded to Celestial things, and they delighted in them because they signified things belonging to Heaven and the Church. For this reason, they placed them not only in their Temples but also in their Houses—not for the sake of worship, but to remember the celestial things they signified. 

Hence in Egypt and elsewhere, there were images of Calves, Oxen, and Serpents, as well as Children, Old Men, and Virgins. This was because Calves and Oxen signified the affections and powers of the natural man; Serpents signified the prudence and also the craftiness of the sensual man; Children signified innocence and charity; Old Men signified wisdom; and Virgins signified the affections for truth; and so forth. 

Posterity, when the science of Correspondences was obliterated, began to worship the Images and Idols set up by the Ancients as Holy, and eventually as Deities, because they were in and near the Temples. For the same reason, the Ancients held Worship in Gardens and Groves according to the species of Trees; and also upon Mountains and Hills. This was because Gardens and Groves signified wisdom and intelligence, and every specific Tree signified something of them—for instance, the Olive signified the good of love, the Vine signified truth from that good, and the Cedar signified rational good and truth. A Mountain signified the highest Heaven, and a Hill the heaven below it. 

That the science of Correspondences remained among many Eastern nations until the Coming of the Lord <note>original: *Adventum Domini*</note> can be seen from the Wise Men from the East <note>The Magi</note> who came to the Lord when He was born; for this reason, a Star went before them, and they brought with them gifts: Gold, Frankincense, and Myrrh (*Matthew 2:1, 2, 9, 10, 11*). The Star that went before them signified knowledge from Heaven; Gold signified celestial good; Frankincense signified spiritual good; and Myrrh signified natural good. From these three, all Worship is composed. 

Nevertheless, the Science of Correspondences was absolutely non-existent among the Israelite and Jewish Nation, even though all their Worship, all the Statutes and Judgments given to them through Moses, and everything in the Word were pure Correspondences. The reason was that they were idolaters at heart, and were such that they did not even want to know that any part of their Worship signified anything Celestial or Spiritual; for they believed that all those things were Holy in themselves. Therefore, if Celestial and Spiritual things had been revealed to them, they would not only have rejected them but would have profaned <note>To treat something sacred with irreverence or to use spiritual truth for selfish ends</note> them. For this reason, Heaven was so closed to them that they hardly knew that eternal Life existed. That this was the case is clearly evident from the fact that they did not recognize the Lord, even though the entire Sacred Scripture prophesied concerning Him and foretold His Coming. They rejected Him for that sole reason: because He taught them about a heavenly Kingdom and not about an earthly Kingdom; for they wanted a Messiah who would exalt them above all Nations in the entire World, and not a Messiah who would look to their eternal salvation.

206. The reason why the Science of Correspondences, through which the spiritual Sense of the Word is given, was not revealed after those times, was because the Christians in the Primitive Church <note>The earliest era of Christianity following the Apostles</note> were so very simple that it could not have been revealed to them; for if it had been revealed, it would have been of no use to them, nor would it have been understood. 

After their times, darkness rose over the entire Christian World, first through the heresies of many spread abroad, and soon after through the consultations and decrees of the COUNCIL OF NICAEA <note>The 325 AD council that established the Nicene Creed and defined the nature of the Trinity</note> concerning three Divine Persons from eternity, and concerning the Person of Christ as the Son of Mary, and not as the Son of Jehovah God. From this sprang the modern Faith of justification, in which three Gods are approached in their order, and upon which faith everything in the modern Church depends, just as the members of a body depend on their Head. Because they have applied everything in the Word to confirm this erroneous Faith, the spiritual Sense could not be revealed; for if it had been revealed, they would have applied that Sense to it as well, and by that very act [would have profaned] the Holy [Word]...

207. The reason why the Science of Correspondences <term>Correspondentia</term> <note>The system of relationships between the spiritual and natural worlds</note>, through which the spiritual sense is given, has been revealed today, is because the Divine Truths of the Church are now coming to light. It is from these truths that the spiritual sense of the Word consists; and while these truths are present in a person, the literal sense of the Word cannot be perverted. For the literal sense of the Word can be turned this way and that; but if it is turned toward what is False, its internal Holiness perishes, and with it the external holiness. However, if it is turned toward what is True, that holiness remains. But more will be said on these matters in what follows. 

That the spiritual sense would be opened today is signified by John seeing **Heaven opened**, and then a **White Horse**; and also by him seeing and hearing that an **Angel standing in the Sun** called everyone to a **great supper**, as described in the Book of Revelation <note>original: "Apocalypfi"</note> Chapter 19:11 to 18. That this sense would not be acknowledged for a long time, however, is signified by the **Beast** and the **Kings of the Earth**, who were to make war with Him that sat upon the White Horse (Revelation 19:19); as also by the **Dragon**, which persecuted the **Woman** who gave birth to the Son, even into the wilderness, and there cast out water from his mouth like a flood to drown her (Revelation 12:13 to 17).

208. V. **THAT THE SPIRITUAL SENSE OF THE WORD WILL NOT BE GIVEN TO ANYONE HEREAFTER, EXCEPT ONE WHO IS IN GENUINE TRUTHS FROM THE LORD:** The reason is that no one can see the spiritual sense except from the Lord alone, and unless they are in Divine truths from the Lord. For the spiritual sense of the Word deals solely with the Lord and His Kingdom, and that sense is what His Angels in Heaven are in, for His Divine Truth is there. A person can violate this if they possess the Science of Correspondences and wish to explore the spiritual sense of the Word from their own intelligence <note>original: "ex propria intelligentia"</note>. For from a few known Correspondences, they might pervert that sense and even use it to confirm what is False. This would be to do violence to Divine Truth, and thus also to Heaven, where that truth dwells. Therefore, if anyone wishes to open that sense from themselves and not from the Lord, Heaven is closed; and when it is closed, the person either sees nothing of the truth or becomes spiritually insane. 

The reason is also that the Lord teaches everyone through the Word, and He teaches from those concepts <term>cognitionibus</term> which a person already has, and does not immediately pour in new ones. Therefore, unless a person is in Divine truths—or if they are in only a few truths and simultaneously in falsehoods—they can falsify truths using those falsehoods, as is done by every heretic regarding the literal sense of the Word itself. So that no one may enter into the spiritual sense and pervert the genuine Truth which belongs to that sense, guards have been placed by the Lord, which in the Word are understood by **Cherubim**. <note>In Swedenborg's theology, Cherubim represent the protection of the Word's internal holiness from being damaged by human error.</note>

209. VI. **WONDERS CONCERNING THE WORD FROM ITS SPIRITUAL SENSE.** In the natural world, no wonders <term>Mirabilia</term> <note>Marvels or miraculous phenomena</note> exist from the Word because the spiritual sense does not appear there, nor is it received by man internally as it is in itself. But in the spiritual world, wonders from the Word do appear, because everyone there is spiritual, and spiritual things affect a spiritual person just as natural things affect a natural person. The wonders that exist from the Word in the spiritual world are many, of which I will mention a few here:

The Word itself, kept in the inner sanctuaries <note>original: "adytis"</note> of the Temples there, shines before the eyes of the Angels like a great Star, and sometimes like a Sun; and from the radiance around it, beautiful rainbows <note>original: "Irides"</note> appear. This happens as soon as the sanctuary is opened. That every single truth of the Word shines was made clear to me by this: that when any verse from the Word is written out on paper, and the paper is thrown into the air, the paper itself shines in the same shape into which it was cut. Therefore, Spirits can produce various shining forms by means of the Word, even the forms of birds and fish. 

Also—and this is even more wonderful—when someone rubs their face, hands, or the clothes they are wearing with the open Word, applying the writing to them, the face, hands, and clothes themselves shine as if the person were standing in a star, surrounded by its light. This I have seen very often and marveled at. From this, it was clear to me why the face of Moses shone when he brought down the Tables of the Covenant from Mount Sinai.

Beyond those, many other Wonders <term>Mirabilia</term> <note>Swedenborg uses this term to describe the objective, supernatural phenomena he witnessed in the spiritual world</note> occur there which are from the Word. For instance, if someone who is in false beliefs looks at the Word as it lies in a holy place, a darkness arises before his eyes, and consequently the Word appears black to him, and sometimes as if covered in soot. If that same person touches the Word, an explosion occurs with a loud crash, and he is thrown into a corner of the room, where he lies as if dead for about an hour. If something from the Word is copied onto paper by someone who is in false beliefs, and that paper is thrown toward Heaven, then a similar explosion occurs in the air between his eye and Heaven, and the paper is torn into shreds and vanishes. The same thing happens if that paper is thrown toward a corner where someone else is standing nearby; I have seen this quite often. From this it was clear to me that those who are in false doctrines have no communication with Heaven through the Word, but that their reading of it flows away on the path and perishes like gunpowder <note>original: "pulvis pyrius"</note> wrapped in paper when it is lit and thrown into the air. The opposite happens with those who are in the truths of doctrine from the Lord through the Word; their reading of the Word penetrates all the way into Heaven and effects a conjunction with the angels there. The angels themselves, when they descend from Heaven to perform some duty below, appear surrounded by small stars, especially around the head, which is a sign that Divine truths from the Word are within them.

Furthermore, in the spiritual world there are families just as on earth, but each and every thing there is of spiritual origin. Thus, gold and silver also exist there, as do precious stones of every kind, and the spiritual origin of these is the literal sense of the Word. This is why, in the Book of Revelation, the foundations of the wall of the New Jerusalem are described by twelve precious stones; the reason is that the foundations of its wall signify the doctrines of the New Church derived from the literal sense of the Word. This is also why there were twelve precious stones in Aaron's Ephod <note>A ceremonial vestment worn by the High Priest of Israel</note>, called the *Urim* and *Thummim* <note>original Hebrew: "Lights and Perfections"</note>, and why answers from Heaven were given through them. Besides these, there are still more Wonders from the Word concerning the power of Truth there, which is so immense that if it were described, it would exceed all belief. For its power is such that it can overturn mountains and hills there, move them to a great distance, and cast them into the sea, among other things; in short, the Power of the Lord from the Word is infinite.

# III.

## *That the Literal Sense of the Word is the Basis, Container, and Support of its Spiritual and Celestial Sense.*

210. In every Divine thing there is a First, a Middle, and a Last <term>Ultimum</term>, and the First goes through the Middle to the Last, and thus it exists and subsists; therefore, the Last is the BASIS. Furthermore, the First is in the Middle, and through the Middle in the Last; thus, the Last is the CONTAINER <term>Continens</term>; and because the Last is the Container and the Basis, it is also the SUPPORT <term>Firmamentum</term>. It is understood by the learned that these three can be called End, Cause, and Effect; also Being <term>Esse</term>, Becoming <term>Fieri</term>, and Existing <term>Existere</term>; and that the End is Being, the Cause is Becoming, and the Effect is Existing. Consequently, in every complete thing, there is a Trinity, which is called First, Middle, and Last, as well as End, Cause, and Effect. When these things are understood, it is also understood that every Divine Work is complete and perfect in its Last stage; and also that in the Last, everything is present, because the prior things are contained within it simultaneously.

211. It is for this reason that by the number THREE in the spiritual sense of the Word, what is complete and perfect is understood, as well as all things together. And because these things are signified by that number, it is used in the Word as often as such a thing is designated; as in these instances: *That Isaiah went naked and barefoot* THREE YEARS (Isaiah 20:3). *That Jehovah called Samuel* THREE TIMES, *and that Samuel ran to Eli* THREE TIMES, *and that Eli understood on the* THIRD TIME (1 Samuel 3:1 to 8). *That Jonathan said to David that he should hide himself...*

212. There are THREE HEAVENS: the HIGHEST, the MIDDLE, and the LOWEST. The HIGHEST HEAVEN makes up the Lord’s Celestial Kingdom, the MIDDLE HEAVEN makes up His Spiritual Kingdom, and the LOWEST HEAVEN makes up His Natural Kingdom. Just as there are three heavens, so also there are THREE SENSES OF THE WORD: the CELESTIAL, the SPIRITUAL, and the NATURAL; with these also coincide those things said above in number 210, namely that the First is in the Middle, and through the Middle in the Last, exactly like the end in the cause, and through the cause in the effect. From this it is clear what the WORD is: namely, that in the <term>literal sense</term> <note>original: "sensus literae"</note>, which is natural, there is an interior sense which is spiritual, and in this an inmost which is celestial; and thus that the lowest sense, which is natural and called the <term>literal sense</term>, is the container of the two interior senses, and thus their basis and support.

213. From these things it follows that the <term>Word</term> without its <term>literal sense</term> would be like a palace without a foundation—that is, like a palace in the air and not upon the earth, which would be merely its shadow that would vanish away. Also, that the <term>Word</term> without its <term>literal sense</term> would be like a temple in which there are many holy things, and in its center a sanctuary <note>original: "Adytum", referring to the Holy of Holies or the most sacred inner chamber of a temple.</note>, but without a roof and walls which are its containers; if these were missing or taken away, its holy things would be plundered by thieves, violated by the beasts of the earth and the birds of heaven, and thus scattered. Similarly, it would be like the <term>Tabernacle</term> of the children of <term>Israel</term> in the desert, in the inmost of which was the Ark of the Covenant, and in its middle the golden lampstand, the golden altar upon which was the incense, and the table upon which was the showbread, but without its outermost parts, which were the curtains, veils, and columns. Indeed, the <term>Word</term> without its <term>literal sense</term> would be like a human body without its coverings, which are called the skin, and without its supports, which are called the bones; without these, all its interior parts would flow away. And it would be like the heart and lungs in the chest without their covering, which is called the pleura, and their supports, which are called the ribs. Or like the brain without its coverings, which are called the dura and pia mater <note>These are the protective membranes surrounding the brain.</note>, and without its general covering, container, and support, which is called the skull. It would be the same with the <term>Word</term> without its <term>literal sense</term>; wherefore it is said in <term>Isaiah</term>, *That Jehovah shall create over all the glory a covering*, Chapter 4:5.

# IV.

## That Divine Truth in the literal sense of the Word is in its Fullness, in its Holiness, and in its Power.

214. That the <term>Word</term> in its <term>literal sense</term> is in its fullness, in its holiness, and in its power, is because the two prior or interior senses, which are called the Spiritual and the Celestial, are in the [natural] sense...
