...in the natural degree, which is the **Sense of the letter**, they exist together, as was stated above in numbers 210 and 212; but how they exist together will be explained further. In both Heaven and the World, there exists **Successive Order** <term>Successive Order: a vertical arrangement where things follow one after another, like levels in a building.</term> and **Simultaneous Order** <term>Simultaneous Order: a horizontal arrangement where things exist at the same time, layered from a center outward.</term>. In Successive Order, one thing succeeds and follows after another, from the highest down to the lowest; but in Simultaneous Order, things are arranged side-by-side, from the innermost to the outermost. Successive Order is like a Column with steps from top to bottom; whereas Simultaneous Order is like a cohesive structure with concentric circles <note>original: "peripheriis", referring to the outer regions or circumferences of a circle.</note> from the Center out to the furthest surface. 

It will now be explained how Successive Order becomes Simultaneous Order in the Final degree; it happens in this way: the highest parts of the Successive Order become the innermost parts of the Simultaneous Order, and the lowest parts of the Successive Order become the outermost parts of the Simultaneous Order. It is, by comparison, like a column of steps subsiding into a cohesive body on a flat plane. Thus, the Simultaneous is formed from the Successive, and this occurs in each and every thing of the natural world, and in each and every thing of the spiritual world; for everywhere there is a First, a Middle, and a Last, and the First tends through the Middle toward its Last. But it must be well understood that there are degrees of purity according to which both types of Order are formed. 

Now to the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scripture or the Bible.</note>: the Celestial, the Spiritual, and the Natural proceed from the Lord in Successive Order, and in the Final degree <note>original: "Ultimo", referring to the literal text of the Bible.</note> they exist in Simultaneous Order; thus, the celestial and spiritual senses of the Word are now present within its natural sense simultaneously. When this is understood, it can be seen how the natural sense of the Word is the container, the basis, and the support of its spiritual and celestial senses; and also how Divine Good and Divine Truth in the sense of the letter of the Word are in their fullness, in their holiness, and in their power. From these things it can be established that the Word becomes truly the Word in its sense of the letter, for within this sense there is spirit and life. This is what the Lord says:

> *The words that I speak to you are Spirit and Life,*

John 6:63; for the Lord spoke His words in the natural sense. The celestial and spiritual senses are not the Word without the natural sense, for they would be like spirit and life without a body; and they are, as was said before in number 213, like a Palace that has no foundation.

215. The truths of the sense of the letter of the Word are, in part, not "naked truths" but are **appearances of truth** <term>Appearances of Truth: spiritual realities described in human or physical terms so that they can be understood by people on earth.</term>, acting like similarities and comparisons taken from things found in nature; thus, they are accommodated and adapted to the grasp of the simple-minded and also of children. However, because they are at the same time **Correspondences** <term>Correspondences: the systematic relationship between a natural object and the spiritual reality it represents.</term>, they are the receptacles and dwellings of genuine truth. They are the vessels that contain it, just as a crystal Cup contains noble Wine, or a silver Platter contains nourishing food; and just as Clothes provide a covering, like swaddling clothes for an infant or beautiful garments for a young woman. They are also like the scientific knowledge of the natural man, which contains within itself the perceptions and affections of spiritual truth. The "naked truths" themselves—which are enclosed, contained, clothed, and encompassed—exist in the spiritual sense of the Word, while the "naked goods" <note>In this theology, "Good" refers to the aspect of love or the will, while "Truth" refers to the aspect of wisdom or the intellect.</note> exist in its celestial sense. But let this be illustrated from the Word:

> *Jesus said, Woe to you Scribes and Pharisees, for you clean the outside of the cup and the platter, but the insides are full of greed and excess; blind Pharisee, clean first the inside of the cup and the platter, so that the outside may also be clean,*

Matthew 23:25-26. Here the Lord spoke through similarities and comparisons which are simultaneously correspondences. He mentioned the "cup" and the "platter." By "Cup" is not only understood but also signified the Truth of the Word, for by the cup is understood Wine, and by wine is signified truth. By the "Platter," however, food is understood, and by food is signified good. Therefore, to "clean the inside of the cup and the platter" signifies to purify the interiors of the mind (which belong to the will and thought) by means of the Word. By the phrase "so that the outside may be clean" is signified that the exteriors (which are works and speech) are thus purified, for these derive their essence from the interiors. Furthermore:

> *Jesus said, there was a certain rich man who was clothed in purple and fine linen, and feasted sumptuously every day; and there was a certain poor man named Lazarus, who was cast at his gateway, full of sores,*

Luke 16:19-20. Here also the Lord spoke through similarities and comparisons which were correspondences, and conti- <note>The text cuts off mid-word ("continuavit" or similar) at the end of the page.</note>

# I. THAT THE TRUTHS OF THE LITERAL SENSE OF THE WORD ARE UNDERSTOOD BY THE PRECIOUS STONES, FROM WHICH THE FOUNDATIONS OF THE NEW JERUSALEM CONSISTED, IN REVELATION CHAPTER 21:17 TO 21.

217. That the precious stones from which the foundations of the wall around the city of the **New Jerusalem** <term>New Jerusalem: a symbolic city representing a new era of the Church and its teachings.</term> are said to be constructed signify the Truths of the doctrine of the New Church follows from this: because by the New Jerusalem is understood the New Church in regard to its doctrine from **the Word**, therefore by its Wall and the foundations of the wall, nothing else can be understood than the external of **the Word**, which is its literal sense; for it is from this that doctrine comes, and through doctrine the Church, and it is like a Wall with foundations that encloses and protects a City. ## 218. II. THAT THE GOODS AND TRUTHS OF THE WORD IN ITS LITERAL SENSE ARE SIGNIFIED BY THE URIM AND THUMMIM ON THE EPHOD OF AARON.

The Urim and Thummim <note>The Urim ("lights") and Thummim ("perfections") were objects used by the High Priest to determine God's will.</note> were upon the Ephod of Aaron. Through Aaron's priesthood, the Lord was represented in terms of Divine Good and the work of salvation; through his garments of priesthood or holiness, Divine Truths from the Lord were represented. Through the Ephod <note>An ornate vest-like garment worn by the High Priest.</note>, Divine Truth in its ultimate <term>ultimate: the most external or physical level of reality; the "bottom floor" of spiritual structure.</term> was represented, and thus the Word in its literal sense, for this is Divine Truth in its final form. Consequently, through the twelve precious stones—bearing the names of the twelve tribes of Israel, which were the Urim and Thummim—Divine Truths derived from Divine Good were represented in their entire complex. Regarding these, we read in the books of Moses:

> "They shall make the Ephod of blue and purple, of scarlet double-dyed and fine-twined linen. Afterwards, they shall make the Breastplate of Judgment according to the workmanship of the Ephod, and you shall fill it with settings of stones; four rows of stones: a Ruby, a Topaz, and an Emerald shall be the first row; a Chrysoprase, a Sapphire, and a Diamond, the second row; a Lapis Lazuli, an Agate, and an Amethyst, the third row; a Beryl, a Sardius, and a Jasper, the fourth row. These stones shall be according to the names of the sons of Israel; like the engravings of a seal, they shall be according to his name for the twelve tribes. And Aaron shall carry the Urim and Thummim upon the Breastplate of Judgment; and let them be upon Aaron’s heart when he enters before Jehovah." (Exodus 28:6, 15–21, 30).

What was represented by Aaron’s garments—his Ephod, Robe, Tunic, Turban, and Belt—is explained in the HEAVENLY SECRETS <note>original: "Arcanis Cælestibus", Swedenborg's multi-volume commentary on Genesis and Exodus published in London.</note> published in London, specifically on that chapter. It is shown there that the Ephod represented Divine Truth in its ultimate; that the precious stones represented truths translucent from good; the twelve stones in four rows represented all those truths from firsts to lasts; the twelve tribes represented all things of the Church; the Breastplate represented Divine Truth from Divine Good in a universal sense; and the Urim and Thummim represented the brilliance of Divine Truth from Divine Good in the ultimates. For *Urim* means "shining fire" and *Thummim* means "brilliance" in the Angelic language, and "integrity" in the Hebrew language. Furthermore, it is shown that answers were given through variations of light, and simultaneously through a silent perception or a living voice, among many other things. From this it can be established that these stones also signified truths from good in the ultimate sense of the Word; nor are answers given from Heaven through any other means, because in that sense, the Divine proceeding is in its fullness.

## 219. III. THAT SIMILAR THINGS ARE SIGNIFIED BY THE PRECIOUS STONES IN THE GARDEN OF EDEN, WHERE THE KING OF TYRE IS SAID TO HAVE BEEN.

We read in Ezekiel: *King of Tyre, you who seal up your measurement, full of wisdom and perfect in beauty; you have been in Eden, the Garden of God; every precious stone was your covering: the Ruby, Topaz, and Diamond, the Beryl, Sardonyx, and Jasper, the Sapphire, Chrysoprase, and Emerald, and Gold.* (Ezekiel 28:12, 13). By "Tyre" in the Word is signified the Church in regard to the knowledges of good and truth; by "the King" is signified the Truth of the Church; by the "Garden of Eden" is signified wisdom and intelligence from the Word; by "precious stones" are signified truths translucent from good, such as those found in the literal sense of the Word. Because these stones signify such things, they are called his "covering." That the literal sense covers the interior things of the Word may be seen above in number 213.

church, which is why its form was shown by Jehovah <note>The Hebrew name for God, often translated as "LORD."</note> upon Mount Sinai; thus, through everything that was in that Tabernacle—which were the **Candlestick**, the **golden Altar for incense**, and the **Table** upon which was the **Bread of the Faces** <note>original: "Panes facierum"; commonly known as the Showbread.</note>—the holy things of Heaven and the Church were represented and signified. ## 221. V. LIKEWISE THROUGH THE EXTERNAL PARTS OF THE TEMPLE OF JERUSALEM.
The reason is that the Heaven and the Church were represented by the Temple just as they were by the Tabernacle; however, the Temple represented the Heaven in which spiritual angels dwell, whereas the Tabernacle represented the Heaven where celestial angels dwell. Spiritual angels are those who are in wisdom from the Word, while celestial angels are those who are in love from the Word. That the **Divine Human** <note>A central concept in Swedenborg’s theology: the Lord's glorified humanity which is one with the Divine.</note> of the Lord was signified by the Temple of Jerusalem in the highest sense, He Himself teaches in John: *Destroy this Temple, and in three days I will raise it up; He was speaking of the TEMPLE OF HIS BODY*, 2:19, 21. And where the Lord is understood, the Word is also understood, because He is the Word. Now, because the internal parts of Heaven and the Church (and thus also the Word) were represented by the interior of the Temple, therefore the external parts of Heaven and the Church (and thus the Word’s literal sense) were represented and signified by its exterior. Regarding the exterior of the Temple, we read: *That it was built of whole stone, not hewn, and of cedar within; and that all its walls within were carved with Cherubim, Palms, and openings of flowers; and that the floor was overlaid with gold*, 1 Kings 6:7, 29, 30. All of these signify the external things of the Word, which are the holy things of its literal sense.

## 222. VI. THAT THE WORD IN ITS GLORY WAS REPRESENTED IN THE LORD WHEN HE WAS TRANSFIGURED.
Regarding the Lord being transfigured <note>original: "transformatus"; the Transfiguration described in the Gospels.</note> before Peter, James, and John, we read: *That His face shone like the sun; His garments became like light: and that Moses and Elijah were seen talking with Him: and that a bright cloud covered the disciples: and that from the cloud a voice was heard, saying, This is my beloved Son, hear Him*, Matthew 17:1 to 5. I have been instructed that the Lord then represented the Word. By His **face**, which shone like the sun, was represented the Divine Good of His Divine Love; by His **garments**, which became like light, the Divine Truth of His Divine Wisdom; by **Moses and Elijah**, the Historical and Prophetic Word (by Moses, the Word written through him and the Historical Word in general, and by Elijah, the whole Prophetic Word); by the **bright cloud** that covered the disciples, the Word in its literal sense. For this reason, the voice was heard from the cloud saying, *This is my beloved Son, hear Him*. For all declarations and responses from Heaven never occur except through <term>ultimes: the outermost or most natural level of reality; here, the literal words of the Bible.</term>, such as those in the literal sense of the Word; for they occur in their fullness from the Lord.

### 223. VII. THAT THE POWER OF THE WORD IN ITS ULTIMATES WAS REPRESENTED BY THE NAZIRITES.

We read in the Book of Judges concerning Samson, that he was a Nazirite from his mother's womb, and that his power consisted in his hair. Indeed, the terms "Nazirite" and "Naziriteship" themselves signify hair. Samson himself revealed that his power resided in his hair when he said, *“A razor has not come upon my head, because I have been a Nazirite from my mother’s womb; if I am shaved, then my strength will leave me, and I shall become weak, and be like any other man,”* Judges 16:17. No one can know why the Naziriteship—which signifies hair—was instituted, or why Samson’s strength came from his hair, unless they understand what the "Head" signifies in the Word. The Head signifies the Intelligence that angels and men receive from the Lord through Divine Truth; consequently, the hair signifies intelligence in its <term>ultimates</term> <note>In this context, "ultimates" refers to the most external or literal level of something—the "base" that holds everything together.</note> or extremes, derived from Divine Truth. 

Because this was what hair signified, it was a statute for the Nazirites *“that they should not shave the hair of their head, because it is the Naziriteship of God upon their head,”* Numbers 6:1 to 21. For the same reason, it was decreed *“that the High Priest and his sons should not shave their heads, lest they die, and lest wrath come upon the whole house of Israel,”* Leviticus 10:6. Since hair was so holy because of this <term>correspondence</term> <note>The spiritual law that physical objects or actions represent specific spiritual realities.</note>, the **SON OF MAN**—who is the Lord in respect to the Word—is also described as having hair *“white like wool, as white as snow,”* Revelation 1:14. The **ANCIENT OF DAYS** <note>A title for God from the Book of Daniel, representing His eternal nature.</note> is described similarly in Daniel 7:9. 

Because hair signifies Truth in its ultimates—and thus the literal sense of the Word—those who despise the Word in the spiritual world become bald. Conversely, those who have held the Word in high esteem and regarded it as holy appear with beautiful hair. It was because of this correspondence that forty-two boys were torn apart by two female bears because they called Elisha “baldhead,” 2 Kings 2:23, 24. This occurred because Elisha represented the Church in respect to Doctrine from the Word, and bears signify the power of truth in its ultimates. The reason the power of Divine Truth, or the Word, resides in its literal sense is that the Word is there in its fullness, and because the angels of both of the Lord’s kingdoms and human beings are present within it simultaneously.

### 224. VIII. ON THE INEFFABLE POWER OF THE WORD.

Hardly anyone today knows that there is actual power within Truth. It is generally thought that Truth is merely a word spoken by someone in authority which must therefore be obeyed—as if Truth were only like breath from the mouth or sound in the ear. Yet, in reality, Truth and Good are the primary principles of everything in both worlds, the Spiritual and the Natural; they are the means through which the universe was created and through which the universe is preserved. They are also the means by which Man was made. Therefore, these two—Truth and Good—are the "all in all." 

That the universe was created through Divine Truth is stated clearly in John: *“In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God... all things were made through Him that were made.”* And *“The world was made through Him,”* Chapter 1:1, 3, 10. Also in David: *“By the Word of Jehovah the heavens were made,”* Psalm 33:6. In both instances, "the Word" means the Divine Truth. Since the universe was created through it, the universe is also preserved through it; for just as subsistence <note>Continuing to exist.</note> is perpetual existence, so preservation is perpetual creation. 

The reason Man was made through Divine Truth is that everything in a human being relates to the Understanding and the Will. The Understanding is the receptacle for Divine Truth, and the Will is the receptacle for Divine Good. Consequently, the human mind—which consists of these two principles—is nothing other than a form of Divine Truth and Divine Good, organized both spiritually and naturally. The human brain is that very form. And because the whole man depends on his mind, everything in his body is an appendage, set in motion and kept alive by these two principles. 

From this, it can now be seen why God came into the world as the Word and became Man. This was for the sake of Redemption. For at that time, God, through the Human—which was Divine Truth—clothed Himself in all power. He cast down the hells (which had grown up even to the heavens where the angels were), subjugated them, and brought them under His obedience. He did this not by a spoken word, but by the Divine Word, which is Divine...

Divine Truth; and afterward he opened a great Chasm between the Hells and the Heavens, which no one from Hell can cross; if they try, at the first step they are tortured, like a serpent placed on a plate of glowing iron, or on a heap of ants. The reason for this is that their will is rooted in evils and their understanding in falsities—entirely opposite to Divine Good and Divine Truth. Because a person consists entirely of these two principles of life, they are struck from head to heel by a sense of total, painful opposition. 

From this it is clear that the Power of Divine Truth is inexpressible. Since the Word, as found in the Christian Church, contains Divine Truth in three levels, it is evident that this is what is meant in the Gospel of John, Chapter 1:3, 10 <note>The passage in John identifies "The Word" (the Logos) as the creator of the world and the light of men.</note>. I could confirm that this Power is inexpressible with many firsthand accounts from the spiritual world; however, because they might exceed belief or seem incredible, I will refrain from listing them here, though you may see some examples mentioned earlier in number 209. From this, a **MEMORABLE NOTE** is given: that the Church, which exists in Divine Truths from the Lord, has power over the Hells. It is this Church of which the Lord spoke to Peter: *“Upon this Rock I will build my Church, and the gates of Hell shall not prevail against it”* (Matthew 16:18). The Lord said this after Peter confessed *“That Christ was the Son of the living God”* (verse 16). This Truth is what is meant by the "Rock" [Petra]; for everywhere in the Word, a Rock signifies the Lord in respect to Divine Truth.

## V.

->*That the Doctrine of the Church must be drawn from the Sense of the letter of the Word, and confirmed by it.*<-

225. In the preceding section, it was shown that the Word in the <term>Sense of the letter</term> <note>The literal, surface-level meaning of the Bible.</note> is in its fullness, its holiness, and its power. Since the Lord is the Word (the First and the Last, as He says in Revelation 1:17), it follows that the Lord is most present in that literal sense, and that from it He teaches and enlightens mankind. These points will be demonstrated in the following order:
I. *That the Word cannot be understood without Doctrine.* 
II. *That Doctrine must be drawn from the Sense of the letter of the Word.* 
III. *But that the Divine Truth which constitutes Doctrine appears only to those who are in enlightenment from the Lord.*

226. I. THE WORD CANNOT BE UNDERSTOOD WITHOUT DOCTRINE. This is because the Word, in its literal sense, consists of <term>Correspondences</term> <note>The symbolic relationship between physical things and spiritual realities.</note>. This is so that spiritual and heavenly things can be present within the text, with every single word acting as a container and support for them. For this reason, Divine Truths in the literal sense are rarely "naked" (plainly stated), but are usually clothed. These are called <term>Appearances of truth</term> <note>Statements that reflect how things "appear" to human perception rather than how they are in absolute reality (e.g., saying the sun "rises").</note>. Many of these are adapted to the understanding of simple people who do not lift their thoughts above what they see with their eyes. There are even things that appear to be contradictions, though when the Word is viewed in its spiritual light, no contradiction exists. Furthermore, in some places in the Prophets, there are lists of names of places and people from which no clear meaning can be drawn. Since the literal sense is structured this way, it is obvious that it cannot be understood without a system of interpretation, or "Doctrine." 

Let examples illustrate this: it is said *“That Jehovah repents”* (Exodus 32:12, 14; Jonah 3:9, 4:2), but it is also said *“That Jehovah does not repent”* (Numbers 23:19; 1 Samuel 15:29). Without Doctrine, these cannot be reconciled. It is said that *“Jehovah visits the iniquity of the fathers upon the children to the third and fourth generation”* (Numbers 14:18), but it is also said *“That the father shall not die for...”*

The son [shall not die] for the father, nor the father for the son, but everyone in his own sin, *Deuteronomy* 24:16; these statements do not disagree but agree when viewed through Doctrine. Jesus says, *Ask, and it shall be given to you; seek, and you shall find; and to him who knocks, it shall be opened, Matthew* 7:7, 8; 21:21, 22. Without Doctrine, it might be believed that everyone will receive whatever they ask for; but from Doctrine it is known that whatever a person asks from the Lord, that is given. This the Lord also teaches: *If you abide in Me, and my words abide in you, ask whatever you will, and it shall be done for you, John* 15:7. The Lord says, *Blessed are the poor, for theirs is the Kingdom of God, Luke* 6:20; without Doctrine one might think that Heaven is for the poor and not for the wealthy; but Doctrine teaches that the "poor in spirit" are meant, for the Lord says, *Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the Kingdom of heaven, Matthew* 5:3. Furthermore, the Lord says, *Judge not, that you be not judged; with what judgment you judge, you shall be judged, Matthew* 7:1, 2. Without Doctrine a person might be led to confirm that one should not judge a wicked person to be wicked; but according to Doctrine it is permitted to judge, provided it is done justly, for the Lord says, *Judge righteous judgment, John* 7:24. Jesus says, " *Do not be called Teacher, for one is your Teacher, Christ; and call no man your father on earth, for one is your Father in Heaven; neither be called Masters, for one is your Master, Christ, Matthew* 23:8, 9, 10. Without Doctrine it would seem that it is not permitted to call anyone a teacher, father, or master; but from Doctrine it is known that it is permitted in a natural sense, but not in a spiritual sense <note>The "natural sense" refers to our everyday world (biological fathers, school teachers), while the "spiritual sense" refers to the source of truth and life, which is God alone.</note>. Jesus said to the Disciples, *When the Son of Man sits on the Throne of his glory, you also shall sit upon twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel, Matthew* 19:28. From these words one might conclude that the Lord's disciples are to be judges, when in fact they can judge no one. Doctrine, therefore, will reveal this secret <term>arcanum: a hidden spiritual truth</term> by showing that the Lord alone, who is omniscient and knows the hearts of all, will judge and is able to judge; and that by His "twelve disciples" is meant the Church in respect to all the truths and goods it has from the Lord through the Word. From this, Doctrine concludes that these truths will judge everyone, according to the Lord’s words in *John* 3:17, 18 and 12:47, 48. There are many other similar instances in the Word, from which it is clearly evident that the Word is not understood without Doctrine.

227. The Word is not only understood through Doctrine, but it also shines in the intellect, for it is like a lampstand <note>original: "Candelabrum"</note> with its lamps lit. A person then sees more than they had seen before, and also understands things they had not understood before. Obscure and discordant things they either do not see and pass over, or they see and explain them so that they agree with Doctrine. Experience in the Christian World testifies that the Word is seen from Doctrine and explained according to it. All the Reformed <note>The various Protestant denominations following the Reformation.</note> see the Word from their own doctrine and explain it accordingly; likewise the Papists <note>Catholics.</note> from theirs, and the Jews from theirs. Consequently, falsities come from false doctrine, and truths from true doctrine. From this it is clear that true Doctrine is like a lamp in the dark and a guidepost on the road.

228. From these things it can be established that those who read the Word without Doctrine are in the dark regarding all truth; their minds are wandering and uncertain, prone to errors and also easy prey for heresies, which they even embrace if favor or authority encourages them and their reputation is not at risk. For the Word to them is like a lampstand without light; they see many things as if in a shadow, and yet they see almost nothing, for Doctrine alone is the lamp. I have seen such people examined by angels, and it was found that they could confirm anything they wished from the Word, and that they did confirm—especially those things that stem from self-love and the love of those they favor. But I saw them stripped of their clothes—a sign that they were without truths; for in the spiritual world, clothes are truths.

229.

The reason is that the Lord is present there, and He teaches and enlightens; for the Lord never operates anything except in fullness, and the Word in its literal sense is

Also, the truths of the Word, as they are multiplied from a love for them, and as they are ordered by this love, so they shine through and appear more and more clearly.

230. For, as was said before in no. 208, a person can falsify the Word through some known correspondences by joining and applying them to confirm whatever is stuck in their mind from a preconceived principle. Furthermore, the spiritual sense is not given to anyone except by the Lord alone, and it is guarded by Him just as the angelic Heaven is guarded, for Heaven resides within that sense.

### 231. III. THAT GENUINE TRUTH, WHICH BELONGS TO DOCTRINE, DOES NOT APPEAR IN THE LITERAL SENSE OF THE WORD TO ANY OTHERS THAN THOSE WHO ARE IN ENLIGHTENMENT FROM THE LORD.

Enlightenment comes from the Lord alone, and it occurs among those who love truths because they are truths and who make them <term>uses</term> <note>In this context, "uses" refers to performing good and useful actions for others as a spiritual practice.</note> of life; among others, enlightenment in the Word is not given. That enlightenment is from the Lord alone is because the Word is from Him, and thus He is in it. That enlightenment happens for those who love truths because they are truths and make them uses of life is because they are in the Lord and the Lord is in them; for the Lord is Truth itself, as was shown in the Chapter on the Lord. The Lord is loved when one lives according to His Divine truths—that is, when uses are performed from them—according to these words in John:

> *In that day you shall know that you are in Me, and I in you; he who has my commandments and does them, he it is who loves Me, and I will love him, and I will manifest Myself to him, and I will come to him and make a dwelling with him,* Chapter XIV: 20, 21, 23.

These are the ones who are in enlightenment when they read the Word, and in whom the Word shines and shines through. The reason the Word shines and shines through for them is because a spiritual and Celestial sense is within each part of the Word, and these senses are in the light of Heaven; therefore, the Lord, through them and their light, flows into the natural sense of the Word and into its light within the person. From this, the person acknowledges Truth from an interior perception, and then sees it in their thought; and this happens as often as they are in the affection of truth for the sake of Truth; for from affection comes perception, from perception thought, and thus acknowledgment occurs, which is called faith.

232. The contrary happens to those who read the Word from a doctrine of false Religion; and even more so to those who confirm that doctrine using the Word while looking toward their own glory and the riches of the world. Among these, the Truths of the Word are as if in the shadow of night, and falsities are as if in the light of day. They read Truths, but do not see them, and if they see even a shadow of them, they falsify them. These are the ones of whom the Lord says,

> *That they have eyes and see not, and ears and understand not,* Matthew XIII: 14, 15.

Consequently, their light in spiritual things (which belong to the Church) becomes merely natural, and the vision of their minds is like one seeing ghosts in bed when waking up, or like sleepwalkers who believe themselves awake when they are sleeping.

233. It has been granted to me to speak with many after death who believed they would shine like Stars in Heaven because, as they said, they held the Word holy, read it through frequently, and collected many things from it by which they confirmed the dogmas of their faith, and for this were celebrated as learned men—from which they believed they would become Michaels and Raphaels <note>Names of high-ranking archangels; the speakers expected to hold the highest positions in heaven.</note>. But many of them were examined as to the love from which they studied the Word, and it was found that some did so from self-love, to be worshipped like leaders of the Church, and some from love of the world, to gain riches. When these were also examined as to what they knew from the Word, it was discovered that they knew nothing of genuine truth from it, but only...

# VI.

## *That through the Literal Sense of the Word there is Conjunction with the Lord and Association with the Angels.*

234. That there is conjunction <note>A close spiritual "joining" or connection.</note> with the Lord through the Word is because He Himself is the Word—that is, the very Divine Truth and Divine Good within it. That there is conjunction through the <term>literal sense</term> <note>The plain, surface-level meaning of the biblical text.</note> is because the Word in that sense is in its fullness, in its holiness, and in its power, as was shown in the previous section. That conjunction is not apparent to the person, but exists in the affection for truth and in the perception of it. That there is an association with the angels of heaven through the literal sense is because within that sense there is a <term>spiritual sense</term> and a <term>celestial sense</term>. The angels are in these deeper senses: the angels of the Lord’s Spiritual Kingdom are in the spiritual sense of the Word, and the angels of His Celestial Kingdom are in its celestial sense. These two senses are unfolded from the natural sense of the Word while a person, who regards the Word as holy, reads it. This unfolding is instantaneous; consequently, the association is also instantaneous.

235. That spiritual angels are in the spiritual sense of the Word, and celestial angels are in its celestial sense, has been made manifest to me by much experience. It was granted to me to perceive that when I read the Word in its literal sense, communication was made with the Heavens—sometimes with this society there, sometimes with that. What I understood according to the natural sense, the spiritual angels understood according to the spiritual sense, and the celestial angels according to the celestial sense, and this in an instant. Because this communication has been perceived several thousand times, no doubt about it remains with me. There are also spirits who are below the Heavens who abuse this communication; for they recite certain sayings from the literal sense of the Word and immediately observe and note the Society with which communication is made; this too I have often seen and heard. From these things, it has been granted me to know through living experience that the Word, as to its literal sense, is the Divine medium of conjunction with the Lord and of association with the angels of Heaven.

236. But it shall be illustrated by examples how spiritual angels perceive their sense, and celestial angels theirs, from the natural sense when a person reads the Word. Let four commandments of the <term>Decalogue</term> <note>The Ten Commandments. Note that Swedenborg uses the numbering common in the Lutheran and Catholic traditions, where "Thou shalt not kill" is the Fifth Commandment.</note> serve as examples. For instance, the **Fifth Commandment**, *Thou shalt not kill*: by this, a person understands not only killing, but also harboring hatred and breathing vengeance even unto death. A spiritual angel, instead of "killing," understands acting as the devil and murdering a person's soul. A celestial angel, however, understands "killing" as hating the Lord and the Word. The **Sixth Commandment**, *Thou shalt not commit adultery*...

THE SEVENTH PRECEPT, *Thou shalt not steal*; a man understands by "stealing" to steal, to defraud, and under some pretext to take away a neighbor's goods; a spiritual angel understands "stealing" as depriving others of the truths and goods of their faith through falsities and evils; however, a celestial angel understands "stealing" as attributing to himself those things which belong to the Lord, and claiming the Lord's justice and merit for himself. THE EIGHTH PRECEPT, *Thou shalt not bear false witness*; a man understands by "bearing false witness" also to lie and to defame someone; an angel <note>Referring here to the spiritual level.</note> understands by "bearing false witness" to say and to persuade others that what is false is true, and what is evil is good, and vice versa; however, a celestial angel understands by "bearing false witness" to blaspheme the Lord and the Word. From these examples it can be seen how the spiritual and celestial meanings are unfolded and extracted from the natural sense of the Word, in which they reside; and what is wonderful, the angels extract their own meanings without even knowing what the man is thinking; yet the thoughts of angels and humans make one through <term>Correspondences</term> <note>A core concept in Swedenborg's work, where natural objects or actions act as a "mirror" or "echo" of higher spiritual realities.</note>, just as end, cause, and effect do; for the "ends" <note>Ultimate purposes or goals.</note> are actually in the celestial kingdom, the causes in the spiritual kingdom, and the effects in the natural kingdom. This is the source of the association of humans with angels through the Word.

237. The reason a spiritual angel extracts and calls forth spiritual things from the literal sense of the Word, and a celestial angel extracts celestial things, is because these agree with their own natures and are homogeneous; that this happens can be illustrated by similar things in the three kingdoms of nature: the Animal, Vegetable, and Mineral. IN THE ANIMAL KINGDOM: from food, when it has been turned into <term>chyle</term> <note>A milky fluid of nutrients produced during digestion.</note>, the vessels draw out and call forth their blood, the nerve fibers their juice, and the substances which are the origins of the fibers, their spirit <note>This refers to "animal spirits," which in 18th-century science were thought to be the most refined fluids of the nervous system.</note>. IN THE VEGETABLE KINGDOM: a tree with its trunk, branches, leaves, and fruits stands upon its root, and from the soil through the root it extracts and calls forth a coarser sap for the trunk, branches, and leaves, a purer sap for the flesh of the fruits, and the purest sap for the seeds within the fruits. IN THE MINERAL KINGDOM: in the womb of the earth in certain places, there are minerals impregnated with gold, silver, copper, and iron; from the vapors and emanations from the rocks, gold draws its own element, silver its own, and iron its own, while a watery medium carries these all around.

238. The Word in its letter is like a casket in which precious stones, pearls, and diadems lie in order; a man who holds the Word as holy and reads it for the sake of the uses of life has thoughts in his mind that are, by comparison, like someone holding such a casket in his hand and sending it toward Heaven; in its ascent, the casket is opened, and the precious things within reach the angels, who are profoundly delighted by seeing and examining them. This delight of theirs is communicated to the man, creating an association and also a communication of perceptions. Because of this association with angels and simultaneous conjunction with the Lord, the HOLY SUPPER was established, in which the BREAD becomes Divine Good in Heaven and the WINE becomes Divine Truth, both from the Lord; such a correspondence exists from Creation, for the purpose that the Angelic Heaven and the Church on earth—and in general the spiritual world and the natural world—may make one, and the Lord may join Himself with both at once.

239. The reason the association of man with angels occurs through the natural or literal sense of the Word is also because in every human being, by creation, there are three <term>degrees of life</term>: celestial, spiritual, and natural; but a person is in the natural as long as they are in the world, and at that time is only in the spiritual-angelic degree to the extent they are in genuine truths, and in the celestial degree to the extent they live according to them; yet they do not actually come into the spiritual and celestial themselves until after death, because these two are enclosed and hidden within their natural ideas; therefore, when the natural passes away through death, the spiritual and celestial remain, from which the ideas of their thought are then formed. From these things it can be established that in the Word alone there is spirit and life, as the Lord says...

### VII.

## **That the Word is in all the Heavens, and that angelic wisdom is derived from it.**

240. That the Word exists in the Heavens has not been known until now; nor could it have been made known as long as the Church was ignorant of the fact that Angels and Spirits are human beings, entirely similar in face and body to people in our world. Everything that exists among humans exists similarly among them, with the sole difference being that they are spiritual, and everything they have is from a spiritual origin, whereas humans in the world are natural, and everything they have is from a natural origin. As long as this remained hidden, it could not be known that the Word also exists in the Heavens, and that it is read by the Angels there, and also by the Spirits who are beneath the Heavens. But so that this might not remain hidden forever, it has been granted to me to be in the company of Angels and Spirits, to speak with them, to see what exists among them, and afterwards to report many things that I saw and heard. This was done in the work <term>HEAVEN AND HELL</term> <note>original: "CÆLO & INFERNO" — Swedenborg's 1758 treatise describing the afterlife and the nature of the spiritual world.</note>, published in London in the year 1758. From that work, it can be seen that Angels and Spirits are humans, and that everything found among humans in the world exists in abundance among them. That Angels and Spirits are humans may be seen in that work, numbers 73 to 77 and 453 to 456. That similar things exist among them as among humans in the world, numbers 170 to 190; and also that <term>Divine Worship</term> and <term>Preaching in Temples</term> exist among them, numbers 221 to 227; and that they have <term>Writings</term> and also <term>Books</term>, numbers 253 to 264; and that they have the <term>Sacred Scripture or the Word</term>, number 259.

241. Regarding the Word in Heaven, it is written in a spiritual style, which is entirely different from a natural style. The spiritual style consists of pure letters, each one of which involves a specific meaning; there are little lines, flourishes, and marks above and between the letters, and within them, which exalt the meaning. Among the Angels of the <term>Spiritual Kingdom</term> <note>The kingdom of angels who are primarily in the light of truth.</note>, the letters are similar to printed letters in our world; but among the Angels of the <term>Celestial Kingdom</term> <note>The higher kingdom of angels who are primarily in the warmth of love.</note>, the letters are, for some, similar to Arabic characters, and for others, like ancient Hebrew letters, but curved above and below, with marks above, between, and within them—each of these also involves an entire sense or meaning. Because their writing is of such a nature, the <term>Names</term> of persons and places in the Word among them are represented by signs; from these, the wise understand the spiritual and celestial reality signified by each one. For example, by <term>Moses</term> they understand the <term>Word of God</term> written through him, and in a general sense the <term>Historical Word</term>; by <term>Elijah</term>, the <term>Prophetic Word</term>; by <term>Abraham</term>, <term>Isaac</term>, and <term>Jacob</term>, the <term>Lord</term> in respect to his Divine Celestial, Divine Spiritual, and Divine Natural aspects; by <term>Aaron</term>, the <term>Priesthood</term>; by <term>David</term>, the <term>Royalty</term> (both belonging to the Lord); by the names of the sons of <term>Jacob</term>, or the twelve <term>Tribes of Israel</term>, various aspects of Heaven and the Church; similar things are understood by the names of the twelve <term>Disciples of the Lord</term>; by <term>Zion</term> and <term>Jerusalem</term>, the <term>Church</term> in respect to its doctrine from the Word; by the land of <term>Canaan</term>, the <term>Church</term> itself; by the <term>Places</term> and <term>Cities</term> there, on both sides of the Jordan, various things belonging to the Church and its doctrine. It is the same with <term>Numbers</term>; these do not appear in the Word that is in Heaven, but in their place are the things to which the numbers correspond. From this it can be established that the Word in Heaven is similar to our Word in its <term>literal sense</term>, and yet corresponds to it, and thus they are one. It is a wonderful thing that the Word in the Heavens is written in such a way that

The Word that exists in our World is similar to the Word of Heaven in this respect: that simple people understand it simply, and wise people wisely; but this happens in a different way.

242. The Angels themselves admit that all wisdom is theirs through the Word, for they are in light only to the extent that they are in the understanding of the Word. The Light of Heaven is Divine Wisdom, which appears as Light before their eyes. This is because the celestial angels are in the "good of love" from the Lord, and the spiritual angels are in the "truths of wisdom" from the Lord; and wherever the good of love is, wisdom resides there at the same time; but where truths are, no more wisdom resides there than there is a corresponding good of love. This is the reason why the Word in the Lord’s Celestial Kingdom is written differently than in His Spiritual Kingdom; for in the Word of the celestial kingdom, the "goods of love" are expressed, and the marks are "affections of love," whereas in the Word of the spiritual kingdom, the "truths of wisdom" are expressed, and the marks are "interior perceptions of truth." From these things it can be concluded what kind of Wisdom lies hidden within the Word that exists in the World; for in it lies hidden all angelic Wisdom, which is inexpressible; and a person who becomes an angel through the Word by the Lord enters into that wisdom after death.

# VIII.

### *That the Church is from the Word, and that its nature in a person depends on their understanding of the Word.*

243. That the Church is from the Word cannot be doubted, for it was shown above that the Word is Divine Truth (numbers 189 to 192); that the Doctrine of the Church is from the Word (numbers 225 to 233), and that through the Word there is conjunction with the Lord (numbers 234 to 239). However, that the *understanding* of the Word makes the Church is something that might be called into doubt, since there are those who believe they belong to the Church simply because they have the Word, read it, or hear it from a Preacher, and know something of its literal sense. Yet, how this or that part of the Word is to be understood, they do not know, and some do not value it much. Therefore, it will be confirmed here that it is not the Word itself that makes the Church, but the understanding of it, and that the nature of the Church is determined by the understanding of the Word among those who are in the Church.

244. The Church depends on the understanding of the Word because the Church is defined by the truths of faith and the "goods of charity" <note>Practical acts of love and kindness performed from a spiritual motive</note>; and these two are universals which are not only scattered throughout the literal sense of the Word, but also lie hidden within like precious things in treasure chests. What is in the literal Sense appears to every person because it flows directly into the eyes; but the things that lie hidden in the Spiritual Sense do not appear except to those who love truths because they are truths, and do good because it is good. To these people, the treasure which the literal Sense covers and guards is manifested; and these are the things that essentially constitute the Church.

Without an understanding of the Word as it is in itself, in its heart and in its depths, it would no more make a Church within a person than those Mines in the Asian world would make a European rich—unless he were their owner and worker. The Word, among those who search for the truths of faith and the goods of life from it, is like the Treasuries <note>original: "Gazæ"</note> belonging to the King of Persia, or to the Emperors of the <term>Mughals<note>original: "Mogolis," referring to the Mughal Empire in India.</note></term> and China, and the people of the Church are like their governors, to whom permission has been given to take as much as they please for their own use. Those who possess the Word and do not draw from it any understanding of genuine truth and a will for genuine good, are like those who believe they are rich based on wealth borrowed from others, or that they own the estates, houses, and merchandise of others; anyone can see that this is a fantasy. They are also like those who walk about in magnificent clothes and are carried in gilded carriages with attendants behind and at their sides, and forerunners, and yet none of these things are their own property.

246. Such was the Jewish Nation. For this reason, because they possessed the Word, they were likened by the Lord to the Rich Man, who was clothed in purple and fine linen and lived splendidly every day, and yet had not drawn even enough truth and good from the Word to have mercy on poor Lazarus, who lay at his gate full of sores. That Nation not only failed to appropriate any truths from the Word for themselves, but they also absorbed <term>falsities<note>Mistaken or perverted spiritual concepts that distort the truth.</note></term> in such abundance that finally no truth appeared to them; for truths are not only covered over by falsities, but are also obliterated and rejected. This was the reason they did not recognize the Messiah, even though all the Prophets had announced His Coming.

## IX.

### *That in every detail of the Word there is a Marriage of the Lord and the Church, and from this, a Marriage of Good and Truth.*

248. That there is a marriage of the Lord and the Church in every detail of the Word, and consequently a marriage of <term>Good and Truth<note>These are the two fundamental components of all spiritual reality: "Good" relates to the heart, love, and will; "Truth" relates to the mind, wisdom, and intellect.</note></term>, has not been seen until now; nor could it be seen, because the <term>Spiritual Sense<note>The deeper, symbolic meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal stories.</note></term> of the Word has not been uncovered before, and that marriage cannot be seen except through that sense. For there are two senses in the Word hidden within the sense of its letter, which are called the **Spiritual** and the **Celestial**. In the Spiritual Sense, the contents refer primarily to the Church; in the Celestial Sense, they refer primarily to the Lord. Furthermore, in the Spiritual Sense, the contents refer to **Divine Truth**, and in the Celestial sense to **Divine Good**. This is the source of that Marriage in the Word. But this is not apparent to anyone unless they know the significations of the words and names from the spiritual and celestial senses of the Word; for certain words and names are predicated on Good, and some on Truth, while others include both. Therefore, without that knowledge, this Marriage in every detail of the Word could not be seen; this is why this <term>Secret<note>original: "Arcanum," a profound spiritual truth previously hidden from human knowledge.</note></term> was not revealed before. Because such a marriage exists in every detail of the Word, there are often two expressions in the Word that appear like repetitions of the same thing. Yet they are not repetitions; rather, one refers to good and the other to truth, and both taken together form a conjunction, and thus one thing. This is also the source of the Divine holiness of the Word; for in every Divine Work, Good is joined to Truth, and Truth to Good.

249. It is said that in every detail of the Word there is a marriage of the Lord and the Church, and hence a marriage of good and truth. # OF THE NEW HEAVEN AND THE NEW CHURCH.

When a person of the Church is in truths, then the Lord flows into their truths with good, and gives them life; or what is the same, while a person of the Church is in the understanding of truth, then the Lord, through the good of charity, flows into their understanding and thus pours life into it. There are two <term>faculties of life<note>Swedenborg uses "faculties" to describe the basic "tools" or capacities of the human mind.</note></term> in every human being, which are called the Understanding and the Will. The Understanding is the receptacle of truth, and thus of wisdom, while the Will is the receptacle of good, and thus of charity. These two faculties must become one so that a person may be a person of the Church; and they become one when a person forms their Understanding from genuine truths—which appears to be done by the person themselves—and when their Will is filled with the good of love, which is done by the Lord. From this, the person possesses the life of truth and the life of good: the life of truth in the Understanding, and the life of good in the Will; when these are united, they do not make two lives, but one. This is the <term>Marriage of the Lord and the Church<note>In this theology, the relationship between God and humanity is likened to a marriage, where God provides the "Good" (love) and the Church/individual provides the "Truth" (faith).</note></term>, as well as the marriage of good and truth within the person.

250. It can be seen by readers who pay close attention that in the Word there are dual expressions that appear like repetitions of the same thing, such as: brother and companion, poor and needy, devastation and solitude, emptiness and void, foe and enemy, sin and iniquity, anger and wrath, nation and people, joy and gladness, mourning and weeping, justice and judgment, and so on. These appear as synonyms, and yet they are not; for *brother, poor, devastation, foe, sin, anger, nation, joy, mourning,* and *justice* are predicated of **good** (and in the opposite sense, of evil); whereas *companion, needy, solitude, void, enemy, iniquity, wrath, people, gladness, weeping,* and *judgment* are predicated of **truth** (and in the opposite sense, of falsity). And yet it appears to a reader who does not know this secret that *poor and needy, devastation and solitude, emptiness and void,* etc., are one and the same thing; however, they are not, but they become one thing through their conjunction. In the Word, many other things are joined in this way, such as fire and flame, gold and silver, brass and iron, wood and stone, bread and wine, purple and fine linen, and so on. This is because fire, gold, brass, wood, bread, and purple are predicated of **good**, while flame, silver, iron, stone, water, wine, and fine linen are predicated of **truth**. Similarly, it is said that they are to love God with all their "heart" and all their "soul," and that God will create in man a "new heart" and a "new spirit"; for the heart is predicated of the good of love, while the soul and spirit are predicated of the truths of faith. There are also words which, because they participate in both good and truth, are used alone without others joined to them. But these and many other things are not evident except to the Angels and to those who, while in the natural sense of the Word, are also in its spiritual sense.

251. To show from the Word that there are two such expressions which appear like repetitions of the same thing would be a lengthy task, for it would fill many pages; but to remove any doubt, I wish to cite passages where **NATION** and **PEOPLE**, and where **JOY** and **GLADNESS**, are mentioned together. The reason why both **Nations** and **Peoples** are mentioned together is because by **Nations** are meant those who are in **good** (and in the opposite sense, those in evil), and by **Peoples** those who are in **truths** (and in the opposite sense, those in falsities). Therefore, those who are of the Lord's <term>Spiritual Kingdom<note>In Swedenborg's theology, the "Spiritual Kingdom" consists of those whose primary motivation is truth and intellectual faith.</note></term> are called **Peoples**, and those who are of the Lord's <term>Celestial Kingdom<note>The "Celestial Kingdom" consists of those whose primary motivation is love and "good."</note></term> are called **Nations**; for in the Spiritual Kingdom all are in **Truths** and thus in Intelligence, but in the Celestial Kingdom all are in **Goods** and thus in Wisdom.

252. It is the same with many other terms; for example, where **JOY** is mentioned, **GLADNESS** is also mentioned, as in these passages: Behold, **JOY** and **GLADNESS** in slaying an ox, *Isaiah 22:13.* **JOY** and **GLADNESS** they shall obtain, and **SORROW** and sighing shall flee away, *Isaiah 35:10; Chapter 51:11.* **GLADNESS** and **JOY** are cut off from the House of our God, *Joel 1:16.* The voice of **JOY** and the voice of **GLADNESS** shall be taken away, *Jeremiah 7:34; Chapter 25:10.* The fast of the tenth month shall be to the house of Judah for **JOY** and **GLADNESS**, *Zechariah 8:19.* **BE GLAD** in Jerusalem, **REJOICE** in her, *Isaiah 66:10.* **REJOICE** and **BE GLAD**, O daughter of Edom, *Lamentations 4:21.* The Heavens shall **BE GLAD**, and the Earth shall **REJOICE**, *Psalm 68:3.* <note>Original: "Psalm LXVIII: 4"</note> They shall make me hear **JOY** and **GLADNESS**, *Psalm 51:8.* <note>Original: "Psalm LI: 10"</note> **JOY** and **GLADNESS** shall be found in Zion, confession and the voice of singing, *Isaiah 51:3.* There shall be **GLADNESS**, and many shall **REJOICE** at His birth, *Luke 1:14.* I will cause the voice of **JOY** and the voice of **GLADNESS**, the voice of the **bridegroom** and the voice of the **bride**, to cease, *Jeremiah 7:34; Chapter 16:9; Chapter 25:10.* There shall yet be heard in this place the voice of **JOY** and the voice of **GLADNESS**, and the voice of the **bridegroom** and the voice of the **bride**, *Jeremiah 33:10, 11;* and elsewhere. The reason why both **Joy** and **Gladness** are mentioned is because Joy is predicated of **Good**, and Gladness of **Truth**; or Joy of **Love**, and Gladness of **Wisdom**; for Joy belongs to the Heart and Gladness to the Spirit, or Joy belongs to the **Will** and Gladness to the **Understanding**. That the **Marriage of the Lord and the Church** is also present in these passages is evident from the fact that it is said, *the voice of Joy and the voice of Gladness, the voice of the Bridegroom and the voice of the Bride, Jeremiah 7:34; Chapter 16:9; Chapter 25:10; Chapter 33:10, 11;* and the Lord is the **Bridegroom** and the Church is the **Bride**. That the Lord is the Bridegroom may be seen in *Matthew 9:15; Mark 2:19, 20; Luke 5:34,* and that the Church is the Bride, *Revelation 21:2, 9; Chapter 22:17;* wherefore John the Baptist said of Jesus, *He who has the Bride is the Bridegroom, John 3:29.*

## X.

### *That Heresies can be gathered from the Sense of the letter of the Word, but that to confirm them is harmful.*

254. It was shown above that the <term>Word</term> <note>The Bible or Sacred Scripture.</note> cannot be understood without <term>Doctrine</term> <note>A framework of teaching that serves as a guide for interpretation.</note>, and that Doctrine is like a Lamp, so that genuine Truths may be seen; and this is for the reason that the Word was written through pure <term>Correspondences</term> <note>A symbolic language where natural things represent spiritual realities.</note>. For this reason, many things therein are <term>Appearances of truth</term> <note>Statements that describe things as they appear to the human eye—like saying "the sun rises"—rather than the absolute spiritual reality.</note>, and not naked truths; and many things are written to suit the grasp of the merely natural man, and yet in such a way that the simple can understand it simply, those who have understanding can understand it intelligently, and the wise can understand it wisely. Now, because the Word is of such a nature, the Appearances of truth—which are truths clothed—can be mistaken for naked truths; when these are confirmed, they become fallacies, which in themselves are falsehoods. From the fact that Appearances of truth have been taken for genuine truths and confirmed, all the <term>Heresies</term> <note>Dissenting religious beliefs or sects.</note> that have existed in the Christian World, and still exist today, have been born. Heresies themselves do not condemn people; rather, it is the confirmation of the falsehoods within a heresy—using the Word and through reasonings from the natural man and a bad life—that condemns. For everyone is born into the Religion of his Country or his Parents, is initiated into it from infancy, and afterwards retains it; nor can he rescue himself from its falsehoods, both because of his business in the World and because of the weakness of his intellect in perceiving truths on its own. But to live wickedly, and to confirm falsehoods even to the destruction of genuine truth, this is what condemns. For whoever remains in his own Religion and believes in God (and within Christianity, believes in the Lord), and holds the Word as holy, and lives according to the precepts of the <term>Decalogue</term> <note>The Ten Commandments.</note> out of religious principle—such a person does not swear by falsehoods. Therefore, when he hears truths and perceives them in his own way, he is able to embrace them and thus be led out of falsehoods. This is not the case, however, with someone who has confirmed the falsehoods of his Religion; for a confirmed falsehood remains and cannot be uprooted. For after confirmation, a falsehood is as if a person had sworn an oath to it, especially if it is bound up with self-love or the pride of one’s own intelligence.

255. I have spoken with some in the <term>spiritual world</term> who lived many centuries ago and had confirmed themselves in the falsehoods of their Religion, and I found that they still remained constantly in them. And I also spoke with some there who were in the same Religion and thought as they did, but did not confirm its falsehoods in themselves; and I found that, having been instructed by <term>Angels</term>, they rejected the falsehoods and received truths, and that these were saved, but not the former. Every person is instructed by Angels after death, and those are received who see truths, and from truths see falsehoods. But only those see truths who have not confirmed themselves in falsehoods; those who have confirmed themselves are unwilling to see truths, and if they do see them, they turn their backs, and then either laugh at them or falsify them. The real cause is that Confirmation enters the will, and the will is the man himself, and it disposes the intellect at its pleasure; but naked knowledge only enters the intellect, and this has no right over the will; thus it is not in the man, except as one who stands in the courtyard or at the gate, but is not yet in the house.

256. But let this be illustrated by an Example: in the Word, in many places, anger, wrath, and vengeance are attributed to God, and it is said that He punishes, casts into Hell, tempts, and many similar things. He who believes this simply, like a child, and therefore fears God and takes care not to sin against Him, is not con-

But he who confirms those things within himself to the point that he believes that anger, wrath, vengeance, and similar things which are evil, are in God, and that He punishes man and casts him into hell out of anger, wrath, and vengeance—he is condemned, because he has destroyed the genuine truth. That truth is that God is Love itself, Mercy itself, and Goodness itself, and He who is these things cannot be angry, wrathful, or vengeful. That these things are attributed to God in the Word <note>The Bible or Sacred Scripture.</note> is because it so appears; such things are <term>appearances of truth</term> <note>original: "apparentiae veri"; These are statements that describe things from a human perspective rather than their actual divine nature.</note>.

257. That many things in the <term>Sense of the letter of the Word</term> <note>The literal, surface-level meaning of the text.</note> are <term>Appearances of truth</term>, in which genuine truths lie hidden, and that it is not harmful to think and even to speak according to appearances of truth in a simple way, but that it is harmful to confirm them (since through confirmation the Divine Truth that lies hidden within is destroyed), can also be illustrated by an Example from nature. Natural examples are brought forward because they illustrate and teach more clearly than spiritual ones. Before the eyes it appears as if the Sun is carried around the Earth every day, and also once every year; hence it is said that the Sun rises and sets, that it makes morning, noon, evening, and night, and also the seasons of spring, summer, autumn, and winter, and thus days and years. Yet the Sun stands unmoved, for it is a fiery Ocean, and the Earth is revolved daily and carried around it yearly. A man who, out of simplicity and ignorance, thinks that the Sun is carried around, does not destroy the natural truth (which is that the Earth rotates on its axis and is carried yearly along the <term>Ecliptic</term> <note>The apparent path of the sun; here used to discuss the Earth's orbit.</note>). But he who confirms the apparent motion of the Sun through reasonings from the natural man—and even more so if he uses the Word because it is said there that the Sun rises and sets—he weakens the truth and destroys it. Afterward, he can hardly see the truth, even if it were shown to his eye that the entire starry Heaven is similarly carried around daily and yearly only in appearance, and yet not even one Star is moved from its fixed place relative to another. That the Sun moves is an <term>apparent truth</term>, but that it does not move is a <term>genuine truth</term>. Nevertheless, everyone speaks according to the apparent truth by saying that the Sun rises and sets, and this is permitted because it cannot be otherwise; but to think according to that appearance as a result of "confirmation" <note>In this context, "confirmation" means a deliberate intellectual effort to prove a false idea is true.</note> dulls and darkens the rational understanding.

258. That it is harmful to confirm <term>appearances of truth</term> which are in the Word (since by doing so a fallacy is created and the Divine Truth hidden within is destroyed) is due to this very cause: each and every thing in the <term>Sense of the letter of the Word</term> communicates with Heaven. For, as shown above, within each and every thing of its <term>sense of the letter</term> there is a <term>spiritual sense</term> <note>The inner, symbolic meaning of the Bible that angels understand.</note>, and this sense is opened as it passes from man to heaven. All things in the <term>Spiritual sense</term> are genuine truths. Therefore, when a man holds false ideas and applies the <term>sense of the letter</term> to them, then falsehoods are present within that sense; and when falsehoods enter, truths are dissipated. This happens on the way from man to heaven. 

This can be compared to a shiny bladder filled with gall <note>A bitter, yellowish-brown fluid; here used as a symbol of something foul or malicious.</note> that is thrown to another person; before it reaches him, it breaks in the air and the gall is scattered. When the other person smells the air infected with gall, he turns away and closes his mouth so it does not touch his tongue. It is also like a leather bottle bound with cedar bark, containing vinegar full of worms; if the bottle ruptures on the road and its stench is smelled by another, he immediately brushes the odor away with a fan out of nausea so it does not flow into his nostrils. It is also like an almond in its shell, inside which, instead of an almond, there is a newborn serpent; when the shell is cracked and that little serpent appears to be carried by the wind toward another's eyes, it is self-evident that he would turn away to avoid it. 

The same is true when the Word is read by a man who holds false ideas and applies parts of the sense of the letter of the Word to his falsehoods; it is then rejected on its way to Heaven, lest such a thing flow in and infest the Angels. For falsehood, when it touches truth, is like the point of a needle touching a nerve fiber or the pupil of the eye. It is well known that a nerve fiber immediately rolls itself into a spiral and withdraws, and similarly, the eye veils itself with the eyelids at the first touch. From these things, it is clear that truth falsified takes away...

259. The Word is like a Garden, which is to be called a Heavenly Paradise, in which there are delicacies and delights of every kind—delicacies from fruits and delights from flowers. In its center are the Trees of Life, and a person actually enjoys its delicacies and delights; however, the person who is not established in truths from <term>Doctrine</term> <note>A systematic body of religious teaching used to interpret Scripture.</note> but relies solely on the <term>Sense of the letter</term> <note>original: "Sensu literæ"; the literal, surface-level meaning of the Bible.</note> stands only on the outskirts and sees only wild growth. But he who is in the doctrine of a false religion, and has confirmed its falsehoods within himself, is not even in the forest, but outside of it in a sandy field where not even grass grows. That such is their state after death was shown in the work *Heaven and Hell* <note>original: "DE CÆLO ET INFERNO"; Swedenborg's 1758 work describing the afterlife.</note>.

260. Furthermore, it should be known that the <term>Sense of the letter</term> is a guard for the genuine truths that lie hidden within, so that they are not harmed. The protection lies in the fact that this Sense can be turned this way and that and explained according to one's grasp, and yet its internal meaning is not harmed or violated. For it does no harm if the sense of the letter is understood differently by one person than by another; but it does harm if a person introduces falsehoods that are against Divine truths—which is done only by those who have confirmed themselves in falsehoods. By this, violence is offered to the Word. To prevent this, the sense of the letter acts as a guard; and it protects those who are in falsehoods because of their religion but do not confirm its false teachings. The literal sense of the Word as a "Guard" is signified by the **Cherubim** in the Word, and is also described by them there. This Guard is signified by the **Cherubim** who, after Adam and his wife were cast out of the Garden of Eden, were placed at its entrance, concerning whom we read:

> *When Jehovah God had driven out the man, he placed* CHERUBIM *at the east of the garden of Eden, and a flaming sword turning every way, to guard the way of the Tree of Life. Genesis III: 23, 24.*

No one can see what these things signify unless he knows what is signified by the **Cherubim**, by the Garden of Eden, by the Tree of Life there, and finally by the flaming sword turning every way. These individual points are explained in the *Heavenly Secrets* <note>original: "ARCANIS CÆLESTIBUS"; Swedenborg's multi-volume commentary on Genesis and Exodus.</note> published in London, in the chapter on this subject. Specifically, by the **Cherubim** is signified a Guard; by the "way of the Tree of Life" is signified the entrance to the Lord, which is available to men through the truths of the spiritual sense of the Word; by the "flaming sword turning every way" is signified Divine Truth in its final forms, which is like the Word in the sense of the letter, which can be so turned. The same is meant by the **CHERUBIM MADE OF GOLD** placed over the two ends of the <term>Mercy Seat</term> <note>The gold lid covering the Ark of the Covenant.</note>, which was over the Ark in the Tabernacle (*Exodus XXV: 18 to 21*). By the Ark was signified the Word, because the <term>Decalogue</term> <note>The Ten Commandments.</note> within it was its primary part; by the Cherubim there was signified a guard; therefore the Lord spoke with Moses from between them (*Exodus XXV: 22; Chapter XXXVI: 9; Numbers VII: 89*). And He spoke in the natural sense, for He does not speak with man except in fullness, and the Divine Truth is in its fullness in the sense of the letter (see above, *numbers 214 to 224*). Nothing else was signified by the **CHERUBIM** upon the curtains of the Tabernacle and upon the Veil (*Exodus XXVI: 31*); for the curtains and veils of the Tabernacle signified the outermost things of Heaven and the Church, and thus also of the Word (see above, *number 220*). Similarly by the **CHERUBIM** carved on the walls and over the doors of the Temple at Jerusalem (*I Kings VI: 29, 32, 35*; see above, *number 221*). Likewise by the **CHERUBIM** in the New Temple (*Ezekiel XLI: 18, 19, 20*). Since by the **Cherubim** was signified a Guard, lest the Lord, Heaven, and Divine Truth (as it is within the Word) be approached directly, but rather mediately through the outermost things, it is therefore said of the King of Tyre:

> *You seal up the sum, full of wisdom and perfect in beauty, you have been in Eden the Garden; every precious stone was your covering... you are the* CHERUB *of expansion that covers: I have destroyed you, O covering* CHERUB, *from the midst of the stones of fire. Ezekiel XXVIII: 12, 13, 14, 16.*

By "Tyre" is signified the Church in respect to the knowledges of truth and good, and therefore by the "King of Tyre" is signified the Word where and from which those knowledges are. That the Word in its outermost form is here signified by him, and the Guard by the **Cherub**, is clear, for...

## XI.

->*That the Lord in the world fulfilled all things of the Word, and thereby became the Word, that is, Divine Truth, even in its ultimates.*<-

261. That the Lord in the world fulfilled all things of the Word, and that He thereby became Divine Truth, or the Word, even in its <term>ultimates</term>, is meant by these words in John: *And the Word was made Flesh, and dwelt among us, and we saw His Glory, the glory as of the Only Begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth*, 1:14. To "become flesh" is to become the Word in its ultimates. What the Lord was like as the Word in its ultimates, He showed to the disciples when He was transformed <note>The Transfiguration, where Jesus's divine nature became visible.</note>, Matthew 17:2, Mark 9:2, Luke 9:28; and there it is said that Moses and Elijah were seen in glory. By "Moses" is meant the Word that was written through him, and the Historical Word in general; and by "Elijah," the Prophetic Word. The Lord as the Word in its ultimates was also represented before John in the Apocalypse, chapter 1:13–16, where all parts of His description signify the ultimates of Divine Truth or the Word. The Lord had indeed been the Word or Divine Truth before, but in its first principles, for it is said: *In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and God was the Word*, John 1:1–2; but when the Word was made Flesh, then the Lord became the Word even in its ultimates. It is for this reason that He is called the *First and the Last*, Revelation 1:8, 11, 17; 2:8; 21:6; 22:12–13; Isaiah 44:6.

262. That the Lord fulfilled all things of the Word is evident from the passages where it is said that the Law and the Scripture were fulfilled by Him, and that all things were finished, as in these: Jesus said, *Do not think that I have come to destroy the Law and the Prophets; I have not come to destroy, but to fulfill*, Matthew 5:17–18. *Jesus entered into the synagogue and stood up to read; then the Book of the prophet Isaiah was handed to Him, and He unrolled the Book and found the place where it was written: The Spirit of Jehovah is upon me, because He has anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor, He has sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives and sight to the blind, to preach the acceptable year of the Lord. Afterward, rolling up the Book, He said, Today this Scripture is fulfilled in your ears*, Luke 4:16–21. *That the Scripture might be fulfilled, he who eats bread with Me has lifted up his heel against Me*, John 13:18. *None of them has perished except the son of perdition, that the Scripture might be fulfilled*, John 17:12. *That the Word might be fulfilled which He spoke: of those whom You gave Me, I have not lost one*, John 18:9. *Jesus said to Peter, Put your sword back in its place... how then would the Scriptures be fulfilled, that it must happen this way? All this was done that the Scriptures might be fulfilled*, Matthew 26:52, 54, 56. *The Son of Man goes as it is written of Him, that there might be fulfilled...*
