That the entire Word was written about Him, and that He came into the world to fulfill it, He also taught the Disciples before He departed, in these words: *He said to them, O fools and slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken, was it not necessary for the Christ to suffer these things, and to enter into glory: and beginning furthermore from* MOSES AND FROM ALL THE PROPHETS, *he interpreted to them in* ALL THE SCRIPTURES THE THINGS CONCERNING HIMSELF, Luke 24:25–27. Furthermore, *Jesus* said, THAT ALL THINGS MUST BE FULFILLED WHICH WERE WRITTEN IN THE LAW OF MOSES, AND THE PROPHETS, AND THE PSALMS CONCERNING ME, Luke 24:44–45. That the Lord in the world fulfilled all things of the Word, even to its most minute details, is clear from these words of His: *Amen I say to you, until heaven and earth pass away, ONE JOT* <note>original: "JOTHA"; referring to the smallest letter of the alphabet.</note> *OR ONE TITTLE* <note>original: "CORNICULUM"; literally "little horn," referring to the smallest stroke or mark in a manuscript.</note> *SHALL NOT PASS FROM THE LAW, UNTIL ALL THINGS ARE DONE*, Matthew 5:18. From these things it can now be clearly seen that by the fact that the Lord fulfilled all things of the Law, it is not meant that He fulfilled all the commandments of the <term>Decalogue</term> <note>The Ten Commandments.</note>, but all things of the Word. That all things of the Word are also meant by "the Law" can be established from these passages: *Jesus said, is it not written in* YOUR LAW, *I said, you are gods*, John 10:34 (this is written in Psalm 82:6). *The crowd answered, we have heard out of the* LAW *that Christ remains forever*, John 12:34 (this is written in Psalm 89:30, Psalm 110:4, Daniel 7:14). That the Word might be fulfilled written in THEIR LAW, *they hated Me without a cause*, John 15:25 (this is written in Psalm 35:19). *It is easier for Heaven and Earth to pass away, than for one tittle of the Law to fail*, Luke 16:17. By "the Law" there, as also elsewhere in various places, the entire Sacred Scripture is meant.

263. How the Lord is the <term>Word</term> <note>The "Word" (Latin: *Verbum*) refers here to Divine Truth or the living expression of God's will.</note> is understood by few; for they think that the Lord can enlighten and teach people through the Word, and yet cannot be called the Word because of that. But let them know that every individual person is their own Will and their own Understanding, and thus one is distinct from another; and because the Will is the vessel of Love (and thus of all the goods belonging to that Love), and the Understanding is the vessel of Wisdom (and thus of all the truths belonging to that wisdom), it follows that every person is their own love and their own wisdom, or what is the same, their own good and their own truth. A person is not a person from any other source, and there is nothing else in them that makes them a person. Regarding the Lord, He is Love itself and Wisdom itself, thus Good itself and Truth itself, which He became because He fulfilled every good and every truth that is in the Word; for one who thinks and speaks nothing but Truth becomes that truth, and one who wills and does nothing but good becomes that good; and because the Lord fulfilled all Divine Truth and Divine Good which are in the Word—both those in its <term>Natural Sense</term> <note>The literal, surface-level meaning of the Bible.</note> and those in its <term>Spiritual Sense</term> <note>The deeper, symbolic meaning that Swedenborg describes as the "soul" of the text.</note>—He became Good itself and Truth itself, and thus the Word.

## XII.

### *That before this Word, which is in the world today, there was a Word that has been lost.*

---

264. That before the Word given to the Israelite nation through Moses and the Prophets, worship through sacrifices was known, and that they prophesied from the mouth of Jehovah, can be established from the accounts in the Books of Moses. That **WORSHIP THROUGH SACRIFICES WAS KNOWN** is clear from these facts: It was commanded that the children of Israel should overturn the altars of the nations, break their statues, and cut down their groves (Exod. 34:13; Deut. 7:5; 12:3). When Israel began to commit harlotry with the daughters of Moab in Shittim, they called the people to the **SACRIFICES** of their gods, and the people ate (Num. 25:1, 2, 3). Balaam, who was from Syria <note>original: "Bileamus". Balaam is a non-Israelite prophet mentioned in the Book of Numbers who was hired to curse Israel but blessed them instead.</note>, had altars built and **SACRIFICED** oxen and sheep (Num. 22:40; 23:1, 2, 14, 29, 30). He also **PROPHESIED CONCERNING THE LORD**, saying that a Star would arise out of Jacob and a Scepter out of Israel (Num. 24:17 <note>The Latin text cites Num. 23:17, but the quote "Star out of Jacob" is found in Num. 24:17.</note>). Furthermore, he **PROPHESIED FROM THE MOUTH OF JEHOVAH** (Num. 22:13, 18; 23:3, 5, 8, 16, 26; 24:1, 13). From these examples it is evident that a Divine worship, almost identical to the worship instituted through Moses in the Israelite nation, existed among the nations. That this also existed before the time of Abraham is clear from the words in Moses (Deut. 32:7, 8), but even more clearly from Melchizedek, King of Salem, in that he brought out **BREAD AND WINE** and blessed Abram, and that Abram gave him **TITHES** of all (Gen. 14:18 to 20); and that Melchizedek represented the Lord, for he is called "Priest to God Most High" (Gen. 14:18); and of the Lord it is said in David, *You are a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek* (Psalm 110:4). For this reason, Melchizedek brought out bread and wine as the most holy things of the church, just as they are holy in the Holy Supper <note>original: "Sacra Coena". Refers to the Eucharist or Holy Communion.</note>. These, along with many other things, are existing signs that before the Israelite Word there was a Word from which such revelations came.

265. That there was a Word among the Ancients is established in Moses, by whom it is mentioned and from which something is taken (Num. 21:14, 15, 27 to 30); and that the historical parts of that Word were called the **WARS OF JEHOVAH**, and the prophetic parts were called **ENUNCIATIONS**. From the historical parts of that Word, this was taken by Moses:
> *Therefore it is said in the* **BOOK OF THE WARS OF JEHOVAH**: *I went to Suphah, and the rivers of Arnon, and the channel of the rivers, which turned aside where Ar is inhabited, and stops at the border of Moab* (Num. 21:14, 15).

By the "Wars of Jehovah" in that Word, as in ours, are meant and described the battles of the Lord with the hells <note>original: "Infernis". In this theological context, these are spiritual conflicts against the powers of evil.</note>, and His victories over them, when He was to come into the world. The same battles are also meant and described in many places in the historical parts of our Word, such as in the wars of Joshua with the nations of the land of Canaan, and in the wars of the Judges and the Kings of Israel. From the prophetic parts of that Word, these things were taken:
> *Therefore the* **ENUNCIATORS** *say: Enter into Heshbon; let the city of Sihon be built and strengthened; for a fire went out from Heshbon, a flame from the city of Sihon; it consumed Ar of Moab, the masters of the high places of Arnon. Woe to you, Moab! You have perished, O people of Chemosh; he gave his sons as fugitives, and his daughters into captivity to Sihon, King of the Amorites; we have finished them with arrows: Heshbon has perished as far as Dibon, and we have laid waste as far as Nophah, which reaches to Medeba* (Num. 21:27 to 30).

Translators render this "composers of proverbs," but they should be called **ENUNCIATORS** or **PROPHETIC ENUNCIATIONS**, as can be seen from the meaning of the word <term>MOSCHALIM</term> <note>Hebrew: מֹשְׁלִים. Often translated as "proverbs" or "parables," but here interpreted as a specific genre of ancient prophetic poetry.</note> in the Hebrew language, which are not only proverbs, but also prophetic enunciations (as in Num. 23:7, 18).

In Numbers <note>The original text refers to "Cap. 266. From these facts, it can be established that an Ancient Word existed in the world, primarily in Asia, before the Israelite Word. This Word is preserved in Heaven among the Angels who lived in those ages; and furthermore, it still exists today among the nations in **GREAT TARTARY** <note>A historical name used by Europeans for a vast region in North and Central Asia. ## XIII.

### *That through the Word there is also Light for those who are outside the Church and do not have the Word.*

267. No connection with Heaven can exist unless there is a Church somewhere on Earth where the Word is, and through which the Lord is known; this is because the Lord is the God of Heaven and Earth, and without the Lord there is no salvation. That connection with the Lord and association with the Angels occurs through the Word was shown above in numbers 234 to 240. It is sufficient that the Church exists where the Word is, even though it may consist of relatively few people; through it, the Lord is nonetheless present in the entire world, for through it Heaven is joined to the Human Race.

268. We will now describe how the presence and connection of the Lord and Heaven occur in all lands through the Word. Before the Lord, the entire Angelic Heaven is like a single Man; the Church on earth is similar. That they actually appear as a Man can be seen in the work *HEAVEN AND HELL* (numbers 59 to 87). In that "Man," the Church where the Word is read and the Lord is known is like the **HEART** and the **LUNGS**: the Lord’s Celestial Kingdom acts as the Heart, and His Spiritual Kingdom acts as the Lungs. Just as all the remaining members, viscera, and organs in the human body survive and live from these two sources of life, so too do all those across the entire world who have a religion, worship one God, and live well. By these means, they are part of that "Man" and correspond to the members and viscera outside the chest where the Heart and Lungs are located. From the connection of the Lord and Heaven with the Church through the Word, they survive and live; for the Word in the Christian Church is life for the rest of humanity from the Lord through Heaven, just as the life of the members and viscera of the whole body comes from the heart and lungs. There is a similar communication between them. This is also why Christians, among whom the Word is read, constitute the Breast of that "Man." They are in the center of all; around them are the Catholics <note>original: "Pontificii", literally "those of the Pope."</note>; around these are the Muslims <note>original: "Mahumedani"</note>, who acknowledge the Lord as the greatest Prophet and as the Son of God; after these are the Africans; and the furthest circumference is made up of the peoples and nations in Asia and the Indies.

269. That this is the case in the whole of Heaven can be concluded from a similar arrangement in every society—

XIV..

...society of heaven, for every individual Society is a Heaven in a smaller form, which is also shaped like a Human; how this occurs may be seen in the work *Heaven and Hell*, numbers 41 to 87. In every Society of Heaven, those who are in its center similarly represent the Heart and the Lung <note>original: "Cor & Pulmonem"</note>, and among them is the greatest light; that Light itself, and the resulting Perception of truth, propagates itself from that center toward the peripheries in every direction—thus to everyone who is in the Society—and constitutes their spiritual life. It has been shown that when those who were in the center, and who constituted the province of the Heart and Lung and possessed the greatest light, were removed, those who were around them fell into a shadow of the intellect and then into such a meager perception of truth that they lamented; but as soon as they returned, the light appeared, and they had a perception of truth just as before. A comparison can be made with the heat and light from the Sun of the World, which give growth to trees and shrubs, even to those on the outskirts and those standing under a cloud, provided the Sun has risen. Thus the Light and Heat of Heaven from the Lord as the Sun there—which Light in its essence is Divine Truth, from which all intelligence and wisdom come to angels and men—is why it is said of the *Word that was with God and was God, that it enlightens every man coming into the World; and that this Light also appears in the darkness* (John 1:1, 5, 9). By "the Word" there is meant the Lord in respect to Divine Truth.

270. From these things it can be established that the Word, which is among the Protestants and the Reformed, enlightens all Nations and Peoples through spiritual communication; also that it is provided by the Lord that there should always be a Church on Earth where the Word is read, and through it the Lord may become known. Therefore, when the Word was almost rejected by the Pontiffs <note>The author refers here to the Roman Catholic Church of the 18th century.</note>, the Reformation was brought about by the Divine Providence of the Lord, and thus the Word was drawn out as if from hiding places and put into use. Furthermore, when the Word among the Jewish Nation was utterly falsified and corrupted, and made as if it were nothing, it then pleased the Lord to descend from Heaven, and to come as the Word, and to fulfill it, and through that to renew and restore it, and again to give light to the Inhabitants of the earth, according to these words of the Lord: *The people sitting in darkness saw a great Light; for those sitting in the region and shadow of death, a Light has arisen for them* (Isaiah 9:1 and Matthew 4:16).

271. Since it was foretold that at the end of this Church darkness would also arise from the lack of knowledge of the Lord as the God of Heaven and Earth, and from the separation of Faith from Charity, lest the genuine understanding of the Word perish by this—and thus the Church—it has therefore pleased the Lord now to reveal the **SPIRITUAL SENSE OF THE WORD**, and to manifest that the Word in that Sense, and from it in the natural Sense, contains countless things by which the Light of truth from the Word, which was almost extinguished, may be restored. That the Light of truth would be almost extinguished at the end of this Church is foretold in many places in the Revelation <note>original: "Apocalypsi"</note>; and it is also understood by these words of the Lord: *Immediately after the affliction of those days the Sun will be darkened, and the Moon will not give its light, and the Stars will fall from Heaven; and the Powers of the Heavens will be moved: and then they will see the Son of Man coming in the clouds of Heaven with glory and power* (Matthew 24:29-30). By the "Sun" there is meant the Lord in respect to love; by the "Moon," the Lord in respect to faith; by the "Stars," in respect to the knowledges of truth and good; by the "Son of Man," the Lord in respect to the Word; by a "Cloud," the Sense of the letter of the Word; by "Glory," the spiritual Sense of the Word and its transparency through the Sense of its letter; and by "Powers," its potency.

272. Through much experience it has been granted to me to know that through the Word there is communication for man with Heaven. While I read through the Word from the first Chapter of Isaiah to the last of Malachi, and the Psalms of David, and held my thought on their spiritual Sense, it was granted to me to perceive clearly that every single Verse communicated with some Society of Heaven, and thus the whole Word with the Universal Heaven: from which it was clear that just as the Lord is the Word, Heaven is also the Word, since Heaven is Heaven from the Lord, and the Lord through the Word is everything in all things of Heaven.

## XIV.

### *That unless there were a Word, no one would know God, Heaven and Hell, and Life after death, and even less the Lord.*

273. There are those who maintain, and have confirmed within themselves, that man could know of the existence of God, and also of Heaven and Hell, along with the other things the Word teaches, without the Word itself. Since they do not believe the Word, but only themselves, it is not possible to argue with them from the Word; one must argue from the natural light of reason. 

Inquire from the light of reason and you will find that there are two faculties of life in man, called the Intellect and the Will, and that the Intellect is subject to the Will, and not the Will to the Intellect. For the Intellect merely teaches and points out what must be done based on the Will. This is why many people of sharp wit, who understand moral matters better than others, nevertheless do not live according to them; it would be different if they willed to do so. 

Inquire further, and you will find that man's Will is his <term>proprium</term> <note>original: "proprium"; a technical term in Swedenborg’s theology referring to the "selfhood" or the inherent nature of a person, which he argues is naturally focused only on self-interest.</note>, and that this is evil from birth, and that from this comes what is false in the intellect. When you have discovered these things, you will see that man, of his own accord, does not want to understand anything except what comes from his own will; and unless there were a source elsewhere from which he might learn, man from his own will would not want to understand anything except what concerns himself and the world. 

Whatever is above that is in thick darkness. Thus, when he sees the Sun, the Moon, and the Stars, if he should happen to think about their origin, he could not think otherwise than that they exist of themselves. Are such people any more enlightened than the many learned men in the world who, although they know of the creation of all things by God from the Word, still acknowledge Nature instead? What then would these same people have done if they had known nothing from the Word? 

Do you believe that the ancient Wise Men <note>original: "Sophi"</note>, such as Aristotle, Cicero, Seneca, and others, who wrote about God and the immortality of the soul, took this first from their own intellect? No, they took it from others by tradition, tracing back to those who first knew it from the Ancient Word <note>Swedenborg believed a lost "Ancient Word" existed before the Hebrew Bible, which was the source of much ancient wisdom and mythology.</note> mentioned above. The writers of natural theology <note>A branch of theology that seeks to prove God's existence through reason and the observation of nature alone.</note> do not draw any such knowledge from themselves; they merely use rational arguments to confirm things they already know from the Church (where the Word is present). Among such writers, there may even be those who confirm these truths without actually believing them.

274. It has been granted to me to see people born on islands who were rational in civil matters but knew nothing at all about God. In the spiritual world, these appear like Sphinxes <note>A symbolic representation of their state: having the potential of a human (the head) but the natural, uninstructed drives of an animal (the body).</note>. However, because they are born human and thus have the capacity to receive spiritual life, they are instructed by angels and are brought to life through knowledge of the Lord as a Man. 

What man is like when left to himself appears clearly from those in Hell. Among them are some high priests <note>original: "Antistites"</note> and learned men who do not even want to hear about God, and therefore cannot even name Him. I have seen these and spoken with them. I have also spoken with those who flew into a fire of anger and rage when they heard someone speaking of the Lord. 

Consider, therefore, what a man would be like who had heard nothing of God, when even some who have spoken, written, and preached about God turn out this way. This happens because the will is evil, and the will—as said before—leads the Intellect and casts out the truth that is there from the Word. 

If man could have known of himself that there is a God and a life after death, why had he not known that a man remains a man after death? Why does he believe that his soul or spirit is like wind or ether, which does not see with eyes, hear with ears, or speak with a mouth, until it is reunited and fused with its corpse and skeleton? 

Suppose, then, a system of Doctrine excluded from everything but the light of reason: would it not result in the worship of oneself? This has happened for ages, and still happens today among those who know from the Word that God alone is to be worshipped. No other worship can arise from what is man's own—not even the worship of the sun and moon.

275. That religion has existed from the most ancient times, and that inhabitants of the world everywhere have known about God and something of life after death, did not stem from themselves or their own intelligence. Rather, it came from the **Ancient Word** <note>original: "Verbo Vetusto"; Swedenborg refers here to a lost, prehistoric scripture that he believed preceded the Old Testament and was the source of early wisdom.</note> (mentioned above in numbers 264 to 266), and later from the **Israelite Word**. From these two Words, religious ideas emanated into the Indies and their islands, and through Egypt and Ethiopia into the kingdoms of Africa, and from the coastal regions of Asia into Greece, and from there into Italy. 

However, because the Word could only be written through **Representations** <note>In this context, "Representations" or "Correspondences" are physical things in the world that mirror and signify spiritual realities.</note>—which are things in the world that correspond to and thus signify heavenly things—the religious beliefs of the Gentiles were eventually turned into idolatry, and in Greece into myths. The Divine attributes and descriptions were turned into as many gods, over whom they placed a supreme deity whom they called **Jove** <note>original: "Jovem"; Jupiter</note>, perhaps derived from **Jehovah**. It is well known that they possessed knowledge of Paradise, the Flood, the sacred fire, and the four ages—from the first, the Golden Age, to the last, the Iron Age—as seen in Daniel chapter 2:31–35.

276. Those who believe they can, by their own intelligence, procure for themselves knowledge of God, Heaven and Hell, and the spiritual matters belonging to the Church, do not realize that the **natural man**, viewed in himself, is opposed to the **spiritual man**. Therefore, the natural man desires to uproot the spiritual things that enter him, or to entangle them in fallacies, which are like worms that consume the roots of vegetables and crops. 

Such people may be compared to those who dream they are sitting upon eagles and are carried on high; or upon **Pegasus** and are flying over Mount Parnassus to Helicon; whereas in reality they are like **Lucifers** in Hell, who even there still call themselves "sons of the morning" (*Isaiah 14:12*). They are like those in the Valley of the Land of **Shinar**, who attempted to build a tower whose top would reach into Heaven (*Genesis 11:2, 4*); and they trust in themselves like **Goliath**, not foreseeing that they might, like him, be struck down by a stone from a sling hitting the forehead. I will describe the lot that awaits them after death: first they become as if drunk, then as if foolish, and finally they become stupid and sit in darkness. Therefore, let them beware of such a delirium.

277. To this I will add the following **MEMORABLE RELATIONS** <note>original: "MEMORABILIA"; these are narrated accounts of Swedenborg’s purported visions or interactions in the spiritual world, intended to illustrate his theological points.</note>:

**FIRST:** One day, while traveling in the spirit through various places in the spiritual world, for the purpose of observing the **Representations** of heavenly things exhibited in many places there, I saw a certain house where angels were. In it, I saw large **purses** <note>original: "Crumenas"</note> in which a great abundance of silver was stored. Because they were open, it seemed as if anyone could take out the silver deposited there, or even plunder it. However, near those purses sat two youths who were guards. The place where they were stored looked like a manger in a stable.

In the next room, I saw modest virgins along with a chaste wife; and near that room stood two infants. It was said that they were not to be played with in a childish way, but treated with wisdom. Afterward, a harlot appeared, and then a horse lying dead.

After these things were seen, I was instructed that they represented the **natural sense of the Word**, within which is the **spiritual sense**. Those large purses full of silver signified the knowledge of truth in great abundance. That they were open, yet guarded by youths, signified that anyone could take knowledge of truth from the Word, but care is taken lest anyone violate the spiritual sense, which contains pure truths. The manger, as in a stable, signified spiritual nourishment for the intellect; a manger has this significance because a **horse**, which eats from it, signifies the **intellect**. 

The modest virgins seen in the next room signified affections for truth, and the chaste wife signified the marriage of good and truth. The infants signified the innocence of wisdom; for the angels of the highest heaven, who are the wisest, appear from a distance as infants because of their innocence. The harlot with the dead horse signified the falsification of truth by many today, by which all understanding of truth... <note>The sentence ends abruptly as the page concludes.</note>

278. **THE SECOND MEMORABLE RELATION.** Once, a small paper written in Hebrew letters was sent down to me from Heaven, but they were written as they were among the Ancients. Among those people, the letters—which today are partially linear—were curved with little horns <note>original: "corniculis"; refers to the decorative flourishes or "tittles" on Hebrew script</note> pointing upwards. They explained what they signified individually and what they signified when joined together. They also explained in my presence the meaning of the Word in *Psalm 32:2* from the letters or syllables alone; they said that the summary of their meaning was **THAT THE LORD IS MERCIFUL EVEN TO THOSE WHO DO EVIL.**

They informed me that writing in the Third Heaven consists of letters that are curved and variously twisted, each of which contains a certain meaning. They said that vowels there are used for sound, which corresponds to affection, and that in that Heaven they cannot pronounce the vowels *i* and *e*, but instead use *y* and *eu*. The vowels *a*, *o*, and *u* are in use because they give a full sound. Furthermore, they do not pronounce any consonant letters harshly, but softly. This is why certain Hebrew letters have dots inside them as a sign that they are to be pronounced softly. They said that harshness in letters is used in the spiritual Heaven because those there are in truths, and truth allows for harshness, whereas good—in which the angels of the Lord’s celestial kingdom or the Third Heaven dwell—does not. They also said they possessed the Word written among them in curved letters with significant horns and tips. From this, it became clear what these words of the Lord mean: *"Not one jot or one tittle shall pass from the law, till all be fulfilled"* (*Matthew 5:18*), and *"It is easier for heaven and earth to pass, than one tittle of the law to fail"* (*Luke 16:17*).

279. **THE THIRD MEMORABLE RELATION.** Seven years ago, when I was collecting those things that *Moses* wrote from those two books called THE WARS OF JEHOVAH and THE ENUNCIATES <note>original: "Bella Jehovae & Enuntiata"; these are lost ancient books mentioned in the Bible in Numbers 21:14 and 21:27</note> (*Numbers 21*), some angels were present and told me that those books were the **Ancient Word**. Its historical parts were called THE WARS OF JEHOVAH, and its prophetic parts were called THE ENUNCIATES. They said that this Word is still preserved in Heaven and is used among the Ancients there, who possessed that Word when they were in the world. 

Those Ancients among whom that Word is preserved in Heaven were partly from the land of *Canaan* and its borders, such as *Syria*, *Mesopotamia*, *Arabia*, *Chaldea*, *Assyria*, *Egypt*, *Zidon*, *Tyre*, and *Nineveh*. The inhabitants of all these kingdoms practiced representative worship and were therefore skilled in the **Science of Correspondences** <term>Science of Correspondences: The ancient knowledge of how physical things represent spiritual realities</term>. The wisdom of that time came from that science, and through it, they possessed interior perception and communication with the Heavens. Those who knew the correspondences of that Word were called "Wise" and "Intelligent," and later "Diviners" and "Magi." 

But because that Word was full of such correspondences—which signified heavenly and spiritual things in a remote way—it began to be falsified by many. Therefore, by the Lord’s Divine Providence, it vanished over time, and another Word written through correspondences that were not so remote was given: this was the Word given through the Prophets among the children of *Israel*. In this Word, many names of places were retained, not only those in the land of *Canaan* but also those surrounding it in *Asia*, all of which signified things and states of the Church; however, the meanings were derived from that Ancient Word. For that reason, *Abram* was commanded to go into that land, and his descendants through *Jacob* were led into it.

**280. THE FOURTH MEMORABLE RELATION.** Once from a distance I saw walkways between rows of trees, and there I saw young men gathered in groups—as many companies as there were circles of people—conversing about matters of wisdom. This was in the spiritual world. I approached, and when I was near, I saw one whom the rest honored as their leader because he excelled in wisdom above the others. When he saw me, he said, "I was surprised as I saw you approaching on the road, for at one moment you came into my sight, and the next you vanished from it; or rather, you were seen by me and then suddenly not seen. Surely you are not in the same state of life as our people."

To this, I replied with a smile: "I am no stage-performer, nor a **Vertumnus** <note>A Roman god of seasons and change, known for his ability to shift shapes</note>, but I am alternating—now in your light, and now in your shadow; thus I am both a foreigner and a native here." At this, the wise man looked at me and said, "You speak strange and wonderful things. Tell me who you are." 

I said, "I am in the world in which you once were, and from which you have departed, which is called the **NATURAL WORLD**; and I am also in the world in which you now are, which is called the **SPIRITUAL WORLD**. This is why I am in a natural state and a spiritual state at the same time: in a natural state with the people of the earth, and in a spiritual state with you. When I am in a natural state, I am not visible to you, but when I am in a spiritual state, I am. That I should be such a person has been granted by the Lord. To you, enlightened man, it is known that a person of the natural world does not see a person of the spiritual world, nor vice versa. Therefore, when I drew my spirit into my body, I was not visible to you, but when I drew it out of the body, I was seen. This occurs because of the distinction between the Spiritual and the Natural."

When he heard about the distinction between the Spiritual and the Natural, he said, "What is this distinction? Is it not like the difference between what is more pure and what is less so? Thus, what is the Spiritual but a purer Natural?" 

I replied, "The distinction is not of that kind. The Natural can never, through any amount of refining, approach the Spiritual so as to become it. For the distinction is like that between the prior and the posterior, between which there is no finite ratio. For the prior is in the posterior as a cause is in its effect, and the posterior exists from the prior as an effect from its cause. This is why one does not appear to the other."

To this the wise man said, "I have meditated on this distinction, but so far in vain; I wish I could perceive it." 

I said, "You shall not only perceive the distinction between the Spiritual and the Natural, you shall even see it." And then I said this: "You are in a spiritual state while you are among your own people, but in a natural state with me. They entered, thought, held the thought, and came out; but when they tried to express the thing they had thought, they could not. They could not find any idea of natural thought adequate to any idea of purely spiritual thought, and thus no words to express it; for the ideas of thought become the words of speech. 

Afterward, they went back in and returned again, confirming for themselves that spiritual ideas were supernatural, inexpressible, ineffable, and incomprehensible to the natural man. Because they are so superior, they said that spiritual ideas or thoughts, compared to natural ones, were the "ideas of ideas" and "thoughts of thoughts," and that therefore through them were expressed the "qualities of qualities" and the "affections of affections." Consequently, spiritual thoughts were the very beginnings and origins of natural thoughts. From this it also became clear that spiritual wisdom was the "wisdom of wisdom," and thus inexpressible to any wise person in the natural world.

Then it was said from a higher heaven that there is yet an even more interior or superior wisdom called **Celestial** <note>In Swedenborg's theology, "Celestial" refers to the highest of the three heavens, characterized by love, while "Spiritual" refers to the middle heaven characterized by intellect</note>. These flow in order according to the heavens from the Divine Wisdom of the Lord, which is Infinite.

To this, the man speaking with me said: "I see this, because I perceive that one natural idea is a container for many spiritual ideas; and also that one spiritual idea is a container for many celestial ideas." ## UNIVERSAL THEOLOGY

<note>This sentence continues from the previous page's discussion on the formation of the mind.</note> ...that form, and the Mind of spirits and **Angels** is formed from spiritual things, and the **Mind** of humans, as long as they live in the **World**, is formed from natural things. After this, a voice was heard from the higher **Heaven** to a certain person who stood by, saying, "Ascend here." He ascended, and upon his return, he said that the **Angels** did not previously know the differences between the <term>Spiritual</term> and the <term>Natural</term> for this reason: because previously, no opportunity for comparison had been granted to any man who was in both **Worlds** at once, and those differences are not knowable without comparison and relation.

Before we departed, we spoke again about this matter, and I said that those distinctions do not exist from any other source than because you in the spiritual **World** are <term>substantial</term> and not material, and <term>substantial</term> things are the beginnings of material things. For what is matter but a gathering of substances? You, therefore, are in the first principles, and thus in individual parts, while we are in the things derived from those principles and in composites. You are in particulars, but we are in generals; and just as general things cannot enter into particular things, so <term>natural</term> things, which are material, cannot enter into <term>spiritual</term> things, which are <term>substantial</term>. It is exactly like a nautical rope that cannot enter or be drawn through the eye of a sewing needle, or like a nerve that cannot be introduced into one of the tiny fibers from which it is made. This is the reason why the **Natural** man cannot think the things that the **Spiritual** man thinks, and therefore cannot speak them; which is why **Paul** calls the things he heard from the <term>Third Heaven</term> <note>original: "ineffabilia"; a reference to 2 Corinthians 12:4 where the apostle Paul describes hearing things "too sacred for words."</note> "unspeakable." 

Furthermore, to think **Spiritually** is to think without time and space, and to think **Naturally** is to think with time and space; for something of time and space clings to every idea of natural thought, but not to any spiritual idea. The reason is that the **Spiritual World** is not in space and time like the natural **World**, but exists in the *appearance* of these two. In this, thoughts and perceptions also differ: wherefore you are able to think of **God’s Essence** and **Omnipresence** from eternity—that is, of **God** before the creation of the **World**—because you think of **God’s Essence** without time, and of His **Omnipresence** without space, and thus you comprehend such things as transcend the natural ideas of man. 

I then related how I once thought about **God’s Essence** and **Omnipresence** from eternity, and because I could not yet remove space and time from the ideas of my thought, I became anxious, because the idea of **Nature** kept entering in place of **God**. But it was said to me, "Remove the ideas of space and time, and you will see." It was granted to me to remove them, and I saw; and from that time I have been able to think of **God** from eternity, and not at all of **Nature** from eternity, because **God** is in all time without being in time, and in all space without being in space. **Nature**, however, in all time is *in* time, and in all space is *in* space; and **Nature** with its time and space could not help but have a beginning. Not so **God**, who is without time and space; wherefore **Nature** is from **God**, not from eternity, but in time together with its own time and space.

II. All the Societies there, which are innumerable, are wonderfully arranged according to natural affections, both good and evil. The Societies arranged according to good natural affections communicate with **Heaven**, and the Societies arranged according to evil affections communicate with **Hell**. 

III. A <term>novice spirit</term> <note>original: "Novitius spiritus"; a person who has recently died and entered the afterlife.</note>, or a Spiritual man, is led and transferred into various Societies, both good and evil, and is explored to see whether he is moved by goods and truths, and in what way, or whether he is moved by evils and falsities, and in what way. 

IV. But this happens to those who lived a life of <term>charity</term> <note>In this context, "charity" refers to active goodwill and moral living, not just giving to the poor.</note> in the World, and thus also a life of faith, which consists in believing in the Lord and fleeing evils as sins.

V. But those who have confirmed themselves in falsities through rationalizations, especially through the **Word** <note>The Holy Scriptures or Bible.</note>, and have thus lived no other life than a merely natural and therefore evil one (for evils accompany falsities, and evils cling to falsities)—these, because they are not moved by goods and truths but by evils and falsities, are led away from good Societies and introduced into evil Societies, and also into various ones, until they come into one corresponding to the lusts of their own love. 

VI. But because in the World they feigned good affections in their external behavior, even though in their internal selves there was nothing but evil affections or lusts, they are held by turns in their external states. Those who were leaders of Assemblies in the World are placed in charge of Societies here and there in the **World of Spirits**, either in general or in part, according to the extent of the offices they previously held. But because they do not love the truth, nor do they love what is just, nor can they be enlightened enough to know what is true and just, they are dismissed after a few days. I have seen such people transferred from one Society to another, and given administration everywhere, but after a short time, they were dismissed just as often.

VII. After frequent dismissals, some—out of weariness—no longer wish to seek offices, while others—out of fear of losing their reputation—do not dare to. Therefore, they withdraw and sit in sadness; then they are led away into a wilderness where there are huts, which they enter. There, some work is given to them to do, and as they do it, they receive food; if they do not do it, they go hungry and receive nothing, so that necessity compels them. The foods there are similar to the foods in our World, but they are of spiritual origin, and are given from **Heaven** by the Lord to everyone according to the uses they perform; to the idle, because they are useless, none are given.

VIII. After some time, they grow weary of the work and leave the huts. If they were **Priests**, they wish to build; and immediately there appear heaps of hewn stones, bricks, beams, and boards, as well as piles of reeds and rushes, clay, lime, and bitumen. When they see these, the lust for building is ignited, and they begin to construct a house, taking now a stone, now wood, now a reed, now mud, and they pile one above another without order, though in their own sight it appears orderly. But what they build during the day falls down at night; yet the next day they gather the fallen material from the rubble and build again, and this continues until they are weary of building. This happens from <term>correspondence</term> <note>The spiritual law where outward surroundings automatically reflect a person's inner thoughts and beliefs.</note>, which is that they have piled up passages from the **Word** to confirm the falsities of their faith; their falsities build a **Church** in no other way.

X. When they have been sent away, their eyes are opened and they see a way leading toward a certain **Cavern**. When they arrive there, a door is opened and they enter, asking if there is food inside. When they are told that there is food, they ask for permission to stay; they are told they may, are led inside, and the door is closed behind them. Their companions also say: "Our Overseer knows what work each person is suited for, and he assigns such work to everyone daily. On the day you finish it, food is given to you; if not, neither food nor clothing is provided." 

If anyone does harm to another, he is cast into a corner of the cavern onto a certain bed of <term>cursed dust</term> <note>original: "pulvere damnato"; likely a reference to a miserable or agonizing place of rest that causes suffering.</note>, where he is miserably tormented until the Overseer sees a sign of repentance in him; only then is he released and ordered back to his work. He is then led further into the cavern where there are <term>harlots</term> <note>original: "Scorta"; in this context, it refers to female spirits associated with these workhouses.</note>, and each man is allowed to take one for himself and call her his woman, but they are forbidden under penalty of punishment to engage in promiscuous debauchery.

Hell consists of many such caverns, which are nothing other than eternal <term>workhouses</term> <note>original: "Ergastula"; a Roman term for a private prison or work-house where slaves or debtors were kept in chains.</note>. Yet they all know no differently than that they were always servants and similar companions." This is because their **interiors** <note>The "inner self" or the true character of the spirit.</note> were similar, even if their exteriors were different, and it is the interior qualities that group people together in the Spiritual World.

Regarding the Hells in general: they consist of nothing but such caverns and workhouses, though they differ depending on whether they house **Satans** or **Devils**. Those who were in falsities and the resulting evils are called **Satans**; those who were in evils and the resulting falsities are called **Devils**. 

In the light of Heaven, **Satans** appear livid like corpses, and some black like mummies; but **Devils** appear in the light of Heaven as a dark, fiery red, and some as black as soot. All of them are monstrous in their faces and bodies. However, in their own light—which is like the light from glowing coals—they do not appear as monsters but as men. This is granted to them so that they are able to live together as a society.

# CHAPTER FIVE
## THE CATECHISM
### OR
# THE DECALOGUE;
## EXPLAINED ACCORDING TO ITS EXTERNAL AND INTERNAL SENSE.

<image-desc>A decorative horizontal border strip consisting of repeating calligraphic scroll and foliage motifs.</image-desc>

282. There is no nation in the whole world that does not know that it is evil to kill, to commit adultery, to steal, and to bear false witness; also, that unless those evils were guarded against by laws, it would be the end for any kingdom, republic, or established society. Who, therefore, can suppose that the Israelite nation was so much more stupid than others that they did not know these were evils? For this reason, one might wonder why those laws—universally known on earth—were proclaimed with such a great miracle from Mount Sinai by <term>Jehovah</term> <note>The personal name of God in the Hebrew Bible, often translated as "The LORD."</note> Himself. But listen: they were proclaimed with such a miracle so that they might know that those laws were not only civil and moral laws, but also Divine Laws; and that to act against them was not only to do evil against a neighbor (that is, a fellow citizen and society), but was also to sin against God. Therefore, through their proclamation from Mount Sinai by Jehovah, those laws were also made laws of religion. It is evident that whatever Jehovah commands, He commands so that it may be a matter of religion, and thus something to be done for the sake of salvation. But before the Commandments are explained, something must be said beforehand regarding their holiness, so that it may be clear that religion is within them.

### *That the Decalogue was Holiness itself in the Israelite Church.*

283. That they were most holy is clearly evident from the following: that the Lord Jehovah Himself descended upon Mount Sinai in fire and with angels, and proclaimed them from there with a living voice; and that the mountain was fenced around so that no one should approach and die; and that neither the priests nor the elders should draw near, but Moses alone. ## UNIVERSAL THEOLOGY

All things of Doctrine and Life relate to love for God and love toward the neighbor; everything regarding these loves is contained in the Decalogue. That the entire Word teaches nothing else is clear from these words of the Lord: *Jesus said, you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind; and your neighbor as yourself;* on these two commandments *hang the Law and the Prophets*, Matthew 22:35–37. *The Law and the Prophets* signify the entire Word. And further, *A certain lawyer testing Jesus said, "Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?" and Jesus said to him, "In the Law what is written? How do you read?" and he answering said, "You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and your neighbor as yourself"; and Jesus said, <term>do this and you shall live</term> <note>original: "hoc fac et vives."</note>,* Luke 10:25 to 28. Now, because love for God and love toward the neighbor are the whole of the Word, and the Decalogue in its First Table contains in summary all things of love for God, and in the Second Table all things of love toward the neighbor, it follows that it contains all things that belong to Doctrine and Life. From the appearance of the two Tables, it is clear that they are so joined that God from His Table looks to man, and man from his Table looks to God in return; and thus there is a <term>reciprocal looking</term> <note>original: "Aspectus reciprocus." This describes a mutual relationship where God's gaze and man's gaze meet through the medium of the Law.</note>, which is of such a nature that on God’s part it is never lacking—He constantly looks to man and works for those things which belong to his salvation—and if man receives and does those things which are in his own Table, a reciprocal conjunction is formed, and then it happens according to the Lord’s words to the lawyer: *Do this and you shall live.*

288. In the Word, the <term>Law</term> is named very often; we shall state what is understood by it in the <term>strict sense</term>, what in the broader, and what in the broadest sense. [the Word] stores away two interior senses, one called the Spiritual and the other the Celestial, and in these senses Divine Truth is in its light and Divine goodness is in its heat. 290. Unless one knows the nature of the Word, they cannot grasp by any idea that there is an infinity in its individual parts—that is, that it contains innumerable things which not even the Angels can exhaust. Everything there can be compared to a seed, which can grow from the ground into a great tree and produce an abundance of seeds, from which similar trees can grow again, making a garden; and from its seeds, gardens again, and so on to infinity. Such is the Word of the Lord in its individual parts, and such is especially the Decalogue; for because it teaches love to God and love toward the neighbor, it is a brief summary of the entire Word. The Lord also explains that the Word is like this through a comparison: *The Kingdom of God is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took and sowed in his field; which is less than all seeds, but when it has grown, it is greater than the herbs, and becomes a tree, so that the birds of heaven come and nest in its branches,* Matthew 13:31, 32; Mark 4:31, 32; Luke 13:18, 19. Compare also Ezekiel, Chapter 17:2 to 8. That there is such an infinity of spiritual seeds or truths in the Word can be seen from <term>Angelic Wisdom</term> <note>original: "Sapientia Angelica." This refers to the higher level of understanding possessed by those in the spiritual world, which is drawn directly from the internal meaning of the Word.</note>, all of which is from the Word; this wisdom grows among them forever, and the wiser they become, the more clearly they see that wisdom is without end. They perceive that they are merely in its courtyard and cannot reach, even in the smallest degree, the Divine Wisdom of the Lord, which they call the <term>Abyss</term> <note>original: "Abyffus." Here used to describe the unfathomable depth and source of Divine knowledge.</note>. Now, since the Word is from this Abyss because it is from the Lord, it is evident that in all its parts there is a certain Infinity.

# THE FIRST COMMANDMENT.

## *You shall have no other God before my face.*

291. These are the words of the First Commandment, Exodus 20:3; Deuteronomy 5:7. By these, in the **NATURAL SENSE**, which is the sense of the letter, it is most directly understood that idols must not be worshiped; for it follows: *You shall not make for yourself a carved image or any likeness of what is in the heavens above, or what is on the earth below, or what is in the waters under the earth: you shall not bow yourself down to them, and you shall not worship them, because I am JEHOVAH YOUR GOD, A JEALOUS GOD,* Exodus 20:4, 5, 6. The reason why this Commandment directly meant that idols were not to be worshiped was that before this time, and after it until the Coming of the Lord, idolatrous worship prevailed in much of the <term>Asian world</term> <note>original: "Orbe Asiatico." A historical term for the Near East and surrounding regions where ancient civilizations practiced polytheism.</note>. The cause of that worship was that all Churches before the Lord were representative and typical; and the types and representations were such that Divine things were presented under various figures and sculptures. When the meanings of these figures were forgotten, the common people began to worship them as gods. That the Israelite nation was also in such worship while in Egypt can be seen from the Golden Calf, which they worshiped in the wilderness instead of Jehovah; and that they were not afterwards estranged from that worship is clear from many places in the Word, both historical and prophetic.

292. By this Commandment, *You shall have no other God before my face*, in the natural sense it is also understood that no man, whether deceased or living, should be worshiped as a God. This was also practiced in the Asian world and various places around it. Many gods of the Gentiles were nothing more than men, such as Baal, Ashtoreth, Chemosh, Milkom, and Beelzebub; and at Athens and Rome: Saturn, Jupiter, Neptune, Pluto, Apollo,

293. In the **Natural Sense**, which is the sense of the letter, this Commandment also means that no person besides God, and nothing besides that which proceeds from God, is to be loved above all things. This is also according to the words of the Lord in Matthew 22:35 to 37 and Luke 10:25 to 28; for he who and that which is loved above all things is, to the lover, God and Divine. Just as he who loves himself or the world above all things, to him he himself or the world is his God; this is the reason why such people do not acknowledge any God in their hearts. Therefore, these individuals are joined with their like in Hell, where all are gathered who have loved themselves and the world above all things.

294. The **Spiritual Sense** of this Commandment is that no other God than the Lord JESUS CHRIST is to be worshipped, because He is Jehovah, who came into the world and performed the <term>Redemption</term><note>In this context, Redemption refers to the process by which the Lord reordered the spiritual world and subdued the power of hell to allow human freedom.</note>, without which no human being nor any Angel could have been saved. That there is no other God besides Him is evident from these passages in the Word:

"**Jehovah** my Rock and my Redeemer," Psalm 19:14. "Thus said **Jehovah** your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: I am **Jehovah** your God," Isaiah 48:17; Chapter 43:24; Chapter 49:7; Chapter 8. This is the spiritual sense of this Commandment.

295. The **Celestial Sense** of this Commandment is that Jehovah the Lord is Infinite, Immense, and Eternal; that He is Omnipotent, Omniscient, and Omnipresent; that He is the First and the Last, the Beginning and the End, Who Was, Is, and Is to Come; that He is Love itself and Wisdom itself, or Goodness itself and Truth itself, and thus Life itself; thus the Only One from Whom all things are.

Those who acknowledge and worship the one who is Jehovah God Himself in Human form, <note>In Swedenborgian theology, this refers to Jesus Christ as the physical manifestation of the one invisible God.</note> and those who do otherwise, sin against this First Precept. Likewise, so do those who persuade themselves of three Divine Persons actually existing from eternity. As these people confirm themselves in that error, they become more and more natural and corporeal; <note>“Natural and corporeal” here describes a state of mind focused only on physical reality and the senses, unable to perceive deeper spiritual truths.</note> they then cannot comprehend any interior Divine Truth, and if they hear and receive it, they nonetheless pollute and shroud it with fallacies. For this reason, such people may be compared to those who live in the lowest or subterranean floor of a house, and therefore do not hear anything that those in the second and third floors speak among themselves, because the ceilings above their heads prevent the sound from penetrating. The human mind is like a house of three stories: in the lowest are those who have confirmed themselves in the belief of three Gods from eternity; in the second and third are those who acknowledge and believe in one God under a visible Human form, and that the Lord God the Savior is He. The sensual and corporeal man, because he is merely natural, is—when viewed in himself—utterly like an animal; he differs no more from a brute beast than in being able to speak and reason. Therefore, he is like someone living in a bestiary <note>A place where wild animals are kept; a menagerie.</note> among wild beasts of every kind, where he acts now the lion, now the bear, now the tiger, the leopard, or the wolf; indeed, he can even act the sheep, but then in his heart he laughs. The merely natural man does not think of Divine truths except from worldly things, and thus from the fallacies of the senses, for he cannot elevate his mind above them. Therefore, the doctrine of his faith may be compared to a pottage made of straw, which he eats as a delicacy; or as was commanded to the Prophet Ezekiel, that he should mix wheat, barley, beans, lentils, and spelt with human or bovine dung, and make himself bread and cakes, and thus represent the Church as it was among the Israelite nation (Chapter 4:9 and following). It is similar with the doctrine of a Church that is founded and built upon three Divine Persons from eternity, each of whom is individually God. Who would not see the enormity of such a faith if it were presented as it is in itself, in a picture before the eyes? For instance, if three stood in order next to one another: the first marked with a scepter and crown; the second holding in his right hand a Book (which is the Word) and in his left a Cross of gold sprinkled with blood; and the third girded with wings, standing on one foot in an effort to fly and work—above whom was written: **THESE THREE PERSONS, BEING AS MANY GODS, ARE ONE GOD.** What wise man, seeing this picture, would not say to himself, "Alas, what a fantasy!" But he would say something else if he saw a painting of one Divine Person with rays of heavenly light around his head, with the inscription: **THIS IS OUR GOD, AT ONCE CREATOR, REDEEMER, AND REGENERATOR, THUS SAVIOR.** Would not that wise man kiss this picture, carry it home in his bosom, and by the sight of it gladden his own mind and those of his wife, children, and servants?

# SECOND COMMANDMENT.

->*Thou shalt not take the Name of Jehovah thy God in vain, for Jehovah will not hold him guiltless who takes His Name in vain.*<-

297. By taking the Name of Jehovah God in vain, in the **NATURAL SENSE** (which is the sense of the letter), is meant the Name itself and its abuse in various conversations, especially in false speech or lies, and in oaths without cause, or for the purpose of exculpation in evil intentions (which are curses), and in sorceries and incantations. But to swear by God and His Holiness, the Word, and the Gospel, at Coronations, in Ordinations to the Priesthood, or in oaths of loyalty, is not taking the Name of God in vain, unless the swearer later rejects his promises as vain. The Name of God, however, because it is Holiness itself, is constantly used...

it must be displayed in the holy things that belong to the Church, such as in prayers, psalms, and in all worship, as well as in preaching and in writings on ecclesiastical matters. The reason for this is that God is in everything regarding religion, and when He is rightly invoked, He is present through His name and hears; in these things, the Name of God is sanctified. That the name **JEHOVAH** <note>original: "Jehovah." In the Hebrew tradition, the four-letter name of God (YHWH) was considered too holy to speak aloud.</note> God is holy in itself is evident from that Name; for after their earliest times, the Jews did not dare, nor do they now dare, to say "Jehovah." For their sake, the Evangelists and Apostles likewise did not wish to use it, which is why they said "Lord" instead of Jehovah. This is clear from various passages translated from the Old Testament into the New, where the Lord is named in place of **JEHOVAH**, such as in Matthew 22:35 and Luke 10:27, when compared with Deuteronomy 6:5, and elsewhere. That the name of Jesus is similarly holy is known from the Apostle saying that at that name every knee should bow, in heaven and on earth; and furthermore, that it cannot even be spoken by any devil in Hell. The names of God are many, and they are not to be taken in vain, such as Jehovah, Jehovah God, Jehovah of Hosts <note>original: "Jehovah Zebaoth," a title emphasizing God's omnipotence and command over the "armies" of heaven.</note>, the Holy One of Israel, Jesus and Christ, and the Holy Spirit.

298. In the **SPIRITUAL SENSE**, the "Name of God" means everything that the Church teaches from the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scripture or the Bible.</note>, and through which the Lord is invoked and worshiped. All those things together are the Name of God in its entirety. Therefore, "taking the Name of God in vain" means taking anything from those teachings and using it in idle talk, false speech, lies, curses, sorcery, or incantations; for this is also to revile and blaspheme God, and thus His Name. That the Word—and what the Church derives from it, and thus all worship—is the Name of God, can be seen from these passages: *From the rising of the sun my name shall be invoked* (Isaiah 26:8, 13). *From the rising of the sun even to its setting, my Name shall be great among the nations; and in every place incense shall be offered to my Name. You profane my Name when you say, "The table of Jehovah is polluted," and you sneer at my Name when you bring what is stolen, lame, and sick* (Malachi 1:11, 12, 13). *All peoples walk in the name of their god, and we will walk in the name of Jehovah our God* (Micah 4:5). *They shall worship Jehovah in one place where He shall put His Name* (Deuteronomy 12:5, 11, 13, 14, 18; Chapter 16:2, 6, 11, 15, 16), which means where He shall place His worship. *Jesus said, where two or three are gathered in my name, there am I in the midst of them* (Matthew 18:20). *As many as received Him, to them gave He power to be the sons of God, even to them that believe in His name* (John 1:12). *He who does not believe is judged already, because he has not believed in the Name of the only-begotten Son of God* (John 3:17). *Those who believe shall have life in His Name* (John 20:3). *Jesus said, I have manifested Your name to men, and I have made known Your name to them* (John 17:26). *The Lord said, I have a few names in Sardis* (Revelation 3:4). In these and many other places, the "Name of God" means the Divine quality that proceeds from God, and through which He is worshiped. Furthermore, by the name **JESUS CHRIST** is meant everything regarding Redemption, and everything regarding His Doctrine, and thus everything regarding salvation; by "Jesus" is meant all salvation through Redemption, and by "Christ" all salvation through His Doctrine.

299. In the **CELESTIAL SENSE** <note>In Swedenborg's levels of meaning, the "Celestial" sense is the highest, relating to the deepest love for the Lord and the inner nature of His divinity.</note>, by "taking the Name of God in vain" is meant what the Lord said to the Pharisees: *Every sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven man, but the blasphemy of the Spirit shall not be forgiven* (Matthew 12:31). By "blasphemy of the Spirit" is meant blasphemy against the Divinity of the Lord’s Humanity, and against the holiness of the Word. That the Divine Human <term>Divine Human: The theological concept that God's humanity is not separate from His divinity, but is itself Divine.</term> of the Lord is meant by the Name of Jehovah God in the celestial or supreme sense is evident from these words: *Jesus said, **FATHER, GLORIFY YOUR NAME**, and a voice came out of heaven saying, I have both glorified it and will glorify it again* (John 12:28). *Whatever you shall ask in my name, that will I do, that the Father may be glorified in the Son; if you shall ask anything in my name, I will do it* (John 14:13, 14). In the Lord’s Prayer <note>original: "Oratione Dominica."</note>, the phrase *Hallowed be Thy name* signifies nothing else in the celestial sense; the same applies to the "Name" in Exodus 23:21 and Isaiah 63:16. Since the blasphemy of the Spirit shall not be forgiven a person according to the words in Matthew 12:31, 32, and this in the [Celestial] Sense...

in the celestial sense; therefore, this is added to this Commandment: *For Jehovah will not hold him guiltless who takes His Name in vain.*

300. That by a person's name is meant not only the name itself, but also their entire quality <note>original: "quale." In this context, it refers to the person’s inner character, essence, or "what kind" of person they are.</note>, is clear from names in the **Spiritual World**. There, no one retains the name they received at baptism, or from their father or ancestry in the world. Instead, everyone there is named according to their character, and the Angels are named according to their moral and spiritual life. These are the ones meant by the Lord’s words: *Jesus said, I am the good Shepherd; the sheep hear his voice, and he calls his own sheep by Name, and leads them out* (John 10:3). Likewise by these words: *I have a few Names in Sardis who have not defiled their garments: He who overcomes, I will write upon him the Name of the city of the New Jerusalem, and my new Name* (Revelation 3:4, 12). Gabriel and Michael are not the names of two specific Persons in Heaven, but by those Names are meant all in Heaven who are in wisdom concerning the Lord and who worship Him. <note>In this theological system, angelic names often represent specific functions or groups of angels rather than solitary individuals.</note> Furthermore, by the Names of Persons and places in the Word, persons and places are not meant, but rather matters of the Church. In the natural world, a Name does not just mean a name alone, but simultaneously the quality of the person, because this quality adheres to their name. In common speech, for instance, it is said: "he does this for the sake of his name," or "for the reputation of his name," or "he has a great name." By this it is signified that he is celebrated for the things that are within him, such as his ingenuity, learning, merits, and so forth. Who does not know that someone who disparages and slanders someone’s Name also disparages and slanders the actions of their life? In our minds, they are joined together, and thus the reputation of the name perishes. Similarly, whoever speaks the Name of a King, Duke, or Nobleman in a shameful way also brings reproach upon their Majesty and Dignity. Likewise, whoever speaks someone’s Name with a tone of contempt also vilifies the acts of their life at the same time. It is the same with every Person; according to the laws of all Kingdoms, it is not permitted to blast or attack someone’s Name—that is, their character and resulting reputation—with insults.

## THE THIRD COMMANDMENT.

> *Remember the Sabbath Day, to keep it holy; six days shalt thou labor,*
> *and do all thy work, but the seventh day is the Sabbath*
> ->to Jehovah thy God.<-

301. That this is the Third Commandment may be seen in Exodus 20:8, 9, 10, and Deuteronomy 5:12, 13. By this, in the **NATURAL SENSE**, which is the <term>literal sense</term>, it is meant that six days are for man and his labors, and the Seventh is for the Lord, and for man’s rest from Him. "Sabbath" in the original language signifies Rest. <note>The Hebrew word *shabbat* literally means "to cease" or "to rest."</note> Among the children of Israel, the Sabbath was the "Holiness of holinesses" because it represented the Lord: the six days represented His labors and battles with the Hells, and the Seventh represented His victory over them, and thus His Rest. Because that day was representative of the conclusion of the Lord's entire work of Redemption, it was Holiness itself. However, when the Lord came into the World, and consequently the representations of Him ceased, this Day became a day of instruction in Divine things, and thus also a day of rest from labors, and of meditation on such things as concern salvation and eternal life, as well as a day of love toward the neighbor. That it became a day of instruction in Divine things is clear from the fact that the Lord taught in the Temple and Synagogues on that Day (Mark 6:2; Luke 4:16, 31, 32; 13:10). It is also clear from His saying to the healed man, *Take up your bed and walk*, and to the Pharisees, that it was lawful for the Disciples to pluck ears of grain and eat on the Sabbath day (Matthew 12:1–9; Mark 2:23 to the end; Luke 6:1–6; John 5:9–19); by each of which...

In the **spiritual sense**, this signifies being instructed in matters of doctrine; that this Day was also made a Day of love toward the neighbor is evident from those things which the Lord did and taught on the Sabbath day (Matthew 12:10–14; Mark 3:1–9; Luke 6:6–12; Chapter 13:10–18; Chapter 14:1–7; John 5:9–19; Chapter 7:22, 23; Chapter 9:14, 16). From all these instances, it is clear why the Lord said that He is also the Lord of the Sabbath (Matthew 12:8; Mark 2:28; Luke 6:5); and because He said this, it follows that the day was a representation of Himself.

302. By this Commandment in the <term>Spiritual Sense</term> <note>original: "Sensu Spirituali"</note> is signified the Reformation and Regeneration of man by the Lord. The "six days of labor" signify the struggle against the flesh and its lusts, and at the same time against the evils and falsities that are within a person from Hell; and the "Seventh day" signifies his conjunction with the Lord, and through that, regeneration. That spiritual Labor continues as long as that struggle lasts, but that when the person is regenerated, they find Rest, will be clear from those things which will be said later in the Chapter on <term>Reformation and Regeneration</term> <note>original: "Reformatione & Regeneratione"</note>; especially from these points there: I. *That Regeneration occurs in a manner similar to how a person is conceived, carried in the womb, born, and educated.* II. *That the first act of the new Generation is called Reformation, which pertains to the understanding; and its second act is called Regeneration, which pertains to the Will and then to the understanding.* III. *That the Internal man must be reformed first, and through it, the External.* IV. *That then a struggle arises between the Internal and External man, and that whoever conquers rules over the other.* V. *That the Regenerated person has a new Will and a new Understanding,* etc. The reason that the reformation and regeneration of man is signified by this Commandment in the spiritual sense is because it coincides with the Lord’s labors and struggles against the Hells, and His Victory over them, and then His Rest; for in the same way that the Lord glorified His Human and made it Divine, He also reforms and regenerates man, and makes him spiritual. This is what is meant by <term>Following Him</term> <note>original: "Sequi Ipsum"</note>. That the Lord’s struggles were called "Labors" is evident in Isaiah (Chapters 53 and 63); and that similar things are called "Labors" regarding men (Isaiah 65:23; Revelation 2:2, 3).

303. In the <term>Celestial Sense</term> <note>original: "Sensu Cælesti"</note>, this Commandment means conjunction with the Lord, and thereafter Peace, because of protection from Hell. For by the "Sabbath" is signified Rest, and in this highest sense, Peace; wherefore the Lord is called the Prince of Peace, and also calls Himself Peace, as is clear from these passages: *A Child is born to us, a Son is given to us, upon whose shoulder is the Sovereignty, and His Name shall be called Wonderful, Counselor, God, Hero, Father of Eternity, Prince of Peace; of the increase of His Sovereignty and Peace there shall be no end* (Isaiah 9:5, 6). *Jesus said, Peace I leave with you, <term>My Peace</term> I give to you* (John 14:27). *Jesus said, these things I have spoken, that <term>in Me you may have Peace</term>* (John 16:33). *How delightful upon the mountains are the feet of him who brings good tidings and makes <term>Peace</term> to be heard, saying, Your King reigns* (Isaiah 52:7). *Jehovah will redeem my soul in Peace* (Psalm 55:18).

-> <term>THE WORK OF JEHOVAH IS PEACE, THE LABOR OF JUSTICE IS REST, AND SECURITY FOREVER, THAT THEY MAY DWELL IN A HABITATION OF PEACE, AND IN TENTS OF SECURITY, AND IN QUIET RESTING PLACES</term> (Isaiah 32:17, 18). <-

*Jesus said to the Seventy whom He sent out: into whatever house you enter, first say <term>Peace of the Lord</term>, and if a <term>son of Peace</term> is there, your Peace shall rest upon him* (Luke 10:5, 6; Matthew 10:12, 13, 14). *Jehovah will speak <term>Peace</term> to His people; <term>Justice and Peace shall kiss each other</term>* (Psalm 85:8, 10). When the Lord Himself appeared to the Disciples, He said, <term>Peace be with you</term> (John 20:19, 21, 26). What Peace is in its essence—in which the Angels of Heaven and those who are in the Lord find themselves—may be seen in the work on <term>Heaven and Hell</term> <note>original: "Cælo et Inferno"</note> (numbers 284 to 290). From these things it is also clear why the Lord calls Himself the Lord of the Sabbath—that is, of Rest and Peace.

## THE FOURTH COMMANDMENT.

->***Honor your Father and your Mother, that your days may be prolonged, and that it may be well with you upon the earth.***<-

305. This Commandment is read thus in Exodus 20:12, and Deuteronomy 5:16. By *honoring your Father and your Mother* in the **NATURAL SENSE**, which is the sense of the letter, is understood honoring parents, obeying them, being devoted to them, and giving thanks to them for their benefits—which are that they feed and clothe them, and introduce them into the world so that they may act as civil and moral persons within it; and also into Heaven through the precepts of religion, thus consulting their temporary prosperity and also their eternal happiness; and they do all these things out of the love in which they are from the Lord, whose place they take. In a relative sense is understood the honor of guardians by wards, if the parents are dead. In a broader sense, by this Commandment is understood honoring the King and magistrates, since these provide for all needs in general, which parents do in particular. In the broadest sense, by this commandment is understood loving the Fatherland, because it nourishes and protects them, wherefore the Fatherland is so called from "Father" <note>In Latin, "Patria" (Fatherland) is derived from "Pater" (Father).</note>; but honors are to be rendered to it and to them by parents, and implanted by them in their children.

306. In the **SPIRITUAL SENSE**, by *honoring Father and Mother* is understood to revere and love God and the Church; in this sense, by Father is understood God, who is the Father of all, and by Mother the Church. Infants and Angels in the Heavens know no other Father nor any other Mother, because they are born anew there by the Lord through the Church; wherefore the Lord says, *Call no man your father on earth, for one is your Father, who is in the Heavens* (Matthew 23:9); these things were said for infants and angels in Heaven, but not for infants and men on earth. The Lord teaches something similar in the common prayer of the Christian Churches: *Our Father, who art in the Heavens, hallowed be Thy Name.* That by Mother in the spiritual sense is understood the Church, is because just as a mother on earth feeds her children with natural food, so the Church feeds them with spiritual food; for which reason the Church is also called Mother everywhere in the Word, as in Hosea: *Plead with* YOUR MOTHER, *she is not my wife, and I am not her husband* (Chapter 2:2, 5). In Isaiah: *Where is the bill of your* MOTHER'S *divorcement, whom I have put away?* (Chapter 50:1) and Ezekiel 16:45; Chapter 19:10. And in the Evangelists: *Jesus stretching out his hand to the Disciples, said, My* MOTHER *and my brothers are those who hear the Word of God and do it* (Matthew 12:48, 49; Mark 3:33, 34, 35; Luke 8:21; John 19:25, 26, 27).

307. In the **CELESTIAL SENSE**, by Father is understood our Lord Jesus Christ, and by Mother the Communion of Saints, by which is understood His Church throughout...

Philip said, show us the Father; Jesus said to him, HE WHO SEES ME SEES THE FATHER; how then do you say, show us the Father? Believe me, that I am in the Father, and the Father is in Me, John 14:7 to 11; Chapter 12:45.
