That by the New Jerusalem is understood the New Church, which is being established by the Lord today, may be seen in *THE APOCALYPSE REVEALED* <note>original: "APOCALYPSIS REVELATA"; a work published by Swedenborg in 1766.</note> numbers 880, 881; this Church, and not the former one, is the Wife and Mother in this sense. The spiritual offspring which are born from this Marriage are the goods of charity and the truths of faith, and those who are in these from the Lord are called children of the marriage, children of God, and born of Him.

308. It must be held that a Divine Sphere of heavenly love continually proceeds from the Lord toward all who embrace the doctrine of His Church, and who—like infants in the world toward their father and mother—obey Him, apply themselves to Him, and wish to be nourished; that is, to be instructed by Him. From this heavenly Sphere arises a Natural Sphere, which is one of love toward infants and children; this is most universal, and affects not only humans, but also birds and beasts, even down to serpents. Not only animate things, but also inanimate things are affected; but so that the Lord might operate into these as He does into spiritual things, He created the Sun to be in the natural world like a Father, and the Earth like a Mother. For the Sun is like a common Father, and the Earth like a common Mother, from whose marriage all the germinations that adorn the surface of the ground exist. From the influx of that heavenly Sphere into the natural world exist those marvelous progressions of vegetation from seed to fruit and to new seeds. From this also it is that there are many kinds of shrubs that turn their faces, as it were, to the Sun during the day, and turn them away when the Sun sets. From this also it is that there are Flowers which open at the rising of the Sun and close at its setting. From this also it is that the songbirds sing sweetly at the first dawn, and likewise after they have been nourished by their mother Earth. These and those honor their father and their mother. All these things are testimonies that the Lord, through the Sun and the Earth in the natural world, provides for all the necessities of the living and the non-living; wherefore it is said in David: *Praise Jehovah from the Heavens, praise Him Sun and Moon; praise Him from the earth, whales and abysses; praise Him fruit tree, all cedars; wild animal and every beast, creeping thing and winged bird; Kings of the earth and all peoples, young men and maidens,* Psalm 148:7 to 12. And in Job: *Ask, I pray, the beasts and they will teach you, or the birds of heaven and they will announce to you, or the shrub of the earth and it will instruct you, and the fish of the sea will tell you; who among all these does not know that the hand of Jehovah has done this,* Chapter 12:7, 8, 9. "Ask and they will teach" signifies to look at, attend to, and judge from them that the Lord Jehovih <note>original: "Dominus Jehovih"; a specific Hebrew form of the name of God often used by the author to denote the Lord in respect to his divine power and love.</note> created them.

# THE FIFTH COMMANDMENT.

## *You Shall Not Kill.*

309. By this Commandment, *You shall not kill*; in the NATURAL SENSE <term>Natural sense: the most literal level of meaning, relating to physical life and worldly behavior</term> it is understood not to *Kill* a human being, and not to inflict any wound from which they might die, and also not to mutilate their body; and furthermore not to bring any deadly harm to their name and reputation, since reputation and life go hand in hand for many. In a broader natural sense, murders include enmities, hatreds, and desires for revenge, which breathe out slaughter; for in those things murder lies hidden, just as fire lies in wood beneath the ash. Infernal fire is nothing else, which is why it is said to burn with hatred and glow with revenge. These are Murders in intention, though not in act; and if the fear of the law and of retaliation and revenge were removed from them, they would break out into the act—especially if the intention contains deceit or ferocity. That hatred is murder is evident from these words of the Lord: *You have heard that it was said by those of old, you shall not kill; and whoever kills shall be liable to judgment: But I say to you, that whoever is angry with his brother rashly shall be liable to the fire of Gehenna* <note>original: "gehennæ ignis"; Matthew 5:21-22. The author emphasizes that internal anger is the seed of physical murder.</note>. The reason is that everything which belongs to the intention also belongs to the will, and is thus essentially the act itself.

310. In the SPIRITUAL SENSE <term>Spiritual sense: the level of meaning relating to the life of the soul and the church</term>, by murders are understood all ways of killing and destroying the Souls of men, which are various and many, such as turning them away from God, Religion, and Divine Worship by throwing scandals against those things and by persuading them of such things as cause aversion and even loathing. All the devils and satans in Hell are of this kind, and those who violate and prostitute the holy things of the Church in this world are joined with them. Those who destroy Souls through falsehoods are understood by the King of the abyss, called Abaddon or Apollyon <note>original: "Abaddon aut Apollyon"; Revelation 9:11. These names mean "Destroyer" in Hebrew and Greek respectively.</note>, that is, the destroyer; and in the Prophetic Word by the Slain, as in these passages: *Jehovah God said, feed the sheep of the Slaughter, whom their possessors have killed*, Zechariah 11:4, 5, 7. *We are killed all day long, we are accounted as a flock for the slaughter*, Psalm 44:22. *Jacob shall cause those who come to take root, for he is killed according to the slaughter of his Slain*, Isaiah 27:6, 7. *The stranger does not come except to steal and to slaughter the sheep; I have come so that they may have life and abundance*, John 10:10; besides elsewhere, as in Isaiah 14:21, Chapter 26:21, Chapter 27:9, Jeremiah 4:31, Chapter 12:3, Revelation 9:4, Chapter 11:7. This is why the Devil is called a *Murderer from the beginning*, John 8:44.

311. In the CELESTIAL SENSE <term>Celestial sense: the highest level of meaning, relating to love for the Lord and the heavens</term>, by Killing is understood to be rashly angry with the Lord, to hold Him in hatred, and to wish to blot out His name. These are they of whom it is said that they crucify Him; which they would also do just as the Jews did if He were to come into the World as He did before. This is understood by the *Lamb standing as if slain*, Revelation 5:6, Chapter 13:8, and by the *Crucified*, Revelation 11:8, Hebrews 6:6, Galatians 3:1.

312. What the Internal of a man is like, unless it is reformed by the Lord, has been made clear to me from the devils and satans in Hell. For these continually carry in their minds the desire to kill the Lord; and because they cannot do this, they are in the effort of killing those who are devoted to the Lord. But since they cannot do this as people do in the World, they attack with every effort to destroy their souls, that is, to destroy faith and charity in them. Hatreds and revenges themselves appear among them like dusky fires and like white fires—hatreds like dusky fires and revenges like white fires—and yet they are not fires, but appearances. The cruelties of their hearts are sometimes seen above them in the air like battles with Angels, and like the slaughter and massacre of them; these are their rages and hatreds against Heaven, from which such dire mockeries arise. # THE SIXTH COMMANDMENT.

->*You Shall Not Commit Adultery.*<-

313. In the Natural Sense <term>Natural Sense: the literal, worldly application of the law to physical behavior</term>, this Commandment is understood to mean not only committing adultery, but also desiring and doing obscene things, and consequently thinking and speaking lasciviously. That merely to lust is to commit adultery is clear from these words of the Lord: *You have heard that it was said by those of old, "You shall not commit adultery"; but I say to you, that if anyone looks at another's wife so as to lust after her, he has already committed adultery with her in his heart*, Matthew 5: 27, 28. The reason is that lust becomes like the deed while it is in the will; for the lure enters only into the understanding, but the intention enters the will, and the intention of lust is the deed itself. However, more on these matters may be seen in the work on *Conjugial Love* <note>Marriage Love</note> and on *Scortatory Love* <note>original: "Amore Scortatorio"; referring to illicit or promiscuous love</note>, published in Amsterdam in the year 1768, which deals with: *the opposition of conjugial love*, nos. 423 to 443; *fornication*, nos. 444 to 460; *adulteries and their types and degrees*, nos. 473 to 499; *the lust of defloration*, nos. 501 to 505; *the lust of varieties*, nos. 506 to 510; *the lust of violation*, nos. 511, 512; *the lust of seducing the innocent*, nos. 513, 514; and *the imputation of both loves, scortatory and conjugial*, nos. 523 to 531. All these things are understood by this Commandment in its Natural Sense.

314. In the Spiritual Sense <term>Spiritual Sense: the internal meaning relating to the soul’s relationship with Divine Truth</term>, by "committing adultery" is meant to adulterate the goods of the Word and to falsify its truths. That this is also understood by "committing adultery" has been unknown until now, because the spiritual sense of the Word has remained hidden. That nothing else is signified by "committing adultery," "adulterating," and "whoring" in the Word is clearly evident from these passages: *Run through the streets of Jerusalem and seek if you can find a man who* ACTS WITH JUDGMENT AND SEEKS THE TRUTH... *when I satisfied them, they committed adultery*, Jeremiah 5:1, 7. *In the prophets of Jerusalem I have seen a horrible thing:* ADULTERATING AND WALKING IN A LIE, Jeremiah 23:14. *They have committed folly in Israel, they have whored, and they have spoken my word falsely*, Jeremiah 29:23. THEY WHORED *because they have forsaken Jehovah*, Hosea 4:7. *I will cut off the soul that looks to mediums and wizards* TO WHORE AFTER THEM, Leviticus 20:5. *No covenant is to be made with the inhabitants of the land, lest they whore after their gods*, Exodus 34:3. Since Babylon <note>Often used by Swedenborg to represent those who use the Church to gain power</note> adulterates and falsifies the Word more than others, she is called the GREAT HARLOT, and these things are said of her in the Apocalypse: *Babylon has made all nations drink from the wine of the wrath of her whoredom*, Chapter 14:8. *The Angel said, I will show you the judgment of...*

That this is the meaning in this sense follows from the previous Spiritual Sense, which is to adulterate the "goods" (the kindness/charity) and falsify the "truths" (the wisdom) of the Word. Those who laugh in their hearts at everything regarding the Church and religion deny and profane the Holiness of the Word; for everything regarding the Church and religion in the Christian world is derived from the Word.

316. There are various reasons that make a person appear chaste, not only to others but even to themselves, while yet they are entirely unchaste. Such a person does not know that lust <note>original: "concupiscentia"</note>, while it is in the will, is equivalent to the act, and that it cannot be removed except by the Lord after repentance. Abstaining from the act does not make one chaste; rather, abstaining from the *will* to do it—when one has the opportunity—because it is a sin, is what makes a person chaste. It is quite different if someone abstains from Adulteries and Whoredom only out of fear of civil law and its penalties; or fear of losing their reputation and honor; fear of diseases; fear of domestic quarrels with a spouse and the resulting unrest; fear of revenge from a husband or relatives, or beatings from their servants; or out of greed; or out of weakness arising from illness, abuse, age, or any other cause of impotence. Indeed, if one abstains from these things based on some natural or moral law, but not simultaneously from a spiritual law, they are still an adulterer and whoremonger inwardly. This is because they still believe these things are not sins, and therefore do not make them unlawful before God in their spirit. Thus, they commit them in spirit even if not in the body before the world. For this reason, after death, when they become a spirit, they speak openly in favor of such acts. Furthermore, adulterers can be compared to treaty-breakers who violate covenants; or to the **Satyrs and Priapi** <note>mythological Greek figures representing unrestrained, often grotesque, sexual lust</note> of the ancients, who wandered in the woods shouting, "Where are the virgins, brides, and wives to play with?" Even in the Spiritual World, adulterers actually appear as Satyrs and Priapi. They can also be compared to stinking goats, or to dogs that run through the streets, looking around and sniffing for other dogs to be wanton with, and so on. Their virile power, when they become husbands, can be compared to the blooming of tulips in the spring, which after a month of days lose their flowers and wither away.

# THE SEVENTH COMMANDMENT.

->*You shall not steal.*<-

317. In the **NATURAL SENSE** <term>Natural Sense: The literal application of the law to physical and social conduct</term>, this Commandment means, according to the letter, not to steal, commit robbery, or act as a pirate in times of peace; and in general, not to take someone else's goods secretly or under any pretext. It also extends to all deceptions and illegal gains, usury <note>charging excessive interest</note>, and extortions; as well as to fraud in paying taxes and duties, or in settling debts. Workers who perform their tasks dishonestly and deceitfully violate this Commandment; so do merchants who cheat in their goods, weights, measures, and accounts; and officials who withhold the pay of soldiers. Judges who rule based on friendship, bribery, family ties, or other...

318. Priests who serve only for the sake of profit or the ambition of honor—and who teach things that they see, or could see from the Word <note>original: "Verbo"; the Holy Scriptures</note>, are not true—are spiritual thieves. This is because they take away from the people the means of salvation, which are the truths of faith. These are also called thieves in the Word in the following places: *He who does not enter by the door into the sheepfold, but climbs up another way, he is a thief and a robber; the thief comes only to steal, to kill, and to destroy*, John 10:1, 10. *Lay up treasures not on earth, but in Heaven, where thieves do not come and steal*, Matthew 6:19, 20. *If thieves come to you, if robbers by night, how you will be cut off! 319. Although these people worship God, they still do not trust in Him, but in themselves; and they do not believe in God, but in themselves.

320. Those who teach falsehoods and heresies and persuade the common people that they are true and orthodox—even though they read the Word and can know from it what is false and what is true—as well as those who confirm the falsehoods of religion through fallacies and seduce others, may be compared to impostors and frauds of every kind. Because these acts are thefts in the spiritual sense, such people can be compared to counterfeiters who strike false coins, gild them, or give them the color of gold, and sell them as pure. They can also be compared to those who know how to skillfully cut and polish crystals and harden them, selling them as diamonds. They are also like those who carry sphinxes or apes dressed as humans, with their faces veiled, through cities on horses or mules, crying out that they are nobles of ancient lineage. They are also like those who apply theatrical masks <note>original: "facies lusorias"</note> painted with colorful pigments over living and natural faces, hiding their true beauty. And they are like those who display selenite <note>A translucent variety of gypsum</note> and mica <note>original: "lapides speculares"</note>, which shine as if made of gold and silver, and sell them as veins of precious metal. They may also be likened to those who lead people away from true Divine Worship in churches to theatrical houses where stage plays are performed. Those who confirm falsehoods of every kind, caring nothing for truths, and who perform the office of the priesthood only for profit and the ambition of honor—and are thus spiritual thieves—can be likened to those thieves who carry master keys <note>original: "claves"</note> with which they can open the doors of all houses; also to leopards and eagles, which look around with sharp eyes for where the richest prey may be.

## THE EIGHTH COMMANDMENT.

->*You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.*<-

321. By this Commandment in a broader Natural Sense are meant all kinds of lies and political hypocrisies which look toward an evil end...

In the broadest **natural sense**, this includes plots, deceits, and evil purposes against anyone from various origins, such as from enmity, hatred, revenge, envy, rivalry, and so on; for these evils hide within themselves the testimony of falsehood.

**322.** In the **SPIRITUAL SENSE** <term>Spiritual Sense: The level of meaning within the Word that relates to the inner life of the spirit and the truths of the church</term>, by "bearing false witness" is meant to persuade others that a falsehood of faith is a truth of faith, and that an evil of life is a good of life, and vice versa. However, this refers to doing so intentionally, and not out of ignorance; that is, to do these things after one knows what is true and good, and not before. For the Lord says: *If you were blind, you would have no sin; but now that you say, "We see," therefore your sin remains*, John 9:41. This falsehood in the Word is understood by "Lie," and the "Purpose" is understood by "Guile" in these places: *We have struck a covenant with death, and with hell we make a vision; we have placed a lie as our trust, and in falsehood we have hidden ourselves*, Isaiah 28:15. *They are a rebellious people, lying children, they do not want to hear the law of Jehovah*, Isaiah 30:9. *From the prophet even to the priest, everyone acts a lie*, Jeremiah 8:10. *The inhabitants speak a lie, and as for the tongue, guile is in their mouth*, Micah 6:12 <note>original: "Mich. V: 12"</note>. *You will destroy those speaking a lie; the man of guile Jehovah abhors*, Psalm 5:6 <note>original: "Psalm V: 7"</note>. *They have taught their tongue to speak a lie; their dwelling is in the midst of guile*, Jeremiah 9:5-6 <note>original: "Jerem. IX: 15"</note>. Because a "Lie" signifies falsehood, the Lord says that the Devil speaks *a lie from his own*, John 8:44 <note>original: "Joh. VIII: 14"</note>. "Lie" signifies falsehood and false speaking also in these places: Jeremiah 9:4; Chapter 23:14, 32; Ezekiel 13:15 to 19; Chapter 21:24; Hosea 7:1; Chapter 12:1; Nahum 3:1; Psalm 120:2, 3.

**323.** In the **CELESTIAL SENSE** <term>Celestial Sense: The highest level of meaning, concerning love for the Lord and the reception of Divine Wisdom</term>, by "bearing false witness" is meant to blaspheme the Lord and the Word, and thus to drive Truth itself away from the Church; for the Lord is Truth itself, and likewise the Word. Conversely, by "Bearing Witness" in this sense is meant to speak the Truth, and by "Testimony" is meant Truth itself; it is for this reason that the Decalogue <note>The Ten Commandments</note> is called the "Testimony," Exodus 25:16, 21, 22 <note>original: "Exod. XXIV: 16"</note>; Chapter 30:7, 18; Chapter 32:15, 16; Chapter 40:20; Leviticus 16:13; Numbers 17:4, 7, 10 <note>original: "Num. XVII: 19, 22, 25"</note>. And because the Lord is Truth itself, He says of Himself that He bears witness. That the Lord is Truth itself, see John 14:6 and Revelation 3:14 <note>original: "Apoc. III"</note>; and that He bears witness and is His own witness, John 3:11; Chapter 8:13 to 19; Chapter 15:26; Chapter 18:37, 38.

**324.** Those who speak falsehoods out of guile or purpose, and utter them with a tone mimicking spiritual affection—and even more so if they interweave truths from the Word which they thus falsify—were called by the Ancients **Enchanters** <note>original: "Incantatores"</note>, concerning whom see *Apocalypse Revealed* <note>A work by Swedenborg published in 1766</note>, n. 462; as well as **Pythons** <term>Python: A term used historically to describe those who speak with a deceptive or oracular spirit, often associated with false divination</term> and **Serpents of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil**. These falsifiers, liars, and deceivers can be likened to those who speak smoothly and politely with enemies, while holding a dagger behind their back with which to kill. They can also be likened to those who dip swords in poison and thus attack enemies; and to those who mix monkshood <note>A highly poisonous plant</note> into waters, and venom into new wine and sugary pastries. They can also be likened to beautiful and alluring harlots infected with a malignant plague; or to thorny bushes which, when brought near the nostrils, hurt the delicate fibers of the sense of smell; or even to sweetened poisons; and also to dung, which when dried in the autumn spreads a fragrant odor. Such people are described in the Word by **leopards** <note>original: "pardos"</note>, see *Apocalypse Revealed*, n. 572.

## THE NINTH AND TENTH COMMANDMENTS.

->*You shall not covet your neighbor’s house; You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his donkey, nor anything that belongs to your neighbor.*<-

**325.** In the catechism currently in use <note>original: "Catechismo, qui hodie in manibus est." Swedenborg refers to the numbering used in the Lutheran and Roman Catholic traditions, where the prohibition against coveting is split into two to maintain the count of ten.</note>, these have been distinguished into two commandments. The **NINTH** is: *You shall not covet your neighbor’s house*; and the **TENTH** is: *You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his donkey, nor anything that belongs to your neighbor.* Because these two commandments deal with a single subject—and in Exodus 20:14 and Deuteronomy 5:18 they form a single verse—I have undertaken to treat them together. I do this not because I wish them to be joined into one commandment, but so they may be distinguished as two, just as before; for these commandments are called the <term>Ten Words: A literal translation of the Hebrew 'Aseret ha-Devarim,' commonly known as the Decalogue or Ten Commandments</term> in Exodus 34:28, Deuteronomy 4:13, and Chapter 10:4.

**326.** These two commandments relate to all the preceding commandments. They teach and enjoin that as evil deeds must not be done, so also they must not be lusted after. Consequently, these commandments belong not only to the **External man**, but also to the **Internal man**. For the person who does not commit evils, yet still lusts to do them, is actually doing them in his spirit. As the Lord says: *If anyone lusts after another's wife, he has already committed adultery with her in his heart* (Matthew 5:27, 28). The external man does not truly become internal—or act as one with the internal—until <term>concupiscences: Strong, disordered desires or lusts for things that are harmful or prohibited</term> have been removed. The Lord also teaches this, saying: *Woe to you, Scribes and Pharisees, for you clean the outside of the cup and the plate, but the insides are full of robbery and lack of self-control. Blind Pharisee, first clean the inside of the cup and plate, so that the outside may also be clean* (Matthew 23:25, 26), and indeed throughout that entire chapter from beginning to end. Those "internal things" which are characteristic of the Pharisees are the lusts for those things forbidden in the First, Second, Fifth, Sixth, Seventh, and Eighth commandments. 

It is well known that while in the world, the Lord taught the internal things of the Church. These internal things consist of not lusting after evils. He taught this so that the internal and external man might act as one; this is what it means to be "born again," of which the Lord spoke to Nicodemus in John 3. No one can be born again or <term>regenerated: The spiritual process of being made new or spiritually reborn through divine influence</term>—and thus become an "internal" person—except by the Lord. 

To ensure these two commandments relate to everything preceding them (enjoining us not to covet them), the "House" is named first, then the "Wife," and then the "manservant, maidservant, ox, and donkey," and finally "everything that belongs to the neighbor." For the "House" includes everything that follows, as the husband, wife, manservant, maidservant, ox, and donkey are within it. The "Wife," who is named next, then includes the things that follow her; for she is the Mistress, just as the husband is the Master in the house, while the servants and animals are under them. Finally, everything that is below or outside of these is covered by the phrase "everything that belongs to your neighbor." From this it is clear that all the previous commandments are regarded in these two, both in general and in particular, and in both a broad and a restricted sense.

**327.** In the **SPIRITUAL SENSE**, these commandments prohibit all <term>lusts: Here, 'concupiscentiæ' refers specifically to desires that oppose spiritual health</term> that are against the spirit—that is, those against the spiritual things of the Church, which primarily relate to faith and charity. Unless these lusts were tamed, the "flesh" would rush into every kind of wickedness according to its own freedom. For it is known from Paul: *The flesh lusts against the spirit, and the spirit against the flesh* (Galatians 5:17); and from James: *Each person is tempted by his own lust, while he is lured away; then Lust, after it has conceived, gives birth to sin; and sin, when it is finished, brings forth* <note>original: "parturit"</note> 
<meta>The text cuts off here with the catchword "parturit," which will be completed on the next page as "parturit mortem" (brings forth death), completing the quotation from James 1:15.</meta>

<summary>This page introduces the Ninth and Tenth Commandments, explaining that while they are often listed separately, they function together to address the internal "lusts" or desires behind all external sins. Swedenborg emphasizes that true spiritual growth (regeneration) requires cleansing the inner mind of these desires, not just following the law outwardly.</summary>

> The Lord reserves the unjust to be punished on the day of judgment, especially those who walk after the flesh in lust,
2nd Epistle 2:9, 10. In short, these two Commandments, when understood in their spiritual sense, refer to all those things previously mentioned in the <term>Spiritual Sense: the deeper, symbolic meaning of scripture that relates to the soul's growth</term> regarding what must not be lusted after; and similarly to all those in the **Celestial Sense**; however, it is unnecessary to repeat those points here.

**328.** The lusts of the flesh, of the eyes, and of the other senses, when separated from the lusts—that is, the affections, desires, and delights—of the spirit, are exactly like the lusts of beasts; for this reason, they are in themselves bestial. But the affections of the spirit are like those of the angels, and therefore are to be called truly human. Consequently, as much as a person indulges in the lusts of the flesh, so much is he a beast and a wild animal; but as much as he <term>litat: sacrifices to or favors</term> the desires of the spirit, so much is he a human and an angel. 

The lusts of the flesh can be compared to parched and burnt grapes or to wild grapes, but the affections of the spirit to succulent and tasty grapes, and also to the taste of the wine pressed from them. The lusts of the flesh can be compared to stables containing donkeys, goats, and pigs, while the affections of the spirit are like stables containing noble horses, as well as sheep and lambs. They differ even as a donkey and a horse, or as a goat and a sheep or lamb, or as a pig; in general, they differ as dross and gold, as lime and silver, as coral and ruby, and so forth. Lust and deed cling together like blood and flesh, or like flame and oil; for lust is within the deed just as air from the lungs is within breathing and speech, as wind is in the sail while the ship moves, or as water is in the wheel that provides the motion and action of a machine.

## *That the Ten Commandments of the Decalogue contain all things belonging to love to God, and all things belonging to love toward the neighbor.*

**329.** In eight of the commandments of the Decalogue—the First, Second, Fifth, Sixth, Seventh, Eighth, Ninth, and Tenth—nothing is said regarding that which belongs to love to God or love toward the neighbor. It is not stated that God must be loved, nor that the Name of God must be hallowed, nor that the neighbor must be loved; thus, it does not say that one must act sincerely and rightly with him. Instead, it says only: *you shall have no other God before my faces; you shall not take the name of God in vain; you shall not kill; you shall not commit adultery; you shall not steal; you shall not bear false witness; you shall not covet those things which are your neighbor's.* Thus, in general, it says that evil must not be willed, thought, or done against God or against the neighbor. 

The reason why such things—which are directly of love and <term>charity: the active practice of love and goodwill</term>—are not commanded, but only those things which are opposite to them and must not be done, is because insofar as a person shuns evils as sins, so far does he will the goods which are of love and charity. That the first part of love to God and love toward the neighbor is *not to do evil*, and the second part is *to do good*, will be seen in the Chapter on CHARITY. These are two opposite Loves: the love of willing and doing good, and the love of willing and doing evil; the latter is infernal love, and the former is heavenly love. For all of Hell is in the love of doing evil, and all of Heaven is in the love of doing good. 

Now, because man is born into evils of every kind, and therefore from birth inclines toward those things which are of Hell, and because he cannot enter Heaven unless he is born again—that is, <term>regenerated: the process of spiritual rebirth and transformation</term>—it is necessary that the evils of Hell be removed first before he can will the goods of Heaven. For no one can be adopted by the Lord before he is separated from the Devil. How these evils are removed and how a person is brought to doing good will be explained in two chapters, one on REPENTANCE and the other on REFOR-

[REFOR]MATION and **REGENERATION**, it will be demonstrated. That evils must first be removed before the good things a person does can become good in the sight of God, the Lord teaches in *Isaiah*: 
> "Wash yourselves, make yourselves clean; remove the evil of your doings from before my eyes; learn to do good; then, if your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; if they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool," Chapter 1:16, 17, 18. 

Similar to this is the passage in *Jeremiah*: 
> "Stand in the gate of the House of Jehovah, and proclaim there this word: Thus says Jehovah of Hosts <note>original: "Jehovah Zebaoth"</note>, the God of Israel: Amend your ways and your doings. Trust not in lying words, saying, 'The Temple of Jehovah, the Temple of Jehovah, the Temple of Jehovah is here' (that is, the Church). Will you steal, murder, commit adultery, and swear falsely, and then come and stand before Me in this House, which is called by My Name, and say, 'We are delivered,' while you do all these abominations? Is this House become a den of thieves? Even I, behold, I have seen it, says Jehovah," Chapter 7:2, 3, 4, 9, 10, 11. 

That prayers to God are not heard before washing or purification from evils is also taught in *Isaiah*: 
> "Jehovah says, woe to the sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity; they have gone away backward; therefore, when you spread forth your hands, I hide my eyes from you; even if you make many prayers, I do not hear," Chapter 1:4, 15. 

That love and charity follow for those who keep the commandments of the Decalogue by fleeing from evils is evident from these words of the Lord in *John*: 
> "Jesus said, he that has my commandments and keeps them, he it is that loves Me; and he that loves Me shall be loved by my Father, and I will love him, and will manifest myself to him, and we will make our abode with him," Chapter 14:21, 23. 

By "commandments" there are specifically understood the precepts of the Decalogue, which state that evils must not be done or lusted after; and thus, a person's love for God and God's love toward the person follow, just as good follows once evil is removed.

**330.** It has been stated that as far as a person flees from evils, so far does he will what is good. The reason is that evils and goods are opposites; for evils are from Hell, and goods are from Heaven. Therefore, as far as Hell (that is, evil) is removed, so far is Heaven approached, and the person looks toward good. That this is so is clearly apparent from the eight commandments of the Decalogue when viewed in this way: 
I. To the extent that one does not worship other gods, to that extent he worships the true God. 
II. To the extent that one does not take the Name of God in vain, to that extent he loves those things which are from God. 
III. To the extent that one does not wish to kill, or to act out of hatred and revenge, to that extent he wishes well to his neighbor. 
IV. To the extent that one does not wish to commit adultery, to that extent he wishes to live chastely with a wife. 
V. To the extent that one does not wish to steal, to that extent he pursues sincerity. 
VI. To the extent that one does not wish to bear false witness, to that extent he wishes to think and speak the truth. 
VII & VIII. To the extent that one does not covet those things which belong to the neighbor, to that extent he wishes for the neighbor to prosper from his own possessions. 

From these it is clear that the commandments of the Decalogue contain all things belonging to love for God and love toward the neighbor. Therefore, Paul says: 
> "He that loves another has fulfilled the law; for this: You shall not commit adultery, You shall not kill, You shall not steal, You shall not bear false witness, You shall not covet; and if there be any other commandment, it is briefly comprehended in this saying, namely, You shall love your neighbor as yourself. Charity <note>original: "Charitas" — often translated as 'Love' or 'Brotherly Love' in this theological context.</note> works no ill to the neighbor; therefore charity is the fulfillment of the Law," Romans 13:8, 9, 10. 

To these should be added two <term>Canons: fundamental principles or rules</term> intended for the use of the New Church: 
I. That no one can flee from evils as sins and do good things that are good in the sight of God from himself; but as far as anyone flees from evils as sins, so far does he do good not from himself, but from the Lord. 
II. That a person ought to flee from evils as sins and fight against them **as if from himself**; but if anyone flees from evils for any other reason than because they are sins, he does not truly flee from them, but merely acts so that they do not appear before the world.

**331.** The reason why evil and good cannot exist together, and why to the extent that evil is removed, good is regarded and felt, is that in the spiritual world a **Sphere** of one's love is exhaled from everyone; this sphere spreads itself around and affects others, causing sympathies and antipathies. By these spheres the good are separated from the evil. That evil must be removed before good is known, perceived, and loved, [is shown...] <meta>catchword: [is shown...] - The Latin catchword 'tur' likely completes 'demonstrabitur' or 'cognoscitur' on the following page.</meta>

[...they are], it can be compared with many things in the <term>Natural World</term> <note>The physical realm of human existence, as opposed to the spiritual world.</note>, such as these: no one can approach another who keeps a leopard and a panther in his room—and because he feeds them, he lives safely with them—unless he first removes those wild beasts. Who, invited to the table of a King and Queen, would not first wash his face and hands before approaching? And who enters the bridal chamber with a bride after the wedding, unless he has first washed himself entirely and clothed himself in a wedding garment? Who does not purify ores by fire and separate them from dross before obtaining pure gold and silver? Who does not separate the tares from the wheat harvest before carrying it into the granary? And who does not strike the husks from the barley harvest with threshing-sledges before gathering it into the house? Who does not skim the froth from raw meat while boiling it before it is edible and placed upon the table? Who does not shake the worms from the leaves of the trees in the garden, lest the leaves be consumed and the fruit thus perish? Who does not feel aversion to filth in houses and courtyards and cleans them, especially when a prince, or a princess-bride, is expected? Who loves a virgin and intends marriage with her if she is tainted by malignant disease or covered in pustules and sores, however much she paints her face, dresses herself splendidly, and studies to offer the allurements of love through the flatteries of her speech?

That a person ought to purify himself from evils and not expect the Lord to do this immediately <note>Swedenborg emphasizes that while the power comes from God, the individual must act "as if of himself" to initiate the process of reformation.</note> is comparatively like a servant walking with his face and clothes befouled with soot and dung who approaches his master and says, "Master, wash me." Would the master not say to him, "You foolish servant, what are you saying? Look, there is water, soap, and a towel. Do you not have hands and the power in them? Wash yourself!" And the Lord God will say, "The means of purification are from Me, and also your will and your power are from Me; therefore, use these gifts and endowments of mine as your own, and you shall be purified." And so on. That the external man is to be cleansed, but by means of the internal man, the Lord teaches in *Matthew* Chapter 23 from the beginning to the end.

332. To these shall be added **FOUR MEMORABLE RELATIONS**: <note>The "Memorabilia" are hallmark sections of Swedenborg’s later works where he describes his visions of heaven and hell to illustrate theological points.</note> **FIRST**, this: Once I heard outcries that gushed out from the lower regions like waters from a whirlpool—one to the left: **OH, HOW JUST!**; another to the right: **OH, HOW LEARNED!**; and a third from behind: **OH, HOW WISE!** And because the thought occurred to me whether there are also just, learned, and wise people in Hell, I was moved by a desire to see if such were there. When I was below, I saw plains covered with thickets interspersed with thorns and nettles. I asked if this was Hell; they said, "It is the lower earth, which is immediately above Hell." Then I proceeded according to the shouts in order. To the first, **OH, HOW JUST!**, and I saw a company of those who in the world had been judges influenced by friendship and bribes. Then to the second shout, **OH, HOW LEARNED!**, and I saw a company of those who in the world had been mere reasoners. And to the third shout, **OH, HOW WISE!**, and I saw a company of those who in the world had been "confirmers" <note>A term for those who use their intellect only to prove a preconceived notion (whether true or false) rather than seeking truth for its own sake.</note>.

...[they] were painted images of birds of the evening and night; but that hearth, and the flashes of light from it onto the forms of those images, were representations of their judgments—showing how they could color the facts of any case with false pretenses, and give them an appearance that suited their own interests. At that moment, I was given an illustration <note>In Swedenborg’s writings, "illustration" refers to a divine enlightenment or an opening of the mental sight to see spiritual truths clearly.</note> from Heaven, through which I perceived the details of whether a matter was lawful or not. I saw how industriously they would veil the unjust and induce a vision of the just upon it. They would select a favorable law from the books and bend the matter of the question toward it, while pushing everything else aside through clever reasoning. After the trials, the sentences were carried out to the clients, friends, and supporters; and these people, to repay the favor, shouted all along the way, "O HOW JUST, O HOW JUST!" <note>original: "O QUAM JUSTI, O QUAM JUSTI"</note>

After this, I spoke about them with the Angels of Heaven and told them some of what I had seen and heard. The Angels said that such judges appear to others as if endowed with a very sharp intellectual edge, yet they see not a bit of what is just and fair. "If you remove the friendship for someone," they said, "they sit in judgment like statues, and merely say, 'I agree; I conform with this one or that one.' The reason is that all their judgments are prejudices, and a prejudice followed by favor pursues a case from its beginning to its end. Therefore, they see nothing but what belongs to their friend. At everything that goes against him, they look askance, watching from the corners of their eyes; and if they take the matter up again, they entangle it in reasonings as a spider traps its prey in threads, and they consume it. Thus, if they do not follow the web of their own prejudice, they see nothing of the law." They were tested to see if they could see the truth, and it was found that they could not. The inhabitants of your world will wonder that this is so, but tell them that this is a truth explored by the Angels of Heaven. 

Because they see nothing of justice, we in Heaven do not look at them as men, but as monstrous images of a man: their heads are made of those things which belong to friendship, their breasts of injustice, their hands and feet of "confirmation" <note>The act of justifying a preconceived idea, regardless of its truth.</note>, and the soles of their feet of justice—which, if it does not favor a friend, they trip up and trample underfoot. You will soon see what they are like when viewed as they truly are, for their end is near. 

And behold, suddenly the ground gaped open, the tables fell upon tables, and they were swallowed up along with the entire amphitheater and cast into caverns and imprisoned. Then it was said to me, "Do you wish to see them there?" And behold, they were seen to have faces like polished steel, bodies from the neck to the loins like carvings dressed in leopard skins, and feet like snakes. I saw the Books of the Law, which they had kept on their tables, turned into playing cards. Now, instead of judging, they were given the task of preparing vermilion <note>A brilliant red pigment.</note> into cosmetics to smear on the faces of harlots, thus turning them into beauties. 

After these things were seen, I wished to go to the two remaining groups—to the one where there were mere "Reasoners," and to the other where there were mere "Confirmers." But it was said to me, "Rest a little; Angelic companions will be given to you from the society directly above them. Through them, light will be given to you from the Lord, and you will see wonders."

### 333. THE SECOND MEMORABLE RELATION.

After some time, I heard again from the lower earth the same voices as before: "O HOW LEARNED, O HOW LEARNED!" <note>original: "O QUAM ERUDITI, O QUAM ERUDITI"</note> I looked around to see who was present, and behold, there were Angels who were in the Heaven immediately above those who were being called "learned." I spoke with them about the shouting, and they said, "Those 'learned' ones are those who only reason *whether it is, or is not*, and rarely think *that it is so*. Therefore, they are like winds that blow and pass away; like the bark around trees that are without heartwood; like the shells around almonds without a kernel; or like the skin around fruit without the flesh; for...

Their minds are without any interior judgment, and are only united with the senses of the body; therefore, if the senses themselves do not judge, they can conclude nothing. In a word, they are merely <term>sensual</term><note>In this context, "sensual" does not mean "lustful," but rather "sensory-bound"—referring to people who believe only what they can see, touch, or hear, and lack spiritual or abstract insight.</note>, and are called by us "Reasoners." They are called <term>Reasoners</term><note>From the Latin *Ratiocinatores*. In Swedenborg's terminology, these are people who argue for the sake of arguing and never reach a settled conclusion or belief.</note> because they never reach a conclusion about anything, but instead take up whatever they hear and dispute whether it is so, constantly contradicting it. They love nothing more than to attack truths and tear them apart by dragging them into disputes; these are the ones who believe themselves to be more learned than everyone else in the world. Having heard these things, I asked the angels to lead me to them, and they led me to a cavern from which steps descended to the lower earth. We went down and followed the shouting:

-> O how learned! <-

And behold, there were several hundred standing in one place, stamping on the ground. Wondering at this, I asked why they stood there stamping the ground with the soles of their feet, adding that they might dig out the soil with their feet. At this, the angels smiled and said, "It appears as though they are standing there because they do not think about *how* a thing is so, but only *whether* it is so; they argue, and since their thought does not progress further, they appear merely to tread and wear down a single clod of earth without moving forward." The angels also said, "Those who drift from the natural world into this one and hear that they are in another world gather together in many places as a group and ask where Heaven is, where Hell is, and where God is. But after they have been instructed, they still begin to reason, dispute, and argue about **WHETHER GOD EXISTS**." <note>original: "NUM DEUS SIT"</note> This happens because there are so many <term>naturalists</term><note>People who believe that nature is the cause of all things, denying the divine or supernatural.</note> in the natural world today; and these people, when the conversation turns to religion, bring this up for debate among themselves and with others. This proposal and debate rarely ends in the affirmative of faith—that God exists. Later, these people associate themselves more and more with the wicked, and this happens because no one can do any good from the love of good unless it is from God.

Afterward, I was led to the assembly, and behold, they appeared to me as men with faces that were not unattractive and in ornate clothing. But the angels said, "They appear like that in their own light; however, if the light from Heaven flows in, their faces change, and so do their clothes." And so it happened: they then appeared with swarthy <note>original: "furvis," meaning dark, gloomy, or somber</note> faces, dressed in black sacks. But once this light was removed, they were seen as before. Presently, I spoke with some of the assembly and said, "I heard the shouting of the crowd around you,

-> O how learned! <-

Therefore, allow me to join in conversation with you regarding matters of the highest learning." They replied, "Say whatever you please, and we will satisfy you." I then asked, "What kind of religion is it through which a person is saved?" They said, "We will divide this question into several parts, and until we have concluded these, we cannot give an answer. The debate shall be: 1. Whether religion is anything. 2. Whether there is salvation or not. 3. Whether one religion accomplishes more than another. 4. Whether there is a Heaven and a Hell. 5. Whether there is an eternal life after death; among several other points."

I asked about the first point—Whether religion is anything—and they began to debate this with a wealth of arguments. I requested that they refer this to the whole congregation, and they did. The general response was that the proposition required so much investigation that it could not be finished before evening. I asked if they could finish it within a year, and one said it could not be done within a hundred years. I said, "In the meantime, you are without religion; and because salvation depends on it, you are without an idea, faith, or hope of salvation." He replied, "Must it not first be demonstrated whether religion exists, and what it is, and whether it is anything? If it is, it will be for the wise; if it is not, it will be only for the common people." <note>original: "vulgo"</note> "It is known," he continued, "that religion is called a 'bond' <note>A reference to the Latin etymology of *religio*, often linked to *religare*, 'to bind.'</note>, but the question is for whom? If only for the common people, it is nothing in itself; if also for the wise, it is."

Hearing this, I said, "You are anything but learned, because you cannot think of anything other than *whether it is so*, and you turn that over from both sides. Who can be learned unless he knows something for certain and progresses into it, just as a person moves step by step, and successively into wisdom? Otherwise, you do not even touch truths with a fingernail, but instead remove them further and further from your sight. Therefore, to reason only *whether it is*, is like reasoning about a hat that is never put on, or a shoe that is never worn. What flows from this, except that you do not know whether anything exists?"

...what it is, and whether it is anything but an idea; whether there is such a thing as salvation, whether there is eternal life after death, whether one religion is better than another, or whether Heaven and Hell exist. You cannot think about these things at all as long as you are stuck at the first step, kicking at the sand there, refusing to move one foot past the other and move forward. Take care that your minds, while they stand outside of judgment in this way, do not harden inside and become like false statues. After saying these things, I left, and they, out of indignation, threw stones after me; and then they appeared to me like carved statues in which there is no human reason. I asked the angels about their fate, and they said that the lowest of them are sent down into the deep, and there into a desert, where they are forced to carry heavy bundles; and because they cannot produce anything from reason, they prattle and speak vanities, and from a distance, they appear like asses carrying burdens.

334. **THE THIRD MEMORABLE RELATION.** After this, one of the angels said, "Follow me to the place where they shout, -> O HOW WISE <-." He added, "You will see wonders of men—you will see faces and bodies that are human, and yet they are not men." I asked, "Are they beasts then?" He replied, "No, they are not beasts, but beast-men; for they are those who are completely unable to see whether truth is truth or not, and yet they can make whatever they want appear as the truth. Among us, such people are called <term>Confirmers</term><note>In Swedenborg's writings, a "Confirmer" is someone who uses their intellect not to find the truth, but to prove that their pre-existing opinions—no matter how false—are true.</note>." 

We followed the shouting and came to the place, and behold, there was a gathering of men, and a crowd around the gathering, and in the crowd were some of noble lineage. When they heard that these men could confirm everything they said and favored themselves with such obvious agreement, they turned and said, -> O HOW WISE <-. 

But the angel said to me, "Let us not go to them, but let us call one out from the gathering." We called one out and went aside with him and spoke of various things, and he confirmed every single one until they appeared completely true. We then asked him if he could also confirm the opposites; he said he could do so just as well as the first. He then spoke openly and from his heart: "What is truth? Is there any truth in the nature of things, other than what a man makes true? Say whatever you like, and I will make it so that it is the truth." I said, "Make this the truth: that Faith is the everything of the Church." He did this so skillfully and cleverly that the learned men standing around wondered and applauded. 

Afterward, I asked him to make it the truth that Charity was the everything of the Church, and he did so. Then, I asked him to prove that Charity is *nothing* to the Church; he took up both positions and dressed them up with such appearances that the bystanders looked at each other and said, "Is this man not wise?" I then said, "Do you not know that to live well is Charity, and to believe well is Faith? Does not he who lives well also believe well? And thus, that Faith belongs to Charity, and Charity to Faith? Do you see that this is true?" He replied, "I will make it true, and then I will see." He did so and said, "Now I see it." But soon after, he made the opposite of it true, and then said, "I also see that *this* is true." At this, we smiled and said, "Are these not opposites? How can two opposites both appear true?" To this, he indignantly replied, "You are mistaken; both are true, since truth is nothing other than what a man makes true." 

Someone was standing nearby who, in the world, had been an Ambassador of the first rank. He was amazed at this and said, "I recognize that something similar happens in the world, but still, you are insane. If you can, make it true that Light is Darkness, and Darkness is Light." The Confirmer replied, "I will do that easily. What are Light and Darkness but states of the eye? Does not light change into shadow when the eye comes in from the bright sun? And when a man fixes his eye intensely on the sun, who does not know that the state of the eye is then changed, and that the light then appears as shadow? Conversely, when the state of the eye returns, that shadow appears as light. Does not the Owl see the darkness of night as the light of day, and the light of day as the darkness of night, and then sees the Sun itself entirely as a dark and murky globe? If a man had eyes like an owl, what would he call light and what would he call darkness? What then is Light but a state of the eye? And if it is only a state of the eye, is not Light Darkness, and Darkness Light? Therefore, one is true and the other is true." But because this confirmation confused some...

...then, I said, I noticed that this <term>Confirmer</term><note>A person who uses logic not to find truth, but to justify any preconceived idea.</note> does not know that there is a **True Light** and a **False Light** <note>original: *Lux vera* and *Lux fatua*. *Lux fatua* refers to a "fool’s light" or a deceptive glow, like a will-o'-the-wisp.</note>, and that both these lights appear as if they were lights. Yet, in itself, the False Light is not light; rather, compared to the True Light, it is thick darkness. Within this False Light is the "Owl," for within its eyes is the lust for hunting and devouring birds. This "light" makes its eyes see at night, much like cats, whose eyes look like candles in cellars; it is the False Light arising from the lust for hunting and devouring mice that produces this effect. From this it is clear that the light of the Sun is True Light, while the light of lust is a False Light. 

After this, the Ambassador asked the Confirmer to make it seem as if it were true that a **Crow is white** and not black. He replied, "I will do that easily as well." He said, "Take a needle or a razor and open the feathers and plumage of the Crow; then remove the feathers and look at the Crow’s skin—is it not white? What is the blackness that surrounds it but a shadow, from which the color of the Crow should not be judged? As for black being merely a shadow, consult those skilled in the science of optics, and they will tell you: either grind a black stone or black glass into a fine powder, and you will see that the powder is white." <note>This refers to a common 18th-century observation that when light-absorbing materials are pulverized, the increased surface area scatters light, making the powder appear lighter or white.</note>

But the Ambassador replied, "Does the Crow not appear black to the sight?" 

The Confirmer replied, "Do you, being a man, wish to think based on appearances? You can certainly speak from appearance and say that a Crow is black, but you cannot *think* it. For example, you can speak from appearance and say that the Sun rises and sets, but because you are a man, you cannot think that is true, because the Sun stands unmoved and the Earth moves forward. It is the same with the Crow; appearance is appearance. Say what you will, the Crow is entirely white; it even turns white when it grows old—this I have seen." 

After this, those standing by looked at me; therefore I said, "It is true that the feathers and plumage of the Crow inside draw from whiteness, as does its skin; but this is the case not only with crows, but with all birds in the Universe. Every person distinguishes birds by the appearance of their color; if this were not done, we would say of every bird that it is white, which is absurd and meaningless."

Later, the Ambassador asked whether he could make it true that **you are insane**. He said, "I can, but I do not wish to; who is not insane?" 

Then they asked him to say from his heart whether he was joking, or whether he truly believed that there is no truth except what a man *makes* true. He replied, "I swear that I believe it." 

After this, that "universal Confirmer" was sent to the Angels so they could explore his character. After their exploration, they said that he did not possess even a grain of understanding, because everything that is **above the rational mind** was closed in him, and only that which is **below the rational mind** was open. 

Above the rational mind is **Spiritual Light**, and below the rational mind is **Natural Light**. This Natural Light in a man is such that it can confirm whatever one pleases. But if Spiritual Light does not flow into the Natural Light, a man cannot see whether any truth is actually true, nor can he see that a falsehood is false. To see both is the result of Spiritual Light being present within Natural Light; and Spiritual Light comes from the God of Heaven, who is the Lord. Therefore, that universal Confirmer is neither a man nor a beast, but is a **beast-man**. 

I asked the Angels about the fate of such people—whether they can live among the living, since a man’s life comes from Spiritual Light, and from this comes his understanding. They said that such people, when they are alone, are unable to think anything and therefore cannot speak, but they stand like mute automatons and as if in a deep sleep; however, they wake up as soon as their ears catch a sound. They added that those who are inwardly evil become like this; in them, Spiritual Light cannot flow in from above, but only a certain "spiritual influence" through the world, which gives them the faculty of confirming. 

When this was said, I heard a voice from the Angels who had explored him, saying: "Form a universal conclusion from what you have heard." 

And I did so: ***That being able to confirm whatever one pleases is not the mark of an intelligent person, but being able to see that truth is truth and that falsehood is falsehood, and to confirm that, is the mark of an intelligent person.*** 

After this, I looked toward the assembly where the Confirmers stood, and the crowd around them was shouting...

O HOW WISE [they seem], and behold, a dark cloud has veiled them; and in that cloud, owls and bats were flying in the morning. For the confirmations of falsities, to the point that they appear as truths, are represented in this world under the forms of birds of the night, whose eyes are illuminated from within by a <term>fool’s light</term><note>original: *lux fatua*. A deceptive or illusory glow, like a will-o'-the-wisp.</note>, by which they see objects in the darkness as if in the light. 335. <term>THE FOURTH MEMORABLE RELATION</term>. At a certain dawn, when I was awakened from sleep, I saw what looked like specters in various forms before my eyes; and afterward, when it was morning, I saw "fool’s lights" in different shapes. Some were like parchments full of writing, which, being folded again and again, finally appeared like falling stars which vanished as they fell through the air; others were like open books, some of which shone like little moons, and some burned like candles. Among these were books that raised themselves up high and perished in the heights, and others that fell to the ground and were dissolved there into dust. From these sights, I conjectured that beneath those atmospheric phenomena stood people who were arguing about imaginary things which they considered of great importance; for in the spiritual world, such phenomena appear in the atmosphere from the reasonings of those standing below. 

Soon my spiritual sight was opened, and I noticed a number of spirits whose heads were encircled with laurel leaves, and whose bodies were clothed in glorified robes, which signified that they were spirits who had been famous for their reputation for learning in the natural world. Because I was in the spirit, I approached and mingled with the assembly; and I then heard that they were arguing sharply and ardently among themselves about <term>INNATE IDEAS</term><note>The philosophical concept that the mind is born with certain knowledge or concepts, rather than being a "blank slate."</note>, whether any were present in humans from birth, as they are in beasts. Those who denied it turned away from those who affirmed it, and at last they stood separated into two groups, like the ranks of two armies about to fight with swords; but because they had no swords, they fought with the sharp points of words. But suddenly, an **Angelic Spirit** stood in their midst and, speaking with a loud voice, said:

> I have heard from a distance, not far from you, that you are both burning in a dispute over innate ideas, whether any exist in humans as they do in beasts; but I say to you, **THAT THERE ARE NO INNATE IDEAS IN HUMANS, AND NEITHER ARE THERE ANY INNATE IDEAS IN BEASTS**. Therefore, you are quarreling over nothing, or as the saying goes, over <term>goat’s wool</term><note>original: *lana caprina*. A Latin idiom meaning a trivial or non-existent matter.</note>, or over the "beard of this age."

Hearing this, they all grew angry and shouted, "Cast this man out! He speaks against common sense!" But when they were in the middle of trying to cast him out, they saw him encircled by heavenly light, through which they could not break, for he was an Angelic Spirit. Therefore, they drew back and moved a little away from him. After that light was drawn back, he said to them: "Why do you grow angry? Listen first, and gather the reasons I shall bring forward, and make a conclusion from them yourselves. I foresee that those who excel in judgment will agree, and the storms that have arisen in your minds will be calmed." At these words, they said with an indignant tone, "Speak then, and we will listen." And then, beginning to speak, he said:

> You believe that beasts have innate ideas, and you have concluded this because their actions appear as if they come from thought. And yet, they have not even a tiny bit of thought, and "ideas" cannot be predicated except from thought. The characteristic of thought is to act *for the sake of this or that* in such or such a way. Consider, therefore, whether a **Spider**, which weaves a web with the greatest artistry, thinks in its tiny head: "I will extend the threads in this order, and I will bind them with cross-threads so that my web does not fall apart when the vibration of the air rushes in; and at the first ends of the threads, which will make the center, I will prepare a seat for myself in which I may perceive whatever falls in, so that I may run there; so that if a fly flies in, it may be entangled, and I will quickly attack and bind it, and it will serve as my food." Furthermore, does a **Bee** think in its little head: "I will fly out; I know where the flowering fields are; and..."

"...there [I will] suck wax from these flowers and honey from those, and from the wax I will build contiguous cells in a series, in such a way that I and my companions, as if through streets, may freely enter and exit; and afterward we will store honey in them abundantly, so that there is enough even for the coming winter, lest we die." These are besides other wonders, in which they not only rival human political and economic prudence, but in some ways exceed it (see above page 11). Furthermore, does a larger wasp <note>original: *Fucus major*. While *fucus* can mean a drone bee, the description of building a "house of thin paper" refers to the nesting habits of wasps or hornets.</note> think in its tiny head, "I and my companions will build a little house out of thin paper, the walls of which we will lead around inside in a labyrinthine form; and within we will prepare it like a forum, into which there will be an entrance and from which an exit, and this with such artifice that no other living thing, except what is of our lineage, shall find the way to the innermost part where we gather"? Again, does the silkworm, while it is still a worm, think in its tiny head, "Now is the time for me to prepare myself to spin silk, and for this purpose: so that when it is spun, I may fly out, and in the air—into which I could not rise before—I may play with my companions and provide for my offspring"? Similarly with other worms, while they crawl along walls and become nymphs, pupae, chrysalises, and finally butterflies. Does a fly have any idea about mating with another fly, that it should be here and not there?

It is similar with animals of a larger body, as with those little creatures, such as birds and winged creatures of every kind: when they mate, when they prepare nests, lay eggs in them, sit on them, hatch the young, offer them food, and raise them until they fly away, and afterward drive them from the nests as if they were not their own offspring—besides innumerable other things. It is similar also with the beasts of the earth, with serpents, and with fish. Who among you cannot see from the things said above that their spontaneous acts do not flow from any thought, of which alone an "idea" can be predicated? The error that beasts have ideas has flowed from no other source than the persuasion that they think just as humans do, and that only speech makes the difference. 

After this, the angelic Spirit looked around, and because he saw them still hesitating whether beasts have thought or not, he continued his discourse and said: "I perceive that from the acts of brute animals similar to human ones, a visionary idea of their thought still clings to you; therefore I will tell you where those acts come from. Namely, to every beast, every bird, every fish, reptile, and insect, there is its own natural, sensual, and corporeal love, whose dwellings are their heads, and in these their brains; through these the <term>Spiritual world</term> flows into their bodily senses immediately, and through these determines their acts. This is the cause why their bodily senses are much more exquisite than human ones. That influx from the spiritual world is what is called <term>Instinct</term>; and it is called instinct because it exists without the mediation of thought. There are also accessories to instinct arising from habit. But their love, through which the determination to acts occurs from the spiritual world, is only for nutrition and propagation—not for any science, intelligence, and wisdom, through which love is successively formed in humans."

That no <term>innate ideas</term> <note>original: *ideæ connatæ*. This refers to the philosophical debate—notably involving Descartes and Locke—over whether humans are born with certain concepts already in their minds.</note> belong even to humans can be clearly established from the fact that no thought is innate to them; and where there is no thought, there is no idea, for the one is the reciprocal of the other. This can be concluded from newborn infants: that they can do nothing besides suckle and breathe. That they are able to suckle is not from something innate, but from continuous suction in the mother's womb; and that they can breathe is because they live, for this is a universal of life. The bodily senses themselves are in the greatest obscurity, and they emerge from this successively through objects; similarly, their movements are learned through habit. And successively, as they learn to babble sounds and sound them first without an idea, there arises some obscure phantasy; as this grows clear, an obscure imagination is born, and from that, thought. According to the formation of this state, ideas exist, which, as was said above, make one with thought; and thought grows from nothing through instructions. Wherefore ideas are present in humans, but they are not [innate]...

# CHAPTER SIX

### CONCERNING

## F A I T H.

336. From the wisdom of the Ancients <note>original: *sapientia Antiquorum*; Swedenborg frequently refers to the "Ancient Church," a symbolic era of humanity that understood the spiritual correspondences of the natural world.</note> flowed this dogma: that the Universe and each and every thing within it relate to the Good and the True. Consequently, all things of the Church relate to Love or Charity and Faith, because everything that flows from Love or Charity is called "Good," and everything that flows from Faith is called "Truth." Now, because Charity and Faith are two distinct things, yet they still act as one in a person so that they may be a "person of the Church"—that is, so the Church may be within the person—there was a controversy and debate among the ancients as to which of those two is First, and thus which is rightfully to be called the Firstborn <term>Firstborn (original: *Primogenitum*): in a biblical and spiritual sense, this refers to that which has priority, seniority, and the right of inheritance.</term>. Some of them said that Truth, and consequently Faith, is first; and some said that Good, and consequently Charity, is first. For they saw that a person, immediately after birth, learns to speak and think, and through these is perfected in understanding by means of various sciences; and thus they learn and understand what is True, and by these means they later learn and understand what is Good. Therefore, they reasoned that Faith comes first, and Charity comes later. Those who understood the matter in this way thought that the Truth of faith is the Firstborn, and that the Good of charity is born afterward; for which reason they attributed the eminence and prerogative right of "Primogeniture" to Faith. But these people overwhelmed their own understanding with such a heap of arguments in favor of Faith that they failed to see that Faith is not faith unless it is joined to Charity, and that Charity is not charity unless it is joined to Faith; and thus they make one. If they do not, then neither one nor the other is anything in the Church. That they act entirely as one will be demonstrated in what follows.

> But in this Preface, I will briefly reveal how or by what reasoning they make one; for it is important that the following things be seen in some degree of light. Specifically: Faith (by which we also mean Truth) is First in time; but Charity (by which we also mean Good) is First in end <note>original: *Primum fine*; in philosophy, the "end" is the ultimate goal or purpose for which a thing exists.</note>. And that which is First in end is actually the First, because it is primary, and thus it is also the Firstborn; whereas that which is First in time is not actually the First, but only apparently so. However, so that this may be understood, it shall be illustrated by Comparisons: with the building of a Temple, as well as a House; with the construction of a Garden; and with the preparation of a Field. In the BUILDING OF A TEMPLE: The first thing in time is to lay the foundation, to erect the walls, to put on the roof, and afterward to bring in the Altar and build the Pulpit; but the first thing in end is the Worship of God within it, for the sake of which those other things are done. In the BUILDING OF A HOUSE: The first thing in time is to build its exterior and to furnish it with various necessities; but the first thing in end is a comfortable Dwelling for oneself and for the others who will be in the House. In the CONSTRUCTION OF A GARDEN: The first thing in time is to level the soil, prepare the ground, plant trees, and sow things that will be of use; but the first thing in end is the enjoyment of the fruit from them. In the PREPARATION OF A FIELD: The first thing in time is to level the earth, plow, harrow, and then sow the seeds; but the first thing in end is the Harvest, and thus the use. From these Comparisons, anyone can conclude what is First in itself. Does not everyone, when they wish to build

Therefore, the Articles of Faith are these: I. *That Saving Faith is in the Lord God the Savior Jesus Christ.* II. *That Faith in summary is: that he who lives well and believes rightly is saved by the Lord.* III. *That a person receives Faith by approaching the Lord, learning truths from the Word, and living according to them.* IV. *That an abundance of truths, hanging together like a bundle, exalts and perfects faith.* V. *That Faith without charity is not faith; and that Charity without faith is not charity; and that neither is alive except from the Lord.* VI. *That the Lord, Charity, and Faith make one, just as Life, Will, and Intellect do in a person; and that if they are divided, each one perishes, like a union collapsed into dust.* VII. *That the Lord is Charity and Faith in a person, and that the person is Charity and Faith in the Lord.* VIII. *That Charity and Faith are together in Good Works.* IX. *That there is true Faith, spurious Faith, and hypocritical Faith.* X. *That there is no faith among the wicked.* These must now be explained individually.
