# OF THE NEW HEAVEN AND THE NEW CHURCH.

...of the only begotten Son of God, John 3:18. *These things are written, that you may believe that Jesus is the Son of God, and that by Believing you may have life in His Name*, John 20:31. UNLESS YOU BELIEVE THAT I AM <note>original: "EGO SIM," referring to the divine "I AM."</note>, you will die in your sins, John 8:24. *Jesus said, when the Paraclete <note>The "Helper" or "Comforter," referring to the Holy Spirit.</note>, the spirit of truth, comes, he will convict the World of Sin, Righteousness, and Judgment; of Sin, because they do not believe in Me*, John 16:8.

338. That the Faith of the Apostles was none other than faith in the Lord Jesus Christ is evident from many places in their Epistles, from which I will only bring forward these: *I no longer live, but Christ lives in me; and what I now live in the flesh, I LIVE IN FAITH, WHICH IS IN THE SON OF GOD*, Galatians 2:20. Paul testified to the *Jews and Greeks repentance toward God, and FAITH IN OUR LORD JESUS CHRIST*, Acts of the Apostles 20:21. *He who led Paul outside said, "What must I do to be saved?" He said, "BELIEVE IN THE LORD JESUS CHRIST, and so you and your house will be saved"*, Acts of the Apostles 16:30, 31. *He who has the Son has life, but he who does not have the Son of God does not have life: I have written these things to you who believe in the Name of the Son of God, that you may know that you have eternal life, and that you may believe in the Name of the Son of God*, 1 John 5:12, 13. We who are by nature *Jews, and not sinners from the Gentiles*, since we know that a person is not justified by the works of the law, *but THROUGH THE FAITH OF JESUS CHRIST, even WE HAVE BELIEVED IN JESUS CHRIST*, Galatians 2:15, 16. Because their faith was in Jesus Christ, and is also from Him, they therefore called it the Faith of Jesus Christ, as just above in Galatians 2:16, and in these following: *The righteousness of God through THE FAITH OF JESUS CHRIST unto all and upon all who believe... That he might be the justifier of him who is of the FAITH OF JESUS*, Romans 3:22, 26. *That he may have the righteousness which is from the FAITH OF CHRIST, the righteousness which is from THE GOD OF FAITH <note>original: "DEO FIDEI."</note>*, Philippians 3:9. *These are they who keep the commandments of God and THE FAITH OF JESUS CHRIST*, Revelation 14:12. *THROUGH THE FAITH WHICH is in Christ Jesus*, 2 Timothy 3:15. *IN JESUS CHRIST THERE IS FAITH WORKING THROUGH CHARITY*, Galatians 5:6. From these it can be established what faith was understood by Paul in that saying so commonly used in the Church today: WE CONCLUDE THEREFORE THAT A PERSON IS JUSTIFIED BY FAITH WITHOUT THE WORKS OF THE LAW, Romans 3:28. This does not refer to faith in God the Father, but in His Son; much less in three Gods in order—one from whom, another for whose sake, and a third through whom. The reason the Church believes that its "tripersonal" <note>Referring to the doctrine of a Trinity of three distinct persons.</note> faith was understood by Paul in that saying is that for fourteen centuries—or ever since the Council of Nicaea—the Church has acknowledged no other faith, and therefore knew of no other. They believed it was the only one, and that no other could be given. Therefore, wherever the word "Faith" is read in the New Testament, it was believed to be that specific faith, and they applied everything there to it. Consequently, the only saving faith, which is in God the Savior, perished; and from this, so many fallacies crept into their doctrines, and so many paradoxes contrary to sound reason. For every doctrine of the Church that teaches and shows the way to Heaven, or to salvation, depends on faith. And because so many fallacies and paradoxes crept into it, as was said, it became necessary for them to proclaim the dogma that the **Understanding must be kept captive under obedience to faith.** Now, since in Paul’s saying in Romans 3:28, "faith" does not mean faith in God the Father but in His Son, and "works of the law" there do not mean the works of the law of the Decalogue <note>The Ten Commandments.</note>, but the works of the *Mosaic* Law for the *Jews* (as is clear from what follows there, and also from similar passages in Galatians 2:14, 15), the foundation stone of modern faith falls, and the temple built upon it falls as well, like a house sinking into the earth until only the tip of the roof sticks out.

339. The reason that we must believe—that is, have faith—in the Lord God the Savior Jesus Christ, is because it is faith in a visible God in whom the invisible God is present; and faith in a visible God, who is Man and God at the same time, enters into a person. For faith in its essence is spiritual, but in its form it is natural; therefore, in a person, it becomes spiritual-natural. For everything spiritual is received in the natural so that it may be something within the person. Purely spiritual things do indeed enter into a person, but they are not received; it is like ether which flows in and out without affecting anything. For in order to affect someone, there must be perception and thus reception...

On the other hand, a purely natural Faith, or a Faith devoid of a Spiritual essence, is not faith, but merely persuasion or knowledge. Persuasion mimics faith in external appearances, but because there is nothing Spiritual within it, it possesses nothing of a Saving nature. Such is the faith found among all those who deny the Divinity of the Lord’s Human; such was the <term>Arian</term><note>Arianism: a 4th-century belief that Jesus was a created being, not co-eternal or of the same substance as God the Father.</note> faith, and such also is the <term>Socinian</term><note>Socinianism: a non-trinitarian system that denies the pre-existence of Christ and views him as a human who attained divinity through his life.</note> faith, because both rejected the Divinity of the Lord. It is like a bird flying above the atmosphere into the ether where, as if in a vacuum, it expires. The dwelling-place of this faith in the human mind can be compared to the dwelling of the winds in the wings of <term>Aeolus</term><note>The Greek god of the winds.</note>, or to the dwelling of light in a falling star; it arises like a comet with a long tail, but it passes away like one and vanishes. In a word, Faith in an invisible God is actually blind, because the human Mind does not see its God; and the light of this faith, because it is not Spiritual-natural, is a <term>will-o'-the-wisp</term><note>original: "Lux fatua." Literally "foolish light," referring to marsh gases or phosphorescence that misleads travelers at night.</note>. This Light is like the light in a glow-worm, or like the light in marshes or over sulfurous soil at night, or like the light in rotting wood. From this light nothing else exists but what belongs to <term>fantasy</term>, in which what appears is believed to be real, and yet is not. Faith in an invisible God shines with no other light, especially when it is thought that God is a Spirit, and "spirit" is thought of as "ether." What follows from this except that man looks upon God as he looks upon the ether? Thus he seeks Him in the Universe, and when he does not find Him there, he believes the Nature of the Universe to be God. This is the origin of the <term>Naturalism</term><note>The belief that only natural laws and forces operate in the universe; a precursor to modern secularism or pantheism.</note> reigning today. Did not the Lord say, *That no one has ever heard the Father’s voice, nor seen His form* (John 5:37)? And also, *That no one has ever seen God, and that the Only Begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, He has revealed Him* (John 1:18). *No one has seen the Father, except He who is with the Father; He has seen the Father* (John 6:46). *Then, that no one comes to the Father except through Him* (John 14:6); and further, *That the man who sees and knows Him, sees and knows the Father* (John 14:7 and following). However, Faith in the Lord God the Savior is different; because He is God and Man, He can be approached and seen in thought. It is not a faith without a destination, but has a point of origin and a destination, and once received, it remains. Just as when someone has seen an Emperor or a King, whenever he remembers them, their image returns. The vision of that faith is like someone seeing a bright Cloud, and in its center an Angel, who invites the man to himself so that he may be raised into Heaven. In this way the Lord appears to those who have faith in Him; He approaches everyone as they recognize and acknowledge Him, which happens as they know and perform His commandments (which are to shun evils and do goods). Finally, He comes into that person’s house and makes His dwelling-place there together with the Father who is in Him, according to these words in John: *Jesus said, he who has my commandments and keeps them, he it is who loves Me; and he who loves Me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him and will manifest Myself to him, and we will come to him and make our dwelling-place with him* (Chapter 14:21, 23). These things were written in the presence of the twelve Apostles of the Lord, who, while I was writing this, were sent to me by the Lord.<note>The author, Emanuel Swedenborg, frequently claimed to be in spiritual communication with figures from the Bible and Christian history while writing his theological works.</note>

...[is mentioned]: but the means of salvation are many, yet each and every one refers back to living well and believing rightly; thus to <term>Charity</term><note>In this theology, charity is not merely almsgiving, but the active practice of "living well" by following the divine commandments in one's daily work and relationships.</note> and <term>Faith</term><note>Defined here as "believing rightly," or holding a correct understanding of God and spiritual truths.</note>, for Charity is living well and Faith is believing rightly. These two general categories of the means of salvation are not only prescribed to man in the Word, but even commanded; and because they are commanded, it follows that man can, through them, provide for himself eternal life by the power implanted in him and given by God. Furthermore, to the extent that man uses that power and looks toward God at the same time, God strengthens it, so that he may perform everything that belongs to natural charity as <term>Spiritual charity</term><note>Actions that are not just outwardly "good" for the sake of reputation, but are motivated by a love for what is good and true.</note>, and everything that belongs to natural faith as <term>Spiritual faith</term>. Thus, God makes dead Charity and Faith alive, and the man along with them. There are two things which must exist together so that it can be said that a man lives well and believes rightly; these two are called in the Church the <term>Internal man</term><note>The inner world of a person's intentions and spirit.</note> and the <term>External man</term><note>The outward world of a person's actions and speech.</note>. When the Internal man wills well and the External acts well, then both act as one: the External from the Internal, and the Internal through the External. Thus, man acts from God, and God acts through man. Conversely, however, if the Internal man wills evil and yet the External acts well, then nonetheless both act from Hell; for his will is from there, and his acting is hypocritical. In every hypocritical act, his internal will lies hidden within, which is hellish—like a snake in the grass, or like a worm in a flower. The man who not only knows that there are an Internal and External man, but also what they are, and that they can act as one actually, and also act as one apparently—and moreover, that the Internal man lives after death and the External is buried—that man possesses in abundance the secrets of Heaven and also of the World. He who joins those two men within himself for good becomes happy forever; but he who divides them, and even more he who joins them in evil, becomes unhappy forever.

341. To believe that a man who lives well and believes rightly is not saved, and that God can save and damn whomever He wills by free choice and pleasure—a man who perishes in this state could rightly accuse God of being unmerciful and unkind, and even of cruelty; indeed, he might deny that God is God. Furthermore, he might claim that in His Word, God spoke in vain and commanded things of no value or trifles. And further, if a man who lives well and believes rightly is not saved, he could also accuse God of violating His covenant which He struck upon Mount Sinai and inscribed with His own finger on the two Tables. That God cannot help but save those who live according to His precepts and have faith in Him is evident from the Lord's words in John Chapter 14:21 to 24. Everyone who possesses religion and sound reason can confirm this for himself while he considers that God—who is constantly present with man and gives him life, as well as the faculty of understanding and loving—cannot do otherwise than love him and, through love, join Himself to him who lives well and believes rightly. Is this not inscribed by God upon every human and every creature? Can a father or mother reject their infants? Or a bird its chicks? Or an animal its cubs? Not even tigers, panthers, or serpents can do this. To do otherwise would be against the order in which God exists and according to which He acts, and also against the order in which He created man. Now, just as it is impossible for God to damn anyone who lives well and believes rightly, so conversely it is impossible for God to save anyone who lives wickedly and consequently believes what is false. This latter is also against order, and therefore against His Omnipotence, which cannot proceed except by the way of Justice. The laws of Justice are truths which cannot be changed, for the Lord says: *It is easier for Heaven and Earth to pass away, than for one tittle of the Law to fall* <note>original: "Facilius est Cælum & Terram transire, quam Legis unum apicem cadere"</note>, Luke 16:17. Everyone who knows anything of the essence of God and the <term>Free Will</term><note>The capacity of a person to choose between good and evil, which the author argues is essential for being truly human.</note> of man can perceive this. As an example, Adam was free to eat from the <term>Tree of Life</term><note>Symbolizing the reception of life and wisdom from God.</note> and also from the <term>Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil</term><note>Symbolizing the belief that life and wisdom originate in oneself.</note>. ### III.

->*That man receives Faith by approaching the Lord, learning Truths from the Word, and living according to them.*<-

343. Before I proceed to demonstrate the **ORIGIN OF FAITH**, which is that the Lord be approached, truths be learned from the Word, and life be lived according to them, it is necessary that Summaries of faith be presented first, from which a general notion can be had regarding the individual parts of faith. For in this way, not only what is handed down in this Chapter on Faith, but also what follows concerning Charity, Free Choice <term>Free Will</term>, Repentance, Reformation and Regeneration, and concerning Imputation, can be more clearly understood; for Faith enters into all and every part of the theological system just as blood enters the limbs of the body and gives them life. What the modern Church teaches about Faith is generally known in the Christian World, and specifically in its Ecclesiastical Order, for books on "Faith alone" <note>original: "Fide sola." The Protestant doctrine that salvation comes through belief without the necessity of good works.</note> and "Only Faith" fill the libraries of the Doctors of the Church; for today, hardly anything is considered properly "Theological" except that. But before those things which the modern Church teaches about its Faith are taken up, examined, and weighed—which will be done in the **APPENDIX**—the General Principles which the New Church teaches about its Faith will be brought forward, which are these that follow.

# UNIVERSAL THEOLOGY

344. **The <term>Being</term> <note>Latin: *Esse*. In theology, this refers to the innermost core or the very "to be" of a thing.</note> of the Faith of the New Church** is: 
1. Confidence in the Lord God the Savior Jesus Christ. 
2. Trust that he who lives well and believes rightly is saved by Him. 

**The <term>Essence</term> <note>Latin: *Essentia*. The defining characteristics that make a thing what it is.</note> of the Faith of the New Church** is Truth from the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note>. 

**The <term>Existence</term> <note>Latin: *Existentia*. The outward manifestation or how a thing comes into being in the world.</note> of the Faith of the New Church** is: 
1. Spiritual Sight. 
2. The harmony of truths. 
3. Conviction. 
4. Acknowledgment inscribed upon the mind. 

**The States of the Faith of the New Church** are: 
1. Infant faith, adolescent faith, and adult faith. 
2. Faith in genuine truth, and faith in the appearances of truth. 
3. Faith of the memory, faith of the reason, and faith of the light. 
4. Natural faith, spiritual faith, and celestial faith. 
5. Living faith and miraculous faith. 
6. Free faith and forced faith. 

**The very Form of the Faith of the New Church, in both its Universal Idea and its Particular Idea**, may be seen above in numbers 2 and 3.

345. Since those things which belong to spiritual faith have been presented in summary, those things which belong to a merely natural faith shall also be presented in summary. In itself, natural faith is a persuasion that counterfeits faith; it is a persuasion of what is false and is called **Heretical Faith**. Its designations are: 
1. **Spurious faith**, in which falsities are mixed with truths. 
2. **Harlot faith**, arising from falsified truths, and **adulterous faith** from adulterated goods. 
3. **Closed or blind faith**, which concerns mystical things that are believed even though it is not known whether they are true or false, or whether they are above reason or contrary to it. 
4. **Erratic faith**, which is faith in several gods. 
5. **One-eyed faith** <note>original: *Fides lusca*. This refers to a "squinting" or partial vision, where one does not see clearly or looks toward the wrong object.</note>, which is faith in a god other than the True One, and among Christians, in a god other than the Lord God the Savior. 
6. **Hypocritical or Pharisaical faith**, which is of the mouth and not of the heart. 
7. **Visionary and preposterous faith**, which is the appearance of falsity as truth resulting from clever confirmation.

346. It was stated above that faith, as to its existence in a person, is spiritual sight. Now, because spiritual sight (which belongs to the understanding and thus the mind) and natural sight (which is the sight of the eye and thus the body) correspond to each other, every state of faith can be compared with the state of the eye and its vision. A state of true faith is like any healthy state of eyesight, while a state of false faith is like every disordered state of eyesight. We shall compare the correspondences of these two types of vision—mind and body—regarding their disordered states: 

**Spurious Faith**, in which falsities are mixed with truths, can be compared to a defect of the eye and its vision called a **white spot** <note>original: *Macula alba*. Likely referring to a corneal opacity or leukoma.</note> over the cornea, which renders the vision dim. 

**Harlot Faith**, which comes from falsified truths, and **Adulterous Faith**, which comes from adulterated goods, can be compared to a defect of the eye and its vision called **Glaucoma** <note>In the 18th century, glaucoma was often described as a drying or hardening of the crystalline lens, similar to what we now call a cataract.</note>, which is a drying out and hardening of the crystalline humor. 

**Closed or Blind Faith**, which is in mystical things believed without knowing if they are true or false, or if they are above or against reason, can be compared to the eye defect called **Gutta serena** and **Amaurosis** <note>These terms were used for "dark blindness," where the patient loses sight but the eye itself appears healthy and clear, usually due to optic nerve damage.</note>. This is the loss of sight while the eye still appears to see perfectly, arising from an obstruction of the optic nerve.

Wandering faith, which is directed toward several Gods, can be compared to a defect of the eye called a **Cataract**, which is a loss of sight arising from an obstruction between the sclerotic coat and the uvea <note>The "sclerotic coat" is the white of the eye; the "uvea" is the pigmented middle layer. Swedenborg uses 18th-century medical understanding to illustrate spiritual blindness.</note>. **SQUINTING FAITH** <note>original: *Fides Lusca*</note>, which is directed toward a god other than the true one—and among Christians, toward a god other than the Lord God the Savior—can be compared to the eye defect called **Strabismus** <note>Commonly known as "crossed eyes" or "squint."</note>. **HYPOCRITICAL or PHARISAICAL FAITH**, which is of the mouth and not of the heart, can be compared to an **Atrophy** of the eye and the resulting loss of sight. **VISIONARY and PREPOSTEROUS FAITH**, which is the appearance of what is false as if it were true through clever confirmation, can be compared to the eye defect called **Nyctalopia**, which is vision produced from a "false light" <note>original: *luce fatua*, likely referring to "ignis fatuus" or "will-o'-the-wisp."</note> in the darkness.

347. Regarding the **FORMATION OF FAITH**, it is formed by a person approaching the Lord, learning Truths from the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Holy Scriptures.</note>, and living according to them. 

*First, That faith is formed by a person approaching the Lord*, is because faith that is truly faith—and thus the faith of salvation—is from the Lord and in the Lord. That it is *from* the Lord is clear from His own words to the Disciples: *Abide in Me, and I in you, because without Me, you can do nothing* (John 15:4, 5). That faith is *in* the Lord is clear from those passages which were brought forward in abundance above in numbers 237 and 238, which state that one must believe in the Son. Now, because Faith is from the Lord and in the Lord, it can be said that the Lord is Faith itself, for its life and essence are in the Lord, and thus from the Lord. 

SECOND, *That faith is formed by a person learning truths from the Word*, the reason is that Faith in its essence is Truth; for all things that enter into faith are truths. Therefore, Faith is nothing other than a complex of truths shining in the human mind. For Truths teach not only what must be believed, but also in whom one must believe and what is to be believed. The reason Truths must be taken from the Word is because all truths that lead to salvation are there, and they contain efficacy because they were given by the Lord and are thereby inscribed upon the whole Angelic Heaven. Thus, when a person learns truths from the Word, they come into communion and association with the Angels, though they may not know it. Faith without truths is like a seed stripped of its marrowy substance, which, when ground, yields only chaff; but Faith from truths is like a fruitful seed which, when ground, yields flour. In a word, the essentials of Faith are truths; if these are not present and composed within it, faith is merely like the shrill sound of a whistle, but when they are present and composed, faith is like the voice of a thing bringing salvation. 

THIRD, *That faith is formed by a person living according to truths*, the reason is that spiritual life is a life according to truths, and truths do not actually "live" until they are in deeds. Truths abstracted from deeds belong to thought alone; if they do not also become part of the will, they sit only on the threshold of the person and are thus not truly inside them. For the will is the person himself, and the thought is only as much of a person, and of such a quality, as the degree to which it has joined itself to the will. He who learns truths and does not do them is like someone who scatters seeds over a field but does not harrow them in; consequently, the seeds swell from the rain and turn into spoiled husks. But he who learns truths and does them is like one who sows and plows the seed in, so that the seeds grow from the rain into a harvest and become useful for nourishment. The Lord says: *If you know these things, blessed are you if you do them* (John 13:17). And elsewhere: *He who was sown on good ground is he who hears the Word and attends to it, and thereafter bears fruit and does it* (Matthew 13:23). Also: *Everyone who hears my words and does them, I will compare to a wise man who built his house upon a rock; but everyone hearing my words, but not doing them, shall be compared to a foolish man who built his house upon the sand* (Matthew 7:24, 26). The Lord's words are all truths.

348. From the things said above, it is clear that there are three things through which Faith is formed in a person: namely, first, to approach the Lord; second, to learn truths from the Word; and third, to live according to them. Now, because there are three things, and one is not the other, it follows that they can be separated; for one can approach the Lord and yet not know truths about God and the Lord except as historical facts; and also one can...

Faith without truths is like a vine bearing wild grapes; but faith from truths is like a vine bearing clusters of noble wine. Faith in the Lord without truths may be compared to a "new star" <note>A *stella nova* or supernova, which appears suddenly and then fades.</note> appearing in the expanse of Heaven, which is obscured in time; but faith in the Lord with truths may be compared to a fixed star, which remains forever. Truth is the essence of faith; therefore, as the truth is, so is the faith—which without truths is wandering, but with them is fixed; indeed, the faith of truths shines in heaven like a star.

## IV.

->*That an abundance of truths cohering together, as if in a bundle,*<-
->*exalts and perfects faith.*<-

349. From the current perception of faith as it exists today, it cannot be known that faith in its full scope is a complex of truths, and even less that a person can contribute anything toward acquiring faith for themselves; yet faith in its essence is truth—for it is truth in its own light—and just as truth can be acquired, so too can faith. Who cannot approach the Lord if they wish? And who cannot collect truths from the Word if they wish? Every truth in the Word and from the Word shines, and truth in light is faith. The Lord, who is Light itself, flows into every person; and in those in whom there are truths from the Word, He causes them to shine and thus to become the things of faith. This is what the Lord says in John: *If they abide in the Lord, and His words abide in them* (Chapter 15:7); the Lord's words are truths. But so that it may be properly understood that an abundance of truths cohering together, as if in a bundle, exalts and perfects faith, the discussion must be divided into these points: 1. *That the truths of faith are capable of being multiplied to infinity.* 2. *That their arrangement is in series, as if in bundles.* 3. *That faith is perfected according to their abundance and coherence.* 4. *That truths, however numerous they are and however diverse they appear, make one from the Lord, who is the Word, the God of Heaven and Earth, the God of all flesh, the God of the Vineyard or Church, the God of faith, and Light, Truth, and Eternal Life itself.*

350. **THAT THE TRUTHS OF FAITH ARE CAPABLE OF BEING MULTIPLIED TO INFINITY** can be established from the wisdom of the Angels of Heaven, which increases to eternity. The Angels even say that there is no end to wisdom anywhere, and wisdom comes from no other source than from...

When Divine Truths are analytically arranged into forms, with the middle light <note>The "middle light" refers to the spiritual illumination that enters the human mind from the Lord, mediating between divine wisdom and human understanding.</note> flowing in from the Lord: then there is human intelligence, which is truly intelligence, and it comes from no other source. The multiplication of Divine Truth is infinite for this reason: because the Lord is Divine Truth itself, or Truth in its infinity, and He draws everyone to Himself; but angels and humans cannot follow the pull of this attraction except according to their own limited measure <note>original: "demensa"</note>, while the effort of that attraction remains constantly infinite. The Word of the Lord is an abyss of truths from which all angelic wisdom comes, even though to a person who knows nothing of its spiritual and heavenly sense, it appears to be no more than water in a jar. This infinite multiplication of the truths of faith can be compared to the seeds of men, from one of whom whole families can be propagated for ages of ages. The proliferation of the truths of faith can also be compared to the proliferation of seeds in a field or garden, which can be propagated into myriads of myriads, and forever; for by "Seed" in the Word nothing else is understood than Truth, by "Field" is meant Doctrine, and by "Garden" is meant wisdom. The human mind is like Soil <note>original: "Humus"</note>, in which spiritual and natural truths are implanted like seeds and can be multiplied without end; a person derives this from the Infinity of God, who, with His light and His heat, and with the faculty of generating, is perpetually present within.

### 351. THAT THE ARRANGEMENT OF THE TRUTHS OF FAITH IS IN SERIES, JUST AS IN BUNDLES;

That it is so arranged is as yet unknown; and it is unknown because spiritual Truths, from which the entire Word is woven together, could not be seen on account of the mystical and enigmatic faith which makes up every point of modern Theology, and therefore they have sunk into the ground like hidden granaries. To understand what is meant by series and bundles, an explanation will be given: The first Chapter of this Book, which deals with God the Creator, is divided into Series, of which the first is about the Unity of God, the second about the *Being* <note>original: "Esse"</note> of God, or Jehovah, the third about the Infinity of God, the fourth about the Essence of God (which is Divine Love and Divine Wisdom), the fifth about the Omnipotence of God, and the sixth about Creation. The individual articulations of each part form series, binding those things within them together like sheaves. These series, in general and in particular, thus both together and separately, contain truths which, according to their abundance and simultaneous coherence, exalt and perfect faith. 

He who does not know that the human Mind is organized, or that it is a spiritual organism ending in a natural organism in which and according to which the Mind operates its ideas or thoughts, cannot help but think that perceptions, thoughts, and ideas are nothing other than radiations and variations of light flowing into the head and presenting forms which a person sees and acknowledges as reasons; but this is a delusion <note>original: "delirum"</note>. For everyone knows that the head is full of brains, and that the brains are organized, and that the Mind dwells in them, and that its ideas are fixed therein and remain as they have been received and confirmed. The question is, therefore, what is that organization like? The answer is that it is an ordering of everything into series, as if into bundles, and that the truths which belong to faith are thus arranged in the human Mind. 

That this is so can be illustrated by the following: the Brain consists of two substances, one of which is glandular and is called the *cortical* <note>The outer layer of the brain, known as gray matter.</note> and *cineritious* <note>Literally "ashen-colored," another term for gray matter.</note> substance, and the other is fibrillar and is called the *medullary* <note>The inner "marrow" or white matter of the brain.</note> substance. The first substance, which is glandular, is arranged into clusters like grapes on a vine; those clusterings are its series. The other substance, called the medullary, consists of perpetual bundlings <note>original: "confasciculationibus"</note> of fibers proceeding from the glands of the first substance; these bundlings are its series. All the nerves that proceed from there and descend into the body to perform various duties are nothing other than sheaves and bundles of fibers; likewise all the muscles, and in general all the viscera and organs of the body. Both these and those are such because they correspond to the series into which the organism of the mind is arranged. Moreover, in all of Nature there is nothing that is not bundled into series: every tree, every shrub, shoot, and legume—indeed, every ear of grain and blade of grass, in general and in part—is so. The universal cause is that Divine Truths are so conformed; for it is written,

that all things were created through the Word, that is, **Divine Truth**, and that the World also was made through it, John 1:1 and following. From these things it can be seen that unless such an organization of substances existed in the human mind, there would be no analytical faculty of reason for man; for this faculty exists in everyone according to that organization—that is, according to the abundance of truths clinging together as if in a bundle—and that organization follows the use of reason from a state of freedom.

### 352. THAT FAITH IS PERFECTED ACCORDING TO THE ABUNDANCE AND COHERENCE OF TRUTHS,
follows from what was said above, and reveals itself to anyone who collects reasons and perceives what multiplied series can achieve when they cling together as one; for then one thing strengthens and confirms another, and together they create a form which, when put into action, performs a single act. Now, because faith in its essence is truth, it follows that according to the abundance and coherence of truths, it becomes more and more perfectly spiritual, and thus less and less natural and sensory; for it is exalted into a higher region of the mind, from which it sees beneath itself the cohorts of its own confirmations in the nature of the World. True faith, through an abundance of truths clinging together as if in a bundle, also becomes more illustrative, perceptible, evident, and clear. It also becomes more capable of being joined with the goods of **Charity**, and thereby more alienated from evils, and successively more remote from the allurements of the eye and the lusts of the flesh, and therefore happier in itself. It becomes, above all, more powerful against evils and falsities, and thus more and more living and saving.

### 353. IT WAS STATED ABOVE,
that every truth shines in Heaven, and therefore that shining truth is faith in its essence; wherefore the beauty and grace of faith resulting from that illumination, when its truths are multiplied, can be compared to various forms, objects, and pictures formed from different colors arranged according to their harmonies. It may therefore be compared with the various colored precious stones in the **Breastplate of Aaron**, which together were called the <term>Urim and Thummim</term> <note>Hebrew for "Lights and Perfections," these were sacred stones used by the High Priest to discern the Divine will.</note>; likewise with the precious stones from which the foundations of the wall of the **New Jerusalem** are to be built, as described in Revelation chapter 21. It can also be compared with the various colored precious stones in a King’s Crown; for precious stones signify the truths of faith. A comparison can also be made with the beauty of a rainbow, with the beauty of a flowering field, and also of a garden in bloom at the first break of spring. The light and glory of faith resulting from the abundance of truths that adorn it can be compared to the illumination of Temples by multiple chandeliers, of houses by lamps, and of streets by lanterns. The exaltation of faith through an abundance of truths can be illustrated by comparison with the exaltation of a trumpet blast combined with a melody from many musical instruments in harmony; and also with the exaltation of fragrance from a bouquet of sweet-smelling flowers, and so on. The power of faith, formed from a plurality of truths against falsities and evils, can be compared to the firmness of a Temple built of stones connected in an orderly way, with columns built into its walls and supporting its ceiling; it can also be compared to a **square military formation**, in which the soldiers stand shoulder to shoulder, and thus form and act as a single strength; it can also be compared to the muscles with which the whole body is interwoven, which, although they are numerous and scattered, nevertheless create one power in actions, and so forth.

### 354. THAT THE TRUTHS OF FAITH, HOWEVER NUMEROUS THEY ARE AND HOWEVER DIVERSE THEY APPEAR, ARE MADE ONE BY THE LORD, WHO IS THE WORD, THE GOD OF HEAVEN AND EARTH, THE GOD OF ALL FLESH, THE GOD OF THE VINEYARD OR THE CHURCH, THE GOD OF FAITH, AND LIGHT ITSELF, TRUTH, AND ETERNAL LIFE.
The truths of faith are various and appear diverse to man; for example, some concern God the Creator, others the Lord the Redeemer, others the Holy Spirit and Divine Operation, others Faith and Charity, and others **Free Will**, **Repentance**, **Reformation** and **Regeneration**, **Imputation**, and so on; yet they make one in the Lord, and in man from the Lord, like many branches in one Vine, John 15:1 and following. For the Lord joins scattered and divided truths as if into one form, in which they present a single view and perform a single act. This can be illustrated by comparison with the members,

As shown previously, it is like a single Great Man. It is also like a Kingdom; although it is divided into many administrations, and also provinces and cities, it nevertheless constitutes a single entity under a King who possesses justice and judgment. 

The reason why the same is true of the Truths of faith (from which the Church becomes the Church from the Lord) is because the Lord is the <term>Word</term> <note>original: "Verbum"; the Divine Truth or Logos.</note>, the God of Heaven and Earth, the God of all flesh, the God of the Vineyard or Church, the God of faith, and Light itself, Truth, and Eternal Life. 

That the Lord is the Word, and thus every Truth of Heaven and the Church, is evident in John: *In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God... and the Word was made Flesh,* Chapter 1:1, 2, 14. 

That the Lord is the God of Heaven and Earth is evident in Matthew: *Jesus said, all power is given unto Me in Heaven and in Earth,* Chapter 28:18. 

That the Lord is the God of all Flesh is in John: *The Father gave the Son power over all flesh,* Chapter 16:2. 

That the Lord is the God of the <term>Vineyard</term> <note>original: "Vinea"; a traditional biblical metaphor for the Church or the Lord's people.</note> or Church is in Isaiah: *My beloved had a vineyard,* Chapter 5:1, 2; and in John: *I am the Vine and you are the branches,* John 15:5. 

That the Lord is the God of faith is in Paul: *You have the justice which is from the faith of Christ, from the God of faith,* Philippians 3:9. 

That the Lord is Light itself is in John: *He was the true Light, which enlightens every man coming into the World,* Chapter 1:9; and elsewhere: *Jesus said, I have come as Light into the World, so that everyone who believes in Me should not remain in darkness,* Chapter 12:46. 

That the Lord is Truth itself is in John: *Jesus said, I am the Way, the Truth, and the Life,* Chapter 14:6. 

That the Lord is Eternal Life is in John: *We know that the Son of God has come into the World, so that we might know the truth, and we are in the Truth in Jesus Christ; He is the True God, and Eternal Life,* 1 John Chapter 5:20, 21.

To these things it must be added that a person, due to their business in the World, can only acquire a few truths of faith for themselves. Yet if they approach the Lord and worship Him Alone, they come into the power of knowing all truths. Therefore, every true worshiper of the Lord—as soon as they hear some truth of faith they did not know before—immediately sees, acknowledges, and receives it. The reason is that the Lord is in them, and they are in the Lord; consequently, the Light of truth is in them, and they are in the light of truth; for as was said above, the Lord is Light itself and Truth itself. 

This can be confirmed by this experience: a Spirit was seen by me who, in the company of others, appeared simple, for the reason that he acknowledged the Lord Alone as the God of Heaven and Earth, and had established this faith of his through several truths from the Word. This spirit was taken up into Heaven among the wiser Angels, and it was told to me that he was just as wise there as they were—indeed, that he spoke truths in abundance, entirely as if from himself, of which he had known nothing at all before. 

Such will be the state of those who are to come into the Lord’s New Church. This is the same state described in Jeremiah: *This shall be the covenant which I will strike with the House of Israel after those days; I will give my law in their midst, and write it upon their hearts: and they shall no longer teach a man his companion, or a man his brother, saying "know the Lord," for all shall know Me, from the least of them even to the greatest of them,* Chapter 31:33, 34. 

That state will also be such as is described in Isaiah: *A rod shall go forth from the stem of Jesse <note>original: "Jiſchaji"</note>, Truth shall be the belt of his loins; then the wolf shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid; the nursing child shall play over the hole of the viper, and the weaned child shall put his hand over the basilisk's den; because the Earth shall be full of the knowledge of Jehovah, as the waters cover the sea; in that day the nations shall seek the Root of Jesse, and His rest shall be glory,* Chapter 11:6 to 10.

# V.

## *That Faith without Charity is not faith, & that Charity without faith is not charity; & that neither has life except from the Lord.*

355. The church of today has separated faith from <term>Charity</term> <note>original: "Charitas"; in this theological context, it refers to active love for one's neighbor and spiritual goodwill, rather than just giving alms.</note>, claiming that **Faith Alone** without the works of the law justifies and saves. They argue that Charity cannot be joined with Faith because Faith is from God, while Charity—insofar as it is expressed in works—is from man. Such a thought never entered the mind of any Apostle, as is clearly evident from their Epistles. Rather, this separation and division was introduced into the Christian Church when they divided the one God into three Persons and assigned equal Divinity to each. 

However, that there is no Faith without Charity, nor Charity without faith, and that neither has life except from the Lord, will be illustrated in the following <term>Lemma</term> <note>original: "Lemmate"; a theme or proposition used as a basis for argument.</note>; here, to clear the way, it will be demonstrated: 1. That man can acquire faith for himself. 2. That he can also acquire Charity. 3. And also the Life of both. 4. Yet, nonetheless, nothing of faith, nothing of charity, and nothing of the life of either is from man, but from the Lord Alone.

356. I. THAT MAN CAN ACQUIRE FAITH FOR HIMSELF was shown in the Third Lemma above (from numbers 243 to 248), and by the fact that Faith in its essence is Truth, and Truths from the Word can be acquired by anyone. To the degree that anyone acquires these for himself and loves them, he initiates faith within himself. To this, the following must be added: unless man could acquire faith for himself, all the commands in the Word concerning Faith would be useless. For it is read there: *That it is the Will of the Father that they believe in the Son, and that he who believes in Him has eternal life, and he who does not believe shall not see life.* It is also read: *that Jesus would send the <term>Paraclete</term> <note>original: "Paracletum"; the Holy Spirit, often translated as the Comforter or Advocate.</note>, who will convict the World of sin, because they do not believe in Me,* besides many more passages cited in numbers 237 and 238. 

Furthermore, all the Apostles preached Faith, and this faith was in the Lord God the Savior Jesus Christ. What would all these commands be if a man were to stand with his hands hanging down like a carved statue with movable joints, waiting for an influx? In such a case, the joints—besides being able to adapt themselves to receive that influx—would be moved from within to something that is not faith. For the modern <term>Orthodoxy</term> in the Christian World (separated from the Roman Catholics) teaches as follows:

*That man is so utterly corrupt and dead to what is good that, in human nature after the fall and before regeneration, not even a spark of spiritual power remains or is left by which he could prepare himself for God's grace, or apprehend it when offered, or be capable of that grace by or through himself. Nor can he, in spiritual things, understand, believe, embrace, think, will, begin, perfect, act, operate, cooperate, or apply or adapt himself to grace, or do anything toward his conversion in whole, in half, or in the slightest part, by himself. And that man in spiritual things, which regard the salvation of the soul, is like the statue of salt of Lot’s wife, and similar to a trunk or a stone lacking life, which has no use of eyes, mouth, or any senses. He does, however, possess the power of motion in that he can govern his external limbs, attend public gatherings, and hear the Word and the Gospel.* 

These things are found in the Book of the Evangelical Church called the **FORMULA OF CONCORD** <note>original: "FORMULA CONCORDIA"; a foundational Lutheran statement of faith from 1577.</note> in the Leipzig Edition of 1756, pages 656, 658, 661, 662, 663, 671, 672, 673. Priests swear to this Book, and thus to this faith, when they are inaugurated. A similar faith is held by the Reformed. But who, possessing reason and religion, would not hiss at these ideas as absurd and ridiculous? For such a person would say to himself: If this were so, what then is the Word? What is Religion? What is the Priesthood? And to what—

357. II. THAT MAN CAN ACQUIRE <term>CHARITY</term> <note>original: "CHARITATEM"; here meaning active love for the neighbor and spiritual goodwill.</note> FOR HIMSELF; this is a similar case to that of faith. For what else does the Word teach than Faith and Charity, since these are the two essentials of salvation? For it is read: *You shall love the Lord from all your heart and from all your soul, and your neighbor as yourself*, Matthew 22:34 to 39; and *Jesus said, a commandment I give to you, that you love one another*; from this *you shall be known that you are my disciples, that you love one another*, John 13:34, 35; likewise Chapter 15:9 and Chapter 16:27. Furthermore, it says that man is to produce fruits like a good tree; and that he who does good things shall be rewarded in the resurrection; besides many similar passages. Why would these exist unless a man could exercise Charity of himself, and acquire it for himself in some way? Can he not give alms, help the needy, do good in his own house and in his office? Can he not live according to the precepts of the <term>Decalogue</term> <note>The Ten Commandments.</note>? Does he not have a soul from which he can perform those actions, and also a rational Mind, by which he can lead himself to act for this or that purpose? Can he not think that he should do those things because they are commanded in the Word, and thus are from God? No man lacks this power; and the reason he does not lack it is because the Lord gives it to every person, and He gives it as if it were something belonging to the person themselves. For who, while performing an act of charity, feels any differently than that he does it from himself?

358. III. THAT MAN CAN ALSO ACQUIRE FOR HIMSELF THE LIFE OF FAITH AND CHARITY is also a similar matter; for he acquires that life for himself while he approaches the Lord, who is Life itself. Access to Him is not blocked for any man, for He continually invites every man to come to Him; for He said, *he who comes to Me shall not hunger, and he who believes in Me shall never thirst; and him who comes to Me, I will not cast out*, John 6:35, 37. *Jesus stood and cried out, if anyone thirsts, let him come to Me and drink*, John 7:37. And elsewhere: *The Kingdom of the Heavens is like a king who made a wedding for his son, and sent his servants to call those invited... and finally said, go to the outlets of the waters, and whomever you find, call to the wedding*, Matthew 22:1 to 9. Who does not know that the Invitation or calling is universal, and also the grace of reception? The reason man obtains Life by approaching the Lord is because the Lord is Life itself—not only the Life of faith, but also the Life of charity. That the Lord is that Life, and that it is given to man by the Lord, is evident from these passages: *In the beginning was the Word... in Him was LIFE, and the LIFE was the light of men*, John 1:1, 4. *Just as the Father raises the dead and gives life, so the Son GIVES LIFE to whom He wills*, John 5:21. *Just as the Father has Life in Himself, so He has given to the Son TO HAVE LIFE IN HIMSELF*, John 5:26. *The bread of God is He who descends from Heaven, and gives LIFE to the World*, John 6:33. *The words which I speak to you are spirit and LIFE*, John 6:63. *Jesus said, he who follows Me... shall have the LIGHT OF LIFE*, John 8:12. *I have come that they might HAVE LIFE, and have it in abundance*, John 10:10. *He who believes in Me, even if he dies, SHALL LIVE*, John 11:25. *I am the way, the truth, and the LIFE*, John 14:6. BECAUSE I LIVE, YOU ALSO SHALL LIVE, John 14:19. *These things are written that you might have LIFE in His name*, John 20:31. That He is ETERNAL LIFE, 1 John 5:21. By the Life in Faith and Charity is meant spiritual life, which is given by the Lord to man within his natural life.

359. IV. From these it follows as a conclusion that just as man naturally prepares himself to receive the Lord, so the Lord enters and makes all things within him spiritual, and thus alive. Conversely, however, to the extent that man does not prepare himself, he removes the Lord from himself and does everything from his own self; and what man does from his own self has no life in it. But these things cannot yet be presented in a clear light to be seen until <term>CHARITY</term> and <term>FREE WILL</term> <note>original: "LIBERO ARBITRIO"; the capacity of a human to choose their own spiritual path.</note> have been treated, and they will be seen later in the chapter on <term>REFORMATION AND REGENERATION</term> <note>The process of spiritual rebirth and the reshaping of one's character.</note>.

360. In the preceding sections it was stated that Faith is at first natural in man, and that as man approaches the Lord, it becomes spiritual—and similarly Charity. But no one has yet known the distinction between natural and spiritual Faith and Charity; therefore, this great <term>Secret</term> <note>original: "Arcanum"; a term Swedenborg frequently uses to describe hidden spiritual truths now being revealed.</note> must be uncovered. There are two Worlds, the Natural and the Spiritual, and in each World there is a Sun. From each Sun, Heat and Light proceed. However, the Heat and Light from the Sun of the spiritual world have life within them; their life is from the Lord, who is in the midst of that Sun. But the Heat and Light from the Sun of the natural world have nothing of life in themselves; rather, they serve the former two as receptacles, just as instrumental causes serve their principal ones in order to convey them to men. It should be known, then, that the Heat and Light from the Sun of the spiritual world are that from which all spiritual things originate; they are indeed spiritual because spirit and life are within them. But the Heat and Light from the Sun of the natural world are that from which all natural things originate, which, viewed in themselves, are without spirit and life.

Now, because Faith is of light and Charity is of heat, it is evident that to the extent a man is in the Light and Heat proceeding from the Sun of the spiritual world, he is in spiritual Faith and Charity; but to the extent he is in the Light and heat proceeding from the Sun of the natural world, he is in natural Faith and Charity. From this it is established that just as Spiritual Light is within natural Light as in its receptacle or its case, and likewise spiritual Heat within natural Heat, so also spiritual Faith is within natural Faith, and likewise spiritual Charity within natural Charity. This occurs in the degree that man progresses from the natural World into the spiritual World; and he progresses as he believes in the Lord, who is the Light itself, the Way, the Truth, and the Life, as He himself teaches. Since this is so, it is evident that when a man is in spiritual Faith, he is then also in natural Faith; for, as was said, spiritual Faith is inside natural Faith. And because Faith is of light, it follows that through this insertion, the Natural part of man becomes, as it were, transparent, and according to how it is joined with charity, it becomes beautifully colored. The reason is that Charity is red and Faith is white; Charity is red from the flame of spiritual fire, and Faith is white from the splendor of the light therefrom. The opposite happens if the Spiritual is not within the Natural, but the Natural is within the Spiritual. This occurs in those who reject faith and charity. In these people, the Internal of their mind—in which they are when they think while left to themselves—is infernal, and they also think from Hell, even though they do not know it. But the External of their mind—from which they speak with associates in the World—is like something spiritual, but it is filled with such uncleanness as exists in Hell. Therefore, these people are in Hell, for they are in an inverted state relative to the former group.

361. Since it is known that the spiritual resides within the natural in those who have faith in the Lord and simultaneously possess <term>Charity</term> <note>original: "Charitas"; spiritual love for one's neighbor</note> toward their neighbor, and that consequently the <term>Natural</term> <note>The external part of the human being that deals with the physical world.</note> in them is transparent, it follows that a person may be wise in spiritual matters and, from that source, also in natural matters. For such a person sees within themselves—while thinking, reading, or hearing—whether a thing is true or not; they perceive this from the Lord, from whom spiritual light and heat flow into the higher sphere of their intellect. To the extent that Faith and Charity become spiritual in a person, they are withdrawn from their <term>proprium</term> <note>original: "proprio"; the "self" or what is one's own, often associated with ego or selfish tendencies.</note> and do not look to themselves, to profit, or to reward, but only to the delight of perceiving the Truths of faith and doing the good works of love. As that spirituality increases, that delight becomes a state of blessing; from this comes their salvation, which is called eternal life.

This state of man can be compared with the most beautiful and pleasant things in the world, and is indeed compared to them in the Word <note>The Bible.</note>: such as to fruit-bearing trees and the gardens in which they grow; to flowery fields; to precious stones; to delicacies; and also to weddings, with their festivities and rejoicings.

However, when the order is reversed—namely, when the Natural is inside the Spiritual—the person is a Devil in their internal self and appears like an Angel in their external self. Then they can be compared to a dead man in a coffin made of precious wood and gilded with gold. They can also be compared to a skeleton dressed in clothes like a living person and carried in a magnificent carriage; or to a corpse in a tomb built like the Temple of Diana <note>original: "Templum Dianæ"; one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, here used as a metaphor for a grand external structure hiding something dead.</note>. Indeed, their internal self can be likened to a nest of snakes in a cave, while the external appears like butterflies whose wings are tinted with colors of every kind, yet who glue their filthy eggs to the leaves of useful trees, by which their fruits are consumed. Furthermore, their internal self may be compared to a hawk and their external to a dove; their Faith and Charity are like a hawk's flight over a fleeing dove, which it eventually exhausts, then attacks and devours.

## VI.

->*That the Lord, Charity, and Faith make one, just as Life, Will, and Intellect do in man; and if they are divided, each one perishes, like a union crumbled into dust.*<-

362. First, certain things will be mentioned which have been unknown until now in the Learned World <note>The academic and scientific community.</note> and consequently in the ecclesiastical order—unknown as if they were buried in the earth. Yet these are treasures of wisdom; unless they are dug up and given to the public, a person strives in vain to arrive at any just knowledge concerning God, Faith, Charity, and the state of their own life, or how they should govern and prepare it for the state of eternal life. These unknown things are as follows:

1. That man is a mere <term>organ of life</term> <note>A vessel or instrument that receives life rather than originating it.</note>.
2. That life, with all its parts, flows in from the God of Heaven, who is the Lord.
3. That there are two faculties of life in man, called the Will and the Intellect; the Will is the receptacle of love, and the Intellect is the receptacle of wisdom. Thus, the Will is the receptacle of Charity, and the Intellect is the receptacle of Faith.
4. That everything a person wills and everything they understand flows in from the outside: the goods of love and charity, and the truths of wisdom and faith, come from the Lord; but everything contrary to these comes from Hell.
5. That it is provided by the Lord that a person should feel those things which flow in from the outside within themselves as if they were their own, and thus produce them from themselves as if they were their own, even though none of these things belong to them.
6. That nonetheless, these things are credited to the person as their own because of <term>Free Will</term> <note>original: "Liberum arbitrium"</note>, in which resides their <term>Willing and Thinking</term> <note>original: "Velle & Cogitare"</note>, and because of the knowledge of good and truth given to them, from which they can freely choose whatever is [necessary] for their temporal life...

...and it conduces to eternal life. A person who looks at these things with a sideways glance or a squint <note>original: "obliquo oculo seu hirquis"; 'hirquis' refers to looking out of the corner of one's eye, often implying a distorted or suspicious perspective.</note> can conclude from them many things that are madness; but a person who looks at them with a straight eye or a clear pupil can conclude many things that are of wisdom. To ensure the latter happens rather than the former, it was necessary to first set forth judgments and dogmas concerning God and the Divine Trinity, and after those to establish judgments and dogmas concerning Faith and <term>Charity</term> <note>Love for the neighbor in a spiritual sense.</note>, concerning <term>Free Will</term> <note>original: "Libero Arbitrio"; the human capacity to choose between good and evil.</note>, and concerning Reformation and Regeneration, as well as concerning <term>Imputation</term> <note>The theological concept of how God credits righteousness or sin to an individual.</note>; and also concerning Repentance, concerning Baptism, and concerning the Holy Supper, as means.

363. Now, in order that this article of faith—which is that the Lord, Charity, and Faith make one, just as Life, Will, and Intellect do in man, and that if they are divided each one perishes like a union collapsed into dust—may be seen and acknowledged as truth, it is important to consider it in this order:
I. That the Lord, with all His Divine love, with all His Divine Wisdom, and thus with all His Divine Life, flows into every person.
II. Consequently, He flows in with every Essence of Faith and Charity.
III. But these are received by a person according to their own form.
IV. However, the person who divides the Lord, Charity, and Faith does not become a receiving form, but a form that destroys them.

364. **I. THAT THE LORD, WITH ALL HIS DIVINE LOVE, WITH ALL HIS DIVINE WISDOM, AND THUS WITH ALL HIS DIVINE LIFE, FLOWS INTO EVERY PERSON.**
In the *Book of Creation* <note>The Book of Genesis.</note> it is read that man was created as the Image of God, and that God breathed into his nostrils the breath of lives <note>original: "animam vitarum"; the plural "lives" reflects the original Hebrew and suggests the animation of both the spiritual and natural parts of man.</note>, *Genesis, Ch. 1:27, Ch. 2:7*, by which it is described that man is an <term>Organ of life</term> <note>A vessel or instrument through which life flows, rather than the source of life itself.</note>, and not life itself. For God could not create another similar to Himself—if He could have done this, there would be as many gods as there are people; nor could He create life, just as light cannot be created, but He could create man as a form of life, just as He created the eye as a form of light. Nor could God—and nor can He—divide His essence, for this is one and individual. Since, therefore, God alone is life, it follows without doubt that God gives life to every person from His own Life, and that without that life-giving, a person would be a mere sponge as to their flesh, and a mere skeleton as to their bones, in which there would be no more life than in a clock, which is moved by a pendulum and simultaneously by a weight or a spring. Since this is the case, it also follows that God flows into every person with all His Divine Life—that is, with all His Divine Love and His Divine Wisdom (these two make up His Divine Life, as seen above in numbers 39 and 40); for the Divine cannot be divided. 

How God flows in with all His Divine Life can be perceived in some way through a similar idea by which it is perceived that the Sun of the World, with all its essence—which consists of heat and light—flows into every tree, and into every shrub and flower, and into every stone, whether humble or noble; and that each individual object draws its portion from this common inflow, and that the Sun does not divide its light and its heat and dispense a part to this and a part to that. It is similar with the <term>Sun of Heaven</term> <note>In this theological context, the spiritual sun which radiates the Lord's love and wisdom.</note>, from which Divine love proceeds as heat, and Divine Wisdom as light; these two flow into human minds, just as the heat and light of the world's sun flow into bodies, and it gives them life according to the quality of their form, each of which takes its necessity from the common inflow. To this is applicable what the Lord says: *Your Father makes His sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the just and the unjust, Matthew 5:45.* The Lord is also omnipresent, and where He is present, He is there with His whole Essence, and it is impossible for Him to take anything away from it and thus give a part to one and a part to another, but He gives it all, and gives the person the opportunity to take a little or a lot; He also says that with those who do His commandments He has a dwelling place, and also that the faithful are in Him and He in them. In a word, all things are full of God, and everyone receives their portion from that fullness. It is similar with every common thing, such as with the atmospheres and oceans; the atmosphere is the same in its smallest parts as in its largest; it does not dispense a part of itself for a person's breathing, or for a bird's flight, or for the sails of a ship, or for the wings of a mill, but each one...

...receives from there his measured portion <note>original: "demensum"; an allotted amount or ration.</note>, and applies to himself as much as is sufficient; it is also like a granary full of wheat, from which the owner daily takes his food, and the granary does not distribute it <note>The storehouse remains full; the person must actively take from it.</note>.

### 365. II. CONSEQUENTLY, THE LORD FLOWS INTO EVERY PERSON WITH THE ENTIRE ESSENCE OF FAITH AND CHARITY:

This follows from the previous proposition <note>original: "Theoremate priori"</note>, since the Life of Divine Wisdom is the essence of faith, and the Life of Divine Love is the essence of <term>charity</term> <note>In this context, charity is the active love of the neighbor.</note>; therefore, when the Lord is present with those things which are properly His—which are Divine Wisdom and Divine Love—He is also present with all the truths belonging to Faith, and with all the goods belonging to Charity. For by Faith is meant every Truth which a person perceives, thinks, and speaks from the Lord; and by Charity is meant every Good with which he is affected from the Lord, and which he subsequently wills and does. It was stated above that Divine Love, which proceeds from the Lord as a <term>Sun</term> <note>The "Spiritual Sun" is a central concept in Swedenborg's theology, representing the source of spiritual heat (love) and light (wisdom).</note>, is perceived by Angels as Heat, and Divine Wisdom is perceived from it as Light. But anyone who does not think beyond appearances might imagine that this Heat is mere heat, and that Light is mere light, like the heat and light proceeding from the sun of our world. However, the Heat and Light proceeding from the Lord as a Sun contain in their bosom all the Infinities that are in the Lord: the Heat contains all the Infinities of His love, and the Light all the Infinities of His wisdom—thus also, in infinity, every good that belongs to Charity and every Truth that belongs to Faith. The reason is that this Sun itself is present everywhere in its heat and in its light; and that Sun is the nearest circle surrounding the Lord, emanating from His Divine Love and at the same time from His Divine Wisdom, for as has been said several times above, the Lord is in the midst of that Sun.

From these things it is now evident that nothing can be lacking to prevent a person, because the Lord is <term>omnipresent</term>, from taking from Him every good of charity and every truth of faith. That nothing of these is lacking is clear from the love and wisdom of the angels of heaven, which are theirs from the Lord—that they are ineffable and incomprehensible to the natural man, and are also capable of being multiplied to eternity. That Infinities are within the Heat and Light which proceed from the Lord, even though they are perceived simply as heat and light, can be illustrated by various things in the natural world, such as these: the sound of a person’s voice and speech is heard only as a simple sound, and yet when the angels hear it, they perceive in it all the affections of his love, and they also manifest what and of what quality they are. That these things lie hidden within the sound, a person can even perceive to some extent for himself from the tone of someone speaking to him—such as whether there is contempt, or mockery, or hatred within it, and also whether there is charity, benevolence, joy, or other affections. Similar things lie hidden in the rays of the eye when it looks at someone. 

It can also be illustrated by the fragrances from a vast garden, or the fragrances from extensive flowery fields; the fragrant odor exhaled from them consists of thousands and myriads of different elements, and yet they are felt as one. It is similar with many other things which, although they appear uniform on the outside, are nevertheless manifold within. <term>Sympathies and antipathies</term> <note>Natural attractions or aversions between people.</note> are nothing other than the exhalations of affections from minds, which affect another person according to similarities and cause aversion according to dissimilarities. Although these are innumerable and are not felt by any sense of the body, they are nevertheless perceived by the sense of the soul as one, and all conjunctions and associations in the <term>Spiritual World</term> occur according to them. These examples are brought forward to illustrate what was said above about Spiritual Light which proceeds from the Lord—that all things of wisdom, and thus all things of faith, are within it; and that this is the Light by which the <term>Understanding</term> sees and perceives rational things analytically, just as the eye sees and perceives natural things symmetrically.

### 366. III. THE THINGS WHICH FLOW IN FROM THE LORD ARE RECEIVED BY A PERSON ACCORDING TO HIS FORM,

By "form" here is meant the state of the person regarding his love and simultaneously his wisdom—consequently also regarding the affections for the goods of charity and simultaneously the perceptions of the truths of his faith. That God is one, individual, and the same from eternity to eternity—not simply the same, but infinite—and that all variation is...

...from the subject in which it exists, as was shown above; that the receiving Form or state introduces variations can be established from the Life of infants, children, youths, adults, and the elderly. The same Life—because the same soul—is in everyone from infancy to old age, but just as its state varies according to age and adaptations, so too is life perceived. The Life of God in all its fullness is present not only with good and pious people, but also with evil and impious ones; likewise with the Angels of Heaven and the Spirits of Hell. The difference is that the evil block the way and shut the door so that God may not enter into the lower parts of their minds, whereas the good clear the way and open the door, and also invite God to enter into the lower parts of their minds just as He dwells in the highest parts. Thus they form the state of the <term>will</term> <note>In Swedenborg’s system, the "will" is the seat of love and intention.</note> for the <term>influx</term> <note>The spiritual process of life "flowing in" from God to the soul.</note> of love and charity, and the state of the <term>understanding</term> <note>The "understanding" is the seat of thought and wisdom.</note> for the influx of wisdom and faith, and consequently for the reception of God. The evil, however, block that influx through various cravings of the flesh and spiritual defilements which they place beneath them and which hinder the passage. Yet God still resides in their highest parts with all His Divine essence, giving them the faculty of willing good and understanding truth—a faculty which belongs to every person and which they would not have at all unless life from God were present in their soul. That this faculty exists even in the evil has been granted to be known through much experience.

That everyone receives life from God according to their own form can be illustrated by comparisons with plants of every kind. Every tree, every shrub, every twig, and every blade of grass receives the influx of heat and light according to its own form; this applies not only to those which are of good use, but also to those which are of evil use. The Sun with its heat does not change their forms, but the forms within themselves change the Sun's effects. It is similar with the subjects of the Mineral Kingdom; every one of them, whether excellent or worthless, receives the influx according to the form of the arrangement of its parts. Thus one stone differs from another, one mineral from another, and one metal from another. Some of them variegate themselves with the most beautiful colors, some transmit light without variation, and some muddle and suffocate the light within themselves.

From these few examples it can be established that just as the Sun of the World, with its heat and light, is equally present in one object as in another, but the receiving forms vary its operations; so likewise does the Lord—from the Sun of Heaven in the midst of which He resides—with His heat (which in its essence is love) and with His light (which in its essence is wisdom). However, the form of the person, which is brought about by the states of their life, varies these operations; consequently, the fault does not lie with the Lord that a person is not reborn and saved, but with the person himself.

## 367. IV. BUT THE PERSON WHO DIVIDES THE LORD, CHARITY, AND FAITH, IS NOT A RECEIVING FORM, BUT A DESTROYING FORM.

For whoever separates the Lord from Charity and Faith separates life from them; and when life is separated, Charity and Faith either do not exist at all, or they are "abortions" <note>In this context, *abortus* refers to something failed or stillborn—a spiritual effort that comes to nothing.</note>. That the Lord is Life itself may be seen above, in number 358. He who acknowledges the Lord but separates charity acknowledges Him only with the lips; his acknowledgment and confession are merely cold, containing no faith, for they lack spiritual essence—since charity is the essence of faith. 

On the other hand, he who practices Charity but does not acknowledge the Lord as the God of Heaven and Earth, one with the Father as He Himself teaches, performs no other charity than that which is merely natural, in which there is no eternal life. The member of the Church knows that all good which is good in itself is from God, and consequently from the Lord, who is the true God and eternal life (1 John 5:21); the same is true of Charity, because good and Charity are one. 

The reason why Faith separated from Charity is not faith is because Faith is the Light of a person’s life, and Charity is the Heat of his life. Therefore, if Charity is separated from faith, it is as when Heat is separated from Light; from this arises a state of the person like the state of the World during winter <note>original: "tempore brumæ"</note>, when everything on Earth dies away. Charity and Faith can no more be separated—if Charity is to be charity and Faith is to be faith—than the Will and the Understanding can be separated. If these are separated, the Understanding becomes nothing, and soon the Will does as well. It is the same with Charity and Faith, because...

It further argues that Faith and Charity are inseparable components of spiritual life, much like heat and light.</summary>
