**Charity** resides in the **Will**, and **Faith** in the **Understanding**. To separate Charity from Faith is like separating essence from form; it is well known in the learned world that essence without form, and form without essence, is nothing. Indeed, Essence has no specific quality except from its Form, nor is Form a self-subsisting entity except from its Essence. Consequently, nothing can be predicated of either if they are separated from each other. Furthermore, Charity is the essence of faith, and faith is the form of Charity—exactly as was stated above, that **Good** is the essence of **Truth**, and Truth is the form of Good.

These two—namely, Good and Truth—are in each and every thing that essentially exists. Therefore, because charity belongs to good and faith belongs to truth, they can be illustrated through comparisons with many things in the human Body and many things upon the Earth. The comparison coincides with the **breathing of the lungs** and the **systolic motion of the heart**; for charity can no more be separated from faith than the heart can be separated from the lungs. If the heartbeat stops, the breathing of the lungs immediately ceases; and if the breathing of the lungs ceases, a <term>fainting</term> <note>original: "deliquium"</note> of all the senses occurs, as well as a loss of movement in all the muscles, and shortly after the heart also stops, and all of life is dissipated. This comparison holds true because the Heart corresponds to the Will (and thus to Charity), and the breathing of the Lungs corresponds to the Understanding (and thus to Faith); for, as was said before, Charity resides in the Will and Faith in the Understanding. Nor is anything else meant in the **Word** <note>In this context, "the Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note> by "Heart" and "Spirit."

The separation of Charity and Faith also coincides with the separation of blood and flesh; for blood separated from the flesh is merely gore and becomes discharge, and flesh separated from the blood gradually rots and breeds worms. In the spiritual sense, "blood" signifies the Truth of wisdom and faith, and "flesh" signifies the good of love and charity. That blood has this significance was shown in *APOCALYPSE REVEALED*, no. 379, and that flesh signifies the same in no. 832. 

Charity and Faith, in order for one or the other to be anything at all, can no more be separated than can **Food** and **Water**, or **Bread** and **Wine**, in a person. Food and Bread taken without water and wine merely distend the stomach and, like undigested masses, ruin it and become like rotting filth; Water and Wine without food and bread also distend the stomach, as well as the vessels and pores, which, being deprived of nutrition, emaciate the body even unto death. This comparison also fits because food and bread in the spiritual sense signify the good of love and charity, and water and wine signify the truth of wisdom and faith (see *APOCALYPSE REVEALED*, nos. 50, 316, 778, 932).

Charity joined to faith, and Faith in turn joined to charity, can be compared to the face of a beautiful young woman, lovely because of the blending of rosy and white tones. This likeness also coincides because **Love** (and thus Charity) glows red from the fire of the Sun in the spiritual world, and **Truth** (and thus Faith) shines white from the light of that same Sun. Therefore, Charity separated from faith can be compared to a face inflamed with pustules, and Faith separated from charity can be compared to the pale face of a corpse.

Faith separated from charity can also be compared to a paralysis of one side, which is called **Hemiplegia**, from which a person dies as it grows stronger. It can also be compared to <term>St. Vitus’ Dance</term> <note>A neurological disorder characterized by rapid, uncoordinated jerking movements; Swedenborg also refers to it as "St. Guy's Dance."</note> or the dance of St. Guy, which happens to a person from the bite of a tarantula. The rational mind becomes like this; it "dances" with madness just as that person does, and believes itself to be alive at the time, yet it can no more gather its reasons into a unity and think about spiritual truths than a person lying in bed oppressed by a **nightmare** <note>original: "incubo," referring to the heavy, suffocating sensation of a night terror.</note>.

These points suffice to demonstrate the two themes of this Chapter. The first: *That Faith without charity is not Faith, and Charity without faith is not Charity, and neither has life unless it is from the Lord.* And the second: *That the Lord, Charity, and Faith make a one, just as Life, Will, and Understanding in a person make a one; and if they are divided, each perishes like a union crumbled into dust.*

# VII.

## *That the Lord is charity and faith in man, and that man is charity and faith in the Lord.*

368. That the person of the Church is in the Lord, and the Lord in them, is evident from these passages in the Word <note>Swedenborg uses "the Word" to refer to the Sacred Scriptures.</note>: *Jesus* said, ABIDE IN ME, AND I IN YOU: I am the *Vine* and you are the *branches*, HE WHO ABIDES IN ME, AND I IN HIM, this person bears much fruit, John 15:4, 5. *He who eats my Flesh and drinks my Blood, ABIDES IN ME AND I IN HIM*, John 6:56. *In that day you will know, that I am in my Father, and you in ME, AND I IN HIM*, John 14:20. *Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God abides in him, and he in God*, 1 John 4:15. But the human being cannot be in the Lord by their own power; rather, it is the Charity and Faith which are from the Lord within the person that are in Him. It is from these two that a human being is essentially a human being. However, so that this Secret <note>original: "Arcanum." Swedenborg often uses this term for deep spiritual truths that are being revealed for the first time.</note> may appear in some light before the understanding, it must be examined in this sequence: I: That there is a conjunction with God, through which salvation and eternal life come to man. II: That conjunction is not possible with God the Father, but with the Lord, and through Him with God the Father. III: That Conjunction with the Lord is reciprocal, which means the Lord is in the human being, and the human being is in the Lord. IV: That this reciprocal conjunction is effected through charity and faith. That these things are so will be made clear by the following explanation.

369. I: THAT THERE IS A CONJUNCTION WITH GOD, THROUGH WHICH SALVATION AND ETERNAL LIFE COME TO MAN. Man was created so that he could be joined to God; for he was created a <term>Native of Heaven</term> <note>original: "Indigena Cæli"</note>, and also a <term>Native of the World</term> <note>original: "Indigena Mundi"</note>. Insofar as he is a native of Heaven, he is spiritual; but insofar as he is a native of the World, he is natural. The spiritual man is able to think about God and perceive those things which belong to God; he is also able to love God and be affected by those things which come from God. From this it follows that he can be joined to God. That a person can think about God and perceive things belonging to God is beyond any doubt, for one can think about the Unity of God, about the Being of God which is <term>Jehovah</term> <note>The personal name of God in the Hebrew Bible, representing His self-existent essence.</note>, about the Immensity and Eternity of God, about the Divine Love and Divine Wisdom (which make up the Essence of God), and about the Omnipotence, Omniscience, and Omnipresence of God. One can think about the Lord the Savior His Son, and about Redemption and Mediation; and also about the Holy Spirit, and finally about the Divine Trinity—all of which belong to God, or rather, are God. Furthermore, one can think about the Operations of God, which are principally Faith and Charity, besides many other things that proceed from those two. That a person can not only think about God but also love God is evident from the two Commandments of God Himself, which sound thus: *You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul; this is the First and Great Commandment: the second is like it, you shall love your neighbor as yourself*, Matthew 22:35, 36, 37; Deuteronomy 6:5. That a person can carry out the precepts of God, and that this is what it means to love God and be loved by God, is evident from these words: *Jesus* said, *he who has my commandments and does them, he it is who loves Me; and he who loves Me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him, and will manifest Myself to him*, John 14:21. Moreover, what is Faith other than conjunction with God through truths, which belong to the understanding and the resulting thought? And what is Love other than conjunction with God through goods, which belong to the will and the resulting affection? God's conjunction with man is a spiritual conjunction within the natural; and man's conjunction with God is a natural conjunction from the spiritual. For the sake of this Conjunction as the final goal, Man was created a Native of Heaven and at the same time of the World...

<margin>original: "Indigena Cœli"</margin> ...world, just as the inhabitant of Heaven is spiritual, and the inhabitant of the World is natural. Therefore, if a human being becomes spiritually rational and at the same time spiritually moral, they are joined to God, and through that conjunction, they have salvation and eternal life. But if a person is merely naturally rational and naturally moral, there is indeed a conjunction of God with them, but not a conjunction of them with God. From this, they have spiritual death, which, seen in itself, is natural life without the spiritual; for the spiritual, in which the life of God resides, is extinguished within them.

## 370. II: THAT CONJUNCTION IS NOT POSSIBLE WITH GOD THE FATHER, BUT WITH THE LORD, AND THROUGH HIM WITH GOD THE FATHER; 

This Scripture teaches, and Reason sees. Scripture teaches that God the Father has never been seen or heard, nor can He be seen or heard; therefore, He cannot work anything from Himself—as He is in His own Being and Essence—within a human being. For the Lord says: *No one has seen the Father, except He who is with the Father; He has seen the Father* (John 6:46). *No one knows the Father except the Son, and anyone to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him* (Matthew 11:27). *You have never heard the Father’s voice, nor seen His form* (John 5:37). The reason for this is that He is in the very firsts and beginnings of all things, so most eminently above every sphere of the human mind; for He is in the firsts and beginnings of all wisdom and all love, with which no conjunction is possible for a human being. Therefore, if He Himself were to approach a human, or a human were to approach Him, the human would be consumed and melt away, like wood in the focus of a large burning glass <note>original: "speculi caustici" — a magnifying or parabolic mirror used to concentrate sunlight and start fires</note>, or rather like an image thrown into the Sun itself. For this reason it was said to Moses, who desired to see God, *That a man cannot see Him and live* (Exodus 33:20). 

However, that God the Father is joined through the Lord is established from what was just brought forward: that not the Father, but the Only-Begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father and has seen the Father, has set forth and revealed those things which are of God and from God. And furthermore from these: *In 그날 그날 you will know that I am in my Father, and you in Me, and I in you* (John 14:20). *The glory which You gave Me, I have given them, that they may be one even as we are one; I in them, and You in Me* (John 17:22, 23, 26). *Jesus said, I am the Way, the Truth, and the Life; no one comes to the Father except through Me.* And then Philip wanted to see the Father, to whom the Lord replied, *He who sees Me, also sees the Father, and he who knows Me also knows the Father* (John 14:6, 7 etc.). And elsewhere, *He who sees Me, sees Him who sent Me* (John 12:45). And furthermore, He says *that He is the Door, and that he who enters through Him shall be saved, and he who climbs up some other way is a thief and a robber* (John 10:1, 9). He also says that he who does not remain in Me is cast out, and like a dried-up branch, shall be thrown into the fire (John 15:6). 

The reason is that our Lord the Savior is Himself Jehovah the Father in Human Form. For Jehovah descended and became Man so that He could approach the human being and the human being could approach Him, and thus a conjunction could be made, and through that conjunction, salvation and eternal life for the human being. For when God became Man, and thus also Man became God, then, accommodated to the human being, He could approach and be joined to them as God-Man and Man-God. There are three things that follow in order: **ACCOMMODATION, APPLICATION, AND CONJUNCTION**. There must be accommodation before application can happen, and accommodation and application together before conjunction can happen. Accommodation on God's part was that He became Man; Application on God's part is perpetual, so far as the human being applies themselves in return; and as this happens, Conjunction also happens. These three follow and proceed in their own order in each and every thing that becomes one and exists together.

## 371: III: THAT CONJUNCTION WITH THE LORD IS RECIPROCAL, WHICH IS THAT THE LORD IS IN THE HUMAN BEING AND THE HUMAN BEING IS IN THE LORD.

Scripture teaches that the conjunction is reciprocal, and Reason also sees it. The Lord teaches concerning His conjunction with His Father that it is reciprocal, for He says to Philip: *Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in Me? Believe me, that I am in the Father and the Father is in Me* (John 14:10, 11). *That you may know and believe that the Father is in Me and I [in Him]* <note>The text ends mid-sentence as a catchword for the next page.</note>

This allows for a reciprocal relationship where God and humanity can be spiritually joined.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the necessity of a spiritual "conjunction" or joining between God and humanity. Having previously established that this must occur through the Lord (Jesus Christ) as the visible human form of God, Swedenborg now explains the mechanics of this relationship, defining it as a "reciprocal" or two-way process that requires human cooperation.</meta>

<page-num>240</page-num>
->### UNIVERSAL THEOLOGY<-

...in the Father, John 10:38. *Jesus* said: *Father, the hour has come; glorify your Son, so that your Son also may glorify You*, John 16:1 <note>original: "Joh: XVI: 1"; this quote actually appears in John 17:1</note>. *Father, all things that are Mine are Yours, and all things that are Yours are Mine*, John 17:10. The Lord says something similar regarding His connection with man—namely, that it is reciprocal. For He says: *Abide in Me and I in you; he who abides in Me and I in him, he bears much fruit*, John 15:4, 5. *He who eats my Flesh and drinks my Blood remains in Me and I in him*, John 6:56. *In that day you will know that I am in my Father, and you in Me and I in you*, John 14:20. *He who does the commands of Christ remains in Him and He in him*, 1 John 3:24; Chapter 4:13. *Whoever confesses that Christ is the Son of God, God remains in him and he in God*, 1 John 4:15. *He who hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in to him, and will dine with him, and he with Me*, Revelation 3:20. 

From these clear statements, it is evident that the joining of the Lord and man is reciprocal. Because it is reciprocal, it follows absolutely that man must join himself to the Lord so that the Lord may join Himself to man. Otherwise, no joining occurs, but rather a withdrawal and a resulting separation—not on the Lord’s part, but on the part of the man. To make this reciprocal joining possible, man has been given **Free Choice**, by which he can enter the path to Heaven or the path to Hell. From this gift of Freedom flows man's "reciprocal" power: that he is able to join himself to the Lord, or join himself to the devil. However, the nature of that Liberty, and the reason it was given to man, will be explained in the following sections concerning <term>Free Will</term>, <term>Repentance</term>, <term>Reformation</term> and <term>Regeneration</term>, and <term>Imputation</term> <note>Imputation: the theological concept of how God "credits" righteousness or sin to a person.</note>.

It is a matter of regret that the reciprocal joining of the Lord and man, even though it stands so clearly in the Word, remains unknown in the Christian Church. It is unknown because of certain assumptions regarding Faith and Free Will. The assumptions regarding Faith are: that Faith is given without a person contributing anything to grasp it, and that a person does not adapt or apply themselves to receive it any more than a <gloss>lifeless log</gloss> would. The assumptions regarding Free Will are: that man does not possess even a grain of free will in spiritual matters. But so that the reciprocal joining of the Lord and man—on which the salvation of the human race depends—is no longer hidden in obscurity, necessity demands it be revealed. This is best done through examples, as these provide clarity. 

There are two types of Reciprocity by which a joining occurs: one is **ALTERNATING**, and the other is **MUTUAL**. 

**ALTERNATING** reciprocity can be illustrated by the breathing of the lungs. A person inhales air, and by doing so expands the chest; soon they release the inhaled air, and by doing so compress the chest. That inhalation and the resulting expansion happen by the pressure of the air acting on it; but the release and resulting compression happen by means of the ribs through the force of the muscles. Such is the reciprocal joining of the air and the lungs, upon which the life of the senses and the movements of the whole body depend; for if breathing stops, both of those fail. 

Reciprocal joining through alternating action can also be illustrated by the connection of the heart with the lungs and the lungs with the heart. The heart pours blood from its right chamber into the lungs, and the lungs pour it back into the left chamber of the heart. Thus, this reciprocal joining occurs, upon which the life of the entire body absolutely depends. A similar joining exists between the blood and the heart: the blood of the entire body flows through the veins into the heart, and flows out from the heart through the arteries into the whole body. Action and reaction create this joining. A similar action and reaction, through which connection persists, exists between an embryo and the mother’s womb. 

But the reciprocal joining of the Lord and man is not like these; rather, it is a **MUTUAL** joining, which does not occur through simple "action and reaction," but through **cooperation**. For the Lord acts, and man receives the action from the Lord, and operates <gloss>as if by himself</gloss>—indeed, from himself, yet from the Lord. This operation of man from the Lord is credited to him as his own, because he is constantly held in Free Will by the Lord. The Free Will resulting from this is that he can will and think from the Lord (that is, from the Word), and also that he can will and think from the devil (that is, against the Lord).

This reciprocal Conjunction, which is mutual, can also be illustrated by various things in man and in the World: such a conjunction exists between the soul and the body in every man; such a conjunction exists between the will and action, and such between thought and speech; and such is the conjunction of the two eyes with each other, the two ears with each other, and the two nostrils with each other. That the conjunction of the two eyes with each other is in its own way reciprocal is evident from the optic Nerve, in which fibers from both hemispheres of the Brain are entwined with each other, and thus entwined they extend to each eye; it is similar with the ears and nostrils. There is a similar reciprocal and mutual conjunction between Light and the Eye, Sound and the Ear, Odor and the Nostril, Taste and the Tongue, and Touch and the Body; for the eye is in the light and the light is in the eye, sound is in the ear and the ear is in the sound, odor is in the nostril and the nostril is in the odor, taste is in the tongue and the tongue is in the taste, and touch is in the body and the body is in the touch. This reciprocal conjunction can also be compared with the conjunction of a Horse and a Carriage, an Ox and a Plow, a Wheel and a Machine, a Sail and the Wind, a Flute and the Air; in short, such a reciprocal conjunction exists between the End and the Cause, and such between the Cause and the Effect; but there is no time to explain these individually, as it would be a work of many pages <note>original: *membranarum*, literally "membranes" or "parchments"</note>.

372. IV: **THAT THIS RECIPROCAL CONJUNCTION OF THE LORD AND MAN IS THROUGH CHARITY AND FAITH.** It is known today that the Church makes up the Body of Christ, and that everyone in whom the Church exists is in some Member of that Body, according to Paul in Ephesians 1:23, 1 Corinthians 12:27, and Romans 12:4, 5. But what is the Body of Christ but Divine Good and Divine Truth? This is understood by the Lord’s words in John: *He who eats my Flesh and drinks my Blood remains in Me and I in him*, Chapter 6:56. By the Lord’s Flesh, as well as by the Bread, is understood Divine Good; and by His Blood, as well as by the Wine, is understood Divine Truth; that these are so understood will be seen in the Chapter on **THE HOLY SUPPER**. From this it follows that as much as a man is in the Goods of charity and the Truths of faith, so much is he in the Lord and the Lord in him; for conjunction with the Lord is a spiritual Conjunction, and spiritual conjunction is uniquely achieved through Charity and Faith. That the Conjunction of the Lord and the Church—and therefore of Good and Truth—exists in each and every part of the Word, was shown in the Chapter on **THE SACRED SCRIPTURE**, numbers 248 to 253; and because Charity is Good and Faith is Truth, the Conjunction of charity and faith is everywhere in the Word. From these things it now follows, **THAT THE LORD IS CHARITY AND FAITH IN MAN, AND THAT MAN IS CHARITY AND FAITH IN THE LORD**; for the Lord is spiritual Charity and Faith within the natural Charity and Faith of man, and Man is natural Charity and faith derived from the spiritual [Charity and Faith] of the Lord, which when joined together make a spiritual-natural Charity and Faith.

# VIII.

## *That Charity and Faith are together in Good Works.*

373. In every Work that proceeds from a man, the whole man is present just as he is in his mind, or as he is essentially; by the mind is understood the affection of his love and the thought derived from it; these form his nature, and in general, his Life. If we look at works in this way, they are like mirrors of the man. This can be illustrated by a comparison with beasts and wild animals: a beast is a beast, and a wild animal is a wild animal in every one of its acts; a wolf is a wolf in everything it does, a tiger is a tiger in everything it does, a fox is a fox...

The Lord says: *A good man out of the good treasure of his heart brings forth good, and an evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart brings forth evil. Luke 6:45.* <note>original Latin: "Bonus homo ex bono thesauro cordis sui profert bonum..."</note> and also: *Every tree is known by its own fruit; for they do not gather figs from thorns, nor do they gather grapes from a bramble bush. Luke 6:44.* <note>original Latin: "Omnis Arbor ex proprio fructu cognoscitur..."</note> That a person is such in each and every thing that proceeds from them as they are in their Internal Man manifests itself vividly after death, since a person then lives as the Internal Man and no longer as the External. That good exists in a person, and that every work proceeding from them is good when the Lord, <term>Charity</term> <note>In this context, Charity refers to spiritual love for others and goodwill, rather than just donating money.</note> and Faith reside in their Internal Man, will be demonstrated in this series:

I. That Charity is willing well, and that good Works are doing well from that willing well.
II. That Charity and Faith are merely mental and fleeting things unless, when possible, they are determined into Works and coexist within them.
III. That Charity alone does not produce good works, and still less Faith alone, but that Charity and Faith act together. 

But let us speak of these individually.

### 374. I: THAT CHARITY IS WILLING WELL, AND THAT GOOD WORKS ARE DOING WELL FROM WILLING WELL.

Charity and Works are as distinct from one another as Will and Action, or as the affection of the Mind is from the operation of the Body. Consequently, they are also like the **Internal** and **External Man**, and these are related to each other as **Cause** and **Effect**. This is because the causes of all things are formed in the Internal Man, and all effects are produced from there in the External; therefore, Charity (because it belongs to the Internal Man) is "willing well," and Works (because they belong to the External Man) are "doing well" from that willing well. 

However, there is an infinite diversity between the "willing well" of one person and another. Everything is believed or appears to flow from "willing well" or benevolence if it is done by someone for the favor of another; yet it is not known whether the good deeds are from charity, much less from what kind of charity—whether genuine or spurious. That infinite diversity between the goodwill of one and another takes its origin from the **End**, the **Intention**, and the resulting **Purpose**. These lie hidden within the Will of acting well, and the quality of every person's will is derived from them. The will seeks the means and ways of reaching its goals (which are the effects) in the **Intellect**; there, it puts itself into the light so that it may not only see the reasons, but also the opportunities of when and how it will determine itself into acts, and thus produce its effects, which are works. At the same time, in the Intellect, the will puts itself into the power of acting. From this it follows that Works are essentially of the Will, formally of the Intellect, and actually of the Body; in this way, Charity descends into good Works. 

These things can be illustrated by a comparison with a tree. A Human Being, in regard to all his parts, is like a Tree. In the seed of the tree, there lies hidden as it were the end, intention, and purpose of producing fruit; in these, the Seed corresponds to the **Will** in a person, in which those three things exist, as was said. Next, the Seed sprouts from the earth through its internal parts and clothes itself with branches, boughs, and leaves, and thus prepares for itself the means to its ends, which are the fruits; in these, the Tree corresponds to the **Intellect** in a person. Finally, when the time is right and the opportunity for determination is given, it blossoms and produces fruit; in these, the Tree corresponds to **good Works** in a person. It is clear that the fruits are essentially of the seed, formally of the boughs and leaves, and actually of the wood of the tree. 

This can also be illustrated by a comparison with a **Temple**. A person is a Temple of God, according to Paul: *1 Corinthians 3:16, 17; 2 Corinthians 6:16; Ephesians 2:21, 22.* The end, intention, and purpose of a person, as a Temple of God, are salvation and eternal life; in these, there is a correspondence with the will, in which those three things reside. Afterward, the person draws the doctrines of faith and charity from parents, teachers, and preachers, and when they become capable of their own judgment, from the Word and from dogmatic books—all of which are means to the end. In these, there is a correspondence with the Intellect. Finally,

### 375. II: THAT CHARITY AND FAITH ARE MERELY MENTAL AND FLEETING THINGS UNLESS, WHENEVER POSSIBLE, THEY ARE DETERMINED INTO WORKS AND COEXIST IN THEM.

Does a human not have a Head and a Body, and a connection between them via the Neck? Is there not in the Head a Mind that wills and thinks, and in the Body a power that acts and executes? If, therefore, a person only willed well or thought from <term>Charity</term> <note>Charity here means spiritual love and goodwill toward others.</note>, but did not do good and perform uses because of it, would that person not be like just a Head, and thus like just a Mind? A mind alone cannot subsist without a body. Who cannot see from this that Charity and Faith are not truly charity and faith while they exist only in the head and its mind and not in the body? For they are then like birds flying in the air without any perch on the ground; or like birds pregnant with eggs but having no nests, so that the eggs would fall into the air or onto the twig of some tree, only to fall to the earth and be destroyed. There is nothing in the Mind to which something in the body does not correspond; and that which corresponds can be called its "embodiment." Therefore, while Charity and Faith are only in the mind, they are not incorporated into the person. They may then be likened to an aerial human, which is called a <term>Phantom</term> <note>original Latin: "Larva," referring to a ghost or disembodied spirit.</note>, such as the figure of **Fame** was depicted by the ancients with laurel around her head and a cornucopia in her hand. Because such phantoms can still think, they cannot help but be agitated by fantasies and by reasonings based on various sophistries. They are much like marsh reeds shaken by the Wind, beneath which shells lie at the bottom and frogs croak on the surface. Who cannot see that such things happen when people merely know something from the **Word** <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scripture or the Bible.</note> regarding Charity and Faith, but do not do them? The Lord also says: *EVERYONE WHO HEARS MY WORDS AND DOES THEM, I will compare to a wise man who built his house upon a rock; but EVERYONE HEARING MY WORDS AND NOT DOING THEM will be compared to a foolish man who built his house upon the sand, or upon the ground without a foundation.* <note>original Latin: "Omnis qui audit verba mea, et facit illa... at omnis audiens verba mea et non faciens illa..."</note> Matthew 7:24, 26; Luke 6:47, 48, 49. Charity and Faith, with their fabricated ideas, when a person does not put them into practice, can also be compared to butterflies in the air, which a sparrow flies toward and swallows up as soon as they are seen. The Lord also says: *A sower went out to sow, and some seeds fell upon the hard path, and the Birds came and ate them.* <note>original Latin: "Exivit seminans ad seminandum..."</note> Matthew 13:3, 4.

## 377. III. THAT CHARITY ALONE DOES NOT PRODUCE GOOD WORKS, STILL LESS FAITH ALONE, BUT THAT CHARITY AND FAITH ACT TOGETHER.

The reason is that Charity without faith is not truly charity, nor is Faith without charity truly faith (as shown above in nos. 355 to 358); therefore, solitary Charity does not exist, nor does solitary Faith. Hence, it cannot be said that Charity by itself produces any good works, nor that Faith does so by itself. This is exactly like the <term>Will</term> and the <term>Understanding</term>: a solitary Will does not exist, and therefore produces nothing; nor does a solitary Understanding exist or produce anything. Rather, all production comes from both together, and it comes from the Understanding acting from the Will. The reason this is a valid comparison is that the Will is the dwelling-place of charity, and the Understanding is the dwelling-place of faith. It is said "still less Faith alone" because Faith is Truth, and its operation is to produce Truths; these in turn illuminate charity and its exercises. That they illuminate them is taught by the Lord, when He says: *HE WHO DOES THE TRUTH COMES TO THE LIGHT, so that his works may be made manifest, because they are done in God,* John 3:21. Therefore, when a person does good works according to truths, he does them in the light—that is, intelligently and wisely.

The conjunction of Charity and Faith is like the marriage of a husband and wife. From the husband as father and the wife as mother, all natural offspring are born; similarly, from Charity as the father and Faith as the mother, all spiritual offspring are born, which are the knowledges of good and truth. By these, the lineage of spiritual families is recognized. Indeed, in the Word, in its spiritual sense, the "Husband" and "Father" signify the Good of Charity, and the "Wife" and "Mother" signify the Truth of faith. From this it is also clear that neither Charity alone nor Faith alone can produce good works, just as a husband alone or a wife alone cannot produce any offspring.

The truths of faith do not only illuminate charity, but they also <term>qualify</term> it <note>To "qualify" here means to give it a specific form or character, defining how the impulse of love should act in a specific situation.</note>; moreover, they nourish it. Therefore, a person who has charity but lacks the truths of faith is like someone walking in a garden at night; he picks fruit from the trees, but he does not know if they are good for use or poisonous. Since the truths of faith not only illuminate charity but also qualify it (as was said), it follows that charity without the truths of faith is like fruit without juice, like a dried-up fig, or like a grape after the wine has been squeezed out of it. Since truths nourish faith (as was also said), it follows that if charity is without the truths of faith, it has no more nourishment than a person would get from eating burnt bread and drinking filthy water from a stagnant pond.

# IX.

## On True Faith, Spurious Faith, and Hypocritical Faith.

378. From its very cradle, the Christian Church began to be infested and divided by schisms and heresies. In the course of time, it was torn and mangled, much like the account of the man who went down from Jerusalem to Jericho and was surrounded by thieves; after they stripped him and inflicted wounds upon him, they left him half-dead, *Luke 10:30.* Hence it has become as we read concerning that Church in Daniel: *At last, upon the wing of abominations shall be desolation, even until the consummation and the decision, it shall drop upon the devastation, Chapter 9:27.* <note>original: "Tandem super avem abominationum desolatio..." This refers to the "abomination of desolation," a prophetic term for the total spiritual decay of the church.</note> And according to these words from the Lord: *Then the end will come, when you see the abomination of desolation predicted by Daniel the Prophet, Matthew 24:14, 15.* The fate of the Church may be compared to a ship loaded with merchandise of the highest value, which, as soon as it left the harbor, was tossed by storms and a little later sank as a shipwreck in the sea; then its cargo was partly spoiled by the waters and partly devoured by fish. 

That the Christian Church has been so vexed and torn from its infancy is clear from Church History. Even in the time of the Apostles, it was troubled by SIMON, a Samaritan by nation and a Magician by profession, mentioned in the *Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 8:9 and following;* and also by HYMENAEUS and PHILETUS, who are mentioned by Paul in his *Epistle to Timothy;* as well as by NICHOLAS, from whom the Nicolaitans were named (mentioned in *Revelation 2:6* and *Acts 6:5*), besides CERINTHUS. <note>original: "Corintho", referring to Cerinthus, an early Gnostic heretic who opposed the Apostle John.</note> After the times of the Apostles, many others arose, such as the MARCIONITES, NOETIANS, VALENTINIANS, ENCRATITES, CATAPHRYGES, QUARTODECIMANS, ALOGIANS, CATHARI, ORIGENISTS or ADAMANTINES, SABELLIANS, SAMOSATENES, MANICHAEANS, MELETIANS, and finally the ARIANS. <note>These groups represent various early theological disputes regarding the nature of Christ, the timing of Easter (Quartodecimans), and the strictness of church discipline (Cathari).</note> After their time, phalanxes of <term>Heresiarchs</term> <note>Leaders of heretical sects.</note> invaded the Church, such as the DONATISTS, PHOTINIANS, ACATIANS or SEMI-ARIANS, EUNOMIANS, MACEDONIANS, NESTORIANS, PREDESTINARIANS, PAPISTS, ZWINGLIANS, ANABAPTISTS, SCHWENCKFELDIANS, SYNERGISTS, SOCINIANS, ANTI-TRINITARIANS, QUAKERS, MORAVIANS, <note>original: "Heerenhuteri", referring to the Herrnhuters or Moravian Brethren.</note> besides many others; and finally, LUTHER, MELANCHTHON, and CALVIN prevailed over these, whose doctrines reign today. 

There are principally three causes for so many divisions and seditions in the Church: FIRST, that the Divine Trinity was not understood; SECOND, that there was no just knowledge of the Lord; THIRD, that the Passion of the cross was taken for <term>Redemption</term> <note>The author argues that the physical suffering on the cross was not the totality of redemption, but rather the last temptation in the process of glorifying Christ's humanity.</note> itself. While these three things are unknown—which are the very essentials of Faith, from which the Church exists and is called a Church—it cannot be otherwise than that all things of the Church would be pulled in a wrong and different direction, and finally into the opposite. When it reaches that point, people still believe they are in the true Faith in God, and in the Faith of all the Truths of God. Such people are like those who cover their eyes with a bandage and walk in their own imagination in a straight line, yet step after step they veer and finally turn in the opposite direction, where there is a cave into which they fall. But the person of the Church can only be led back from his wandering into the way of truth by knowing what True Faith is, what Spurious Faith is, and what Hypocritical Faith is. Therefore, it will be demonstrated: 

I. That True Faith is unique; it is in the Lord God the Savior Jesus Christ, and it exists among those who believe Him to be the Son of God, the God of Heaven and Earth, and one with the Father. 

II. That Spurious Faith is every faith that departs from the true one, which is unique; it exists among those who climb up some other way, and regard the Lord not as God, but only as a Man. 

III. That Hypocritical Faith is no faith at all.

379. I. THAT TRUE FAITH IS UNIQUE, AND THAT IT IS IN THE LORD GOD THE SAVIOR JESUS CHRIST, AND THAT IT EXISTS AMONG THOSE WHO BELIEVE HIM TO BE...

That true faith is unique is because faith is truth, and truth cannot be shattered and cut in two so that one part of it leans to the left and another part to the right and yet remains truth. Faith, in a general sense, consists of innumerable truths, for it is a complex of them; but these innumerable truths form, as it were, a single Body, and in that Body, the truths constitute its members. Some truths constitute the members that depend on the chest, such as the arms and hands; some depend on the loins, such as the feet and the soles of the feet. Interior truths, however, constitute the Head, and the truths that proceed directly from there constitute the sensory organs located in the face. The reason interior truths constitute the Head is that when "Interior" is mentioned, "Superior" is also understood; for in the spiritual world, all interior things are also superior, as is the case with the three Heavens there. <note>In the theology of this period, particularly in Swedenborgian thought, the spiritual world is organized by "degrees." What is "within" or "interior" is considered more perfect and "higher" or "superior" in rank.</note> The Soul and Life of this Body and all its members is the Lord God the Savior. From this, it follows that the Church was called by Paul the *Body of Christ,* and that the people of the Church, according to the states of charity and faith within them, constitute its members. That true faith is unique is also taught by Paul thus: *There is one Body and one Spirit, one Lord, ONE FAITH, one Baptism, one God; he gave the work of ministry for the building up of the BODY OF CHRIST, until we all come into the Unity of FAITH, and the knowledge of the Son of God, and a perfect life into the measure of the age of the fullness of Christ,* Ephesians 4:4, 5, 6, 12, 13. That true faith, which is unique, is directed toward the Lord God the Savior Jesus Christ, was fully shown above in numbers 337, 338, and 339.

The reason why true faith exists among those who believe the Lord to be the Son of God is that they also believe Him to be God, and faith is not faith unless it is in God. That this is the primary <term>fundamental principle</term><gloss>original: primarium</gloss> of all truths that enter into and form Faith is evident from the Lord's words to Peter when he said: *You are the CHRIST, THE SON OF THE LIVING GOD; blessed are you, Simon, I say to you, upon this Rock I will build my Church, and the gates of Hell shall not prevail against it,* Matthew 16:16, 17. By the "Rock" here, as elsewhere in the Word, is meant the Lord in respect to Divine Truth, and also Divine Truth from the Lord. <note>The "Rock" (Petra) is traditionally interpreted by some as Peter himself, but here the author interprets it as the "Divine Truth" that Peter had just confessed.</note> That this Truth is primary, and like a crown upon the head and a scepter in the hand of the Body of Christ, is clear from the Lord's words: that upon that Rock He would build His Church, and that the gates of Hell would not prevail against it. That faith is of such a character is also clear from these words in John: *Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God remains in him, and he in God,* 1 John 4:15.

Besides this <term>characteristic mark</term><gloss>original: characteristicon</gloss> of being in the true and unique faith, there is also a second: that they believe the Lord to be the God of Heaven and Earth. This follows from the first—that He is the Son of God—and from these verses: *That in Him is all the fullness of the Divinity,* Colossians 2:9; *That He is God of Heaven and Earth,* Matthew 28:18; and *That all things of the Father are His,* John 3:35, Chapter 16:15. 

A third indication that those who believe in the Lord are interiorly in faith in Him—and thus in the true and unique faith—is that they believe the Lord is one with God the Father. That He is one with God the Father, and that He is the Father Himself in the Human, was fully shown in the Chapter on the Lord and Redemption, and is clearly evident from the Lord's own words: *That the Father and He are one,* John 10:30; *That the Father is in Him and He in the Father,* John 10:38, Chapter 14:10, 11; *That He said to the Disciples that from now on they have seen and known the Father, and that He looked at Philip and said that he now sees and knows the Father,* John 14:7 and following. 

The reason these Three are characteristic testimonies of being in faith in the Lord—and thus in the true and unique faith—is that not all those who approach the Lord are in faith in Him; for true faith is internal and external at the same time. Those with whom these three precious elements of faith exist are in both the internals and externals of that faith. Thus, it is not only a treasure in their heart, but also a <term>prized heirloom</term><gloss>original: cimelium</gloss> in their mouth. It is otherwise with those who do not acknowledge Him as the God of Heaven and Earth, and as One with the Father; these look interiorly toward other Gods who possess similar power, but they believe this power is to be exercised by the Son either as a Deputy, or as one who, on account of Re-

...redemption, He merited the right to reign over those whom He redeemed; but these people shatter true faith by dividing the unity of God. They are like milestones or signposts along the roads that show the way to the Temple where the one true God is worshiped; and they are like lamps upon rocks at sea, by which sailors at night know where they are and in what direction to steer their ships. The first characteristic of faith, which is that the Lord is the Son of the living God, is like the Morning Star to all who enter His Church.

### 380. II. THAT SPURIOUS FAITH IS EVERY FAITH THAT DEPARTS FROM THE TRUE FAITH, WHICH IS THE ONLY ONE; AND THAT IT IS AMONG THOSE WHO CLIMB UP SOME OTHER WAY, AND LOOK TO THE LORD NOT AS GOD BUT ONLY AS A MAN.

That spurious faith is every faith which departs from the true faith (which is unique) is self-evident; for since truth is unique, it follows that whatever departs from it is not true. All the good and truth of the Church are propagated from the Marriage of the Lord and the Church; thus, everything that is essentially charity and essentially faith is from that marriage. But whatever of these two is not from that source is not from a legitimate bed, but an illegitimate one—either from a polygamous marriage or from adultery. From a polygamous marriage comes every faith that acknowledges the Lord but adopts the false ideas of heresies. Faith from adultery belongs to those who acknowledge three Lords of one Church; for such a person is like a harlot, or like a woman married to one man who grants her nights to two others, and while sleeping with them calls each one her husband. Hence it is that their faith is called spurious. The Lord calls such people "adulterers" in many places, and He also means them by the "thieves and robbers" in the Gospel of John, <margin>Chapter 10: 1, 9;</margin> *Truly, truly I say to you, he who does not enter by the Door into the Sheepfold, BUT CLIMBS UP SOME OTHER WAY, is a thief and a robber: I am the Door; if anyone enters through Me, he shall be saved.* To enter the "Sheepfold" is to enter the Church, and also to enter Heaven. It also means entering Heaven because the two make one, and nothing else makes Heaven except the Church there; therefore, just as the Lord is the Bridegroom and Husband of the Church, so He is also the Bridegroom and Husband of Heaven. 

It can be examined and known whether a Faith is a legitimate offspring or a spurious one by its three indicators (mentioned above): the acknowledgment of the Lord as the Son of God, the acknowledgment of Him as the God of Heaven and Earth, and the acknowledgment that He is one with the Father. To the extent, then, that any Faith departs from these its essentials, to that extent it is spurious. Spurious and at the same time adulterous faith is found among those who look at the Lord not as God, but only as a man. That this is so is clearly seen from those two abominable heresies, the ARIAN and SOCINIAN <note>Arianism and Socinianism are historical theological movements that deny the full divinity of Jesus Christ. Arians viewed Him as a created being, while Socinians viewed Him as a human prophet who was later divinized.</note>, which were cursed and excommunicated from the Christian Church because they deny the Divinity of the Lord and "climb up some other way." 

But I fear that these abominations lie hidden today in the general spirit of the people of the Church. It is a strange thing that the more someone believes themselves to be superior to others in learning and judgment, the more prone they are to seize upon and adopt ideas of the Lord as being a Man and not God—reasoning that because He is a Man He cannot be God. Whoever adopts these ideas for themselves enters into the company of the Arians and Socinians, who are in Hell in the spiritual world. The reason the general spirit of the people of the Church is like this today is that every man has a conscious spirit; for without it, a human could not think analytically, rationally, or spiritually, and thus would not be a man but a beast. Every man takes to himself a spirit similar to the affection of his own will and the perception of his understanding. He who leads himself into good affections through truths from the Word and by a life according to them, has an Angel from Heaven joined to him; but he who leads himself into evil affections by confirming falsehoods and by an evil life, to him...

...a spirit from Hell joins him; once joined, the man enters more and more into a kind of brotherhood with Satans, and then confirms himself more and more in falsehoods against the truths in the Word, and in the Arian and Socinian abominations <note>Arianism and Socinianism were theological movements that denied the full divinity of Jesus Christ, viewing him either as a created being or merely a divinely inspired man.</note> against the Lord. The reason is that all Satans cannot bear to hear any truth from the Word, nor can they endure the name of Jesus to be spoken; if they hear these things, they become like furies, running about and blaspheming. Then, if light from Heaven flows in, they cast themselves headlong into caverns and into their own thick darkness, in which they have light just as owls do in the dark, or as cats do in cellars while they hunt mice. Such do all become after death who deny the Divinity of the Lord and the holiness of the Word from their heart and faith. Their internal man is of such a quality, however much the external man acts the part of a mime <note>original: "Mimum," referring to a masked actor or hypocrite</note> and lies about being a Christian; I know that this is so, because I have seen and heard it. All who honor the Lord as Redeemer and Savior with the mouth and lips only, but in heart and spirit look upon Him as a mere man, when they speak and teach these things, their mouth is like a jar of honey, but their heart is like a jar of gall; their words are like sugar-coated breads, but their thoughts are like a sweet drink made of hemlock <note>original: "aconitis," referring to wolfsbane or monkshood, a deadly poison</note>; and they are like rolls of pastry in which vipers are hidden. If they are priests, they are like pirates at sea who hang out the flag of a kingdom of peace, but when a nearby ship approaches them as friends, they raise the pirate flag in place of the first one, and lead the ship and its people away into captivity. They are also like the serpents of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, who approach like angels of light, holding in their hands apples painted with golden colors as if taken from the Tree of Life, and they reach them out and say, *God knows that on the day you eat of them, your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God, knowing good and evil*, Genesis 3:5. And when they have eaten, they follow the Serpent into Hell <note>original: "Oreum/Orcum," terms for the underworld or hell</note> and dwell together. Around that Hell are Satans who have eaten from the apples of Arius and Socinus. Such people are also understood by the one who entered without being clothed in a wedding garment, and was cast into outer darkness, Matthew 22:11, 12, 13; the wedding garment is faith in the Lord as the Son of God, the God of Heaven and Earth, and one with the Father. Those who honor the Lord only with mouth and lips, but in heart and spirit look upon Him as a mere man, if they open their thoughts and persuade others, are spiritual murderers, and the worst of them are spiritual cannibals <term>spiritual anthropophagi: "man-eaters"; those who destroy the spiritual life of others by taking away the truths that sustain the soul</term>. For a person’s life comes from love and faith in the Lord, but if this essential of faith and love—that the Lord is God-Man and Man-God—is removed, his life becomes death; thus the person is killed and devoured like a lamb by a wolf.

## 381. III. THAT HYPOCRITICAL FAITH IS NO FAITH.

A person becomes a hypocrite when he thinks much of himself and prefers himself above others; for in this way he directs and pours the thoughts and affections of his mind into his body, and joins them with its senses. From this he becomes a natural, sensual, and corporeal man, and then his mind cannot be drawn away from the flesh with which it sticks fast, nor be elevated to God and see anything of God in the light of Heaven—that is, anything spiritual. And because he is a fleshly man, the spiritual things that enter (which happens through hearing into the understanding) appear to him as nothing else than phantoms <note>original: "larvae"</note> and like dust motes in the air—indeed, like flies around the head of a running and sweating horse. Therefore, in his heart he mocks them; for it is well known that the natural man regards the things of the Spirit, or spiritual things, as delusions. A hypocrite among natural men is the lowest kind of natural man, for he is sensual; his mind is tightly bound with the senses of his body, and therefore he loves to see nothing other than what his senses suggest. Because the senses are in nature, they force the mind to think about everything from nature, and thus also about all things of faith. If such a hypocrite becomes a preacher <note>original: "Concionator"</note>, he retains in his memory such things as were said about faith in his childhood and youth; but because there is nothing spiritual within them, but they are merely natural, when he brings them forth before a congregation, they are nothing but inanimate voices. That they sound as if they were animated is due to the delights of his love for himself and the world, from which they blare out according to his eloquence, and they soothe the ears much like the harmonies of a song. When a hypocrite preacher returns home after a sermon, to all the things concerning faith and from the Word which he...

A hypocrite is like a carved statue with a double head, one within the other; the internal head is connected to the trunk or body, while the external head—which can be moved—surrounds the internal one. The front of this external head is painted in lifelike colors like a human face, not unlike the wooden heads displayed at the shops of craftsmen who make wigs. He is like a small boat that a sailor, by adjusting the sail, can steer with or against the wind at his pleasure; his "sailing" is to favor everyone who indulges in the delights of the flesh and the senses. Ministers who are hypocrites are perfect comedians, mimes, and stage actors, who can play the parts of Kings, Dukes, Primates, and Bishops; yet as soon as they take off their theatrical costumes, they enter brothels and live with harlots. For what is truly remarkable is that during the time they are performing holy duties and teaching truths from the Word, they do not know but that they actually believe them, for at those times the door toward hell is closed. But as soon as they return home, they do not believe a bit of it, for then the door toward heaven is closed. Among the most extreme hypocrites, there is an internal enmity against truly spiritual men, of the same kind that exists between Satans and the Angels of Heaven. They do not feel this while they live in the world, but it manifests itself after death when their external—through which they faked being a spiritual man—is taken away, because it is their Internal man who is such a Satan. But let me describe how spiritual hypocrites—who are *those who go about in sheep's clothing, but inwardly are ravening wolves* <note>Matthew 7:15</note>—appear before the Angels of Heaven. They appear like fortune-tellers walking on the palms of their hands, praying, who cry out to demons from the heart with their mouths and kiss them, but they clap their shoes together in the air, and in this way make a sound toward God. But when they stand on their feet, they appear to the eyes like leopards, in their gait like wolves, in their mouth like foxes, in their teeth like crocodiles, and in their faith like vultures.

# X.

## *That there is no faith among the evil.*

382. All those are evil who deny the creation of the world by God, and thus deny God, for they are atheistic <term>Naturalists</term> <note>In this context, Naturalists are those who believe nature is the sole cause of all things, denying the supernatural or divine.</note>. The reason all these are evil is because all good—which is good not only naturally but also spiritually—is from God; therefore, those who deny God are unwilling, and thus unable, to receive any good from any source other than their own <term>proprium</term> <note>The "proprium" is a technical term for a person's "selfhood" or what belongs to them naturally, which Swedenborg describes as being inherently inclined toward selfish desires.</note>. A man’s selfhood is the lust of his flesh, and whatever proceeds from this is spiritually evil, however good it may appear naturally. These are the "theoretically evil." But the "practically evil" are those who set at naught the Divine Commandments (which are contained in summary in the Decalogue) and live as though they were outside the law. That these people also deny God in their heart, even if many of them confess God with their mouth, is because God and His Commandments make one; for this reason, the ten Commandments of the Decalogue were called "JEHOVAH THERE" <note>original: "JEHOVAH IBI." Referring to the presence of God within the Law.</note> (Numbers 10:35, 36; Psalm 132:7, 8). But so that it may be more clearly seen that there is no faith among the evil, a conclusion will be drawn from these two propositions: *I. That the evil have no faith, because evil belongs to Hell, and faith belongs to Heaven. II. That all those in Christendom have no faith who reject the Lord and the Word, even though they live morally and speak, teach, and write rationally about faith*; but we shall discuss these individually.

## 383. I. THAT THE WICKED HAVE NO FAITH, BECAUSE EVIL IS OF HELL, AND FAITH IS OF HEAVEN.

That evil is of Hell is because all evil originates from there; that faith is of Heaven is because every truth belonging to faith is from Heaven. As long as a man lives in the world, he is held and walks in the middle between Heaven and Hell, and there he exists in a spiritual equilibrium, which is his **Free Will** <term>Free Will: The spiritual ability to choose between good and evil</term>. Hell is beneath his feet, and Heaven is above his head, and whatever ascends from Hell is evil and false, while whatever descends from Heaven is good and true. Because man is in the middle between those two opposites, and simultaneously in a state of spiritual equilibrium, he is able to choose, adopt, and make either one his own by his own freedom. If he chooses evil and the false, he joins himself with Hell; but if he chooses good and truth, he joins himself with Heaven.

From these facts, it is not only clear that evil is of Hell and faith is of Heaven, but also that these two cannot exist together in one subject or person. For if they were together, the man would be pulled apart as if tied with two ropes, pulled by one upward and by the other downward, and thus he would become like something hanging suspended in the air. This would be as if he flew, like a blackbird <note>original: "merula"</note>, now upward and now downward; when flying upward, he would worship God, and when downward, he would worship the Devil. Anyone can see that this would be profane.

> *“No one can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one and love the other,”* the Lord teaches in Matthew, Chapter 6:24.

Where there is evil, there is no faith; this can be illustrated by various comparisons such as these: evil is like fire—infernal fire being nothing other than the love of evil—and it consumes faith like stubble, reducing it and everything belonging to it to ashes. Evil dwells in darkness <note>original: "caligine"</note>, and faith in light; evil extinguishes faith through falsehoods, just as darkness extinguishes light. Evil is black like ink, and faith is white like snow and clear like water; evil blackens faith just as ink blackens snow and water. Furthermore, evil and the truth of faith can no more be joined than something rotten with something fragrant, or urine <note>original: "lotium"</note> with flavorful wine; they cannot exist together any more than a foul-smelling corpse and a living person in one bed. They can no more dwell together than a wolf in a sheepfold, a hawk in a dovecote, or a fox in a chicken coop.

## 384. II. THAT ALL THOSE IN CHRISTENDOM HAVE NO FAITH WHO REJECT THE LORD AND THE WORD, EVEN THOUGH THEY LIVE MORALLY AND SPEAK, TEACH, AND WRITE RATIONALLY ABOUT FAITH.

This follows as a conclusion from everything that precedes it. For it has been shown that Faith—the true and only Faith—is in the Lord and from the Lord, and that faith which is not in Him and from Him is not spiritual faith, but natural; and a purely natural faith does not have the essence of faith within it. Moreover, Faith is from the Word and nowhere else, because the Word is from the Lord, and therefore the Lord Himself is in the Word; wherefore He says *“that He is the Word,”* (John 1:1, 2). It follows from this that those who reject the Word also reject the Lord, for they are bound together as one. Likewise, those who reject one or the other also reject the Church, because the Church exists from the Lord through the Word. And further, those who reject the Church are outside of Heaven, for the Church is what introduces one into Heaven; and those who are outside of Heaven are among the damned, and they have no faith.

The reason those who reject the Lord and the Word have no faith—even though they live morally and speak, teach, and write rationally about faith—is because they do not possess a spiritual moral life, but only a natural one. Nor do they have a spiritual rational mind, but only a natural one. A purely natural morality and rationality is dead in itself; therefore, as they are dead, they have no faith. A person who is purely natural and dead regarding faith can indeed speak and teach about Faith, Charity, and God, but not *from* Faith, *from* Charity, or *from* God. That only those who believe in the Lord have Faith, and that others do not, is clear from these passages:

> *“He who believes in the Son is not judged; but he who does not believe is judged already, because he has not believed in the name of the only-begotten Son of God,”* (John 3:18).
> *“He who believes in the Son has eternal life; but he who does not believe the Son shall not see life, but the anger of God remains upon him,”* (John 3:36).

Jesus said, *“when the Spirit of truth comes...”*

I will demonstrate it to your eyes." I replied, "Demonstrate it." And he said, "Think of Light and Heat instead of Faith and Charity, and you will see clearly. Faith in its essence is Truth, which belongs to wisdom; and Charity in its essence is the Affection of love. In Heaven, the Truth of wisdom is Light, and the Affection of love is Heat. The Light and Heat in which the Angels live are essentially nothing else. From this, you can see clearly what Faith separated from Charity is, and what Faith joined to Charity is. Faith separated from Charity is like winter light; but Faith joined to Charity is like spring light. Winter light—which is Light separated from Heat—is joined to cold; it completely strips the trees, even of their leaves, kills the grass, hardens the ground, and freezes the waters. But spring light—which is Light joined to heat—causes the trees to grow, first into leaves, then into flowers, and finally into fruits; it opens and softens the ground so that it may produce grasses, herbs, flowers, and shrubs, and it also melts the ice so that the waters flow from their springs. It is exactly the same with Faith and Charity. Faith separated from Charity brings death to all things, and Faith joined to Charity gives life to all things. This giving of life and this bringing of death can be seen to the life in our spiritual world, because here Faith is Light and Charity is Heat. For where Faith is joined to Charity, there are paradisal gardens, flower-beds, and green fields in their loveliness, according to the level of that union. But where Faith is separated from Charity, there is not even grass; and where there is green, it is made of briars and thorns." 

There were then some of the Clergy nearby, whom the Angel called "Justifiers and Sanctifiers of men through faith alone," and also "Keepers of Mysteries" <note>original: "Arcanistas"</note>. We said these same things to them and demonstrated them until they saw that it was so. But when we asked them, "Is it not so?" they turned away and said, "We did not hear you." This would indeed have happened had the Lord not driven those Spirits away and liberated me. This seemed marvelous to me...

### 386. THE SECOND MEMORABLE RELATION.

One morning, waking from sleep, I saw two Angels descending from Heaven—one from the South of Heaven and the other from the East. Both were in chariots drawn by white horses. The chariot in which the Angel from the South was carried shone as if made of silver, and the chariot in which the Angel from the East was carried shone as if made of gold. The reins they held in their hands gleamed like the flaming light of dawn. 

This is how those two Angels appeared to me from a distance, but when they came near, they no longer appeared in a chariot but in their own angelic form, which is human. He who came from the East was dressed in a shining purple garment, and he from the South in a garment of hyacinthine blue. When they reached the lower regions below the Heavens, they ran toward each other as if competing to see who would arrive first, and they embraced and kissed one another. I heard that these two Angels, while they lived in the world, had been joined by a deep interior friendship; but now, one dwells in the Eastern Heaven and the other in the Southern Heaven. In the Eastern Heaven are those who are in love from the Lord; in the Southern Heaven are those who are in wisdom from the Lord. 

After they had talked for a while about the magnificence of their respective Heavens, their conversation turned to this question: whether Heaven in its essence is Love, or whether it is Wisdom. They agreed at once that each belongs to the other, but they debated which was the primary source. 

The Angel from the Heaven of wisdom asked the other what Love is. He replied that Love, originating from the Lord as the Sun, is the heat of life for angels and men—it is their very life. He explained that the offshoots of love are called "affections," and through these, perceptions and thus thoughts are produced. From this it follows that Wisdom, in its origin, is Love; consequently, Thought in its origin is the affection of that love. This can be seen if one examines these derivations in their proper order: Thought is nothing other than the *form* of affection. This remains unknown to most because thoughts exist in light, while affections exist in heat; therefore, people reflect upon their thoughts, but not upon their affections. 

That Thought is nothing other than the form of the affection of some love can also be illustrated by speech: speech is nothing other than the form of sound. This is a perfect analogy because Sound corresponds to affection and speech to thought; thus, affection "sounds" and thought "speaks." This becomes clear when one considers: if you take the sound away from speech, is anything left of the speech? Likewise, if you take affection away from thought, does anything of the thought remain? 

From this it is now evident that Love is the "all" of Wisdom; consequently, the Essence of the heavens is Love, and their Existence is Wisdom. Or, to say the same thing: the Heavens are from Divine Love, and they exist from Divine Love *through* Divine Wisdom. Therefore, as was said before, each belongs to the other. 

At that moment, a novice Spirit <note>A "novice" spirit refers to a person who has recently died and is still adjusting to the spiritual world.</note> was with me. Hearing these things, he asked whether it is the same with Charity and Faith, since Charity belongs to affection and Faith belongs to thought. The Angel replied, "It is exactly the same. Faith is nothing other than the form of charity, just as Sound is [for-]"

### 387. THE THIRD MEMORABLE RELATION. 

After those two Angels were out of my sight, I saw a certain Garden on the right side, where there were olives, figs, laurels, and palms, arranged in order according to <term>correspondences: the spiritual law that outward physical things reflect inward spiritual realities.</term> I looked toward that place, and among the trees, I saw Angels and Spirits walking and talking together. Then one angelic spirit looked toward me; those who are being prepared for Heaven in the <term>World of Spirits</term> are called Angelic Spirits. He came from that Garden to me and said, "Do you wish to come with me into our Paradise? You shall hear and see wonders." 

I went with him, and then he said to me, "These whom you see (for there were many) are all in the love of truth, and consequently in the light of wisdom. There is also a Palace here, which we call THE TEMPLE OF WISDOM; but no one can see it who believes himself to be very wise, still less he who believes he is wise enough, and least of all he who believes he is wise from himself. The reason is that such people are not in the reception of the light of Heaven from the love of genuine wisdom. Genuine wisdom consists in this: that a person sees from the light of Heaven that what he knows, understands, and is wise in, is so little compared to what he does not know, understand, and is not wise in, that it is like a drop to the Ocean—consequently, almost nothing. Everyone who is in this paradise-garden, and acknowledges within himself from perception and sight that he is relatively so little wise, sees that TEMPLE OF WISDOM; for it is the interior light in a person’s mind that enables them to see it, not their exterior light without the interior." 

Now, because I had often thought on this, first from knowledge, then from perception, and finally from interior light, and had acknowledged that man is so little wise, behold, it was granted to me to see that Temple. It was wonderful in its form, raised high above the ground, quadrangular, with walls of crystal and a roof of transparent jasper elegantly arched; the foundation was of various precious stones. The steps by which one ascended into it were of polished alabaster; at the sides of the steps appeared figures like lions with their cubs. 

I then asked if I might enter, and I was told that I might; so I ascended, and when I entered, I saw what looked like <term>Cherubim</term> flying under the roof, but they soon vanished. The floor upon which we walked was made of cedar, and the whole Temple, because of the transparency of the roof and walls, was built in the very form of light. 

The Angelic Spirit entered with me, to whom I related what I had heard from the two Angels concerning LOVE and WISDOM, and concerning Charity and Faith. Then he said, "Did they not also speak of the Third?" I asked, "What third thing?" He replied, "It is THE GOOD OF USE. Love and Wisdom without the Good of Use are nothing; they are merely <term>ideal entities: things that exist only as abstract ideas without substance.</term> They do not become real until they are in Use. For Love, Wisdom, and Use are three things that cannot be separated; if they are separated, none of them is anything. Love is nothing without Wisdom, but in Wisdom, it is formed into something. This 'something' into which it is formed is Use. Therefore, when love, through wisdom, is in use, it then truly exists, because it exists actually. They are exactly like end, cause, and effect; the end is nothing unless, through the cause, it exists in the effect. If one of these three is dissolved, the whole is dissolved and becomes as nothing. It is the same with Charity, Faith, and Works. Charity without faith is nothing, nor is Faith anything without charity, nor are Charity and Faith anything without Works; but in Works they are something, and of such a quality...

## 388. THE FOURTH MEMORABLE RELATION. 
I spoke with certain people who are understood by the **dragon** in the **Apocalypse** <note>The Book of Revelation</note>. In the spiritual world, all things appear at a distance according to **correspondences**; when these appear in forms, they are called **representations** of spiritual things in objects similar to natural ones.

The emissary understood this, for every devil can understand truth when he hears it, but he cannot retain it, because the affection for evil—which is the lust of the flesh within him—casts out the thought of truth when it returns. "I can almost say," he remarked, "that there is no more spirituality in your **Faith** than in thinking about the **Kingdom of the Mogul** <note>original: "Regno Mogolis" — referring to the Mughal Empire in India, used here as a metaphor for something distant, worldly, and purely intellectual.</note>, or about the diamond mine there, or the treasury and court of that Emperor."

This fire from Heaven was an appearance of the anger and hatred they felt against those in the city, because they had cast **Faith** down from the first place to the second—and indeed to the lowest place beneath **Charity**—by saying it was not truly faith. The reason they appeared to be consumed by fire was that hell opened beneath their feet and they were swallowed up. ## 389. THE FIFTH MEMORABLE RELATION.

Once a Letter was seen sent down from Heaven into a certain society in the **World of Spirits** <note>The intermediate state between Heaven and Hell.</note>, where there were two **Prelates of the Church** with **Canons** and **Priests** under them. In that Letter was an exhortation that they should acknowledge the Lord Jesus Christ as the God of Heaven and Earth, just as He Himself taught (Matthew 28:18), and that they should turn away from the doctrine of justifying **Faith** without the works of the law, because it is erroneous. 

That Letter was read and copied by many, and many thought and spoke about its contents with good judgment. But after they received it, they said to one another, "Let us hear the **Prelates**." They were heard, but they spoke against it and disapproved. Indeed, the **Prelates** of that society were hard-hearted because of the falsehoods they had been steeped in while in the former world. Therefore, after a brief consultation among themselves, they sent the Letter back to Heaven from whence it came. 

Once this was done, after some murmuring, most of the **Laity** withdrew from their previous agreement, and then the light of their judgment in spiritual matters—which had previously shone forth—was suddenly extinguished. After they were warned again, but in vain, I saw that society sinking down—though I did not see how deep—and thus withdrawn from the sight of those who worship the Lord alone and turn away from "faith alone" justification. 

But after some days, I saw nearly a hundred people ascending from the lower earth, to where that little society had sunk. They came to me, and one of them spoke, saying: "Hear a wonder! While we were sinking, the place appeared to us first like a pond, but soon like dry land, and afterward like a small city in which many had their own houses. After a day, we consulted among ourselves what should be done. Many said that the two **Prelates of the Church** should be approached and mildly rebuked, because they sent back the Letter to Heaven from which it had been sent down, and because of that, this has happened to us." They chose some men who went to the **Prelates** (the speaker said he was one of them). "And then one among us, excelling in wisdom, spoke to the **Prelates** thus: 'We believed that the Church and Religion were with us more than others, because we heard it said that we are in the highest light of the Gospel. But illustration from Heaven was given to some of us, and in that illustration, a perception that today in the **Christian World** <note>original: "Orbe Christiano"</note> there is no longer a Church, because there is no Religion.'" The Prelates replied, "What are you say—"
