...[I] give, the Good of love and Charity, and the Truth of wisdom and faith, flow in; and that those things which flow in appear in man exactly as if they were his own, and proceed from him as if they were his own. This can be clearly seen from the senses of sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch: all things sensed in the organs of those senses flow in from the outside and are felt within them. It is the same in the organs of the internal senses, with the only difference being that spiritual things (which do not appear to the eyes) flow into the internal organs, while natural things (which do appear) flow into the external ones. In a word, man is an organized vessel <term>organum: an organized structure or instrument designed to receive something</term> receiving life from God; consequently, he is a recipient of good to the extent that he stops doing evil.

The Lord grants every person the power to stop doing evil because He grants the ability to will and to understand; and whatever a person does from the will according to the understanding—or, what is the same, whatever one does from the freedom of the will according to the reason of the understanding—this remains. Through this, the Lord brings man into a state of conjunction <note>A state of being spiritually "joined" or "connected" to the Divine.</note> with Himself, and in this state He reforms, regenerates, and saves him. The Life that flows in is the Life proceeding from the Lord, which is also called the Spirit of God, and in the Word, the Holy Spirit; of which it is also said that it enlightens and vivifies—indeed, that it operates within man. But this Life is varied and modified according to the "organization" <note>The internal spiritual structure formed by a person's choices and loves.</note> induced by love.

You can also know that all the good of love and charity, and all the truth of wisdom and faith, flow in and are not inherently in man, from this fact: whoever thinks such things belong to man from creation cannot eventually help but think that God infused Himself into man, and thus that men were, in part, Gods. Yet those who think this from their faith become devils, and among us in the spiritual world, they smell like corpses. Furthermore, what is human action but the Mind acting? For what the Mind wills and thinks, it acts and speaks through its body, its organ; therefore, while the Mind is led by the Lord, Action and Speech are also led. And Action and Speech are led by the Lord when one believes in Him.

If it were not so, tell me if you can: why has the Lord commanded in His Word in a thousand places that man should love his neighbor, perform the good works of charity, bear fruit like a tree, and follow the commandments—this and that—so that he may be saved? And why did He say that man would be judged according to his deeds or works—those who do good to Heaven and Life, and those who do evil to Hell and Death? How could the Lord speak such things if everything that proceeds from man were <term>meritorious: the prideful belief that one's own actions deserve a reward from God, which Swedenborg views as a spiritual error</term> and therefore evil? Know then, that if the Mind is Charity, the Action is also Charity; but if the Mind is "Faith alone"—which is faith separated from spiritual Charity—then the Action is also that Faith.

Having heard these things, those sitting under the Laurel said, "We understand that you have spoken rightly, but we still do not comprehend." To whom I replied: "You understand that I have spoken rightly from *common perception*, which a person has from the influx of light from Heaven when they hear a truth; but you do not yet comprehend from your *own perception*, which a person has from the influx of light from the World. These two perceptions—the internal and external, or the spiritual and natural—become one among the wise. You also can make them one if you look to the Lord and remove evils." Because they understood this, I took some branches from a certain Vine and offered them, saying, "Do you believe this is from me, or from the Lord?" And they said, "From you, through the Lord." And behold, those branches in their hands put forth grapes.

But when I withdrew, I saw a cedar table upon which was a book, under a green olive tree whose trunk was encircled by a vine. I looked, and behold, it was a book written by me, called *HEAVENLY SECRETS* <note>original: "ARCANA CÆLESTIA" – Swedenborg's primary work (published 1749–1756), a multi-volume commentary on the internal sense of Genesis and Exodus.</note>. I told them that in that book it is fully shown that Man is an organized vessel receiving life, and not life itself; and that life cannot be created—and thus be present within man as something created—any more than light can be in the eye independently.

But I kept my eyes on the **Great Reddish Head**, and I saw that it had a face like a human being, and it spoke with the boys and girls sitting on the benches, and licked their hands; then the boys and girls stroked them and gave them sumptuous and precious food, as well as expensive items like all-silk for clothes, thyine wood <note>original: "lignum thyinum" — a fragrant, precious wood mentioned in Revelation 18:12, often associated with luxury.</note> for tables, purple for decorations, and **SCARLET FOR DYEING** <note>original: "infucationes" — while meaning "dyeing," this term often carries a connotation of "painting over" or creating a false appearance.</note>. Seeing these things, I desired to know what they represented, for I knew that all things that appear in the spiritual world are *Correspondences* <term>Correspondentiæ: the relationship between spiritual causes and the natural effects that represent them</term>, and represent spiritual things belonging to affection and the thought coming from it.

Then they spoke with me from Heaven, saying: "You know yourself what a **Naval Yard** represents, and what ships represent, as well as the boys and girls upon them, but you do not know what the **Tortoises** represent." And they said: "The tortoises represent those among the Clergy there who entirely separate *Faith* from *Charity* and its good works, affirming to themselves that there is plainly no connection between them. Instead, they claim that the *Holy Spirit*, through *Faith in God the Father* for the sake of the *Son's* merit, enters into a person and purifies their internal parts all the way to their own Will. They treat this will as an 'oval plane,' and claim that when the operation of the *Holy Spirit* approaches that plane, it deflects around it to the left side and does not touch it at all. Thus, the interior or superior part of a person's character is for God, while the exterior or inferior part is for the person. Because of this, they believe nothing a person does appears before God—neither the good nor the evil. The good does not appear because it is meritorious <term>meritorium: the belief that one can earn salvation or "merit" through their own deeds, which these clergy viewed as a sin of pride</term>, and the evil does not appear because it is simply evil; for if these were to appear before God, the person would perish from both. Since this is their belief, they think it is permissible for a person to will, think, speak, and do whatever they please, provided they are careful before the World."

I asked whether they also claim that it is permissible to think of God as if He were not Omnipresent and Omniscient. They said from Heaven that this also is permissible for them; for God, in the case of one who has attained Faith and has been purified and justified through it, does not look at any of their thoughts or intentions. They claim such a person still retains, in the inner bosom or superior region of their mind, the Faith they received in that one act, and that this act can sometimes return without the person even knowing it.

These things are what the **SMALL HEAD** represents, which they pull into the front of the body and also insert into the **LARGE HEAD** while they speak with the Laity. For they do not speak with the people from the Small Head, but from the Large one, which appears in front with a human face. They speak to them from the *Word* <note>The Bible</note> about *Love*, *Charity*, *Good Works*, the *Commandments of the Decalogue*, and *Repentance*; they take from the Word almost everything found there on those subjects. But then they insert the small head into the large one, from which they understand within themselves that all those things are not to be done for the sake of God and salvation, but only for the sake of the public and private good. However, because they speak of these things from the *Word*—especially the *Gospel*, the operation of the *Holy Spirit*, and *Salvation*—sweetly and elegantly, they appear to their listeners like beautiful men, and wise above all others in the world. This is why you saw sumptuous and precious things given to them by the boys and girls sitting on the benches of the ships.

These, therefore, are the ones you saw represented as Tortoises. In your world, they are hardly distinguished from others, except by the fact that they believe themselves to be wiser than everyone else and laugh at others—even at those who hold similar doctrines regarding Faith but are not initiated into these secrets. They carry a certain seal with them on their clothing, by which they make themselves known to one another." The one speaking with me said: "I will not tell you what they think about other matters of Faith, such as *Election*, *Free Will*, *Baptism*, and the *Holy Supper*, which are such that they do not make them public, but we in Heaven know them. Truly, because..."

Such people are like this in the world, and after death, it is not permitted for anyone to speak differently than they think. Because they then cannot do otherwise than speak from the insanity of their own thoughts, they are regarded as insane and are cast out of their societies. At last, they are sent down into the **Bottomless Pit** <note>original: "Puteum abyssi" — the pit described in Revelation 9:2, often interpreted as a state of deep self-delusion and spiritual darkness.</note>, concerning which we read in Revelation Chapter 9:2. There they become corporeal spirits and appear like **Egyptian Mummies**; for a callus has been induced upon the interior parts of their minds, because in the world they had also placed a fence <note>i.e., a mental barrier</note> between their thoughts and their actions. The hellish society made up of these people is on the border of the hellish society of the **Machiavellians** <note>Followers of Niccolò Machiavelli, known here for political cunning and the separation of private morality from public action.</note>, and they pass back and forth from one to the other, calling each other "Comrades," but they eventually leave because there is a difference between them: among the former, there was some religious element regarding the act of **justification by faith** <term>Justification by faith: the theological doctrine that a person is made righteous before God by belief alone, without the need for good works.</term>, whereas among the Machiavellians, there was none.

After I saw them cast out of their societies and gathered together to be thrown down, I saw a **Vessel** <note>original: "Navigium" — a small ship or boat.</note> flying in the air with seven sails, and in it were captains and sailors dressed in purple clothing, wearing magnificent laurels upon their hats, shouting:

> "Behold us in Heaven! We are doctors in purple, and laureated above all others, because we are the heads of the wise from among the entire Clergy of Europe."

I wondered what this was, and it was told to me that these were images of pride and "ideal thoughts" which are called **phantasies**. These originated from those who were previously seen as **Tortoises**, and who were now seen as insane people cast out of their societies and gathered in one place. I then desired to speak with them; I went to the place where they stood, greeted them, and said: "Are you the ones who have separated the internal things of men from their external things—such as the operation of the Holy Spirit (as if it were only in Faith) from His cooperation with man (outside of Faith)? In doing so, you have separated God from man. Have you not thus removed not only **Charity** and its works from faith, as many other doctors of the Clergy have done, but also Faith itself from its manifestation before God by man? But I ask you, would you like me to speak with you about this matter from **Reason**, or from **Sacred Scripture**?" They said: "Speak first from Reason." And I spoke, saying:

> "How can the Internal and the External be separated in a human being? Who does not see, or cannot see from common perception, that all the interior things of a man proceed and continue into his exterior things, and even into his extremes <note>The "extremes" refer to the outermost parts of the body, such as the skin or the hands.</note>, so that they may produce their effects and perform their works? Are not internal things there for the sake of the external, so that they may end in them, subsist in them, and thus exist—hardly different than a column stands upon its **pedestal** <note>original: "stylobata" — the base or platform supporting a column.</note>? You can see that unless there was a continuation, and thus a conjunction, the outermost parts would dissolve and scatter like bubbles in the air. Who can deny that the interior operations of God within man are myriads of myriads, of which man knows nothing? And what does it help to know those things, provided he knows the extremes, in which he is present with God together with his own thought and will? 

> But this shall be illustrated by an example: Does a man know the interior operations of his own speech? Such as how the **Lungs** draw in air and fill the vesicles, the bronchi, and the lobes? How they emit that air into the **Trachea** and there turn it into sound? How that sound is modified in the glottis by the help of the larynx? And how the tongue then articulates it, and the lips complete the articulation so that it becomes speech? Are not all those interior operations, of which man knows nothing, for the sake of the extreme <note>The final result.</note>, so that man is able to speak? Remove or separate one of those internal things from its continuity with the extremes, and could the man speak any more than a **log** <note>original: "stipes" — a tree trunk, post, or blockhead.</note>? 

> Take another example: the two hands are the ultimate parts of man. Are not the interior things which continue into them from the head through the neck, then through the chest, shoulders, arms, and forearms? There are innumerable muscular tissues, innumerable phalanxes of motor fibers, innumerable bundles of nerves and blood vessels, and many **hinge-joints** <note>original: "ginglymi" — a type of joint that allows movement in only one plane, like a door hinge.</note> of bones with their ligaments and membranes. Does a man know anything of these? And yet his hands operate from each and every one of them. Suppose that those interior things around the joint of the hand were to bend away to the left or right, and did not enter through a continuum—would not the hand fall off from the arm and rot like something torn away and lifeless? Indeed, if you are willing to believe it, it would be as it is with the body if a man were decapitated."

It would be the same with the human mind and its two "lives," the **Will** and the **Intellect** <term>Intellect: the part of the mind that understands and thinks, as opposed to the Will which desires and acts.</term>, if the Divine Operations—those of **Faith** and **Charity**—were to stop halfway and not extend through a continuous path to the human being. Truly, in such a case, a person would be not only a brute animal but a rotten stump. These points are in accordance with reason. Now, if you wish to listen, these same points are supported by **Sacred Scripture**. Does the Lord not say, *“Abide in Me, and I in you; I am the Vine and you are the branches; he who abides in Me, and I in him, bears much fruit”* (John 15:4–5)? (Matthew 25:14–34; Luke 19:13–26). Also, that *“He gives a reward to everyone according to their labor in His Vineyard”* (Matthew 20:1–17). 

But these are only a few examples; whole parchments could be filled with passages from the **Word** <note>original: "Verbum" — a term used to refer to the Bible as the Divinely inspired Word of God.</note> about how a person must produce fruit like a tree, act according to the commandments, and love God and their neighbor, and much more. Yet I know that your own self-derived intelligence cannot have a true connection with these things from the Word; even though you may speak the words, your underlying ideas pervert them. You cannot do otherwise, because you remove everything belonging to God from the human being in terms of communication and thus conjunction. What remains then, but also to remove everything belonging to **Worship**? 

Afterward, I saw them in the **light of Heaven**, which reveals and makes manifest the true nature of everyone. Then they no longer appeared as they did before—in a ship in the air as if in Heaven, wearing purple garments and laurel wreaths on their heads. Instead, they appeared in a sandy place, wearing clothes made of rags and wrapped in what looked like fishing nets around their waists, through which their nakedness was visible. They were then cast down into a society that bordered the **Machiavellians** <note>Followers of political cunning who separate morality from action; here, they represent those who separate faith from life.</note>.

# CHAPTER EIGHT

## FREE WILL.

463. Before I set myself to the task of presenting the Teaching of the **New Church** <term>New Church: The author's term for a new spiritual era characterized by a direct internal understanding of the Word.</term> concerning **FREE WILL** <term>Free Will: The ability to choose and act according to one's own determination, particularly regarding spiritual life and salvation.</term>, it is necessary to first state what the Contemporary Church teaches on this subject in its own official books of doctrine. For unless this is done, a person possessing sound reason and religion might believe it is not worth the effort to write anything new about it. Such a person would say to themselves: "Who does not know that man has Free Will in spiritual matters? Otherwise, why would priests preach that people should believe in God, convert themselves, live according to the commandments in the Word, fight against the lusts of their flesh, and prepare themselves to be a 'new creature,' among many other similar things?" Therefore, they cannot think otherwise than that such words would be merely empty wind if there were no Free Will in matters of salvation, and that to deny it would be insane because it goes against common sense. Yet, that the Contemporary Church actually takes the opposite view and casts Free Will out from its temples is evident from the book called the **FORMULA OF CONCORD** <note>original: "Formula Concordiae" — a definitive Lutheran doctrinal statement published in 1577.</note>, to which the Evangelicals swear allegiance. This is also evident from the passages that follow. That a similar doctrine—and the faith resulting from it—regarding Free Will exists among the Reformed, and indeed throughout the entire Christian world (including Germany, Sweden, Denmark, England, and Holland), is clear from their own books of doctrine. The following are therefore transcripts from the **FORMULA OF CONCORD**, Leipzig edition, 1756.

464. "I. The Teachers of the **Augsburg Confession** <note>original: "Augustanae Confessionis" — the primary confession of faith for the Lutheran Church.</note> assert that, since the fall of our first parents, humans are so thoroughly corrupted that in spiritual matters, which pertain to our conversion and salvation, we are by nature blind. Thus, we neither understand nor are able to understand the Word of God when it is preached, but judge it to be a foolish thing; we never approach God of our own accord, but rather remain enemies of God until, by the power of the **Holy Spirit** through the Word preached and heard, out of pure grace and without any of our own cooperation, we are converted, gifted with faith, regenerated, and renewed (page 656). II. We believe that in spiritual and Divine matters, the intellect, heart, and will of the unregenerate person are unable, by their own natural powers, to understand, believe, embrace, think, will, begin, perfect, act, operate, or cooperate in anything at all. Instead, man is so utterly corrupted and dead to what is good that in human nature after the Fall, and before regeneration, not even a spark of spiritual power remains by which he could prepare himself for the grace of God, or apprehend it when offered, or adapt himself to be capable of it by himself. Nor can he, by his own powers, contribute anything to his own conversion—not the whole of it, nor half, nor the smallest part—nor act, operate, or cooperate from himself or as if from himself. Rather, man is a servant of sin and a slave of Satan, by whom he is driven; hence his natural Free Will, by reason of his corrupted powers and depraved nature, is active and effective only in those things which displease God and are opposed to Him (page 656). III. That in civil and natural affairs man is industrious and ingenious, but in spiritual and Divine matters, which pertain to the salvation of the soul, he is like a stump, a stone, or the statue of salt that was Lot's wife, which has use of neither eyes, mouth, nor any—" <note>The text ends mid-sentence here as it continues onto the next page.</note>

,, [they still have] the use of their senses (page 661). IV. That although a human being can use their external limbs for movement, hear the *Gospel*, and meditate upon it in some way, they nonetheless despise it in their secret thoughts as a foolish thing and are unable to believe; in this respect, a person is "worse than a wooden trunk" <note>original: "deterior est trunco"</note> unless the *Holy Spirit* is active within them, kindling and working faith and other virtues approved by God, as well as obedience (page 662). V. In a certain sense, it can be said that a human is not a stone or a log; a stone or a log does not resist, nor does it understand or feel what is happening to it, whereas a human resists God by their own will until they have been converted. And yet, it remains true that before conversion, a human is a rational creature who possesses an intellect—but not in *Divine* matters—and a will—but not such that they desire any saving good. Nevertheless, they can contribute nothing to their own conversion, and in this regard, they are "worse than a log or a stone" (pages 672, 673). VI. That the entire conversion is the operation, gift, and work of the *Holy Spirit* alone, who effects and works it by His power and strength, through the *Word*, in the intellect, heart, and will of the human as if in a "passive subject" <term>passive subject: A philosophical term (subjecto patiente) describing something that is acted upon by an external force without contributing any action of its own.</term>, where the human does nothing but merely undergoes the process. However, this does not happen in the same way a statue is carved from stone or a seal is pressed into wax, because wax has neither knowledge nor will (page 681). VII. According to the sayings of certain *Church Fathers* and *more recent Doctors*, it is said that "God draws, but He draws the willing" <note>original: "trahat sed volentem"</note>, suggesting that the human will does something in conversion; however, these sayings are not in harmony with the Holy Words [of Scripture], for they confirm a false opinion regarding the powers of Human Choice in conversion (page 582). VIII. That in the external affairs of the *World* which are subject to reason, there remains in the human being some intellect, strength, and ability, even though these are wretchedly weak; and indeed, these very things, however small they may be, are poisoned and contaminated by "hereditary disease" <term>hereditary disease: A traditional way of describing original sin as a condition inherited by all humans from birth.</term>, such that they are of no significance in the sight of God (page 641). IX. That in conversion, by which a child of wrath becomes a child of grace, the human does not cooperate with the *Holy Spirit*, since the conversion of a human is the work of the Spirit alone (pages 219, 519 and following, 663 and following; appendix page 143). Yet, a person who is "born again" through the power of the *Holy Spirit* can cooperate, although much weakness still interferes; they perform good works as much and as long as they are led, ruled, and governed by the Holy Spirit. Even then, they do not cooperate with the Holy Spirit "as two horses pull a single cart together" (page 674). X. *Original sin* is not a specific crime committed by an act, but is intimately fixed within the nature, substance, and essence of the human; it is the "fountainhead" <note>original: "scaturigo"</note> of all actual sins, such as wicked thoughts, conversations, and evil deeds (page 577). This hereditary disease, through which the entire nature is corrupted, is a horrible sin, and indeed the principle and head of all sins, from which all transgressions flow as if from a root or a spring (page 640). That *Nature* itself, through this sin, is totally infected and corrupted before God—even in its innermost marrow and the deepest recesses of the heart—as if by a "spiritual leprosy" <note>original: "lepra spiritualem"</note>. Because of this corruption, the person is accused and condemned by the law of God, so that by nature we are children of wrath and slaves to death and damnation, unless we are delivered and saved from these evils by the benefit of Christ's merit (page 639). From this results a total lack or deprivation of the "original righteousness" <term>original righteousness: The state of moral perfection and harmony humans were believed to possess in Paradise before the Fall.</term> or "Image of God" created in *Paradise*. From this also comes the impotence, unfitness, and stupidity by which a human is utterly useless for all Divine or spiritual things. In place of the lost Image of God, there is in the human an internal, most wicked, deep, inscrutable, and inexpressible corruption of the entire nature and all powers, especially the higher and principal faculties of the soul in the mind, intellect, heart, and will (page 640).

## *That in the Garden of Eden two trees were placed, one of life and the other of the knowledge of good and evil, signifies that Free Will in spiritual matters has been given to man.*

466. That by Adam and Eve <note>original: "Adamum & Chaivam"</note> in the Book of Moses, the first-created humans are not meant, has been believed by many; to confirm this, they have brought forward arguments regarding "Pre-Adamites" <note>A theory that humans existed before the biblical Adam.</note> based on the calculations and chronologies of certain nations. They also point to the statement of Cain, Adam's firstborn, to Jehovah: *I shall be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth, so that whoever finds me will kill me; therefore Jehovah set a mark upon Cain, so that whoever found him should not kill him*, Genesis 4:14, 15; and after he went out from the face of Jehovah, he dwelt in the land of Nod and built a city, verses 16, 17. Consequently, the Earth must have been inhabited before Adam. However, that by Adam and his wife is meant the "Most Ancient Church" <note>In Swedenborg's theology, the "Most Ancient Church" represents the first spiritual era of humanity, characterized by direct perception of divine truth.</note> on this planet has been demonstrated at length by me in **HEAVENLY SECRETS** <note>original: *Arcanis Cælestibus*</note>, published by me in London. It is also shown there that by the "Garden of Eden" is meant the wisdom of the people of that Church; by the "Tree of Life," the Lord in man and man in the Lord; and by the "Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil," man not in the Lord but in his own selfhood <term>selfhood: The Latin *proprium* refers to the human ego or the sense that one's life and goodness belong to oneself rather than being a gift from God.</term>, such as one who believes he does everything from himself, even what is good. By the eating from this tree is meant the appropriation of evil.

467. In the Word <note>The Bible.</note>, the "Garden of Eden" does not mean a physical garden, but Intelligence; nor does a "Tree" mean a literal tree, but man. That the Garden of Eden signifies intelligence and wisdom can be established from these passages: **IN YOUR INTELLIGENCE AND WISDOM** you had made for yourself wealth; **YOU WERE IN EDEN, THE GARDEN OF GOD**, and in what follows there: full of **WISDOM**, **YOU WERE IN EDEN, THE GARDEN OF GOD**, *every precious stone was your covering*, Ezekiel 28:4, 12, 13. This is said of the Prince and the King of Tyre, of whom wisdom is predicated, because by "Tyre" in the Word is signified the Church in respect to the knowledge of truth and good, through which wisdom comes. By the precious stones which were his covering, the knowledge of truth and good is also signified; for the Prince and King of Tyre were never literally in the Garden of Eden. And elsewhere in Ezekiel: *Ashur was a cedar in Lebanon, the cedars in the* **GARDEN OF GOD** *did not hide him, no tree in the* **GARDEN OF GOD** *was equal to him in beauty; all the* **TREES OF EDEN** *in the* **GARDEN OF GOD** *envied him*, Chapter 31:1, 8; and further: *To whom have you been made similar in glory and in magnitude among the* **TREES OF EDEN**, verse 18. This is said of Ashur <note>Assyria.</note> because by him in the Word is signified Rationality and the Intelligence derived from it. In Isaiah: *Jehovah will comfort Zion, and will make her desert like* **EDEN**, *and her wilderness like the* **GARDEN OF JEHOVAH**, Chapter 51:3. Zion there is the Church, and Eden and the Garden of Jehovah are wisdom and intelligence. In Revelation: *To him who overcomes I will give to eat of the* **TREE OF LIFE**, *which is in the* **MIDST OF THE PARADISE OF GOD**, Chapter 2:7. *In the midst of the street of the river on either side shall be the Tree of Life*, Chapter 22:2. From these it is clearly evident that by the Garden in Eden, in which Adam is said to have been placed, is meant Intelligence and Wisdom, because similar things are said of Tyre, Ashur, and Zion. By a "Garden" intelligence is also signified elsewhere in the Word, as in Isaiah 58:11, Chapter 61:11, Jeremiah 31:12, Amos 9:14, and Numbers 24:6. This spiritual understanding of the "Garden" takes its cause from representations in the spiritual world; there, Paradises appear wherever the Angels are in intelligence and wisdom.

469. Anyone today who is interiorly wise can perceive or guess that those things written about Adam and his Wife involve spiritual matters which no one until now has known, because the spiritual sense of the Word has not been revealed until this time. Who cannot see from a distance that Jehovah would not have placed two trees in the Garden, one as a stumbling block, unless they represented something spiritual? And that because they both ate from a certain tree, they were cursed, and that this curse should cling to every person after them? To think that the whole human race was condemned on account of the fault of one man—in which there was no evil of the lust of the flesh or iniquity of the heart—does this square with Divine Justice? Above all, why did Jehovah not pull him away from eating it, since He saw it happening? And why did He not cast the Serpent into hell before it persuaded them? But, my friend, God did not do this, because he would have thereby taken away the human's <term>Liberum Arbitrium</term> <note>Free Will or Free Choice.</note>, which is what makes a human a human and not a beast. When this is known, it becomes evident that by those two trees—one for life and the other for death—the human's Free Will in spiritual matters was represented. Furthermore, hereditary evil is not from that event, but from parents, from whom an inclination toward the evil in which they themselves lived is passed down to their children. That this is so can be seen by anyone who examines the manners, minds, and faces of children—even of whole families from one father. Yet it still depends on each person in the family whether they wish to approach or turn away from it, because everyone is left to their own choice. What specifically is signified by the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil is fully explained in the MEMORABLE RELATION above at number 48, which should be consulted.

470. It is commonly believed that Life is in the man, as his own, so that he is not only a receptacle of life but actually Life itself. That this is commonly believed is due to the appearance, because he lives—that is, he feels, thinks, speaks, and acts exactly as if of himself. The cause of this false belief—that man is also life, and consequently that life in man is uncreated and afterward propagated through descent <term>tradux: the theological theory that the soul is transmitted from parents to children through natural generation</term>—I have derived from appearance. However, the cause of the fallacy from appearance is that most people today are natural, and few are spiritual. The natural man judges from appearances and therefore from fallacies, and these are diametrically opposed to this truth: that man is only a receptacle of life and not life itself. That man is not life, but a receptacle of life from God, is evident from these clear testimonies: that all things which are created are in themselves finite, and that man, because he is finite, could not be created except from finite things. Therefore, in the *Book of Creation* <note>The book of Genesis.</note> it is said that Adam was made from the earth and its dust, from which he was also named; for *Adam* signifies the ground of the earth. And every man actually consists only of such things as are in the earth, and from the earth in the atmospheres. Those things in the atmospheres which are from the earth, man absorbs through the lungs and through the pores of the whole body; the coarser things he takes in through foods made from earthly materials. 

As for the spirit of man, that too was created from finite things. For what is the spirit of man but a receptacle of the life of the mind? The finite things from which it is made are spiritual substances, which are in the spiritual world, and which are also brought down into our earth and hidden therein. Unless these spiritual substances were present together with material ones, no seed could be impregnated from its inmost parts, and thereafter grow wonderfully without any deviation from the first sprout all the way to fruits and new seeds. Nor would any worms be procreated from the effluvia of the earth and the exhalation of vapors from vegetables, with which the atmospheres are impregnated. Who can think from reason that the Infinite could create anything other than the finite? Or that man, because he is finite, is anything other than a form which the Infinite can vivify from the life within Himself? And this is understood by these words: *Jehovah God formed man, the dust from the earth, and breathed into his nostrils the soul of lives,* Genesis 2:7. God, because He is Infinite, is Life in Himself; this He cannot create and thus transcribe into man, for that would be to make him God. That this was done was the insanity of the serpent or the devil, and from him, it became the insanity of Eve <note>original: "Chaivae"</note> and Adam; for the serpent said, *In the day you eat of the fruit of this tree, your eyes shall be opened, and you shall be as God,* Genesis 3:5. That this dire persuasion—that God had transfused and transcribed Himself into men—belonged to the men of the Most Ancient Church at its end when it was consumed, I have heard from their own mouths. Because of that horrendous faith, believing they were thus gods, they lie deeply hidden in a cavern, which no one can approach without being overcome by an inner dizziness. That the Most Ancient Church is understood and described by Adam and his wife was made known in the preceding Article.

471. Who cannot see—if he is able to think from reason elevated above the senses of the body—that life is not creatable? For what is life, but the inmost activity of Love and Wisdom, which are in God and are God? This life can also be called the living force itself. He who sees this can also see that this life cannot be transcribed into any man, except together with love and wisdom. Who denies, or can deny, that every good of love and every truth of wisdom are solely from God? And that as much as a man receives these from God, so much he lives from God, and is said to be born of God—that is, regenerated. Conversely, as much as one does not receive love and wisdom (or what is the same, charity and faith), so much he does not receive the life which is life in itself from God, but from hell; and this is no other life than inverted life, which is called spiritual death.

472. From the things said above, it can be perceived and concluded that the following things are not creatable, namely:
1. The Infinite.
2. Love and Wisdom.
3. Consequently, Life.
4. Nor Light and Heat.
5. Indeed, not even activity itself, viewed in itself.
But the organs that receive them are creatable and created. These things can be illustrated by these comparisons: Light is not creatable, but its organ, which is the eye, is;

that sound, which is the activity of the atmosphere, is not something that can be created, but rather its organ, which is the ear; likewise, heat, which is the primary active force, to receive which all things in the three kingdoms of nature were created, which do not act of themselves but are acted upon according to how they receive it. It is a law of Creation that where there are active forces, there are also passive ones, and that these two join together as one. If active forces were creatable like passive ones, there would have been no need for the Sun, nor for the heat and light coming from it; instead, all created things would exist without them, even though the created Universe would collapse into Chaos if they were removed. The Sun of this world itself consists of created substances, the activity of which produces fire. These examples are brought forward for the sake of illustration. If it were denied that man is a <term>Forma recipiens: a receiving form or receptacle</term> of love and wisdom from God, then <term>influx: the spiritual process of life flowing from God into creation</term> would also be denied, and thus the truth that all good is from God; conjunction with God would also be denied, and therefore the phrase that man can be the "dwelling place and temple of God" would be a meaningless sound.

473. But the reason man does not know this from any light of reason is that fallacies—arising from the trusted appearances of the body's external senses—shadow that light. That man feels no differently than if he lived from his own life is because the <term>instrumental cause: the tool or medium through which an action is performed</term> feels the <term>principal cause: the primary source or driver of an action</term> as its own, and therefore cannot distinguish between them. For the principal cause and the instrumental cause act together as one cause, according to a theorem well known in the learned world. The principal cause is life, and the instrumental cause is the mind of man. It appears as if beasts also possess life created within themselves, but this is a similar fallacy; for they are Organs created to receive light and heat from the natural world and simultaneously from the spiritual world. Every species is a form of some natural love, and it receives light and heat from the spiritual world mediately through heaven and hell—the gentle beasts through heaven, and the fierce ones through hell. Man alone receives light and heat—that is, wisdom and love—immediately from the Lord. This is the difference.

474. That the Lord is Life in Himself, and thus Life itself, He teaches Himself in the Gospel of John: *The Word was with God, and the Word was God... in Him was Life, and the Life was the Light of men* <note>original: "Verbum erat apud Deum, & Deus erat Verbum, in Ipso Vita erat & Vita erat Lux hominum"</note>, John 1:1, 4. In the same: *As the Father has Life in Himself, so has He given to the Son to have life in Himself* <note>original: "Sicut Pater habet Vitam in Se Ipso, ita dedit Filio vitam habere in Se Ipso"</note>, Ch. 5:26. In the same: *I am the Way, the Truth, and the Life* <note>original: "Ego sum Via, Veritas, & Vita"</note>, Ch. 14:6. ## ***That man, as long as he lives in the World, is held in the middle between Heaven and Hell, and there in a spiritual Equilibrium, which is Free Will.***

475. To understand what and of what quality <term>Liberum Arbitrium: free will or free choice</term> is, it is necessary to know where it comes from; by knowing its origin, one recognizes not only that it exists, but what its nature is. Its origin is from the spiritual World, where the mind of man is held by the Lord. The mind of man is his spirit, which lives after death, and his spirit is continually in company with those like himself in that world; yet through the material body which surrounds him, his spirit is with men in the natural world. The reason man does not know that he is in the midst of spirits as to his mind is that those spirits with whom he is in company in the spiritual world think and speak spiritually, whereas the spirit of man, as long as it is in the material body, thinks naturally. Spiritual thought and speech cannot be understood or perceived by the natural man, nor vice-versa, which is why they cannot even be seen. But when the spirit of man is in socie-

<note>original: "societate"</note> communion with spirits in their world, then he is also in spiritual thought and speech with them. This is because his mind is interiorly spiritual, but exteriorly natural; therefore, through his interiors he communicates with spirits, but through his exteriors he communicates with men. It is through this communication that a person perceives things and thinks about them analytically; if man did not have this, he would think no more nor differently than a beast. Furthermore, if all commerce with spirits were taken away from him, he would die in an instant. 

But so that it may be understood how man can be held in the middle between Heaven and Hell, and thereby in spiritual equilibrium—from which he possesses <term>Liberum arbitrium: free will</term>—a few things must be said. The spiritual world consists of Heaven and Hell. Heaven is there above the head, and Hell is there beneath the feet; yet Hell is not in the physical center of the Earth inhabited by men, but beneath the lands of that spiritual world, which are also of spiritual origin. Consequently, they are not in physical extension, but in the appearance of extension. Between Heaven and Hell there is a great <term>Interstitium: an intermediate space or interval</term>, which appears to those who are there like an entire world. Into this interval, evil exhales from Hell in all abundance, and from Heaven, in turn, good flows into it, also in all abundance. This is the interval of which Abraham spoke to the rich man in Hell: *Between us and you a great gulf is fixed, so that those who want to cross from here to you cannot, nor can those from there cross to us,* Luke 16:26. Every person, as to their spirit, is in the middle of this interval, solely for the reason that they may be in free will. Because this interval is so vast and appears to those there like a great world, it is called the **WORLD OF SPIRITS**. It is also full of spirits, because every person comes there first after death, and is prepared there for either heaven or hell. There, a person is in the company of others, just as they were previously among men in the former world. Nor is there a Purgatory there; that is a fable invented by the Roman Catholics. But that world is specifically dealt with in the work **HEAVEN AND HELL**, published in London in the year 1758, from numbers 536 to 603.

476. Every person, from infancy until old age, changes their location or position in this world. An **INFANT** is held in the eastern quarter toward the north there; a **BOY**, as he learns the rudiments of religion, successively moves away from the north toward the south; a **YOUTH**, as he begins to think from his own mind, is carried toward the south; and afterward, when he becomes of his own judgment and master of himself, according to his growth in things that interiorly regard God and love toward the neighbor, he moves from the south toward the east. But if he favors evil and absorbs it, he progresses toward the west. For all in the spiritual world dwell according to the quarters: in the **EAST** are those who are in good from the Lord, for there is the Sun, in the midst of which is the Lord; in the **NORTH** are those who are in ignorance; in the **SOUTH** are those in intelligence; and in the **WEST** are those who are in evil. The person himself is not held in that interval or center as to his body, but as to his spirit; and as his spirit changes its state by approaching good or evil, it is transferred to locations or sites in this or that quarter, and there comes into the company of the inhabitants. But it must be known that the Lord does not transfer the person here or there, but the person transfers himself in various ways. If he chooses good, then the person, together with the Lord—or rather the Lord together with the person—transfers his spirit toward the East; but if the person chooses evil, then the person, together with the devil—or rather the devil together with the person—transfers his spirit toward the West. It should be observed that where "Heaven" is mentioned here, it also means the Lord, because the Lord is everything in all things of heaven; and where the "devil" is mentioned, it means Hell, because all who are there are devils.

477. That man is held in this great interval, and continually in the middle of it, is solely for the sake of his having free will in spiritual things; for this equilibrium is a spiritual equilibrium, because it is between Heaven and Hell, and thus between good and evil. All who are in that great interval are, as to their interiors, joined either with the Angels of heaven or with the devils of hell; but today <note>Referring to the time of the "Last Judgment" in the spiritual world described by Swedenborg</note> they are joined either with the Angels of Michael or with the angels of the dragon. <note>original: "partem" (referring to the soul/spirit's part)</note> part, he betakes himself to his own in that Intermediate Space, and joins himself with those who are in a similar love; for Love joins everyone there with their like, and makes it so that he breathes his life freely and is in the state of his former life. But then, successively, external things are stripped away, which do not make one with his internal character. Once this is done, the good person is elevated into Heaven, and the evil person betakes himself to Hell, each to those with whom he makes one regarding his ruling love.

478. But this spiritual Equilibrium, which is <term>Liberum Arbitrium: Free Will</term>, can be illustrated by natural equilibria. It is like the equilibrium of a man tied around the body or by the arms between two men of equal strength, one of whom pulls the man in the middle to the right, and the other to the left; then the man in the middle can freely turn himself here and there as if not acted upon by any force. If he moves toward the right, he pulls the man on the left with violence toward himself, until the man on the left falls to the ground. Similarly if anyone, even a weak person, were tied between three men on the right and as many on the left of the same power; and similarly if between camels or horses. 

Spiritual Equilibrium, which is Free Will, can be compared with a balance scale, in each of whose pans are placed balancing weights; if then a little is added to the scale on one side, the axis of the balance vibrates above. It is also similar with a lever, or with a large beam placed upon its <term>hypomochlio: fulcrum or pivot point</term>. All and each of the things within man, such as the heart, lungs, stomach, liver, pancreas, spleen, intestines, and the rest, are in such equilibrium; it is because of this that each one can perform its functions in the greatest quiet. Similarly all the muscles; without such equilibrium, all action and reaction would cease, and man would no longer act as a man. 

Since therefore all things in the Body are in such equilibrium, even all things in the Brain are in a similar state, and consequently all things in the mind there, which relate to the will and understanding. Beasts, birds, fish, and insects also have freedom, but these are carried by the senses of their body, as appetite and pleasure suggest. Man would be not unlike these if his freedom of action were the same as his freedom of thinking; he too would then be carried only by the senses of his body as lust and pleasure suggest. It is different, however, for one who drinks in the spiritual truths of the Church and restrains his free will through them; he is led away by the Lord from lusts and evil pleasures, and the innate cravings for them. He seeks good and turns away from evil. This person is then transferred by the Lord closer to the "east" and at the same time to the "south" <note>In Swedenborg's spiritual geography, the East represents love and the South represents wisdom.</note> in the spiritual World, and is let into heavenly Freedom, which is truly free.

## *That it is clearly evident that man has Free Will in spiritual matters from the Permission of Evil, in which the internal man of everyone exists.*

479. That man has Free Will in spiritual matters must first be confirmed from common examples, and afterwards from particulars, which everyone will acknowledge at the first hearing. These common examples are: 
1. That the wisest of men, Adam and his Wife, allowed themselves to be seduced by the Serpent. 
2. That their first son Cain killed his brother Abel, and Jehovah God did not lead them away by speaking with them, but only by cursing them after the deeds. 
3. That the Israelite Nation worshipped the Golden Calf in the desert, even though Jehovah saw this from Mount Sinai and did not prevent it. 
4. That David numbered the people, and therefore a plague was sent, from which so many thousands of people perished; and that God sent the prophet Gad to him not before, but after the deed, and announced the punishment. 
5. That it was permitted to Solomon to establish idolatrous worship. 
6. And to many kings after him to profane the Temple and the Holy things of the Church.

480. **THE PARTICULARS** of how Free Will exists in spiritual things just as much as in natural things are innumerable. Let anyone consult himself, if he pleases, whether he cannot think seventy times in a day, or three hundred times in a week, about God, about the Lord, about the Holy Spirit, and about the Divine things which are called the spiritual things of the Church. Does he then feel any compulsion, even if he is carried toward it out of some pleasure, or even out of some desire, and this whether he has faith or no faith? Investigate also, in whatever state you are, whether you can think anything without free will, both in your speech and in your prayers to God, as well as in preaching and in listening. Does not Free Will carry every point in them? Indeed, without Free Will in each thing—even in the most specific details—you would no more breathe than a statue, for breathing follows thought and hence speech at every step. I say no more than a statue, rather than no more than a beast, because a beast breathes from a natural free will. Man, however, breathes from Free Will in natural and spiritual things simultaneously. For man is not born like a beast; a beast is born with all the attendant ideas of its natural love, concerning such things as nutrition and procreation. But man is born without innate ideas, having only the faculty for knowing, understanding, and becoming wise, and an inclination toward loving himself and the world, and also the neighbor and God. Therefore it is said that if Free Will were taken away from him in each thing that he wills and thinks, he would no more breathe than a statue; it is not said "no more than a beast."

481. That man has Free Will in natural things is not denied, but this is given to man because of his Free Will in spiritual things. For the Lord flows in from a higher or more internal level into every man with Divine Good and Divine Truth (as shown previously) and by this He inspires a life into man distinct from the life of beasts. To receive those things and to act from them, He gives man the <note>original: "posse et velle"</note> **ability and the will**, and He never takes this away from anyone. From this it follows that it is the Lord’s perpetual will that man receive truth and do good, and thus become spiritual, for which he was born. But to become spiritual without free will in spiritual things is as impossible as it is to thrust a camel through the eye of a sewing needle, or to touch a star in the sky with one's hand. That the ability to understand truth and the will to do it is given to every man—and even to devils—and is never taken away, has been shown to me by living experience. 

One of those who were in Hell was once lifted up into the <term>World of Spirits: mundum spirituum</term> <note>the intermediate state between Heaven and Hell</note>, and there he was asked by Angels from Heaven whether he could understand those things they were speaking with him (which were Divine spiritual things). He replied that he did understand. When asked why he did not receive such things, he said that he did not love them, and therefore he did not will them. Again it was said to him that he *could* have willed them; he marveled at this and said no. Therefore the Angels inspired into his understanding the "glory of reputation" along with its delight. Once he received this, he then also willed and loved those things. From these things it is clear that a person is human because of free will in spiritual matters; without it, a person would be a log, a stone, or the pillar of Lot’s wife <note>A reference to the biblical story in Genesis 19:26, where Lot's wife is turned into a pillar of salt for looking back at a destroyed city; here it symbolizes a human being deprived of spiritual life and movement</note>.

482. That a person would have no free will in civil, moral, and natural matters if they did not have some <term>Free Will: Liberum arbitrium</term> in spiritual matters is evident from this: that spiritual things, which are called Theological, reside in the highest region of the human mind, just as the soul resides in the body. They reside there because that is the "door" through which the Lord enters the human being. Below these are civil, moral, and natural matters, which receive all their life in a person from the spiritual things that sit above them. Because life flows in from the Lord from the highest points, and because human life consists in the ability to freely think, will, and from there to speak and act, it follows that free will in political and natural matters comes from that source and no other. From that spiritual Freedom, a person possesses a perception of what is good and true, and what is just and right in civil matters—this perception is the intellect itself in its essence. A person’s free will in spiritual matters is, by comparison, like the air in the lungs, which is drawn in, held, and let out according to every turn of his thought; without it, he would be in a worse state than one suffering from a nightmare, <term>strangulation: angina</term>, or asthma. It is also like the blood in the heart; if it began to fail, the heart would first palpitate and then, after convulsions, would stop entirely. It would be like a body in motion, which is carried along as long as there is <term>Living endeavor: Conatus vivus</term> within it, but both stop at the same time. So it is with free will, in which the human will resides; both free will and will together in a person can be called a "living endeavor," for when the will ceases, action ceases, and when free will ceases, the will ceases. If spiritual freedom were taken away from a person, it would also be comparable to taking the wheels from machines, the arms that catch the air from windmills, or the sails from ships. Indeed, it would be like a person who "gives up the ghost" <note>original: "spiritum emittit", meaning to die or breathe one's last</note> when he dies; for the life of a person's spirit consists in his free will in spiritual things. Angels groan when it is said that this Free Will is denied by many Ministers of the Church today, and they call the denial of it madness upon madness <note>original: "delirium supra delirium"</note>.

## *That without Free Will in spiritual matters, the Word would be of no use, and consequently the Church would be nothing.*

483. It is known throughout the whole Christian world that the <term>Word: Verbum</term> <note>referring to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible</note> is, in a broad sense, the Law, or a Book of laws, according to which a person is to live in order to obtain eternal life. And what is more frequently stated there than that a person must do good and not evil, and that he must believe in God and not in idols? The Word is full of commands and exhortations to these things, as well as blessings and promises of rewards for those who do them, and curses and threats for those who do not. To what purpose would all this be if a person had no Free Will in spiritual matters—that is, in those things which concern salvation and eternal life? They would be nothing but vanities that serve no use. If a person were stuck in the idea that they had no power and no liberty in spiritual things, and were thus separated from any power of the will in them, would the Sacred Scripture then appear to them as anything other than blank paper without syllables, or like paper upon which an entire inkwell has been thrown, or like mere dots and iotas <note>original: "apices aut jothæ", referring to the smallest strokes in Hebrew writing</note> without letters—an empty book? There would be no need to prove this from the Word, but because the Churches today have plunged themselves into an emptiness of mind regarding spiritual things, and have brought forth certain passages from the Word (which they have interpreted falsely) to confirm that emptiness, it is necessary to bring forward some passages which command a person to act and believe. These include: *The Kingdom of God shall be taken from you and given to a nation producing its fruits* (Matthew 21:43). *Produce fruits worthy of repentance, for now*

## *That without <term>Free Will</term><note>Latin: Liberum Arbitrium. The capacity to choose and act in spiritual matters.</note> in spiritual things, there would be nothing in a person by which they could join themselves to the Lord in return; and consequently, there would be no <term>Imputation</term><note>In theology, "imputation" is the process by which God credits righteousness or guilt to a person.</note>, but mere Predestination, which is detestable.*

485. It has been fully shown in the chapter on Faith that without Free Will in spiritual things, there would be neither charity nor faith in any person, much less a conjunction of those two. From this it follows that without Free Will in spiritual things, there would be nothing in a person through which the Lord could join Himself to them; and yet, without a reciprocal conjunction, no reformation or regeneration—and thus no salvation—is possible. That there would be no Imputation without this reciprocal conjunction of a person with the Lord, and the Lord with the person, is an undeniable consequence. There are many other consequences—and enormous ones at that—stemming from the proof that there is no imputation of good and evil without Free Will in spiritual things. These will be uncovered in the final part of this work, which deals with the heresies, paradoxes, and contradictions arising from the modern "imputative faith" regarding the merit and justice of the Lord God the Savior.

486. <term>Predestination</term><note>The doctrine that God has pre-determined from eternity who will be saved and who will be damned, regardless of their choices.</note> is the offspring of the faith of the modern Church because it is born from a belief in absolute impotence and a lack of any choice in spiritual matters. It arises from that, and also from the idea that a person’s conversion is like that of an inanimate object—that a person becomes like a "trunk" or a log, and thereafter, having no conscience, cannot know whether that "trunk" has been brought to life by grace or not. For it is said that election <note>The process by which God chooses "the elect" for salvation.</note> happens out of God's mere grace, excluding any human action, whether it proceeds from the powers of nature or of reason; and that election occurs where and when God wills, according to His good pleasure. Works, which follow faith as testimonies, appear to the reflective eye as similar to "works of the flesh," and the Spirit who works them does not reveal their origin, but makes them matters of grace or "good pleasure," just like faith itself. 

From this it is clear that the modern Church’s dogma of Predestination came forth from that faith like a shoot from a seed. I can even say that it flowed out as an almost unavoidable consequence of that faith. This first occurred among the <term>Predestinarians</term><note>A 5th and 9th-century theological movement emphasizing strict predestination.</note>, beginning with Gottschalk <note>A 9th-century monk whose teachings on "double predestination" (both to heaven and hell) were highly controversial.</note>, then later with Calvin and his followers, and was finally firmly established by the Synod of Dort <note>An international assembly held in 1618–1619 to settle the controversy over Arminianism; it solidified the "five points" of Calvinism.</note>. From there, it was carried into their church as the "Palladium" <note>A safeguard or foundational belief (referencing the statue of Pallas Athena that protected Troy).</note> of religion—or rather, like the head of a Gorgon or Medusa engraved on the shield of Pallas—by the <term>Supralapsarians and Infralapsarians</term><note>Factions of Calvinist thought debating whether God’s decree of predestination occurred before (Supra-) or after (Infra-) He foresaw the Fall of Man.</note>. 

But what could be more harmful to devise, and what more cruel could be believed about God, than that some of the human race are damned by predestination? For it would be a cruel faith indeed to believe that the Lord, who is Love itself and Mercy itself, would want a multitude of people to be born for Hell, or that myriads of myriads should be born devoted to destruction—that is, born to be Devils and Satans. And to believe that He did not, out of His Divine Wisdom (which is infinite), provide and still provides that those who live well and acknowledge God should not be cast into eternal fire and torment. Yet the Lord is the Creator and Savior of all, and He alone leads everyone, and He wills the death of no one. What, then, can be more monstrously believed or thought than that entire assemblies of nations and peoples, under His protection and under His very gaze, should be handed over by predestination to the Devil as prey to satisfy his greed? But this is the offspring of the faith of the modern Church; yet the Faith of the New Church abhors it as a monster.

...was done by so many chosen members of the Clergy in the <note>original: "Synodo Dordrechti"</note> <term>Synod of Dort</term><note>A famous international gathering of Reformed theologians held in the Netherlands (1618–1619) to settle a controversy regarding Calvinism and predestination.</note> in Holland, and was afterwards neatly written and published; so that I might not doubt it, some of those who were involved in the decrees of that Synod were summoned to me. When they were seen standing near me, I said: "Who, using any sound reason, can conclude in favor of <term>Predestination</term>? Can anything else flow from it but cruel ideas about God and shameful ideas about Religion? Can anyone who has carved <term>Predestination</term> into their heart through constant affirmations think of anything regarding the Church except that its teachings are vain, and likewise regarding the Word? And what can they think of God—who has predestined so many myriads of people to Hell—except that He is a tyrant?" 

When I said these things, they looked at me with a satanic expression, saying: "We were among those chosen for the Synod of Dort, and both then and even more so afterward, we confirmed ourselves in many things concerning God, the Word, and Religion which we did not dare to make public. But when we spoke and taught about it, we wove and twisted a web from threads of various colors, and over it we spread feathers borrowed from the wings of peacocks." 

But because they wished to do the same thing now, the Angels, by the power given to them by the Lord, closed the *External* parts of their minds and opened their *Internal* parts; and from these they were compelled to speak. Then they said: "Our faith, which we formed through conclusions—one following the other—was and still is this: 

1. That there is no 'Word of Jehovah God,' but only some windy thing breathed out from the mouths of prophets. We thought this because the Word predestines everyone to Heaven, and says that a person is only at fault if they do not walk the paths that lead there. 
2. That Religion exists because it must, but it is like a storm carrying a fragrant scent for the Common People; that it must therefore be taught by Ministers both small and great, and taught from the Word, because the Word is accepted. We thought this because where there is predestination, Religion is nothing. 
3. That the civil laws of justice are the real Religion; but that <term>Predestination</term> is not based on a life lived according to those laws, but on the pure good-pleasure of God, like a King with absolute power who chooses based only on a person's face. 
4. That everything the Church teaches should be exploded as vanities and rejected as trash, except for the fact **THAT GOD EXISTS.** 
5. That spiritual things, which are put up for sale, are nothing more than ethereal mists under the Sun, which—if they penetrate deeply into a person—induce dizziness and stupor, and make them a detestable monster before God." 

6. When they were asked about the Faith from which they deduced <term>Predestination</term>, and whether they believed it to be spiritual, they said it was something that happened to them, but that when it is given, they are like logs—by which they are indeed given life, but not in a spiritual way. 

After these dreadful utterances, they wished to withdraw, but I said to them: "Stay a little longer, and I will read to you from Isaiah." I read these words: *“Rejoice not, thou whole Philistia, because the rod of him that smote thee is broken: for out of the serpent's root shall come forth a basilisk, and his fruit shall be a fiery flying serpent”* <note>original: "prester volans"</note> (*Chapter 14:29*). I explained this through the spiritual sense: that by <term>Philistia</term> is meant a Church separated from charity; that by the <term>basilisk</term> <note>A legendary serpent-king. In Swedenborg's symbolism, it represents a deadly false doctrine.</note> that comes from the serpent’s root is meant its doctrine of three Gods and of an "imputed faith" applied to each person individually; and that by its fruit, which is a fiery flying serpent, is meant the idea that there is no imputation of good and evil, but only immediate Mercy, whether a person has lived well or poorly. 

Upon hearing this, they said, "That may be so, but from that Book you call the Holy Word, bring forth something regarding <term>Predestination</term>." I opened it and found this in the same Prophet, which agreed with the point: *“They hatched the eggs of an asp, and wove the spider's webs: he that eateth of their eggs dieth, and when one is crushed, a viper breaks out”* (*Chapter 59:5*). When they heard this, they could not endure the explanation; but some of those who had been summoned—there were five of them—rushed away into a Cave, around which a dark fire appeared—a sign that they had neither faith nor charity. 

From this it is clear that the "Synodal Secret" regarding <term>Predestination</term> is not only an insane heresy, but also a cruel heresy; therefore it must be rooted out of the brain so thoroughly that not even a single trace <note>original: "apex" - literally the tip or small mark on a letter.</note> of it remains.

488. It is a monstrous faith that God predestines humans to Hell. It can be compared with the cruelty of fathers among certain barbarian nations, who sacrifice their nursing infants...

## That without **Free Will** in spiritual matters, God would be the cause of evil, and thus there would be no **Imputation**.

489. That God would be the cause of evil follows from the modern faith, which was first hatched by those who held the Council in the city of <term>Nicaea</term><note>The Council of Nicaea (AD 325) was a gathering of Christian bishops that defined the nature of the Son of God in relation to the Father, resulting in the Nicene Creed.</note>. There, a heresy was fabricated and forged—which still persists—claiming that there were three Divine Persons from eternity, each one being God by Himself. Once this "egg" was hatched, their followers could do no other than approach each Person separately as God. They compiled a faith based on the <term>imputation</term><note>In theology, "imputation" is the idea that the merit of Christ or the guilt of Adam is legally assigned to an individual's account by God.</note> of the merit or righteousness of the Lord God the Savior; and so that no human might share in that merit with the Lord, they took away from man all **Free Will** in spiritual matters, and introduced a state of total helplessness regarding that faith. And because they derived every spiritual aspect of the Church from that faith alone, they declared a similar helplessness regarding everything the Church teaches concerning salvation. From this, dire heresies have sprung up, one after another, founded upon that faith and man's helplessness in spiritual matters. Among these is that most damaging doctrine of **Predestination**, which was discussed in the preceding article. All of these imply either that God is the cause of evil, or that God created both good and evil. 

But, my friend, do not put your faith in any Council, but put your faith in the **Word of the Lord**, which is above Councils. Consider what the Roman Catholic Councils have brought forth, and what the Protestant ones have produced, from which **Predestination**—that horrid viper—was drawn out. It might be thought that the **Free Will** given to man in spiritual matters was the intermediate cause of evil, and consequently, if such **Free Will** had not been given to him, man could not have transgressed. But, my friend, stop right here and consider: could any man, in order to be a man, have been created without **Free Will** in spiritual matters? If that were taken away from him, he would no longer be a man, but merely a statue. What is **Free Will** but the power to will and to do, and to think and to speak, in every appearance as if from oneself? Since this was given to man so that he might live as a man, two trees were placed in the Garden of Eden: the **Tree of Life** and the **Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil**. This signifies that, from the freedom given to him, he could eat of the fruit of the **Tree of Life**, or from the fruit of the **Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil**.

490. That everything God created was good is clear from the first chapter of <note>original: "Geneseos"</note> **Genesis**, where it says in verses 10, 12, 18, 21, and 25, *God saw that it was good*, and finally in verse 31, *God saw everything that He had made, and behold, it was very good*; and also from the original state of man in Paradise. But that evil originated from man is clear from the state of Adam after the fall, in that he was expelled from Paradise. From these things it is clear that unless **Free Will** in spiritual matters had been given to man, God Himself would have been the cause of evil and not man; and thus God would have created both good and evil—to even think that evil [comes from God] is a wicked thing. 

The reason God did not create evil—even though He implanted **Free Will** in spiritual matters in man—and the reason He never inspires any evil in him, is because He is **Goodness** itself. In this Goodness, God is omnipresent, and He continually urges and demands to be received; and even if He is not received, He still does not withdraw. For if He were to withdraw, man would die in an instant; indeed, he would crumble into nothingness, for man's life, and the continued existence of everything he consists of, is from God.

## THE NEW HEAVEN AND THE NEW CHURCH

The reason why God did not create evil, but man introduced it, is that man turns the good—which flows continually from God—into evil. This happens when man turns away from God and toward himself. When this occurs, the "delight" of the good remains, but it then becomes the "delight" of evil. Without this remaining delight, which acts as a kind of likeness of the original, man would not live, for delight constitutes the very life of his love. However, these two kinds of delight are diametrically opposed to one another. Man does not know this as long as he lives in the world, but after death, he will know it and perceive it clearly. For then, the delight of the love of good is turned into heavenly bliss, while the delight of the love of evil is turned into a hideous infernal state. From what has been stated, it is clear that every person is predestined for Heaven and no one for Hell; rather, a person consigns themselves to Hell by the abuse of their <term>Free Will</term><note>original: "Liberum arbitrium"; the capacity of a human being to choose their own spiritual path without being forced by God.</note> in spiritual matters. By this abuse, they embrace things that exhale from Hell. For, as said above, every person is held in the midpoint between Heaven and Hell, so that they may be in equilibrium between good and evil, and thus possess free will in spiritual things.

491. That God has granted Freedom not only to man, but also to every beast, and even an "analog" of it to inanimate things—each according to its nature—and that He provides good to all of them, but that objects turn that good into evil, can be illustrated by comparisons. The atmosphere gives every person the opportunity to breathe, and likewise to every beast and wild animal, and every bird, whether it be an owl or a dove; it also gives them the ability to fly. Yet, the atmosphere is not the cause of this capacity being received by creatures of opposite natures and dispositions. The ocean provides a home within itself and brings nourishment to every fish, but it is not the cause of one fish swallowing another, or of a crocodile turning that nourishment into the venom with which it kills a man. The sun provides all things with light and heat, but objects—which are the various plants of the earth—receive them differently: a good tree or a good shrub receives them one way, while a thorn or a briar receives them another; an innocent herb receives them differently than a poisonous one. Rain falls from the upper region of the atmosphere everywhere upon the lands, providing water to every little tree, herb, and blade of grass; and each of these applies that water to itself according to its need. This is what is called an <term>analog of Free Will</term><note>A "correspondence" or "similarity" found in nature. While plants don't "choose" in a human sense, they "freely" absorb nutrients through their natural structures as if choosing what they need to grow.</note>, because they absorb it freely through their "mouths," pores, and passages, which stand open in the time of heat. The earth merely suggests both the juices and elements, and the shrubs draw them in according to a certain likeness of thirst and hunger.

It is the same with humans: the Lord flows into every person with <term>Spiritual Heat</term><note>The divine influence of love.</note>, which in its essence is the good of love, and with <term>Spiritual Light</term><note>The divine influence of wisdom.</note>, which in its essence is the truth of wisdom. But man receives these according to his "turning"—either toward God or toward himself. Therefore, the Lord says, when teaching about love toward one's neighbor: 
> That you may be children of your Father, who makes His sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sends rain on the just and on the unjust (Matthew 5:45);
and elsewhere, that He wills the salvation of all.

492. To this I will add this <term>Memorable Occurrence</term><note>original: "Memorabile"; a common feature in Swedenborg’s writings where he recounts a vision or experience from the spiritual world to illustrate a point.</note>: several times I have heard voices sent down from Heaven concerning the good of <term>charity</term><note>Spiritual love and active goodwill toward others.</note>. These voices passed through the World of Spirits and penetrated into Hell, even to its very depths. In their progression, those voices were turned into things that were plainly opposite to the good of charity, and finally into things that were characterized by hatred against the neighbor. This is a sign that everything proceeding from the Lord is good, and that it is turned into evil by the spirits in Hell. The same thing happened with certain truths of <term>faith</term><note>Spiritual belief and understanding.</note>, which in their progress were turned into the falsities opposite to those truths. For the receiving form itself turns whatever falls into it into something that agrees with its own nature.
