## *That everything spiritual of the Church which enters in freedom, and is received from freedom, remains; but not the reverse.*

493. The reason why what is received by a person in freedom remains with them is because <term>Free Will</term><note>original: "Liberum"; the state of being able to choose or act without compulsion.</note> belongs to their <term>Will</term><note>original: "Voluntas"; the faculty of the mind that desires and loves.</note>, and because it belongs to the Will, it also belongs to their love. For it has been shown elsewhere that the Will is the vessel that receives love. Everyone understands that everything done in freedom is a matter of love, and that this is also a matter of the Will, when they say: "I want this because I love it," and conversely, "Because I love this, I also want it." However, the human Will is twofold: interior and exterior—or that of the <term>Internal Man</term> and the <term>External Man</term>. Therefore, a hypocrite can act and speak one way before the world, and another way with their close companions. Before the world, they act and speak from the will of their External Man, but with companions, they act from the Will of their Internal Man. But what is meant here is the Will of the Internal Man, where their ruling love resides. From these few points, it is clear that the interior Will is the person themselves, for there is the "being" and essence of their life; the <term>Understanding</term><note>original: "Intellectus"; the faculty of the mind that thinks and perceives truth.</note> is its form, through which the Will makes its love visible. Everything that a person loves, and wills from that love, is free; for whatever proceeds from the love of the internal Will is the <term>delight</term><note>original: "jucundum"; the pleasant feeling or satisfaction that comes from following one's love.</note> of their life. And because this is the very "being" of their life, it is also their <term>Selfhood</term><note>original: "Proprium"; a technical term in this context referring to what a person feels belongs to them or constitutes their unique identity, as opposed to what flows from God.</note>. This is why whatever is received from the freedom of this Will remains—it adds itself to one's selfhood. The opposite is true if something is introduced in a state of non-freedom; it is not received in the same way. But more on this in what follows.

494. But it must be well understood that the spiritual matters of the Word and the Church which a person absorbs from love, and which the understanding confirms, remain with them; however, civil and political matters do not remain in the same way. This is because spiritual things ascend into the highest region of the mind and take shape there. The reason is that this is the entrance for the Lord, with His Divine truths and goods, into the human being—it is like a temple in which He dwells. But civil and political matters, because they belong to the world, occupy the lower regions of the mind; some are like small outbuildings outside the temple, and some are like the courtyards through which one must enter. Another reason why the spiritual things of the Church live in the highest region of the mind is that they belong to the soul and concern its eternal life. The soul resides in the highest parts, and its nourishment comes from no other food than spiritual things. This is why the Lord calls Himself "Bread," for He says: *I am the living Bread, which came down from Heaven; if anyone eats of this Bread, they shall live forever* (John 6:51). In that highest region also resides the love of the person, which creates their happiness after death; and there also resides their <term>Free Will in spiritual matters</term> principally. From this, all freedom that a person has in natural matters descends; and because its origin is there, it communicates that freedom to all choices in natural matters. Through these natural choices, the love ruling in the highest parts takes up everything that serves its purpose. This communication is like the veins of a spring with its waters, or like the life-giving power of a seed flowing through every part of a tree, especially into the fruits, in which it renews itself. If, however, someone denies Free Will in spiritual matters and rejects it, they create another spring for themselves and open a vein there, changing spiritual freedom into merely natural freedom, and finally into infernal freedom. This freedom also becomes like the life-giving power of a seed, which passes freely through the trunk and branches into fruits, but fruits that are rotten inside from their very source.

495. All freedom that comes from the Lord is true freedom, but that which comes from hell and is found in a person is slavery. Yet it cannot be otherwise than that spiritual freedom appears like slavery to one who is in infernal freedom, because they are opposites. Nevertheless, all who are in spiritual freedom not only know, but even perceive, that infernal freedom is slavery. For this reason, the <term>Angels</term> feel an aversion to it as if it were a cadaverous stench, while those in <term>Hell</term><note>original: "Infernales"; those dwelling in the lower or hellish states.</note> draw it in as if it were an aromatic fragrance. It is known from the Word <margin>catchword: that...</margin>

496. The reason why that which is received in freedom remains is because the <term>Will</term><note>The faculty of the mind that drives desire and love.</note> of man adopts and appropriates it to itself, and because it enters into his love, and the love acknowledges it as its own and forms itself through it. This will be illustrated by comparisons, but because these are taken from natural things, "Heat" will be used in place of "Love." It is well known that through heat, and according to its degree of fertility, the "doors" are opened in every plant; and as these are opened, the plant returns inwardly into the form of its own nature, spontaneously receives its nutrients, retains what is suitable, and grows. The same happens with an animal; everything that it chooses and eats from the love of nutrition (which is called appetite), adds itself to its body and thus remains. The reason that what is suitable constantly adds itself to the body is because all things that compose it are perpetually renewed; that this is so is known, but to few. Heat also, in animals, opens all things of their body and causes their natural love to act freely. This is why in the time of spring and summer they enter into and return to the instinct of procreation and the education of their offspring, which happens from the utmost freedom, because it belongs to the ruling love implanted in them from creation for the sake of preserving the universe in its created state.

The reason that the freedom of love is illustrated by the freedom induced by heat is because love produces heat—which is evident from its effects, such as a person becoming "fired up," growing warm, and being inflamed as love is exalted into zeal or into the burning heat of anger. The heat of the blood, or the vital heat of humans and animals in general, comes from no other source. It is from this <term>correspondence</term><note>A central concept in Swedenborg’s philosophy where natural things perfectly mirror spiritual realities.</note> that bodily things are adapted through heat to freely receive those things toward which the love breathes. All things that are within a person are in such an equilibrium and consequent freedom. In such freedom, the heart drives its blood equally upward and downward, the mesentery its <term>chyle</term><note>A milky fluid containing fat droplets, drained from the small intestine during digestion.</note>, the liver performs its blood-making, the kidneys secrete, the glands strain, and so on; if equilibrium were to suffer, the organ would sicken and suffer from paralysis or <term>ataxia</term><note>Incoordination or lack of order in physical movement or function.</note>. Here, equilibrium and freedom are one. In the created universe, there is no substance that does not tend toward equilibrium, so that it may be in freedom.

### *That the Will and Understanding of man are in this Free Will; but that doing evil in both worlds, Spiritual and Natural, is restrained by laws, because otherwise society in both would perish.*

497. Who cannot think freely about God, the Trinity, Charity and the Neighbor, Faith and its operation, the Word and all things that come from it? And after learning <term>Theology</term>, about the individual parts of it? Who cannot think both for and against these things, and even conclude, teach, and write about them? From the mere observation of your own thought, you are able to reject and renounce that discordant and harmful heresy which today in Christianity has brought a lethargy upon the heavenly Doctrine concerning Charity and Faith, and thereby upon salvation and eternal life. The reasons why that Free Will resides in the Will and Understanding of man are these:

1. Because those two faculties must first be instructed and reformed, and through them the two faculties of the external man, which cause him to speak and act.
2. Because those two faculties of the <term>Internal Man</term><note>The spiritual or inner level of the human mind that communicates with heaven.</note> constitute his spirit, which lives after death and is under no law other than the Divine law. The primary requirement of this law is that man should think the law, perform it, and obey it as if from himself, though it is actually from the Lord.
3. Because man, as to his spirit, stands in the middle between Heaven and Hell, and thus between good and evil; consequently, he is in an equilibrium. From this, he has Free Will in spiritual matters (concerning this equilibrium, see above, no. 445 *and following*). Yet as long as he lives in the world, he is, as to his spirit, in an Equilibrium between Heaven and the World. Man then hardly knows that the more he recedes from Heaven and approaches the World, the more he approaches Hell; he knows this and yet does not know it, for the reason that he may be in freedom regarding this as well, and so be reformed.
4. Because those two, the will and the understanding, are two <term>receptacles</term><note>Vessels or containers designed to receive and hold divine influence.</note> of the Lord: the will is the receptacle of Love and Charity, and the Understanding is the receptacle of Wisdom and Faith. The Lord operates each of these in man’s full freedom, so that there may be a mutual and reciprocal conjunction, through which salvation occurs.
5. Because every judgment that happens to a man after death is made according to his exercise of Free Will in spiritual matters.

498. From these points, it follows that Free Will in spiritual things resides in the soul of man in all perfection; and from there, like a vein into a fountain, it flows into his mind—into its two parts, which are the will and the understanding—and through these into the senses of the body, and into speech and actions. For there are three degrees of life in man: the Soul, the Mind, and the Sensual Body. Everything that is in a higher degree is in a state of perfection above that which is in a lower degree. This is man’s freedom, through which, in which, and with which the Lord is present in man, and unceasingly urges the reception of Himself. Yet He never removes or takes away freedom, since—as was said above—anything in spiritual matters that is not done by man from freedom does not remain. Therefore, it can be said that this Free Will of man is the place where the Lord dwells with him in his soul. 

However, it is obvious without explanation that doing evil is restrained by laws in both the Spiritual and Natural worlds, since otherwise society could not subsist anywhere. But it will still be illustrated that without those external bonds, not only would society not subsist, but the entire human race would perish. For man is enticed by two loves: the love of ruling over everyone, and the love of possessing the wealth of everyone. These loves, if their reins were loosened, would rush onward to infinity. The hereditary evils into which man is born have primarily arisen from these two loves. Nor did Adam have any other desire than to become like God, which the evil serpent instilled in him, as we read. Therefore, in his curse, it is said that the earth shall bring forth to him thorns and thistles <note>original: "spinam & tribulum"</note>, *Genesis 3:5, 18*, by which is understood all evil and the resulting falsity. 

All who are enslaved to those loves view themselves as the only ones for whom and through whom all others exist. Such people have no mercy, no fear of God, no love of neighbor; consequently, they possess pitilessness, savagery, and cruelty, along with a hellish lust and greed for plundering and robbery, using craftiness and deceit to achieve them. Such things are not innate to the beasts of the earth; they kill and devour others from no other love than to satisfy their bellies and protect themselves. Therefore, a wicked man, viewed in terms of those loves, is more savage, more fierce, and worse than any beast. That man is such within manifests itself in seditious mobs, in which the bonds of law are loosened, and also in massacres and robberies when the signal is given for the freedom to exercise fury upon the defeated and besieged; from this hardly one person abstains until the drum is heard signaling that they must stop. From these things it is clear that if no fear of punishments from the laws restrained men, not only Society but the entire Human Race would be destroy—

### NEW HEAVENS AND THE NEW CHURCH

...[rem]oved. But all these things are removed solely through the true use of **Free Will** <term>Free Will</term><note>The Latin term used is *Liberum Arbitrium*, referring to the capacity to choose and judge for oneself.</note> in spiritual matters, which consists in directing the mind toward thinking about the state of life after death.

499. But this will be further illustrated through the following comparisons; for unless a certain kind of Free Will existed in all created things, both animate and inanimate, no Creation could have taken place. For without free will in natural things regarding beasts, there would be no choice of food conducive to their nourishment, nor any procreation and preservation of offspring; thus, there would be no beast. If such freedom did not exist for the fish of the sea and the shellfish at its bottom, there would be no fish or shellfish. Similarly, unless it existed in every little insect, there would be no silkworm to provide silk, nor any bee to provide honey and wax, nor any butterfly to play with its mate in the air, nourishing itself on the juices of flowers and representing the blessed state of man in the heavenly aura after he has shed his skin like a worm. Unless an analogue of Free Will existed in the soil of the earth, in the seed cast into it, and in every part of the tree that germinates from it—in its fruits and again in new seeds—there would be no plant life. 

If an analogue of Free Will did not exist in every metal and in every stone, both noble and common, there would be no metal, nor stone, nor even a grain of sand. For even these freely absorb the <term>ether</term><note>A subtle substance once believed by scientists and philosophers to fill all space and permeate all matter.</note> and breathe out their own native essences, rejecting what is obsolete and renewing themselves with new substances. From this comes the **magnetic sphere** <note>original: "sphæra magnetica"</note> around a magnet, the iron sphere around iron, the copper around copper, the silver around silver, the gold around gold, the stone around stone, the nitrous around nitre, the sulfurous around sulfur, and various spheres around every speck of dust on the earth. It is from this sphere that the innermost part of every seed is impregnated and its prolific growth is vegetated; for without such an "exhalation" from every little particle of the earth, there would be no beginning of germination and thus no continuation of it. How else could the earth penetrate into the innermost center of a grain sown with dust and water, except through what is exhaled from it? It is like the *grain of mustard seed, which is smaller than all seeds, but when it has grown, it is larger than garden plants and becomes a great tree* <note>original: "granum sinapis, quod minus est omnibus seminibus, cum autem excrevit, majus est oleribus, & fit grandis arbor"</note>, Matthew 13:31–32; Mark 4:30–32. Since, therefore, freedom has been implanted in all created subjects, each according to its nature, why should Free Will not be given to man according to his nature, which is to be spiritual? Hence it is that Free Will in spiritual matters is given to man from the womb until his final age in the world, and thereafter into eternity.

500. That God, without giving men Free Will in spiritual matters, could lead everyone in the whole world to believe in Him within a single day, follows as a supposed truth from a misunderstood <term>Divine Omnipotence</term><note>The concept that God is all-powerful; here, the author argues that power must operate according to "Order" rather than through raw force.</note>. Those who do not understand Divine Omnipotence may imagine either that there is no "Order," or that God can act just as easily against Order as according to it; and yet, without Order, no Creation was possible. The primary rule of Order is that man should be an "image of God," and consequently that he should be perfected in love and wisdom, and thus become that image more and more. God works this continually in man; but without Free Will in spiritual matters—by which man can turn himself to God and in turn join himself to Him—this work would be in vain because it would be impossible. For Order is that from which and according to which the whole world, with each and every part of it, was created; and because it is from that and according to...

# UNIVERSAL THEOLOGY

...since through Him all creation was made, therefore God is called **Order** itself. For this reason, it is the same whether you say "to act against Divine Order" or "to act against God." Indeed, God Himself cannot act against His own Divine Order, since this would be to act against Himself. Therefore, He leads every person according to that Order—guiding those who wander and those who have fallen back into it, and even leading those who resist it. 

If man could have been created without **Free Will** <term>Free Will</term><note>Latin: *Liberum Arbitrium*. This refers to the human capacity to choose and judge spiritual matters without being forced by God.</note> in spiritual matters, what then would be easier for the Almighty God than to bring everyone in the entire world to believe in the Lord? Could He not have instilled this faith in everyone, both immediately and mediately? He could have done so immediately through His absolute power and His irresistible operation, which is constant so that man may be saved; or mediately through the torments of conscience inflicted upon him, through deadly convulsions of the body, and grave threats of death if he does not receive it. Furthermore, He could have done so through the opening of hell and the presence of devils holding terrifying torches in their hands, or through the summoning of the dead whom they had known, appearing in the form of terrible ghosts. But to these suggestions, an answer is given from the words of Abraham to the rich man in Hell:

> *If they do not listen to Moses and the Prophets, neither will they be persuaded even if someone should rise from the dead.* (Luke 16:31)

501. The question is asked today why miracles do not happen as they once did, for it is believed that if they did occur, everyone would acknowledge the truth in their heart. But the reason they do not happen today as they did before is that miracles compel, and they take away free will in spiritual matters, turning a person from a spiritual being into a purely "natural" one <note>In this context, "natural" refers to someone who only believes what they can see or feel with their physical senses, lacking inner spiritual perception.</note>. Every person in the Christian world since the Coming of the Lord has the potential to become spiritual, and one becomes spiritual solely from the Lord through the Word. This capacity would perish if a person were forced to believe through miracles. As stated above, miracles compel and strip away free will in spiritual matters; and everything compelled in such matters forces itself only into the "natural" man. This shuts the door on the spiritual man—who is truly the **Internal Man**—and deprives him of any power to see truth in the light. 

Consequently, such a person later reasons about spiritual things only from the natural mind, which sees everything truly spiritual in reverse. The reason miracles were performed before the Coming of the Lord was that the people of the Church then were "natural," and spiritual things (which belong to the internal Church) could not be opened to them, for if they had been, they would have profaned them. Therefore, all their worship consisted of rituals that merely represented and signified the internal things of the Church, and these people could not be brought to perform those rituals properly except through miracles. 

Even then, miracles were not truly effective because an internal spiritual meaning resided within those representations. This is clear from the children of Israel in the wilderness. Although they saw so many miracles in Egypt and later that greatest miracle upon **Mount Sinai**, yet after only a month's time while Moses was away, they danced around the **Golden Calf** and shouted that it was the god who had led them out of Egypt. They did similar things in the land of Canaan, even though they saw the magnificent miracles performed by Elijah and Elisha, and finally the Divine miracles performed by the Lord Himself. 

Miracles do not happen today primarily for this reason: the Church has already taken away all free will from man by decreeing that man can contribute absolutely nothing toward receiving faith, nor toward conversion, nor toward salvation in general (see above, no. 464). A person who believes this becomes more and more "natural." As stated before, the natural man views everything spiritual in reverse and thus thinks against it. The higher region of the human mind, where **Free Will** in spiritual matters primarily resides, would be closed up. Meanwhile, spiritual truths, which had been seemingly confirmed by miracles, would occupy only the lower, purely natural region of the mind. This would leave false ideas about faith, conversion, and salvation sitting above them. The result would be that "Satans" <note>The author uses "Satans" to represent false or evil thoughts and influences.</note> would dwell above and "Angels" below, like vultures hovering over chickens. After some time, these Satans would break the barrier and burst with fury into the spiritual things placed below them; they would not only deny them, but even blaspheme and profane them. Thus, the final state of man would become much worse than the first.

It argues that miracles are no longer used because they compel the mind, potentially leading to the profanation of truth and a worse spiritual state for humanity.</summary>

# OF THE NEW HEAVEN AND THE NEW CHURCH

502. A person who has become merely natural <term>natural</term><note>In Swedenborg's theology, a "natural" person is someone focused only on the physical world and self-interest, lacking spiritual insight.</note> through falsehoods regarding the spiritual aspects of the Church cannot think of Divine Omnipotence in any other way than as something above order—that is, as a Divine Omnipotence existing without Order. Consequently, such a person might fall into these frantic thoughts: Why did the Lord come into the world, and why was Redemption achieved in that specific way, when God, by His Omnipotence, could have accomplished the same thing from Heaven as He did on earth? Why did He not save the entire human race through Redemption without exception? Why is the devil afterward able to prevail over the Redeemer within a person? Why is there a Hell? Could not God, by His Omnipotence, have destroyed it, or even now destroy it, or bring everyone out from there and make them angels of heaven? Why is there a Last Judgment? Could He not transfer all the "goats" on the left hand to the right and make them "sheep"? <note>This refers to the biblical parable in Matthew 25:31-46, where sheep represent the saved and goats the condemned.</note> Why did He cast down the angels of the dragon and the dragon himself from Heaven, rather than changing them into angels of Michael? Why does He not give faith to both these and those, and impute the merit of His Son, and thus remit their sins, justifying and sanctifying them? Why does He not make the beasts of the earth, the birds of the air, and the fish of the sea speak, give them intelligence, and introduce them into Heaven along with humans? Why did He not make the whole world a Paradise—or why does He not do so now—in which there would be no tree of the knowledge of good and evil, and no serpent, and where all the hills would flow with fine wine and produce both native gold and silver, so that everyone there might live as images of God in shouting and singing, and thus in perpetual festivities and joys? Would these things not be worthy of an Omnipotent God? These are but a few of the similar questions they might ask. 

But, my friend, all these thoughts are empty talk. Divine Omnipotence is not without order; God Himself is Order. Because all things were created from God, they were also created from Order, in Order, and for Order. There is a specific order into which man was created: his blessing or his curse depends on his **Free Will** in spiritual matters. For, as stated above, man could not have been created without Free Will—not even a beast, bird, or fish could exist without it. However, beasts possess only a natural Free Will, whereas man possesses both natural and spiritual Free Will simultaneously.

503. To these points will be added these **MEMORABLE RELATIONS**; **THE FIRST**: I heard that an Assembly had been summoned to deliberate on the **Free Will** of man in spiritual matters. This took place in the spiritual world. From every quarter there were learned men who, in the world where they previously lived, had thought about this subject; many of them had been present in the Councils and Synods both before and after the Council of Nicaea. <note>The Council of Nicaea (325 AD) was a landmark meeting of Christian bishops that defined early Church doctrine.</note> They were gathered in a certain round Temple, similar to the Temple in Rome called the **Pantheon**, which was formerly consecrated to the worship of all the gods, and later dedicated by the Papal Throne to the worship of all the Holy Martyrs. In this Temple, there were also structures like altars against the walls, but at each one were benches upon which those assembled rested themselves, leaning their elbows on the altars as if they were tables. 

No specific President had been appointed to act as the leader among them, but individuals, whenever the urge struck them, rushed into the center and poured out the "holy" thoughts of their hearts for all to hear. To my surprise, everyone in that Assembly was full of arguments confirming man's total impotence in spiritual matters; thus, they were mockers of Free Will. 

When they had gathered, one suddenly rushed into the center and breathed out these words in a loud voice: "Man has no more **Free Will** in spiritual matters than **Lot's wife** had after she was turned into a pillar of salt! <note>A reference to Genesis 19:26. The speaker argues that humans are spiritually inanimate or paralyzed without God's direct action.</note> For if man had any more free will than that, he would surely claim for himself the faith of our Church by his own power. Our faith teaches that God the Father gives it freely, out of His total Liberty and Good Pleasure, to whom He wills and when He wills. This 'good pleasure' and 'free gift' would in no way belong to God if man, by some choice or pleasure of his own, could also claim it for himself. For if that were so, our Faith—which is like a star shining before us day and..."

I stood by and listened to all these things intently, and because my spirit boiled over with indignation, I asked in a loud voice: "If you make a human being a pillar of salt, a beast, blind, and insane in spiritual things, what then are your <term>Theological teachings</term>? Are they not, each and every one, spiritual?" To this, after some silence, they replied: "In our entire Theology there is nothing at all spiritual that the reason can grasp. Our Faith alone is spiritual there; but we have carefully locked this away so that no one may look into it, and we have taken care that no spiritual ray may flow out from it and appear before the understanding. Furthermore, a person contributes not even a tiny bit to it from any choice of their own. We have also removed <term>Charity</term> from everything spiritual and made it merely moral, and the same for the Decalogue <note>The Ten Commandments.</note>. Regarding justification, the remission of sins, regeneration, and salvation thereafter, we teach nothing spiritual; we say that Faith works these things, but how, we simply do not know. In place of repentance, we have taken up <term>contrition</term>, and lest it be believed to be spiritual, we have removed it from faith as far as any contact is concerned. Regarding <term>Redemption</term>, we have adopted only purely natural ideas: which are, that God the Father shut up the human race under damnation, and that His Son took that damnation upon Himself, suffered Himself to be hung on a cross, and thus forced His Father to mercy—besides many similar things in which you will not find anything spiritual, but only what is natural."

But then, in the indignation I had previously conceived, I continued by saying: "If a human being had no free will in spiritual things, what would a human be then but a brute? Does a human being not stand out above brute beasts because of it? Without it, what is the Church but the black face of a <term>fuller</term><note>original: *fullonis*. A worker who cleans and thickens cloth. The metaphor implies a mask or a face darkened by soot or chemicals, sightless and grimy.</note>, in whose eyes there is a white cataract? What is the Word without it but an empty book? What is more frequently said and commanded there than that a person is to love God, and that they are to love their neighbor, and also that they are to believe, and that salvation and life are theirs, just as—"

504. THE SECOND <term>MEMORABLE RELATION</term><note>Latin: *Memorabile*. These are Swedenborg's accounts of things seen and heard in the spiritual world.</note>: I was in an interior spiritual vision, in which the <term>Angels</term> of the higher <term>Heaven</term> dwell, but I was then in the world of spirits; and I saw two <term>Spirits</term> not far from me, yet distant from each other. I perceived that one of them loved good and truth, and was thereby joined to Heaven, and that the other loved evil and falsity, and was thereby joined to <term>Hell</term>. I approached and called them together, and from their tones and responses I gathered that the one as much as the other could perceive truths, acknowledge them when perceived, and thus think from the <term>Intellect</term>; they could also determine intellectual matters as they pleased, and matters of the will as they liked. Consequently, both were in a similar state of <term>Free Will</term> regarding rational things. I observed, moreover, that from that freedom, a light appeared in their minds from the first sight (which was of perception) to the last sight (which was of the eye).

However, when the one who loved evil and falsity was left to his own thoughts, I noticed that a smoke, as it were, ascended from Hell and extinguished the light that was above the memory. This left him in a darkness there, like that of midnight; yet I also saw that this smoke, when ignited, burned like a flame which illuminated the region of the mind that was below the memory, from which he thought of enormous falsities derived from the evils of his self-love. 

But with the other, who loved good and truth, when he was left to himself, I saw as it were a gentle flame flowing down from Heaven, which illuminated the region of his mind above the memory, and also the region below it all the way to the eye; and the light from that flame shone more and more as he perceived and thought of truth from the love of good. From these sights it was clear to me that every person, both the evil and the good, possesses spiritual Free Will; but that Hell sometimes extinguishes it in the evil, while Heaven exalts and enkindles it in the good. 

After this I spoke with both, and first with the one who loved evil and falsity. After some talk about his lot, when I mentioned Free Will, he grew heated and said, "Ah, what madness it is to believe that man has Free Will in spiritual things! What person can take faith upon themselves and do good from themselves? Does not the Priesthood today teach from the Word that no one can take anything unless it be given from Heaven? And the <term>Lord Christ</term> said to His disciples, 'Without Me you can do nothing.' To which I add this: that no one can move a foot or a hand to do any good, nor move the tongue to speak any good. Therefore the Church, from its wise men, has concluded that man cannot will, understand, or think anything spiritual, nor even adapt himself to willing, understanding, or thinking it, any more than a statue, a stump, or a stone. They say that instead, by the good pleasure of God—who alone has the most free and unlimited power—faith is inspired. This faith, without any work or power of ours, through the operation of the <term>Holy Spirit</term>, produces everything which the unlearned attribute to man." 

Then I spoke with the other, who loved good and truth, and after some talk about his lot, when I mentioned Free Will, he said, "What madness it is to deny Free Will in spiritual things! Who is not able...

willing and doing good, as well as thinking and speaking truth, from oneself from the <term>Word</term><note>The Bible, which Swedenborg considers the direct source of divine truth.</note>, and thus from the Lord who is the Word; for He said, *Produce good fruits, and believe in the Light*, and also *love one another, and love God*; as well as *he who hears and does my commandments, he loves Me, and I will love him*; besides thousands of similar passages in the whole Word. Therefore, regarding this Word, if a person were able to will and think nothing—and from that, do and speak nothing—of what is commanded there; without that power in the human being, what would Religion and the Church be, except like a shipwrecked ship lying at the bottom of the sea? Upon the very top of its mast stands the pilot, crying out, "I can do nothing," while he watches the other sailors sail away in small boats with their sails set. 

Was not <term>Adam</term> given the <term>Free Will</term> to eat from the Tree of Life, and also from the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil? And because from his own Free Will he ate from this latter Tree, smoke from the serpent (that is, from Hell) entered his mind, because of which he was cast out of Paradise and cursed. And yet he did not lose Free Will, for we read that the way to the Tree of Life was guarded by a <term>Cherub</term><note>A celestial being acting as a guardian; here, protecting the inner sanctity of life.</note>; unless this had been done, he would still have been able to will to eat from it.

When these things were proclaimed, the other man, who loved what is evil and false, said: "What I have heard, I leave behind; I retain with me what I have put forward. For who does not know that God alone is alive and therefore active, and that man from himself is dead and therefore merely passive? How can such a one, who is dead in himself and merely passive, take unto himself anything living and active?" 

To this I replied: Man is an <term>Organ of life</term><note>In Swedenborg’s philosophy, humans do not have life "in themselves" but are instruments or vessels designed to receive and manifest the life flowing from God.</note>, and God alone is Life. God pours His life into the Organ and all its parts, just as the Sun pours its heat into a Tree and all its parts. God grants that man feels that life in himself as if it were his own; and God wills that he feel it so, for this reason: so that man might live as if from himself according to the Laws of order (which are as many as the commandments in the Word) and so dispose himself to receive the Love of God. And yet, God perpetually holds the plumb line with His finger over the balance and moderates it, but He never violates Free Will by forcing it. A tree cannot receive anything that the heat of the sun brings in through the root unless it grows warm and heated in every one of its fibers; nor can the elements rise up through the root unless each of its fibers, from the heat it has received, also gives off heat, and thus contributes to the passage. Similarly, it is with man from the heat of life received from God. But man, unlike a tree, feels that life as his own, even though it is not his. Yet, to the extent that he believes it is his own and not God’s, he receives the light of life, but not the heat of love from God; instead, he receives the heat of love from Hell. This heat, because it is thick and murky, obstructs and closes off the purer little branches of the Organ, just as impure blood clogs the capillary vessels of the body. Thus, man makes himself merely natural instead of spiritual. 

Free Will exists for man because he feels life in himself as his own, and because God allows man to feel it this way so that a conjunction may occur—which is not possible unless it is reciprocal. It becomes reciprocal when a man acts from Free Will exactly as if from himself. If God had not left this to man, man would not be man, nor would there be eternal life for him; for it is the reciprocal conjunction with God that makes a man a man and not a beast, and also ensures that he lives forever after death. Free Will in spiritual matters achieves this.

When he heard this, that evil Spirit moved away to a distance, and then I saw a flying serpent, which is called a <term>prester</term><note>original: "prester." A term for a "fiery" or "swelling" serpent, used here to symbolize a dangerous or deceptive spiritual state.</note>, upon a certain tree, which held out fruit from it to someone. Then I approached the place in spirit, and there, in place of the serpent, a monstrous man was seen, whose face was so covered by a beard that nothing was visible except his nose. In place of the tree was a glowing firebrand, by which stood the man whose mind the smoke had previously entered, and who afterwards rejected Free Will in spiritual matters. Suddenly, similar smoke came out of the firebrand and surrounded them both; and because they were thus withdrawn from my sight, I went away. But the other man, who loved what is good and true and asserted that man has free will in spiritual matters, accompanied me home.

### 505. THE THIRD MEMORABLE RELATION
Once I heard a grating sound like two millstones grinding against each other. I approached the sound, and it began to fade. I saw a narrow gate tending obliquely downward to a certain vaulted house, in which there were many chambers. In these chambers were cells, in each of which sat two people who were collecting proofs from the Word to confirm <term>justification by faith alone</term><note>The theological doctrine that salvation is achieved solely through belief, without the necessity of good works.</note>. One was collecting,

...one was [dictating] and another was writing, and this by turns. I approached one small cell that was near the door and asked, "What are you collecting and writing?" They said, "About the <term>Act of Justification</term><note>The specific moment or process by which a person is declared righteous by God.</note> or about <term>Faith in Act</term>, which is the very faith that justifies, gives life, and saves; it is the head of the doctrines of the Church in our Christianity." Then I said to him, "Tell me some sign of that Act, when that faith is brought into the heart and soul of a man." 

He replied, "The sign of that Act is in the moment when a man, struck by the pain of being damned, and while in that contrition, thinks of Christ—that He took away the damnation of the Law—and with trust he grasps His merit; and with this in his thought, he approaches God the Father and prays." 

Then I said, "So the act happens, and this is the moment." And I asked, "How am I to understand what is said about this Act—that nothing of the human concurs with it, any more than if he were a log or a stone? And that regarding that Act, a person can begin nothing, will, understand, think, work, cooperate, apply, or accommodate himself? Tell me, how does this hold together with your words—that the Act occurs when a man thinks of the law's right, of its damnation being removed by Christ, of the trust in which he grasps that merit, and in the thought of this approaches God the Father and prays? Are all those things not done by the human?" 

But he said, "They are not done actively by the man, but passively." 

And I responded, "How can anyone think, have trust, and pray passively? If you take away the active and cooperative power from a man, do you not also take away his receptivity? If you take away everything, including the Act itself, what is your 'Act' then, except a pure ideal, which is called a mental construct <note>original: "ens rationis"</note>? I hope you do not believe, as some do, that such an Act is only given to the <term>Predestined</term><note>Those supposedly chosen by God for salvation regardless of their actions.</note>, who know nothing at all about the infusion of faith within themselves; such people can play with these ideas and use them to wonder whether faith has been infused into them or not. 

Therefore, my friend, believe that a person, regarding faith and charity, works of himself from the Lord, and that without this operation, your 'act of faith'—which you called the Head of Church Doctrines—is nothing but the statue of <term>Lot's wife</term><note>In Genesis 19:26, Lot's wife is turned into a pillar of salt for looking back; Swedenborg uses her here as a symbol of spiritual lifelessness and fixation on dead doctrines.</note>, tinkling from mere salt, or scratched by the pen of a scribe or his fingernail (Luke 16:32<note>Though the text cites XVI:32, the reference to Lot's wife is found in Luke 17:32.</note>). I said this because you make yourselves like statues regarding that Act." 

When I said this, he took up a candlestick to throw it in my face with the force of his hand, but the light was suddenly extinguished and he threw it into his companion’s forehead, and I went away laughing.

## 506. Fourth Memorable Relation.

Two flocks were seen in the **Spiritual World**, one was of **Goats**, and the other was of **Sheep**. I wondered who they were, for I knew that the animals seen in the spiritual world are not animals, but are <term>Correspondences</term><note>A key concept in Swedenborg's system: outward appearances in the spirit world reflect the inner qualities or "affections" of the people there.</note> of the affections and the resulting thoughts of those who are there. Therefore, I approached closer, and as I approached, the likenesses of animals disappeared, and in their place men were seen. It was revealed that those who made up the flock of goats were those who had confirmed themselves in the doctrine of <term>Justification by Faith Alone</term>, and those who made up the flock of sheep were those who believed that **Charity** and **Faith** are one, just as **Good** and **Truth** are one. 

And then I spoke with those who had appeared as goats and said, "Why are you gathered like this?" Most were from the clergy, who boasted of their reputation for learning because they knew the secrets of justification by faith alone. They said they were gathered to hold a council, because they heard that the saying of Paul in Romans 3:28—*That a man is justified by Faith without the works of the law*—had not been correctly understood. They argued that by "Faith" there, Paul did not mean the faith of today's Church (which is in three Divine Persons from eternity), but faith in the Lord God the Savior Jesus Christ; and by "Works of the Law," he did not mean the works of the Law of the Decalogue, but the works of the Mosaic Law which were for the Jews. They said that from those few words, people had concluded two enormous falsehoods through a sinister interpretation: namely, that they understood the faith of today's Church and the works of the Law of the Decalogue. That Paul did not mean these, but the works of the Mosaic Law (which were for the Jews), is clearly evident from his own words to Peter, whom he rebuked for "Judaizing," even though he knew that no one is justified by the works of the Law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ (Galatians 2:14).

Because by the "works of the law" Paul understood the works of the Mosaic Law, he therefore distinguished between the Law of Faith and the Law of Works, and between Jews and Gentiles—or the Circumcision and the Uncircumcision. By "Circumcision," Judaism is signified, as it is everywhere else. He also concludes these points with these words: *Do we then make void the Law through Faith? God forbid; on the contrary, we establish the Law.* He says all these things in one sequence in Romans 3:27, 28, 29, 30, 31. He also says in the preceding chapter: *Not the hearers of the Law will be justified by God, but the doers of the Law will be justified* (Romans 2:13); then, *That God will render to every man according to his works* (Romans 2:6); and further, *We must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to what he hath done, whether it be good or bad* (2 Corinthians 5:10); besides many other passages in his writings. From these it is clear that Paul rejected "Faith without good works" just as much as James did in his Epistle, Chapter 2:17 to 26. 

That Paul understood the "works of the Mosaic Law," which were for the Jews, we are further confirmed by the fact that all the statutes for the Jews in the books of Moses are called "The Law," and thus are "works of the law." We see this from these passages: *This is the law of the grain offering* <note>original: "Minchæ"</note> (Leviticus 7:7, 11 etc.); *This is the law for the burnt offering, for the grain offering, for the sin and guilt offering, and for the consecrations* (Leviticus 7:38); *This is the law of the beast and the bird* (Leviticus 11:46 etc.); *This is the law for her that gives birth to a son or a daughter* (Leviticus 12:7); *This is the law of leprosy* (Leviticus 13:59; Chapter 14:2, 32, 54, 57); *This is the law for him that has a discharge* (Leviticus 15:31); *This is the law of jealousy* (Numbers 5:29, 30); *This is the law of the Nazirite* (Numbers 6:13, 21); *This is the law of cleansing* (Numbers 19:14); *This is the law of the red heifer* (Numbers 19:2); *The law for the King* (Deuteronomy 17:15 to 19). Indeed, *the entire book of Moses is called the Book of the Law* (Deuteronomy 31:9, 11, 12, 26; and also Luke 2:22; Chapter 24:24; John 1:46; Chapter 7:22, 23; Chapter 8:5). 

To these things they also added that they had seen in Paul that the Law of the Decalogue <note>The Ten Commandments</note> must be lived, and that it is fulfilled by Charity (Romans 13:8, 9, 10, 11), and that he says there are three: *Faith, Hope, and Charity, and that the greatest of these is Charity* (1 Corinthians 13:13), thus not Faith. They said they were called together because of these things. 

But so as not to disturb them, I stepped back; and then again from a distance they were seen like **Goats** <note>In this spiritual context, goats often represent those who separate faith from life or charity.</note>, sometimes as if lying down and sometimes as if standing, but they turned themselves away from the **Flock of Sheep**. They appeared as if lying down when they were deliberating, and as if standing when they were drawing conclusions. I kept my gaze fixed on their horns, and I was amazed that the horns on their foreheads now appeared as if stretched forward and upward, now curved backward toward the spine, and finally completely bent back. Then suddenly they turned themselves toward the Flock of Sheep, but they still appeared as Goats. Therefore, I approached again and asked, "What now?" They said they had concluded that **Faith Alone** produces the good things of Charity, just as a tree produces fruit. 

But then thunder was heard and lightning was seen from above; and soon an Angel appeared, standing between those two flocks, and he cried out to the flock of sheep: "Do not listen! They have not retreated from their former Faith, which is that Faith Alone justifies and saves, and that actual Charity is absolutely nothing. Nor is Faith a tree; rather, man is the tree. But perform repentance and look to the Lord, and you shall have Faith; Faith before that is not a faith in which there is anything living." 

Then the goats with the bent-back horns wanted to approach the sheep; but the Angel standing between them divided the sheep into two flocks, and said to those on the left: "Join yourselves to the goats, but I tell you that a wolf is coming who will snatch them away, and you with them."

But after the two flocks of sheep were separated, and those on the left heard the threatening words of the Angel, they looked at one another and said, "Let us speak with our former associates." And then the flock on the left spoke to the one on the right, saying, "Why have you withdrawn from our shepherds? Are not Faith and Charity one, just as the tree and the fruit are one? For the tree is continued through the branches into the fruit; pull anything away from the branch through which the tree flows continuously into the fruit, and will not the fruit perish, and along with the fruit every seed of some tree that was to be born anew? Ask our priests if this is not so." And then they asked, and looked around

And then one of the priests, who was among the sheep on the right <note>A reference to Matthew 25, where the sheep on the right hand represent the saved/charitable, and the goats on the left represent those without charity.</note>, stood up and said: "They have answered you that it is so, but to their own people they say it is not so, for they think differently." They then asked how they think, and whether they think as they teach. He said: "No; they think that every good of charity—which is called a 'good work'—done by man for the sake of salvation and eternal life, is not good in the least part. This is because a man wants to save himself through a work done by himself, thereby claiming for himself the justice and merit of the one Savior; they believe this is the case with every good Work in which a man feels his own will. For this reason, they assert that there is absolutely no conjunction of faith and charity, and not even that Faith is retained or preserved through good works."

But those from the flock on the left <note>referring to those who separate faith from charity</note> said: "You are telling lies against them! Do they not openly preach Charity and its Works, which they call 'Works of faith,' in our presence?" And he responded: "You do not understand their preachings; only the <term>Cleric</term> <note>original: "Clericus"; here referring to the ordained ministry who understand the underlying systematic theology.</note> who is present pays attention and understands. They think only of moral Charity, and its civil and political Goods; these they call 'works of faith,' though they are nothing of the sort, for an atheist can do those things in the same way and under the same form. Therefore they say unanimously that no one is saved by any works, but by faith alone. 

But let this be illustrated by comparisons: An apple-bearing tree produces apples; but if a man does good for the sake of salvation, just as that tree produces apples through a continuous process, then those apples are rotten inside and full of worms. They also say that a vine produces grapes; but if a man were to perform spiritual goods just as a vine produces grapes, he would produce only wild grapes." 

But then they asked what kind of goods of Charity or works they consider to be the 'fruits of faith.' He responded that perhaps they are inconspicuous, somewhere near faith, to which they are nevertheless not attached; they are like a shadow that follows a man from behind when he looks toward the sun, a shadow which he does not notice unless he turns himself around. "Indeed," he said, "I can say that they are like horse tails, which today are cut off in many places, people saying: 'What use are they? They serve no purpose, and if they stay on the horse, they are easily defiled.'" 

Upon hearing these things, someone from the left flock of sheep said indignantly: "There is certainly some connection! How else can they be called 'works of faith'? Perhaps the goods of charity are instilled by God into the voluntary works of man through some influx—such as through some affection, aspiration, inspiration, incitement, or excitation of the will, a silent perception in thought, and thence an exhortation, contrition, and thus a conscience, and then an impulse to action, an obedience to the <term>Decalogue</term> <note>The Ten Commandments.</note> and the Word, whether like an infant or a wise man, or through some other intermediary similar to these; how else can they be called fruits of faith?" 

To this the Priest responded: "No. And if they say that it happens through such a thing, they nevertheless stuff their speeches with words from which it results that these do not come from Faith. Some still hand down such things, but **AS SIGNS OF FAITH, BUT NOT AS ITS BONDS WITH CHARITY.** Yet some have devised a conjunction through the Word." And then they said: "Is there not a conjunction in that way?" But he responded: "They do not think this, but only through the hearing of the Word; for they assert that everything rational and everything voluntary in a man regarding matters of faith is impure and merit-seeking <note>meaning the person is trying to take credit for their own salvation</note>, because in spiritual things a man can no more understand, will, operate, or cooperate than a <term>stock</term> <note>original: "stipes"; a common theological metaphor in the 18th century comparing an unregenerate person to a dead log or stone pillar.</note>."

But when one heard that a man is believed to be such in all things pertaining to faith and salvation, he said: "I heard someone saying, 'I have planted a vineyard, now I will drink wine even unto drunkenness.'" But another asked: "Will you drink the wine from your own cup with your own right hand?" and he said, "No, but from an inconspicuous cup by an inconspicuous hand." And the other responded: "Certainly then you will not get drunk!" Presently the same man said: "But hear me, I pray: I say to you, drink Wine from the Word understood. Do you not know that the Lord is the Word? Is the Word not from the Lord?"

507. **THE FIFTH MEMORABLE RELATION.** I was in conversation with Angels, and finally, concerning the Lust <term>concupiscentia: an inherited, driving desire for evil things</term> for evil in which every human being is born, one angel said that in the world where he is, those who are in such lust appear to us angels like fools; yet to themselves, they seem supremely wise. Therefore, so that they may be drawn out of their foolishness, they are alternately sent back into it, and then into the rational state which they possess in their external selves. In this state, they see, acknowledge, and confess their insanity; yet they still long to return from their rational state into their insane state, and they cast themselves into it as if moving from what is forced and unpleasant into what is free and delightful. Thus, it is lust that delights them inwardly, and not intelligence.

There are three universal Loves <term>Amores: the fundamental motivations or affections that define a person's life</term> from which every person has been formed since Creation: *Love of the neighbor*, which is also the *Love of performing uses* <note>In this context, a "use" is any helpful service or good work done for the benefit of society or others</note>; this love is spiritual. Next is the *Love of the World*, which is also the *love of possessing wealth*; this love is material. Finally, the *Love of self*, which is also the *love of ruling over others*; and this love is corporeal. A person is truly human when the *Love of the neighbor* (or the love of performing uses) forms the Head, and the *Love of the World* (the love of possessing wealth) forms the Chest and Belly, and the *Love of self* (the love of ruling) forms the Feet and the Soles of the feet. 

However, if the *Love of the world* forms the Head, the person is not truly human except like a hunchback. But if the *Love of self* forms the Head, he is not like a man standing on his feet, but like one standing on the palms of his hands with his head downward and his buttocks upward. When the *Love of performing uses* forms the Head, and the other two loves form the body and feet in order, that person appears in Heaven with an angelic face and a beautiful rainbow around his head. But if the *love of the World* or of wealth forms the Head, he appears from Heaven with a pale face like a dead man's, with a yellow circle around his head. If, however, the *love of self* or of ruling over others forms the Head, he appears from Heaven with a fiery-dark face and a white circle around his head. 

To this I asked: "What do the circles around the heads represent?" They replied: "They represent intelligence. The white circle around the head of the fiery-dark face represents that his intelligence is in his externals, or around him, but insanity is in his internals, or within him. Such a man is wise while he is in the body, but insane while in the spirit. No man is wise in spirit except from the Lord, which happens when he is generated and created anew by Him." 

After these words, the earth opened to the left, and through the opening I saw a Devil rising up with a fiery-dark face and a white circle around his head. I inquired: "Who are you?" He said: "I am *Lucifer, son of the morning* <note>original: "Lucifer filius aurorae"; a reference to Isaiah 14:12</note>, and because I made myself like the Most High, I was cast down, as I am described in *Isaiah 14*." But he was not actually that Lucifer, though he believed himself to be. I said: "Since you were cast down, how can you rise up from Hell?" He replied: "There I am a Devil, but here I am an *Angel of light*. Do you not see my head bound with a white band? And also, if you wish, you will see that I am *moral among the moral, and rational among the rational, yes, even spiritual among the spiritual*;"

He said, "Against cheaters, against adulterers, and against all infernal loves; indeed, at that time I called myself Lucifer, the Devil, and I swore against myself as that character, and for that reason I was raised up to Heaven with praises. That is why I was called 'Son of the Morning' <note>original: *filius auroræ*, a reference to Lucifer in Isaiah 14:12</note>. And what surprised me myself was that when I was in the pulpit, I did not think otherwise than that I was speaking rightly and properly. But the cause was revealed to me: it was because I was in my 'externals,' and these were then separated from my 'internals.' And although this was revealed to me, I still could not change myself, because I had raised myself above the Most High and exalted myself against Him." Then I asked, "How could you speak like that when you yourself are a cheater and an adulterer?" He answered, "I am one person while in externals or in the body, and another while in internals or in the spirit. In the body I am an Angel, but in the spirit I am a Devil; for in the body I am in the <term>intellect</term><note>The faculty of the mind associated with thought and understanding</note>, but in the spirit I am in the <term>will</term><note>The faculty of the mind associated with desire and intent</note>. The intellect carries me upward, but the will carries me downward. And while I am in the intellect, a white headband veils my head; but when the intellect gives itself up entirely to the will and becomes its own—which is our final lot—then the headband turns black and disappears, and once that happens, I can no longer ascend into this light." But suddenly, as he saw the Angels with me, he became inflamed in face and voice and turned black, even as to the headband around his head, and through the opening by which he had risen, he sank back down into Hell. The bystanders, from what they had seen and heard, reached this conclusion: that a person is defined by his Will, and not by his Intellect, because the Will easily draws the Intellect over to its side and enslaves it.

Then I asked the Angels, "From where do devils get their rationality?" And they said, "It is from the glory of self-love. For self-love is surrounded by glory—for this is the splendor of its fire—and that glory elevates the intellect almost into the light of Heaven. For the Intellect in every person is capable of being elevated according to knowledge, but the Will is not, except through a life according to the Church and the truths of Reason. This is why even atheists, who are in the glory of reputation from self-love, and thus in the pride of their own intelligence, enjoy a higher rationality than many others—but only when they are in the thought of the intellect, not when they are in the love of the Will. The love of the Will possesses the Internal man, but the thought of the intellect possesses the External." Furthermore, the Angel explained the reason why man is composed of three Loves: namely, the love of Use, the love of the World, and the love of Self. The reason is so that man may think from God, even if it is entirely as if from himself. He said that the highest things in the human mind are turned upward toward God, the middle things there are turned outward toward the World, and the lowest things there are turned downward into the body; and because these are turned downward, man thinks entirely as if from himself, even though it is actually from God.

### 508. THE SIXTH MEMORABLE RELATION
One day there appeared to me a magnificent Temple of square shape, whose roof was like a crown, arched above and elevated all around. Its walls were continuous windows made of crystals, and the door was of a pearly substance. Inside, on the south side toward the west, was a pulpit <note>original: *suggestum*, a raised platform for speaking</note>, upon which on the right lay an open Word <note>The Bible</note> surrounded by a sphere of light, whose splendor circled and illuminated the entire pulpit. In the center of the Temple was a Sanctuary <note>original: *adytum*, the innermost holy chamber</note>, before which was a veil, but now it was lifted; there stood a Cherub made of gold with a sword vibrating to and fro in his hand. While I gazed at these things, the significance of each detail flowed into my meditation: namely, that the Temple signified the **New Church**; the door of pearly substance, the entrance into it; the windows of crystals, the Truths that illuminate it; the pulpit, the priesthood and preachings; the Word open upon it and illuminating the upper part of the pulpit, its internal sense (which is spiritual) now being revealed; the Sanctuary in the center of the Temple, the conjunction of that Church with the angelic Heaven; the golden Cherub within, the Word in the sense of the letter; the sword vibrating in his hand signified that this sense [of the letter] can be turned this way and that, provided it is applied to some Truth; and that the veil before the Cherub was lifted signified...

Afterward, when I approached closer, I saw an inscription above the gate, which read: NOW IT IS PERMITTED, which signified that it is now permitted to enter intellectually into the secrets of faith. From seeing this inscription, the thought occurred to me that it is very dangerous to enter with the intellect into the <term>dogmas of faith</term><note>established religious doctrines</note> which are fashioned from one's own intelligence and thus from falsities, and even more so to confirm them from the <term>Word</term>; for by this the intellect is closed above and gradually below, to such an extent that theological matters are not only loathed but even erased, just as writing on paper is destroyed by moths, or the wool of cloth by beetles. The intellect then remains only in political matters which concern one's life in the domain where one lives, in civil matters which belong to one's office, and in domestic matters which belong to one's own house. In all these things, a person continually kisses nature and loves her for the allurements of her pleasures, like an idolater loves a golden statue in his lap. Now, because the dogmas in today's <term>Christian Churches</term> are not from the Word, but from self-intelligence and therefore from falsities, and are also confirmed by certain things from the Word, therefore, by the Lord's Divine Providence, the Word has been taken away from the laity among Roman Catholics; and among Protestants, though it is open, it is still closed by their common saying that the intellect must be kept captive under obedience to their faith. 

But in the <term>New Church</term><note>Swedenborg's term for a new spiritual era and a new understanding of Christianity</note> the opposite occurs; in this it is permitted to enter with the intellect and penetrate into all its secrets, and also to confirm them by the Word. The reason is that its doctrines are continuous truths revealed by the Lord through the Word, and confirming them by rational means causes the intellect to be opened wider and wider above, and thus to be elevated into the light in which the angels of heaven dwell. That light in its essence is Truth, and in this light, the acknowledgment of the Lord as the God of Heaven and Earth shines in its glory. This is what is meant by the inscription over the gate of the temple, NOW IT IS PERMITTED, and also by the fact that the veil of the sanctuary before the Cherub has been lifted. For it is a canon of the New Church that falsities close the intellect, and that truths open it. 

After this, I saw what looked like an infant above my head, holding a paper in his hand. As he approached me, he grew to the stature of a medium-sized man; he was an Angel from the third heaven, where everyone from a distance appears like infants. When he was with me, he handed me the paper, but because it was written in cursive letters, such as they use in that heaven, I returned it and asked that they themselves express the sense of the words there in terms suited to the ideas of my thought. He reported that this was written there: ENTER HENCEFORTH INTO THE MYSTERIES OF THE WORD HITHERTO CLOSED, FOR ITS INDIVIDUAL TRUTHS ARE SO MANY MIRRORS OF THE LORD.

# CHAPTER NINE

### CONCERNING

# REPENTANCE.

509. After the treatments of <term>Faith</term><note>original: *Fide*</note>, <term>Charity</term><note>original: *Charitate*</note>, and <term>Free Will</term><note>original: *Libero Arbitrio*</note>, <term>Repentance</term><note>original: *Pænitentia*</note> follows in logical connection. This is because true Faith and genuine Charity are not possible without Repentance, and no one can practice repentance without Free Will. The reason Repentance is treated here is also because the subject of <term>Regeneration</term><note>original: *Regeneratione*; the process of being spiritually reborn or "born again"</note> follows; no one can be regenerated until the more grievous evils—which make a person detestable in the sight of God—are removed, and these are removed through Repentance. For what is an unregenerate person but one who is impenitent? And what is an impenitent person but one in a state of lethargy, who knows nothing of sin and therefore fosters it in his own heart, kissing it daily just as an adulterer might kiss a prostitute in his bed. But so that it may be known what Repentance is and what it accomplishes, this treatment is divided into Articles.

### *That Repentance is the First thing of the Church within a person.*

510. The community called the <term>Church</term><note>original: *Ecclesia*</note> consists of all those individual people in whom the Church exists. The Church enters into a person when they are being regenerated, and everyone is regenerated by abstaining from the evils of sin and fleeing from them, just as one would flee upon seeing infernal mobs with torches attempting to attack him and throw him onto a funeral pyre. There are many things that prepare a person during their early years for the Church and introduce them into it; however, the things that actually establish the Church within a person are acts of repentance. Acts of repentance are all those actions that ensure a person does not **will**, and consequently does not do, the Evils that are sins against God. For until this happens, a person stands outside of regeneration. At that time, if any thought of eternal salvation enters, the person turns toward it, but soon turns away; for it does not enter any further into the person than into the ideas of their thought, and from there it exits through the words of their speech, and perhaps through some gestures matching that speech. 

But when it enters the **will**, then it is truly in the person; for the **will** is the person themselves, because their love dwells there. Thought, however, is outside the person unless it proceeds from their **will**. If this occurs, then the **will** and the **thought** act as one and together constitute the person. From this it follows that for repentance to be true repentance and effective in a person, it must be of the **Will** and thence of the thought—not of the thought alone. Therefore, it must be **actual**, and not merely **oral**. That Repentance is the First thing of the Church is clearly evident from the <term>Word</term><note>original: *Verbo*; the Sacred Scriptures</note>. <term>John the Baptist</term><note>original: *Johannes Baptista*</note>, who was sent ahead to prepare people for the Church that the Lord was about to establish, preached repentance while he baptized. For this reason, his <term>Baptism</term><note>original: *Baptisma*</note> was called the "Baptism of repentance," because Baptism signified spiritual washing, which is a cleansing from sins. He did this in the <term>Jordan</term><note>original: *Jordanes*</note> because the Jordan signified introduction into the Church, being the first boundary of the land of <term>Canaan</term><note>original: *Canaanis*</note> where the Church was located. The Lord Himself also preached Repentance for the remission of sins, by which He taught that Repentance is the First thing of the Church, and that...

to the extent a person practices it, to that degree sins are removed within them; and as much as these are removed, so much are they forgiven. Furthermore, the Lord commanded the twelve Apostles, and also the Seventy whom He sent out, to preach <term>Repentance</term><note>original: *Pænitentiam*</note>. From these facts, it is clear that the first thing of the Church is Repentance.

511. Anyone can conclude from reason that the Church does not exist within a person until after their sins are removed. This can be illustrated by the following comparisons: who can introduce sheep, kids, and lambs into fields or woods where there are wild beasts of every kind, before he has driven the beasts out? Who can prepare a land overgrown with thorns, briars, and nettles into a Garden, before he has uprooted those noxious weeds? Who can establish a form of judicial administration and found a city in a Town occupied by enemies, before he has expelled those enemies? It is the same with the evils within a person; they are like wild beasts, like briars and thorns, and like enemies. The Church can no more cohabit with them than a person can live in a <term>Beastiary</term><note>A place where wild animals are kept; a menagerie.</note> where there are tigers and leopards; or no more than one can lie in a bed where poisonous plants are spread beneath the covers and stuffed into the pillows; or no more than one can sleep at night in a Temple under whose floor are tombs containing corpses—would not ghosts, like <term>furies</term><note>original: *furiæ*; in classical mythology, female spirits of vengeance; here used to mean tormenting or terrifying spirits.</note>, haunt him there?

## *That Contrition, which is said today to precede Faith, and which is followed by the consolation of the Gospel, is not Repentance.*

512. In the <term>Reformed Christian World</term><note>Referring to the Protestant denominations following the Reformation.</note>, a certain species of anxiety, grief, and terror is handed down, which they call <term>Contrition</term><note>original: *Contritionem*; a state of feeling remorseful and penitent.</note>. Among those about to be regenerated, this precedes their faith and is followed by the consolation of the <term>Gospel</term><note>original: *Evangelii*</note>. They say that this contrition arises in them from the fear of the just wrath of God and the resulting eternal damnation that is inherent in everyone due to <term>Adam’s sin</term><note>original: *peccato Adami*; the theological concept of Original Sin.</note> and the subsequent inclination toward evils. They claim that without this Contrition, the faith—which is the <term>imputation</term><note>The theological idea that Christ's righteousness is "credited" to a person's account.</note> of the merit and righteousness of the Lord the Savior—is not granted. They further teach that those who have attained this faith receive the "consolation of the Gospel," which is that they are <term>justified</term><note>Declared righteous in the sight of God.</note>—that is, renewed, regenerated, and sanctified—without any cooperation on their part. Thus, they are transferred from damnation into eternal blessing, which is life eternal. But regarding this "Contrition," we must weigh: 1. Whether it is repentance. 2. Whether it is of any importance. 3. Whether it actually exists.

513. **WHETHER THAT CONTRITION IS REPENTANCE OR NOT** can be concluded from the description of Repentance in the following sections: it cannot exist unless a person knows not only in a general way but also in specific detail that they are a sinner. No one can know this unless they examine themselves, see the evils within themselves, and condemn themselves on account of them. However, that Contrition which is preached as necessary for faith holds nothing in common with these things; for it is merely a thought, and a subsequent confession, that one was born into Adam's sin and into the inclination toward evils gushing forth from it, and that for this reason the wrath of God is upon them, resulting in deserved damnation, devotion to [hell], and eternal death. From this it is clear that this contrition is not repentance.

514. The second point is: since that Contrition is not Repentance, **WHETHER IT IS OF ANY IMPORTANCE**. It is said that it contributes to faith, as a preceding thing to a following thing, but that it nevertheless does not enter into that faith or join with it by mixing itself in. But what is the faith that follows other than that God the Father <term>imputes</term><note>Credits or assigns the merit of one person to another.</note> the righteousness of His Son, and then declares the person—who is not conscious of any sin—to be just, new, and holy? Thus, He clothes them in a robe washed and made white by the blood of the Lamb. When the person walks in this robe, what then are the evils of their life but like sulfurous stones cast into the depths of the sea? And what then is Adam's sin, but something either covered over or...
