...removed, or led away by the imputed justice of Christ; when a person walks from that faith in justice and then simultaneously in the innocence of God the Savior, what then does that Contrition serve, except for a confidence that they are in the <term>bosom of Abraham</term><note>A biblical expression referring to a place of comfort in the afterlife.</note>, and from there they look upon those not contrite before faith as miserable in hell, or as dead; for it is said that living faith is not in those who lack contrition; therefore it can be said that if they have plunged themselves, or do plunge themselves, into damnable evils, they pay no more attention to them, and loathe them no more, than piglets lying in the mud in street gutters loathe the stench. From these things it is clear that such Contrition, when it is not Repentance, becomes nothing.

515. The Third Point, which is to be weighed, is **WHETHER SUCH CONTRITION IS GIVEN WITHOUT REPENTANCE**; in the spiritual world I asked many who had confirmed in themselves the <term>imputative faith</term><note>The doctrine that Christ's merit or righteousness is legally credited to the believer.</note> of the merit of Christ, whether they had any Contrition, and they responded: "What is Contrition, when from childhood we have believed for certain that Christ by His passion took away all our sins?" Contrition does not square with this faith, for Contrition is to cast oneself into hell and to torture the conscience, when yet they know they are redeemed, and thus exempt from hell, and hence safe from harm. To these things they added that the decree of Contrition is nothing but a fiction which was accepted in place of Repentance, which is so often mentioned in the Word and also enjoined; that perhaps there is some emotion of the mind among the simple who know but little of the Gospel when they hear or think about the torments in hell; and they said that the consolation of the Gospel, impressed upon them from early youth, removed Contrition so that they laughed at it in their hearts when it was named, and that Hell could no more strike terror into them than can the fire of Vesuvius and Etna strike those who live in Warsaw and Vienna; nor more than <term>basilisks</term><note>Legendary reptiles said to have a lethal stare.</note> and vipers in the deserts of Arabia, or tigers and lions in the forests of Tartary, can strike those who are in some city of Europe in safety, tranquility, and peace; and that the anger of God no more terrified and crushed them than can the anger of the King of Persia terrify those who are in Pennsylvania. From these things, and also from reasons deduced from their traditions, I was confirmed that Contrition, unless it be Repentance, such as is described in what follows, is nothing other than a play of the imagination. That the Reformed assumed Contrition in place of repentance was also a cause for them to be severed from the Roman Catholics, who urge Repentance and simultaneously <term>Charity</term><note>In this context, active good works and love for neighbor.</note>; and after they confirmed justification through faith alone, they alleged the reason that through Repentance, as through Charity, something of the person which tastes of "merit" would enter into their faith and blacken it.

## *That oral Confession alone, that one is a Sinner, is not Repentance.*

516. Concerning this oral Confession, the Reformed who are addicted to the <term>Augsburg Confession</term><note>The primary confession of faith of the Lutheran Church.</note> teach thus: "No one anywhere can know his sins, therefore they cannot be enumerated; they are also internal and hidden, wherefore confession would be false, uncertain, lacking, and mutilated; but he who confesses that he is entirely mere sin, he comprehends all sins, excludes none, and forgets none. Yet still the enumeration of sins, although it is not necessary, is not to be abolished, on account of tender and fearful consciences, but this is merely a childish and common form of confession for the simpler and ruder folk." <term>FORMULA OF CONCORD</term><note>A definitive Lutheran doctrinal statement published in 1577.</note> pages 327, 331, 380. But this Confession was accepted by the Reformed in place of actual Repentance after they had separated themselves from the Roman Catholics, because it is founded upon their imputative Faith, which alone without Charity, and thus also without Repentance, works the remission of sins and regenerates the person; and also upon...

...by this, because it is an inseparable appendix of that faith, that there is no **Cooperation** of man with the Holy Spirit in the act of justification; and furthermore, that there is no **Free Will** in spiritual matters; and again upon this, that all things are of immediate **Mercy**, and not a whit is mediated by or through man.

517. Among many reasons why a mere oral **Confession** of being a sinner is not **Repentance** <term>pœnitentia</term><note>In this context, the author distinguishes between simply saying "I am a sinner" and the active process of self-examination and turning away from specific sins.</note>, is this: that any person—even a wicked one or the **Devil** himself—can cry this out, even with outward devotion, when they think of the imminent or present torments in hell. But who does not see that this does not come from any internal devotion? Therefore, it is a product of the imagination, and thus "of the lungs" <note>original: *pulmonicum*; meaning it is merely physical breath and speech</note>, but not of the will from within, and thus not "of the heart" <note>original: *cardiacum*</note>. For the wicked and the devil still burn inwardly with the lusts of the love of doing evil, by which they are driven like mills turned by storms. Thus, such an exclamation is nothing other than a scheme to deceive God or to trick the simple-minded for the sake of being delivered. For what is easier than to move the lips to shouting, to adjust the breath of the mouth to it, to lift the eyes, and to raise the hands upward? This is the same as what the Lord says in Mark: *Isaiah prophesied rightly of you hypocrites; this people honors Me with their lips, but their heart is far from Me* (Chapter 7:6). And in Matthew: *Woe to you, Scribes and Pharisees, because you clean the outside of the cup and the plate, but the insides are full of robbery and excess. Blind Pharisee, first clean the inside of the cup and the plate, so that the outside may also become clean* (Chapter 23:25, 26), and more in the same chapter.

518. Those who have confirmed in themselves the modern **Faith**—that the Lord through the Passion of the cross took away all the sins of the world—are in a similar hypocritical state of worship. By this, they understand the sins of every individual, provided they pray the formulas concerning **Propitiation** and **Mediation**. Some of these people can, from the pulpits with a loud voice and as if with burning zeal, pour out many holy things about **Repentance** and **Charity**, yet they consider both of these to be useless for salvation. For they understand no other repentance than oral confession, and no other charity than a public or legal one; but they do this for the sake of the people. These are the ones who are meant by these words of the Lord: *Many will say to Me on that day, "Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in Your Name and perform many miracles in Your Name?" but then I will confess to them, "I do not know you; depart from Me, you workers of iniquity"* (Matthew 7:22, 23). Once in the **Spiritual World**, I heard someone praying like this: 

> I am full of scabs, a leper, foul from my mother’s womb; there is no soundness in me from my head to the sole of my foot; I am not worthy to lift my eyes up to God; I am guilty of death and eternal damnation; have mercy on me for the sake of Your Son; with His blood purify me; in Your good pleasure is the salvation of all; I implore mercy. 

Those standing nearby, having heard these things, asked: "How do you know that you are like that?" He replied: "I know because I have heard it." But then he was sent to the **Scout Angels** <term>Angelos exploratores</term><note>Angelic examiners who investigate the true internal character of spirits in the afterlife.</note>, before whom he spoke similar things. After their investigation was made, they reported that he had spoken truths about himself, but that he still did not know a single evil within himself, because he had never examined himself. He had believed that after oral confession, evils were no longer evils before God—both because God turns His eyes away from them and because He has been appeased—and that for this reason he had not desisted from any of them, even though he was a deliberate adulterer, a thief, a deceitful slanderer, and a burning seeker of revenge. He was such in his will and heart, and therefore such in his speech and deeds, unless the fear of the law and the loss of reputation held him back. After it was discovered that he was such a person, he was judged and cast down to the hypocrites in Hell.

519. What such people are like can be illustrated by **Comparisons**: they are like Temples in which only the spirits of the **Dragon**, and those who are understood by the **Locusts** in the Apocalypse, are gathered; and they are like the pulpits there where the Word is not present, because it is placed under the feet. They are like plastered walls, where the plastering is beautifully colored, but inside which—when the windows are opened—owls and dire birds of the night fly about. They are like **whitewashed tombs** <note>original: *Sepulchra dealbata*</note> which contain the bones of the dead. They are like coins made from dregs...

## *That man is born to evils of every kind, and that unless he removes them in part through repentance, he remains in them, and he who remains in them cannot be saved.*

520. That every man is born to evils, so that from his mother's womb he is nothing but evil, is known in the Church; and it has become known for this reason: because it has been handed down by the Councils and the Prelates of the Churches that the <term>sin of Adam</term> <note>original: peccatum Adami</note> has been transmitted into all posterity, and that this is the only thing on account of which every man after him is damned along with him, and that this is what clings to everyone from birth. Furthermore, many other things which the Churches teach are founded upon this assertion, such as that the <term>Washing of regeneration</term> <note>original: Lavacrum regenerationis</note>, which is called <term>Baptism</term> <note>original: Baptisma</note>, was instituted by the Lord so that this sin might be removed; and that this was the cause of the Lord's Advent, and that Faith in His merit is the means through which it is removed—along with many other things which the Churches have founded upon this assertion. But that there is no hereditary evil from that origin can be established from those things shown above in number 466 and following: that Adam was not the first of men, but that by Adam and his wife is representatively described the first Church on this Orb; and by the Garden of Eden, its wisdom; and by the Tree of Life, its looking toward the Lord who was to come; and by the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil, its looking toward itself and not toward the Lord. That this Church was representatively described through the first chapters of Genesis has been proved from many parallel passages in the Word in the *HEAVENLY SECRETS* <note>original: ARCANIS CÆLESTIBUS</note> published in London. When these things are understood and accepted, the opinion hitherto cherished—that the evil innate to man from his parents is from that source—falls away, since it does not draw its origin from there, but from elsewhere. That the Tree of Life and the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil are within every man, and that their being said to be "placed in a garden" signified the <term>Free Will</term> <note>original: Liberum arbitrium</note> of turning oneself toward the Lord or turning oneself away from Him, was fully demonstrated in the chapter on FREE WILL.

521. But, my friend, <term>hereditary evil</term> <note>original: malum hæreditarium</note> is from no other source than from parents; not indeed the evil itself which a man actually commits, but the inclination toward it. Anyone will acknowledge that this is so, provided they join reason to experience; for who does not know that children are born into a general likeness of their parents in terms of their faces, manners, and minds? And even grandchildren and great-grandchildren into the likeness of their grandfathers and great-grandfathers, so that by this means families are distinguished by many, and also nations—such as Africans from Europeans, Neapolitans from Germans, the English from the French, and so on. And who does not recognize a Jew from his face, eyes, speech, and gestures? And if you were able to perceive the sphere of life flowing out from anyone's native disposition, you could be similarly convinced of the likeness of souls and minds. From these things it follows that man does not...

is born into these very evils, but only into an inclination toward evils, being more or less prone to specific ones. Therefore, after death, no one is judged based on any hereditary evil, but based on the actual sins which he himself committed. This is also evident from this statute of the Lord: 
> *The father shall not die for the son, and the son shall not die for the father; everyone shall die for his own sin,* 
Deuteronomy 24:16. This has been made certain to me in the <term>Spiritual World</term> <note>The realm where souls go after death, a central concept in Swedenborg's theology</note> from infants who die; they only incline toward evils, so that they will them, but they do not yet do them; for they are educated under the Lord’s protection and are saved. This aforementioned inclination and proclivity toward evils, handed down from parents to children and to descendants, is broken solely through a new birth from the Lord, which is called <term>Regeneration</term> <note>The process of being spiritually reborn and reformed</note>. Without this, that inclination not only remains uninterrupted but also increases through successive parents and becomes more prone to evils, and finally to every kind of them. This is why the Jews are still images of their father Judah, who took a Canaanite woman as a wife, and from adultery with his daughter-in-law Tamar, fathered three of their lineages; therefore, this hereditary nature has so increased among them over time that they cannot embrace the Christian religion from a faith of the heart. It is said that they "cannot" because the interior will of their mind is opposed, and this will produces the inability.

522. That every evil remains with a person unless it is removed, and that if a person remains in his evils, he cannot be saved, follows of itself. That no evil can be removed except by the Lord in those who believe in Him and love their neighbor can be clearly established from what has been previously discussed; especially from these points in the chapter on **FAITH**: *That the Lord, Charity, and Faith make one, just as life, will, and understanding do; and if they are divided, each perishes like a union crumbled into dust.* <note>original: "pollinem"</note> And from these points there: *That the Lord is Charity and Faith in man, and that man is Charity and Faith in the Lord.* But it is asked, how can a person enter into that union? The answer is: he cannot, unless he removes his evils in part through <term>repentance</term>. It is said that "man" should remove them, because the Lord does not do this immediately without the cooperation of man; this was also fully shown in that same chapter, and in the following one on **FREE WILL**.

523. It is maintained that no one can fulfill the Law, and even less so because he who transgresses against one commandment of the <term>Decalogue</term> <note>The Ten Commandments</note> transgresses against all. However, this form of speaking is not exactly as it sounds; for it must be understood thus: that he who acts from purpose or from a confirmed habit against one commandment, acts against the rest, because to act from purpose and confirmation is to utterly deny that it is a sin, and if it is said to be one, to reject it as nothing. And he who so denies and rejects sin, thinks nothing of everything that is called sin. Those who do not want to hear anything about Repentance fall into this category. Conversely, those who have removed some evils which are sins through repentance come into the purpose of believing in the Lord and loving the neighbor; these are held by the Lord in the purpose of abstaining from more sins. Therefore, if these people sin out of ignorance or from some overpowering lust, it is not imputed to them, because they did not intend it for themselves, nor do they confirm it within themselves. This can be confirmed by the following: in the Spiritual World I met many who in the Natural World had lived similarly to others, dressing splendidly, feasting sumptuously, trading with interest <note>original: "fænore," likely referring to usury or standard business profit</note> like others, watching theatrical plays, joking about lovers as if from lust, and other similar things. Yet the Angels blamed those things as evils of sin for some, and for others they did not blame them as evils, and declared the latter innocent and the former guilty. To the question of why this was so, since they had done the same things, the Angels replied that they view everyone from purpose, intention, and end, and distinguish them according to these; and that therefore they excuse or condemn those whom the "end" <note>The ultimate goal or motivation</note> either excuses or condemns, since the end of good is in all who are in Heaven, and the end of evil is in all who are in Hell.

524. But these things shall be illustrated by Comparisons; with sins retained in a per—

[An] impenitent man [can be compared] to someone with various diseases, where if medicines are not applied to remove the malignant parts, the person dies. This is especially true of the disease called gangrene, which if not cured in time, spreads and leads to unavoidable death. It is similar with boils and abscesses: unless they are lanced and opened, they lead to <term>empyemas</term> <note>Internal collections of pus</note> which spill into neighboring areas, then into the connected internal organs, and finally into the heart, causing death. He can also be compared to tigers, leopards, lions, wolves, and foxes, which unless kept in cages or bound with chains or ropes, would attack the herd and flock—and the fox, the chickens—and slaughter them. Also to poisonous snakes, which unless held down with pegs or their teeth removed, would inflict lethal bites on a person. An entire flock, if left in fields where there are poisonous plants, would perish unless led away by the shepherd into safe pastures. Even the <term>silkworm</term> <note>original: "bombyx"</note> would perish, and thus all silk would be lost, if foreign worms were not shaken off the leaves of its tree. He can also be compared to grain in barns or houses, which would become moldy and rancid and thus useless if air were not allowed to pass through to remove the damage. A fire, unless extinguished at the very start, would devastate an entire city or forest. A garden would be completely overtaken by briars, thistles, and thorns unless they were pulled up. Master gardeners know that as long as a bad tree brings its bad sap from the seed and root into the trunk of a good tree that has been grafted or budded onto it, those bad juices that enter are turned into good juices and produce useful fruit. A similar thing happens to a person through the removal of evil by means of repentance; for through this, a person is grafted into the Lord like a branch of the Vine, and bears good fruit, John 15:4, 5, 6.

### *That the knowledge of sin, and the examination of oneself, begins repentance.*

525. Knowledge of sin cannot be lacking to anyone in the Christian world; for everyone there is instructed from infancy about what is evil, and from childhood about what the evil of sin is. All youths learn this from parents and teachers, and also from the <term>Decalogue</term> <note>The Ten Commandments</note>, which is the introductory book for everyone in the Christian world; later on, in their progress, from sermons in churches and instructions at home; and in fullness from the Word; and moreover from civil laws of justice, which teach things similar to the Decalogue and the Word elsewhere. For the evil of sin is nothing other than evil against one's neighbor, and evil against one's neighbor is also evil against God, which is sin. But the knowledge of sin does nothing unless a person examines the acts of his own life and sees whether he has done any such thing in secret or in public. Before this, all that knowledge is merely theoretical, and then what the preacher says is just a sound in the left ear that passes out through the right and vanishes. Eventually, it becomes merely something thought about—a "devotion of the lungs" <note>An expression meaning empty words or superficial piety</note>—and for many, something imaginary and delusional. But it is quite different if a person examines himself according to his knowledge of what sin is, and finds something in himself, and says to himself, "this evil is a sin," and refrains from it out of fear of eternal punishment. Then for the first time, the instructive and eloquent preaching in the churches is received with both ears, and is taken into the heart, and the person changes from a pagan into a Christian.

526. What could be better known in the whole Christian world than that it is necessary for a person to examine himself? For everywhere, in empires and kingdoms devoted to both the Roman Catholic and the <term>Evangelical</term> <note>Protestant</note> religions, before approaching the Holy Supper, people are taught and warned to examine themselves, and to know and acknowledge their sins, and to live a new and different life. And this is done with fearsome warnings in the domains of England, where the following is read and proclaimed by the priest from the altar during the prayer preceding the Communion: "This is the way..."

> "And this is the means by which one becomes a worthy participant in the **Holy Supper**: the primary requirement is that he examines the deeds and dealings of his life according to the standard of God’s commandments; and in whatever ways he notices he has offended—whether in will, speech, or deed—he should then lament his own fallen nature and make confession before Almighty God, with a full purpose of amending his life. And if he notices that such offenses are not only against God but also against his neighbor, he shall then reconcile himself to him, and be ready to make restitution and satisfaction to the best of his power for the injuries and evils done to anyone; and likewise, he shall be ready to forgive others’ offenses, just as he wishes his own offenses to be forgiven by God. Otherwise, the reception of **Holy Communion** does nothing but increase his damnation. Therefore, if any of you is a blasphemer of God, a slanderer or mocker of His Word, an adulterer, or is in a state of malice or ill-will, or any other enormous crime, repent of your sin; if not, do not approach the Holy Communion, lest after receiving it, the devil enter into you, as he entered into Judas, and fill you with all iniquity, and destroy both body and soul." <note>This quoted passage mirrors the traditional exhortations found in the liturgy of the Lord's Supper, specifically emphasizing the danger of "unworthy" participation.</note>

527. Yet there are still some who cannot examine themselves, such as infants and young children before they reach an age where they become capable of their own insight; likewise the simple-minded, who are incapable of reflection; also all those who lack the fear of God; and besides these, some who are sick in mind and body. Furthermore, there are those who, having been confirmed in the doctrine of <term>justification by faith alone</term> <note>The theological belief that salvation is achieved solely through belief in Christ's merit, without the necessity of human works</note>, have persuaded themselves that through self-examination and the resulting repentance, something of the human self might enter in, which would undermine faith and thus cast salvation out of its only proper place. For all of these, a spoken confession serves the purpose, though it has been shown earlier in this chapter that such a confession is not the same as actual repentance. 

But those who know what sin is—and even more so those who know much from the Word and teach it to others—and yet do not examine themselves and therefore see no sin in themselves, may be compared to those who scrape together wealth and hide it away in chests and boxes for no other use than to look at it and count it. They are like those who collect <term>jewelry</term> <note>original: "Clenodia," meaning precious ornaments or treasures</note> of gold and silver in a treasury and lock them in cellars for the sole purpose of being wealthy. They are like the businessman who hid his <term>talent</term> <note>A unit of currency in the Bible</note> in the earth, or the one who hid his <term>mina</term> in a cloth (Matthew 25:25; Luke 19:20). They are also like the hard paths and rocks upon which the seed falls (Matthew 13:4), and like fig trees overflowing with leaves but bearing no fruit (Mark 11:12). They have hearts of adamant that do not become hearts of flesh (Zechariah 7:12). They are *like partridges that gather what they did not hatch; they acquire riches but not with judgment; in the midst of their days they leave them behind, and in their end, they become fools* (Jeremiah 17:11). They are like the five virgins who had lamps but no oil (Matthew 25:1–12). 

Those who draw much from the Word concerning charity and repentance, and know the commandments in abundance, yet do not live according to them, may be compared to gluttons who cram food into their mouths in large chunks and swallow it into the stomach without chewing it with their teeth; there it remains undigested, and the fluids squeezed from it contaminate the <term>chyle</term> <note>A milky fluid of fat and lymph formed during digestion</note>, leading to slow-acting diseases from which they eventually die miserably. Because such people are without spiritual heat, no matter how much light they are in, they might be called winters, frozen lands, arctic climates—even snow and ice.

## *That actual Repentance consists in examining oneself, knowing and acknowledging one's sins, supplicating the Lord, and beginning a new life.*

528. That repentance is absolutely necessary, and that a person's salvation depends upon it, is evident from many places and plain statements of the Lord in the Word <note>Swedenborg uses "the Word" to refer specifically to the Sacred Scriptures (the Bible).</note>, of which the following are here cited: *John preached the baptism of repentance, and said, bring forth fruits worthy of repentance,* Luke 3:3, 8; Mark 1:4. *Jesus began to preach and to say, Repent,* Matthew 4:17. *And He said, because the Kingdom of God is at hand, repent,* Mark 1:14, 15. Also, *Unless you repent, you will all perish,* Luke 13:5. *Jesus commanded His disciples that repentance and the remission of sins should be preached in His Name to all nations,* Luke 24:47; Mark 6:12. *Therefore Peter preached repentance and baptism in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins,* Acts 2:38; *and also said, Repent and be converted, so that your sins may be blotted out,* Acts 3:19. *Paul preached to everyone everywhere that they should repent,* Acts 17:30. *Paul also in Damascus, in Jerusalem, throughout the whole region of Judea, and to the nations, announced that they should repent and turn to God, and do works worthy of repentance,* Acts 26:20. *And also testified both to Jews and Greeks of repentance toward God, and faith in the Lord Jesus Christ,* Acts 20:21. *The Lord said to the church in Ephesus, I have this against you, that you have left your first charity; repent, or else I will remove your lampstand out of its place, unless you repent,* Revelation 2:2, 4, 5. *To the church in Pergamum, I know your works; repent,* Revelation 2:16. *To the church in Thyatira, I will deliver her into affliction if she does not repent of her works,* Revelation 2:19, 22, 23. *To the church of the Laodiceans, I know your works; be zealous and repent,* Revelation 3:15, 19. *There is joy in Heaven over one sinner who repents,* Luke 15:7; besides elsewhere. From these passages it is clear that repentance is absolutely necessary; but what kind it is and how it is done will be revealed in what follows.

529. Who cannot understand, from the reason given to him, that repentance does not consist merely in confessing with the mouth that one is a sinner, and speaking many things about it, like the hypocrite mentioned above in number 518? For what is easier for a person when they are in distress and agony than to breathe out from the lungs, and then pour out sighs and groans through the lips, and also to beat the breast and make oneself guilty of all sins, when nevertheless they are not conscious of any sin within themselves? Does the diabolical crowd <note>The author uses "diabolical crowd" or "horde" to describe the collective of evil spirits and selfish desires that inhabit an unrepentant person's internal life.</note> that resides in his loves depart at the same time as that sigh? Does it not rather hiss at those sighs and remain in him as before, as if in its own home? From this it is clear that such repentance is not what is meant in the Word, but rather a repentance from evil works, as it is called.

530. It is asked, therefore, how repentance is to be performed. The answer is: *actually*. And this is: to examine oneself, to know and acknowledge one's sins, to pray to the Lord, and to begin a new life. It was shown in the preceding article that repentance is not possible without self-examination; but what is the purpose of examination unless one might know his sins? And what is the purpose of knowing them unless he acknowledges that they are within him? And what is the purpose of those three things, unless he confesses them before the Lord and prays for help, and from this begins a new life, which is the end or goal for which the rest exists? This is actual repentance. That one must proceed and act in this way can be known by every person after their first years of life, and more and more as they become their own master and reach their own use of reason after Baptism <note>Swedenborg views Baptism as a symbolic "washing" representing the internal process of regeneration or spiritual rebirth.</note>, through whose washing is understood Regeneration; for in that rite, the godparents for...

<summary>This page establishes that true repentance is not mere oral confession or emotional display, but a four-step active process: self-examination, recognition of specific sins, prayer for divine aid, and the commencement of a new life.</summary>

they promised in that <note>original: "illo," referring to the rite of baptism mentioned on the previous page</note> that they would reject the devil and all his works. Likewise, this is clear from the Holy Supper <note>The sacrament of Communion</note>, before whose worthy attendance all are pre-warned to perform repentance for their sins, turn themselves to God, and enter into a new life. It is also evident from the <term>Decalogue</term> <note>The Ten Commandments</note> or Catechism, which is in the hands of all Christians; in the six commandments of the Decalogue, nothing else is commanded but that they should not do evil things. Unless someone removes these evils through repentance, they cannot love their neighbor, and much less God; yet upon these two commandments hang the Law and the Prophets—that is, the Word, and therefore salvation. <term>Actual repentance</term> <note>Repentance performed through specific, conscious actions rather than just a general feeling of regret</note>, if it is performed at alternating intervals—namely, as often as a person prepares themselves for the communion of the Holy Supper—is sufficient to initiate one into a state of active spirituality. If, after such preparation, a person abstains from one or another sin which they then discover in themselves, they are on the way to Heaven; for then a person begins to become spiritual instead of natural, and to be born anew from the Lord.

531. This can be illustrated through the following comparisons: A person before repentance is like a desert in which there are terrifying wild beasts, dragons, owls, vipers, and venomous serpents, and in the thickets there are <term>ochim</term> and <term>tziim</term> <note>original Hebrew: "אֹחִים" (ochim) and "צִיִּים" (tziim). These are terms from Isaiah 13:21 referring to "howling creatures" and "desert dwellers" or "wild cats."</note>, and where satyrs dance. But after these are cast out by human industry and labor, that desert can be plowed and cultivated into fields, and be sown first with oats, beans, and flax, and afterward with barley and wheat. It can also be compared with the wickedness that reigns in abundance among men; unless the malicious were corrected and punished by lashes or death according to the laws, no city could stand, nor likewise any kingdom. A human being is like a society in its smallest form; unless they acted toward themselves in a spiritual way, just as the malicious are dealt with in a large society in a natural way, they would be corrected and punished after death. This would continue until they no longer did evil out of fear of punishment, although they could never be brought to do good out of a love for what is good.

### *That true Repentance is to explore not only the acts of one's life, but also the intentions of one's will.*

532. The reason why true repentance is to explore not only the acts of one's life, but also the intentions of one's will, is because the <term>Understanding</term> and the <term>Will</term> produce the acts. For a person speaks from thought and acts from will; therefore, speech is thought speaking, and action is will acting. Because speech and action originate from there, it follows beyond doubt that it is those two which sin when the body sins. A person can perform repentance for the evils they have done with the body and still think and will evil; but this is like cutting off the trunk of a bad tree and leaving its root in the ground, from which the same bad tree grows up again and spreads itself around. It is quite different when the root is also pulled out; and this happens in a person when they simultaneously explore the intentions of their will and remove evils through repentance. A person explores the intentions of their will while they explore their thoughts, for intentions manifest themselves in the thoughts; for instance, when one thinks about, wills, and intends revenge, adulteries, thefts, and false witness, as well as the lusts for those things, and also blasphemies against God, the Holy Word, and the Church, and so on. If the person then focuses their mind on this and examines whether they would do those things if the fear of the law and of their reputation did not stand in the way—and if, after this scrutiny, they think that they do not want to do them because they are sins—that person is performing true and interior repentance. This is even more the case when they are in the middle of the delight of those evils and at the same time have the freedom to do them, and yet they resist and abstain. Whoever practices this repeatedly will perceive the delights of evils as unpleasant when they return, and eventually condemn them to hell. This is what is meant by these words of the Lord: *Whoever wants to find his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life for my sake will find it,* Matthew 10:39. He who [removes] the evils of his will through this [repentance]...

removes [evils through] repentance, is like one who pulls out weeds <note>original: "zizania," often translated as tares or darnel</note> sown by the Devil from a field in due time, whereby the seeds implanted by the Lord God Savior find free soil and sprout into a harvest. **Matthew 13:25 to 31.**

533. There are two loves that have been rooted in the human race for a long time: the **love of ruling over all**, and the **love of possessing the goods of all**. If the reins are loosened on the former love, it rushes onward until it wishes to be the God of heaven; and if the reins are loosened on the latter love, it rushes onward until it wishes to be the God of the world. All other evil loves, which are like an army, are subordinate to these two. But to explore those two is exceedingly difficult, because they reside in the most internal parts and hide themselves; for they are like vipers concealed in a porous rock, which hold back their venom so that when someone lies down upon that rock, they inflict lethal strikes and then withdraw. They are also like the <term>Sirens</term> <note>Mythological creatures whose beautiful singing lured sailors to their destruction</note> of the ancients, who enticed men with their song and killed them by it. These two loves also adorn themselves in splendid robes and tunics, just as the devil does through magical fantasy among his own, and among others whom he wishes to deceive. 

But it should be well known that these two loves can reign more among the lowly than among the great, among the poor than among the wealthy, and among subjects than among Kings; for the latter are born to dominion and to wealth, which they eventually look upon in no other way than a person looks upon their servants and possessions, a governor upon his own, an administrator upon his own, or a sea-captain upon his own—even as a poor farmer looks upon his. It is quite different, however, for Kings who [crave] dominion over the kingdoms of others. The reason why the intentions of the **Will** <note>In this context, the Will is the seat of a person's desires and loves, distinct from the Intellect or thinking faculty</note> must be explored is because love resides in the Will; for the Will is its receptacle, as was shown above. Every love breathes out its delights from there into the perceptions and thoughts of the **Intellect**; for these do not act at all from themselves, but from the Will. They favor it, agree with it, and confirm all things that belong to its love. Therefore, the Will is the house itself in which the person lives, and the Intellect is the courtyard through which they exit and enter. This is why it is said that the intentions of the Will must be explored; when these are explored and removed, a person is elevated from the natural Will, in which hereditary and actual evils reside, into a spiritual Will, through which the Lord reforms and regenerates the natural [will], and by this means, the sensory and voluntary parts of the body—thus the whole person.

534. Those who do not explore themselves are like sick people whose blood is corrupted from the closing of the smallest vessels, leading to wasting away <note>original: "atrophia"</note>, numbness of the limbs, and acute chronic diseases arising from the thickness, tenacity, sharpness, and acidity of the humors <note>In older medicine, "humors" were bodily fluids believed to control health and temperament</note>, and consequently the blood. But truly, those who explore themselves, even regarding the intentions of the Will, are like those who have been healed of those diseases and return to the life they enjoyed when they were young. Those who rightly explore themselves are like ships from <term>Ophir</term> <note>A legendary region mentioned in the Bible, famous for its high-quality gold and riches</note> filled with gold, silver, and precious things; but before they explored themselves, they were like ships loaded with filth, used to carry away the mire and dung of the streets. Those who interiorly explore themselves become like mines whose walls all shine with the ores of noble metal; but before, they were like stinking swamps inhabited by cobras and poisonous serpents with glittering scales, and harmful insects with shining wings. Those who do not explore themselves are like **dry bones in a valley**; but after they have explored themselves, they are like those same bones upon which the <term>Lord Jehovih</term> <note>A specific name for God emphasizing His divine power and love</note> laid sinews, caused flesh to grow, covered with skin, and into which He put breath, and they lived. **Ezekiel 37:1 to 14.** <note>The Latin text cites Chapter 27 (XXVII), but the description matches the vision of the dry bones in Chapter 37 (XXXVII).</note>

## *That those also perform Repentance, who do not examine themselves, but nevertheless desist from evils because they are sins; and that this repentance is performed by those who do works of Charity from religion.*

535. Because actual Repentance—which is to examine oneself, to recognize and acknowledge one's sins, to pray to the Lord, and to begin a new life—is exceedingly difficult in the Reformed <term>Christian World</term> <note>This refers to the Protestant nations of 18th-century Europe, where Swedenborg argued that the doctrine of "faith alone" had made people neglect the practice of self-examination.</note> for many reasons (which will be discussed in the final article of this chapter), a easier kind of Repentance is therefore presented. It is this: when someone turns an evil over in their mind and intends it, they say to themselves, *“I am thinking this, and I intend this, but because it is a sin, I will not do it.”* By this means, the temptation injected from Hell is broken, and its further entry is blocked. It is a wonderful thing that anyone can rebuke another person who intends evil and say, "Do not do that because it is a sin," and yet it is difficult for that same person to say it to themselves; the reason is that saying it to oneself moves the will, while saying it to another only moves a thought near to one's hearing. 

When it was investigated in the <term>spiritual world</term> who was able to do this latter thing, they were found to be as few as doves in a vast desert. Some said they could certainly do it, but that they could not examine themselves and confess their sins before God. Yet all those who do good from a religious principle avoid active evils; however, they very rarely reflect upon the interior things that belong to the Will, believing that they are not in evil because they are in good—indeed, believing that their good deeds cover their evils. But, my friend! The primary thing of <term>Charity</term> <note>original: "Charitas." In this context, it refers to the active love of neighbor expressed through useful service and moral living.</note> is to flee from evils. This is taught by the Word, the <term>Decalogue</term> <note>The Ten Commandments</note>, Baptism, the Holy Supper, and even by Reason; for how can anyone escape evils and cast them away without some intuition of themselves? And how can good become truly good unless it is internally purified? I know that all pious people, and also those of sound reason, will nod in agreement when they read this and see it as genuine truth, and yet few will actually do it.

536. Nevertheless, all who do good from religion—not only Christians but also pagans—are accepted by the Lord and adopted after death; for the Lord said:
> “*For I was hungry, and you gave Me to eat; I was thirsty, and you gave Me to drink; I was a stranger, and you took Me in; I was sick, and you visited Me; I was in prison, and you came to Me,*”
and He said,
> “*Inasmuch as you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to Me; come, you blessed, and possess as an inheritance the Kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.*”
—*Matthew 25:31 and following.*

To this I will add this new information: all those who do good from religion, after death, reject the doctrine of today’s Church regarding three Divine persons from eternity, and also its Faith as applied to those three in order. They turn themselves to the Lord God Savior and drink in with delight those things which belong to the <term>New Church</term>. The others, however, who did not practice Charity from religion, have "adamantine hearts" <note>Hearts as hard as diamond or unbreakable stone, signifying a refusal to be moved by spiritual truth.</note>, so hard that they first go toward three Gods, then to the Father alone, and finally to no God at all. They look upon the Lord God Savior as only the son of Mary, born from the marriage bed with Joseph, and not as the Son of God; then they shake off all the goods and truths of the New Church, and soon join themselves to the spirits of the dragon <note>A reference to the "dragon" in the Book of Revelation, which Swedenborg interprets as those who separate faith from charity.</note>, and are driven away with them into deserts or into caves which are at the furthest borders of what is called the Christian world. After a time, because they are separated from the New Heaven, they rush into crimes and are therefore cast down into Hell. Such is the lot of those who do not perform works of Charity from religion, based on the belief that no one can do good from himself unless it is "meritorious" <note>The idea that doing good is a selfish attempt to "earn" one's way into heaven.</note>, and thus they omit those works and group themselves with the goats, who are condemned and cast into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels, because they did not do the things that the sheep did. *Matthew 25:41 and following.* It does not say there that they did evils, but that [they did not do good]...

those who have not done good works, and those who do good things but not out of a sense of religion, do evil, *since no one can serve two masters without hating the one and loving the other, or being devoted to one and neglecting the other*, Matthew 6:24. 537. It should be known that those who do good out of mere natural goodness alone, and not also out of religion, are not accepted after death. This is because their charity contains only natural good and not spiritual good, and it is the spiritual that joins the Lord to man; the natural without the spiritual cannot do this. Natural goodness belongs to the flesh alone, inherited from one's parents, but <term>spiritual goodness</term> <note>In this context, spiritual goodness refers to a character shaped by divine principles rather than just biological temperament.</note> belongs to the spirit, born anew from the Lord. Those who perform the works of Charity out of religion, and thus do not do evil, even before they have accepted the Doctrine of the <term>New Church</term> <note>Swedenborg uses "New Church" to refer to a new spiritual era or dispensation of Christianity that he believed was beginning in his time.</note> concerning the Lord, can be compared to trees that bear good fruit, even if only a few; and also to trees that bear small but noble fruits, which are nevertheless preserved in gardens. They may also be compared to olive and fig trees in the forests, or even to fragrant herbs and balsamic shrubs upon the hills. They are like little shrines or houses of God in which pious worship is conducted; for they are the sheep on the right hand, and the rams which the male goats attack, according to Daniel 8: 2 to 14. In Heaven, they are clothed in garments of a red color, and after they have been initiated into the goods of the New Church, they are clothed in garments of a purple color, which take on a beautiful golden glow as they also receive truths.

## *That Confession before the Lord God the Savior ought to be made, and then supplication for help and power to resist evils.*

538. The reason the Lord God the Savior must be approached is that He is the God of Heaven and Earth, the Redeemer and Savior, to whom belong Omnipotence, Omniscience, Omnipresence, Mercy itself, and at the same time Justice. Furthermore, man is His creature, and the Church is His sheepfold. He commanded many times in the New Covenant that people should approach, worship, and adore Him. He enjoined that He alone is to be approached in these words in John: *“Truly, truly, I say to you, he who does not enter the sheepfold through the door, but climbs up another way, is a thief and a robber; but he who enters through the door is the shepherd of the sheep. I am the Door; if anyone enters through Me, he will be saved, and will find pasture; the thief comes only to steal, kill, and destroy; I have come that they may have life and abundance. I am the good Shepherd,”* Chapter 10: 1, 2, 9, 10, 11. The reason man must not "climb up another way" is so that he does not try to reach God the Father, because the Father is invisible, and therefore inaccessible and impossible to be joined with. For this reason, He Himself came into the world and made Himself visible, accessible, and joinable, solely for the purpose that man might be saved. For unless God is approached in one’s thought as a Man, every idea of God perishes; it falls like sight into the universe—into an empty nothingness, or into nature, or into things found within nature. That God Himself, who from eternity is One, came into the world, is clearly evident from the birth of the Lord the Savior...

that he was conceived from the power of the Most High through the Holy Spirit, and that His <term>Human</term><note>Latin: *Humanum*. In this theology, the "Human" refers specifically to the bodily and psychological nature Jesus took on through Mary, which was gradually made Divine.</note> was born from the Virgin Mary. From this it follows that His Soul was the Divine Itself, which is called the Father—for God is indivisible—and that the Human born from it is the Human of God the Father, which is called the Son of God (Luke 1:32, 34, 35). From these points it follows again that when the Lord God the Savior is approached, God the Father is also approached. This is why He replied to Philip, who requested to see the Father: *"He who sees Me, sees the Father; how then can you say, show us the Father? Do you not believe that I am in the Father, and the Father is in Me? Believe Me, that I am in the Father, and the Father is in Me"* (John 14:6 to 11). But more may be seen on these subjects in the chapters concerning God, the Lord, the Holy Spirit, and the Trinity.

559. There are two duties incumbent upon a person to perform after self-examination: Supplication and Confession. **Supplication** is the act of praying that the Lord may have mercy, give the power to resist the evils one has repented of, and provide the inclination and affection for doing good, *since without Him, man can do nothing* (John 15:5). **Confession** is the act of seeing, knowing, and acknowledging one's evils, and finding oneself to be a miserable sinner. Before the Lord, there is no need for an exhaustive listing of sins, nor to plead for their "remission" <note>Original: *Remissio peccatorum*. While traditionally translated as "forgiveness," the author argues it is actually the "removal" of the grip of sin.</note>. There is no need for a list of sins because the person has already searched them out and seen them within himself, and therefore they are present before the Lord because they are present to the person. Indeed, the Lord guided the person during that self-examination, opened the sins to view, inspired sorrow, and along with this, gave the effort to desist from them and begin a new life. There are two reasons why one should not plead before the Lord for the "remission" of sins: First, because sins are not simply wiped away but are *removed*, and they are removed only as a person subsequently stops doing them and enters a new life. For there are countless <term>Lusts</term><note>Latin: *Concupiscentiæ*. These are deep-seated selfish desires that lead to sinful actions.</note> clinging to every evil, like a tangled ball of yarn, which cannot be removed in a single moment, but only gradually as a person allows himself to be reformed and regenerated. The second reason is that the Lord, being Mercy Itself, remits (forgives) everyone their sins and does not hold a single one against anyone; for He says, *they know not what they do*. Yet they are not taken away for that reason alone. For when Peter asked how many times he should forgive his brother’s offenses, whether up to seven times, Jesus said, *“I do not say to you seven times, but up to seventy times seven”* (Matthew 18:21, 22). How much more, then, does the Lord forgive? Nevertheless, it does no harm if someone burdened in conscience, in order to find relief, lists his sins before a minister of the Church for the sake of absolution; for this helps introduce the habit of examining oneself and reflecting on daily evils. However, this type of Confession is "natural," whereas the one described above is "spiritual."

560. To worship any "Vicar" <note>A reference to the Pope, often called the "Vicar of Christ."</note> on earth, or to call upon any Saint as a god, has no more value in Heaven than praying to the sun, moon, and stars, or asking a fortune-teller for an answer and believing their word, which is vanity. This would also be like worshipping a Temple building rather than the God within the Temple. It would be like a subject asking the King's servant—who merely carries the King's scepter and crown—for honors and glory, rather than asking the King himself. This would be as useless as trying to kiss the shimmer of purple fabric, the light, or the golden rays of the sun while ignoring the person or object they come from. For those who do such things, let these words from John be remembered: *“We remain in the truth in Jesus Christ; This is the true God and eternal Life; little children, keep yourselves from idols”* (1 Epistle 5:20, 21).

## *That actual Repentance is easy for those who have practiced it several times, but is highly resistant to those who have not.*

561. <term>Actual repentance</term><note>Latin: *pænitentia actualis*. This refers to the specific, lived practice of identifying and turning away from particular sins, as opposed to a general feeling of being a sinner.</note> consists in examining oneself, recognizing one's sins, confessing them before the Lord, and thus beginning a new life; it follows the description given previously. In the <term>Reformed Christian World</term><note>A term used by the author to describe the various Protestant denominations that broke away from the Roman Catholic Church.</note>—by which is meant all those separated from the Roman Catholic Church, as well as those still within it who have not practiced any actual repentance—this practice is met with extreme resistance. The reason is that some are unwilling, some are afraid, and long-standing habit becomes a fixed part of a person's nature, leading to a lack of will and, eventually, a reasoned intellectual refusal. For some, the very idea of it brings about sorrow, dread, and terror.

The primary reason why actual repentance is so resisted in the Reformed Christian World is their doctrine of **Faith Alone** <note>original: *Fides sola*</note>. They believe that repentance and charity contribute nothing to salvation, but that faith alone—by the <term>imputation</term><note>The theological concept that Christ's righteousness is "credited" to the believer's account, regardless of their own actions.</note> of which follows the forgiveness of sins, justification, renewal, regeneration, sanctification, and eternal salvation. Furthermore, their teachers claim that for a person to cooperate of themselves, or as if of themselves, is useless and even contrary, repugnant, and insulting to Christ's merit. This idea has been sown among the common people—even if they are ignorant of the complex mysteries of that faith—through the simple phrases: "Faith alone saves," and "Who can do good on their own?" Consequently, among the Reformed, Repentance is like a nest with chicks abandoned by birds that have been caught and killed by a fowler. To this cause is added another: that a person in the Reformed tradition, as to their spirit, associates in the spiritual world only with those like themselves, who introduce such ideas into their thoughts and lead them away from even the first step of looking into and examining themselves.

562. I have questioned many of the Reformed in the spiritual world why they did not perform actual repentance, even though it was commanded of them both in the Word and at their Baptism, and also before Holy Communion in all their churches. They gave various answers. **SOME** said that <term>contrition</term><note>A feeling of remorse or guilt, as opposed to the active change of behavior found in repentance.</note> is enough, followed by an oral confession that one is a sinner. **SOME** said that such repentance, because it is performed by a person acting from their own will, does not align with the universally accepted faith. **SOME** asked, "Who can examine himself when he knows he is nothing but sin? That would be like casting a net into a lake that is full of mud and stinging worms from the bottom to the surface." **SOME** asked, "Who can look so deeply into himself as to see the **sin of Adam** <note>original: *peccatum Adami*</note>, from which all his actual evils flow? Have these not all been washed away with that sin by the waters of baptism, and wiped away and covered by the merit of Christ? What is repentance then but a burden that severely disturbs the conscience? Is not the Gospel a message of grace, rather than the harsh law of such repentance?" and many other things besides. **SOME** said that whenever they intended to examine themselves, they were seized by dread and terror, as if they saw a monster by their bed in the early dawn. 

From these instances, the reasons are revealed why actual repentance in the Reformed Christian World has been cast aside, as if left to decay. I then questioned some followers of the Roman Catholic religion in their presence about their practice of **Actual Confession** before their ministers, and whether they found it resistant. They replied that once they were initiated into it, they did not fear recounting their faults before a confessor who was not severe; they found a certain pleasure in collecting their thoughts and cheerfully stating their lighter faults, and even their more serious ones with only a little fear. They returned freely to this custom every year, and after absolution, they entered into a state of festivity. They even remarked that they look upon all who are unwilling to open the defilements of their hearts as "impure." Upon hearing this, the Reformed who were present fled—some laughing and mocking, others struck with amazement yet full of praise. Afterwards...

...certain people belonging to the same Church [the Reformed] joined them, but lived in regions where the Reformed reside. In accordance with the custom established there, they did not make a specific confession like their brothers elsewhere, but only a general one before their <term>Key-bearer</term><note>Latin: *Claviger*. This refers to a minister or priest who, according to church doctrine, holds the "power of the keys" to forgive or retain sins.</note>. These people said that they were completely unable to search out, track down, and disclose their actual evils and the secrets of their thoughts; they felt this was as repulsive and terrifying as wanting to cross a ditch toward a defensive wall where an armed soldier stands and shouts, "Do not approach!" From this, it is now clear that <term>actual repentance</term><note>The practice of identifying and turning away from specific, individual sins in one's life.</note> is easy for those who have practiced it several times, but extremely resistant to those who have not.

563. It is well known that habit becomes second nature, and thus what is easy for one is difficult for another; so it is also with exploring oneself and confessing what has been explored. What is easier for a hired hand, a porter, or a farmer than to work with their arms from morning until evening? Yet a man of high rank and delicate living cannot do the same for half an hour without exhaustion and sweat. It is easy for a runner with a staff and soft shoes to travel a path of a thousand paces, while one accustomed to being carried in a carriage can hardly run slowly from one street to another. Every craftsman who is diligent in his work performs it easily and gladly, and when leaving it, longs to return; whereas another who knows the same craft but is lazy can hardly be forced to do it. The same is true for everyone in any function or study. What is easier for one devoted to piety than to pray to God, and what is harder for one given over to impiety?—and vice versa. What priest, preaching for the first time before the King, does not feel fear? But after he has become practiced, he proceeds fearlessly. What is easier for an <term>angelic man</term><note>A person whose inner life is aligned with the unselfish love and wisdom of heaven.</note> than to raise his eyes to Heaven? And what is easier for a <term>diabolical man</term><note>A person whose inner life is driven by selfish or worldly lusts.</note> than to cast his eyes down toward hell? Yet if the latter becomes a hypocrite, he can similarly look up toward Heaven, but with an averted heart. The **purpose** for which one acts, and the habit resulting from it, imbues every person.

->*That he who has never practiced Repentance, or has not looked within*<-
->*and examined himself, eventually does not know what is a damnable*<-
->*evil, and what is a saving good.*<-

564. Since few in the Reformed Christian World practice repentance, this point is added: he who has not looked within and examined himself eventually does not know what is a damnable evil and what is a saving good. For he has no religion from which to know this. For the evil that a person does not see, recognize, and acknowledge remains; and what remains takes root more and more until it obstructs the inner parts of his mind. Because of this, a person becomes first **natural**, then **sensual**, and finally **corporeal**; and such a person knows nothing of damnable evil or saving good. He becomes like a tree on a hard rock, which spreads its roots into the crevices, and eventually withers because it lacks moisture. Every well-bred person is rational and moral; but there are two ways to <term>rationality</term><note>The capacity to understand and process truth.</note>: one from the World, the other from Heaven. He who has become rational and moral from the World, and not also from Heaven, is rational and moral only in speech and gesture, but inside he is a beast—even a wild animal—because he acts as one with those in Hell, where all are such. But he who is rational and moral also from Heaven is truly rational and moral, because he is so in spirit, speech, and body simultaneously. In these two, there is a spiritual element within, like a soul, which activates the natural, sensual, and corporeal levels; he also acts as one with those in Heaven. Therefore, there is a **spiritual-rational** and **moral** man, and also a **merely natural-rational** and **moral** man. One cannot be distinguished from the other in the World, especially if he has trained himself in the practice of hypocrisy; but they are distinguished by the angels in Heaven as clearly as doves from owls, and as sheep from tigers. The merely natural man can see evils and goods in others and even rebuke them; but because he has not looked within and examined himself, he does not see any <margin>catchword: quod.</margin>

...because the evil within him—and if any is detected by another—he veils it with his <term>rational mind</term><note>The faculty of the mind that uses logic and reasoning, which Swedenborg argues can be used either to confirm truth or to mask evil.</note>, just as a serpent hides its head in the dust, or a hornet buries itself in dung. This is caused by the "delight of evil," which surrounds him like a fog over a swamp, absorbing and suffocating the rays of light. The delight of hell is nothing else; it exhales from there and flows into every person, but it enters through the soles of the feet, the back, and the back of the head. However, if this delight is received by the head in the forehead, and by the body in the chest, that person is surrendered to hell. The reason is that the human <term>Cerebrum</term><note>The larger, forward part of the brain; associated here with the intellect.</note> is dedicated to the intellect and thus to wisdom, while the <term>Cerebellum</term><note>The smaller, rear part of the brain; associated here with the will.</note> is dedicated to the will and its love; this is why there are two brains. But that infernal delight can only be amended, reformed, and overturned through a spiritual, rational, and moral life.

565. There now follows a description of the merely natural, rational, and moral man, who, when viewed in himself, is "sensual," and if he continues in this state, becomes "corporeal" or "fleshly." This description is provided in a <term>sketch</term><note>original: "sciagraphia"</note> divided into parts:
*   The <term>sensual</term><note>In Swedenborg’s terminology, "sensual" refers to the lowest level of thought, which relies entirely on the physical senses and rejects anything it cannot see or touch.</note> is the lowest level of the life of the human mind, adhering to and clinging to the five senses of the body.
*   A person is called a **sensual man** who judges everything by the bodily senses and who believes nothing except what he can see with his eyes and touch with his hands, saying that these are "something" and rejecting the rest.
*   The interiors of his mind, which see by the light of Heaven, are closed, so that he sees nothing of the truth belonging to Heaven and the Church.
*   Such a man thinks in extremes and not inwardly from any spiritual light, because he exists in a thick natural light. This is why he is inwardly opposed to the things of Heaven and the Church, even though outwardly he can speak in favor of them—sometimes even ardently—depending on his hope for power or wealth through them.
*   The learned and the scholarly, who have deeply confirmed themselves in falsehoods (and especially those who have confirmed themselves against the truths of the Word), are more sensual than others.
*   Sensual men reason sharply and cleverly because their thought is so close to their speech that it is almost in it, as if on their lips; they place all intelligence in speaking from memory alone.
*   They are skilled at confirming falsehoods, and after doing so, they believe them to be true; however, they reason and confirm based on the fallacies of the senses, by which the common people are captivated and persuaded.
*   Sensual men are more cunning and malicious than others.
*   The greedy, adulterous, and deceitful are primarily sensual, even if they appear clever to the world.
*   The interiors of their minds are foul and filthy; through these, they communicate with the hells. In the Word, they are called "the dead."
*   Those who are in the hells are sensual, and the deeper they are, the more sensual they are. The sphere of infernal spirits joins itself with the sensual part of a man from behind; in the light of Heaven, the back of their heads appears hollowed out.
*   Those who reasoned from the senses alone were called by the ancients "**serpents of the Tree of Knowledge**."
*   Sensual things ought to occupy the last place, not the first; in a wise and intelligent man, they are in the last place and subject to the interiors, but in a foolish man, they are in the first place and dominate.
*   If sensual things are in the last place, a way is opened through them to the intellect, and truths are nourished by a process of extraction.
*   These sensual things stand closest to the world; they admit what flows in from the world and, as it were, sift it.
*   Man communicates with the world through the sensual, and with Heaven through the rational.
*   Sensual things supply what serves the interiors of the mind.
*   There are sensual things that serve the intellectual part and those that serve the voluntary part.
*   Unless thought is elevated above sensual things, a man has little wisdom. When a man's thought is elevated above the sensual, he comes into a clearer light, and finally into heavenly light, where he perceives things flowing down from Heaven.
*   The lowest part of the intellect is natural scientific knowledge, and the lowest part of the will is sensual delight.

566. Regarding the natural man, he is like a beast; he takes on the image of a beast through his life. Therefore, in the spiritual world, beasts of every kind appear around such people, which are <term>correspondences</term><note>A key concept in Swedenborg's work where physical objects or animals act as outward symbols reflecting a person's inner spiritual state.</note>. For the natural part of man, viewed in itself, is merely animal; but because the spiritual is added to it, he can become a man, and...

...if it does not arise from a genuine capacity to be truly human, he may mimic a person, but he remains a **speaking beast**. For such a person speaks from a <term>natural-rational</term><note>A level of reasoning based only on the physical world and the senses, disconnected from spiritual truth.</note> mind, but thinks from a **spiritual madness**; he acts from a natural-moral place, but loves from a **spiritual lust**. When viewed by a <term>spiritual-rational</term> man, his actions are seen as little more than the twitching leaps of someone bitten by a tarantula, a condition called **St. Vitus’ or St. Guy's dance**<note>original: "S. Vitis seu Gui." A historical term for Sydenham's chorea, a disorder characterized by rapid, jerky movements; here used as a metaphor for spiritual instability.</note>. Who does not know that a hypocrite can speak of God, a thief of sincerity, or an adulterer of chastity? Yet, unless a person had the gift of closing and opening the door between thoughts and speech, and between intentions and actions—with **prudence** or **cunning** serving as the doorkeeper—he would rush more fiercely than any wild beast into wicked and cruel deeds. That door, however, is opened for everyone after death, and only then does his true nature appear; in the meantime, the wicked are held in check by punishments and guards in <term>Hell</term>. Therefore, kind reader, look into yourself, and seek out one or another evil within you, and turn away from it **out of Religion**; for if you turn away from evil for any other purpose or end, you only hide it so that it does not appear before the world.

<center>***</center>

567. To these points, the following **MEMORABLE RELATIONS** are added: First, this one. I was suddenly seized by a nearly lethal disease; my whole head was heavy. A pestilential smoke was let in from the **Jerusalem** which is called **Sodom and Egypt**<note>A reference to Revelation 11:8, often used by Swedenborg to symbolize a church that has lost its spiritual life through hollow external worship (Egypt) and evil desires (Sodom).</note>. I was half-dead with cruel pain and expected the end. Thus I lay in my bed for three and a half days; my spirit became such, and from the spirit, my body. Then I heard voices around me saying: "Look, he who preached Repentance for the remission of sins, and Christ as the only man, lies dead in the street of our City." And they asked some of the clergy whether he was worthy of burial; they said no, let him lie and be looked at. They went away, returned, and mocked me. This actually happened to me while the eleventh chapter of the **Revelation** was being explained.

Then, the heavy voices of those mocking were heard, especially these: "How can Repentance be performed without faith? How can the man Christ be adored as God? Since we are saved freely without any merit of our own, what is needed then except the faith alone that God the Father sent the Son to take away the condemnation of the Law, impute His merit to us, and thus justify us before Himself? He absolves us from sins through the priest’s proclamation, and then gives the Holy Spirit to work all good within us. Are these things not according to Scripture, and also according to reason?" The standing crowd applauded these words.

I heard this, but could not respond, because I lay almost dead. But after three and a half days, my spirit recovered, and in my spirit, I went out from the street into the City and said again: "**Repent, and believe in Christ, and your sins will be forgiven, and you will be saved; if not, you will perish.**" Did not the Lord Himself preach repentance for the remission of sins, and that they should believe in Him? Did He not command the Disciples to preach the same? Does not a total neglect of life follow from your dogma of faith? But they said, "What are you prattling? Has the Son not made satisfaction? Does the Father not impute it? He justifies us who have believed this; we are led by the spirit of grace. What then is sin in us, what then is death to us? Do you grasp this Gospel, you preacher of sin and repentance?"

But then a voice came from Heaven, saying: "**What is the faith of an impenitent man but a dead faith? The end has come, the end has come upon you who are secure, blameless in your own eyes, justified in your faith—you satans!**" And suddenly an abyss opened in the middle of the City and widened; house fell upon house, and they were swallowed up. Soon, water bubbled up from the wide gulf and flooded the wasteland.

When they were thus submerged and seen to be flooded, I desired to know their fate in the deep. It was told to me from Heaven, "You shall see and hear." Then the waters, by which they seemed to be flooded, disappeared before my eyes; for in the <term>Spiritual World</term>, **Waters** are <term>Correspondences</term><note>A central concept in Swedenborg's thought where physical objects represent spiritual realities. Here, water represents "falsities" or incorrect religious doctrines that overwhelm the mind.</note>, and thus they appear around those who are in falsities. And then...
