...I saw people on a **sandy ground**, where there were heaps of stones piled up, between which they were running and lamenting because they had been cast out of their great City. They were shouting and crying out: "Why has this happened to us? Are we not, through our **Faith**, clean, pure, just, and holy? Are we not, through our **Faith**, cleansed, purified, justified, and sanctified? and others cried: "Have we not through our faith been made such that we appear, are seen, and are reputed as such before God the Father, and are declared clean, pure, just, and holy before the Angels? Are we not reconciled, propitiated, atoned for, and thus released, washed, and wiped clean from sins? Has not the condemnation of the **Law** been removed by Christ? Why then are we cast here as if we were damned? We heard from a bold preacher against sin in our great City: 'believe in Christ and perform repentance.' Did we not believe in Christ when we believed in His Merit? And did we not perform repentance when we confessed that we were sinners? Why then has this happened to us?"

But then a voice was heard speaking to them from the side: "Do you know of a single sin that you are in? Have you ever examined yourselves? Have you ever shunned any evil as a sin against God? For he who does not shun evil remains in it. Is not sin the devil? Therefore, you are those of whom the Lord says: *Then you will begin to say, we ate and drank in Your presence, and You taught in our streets; but He will say, I tell you, I do not know where you are from; depart from Me, all you workers of iniquity,* Luke 13:26, 27; as well as those mentioned in Matthew 7:22, 23. Go away, therefore, each to his own place. You see the openings into the Caverns; enter there, and each of you will be given your own work to do, and then food will be given in proportion to your work; if not, hunger will eventually drive you to enter."

Afterward, a voice from Heaven spoke to certain people upon the earth who were outside that great city (of whom mention is also made in Revelation 11:13<note>Swedenborg frequently cites the Book of Revelation, interpreting the "Great City" as a symbol of the corrupt state of the church.</note>), saying loudly: "Watch yourselves! Watch yourselves from associating with those like them! Can you not understand that evils, which are called sins and iniquities, render a person unclean and impure? How can a man be cleansed and purified from them except by <term>actual repentance</term><note>A key Swedenborgian concept: repentance that involves specific self-examination and change of behavior, rather than just a general confession of being a sinner.</note> and by faith in the Lord Jesus Christ? **Actual repentance** is to examine oneself, to know and acknowledge one's sins, to hold oneself guilty, to confess them before the Lord, to implore help and the power to resist them, and thus to desist from them and lead a new life; and all of this as if of yourselves. Do this once or twice a year when you approach the **Holy Communion**; and afterward, when the sins of which you found yourself guilty recur, then say to yourselves, 'we do not want them, because they are sins against God.' This is **actual repentance**.

Who cannot understand that he who does not examine and see his sins remains in them? For every evil is pleasant from birth; it is pleasant to take revenge, to commit adultery, to defraud, to blaspheme, and especially to rule from the love of self. Does not this pleasure act so that they are not seen? And if it happens to be said that they are sins, do you not excuse them because of that pleasure? Indeed, you confirm through falsehoods that they are not sins, and so you remain in them and do them afterward more than before, and this continues until you no longer know what sin is, or indeed whether there even is such a thing as sin. It happens differently for anyone who has actually performed **Repentance**: he calls his evils, which he has known and acknowledged, 'sins,' and therefore he begins to shun and turn away from them, and finally to feel their pleasure as unpleasant. And to the extent that this is done, he sees and loves what is good, and finally feels the pleasure of these things, which is the pleasure of the **Angels of Heaven**. In a word, as much as anyone rejects the devil to his back, so much is he adopted by the Lord, and is taught, led, and withheld from evils by Him, and held in good. This is the way, and no other, from **Hell to Heaven**."

It is a wonder that a certain inherent reluctance, evasion, and aversion to **actual Repentance** exists among the <term>Reformed</term><note>The "Reformed" refers to the Protestant churches stemming from the Reformation, particularly those following the doctrines of Luther or Calvin.</note>, which is so great that they cannot bring themselves to examine themselves, to see their sins, and to confess them before God; it is as if a horror seizes them when they intend to do it. I have asked many in the spiritual world about this, and they all said that this was beyond their power. When they heard that the <term>Catholics</term><note>original: "Pontificii," referring to those under the authority of the Pope.</note>...

...until they do this—that is, until they examine themselves and openly confess their sins before a Monk. They were greatly amazed at this, and moreover, that the Reformed <note>The "Reformed" refers to Protestant denominations arising from the Reformation.</note> are unable to do this in secret before God, even though it is equally enjoined upon them before they approach the Holy Supper. Some there inquired why this was so, and they found that **Faith Alone** <term>Sola Fide (Faith Alone): the doctrine that salvation comes through belief alone, without the need for good works or personal repentance.</term> had brought about such a state of impenitence and such a heart. It was then granted to them to see that those among the Catholics who worship Christ, and do not invoke the Saints, are saved.

After this, a sound like thunder was heard, and a voice speaking from Heaven, saying: "We are amazed; say to the assembly of the Reformed: Believe in Christ, and perform **Repentance**, and you shall be saved." And I spoke, and added: "Is not **BAPTISM** the Sacrament of Repentance, and thus an Introduction into the Church? What else do Godparents promise for the one being baptized, other than that they should renounce the devil and his works? Is not the **HOLY SUPPER** the Sacrament of Repentance, and thus an Introduction into Heaven? Is it not said to the Communicants that they must by all means perform repentance before approaching? Is not the **CATECHISM** the Universal Doctrine of the Christian Church that teaches repentance? Does it not say there, in the six Precepts of the Second Table <note>The "Second Table" refers to the last six of the Ten Commandments, which govern a person’s relationship with their neighbor.</note>, 'you shall not do this or that Evil,' and it does not say, 'you shall do this or that Good'? From this you may know, that as much as one renounces and turns away from Evil, so much does he desire and love Good; and that before this, he does not know what Good is, nor indeed even what Evil is."

### 568. THE SECOND MEMORABLE RELATION.

What pious and wise person does not wish to know the lot of his life after death? Therefore, I shall make known the common things so that he may know. Every person after death, when they feel that they are still alive and that they are in another World, and hear that above them is Heaven where there are eternal joys, and below them is Hell where there are eternal pains, is first sent back into their **Externals**, in which they were in the former World. At that time, they believe they will certainly come into Heaven, and they speak intelligently and act prudently. Some say, "We have lived morally, we have pursued honest things, we have not done evil by purpose"; others say, "We have frequented churches, listened to masses, kissed holy images, and poured out prayers on our knees." Some say, "We have given to the poor, helped the needy, read books of piety, and also the Word," besides many similar things. 

But after they have said these things, Angels stand by and say: "All those things you have recounted, you did in your **Externals**, but you do not yet know what you are like in your **Internals**. Now you are spirits in a substantial body, and the Spirit is your internal man; it is this within you which thinks what it wills, and wills what it loves, and this is the delight of its life." Every person from infancy begins life from Externals, and learns to act morally and to speak intelligently; and when they first grasp the idea of Heaven and the happiness there, they begin to pray, frequent churches, and observe the solemnities of worship. And yet, they may hide away evils—while they gush forth from their native fountain—in the breast of their own mind, and also cleverly veil them with reasonings based on fallacies, even to the point that they themselves do not know that evil is evil. And then, because the evils are veiled and covered with dust, they no longer think about them, taking care only that they do not appear before the World. Thus, they study only the moral life in externals, and so become a "double man"—a sheep in externals and a wolf in internals; like a golden box that contains poison inside; like one with foul breath holding an aromatic in his mouth so it is not noticed by those standing by; or like a mouse skin that smells of balsam. 

You have said that you lived morally and pursued studies of piety, but I ask: have you ever explored your **Internal man** and perceived any lusts for revenging even unto death, for lusting even unto adultery, for defrauding even unto theft, for lying even unto false witness? In the four Precepts of the Decalogue <note>The Ten Commandments.</note> it is said "you shall not do those things," and in the last two it is said "you shall not covet those things." Do you believe that your Internal man has been like your External in these matters? If you believe this, perhaps you are deceived. But to this they responded: "What is the Internal man? Is he and the External not one and the same? We have heard from our Ministers that the Internal man is nothing other..."

<summary>Swedenborg argues that true Christianity requires active repentance and self-examination of one's internal motives, rather than just outward moral behavior or "faith alone." He describes how, after death, people are initially judged by their external actions before their true internal character—often hidden during life—is revealed.</summary>

...is nothing else than Faith, and that piety of the mouth and the morality of one’s life are its sign, because they are its operation. To these the Angels responded: "Saving Faith exists in the **Internal Man** <note>In this theology, the "Internal Man" refers to the soul’s inner intentions and will, while the "External Man" refers to outward actions and speech.</note>, and Charity likewise. From these come Christian Fidelity and Morality in the **External Man**. But if the aforementioned lusts remain in the Internal Man—that is, in the will and thus in the thought—and if you love them inwardly yet act and speak differently in external matters, then with you, evil is placed above good, and good is placed beneath evil. Therefore, however much you may speak from the intellect and act from [apparent] love, inwardly there is evil, and it is thus veiled over. In that state, you are like **cunning apes** <note>Original Latin: "Fingae," likely referring to mimics or apes known for imitating human behavior.</note> which feign actions similar to humans, but their heart is far away. What your Internal Man is truly like—of which you know nothing because you have not examined yourselves, and after such examination have not performed repentance—you will see after a time, when you are stripped of the External Man and let into the Internal. When this happens, you will no longer be recognized by your companions, nor even by yourselves. I have seen those who were 'moral' yet evil then appearing like wild beasts, looking at their neighbor with fierce eyes, burning with deadly hatred, and blaspheming God, whom they had worshipped in the External Man." Upon hearing this, they withdrew; and the Angels then said, "You will see the quality of your life hereafter, for soon the External Man will be taken from you, and you will enter into the Internal, which is now your Spirit."

### 569. THIRD MEMORABLE OCCURRENCE.

Every Love breathes out a **delight** <term>Jucundum: a specific spiritual "delight" or "atmosphere" that emanates from a person's inner love, which becomes perceptible in the afterlife.</term> through which it makes itself felt. It breathes this out first into the spirit and then into the body; the delight of a person's love, together with the pleasantness of their thought, makes up their life. These delights and pleasantnesses are only obscurely felt by a person while they live in the natural body, because this body absorbs and dulls them. But after death, when the material body is taken away, and thus the covering or garment of the spirit is removed, then the delights of their love and the pleasantnesses of their thought are clearly felt and perceived—and what is wonderful, they are sometimes perceived as **odors**.

It is for this reason that all in the Spiritual World are associated according to their loves: those in Heaven according to theirs, and those in Hell according to theirs. The odors into which the delights of love are turned in Heaven are all perceived as such fragrances, sweet smells, pleasant breezes, and delicious perceptions as are felt in gardens, flowerbeds, fields, and woods in the mornings during springtime. However, the odors into which the delights of the loves of those in Hell are turned are perceived as stenches, foul smells, and rottings, such as those from latrines, corpses, and stagnant pits filled with rubbish and dung. And what is wonderful, the **devils** and **satans** <note>In this context, "devils" usually refers to those in evils of the will, while "satans" refers to those in falsities of the understanding.</note> there perceive these as balsams, spices, and incense, which refresh their nostrils and hearts.

In the natural world, it is also granted to beasts, birds, and worms to be associated according to odors, but not to men until they have laid aside their bodies as cast-off skins. Because of this, Heaven is most distinctly ordered according to all the varieties of the love of good, and Hell, in opposition, according to all the varieties of the love of evil. Because of this opposition, there is a **Gap** <term>Hiatus: a great chasm or spiritual divide that separates the heavens from the hells.</term> between Heaven and Hell which cannot be crossed. For those who are in Heaven cannot endure any odor of Hell—it excites nausea and vomiting, and threatens fainting if they breathe it in. The same happens to those in Hell if they cross the **midpoint** <note>Original Latin: "Meditullium," referring to the center or neutral zone of the chasm.</note> of that Gap.

Once I saw a certain devil appearing from a distance like a **Leopard**, who a few days before had been seen among the angels of the lowest heaven. He was skilled in the art of making himself appear as an "angel of light." He was crossing the Midpoint and standing between two olive trees, not feeling any odor offensive to his life. The reason was that no angels were present. But as soon as they were present, he was seized with convulsions and fell down with all his limbs contracted; he then appeared like a great serpent twisting itself into coils, and finally he cast himself down through the Gap. He was received by his own and carried away into a cavern, where he revived from the foul-smelling odor of his own delight.

I also once saw a certain Satan being punished by his own companions. I asked the cause, and it was said that he, with his nostrils stopped up, had approached those who were in the odor of Heaven, and that he had returned and brought that odor back upon his clothes...

...carried with him. It has happened several times that when a cavern of Hell was opened, a stench like that of a corpse struck my nostrils and brought on vomiting. From these things it can be established why it is that in the Word <note>The "Word" is the term used by Swedenborg to refer to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note> "Smell" signifies perception. For it is often said that Jehovah "smelled a pleasing odor" from burnt offerings; it is also why the oil of anointing and the incense were prepared from fragrant substances. Conversely, it explains why it was commanded to the children of Israel that the unclean should be carried out of their camps, and that they should dig a hole and cover their excrement (Deuteronomy 23:14–15). The reason was that the camps of Israel represented Heaven, while the desert outside the camps represented Hell.

### 570. **FOURTH MEMORABLE RELATION.**

Once I spoke with a novice spirit who, while he was in the world, meditated much on Heaven and Hell. By "novice spirits" are meant men who have recently died, who are called spirits because they are then spiritual men. As soon as he entered the spiritual world, he began to meditate in a similar way about Heaven and Hell, and he seemed to himself to be in joy when thinking of Heaven, and in sadness when thinking of Hell. When he noticed he was in the spiritual world, he immediately asked where Heaven and Hell were, and what the nature of each was. They answered: "Heaven is above your head, and Hell is beneath your feet, for you are now in the world of spirits, which is in the middle between Heaven and Hell. But what and of what quality Heaven and Hell are, we cannot describe in a few words." Then, because he burned with a desire for knowing, he threw himself upon his knees and prayed devoutly to God that he might be instructed. And behold, an angel appeared at his right hand and raised him up, saying, "You have prayed to be instructed about Heaven and Hell. **INQUIRE AND LEARN WHAT THE DELIGHTFUL IS, AND YOU WILL KNOW.**" <note>The Latin "Jucundum" refers to the underlying pleasure or delight that drives a person's life and will.</note> With these words, the angel was taken up. 

Then the novice spirit said to himself, "What does this mean: *Inquire and learn what the Delightful is, and you will know what and of what quality Heaven and Hell are?*" Soon leaving that place, he wandered around and asked those he met, "Tell me, if you please, what is 'the Delightful'?" Some said, "What kind of question is this? Who does not know what the delightful is? Is it not joy and gladness? Therefore, the delightful is the delightful; one is like the other; we know no difference." Others said that the delightful was the laughter of the mind, for while the mind laughs, the face is cheerful, the speech is jocular, the gestures are playful, and the whole man is in delight. Some, however, said, "The delightful is nothing other than feasting and eating delicacies, and drinking and getting drunk with noble wine, and then chatting about various things, especially about the games of Venus and Cupid." <note>A poetic way of referring to sexual pleasures and romantic lusts.</note> 

Hearing these things, the novice spirit said indignantly to himself, "These responses are unrefined and not civilized; these delights are neither Heaven nor Hell. I wish I could meet some wise people." He went away from them and asked where the wise were. At that moment, he was seen by a certain angelic spirit, who said: "I perceive that you are fired with a desire for knowing that which is the Universal of Heaven and the Universal of Hell. Because this is **THE DELIGHTFUL**, I will lead you up a hill where those gather daily who examine Effects, those who investigate Causes, and those who explore Ends." <note>In this philosophical framework, "Ends" are the primary purposes or goals, "Causes" are the methods, and "Effects" are the final results.</note> Those there who examine Effects are called Spirits of Sciences (and abstractly, Sciences); those who investigate Causes are called Spirits of Intelligence (and abstractly, Intelligences); and those who explore Ends are called Spirits of Wisdom (abstractly, Wisdoms). Directly above them in Heaven are angels who see causes from ends, and effects from causes; from these angels, those three groups receive enlightenment. 

Then, taking the novice spirit by the hand, he led him up the hill to the assembly of those who explore Ends and are called Wisdoms. He said to them: "Pardon me for ascending to you; the reason is that from my childhood I have meditated on Heaven and Hell, and I have recently come into this world. Some who were then associated with me said that here Heaven is above my head and Hell is beneath my feet, but they did not say what the nature of each was. Therefore, having become anxious from constant thought about them, I prayed to God, and then..."

...an Angel stood and said, “INQUIRE AND LEARN WHAT IS DELIGHTFUL, AND YOU SHALL KNOW.” I inquired, but so far in vain; I therefore ask that, if it please you, you would teach me what is Delightful. To these words the Wisdoms <note>Swedenborg often refers to groups of angels by the quality they embody, here "the Wisdoms" (*Sapientiæ*).</note> replied: Delight is the all of life for everyone in Heaven, and the all of life for everyone in Hell. For those who are in Heaven, it is the Delight of good and truth; but for those who are in Hell, it is the Delight of evil and falsity. For every Delight belongs to love, and Love is the <term>Being (*Esse*)</term> <note>The essential, innermost core of life.</note> of a human’s life. Therefore, just as a human is a human according to the quality of his Love, so he is a human according to the quality of his Delight. The activity of love creates the sense of delight; its activity in Heaven is joined with wisdom, and its activity in Hell is joined with insanity. Each presents Delight in its subjects. However, the Heavens and the Hells are in opposite Delights: the Heavens are in the Love of good and the resulting Delight of doing good, while the Hells are in the love of evil and the resulting Delight of doing evil. If, therefore, you know what Delight is, you will know what and of what quality Heaven and Hell are.

But inquire and learn further what Delight is from those who investigate causes and are called the Intelligences; they are from here to the right. And he went away and approached them, stated the reason for his coming, and asked that they would instruct him on what Delight is. These, gladdened by the question, said: It is true that he who knows Delight knows what and of what quality Heaven and Hell are. The Will, from which a human is a human, is not moved even a tiny point except by Delight; for the Will, viewed in itself, is nothing but the affection of some love, and thus of delight—for it is something pleasurable, and thus a matter of choice, which causes one to will. And because the Will moves the Intellect to think, not the least bit of thought is given except from the delightful influx of the will. The reason this is so is that the Lord, through influx from Himself, actuates all things of the soul and all things of the mind in angels, spirits, and men; and He actuates them through the influx of love and wisdom. This influx is the very activity from which all delight comes, which in its origin is called <term>blessed, prosperous, and happy</term>, and in its derivation is called delightful, pleasant, and pleasurable, and in a universal sense, Good. But the spirits of Hell invert all things in themselves; thus they turn Good into Evil and Truth into Falsity, while the Delight remains constantly. For without the permanence of Delight, they would have no Will, no sensation, and thus no life. From these things it is clear what, of what quality, and from where the Delight of Hell is, as well as what, of what quality, and from where the Delight of Heaven is.

After hearing these things, he was led to the third group, where those were who examine effects and are called the *Sciences*. These said: Descend into the lower Earth and ascend into the upper Earth; in these you will perceive and feel the Delights of both Heaven and Hell.

But look! Just then, at a distance from them, the earth opened, and through the gap three Devils ascended, appearing as if ignited by the delight of their love. And because the Angels associated with the novice spirit perceived that these three had ascended from Hell by Divine Providence, they cried out to the devils: "Do not come any closer! But from the place where you are, tell us something about your Delights." They replied: "Know that everyone, whether they are called good or evil, is in their own Delight—the so-called 'Good' in theirs, and the so-called 'Evil' in theirs." They asked: "What is your Delight?" The devils said it was the Delight of <term>whoredom, revenge, cheating, and blaspheming</term>. They asked again: "What quality do those Delights have for you?" They said that they are perceived by others as stenches from dung, putridity from corpses, and the reek from stagnant urine. They asked: "Are those things delightful to you?" They said: "They are most delightful!" And they said: "Then you are like the unclean beasts that live in such things." They responded: "If we are, we are; but such things are the delicacies of our nostrils." They asked: "What more?" They said: "That everyone is allowed to be in their own Delight, even the most 'unclean' as they call it, provided they do not infest good spirits and angels. But because we could not help but infest them because of our Delight, we were cast into workhouses <note>Latin: *Ergastula*, meaning houses of correction or prisons where hard labor was performed.</note> where we suffer hardships. The inhibition and withdrawal of our Delights there is what is called the torment of Hell; it is also an interior pain." They asked: "Why did you infest the good?" They said they could not do otherwise—it is as if a fury seizes them...

# CHAPTER TEN

## ON

# REFORMATION AND REGENERATION.

571. After the subject of Repentance has been treated, there follows in its proper order the subject of Reformation and Regeneration, because these follow Repentance and, through Repentance, advance by degrees. There are two states that a person must enter and undergo while passing from being <term>Natural</term> <note>In this context, "Natural" refers to the inherited state of a person focused only on the world and self, before spiritual awakening.</note> to being <term>Spiritual</term>. The first state is called REFORMATION, and the second REGENERATION. In the first state, a person looks from his natural self toward the spiritual and desires it; in the second state, he becomes a "naturally spiritual" person. The first state is formed by the truths which belong to faith, through which he looks toward <term>Charity</term> <note>Swedenborg uses "Charity" not just as almsgiving, but as the active love of one's neighbor and doing good from a spiritual motive.</note>; the second state is formed by the "goods" of charity, and from these, he enters into the truths of faith. Or, what is the same thing, the first state is one of thought from the understanding, but the second is one of love from the will. When this second state begins and progresses, a change occurs in the mind; for a turn takes place, because then the love of the will flows into the understanding, and acts upon it and leads it to think in harmony and agreement with its love. Therefore, to the extent that the Good of love then plays the primary role and the truths of faith the secondary, the person is spiritual and is a **New Creature**. He then acts from Charity and speaks from Faith; he feels the "good" of charity and perceives the "truth" of faith; he is then in the Lord, and in Peace, and is thus Regenerated. 

A person who has begun the first state in the world can, after death, be introduced into the second; but he who did not enter the first state in the world cannot be introduced into the second after death, and thus cannot be regenerated. These two states may be compared with the progression of light and heat during the days of springtime: the first with the first glimmer of dawn or the <term>cock-crow</term> <note>original: "gallinaceo". This refers to the very earliest light before sunrise.</note>, the second with the morning and the sunrise; and the progression of this state is like the progression of the day toward noon, and thus into full light and heat. It may also be compared to a harvest, which is first the blade, then grows into ears and spikes, and afterwards the grain is formed within them. Also, it is like a tree, which first grows out of the earth from a seed, then becomes a trunk from which branches go out, and these are adorned with leaves; then it blossoms, and from the innermost part of the flowers, the fruits are initiated, which, as they ripen, produce new seeds like new offspring. The first state, which is that of Reformation, can also be compared to the state of a <term>silkworm</term> <note>original: "bombycis". Swedenborg frequently used the metamorphosis of insects as a metaphor for human spiritual transformation.</note> when it draws out and unfolds from itself filaments of silk; and after its industrious labor, it flies out into the air, nourishing itself no longer on leaves as before, but on the juices of flowers.

->*That unless a person is born again, and as it were created anew, he cannot enter into the Kingdom of God.*<-

572. That unless a person is born again, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God, is the Doctrine of the Lord in the Gospel of John, where it says: "*Jesus said to Nicodemus, Amen, amen, I say to you, unless someone is born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God: and again, amen, amen...*" <note>original: "amen, amen, dico tibi, nisi quis generetur denuo, non potest videre regnum Dei". This is a reference to John 3:3.</note>

“Truly, truly, I say to you, unless anyone is born of water and the spirit, he cannot enter into the *Kingdom of God*; that which is born of the flesh is *flesh*, and that which is generated of the spirit is *spirit*” (John Chapter III: 3, 5, 6). By the *Kingdom of God* is understood both *Heaven* and the *Church*, for the *Kingdom of God* on earth is the *Church*. Similarly, the Kingdom of God is named elsewhere, as in Matthew 11:11, Chapter 12:28, Chapter 21:43; Luke 4:43, Chapter 6:20, Chapter 8:1, 10, Chapter 9:11, 60, 62, Chapter 17:21, and elsewhere. To be generated by water and spirit signifies being born through the truths of Faith and through a life led according to them. That "water" signifies truths may be seen in *The Apocalypse Revealed* <note>original: "Apocalypsi Revelata"—this refers to an earlier work by Swedenborg published in 1766</note>, numbers 50, 614, 615, 685, 932. That "spirit" signifies a life according to Divine truths is evident from the Lord's words in John Chapter 6:63. By the words *Amen, Amen* <note>translated from the Latin "amen, amen," which is itself a transliteration of the Hebrew for "truly" or "verily"</note>, it is signified that something is the truth; and because the Lord was Truth itself, He said it so often. He is even called the *Amen* in Revelation Chapter 3:14. Those who are regenerated are called in the Word <note>The "Word" is the technical term Swedenborg uses for the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note> the *Sons of God* and *Born of God*; and Regeneration is described as a *new heart* and a *new spirit*.

573. Since "to be created" also signifies being regenerated, it is said of one who is born again that they are, as it were, created anew. That "to be created" signifies this in the Word is established by these passages:
> *CREATE in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a steadfast spirit within me* (Psalm 51:12).
> *You open your hand, they are satisfied with good; You send forth your spirit, they are CREATED* (Psalm 104:28, 30).
> *The people who shall be CREATED shall praise Jah* (Psalm 102:18).
> *Behold, I am about to CREATE Jerusalem as an exultation* (Isaiah 65:18).
> *Thus said Jehovah, your Creator, O Jacob, your Former, O Israel: I have redeemed you; I have called everyone by my name, for my glory I have CREATED him* (Isaiah 43:1, 7).
> That they may see, know, consider, and understand that the Holy One of Israel has CREATED this (Isaiah 41:19/20); besides other places where the Lord is called Creator, Former, and Maker. From this, it becomes clear what is meant by these words of the Lord to His disciples:
> *Going into the entire world, preach the Gospel to every CREATURE* (Mark 16:15).
By "creatures" are meant all those who are capable of being regenerated; see also Revelation 3:14 and 2 Corinthians 5:16, 17.

<note>The following paragraph is numbered 474 in the original print, though it falls sequentially between 573 and 575.</note>

474. That a person must be regenerated is evident from all reason; for a person is born into evils of every kind from their parents, and these reside in their <term>natural man</term> <note>The "natural man" refers to our physical and worldly self, driven by inherited instincts and selfish desires, as opposed to the "spiritual man" which is focused on God and the neighbor.</note>, which of itself is diametrically opposed to the spiritual man. And yet, a person is born for Heaven, and no one comes to Heaven unless they become spiritual, which happens solely through regeneration. It follows by necessity that the natural man with its lusts must be tamed, subjugated, and turned upside down; otherwise, one cannot take a single step toward Heaven but sinks deeper and deeper into hell. Who does not see this, if they believe they are born into evils of every kind, and if they acknowledge that there are such things as good and evil, and that one is against the other? And if one believes in life after death, and in hell and heaven—that evils create hell and goods create Heaven. The natural man, viewed in himself regarding his nature, does not differ a bit from the nature of beasts; he is similarly wild, but he is such in regards to his will. However, he differs from beasts in regards to his intellect. The intellect can be elevated above the lusts of the will, and not only see them, but also moderate them. Hence it is that a person can think from the intellect and speak from thought, which beasts cannot do. What a person is like from birth, and what they would be like if they were not regenerated, can be seen from wild animals of every kind: they would be a tiger, a panther, a leopard, a wild pig, a scorpion, a tarantula, a viper, a crocodile, etc. If one were not transformed into a sheep through regeneration, what else would they be but a devil among devils in hell? If the laws of the kingdom did not restrain such people from their innate ferocities, would they not rush upon one another and slaughter each other, or strip one another even to their breeches? How many of the human race are there who are not born as <term>satyrs</term> <note>Mythological creatures known for lust and rowdiness.</note> and <term>priapi</term> <note>A reference to Priapus, a Greek god of fertility, here used to denote excessive sexual lust.</note>, or four-legged lizards? And who among these would not become an ape unless they were regenerated? It is only external morality, learned for the sake of covering up one's inner nature, that prevents this.

575. What an unregenerated person is like can be further described by these comparisons and likenesses in Isaiah:
> *The pelican and the bittern shall possess it, and the owl and the raven shall dwell there; he shall stretch over it the line of emptiness, and...*

## *That the new Generation or Creation is effected by the Lord Alone through Charity and Faith, as the two Means, with the cooperation of man.*

576. That <term>Regeneration</term> <note>the process of being spiritually reborn or "created anew"</note> is effected by the Lord through <term>Charity</term> <note>spiritual love for one’s neighbor</note> and <term>Faith</term> <note>the internal recognition of truth</note> follows from what was demonstrated in the chapters on Charity and Faith—specifically from the point that the Lord, Charity, and Faith make one, just as life, will, and intellect do; and that if they are divided, each of them perishes like a union that has crumbled into dust. These two, Charity and Faith, are called "means" because they join a person with the Lord, and they make charity truly charity and faith truly faith. This cannot happen unless the person also plays a part in the process of Regeneration; this is why it is said to happen "with the cooperation of man." In the preceding discussions, the cooperation of man with the Lord has been mentioned several times; but because the human mind is such that it perceives this in no other way than that a person effects it by their own power, this point will be illustrated again. 

In every movement, and consequently in every action, there is an active and a passive—that is, the "actor" acts, and the "receiver" <note>original: "patiens," the passive element that undergoes the action</note> acts *from* the actor; thus, from both comes a single action. By way of comparison, it is like a mill moved by a wheel, a carriage by a horse, motion by endeavor, an effect by a cause, or a dead force by a living one. In general, it is like the "instrumental" acting with the "principal"; everyone knows that these two together perform one single action. Regarding Charity and Faith, the Lord acts, and the person acts from the Lord, for the Lord’s active power is within the person’s passive reception. Therefore, the power to act well is from the Lord, and the resulting will to act is *as if* it were the person's own, because they possess <term>Free Will</term> <note>original: "libero arbitrio," the ability to choose or act freely</note>. Through this free will, a person can act as one with the Lord and so be conjoined to Him; or they can act from the power of hell, which is external, and so separate themselves. The action of a person that is in harmony with the action of the Lord is what is meant here by "Cooperation." To make this more clearly understood, it will be further illustrated by comparisons below.

577. From this it also follows that the Lord is continually in the act of regenerating a person, because He is continually in the act of saving them; and no one can be saved unless they are regenerated, according to the Lord’s own words in John: *That he who is not born anew cannot see the kingdom of God*, Chapter 3: 3, 5, 6. Regeneration is therefore the means of salvation, and Charity and Faith are the means of regeneration. To claim that Regeneration follows the faith of the church today—which is a faith without the cooperation of man—is the vanity of vanities. 

Action and cooperation, as described, can be seen in everything that possesses activity and movement. Such action and cooperation exist in the heart and in all its arteries: the heart acts, and the artery, from its coverings or tunics, cooperates; hence, circulation. It is the same with the lungs: the air acts by its weight according to the height of the atmosphere, and the ribs first cooperate with the lungs, and soon after the lungs with the ribs; hence, respiration. This occurs in every membrane in the body; thus the <term>meninges</term> <note>membranes covering the brain</note> of the brain, the <term>pleura</term> <note>lining of the lungs</note>, the <term>peritoneum</term> <note>lining of the abdominal cavity</note>, the diaphragm, and the rest that cover the internal organs and compose them within, act and are acted upon, and thus cooperate, for they are elastic; from this comes their existence and continued state. It is the same in every fiber and nerve, and in every muscle—indeed, even in cartilage—it is well known that in each of these there is action and cooperation. Such cooperation is also in every sense; for the sensory organs, like the motor organs of the body, consist of fibers, membranes, and muscles. But to describe the cooperation of each one is unnecessary; for it is known that light acts upon the eye, sound upon the ear—

It asserts that while the power to do good comes from the Lord, humans must use their free will to act in harmony with that power.</summary>

If life alone acted, and the human did not cooperate as if of himself, he could no more think than a tree trunk, or than a temple when the Minister is preaching; the temple might indeed feel the sound like an echo rebounding from its doors, but it would understand nothing of the speech. 578. It can also be illustrated by comparisons what a human would be like if he did not cooperate with the Lord: when he perceives and feels something spiritual of Heaven and the Church, it would feel as if something antipathetic or discordant were flowing in—like a stench to the nose, a discord to the ear, a monstrosity to the eye, and a foulness to the tongue. If the delight of charity and the pleasantness of faith were to flow into the spiritual organism of the mind of those who are in the delight of evil and falsity, and if those delights and pleasantnesses were forced in, they would be distressed and tortured, and finally they would fall into a faint. Because that organism consists of perpetual <term>helices</term> <note>original: "helicibus," referring to spiral-like spiritual structures</note>, in such people it would wrap itself into coils and be twisted like a snake on a pile of ants. That this is so has been witnessed by me from much experience in the **Spiritual World**.

### *That everyone, because everyone has been redeemed, can be regenerated, each according to their own state.*

579. In order that these things may be understood, something must first be presented regarding <term>Redemption</term>; the Lord came into the world primarily for these two reasons: to remove hell from the angel and from the human, and to <term>glorify His Human</term> <note>the process by which Jesus made His human nature Divine</note>. For before the Lord's coming, hell had grown to such an extent that it infested the angels of heaven, and by interposing itself between heaven and the world, it cut off the Lord's communication with the people of the earth. Because of this, no Divine Truth or Good could pass through from the Lord to humans; consequently, total Damnation threatened the entire human race, and even the Angels of heaven could not have long remained in their integrity. Therefore, so that hell might be moved back, and thus that imminent damnation removed, the Lord came into the World; He removed hell, subjugated it, and thus opened Heaven, so that afterward He could be present with the people of the earth and save those who live according to His precepts—consequently, to regenerate and save them, for those who are regenerated are saved. This is how it is understood that "everyone, because everyone has been redeemed, can be regenerated," and because regeneration and salvation make one, that everyone can be saved. Thus, the Church's teaching that "without the Lord's coming no one could have been saved" is to be understood as: without the Lord's coming no one could have been regenerated. As for the other purpose for which the Lord came into the world, which is to glorify His Human, it was because he thus became the **Redeemer**, **Regenerator**, and **Savior** forever; for it is not to be believed that by a Redemption performed once in the World, all were redeemed thereafter, but that He perpetually redeems those who believe in Him and do His words. But more on these matters may be seen in the Chapter on Redemption.

# NEW HEAVENS AND THE NEW CHURCH.

...constitute the Lord's Church, and those who constitute the internal Church do so differently; this variety is infinite, just as the variety of faces and minds is infinite; yet every person can be <term>regenerated</term> <note>Regeneration is the process of being spiritually reborn or made new by God.</note> and saved according to their own state. That this is so can be seen from the Heavens, into which all who are regenerated enter. There are three: the Highest, the Middle, and the Last. Into the Highest enter those who, through regeneration, receive love for the Lord; into the Middle, those who receive love toward the neighbor; and into the Last, those who simply practice external <term>charity</term> while simultaneously acknowledging the Lord as God the Redeemer and Savior. All these are saved, but in different ways. That everyone is able to be regenerated and thus saved is because the Lord, with His Divine Good and Truth, is present with every human being; from this comes the life of every person, and from this comes the faculty of understanding and willing, and with these, **Free Will** in spiritual matters. These are lacking in no one. Means for this have also been given: to Christians in the **Word**, and to Gentiles in their respective religions, which teach that there is a God and provide precepts concerning good and evil. From this it follows that anyone can be saved; consequently, if a person is not saved, the fault does not lie with the Lord, but with the person for failing to cooperate.

581. That <term>Redemption</term> and the **Passion of the Cross** are two distinct things, which must not be confused at all, and that the Lord, through both, placed Himself in the power to regenerate and save humanity, was shown in the chapter on Redemption. From the faith accepted by the modern Church regarding the Passion of the Cross—that it was Redemption itself—there have arisen ranks of horrible falsehoods concerning God, Faith, Charity, and the rest of the things that hang from these three in an unbroken chain. Regarding God, for instance, it is falsely taught that He concluded the damnation of the human race and wished to be moved to mercy only through the damnation imposed upon His Son, or received by the Son upon Himself; and that only those are saved to whom the merit of Christ is given, either by foresight or predestination. From that fallacy, this too was excluded from their faith: that those gifted with such faith are regenerated at the same time without any cooperation of their own—indeed, that they are thus absolved from the damnation of the law and are no longer under the law, but under grace. This is claimed even though the Lord said *that He did not remove even a tittle of the law* <note>original: "quod ne quidem apicem legis sustulerit." This refers to Matthew 5:18-19 and Luke 16:17, emphasizing that the moral law remains in effect.</note>, Matthew 5:18, 19; Luke 16:17; and He also commanded His disciples to preach repentance for the remission of sins, Luke 24:47; Mark 6:12; and He Himself said, *The Kingdom of God is at hand; repent, and believe the Gospel*, Mark 1:15. By the "Gospel," it is meant that they can be regenerated and thus saved; which could not have happened unless the Lord had accomplished Redemption—that is, unless He had taken away the power of Hell through battles against it and victories over it, and unless He had glorified His **Humanity**, that is, made it Divine.

582. Consider from rational thought what the entire human race would be like if the faith of the modern Church were to persist—the belief that people are redeemed solely by the Passion of the Cross, and that those gifted with that merit of the Lord are not under the damnation of the law. Consider also the idea that this faith (which a person cannot even know is present within them) remits sins and regenerates, and that a human’s cooperation in the act of faith—that is, while it is being given and entering—would destroy that faith and take away salvation with it, because the person would be mixing their own merit with the merit of Christ. Consider, I say, from rational thought, whether the whole **Word** would not thus be rejected, where it is primarily taught that <term>regeneration</term> occurs through spiritual washing from evils and through the exercise of charity. What then is the **Decalogue** <note>The Ten Commandments.</note>, the very beginning of reformation, other than paper sold in shops and shaped into wrappers for spices? What then is Religion, but a kind of lamentation that one is a sinner, and a plea that God the Father have mercy for the sake of His Son’s passion—a thing of the mouth and lungs only, with no action from the heart? And what then is Redemption but a "papal indulgence," or little more than the self-flagellation of a monk on behalf of a whole congregation, as is sometimes done? If that faith alone were to regenerate a person, and Repentance and Charity contributed nothing, what then would the internal man be (which is the spirit that lives after death) but like a city set on fire, whose ruins make up the external man? Or like a field or plain devasta-

### That Regeneration occurs in the same way a human is conceived, carried in the womb, born, and educated.

583. In a human being, there is a perpetual <term>correspondence</term> <note>Correspondence is the relationship between the spiritual world and the natural world, where physical things reflect spiritual realities.</note> between those things that happen naturally and those that happen spiritually—or those things done by the body and those by the spirit. The reason for this is that a human is born spiritual as to the soul, but is clothed with a natural layer that constitutes the material body. Therefore, when this body is laid aside, the soul—now clothed in a spiritual body—enters the World where all things are spiritual, and is there joined with its like. Now, because the spiritual body must be formed within the material body, and is formed through the truths and goods <note>In this context, "truths" refer to spiritual insights and "goods" refer to acts of love and kindness.</note> that flow in from the Lord through the spiritual World and are received by the person within those things of the natural world called civil and moral virtues, it is clear how its formation occurs. And because, as was said, there is a perpetual correspondence in a human between the natural and spiritual processes, it follows that it is like conception, gestation in the womb, birth, and education. For this reason, in the **Word** <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note>, natural births signify spiritual births, which are births of good and truth; for whatever is in the literal sense of the Word, which is natural, involves and signifies something spiritual. It has been fully shown in the chapter on <term>Sacred Scripture</term> that there is a spiritual sense in each and every part of the literal sense of the Word. That the natural births named in the Word involve spiritual births is clearly evident from these passages:

*"We have conceived, we have been in pain, we have as it were brought forth; we have not wrought any salvation,"* <note>original: "Concepimus, parturivimus, quasi peperimus, salutes non fecimus"</note> Isaiah 26:16. *"The earth travailed before the Lord,"* <note>original: "A coram Domino parturrit terra"</note> Psalm 114:7. *"Shall the earth be made to bring forth in one day? Shall I break open and not cause to bring forth, and shall I cause to be born and shut the womb?"* <note>original: "Num parturivit terra die uno, num Ego frangam & non generem, & generari faciam, & non concluderim"</note> Isaiah 66:7–10. *"Sin shall be in great pain and shall not break through,"* <note>original: "Parturit Sin & non erit ad perrumpendum"</note> Ezekiel 30:15–16. *"The sorrows of a woman in travail shall come upon Ephraim; he is an unwise son, for the time should not stay in the womb of sons,"* <note>original: "Dolores parturientis venient Ephraimo, ille filius non sapiens, quia tempus non stat in utero filiorum"</note> Hosea 13:12–13; and likewise in many other places. 

Since natural generations signify spiritual generations in the Word, and these are from the Lord, He is therefore called the **Former** and the **Bringer-forth from the womb**, as is clear from these passages: *"Jehovah your Maker, and your Former from the womb,"* Isaiah 44:2. *"My Bringer-forth from the womb,"* Psalm 22:10. *"Upon Thee I have been cast from the womb; from the bowels of my mother Thou art my Bringer-forth,"* Psalm 71:6. *"Listen to Me, you who are carried from the womb, borne from the vulva,"* Isaiah 46:3; besides other places. For this reason, the Lord is called **Father**, as in Isaiah 9:5, Chapter 63:16, John 10:30, Chapter 14:8–9; and those who are in goods and truths from Him are called "sons" and "born of God," and "brothers" to one another, Matthew 23:8. Similarly, the **Church** is called **Mother**, Hosea 2:2, 5, Ezekiel 16:45.

584. From these points it is now clear that there is a Correspondence between natural generations and spiritual generations. And because there is a Correspondence, it follows that not only can conception, gestation in the womb, birth, and education be predicated of the new generation [regeneration], but they actually occur. What their nature is will be shown in its proper order in this Article on Regeneration. Here, it need only be said that the "seed" of a human is conceived inwardly in the understanding, and is formed in the will, and from there is transferred to the testis, where it clothes itself with a natural covering, and is thus carried into the womb and enters the world. Furthermore, there is a correspondence of human regeneration with all things in the vegetable kingdom; which is why in the Word a human is described by a Tree, its truth...

through seed, and its good through fruit. That an evil tree can be as if born anew, and afterwards bear good fruit and good seed, is clear from graftings and inoculations; for then, even though the same sap ascends from the root through the trunk all the way to the graft or the bud, it is turned into good sap and makes the tree good. It is similar in the Church with those who are grafted into the Lord, as He teaches in these words: *"I am the Vine, you are the branches; he who abides in Me, and I in him, bears much fruit; unless a person abides in Me, he is cast out like a branch, and having withered, is thrown into the fire"* (John 15:5, 6).

585. That the growth of not only trees but also all shrubs <term>corresponds</term> <note>Correspondence is the spiritual principle that natural things reflect or mirror spiritual realities.</note> to the reproduction of humans has been handed down by many learned men; therefore, as a finishing touch, I will add something about this. In trees and in all other subjects of the **Vegetable Kingdom**, there are not two sexes, male and female, but every single thing there is male; the Earth or soil alone is the common Mother, acting as the Female. For she receives the seeds of all plants, opens them, carries them as if in a womb, and then nourishes and gives birth to them—that is, brings them out into the light of day—and afterwards clothes and sustains them. When the Earth first opens a seed, she begins with the root, which is like a heart; from there she sends out and transmits sap like blood, and thus creates a body equipped with limbs. Its "body" is the trunk itself, while the branches and their twigs are its limbs. The leaves, which she brings forth immediately after "birth," serve as lungs; for just as the heart without the lungs does not produce motion or sensation and thus does not give life to a human, so the root does not grow a tree or shrub without leaves. The flowers that precede the fruit are the means of refining the sap (its blood) and separating its coarser parts from the purer ones; they also serve to form a new little trunk within their bosom for the influx of these purer parts, through which the refined sap may flow, and thus initiate and gradually form the fruit—which can be compared to a womb in which the seeds are perfected.

The **vegetative soul**, which reigns intimately in every particle of the sap, or its reproductive essence, comes from no other source than the heat of the spiritual world. Because this heat is from the spiritual Sun there, it breathes nothing but generation and, through this, the continuation of creation. And because it essentially breathes the generation of the human being, it induces a certain likeness of a human upon whatever it generates. Let no one wonder at the statement that the subjects of the vegetable kingdom are only male, and that the Earth or soil alone is like a common Mother or female; this will be illustrated by a similar case among bees. According to the firsthand observations of **SWAMMERDAM** <note>Jan Swammerdam (1637–1680) was a Dutch biologist famous for his microscopic studies of insects.</note> in his *The Bible of Nature* <note>original: "Biblia Naturae"</note>, there is only one common mother from whom all the offspring of the entire hive are produced. Since these small animals have only one common mother, why should it not be so for all shrubs? That the Earth is a common mother can also be illustrated spiritually; it is shown by the fact that the "Earth" in the Word <note>Swedenborg uses "the Word" to refer to the Sacred Scriptures.</note> signifies the Church, and the Church is the common Mother, as she is also called in the Word. For the fact that the Earth signifies the Church, consult *The Apocalypse Revealed* <note>original: "Apocalypsin Revelatam"</note>, numbers 285 and 902, where this is shown. Furthermore, the reason the earth or soil can enter into the innermost part of the seed all the way to its reproductive center, and draw this out and carry it around, is because every tiny grain of dust or pollen exhales something subtle from its essence, like an effluvium that penetrates; this occurs through the active force of heat from the spiritual world.

586. That a human being cannot be <term>regenerated</term> except gradually [successively] can be illustrated by each and every thing that exists in the natural world. A tree cannot grow into a tree in one day; rather, it develops first from a seed, then from a root, and then from a shoot, from which a trunk is formed, and from this proceed branches with leaves, and finally flowers and fruit. Nor does wheat or barley rise into a harvest in one day. A house is not built in a day, nor does a human reach their full stature in one day—much less their wisdom. Nor is the Church established and perfected in a day; nor is there any progression toward an end unless there is a beginning from which to start. Those who conceive of **Regeneration** otherwise know nothing of Charity...

## *That the first act of the new generation is called Reformation, which is of the understanding; and that the second act is called Regeneration, which is of the will and from there of the understanding.*

587. Since here and in what follows we deal with <term>Reformation</term> <note>Reformation is the intellectual stage of spiritual growth where a person learns and accepts truths.</note> and with <term>Regeneration</term> <note>Regeneration is the deeper stage where those truths are put into practice and change the person's heart or will.</note>, and Reformation is ascribed to the **Understanding** while Regeneration is ascribed to the **Will**, it is necessary that the differences between the Understanding and the Will be known. These were described above in number 397; therefore it is advisable that those be read first, and afterwards what is in this Article. It was also shown there that the evils into which a person is born are ingrained in the Will of the <term>natural man</term> <note>The "natural man" refers to the part of the human personality focused on the physical world and self-interest.</note>, and that the Will leads the understanding to favor it by thinking in a way that agrees with its desires. Therefore, for a human to be regenerated, it is necessary that this occurs through the Understanding as an intermediate cause. This happens through the instructions the Understanding receives, which come first from parents and teachers, and later from reading the **Word** <note>The Word refers to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note>, from sermons, books, and conversations. 

Those things which the understanding receives from these sources are called **truths**; therefore, it is the same whether one says that Reformation occurs through the Understanding, or that it occurs through Truths which the understanding receives. For truths teach a person in Whom and what to believe, as well as what to do, and thus what to will; for whatever a person does, they do from the will according to the understanding. Since, therefore, the human Will itself is evil from birth, and because the Understanding teaches what is evil and good, and one is able to will the one and not the other, it follows that a human must be reformed through the Understanding. As long as someone sees and acknowledges in the mind that evil is evil and good is good, and thinks that the good ought to be chosen, that state is called **Reformation**; but when they actually will to flee evil and do good, the state of **Regeneration** begins.

588. For this purpose, the faculty of elevating the understanding almost into the light in which the Angels of heaven are was given to man. This allows him to see what he ought to will and then do, so that he may be prosperous in the World for a time and blessed after death forever. A person becomes prosperous and blessed if they acquire wisdom and keep the will under its obedience; but they become unprosperous and unhappy if they place their understanding under the obedience of the will. 

The reason for this is that the Will, from birth, inclines toward evils—even enormous ones. Therefore, unless it were restrained by the understanding, a human left to the freedom of their own will would rush into wicked deeds. From an innate wild nature, they would plunder and slaughter for their own sake anyone who does not favor them or indulge their desires. Furthermore, unless the Understanding could be perfected separately, and the Will through it, a human would not be a human, but a beast. Without that separation and without the ascent of the understanding above the will, a person could not think or speak from thought, but would only make sounds expressing their raw emotion; nor could they act from reason, but only from instinct. Still less could they have known the things of God, and through them known God Himself, and thus be joined to Him and live forever. 

A human thinks and wills <term>as if from himself</term> <note>original: "sicut a se". This is a central concept in Swedenborg's theology: the appearance that we act on our own power, which is necessary for true human life and connection with the Divine.</note>, and this "as if from himself" is the reciprocal side of the connection; for a connection without a reciprocal response is impossible, just as there is no connection of an active force with a passive one without some adaptation or application. God alone acts, and man allows himself to be acted upon, yet he cooperates in every appearance "as if from himself," even though inwardly the power is from God. From these things, if rightly perceived, it can be seen what the love of the human will is like if it is elevated through the understanding, and what it is like if it is not—and thus, what kind of person they truly are.

->THE NEW HEAVEN AND THE NEW CHURCH<-

589. It should be known that the capacity to elevate the understanding even to the level of intelligence found among the **Angels of Heaven** is inherent in every human being from creation—whether they are evil or good—and indeed even in every devil in hell, for all who are in hell were once humans. This has been shown to me many times through living experience. However, the reason they are not truly in a state of intelligence, but rather in a state of spiritual insanity, is because they do not will what is good, but what is evil. Consequently, they are averse to knowing and understanding truths, for truths are for the sake of good and stand against evil. From this it is also clear that the **First** stage of the new generation <note>The "new generation" refers to the process of being "born again" or spiritually recreated.</note> is the reception of truths in the understanding; and the **Second** stage is that the person wills to act according to those truths, and eventually actually does them. Truly, no one can be called "reformed" by a mere knowledge of truths alone; for a human, by the capacity to elevate the understanding above the love of the will, can grasp truths and even speak, teach, and preach them. But that person is **Reformed** who is in the affection of truth for the sake of truth; for this affection joins itself with the will, and if it continues, it joins the will to the understanding. It is then that **Regeneration** begins. How regeneration proceeds and is perfected thereafter will be discussed in the following sections.

590. What a person is like whose understanding is elevated, but whose will’s love is not, can be illustrated through comparisons. Such a person is like an eagle flying on high, but as soon as it sees food below—such as poultry, cygnets <note>Young swans.</note>, or even lambs—it drops down in a moment and devours them. He is also like an adulterer who hides a prostitute in a cellar below, but goes up to the highest room of the house to speak wisely about chastity with those staying there in the presence of his wife, and then steals away from the company to satisfy his lust below with the prostitute. He is also like the marsh-flies that fly in a column over the head of a running horse, but when the horse stops, they fall down and immerse themselves in their marsh. Such is the person who is in a state of elevation regarding the understanding, while the love of the will remains below at the foot, immersed in the uncleanness of nature and the lusts of the senses. But because they shine as if from wisdom in their understanding, even though the will is against it, they may also be compared to serpents with glittering scales, or to beetles that shine as if made of gold, as well as to <term>will-o'-the-wisps</term> <note>Ghostly lights seen over marshes, known as "ignis fatuus" in Latin.</note> in marshes, to glowing rotten wood, and to phosphorus. Among these are those who can mimic **angels of light**, both among people in the world and, after death, among the angels of heaven; but after a brief examination, these are stripped of their garments and cast down naked. This same thing cannot happen in the world, however, because their spirit is not open there, but is covered over by a persona, like that of actors on a stage. The fact that they can mimic angels of light with their face and speech is both the cause and the proof that they can elevate the understanding almost to angelic wisdom, far above the love of the will, as has been said. Now, because the internal and external of a human can thus go in opposite directions, and because the body is cast off while the spirit remains, it is clear that a dark spirit can dwell under a fair face, and a fiery one behind a smooth mouth. Therefore, my friend, judge a person not by his mouth but by his heart—that is, not by his speech, but by his deeds. For the Lord says:

->*Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly are ravenous wolves; by their fruits you shall know them.* <note>Matthew 7:15–16. original: "Cavete vobis a pseudoprophetis, qui veniunt ad vos in indumentis ovium, intrinsecus autem sunt lupi rapaces; e fructibus eorum cognoscite eos."</note><-

### *That the Internal man is first to be reformed, and through this the External, and that the person is thus regenerated.*

591. That the <term>Internal man</term> <note>The "Internal man" refers to the higher, spiritual part of the human mind that communicates with heaven, as opposed to the "External man" which deals with the physical world.</note> is first to be regenerated and through it the **External**, is commonly said in the Church today; but by the "Internal man" nothing else is thought of than **Faith**, which is the belief that God the Father imputes the merit and righteousness of His Son, and sends the Holy Spirit. ...that from it the **External** flows forth, which is the moral, natural person, and that this is merely an appendix to it—comparable to the tail of a horse or an ox, or like the tail of a peacock or a bird of paradise, which is attached to its rear without being truly joined. For it is said that **Charity** "follows" that faith, but if charity enters from the person's own will, that faith perishes. Truly, because no other **Internal man** is acknowledged in the Church today, there is no real Internal man at all; for no one knows whether that faith has been granted to them. Moreover, it has been shown above that such a faith is impossible and therefore imaginary. It follows from this that today, among those who have confirmed themselves in that faith, there is no Internal man other than the natural one, which from birth overflows with every kind of evil. Additionally, they believe that **Regeneration** and sanctification follow that faith of their own accord, and that human cooperation—the only means by which regeneration actually occurs—must be excluded. This is why Regeneration is not understood in today's Church, despite the Lord's clear statement that "unless a person is born again, they cannot see the kingdom of God."

592. But the **Internal and External man** of the New Church are completely different. The **Internal man** belongs to a person's **Will**, from which they think when left to themselves, as if they were "at home." But the **External man** is the person's action and speech, which they perform in a Gathering, and thus "abroad." Consequently, the Internal man is **Charity**, because charity belongs to the will; and it is simultaneously **Faith**, which belongs to the thought. Before regeneration, both of these constitute the "natural man," who is thus divided into internal and external. This is evident from the fact that a person is not allowed to act and speak in a Gathering or in public in the same way they do when left to themselves at home. The cause of this division is that civil laws prescribe punishments for those who act wickedly and rewards for those who act well; thus, people force themselves to separate the External man from the Internal. No one wants to be punished, and everyone wants to be rewarded with wealth and honors. A person cannot achieve these things unless they live according to those laws. This is why morality and benevolence exist in external behaviors, even among those who have no morality or benevolence in their internal selves. This is the origin of all hypocrisy, flattery, and pretense.

593. Regarding the division of the natural man into two forms: there is an actual division of both the will and the thought. Every action of a person proceeds from their will, and every speech from their thought. Therefore, another "will" is formed by the person beneath the previous one, and similarly another "thought"; yet both together constitute the natural man. This will formed by the person can be called the <term>corporeal will</term> <note>A "corporeal" or bodily will is one directed entirely toward outward appearances and social survival.</note>, because it moves the body to carry itself morally; and that thought can be called <term>pulmonary thought</term> <note>Literally "thought of the lungs," referring to the physical act of producing speech as opposed to the internal intention of the mind.</note>, because it moves the tongue and lips to speak things that belong to the intellect. 

This thought and that will together can be compared to the <term>bast</term> <note>original: *philyra*; the fibrous inner bark of a tree</note> that adheres to the inside of a tree's bark, or to the membrane of an eggshell. Between these lies the internal natural man. If that internal man is evil, it can be compared to the wood of a rotten tree, around which the bark and its inner layer appear healthy, or to a rotten egg inside a white shell. What the internal natural man is like from birth must be stated: his will inclines toward evils of every kind, and his thought consequently inclines toward falsities of every kind. 

This, therefore, is the internal man who must be **Regenerated**. Unless this part is regenerated, there is nothing but hatred against everything belonging to charity, and a burning anger against everything belonging to faith. It follows that the internal natural man must be regenerated first, and through him the external. This is according to order. To attempt to regenerate the internal through the external is against order. For the internal is like a soul in the external—not only in general but in every specific detail. It resides in every word a person speaks, even without the person knowing it. Because of this, **Angels** can perceive the quality of a person's will from a single action, and the quality of their thought from a single word—whether it be hellish or heavenly. They know the whole person from these; they perceive the "affection" (the feeling) of the thought from the sound of the voice, and the "love" of the will from the gesture or form of the action. They perceive these things no matter how much the person pretends to be a Christian or a moral citizen.

594. The regeneration of man is described in Ezekiel by the dry bones, upon which sinews were laid, then flesh and skin, and finally the spirit was breathed into them, by which they lived again (Chapter 37:1–14). That regeneration was represented by these things is clearly evident from the words there: *These bones are the whole house of Israel* (Verse 11). It is also compared there to graves, for it is read that He would open the graves, and cause the bones to come up from there, and put a spirit in them, and place them upon the land of Israel (Verses 12, 13, 14); by the "land of Israel," here and elsewhere, is understood the Church. The reason regeneration was represented by bones and graves is that an unregenerate man is called "dead," and a regenerate man "alive"; for in the latter there is spiritual life, but in the former, spiritual death.

595. In every created thing in the world, whether living or dead, there is an **Internal** and an **External**; one is never found without the other, just as there is no effect without a cause. Every created thing is valued according to its internal goodness, and is held in contempt for its internal wickedness; likewise, external goodness is [disregarded] if there is internal wickedness within it. Every wise man in the world and every angel in heaven judges in this way. But what the unregenerate man is like, and what the regenerate man is like, can be illustrated by comparisons.

The unregenerate man, who mimics a moral citizen and a Christian man, can be compared to a corpse wrapped in spices, which nevertheless spreads a stench that infects the spices, works its way into the nostrils, and harms the brain. He can also be compared to a gilded mummy, or one placed in a silver casket, which, when looked into, reveals a hideously black body. He may be compared to bones or skeletons in a tomb adorned with lapis lazuli <note>A deep-blue metamorphic rock prized since antiquity for its intense color.</note> and other precious things. He may also be compared to the rich man who was clothed in purple and fine linen, whose internal, however, was infernal (Luke 16). He may further be compared to poison with a sugary taste; to flowering hemlock; to fruits in shining rinds whose pits are eaten away by worms; and also to an ulcer covered with a plaster and then a thin skin, in which there is nothing but corruption. 

In the world, the internal can be judged by the external, but only by those who do not possess internal good themselves and who therefore judge by appearances. It is quite different in heaven; for when the versatile body—which surrounds the spirit and is flexible from evil to good—is separated by death, then the internal remains, for this constitutes the person’s spirit. Then it appears, even from a distance, like a snake that has cast its skin, or like rotten wood stripped of the bark or rind in which it shone.

But it is otherwise with the regenerate man. His **Internal** is good, and although his **External** is similar to the external of the other, his external differs from that of the former as heaven differs from hell, because a soul of good is within it. It does not matter whether he is a great nobleman who lives in a palace and walks surrounded by attendants, or whether he lives in a cottage and is served by a single boy; indeed, it matters not whether he is a Primate <note>original: "Primas"; a high-ranking bishop or archbishop.</note> girded in a purple cloak and a two-tiered miter <note>original: "cidari duorum graduum"; a ceremonial headcovering representing ecclesiastical rank.</note>, or whether he is a shepherd of a few sheep in the forest, covered in a loose rustic cloak and with his head covered by a simple cap. Gold is still gold, whether it shines when placed in the fire or whether its surface has been blackened over smoke; and whether it has been cast into a beautiful form like that of an infant, or an unappealing form like that of a mouse. Mice made of gold and placed next to the Ark were even accepted and were pleasing (1 Samuel 6:3, 4, 5, etc.), for gold signifies internal good. A diamond and a ruby, in whatever matrix <note>The surrounding rock or stony material in which a gem or crystal is embedded.</note> of limestone or clay they are removed from, are similarly valued for their internal goodness, just like those in a Queen’s necklace, and so forth. From these things it is clear that the external is valued by the internal, and not the other way around.
