### *Since this is the case, a battle arises between the Internal and External man, and then the one who wins rules over the other.*

596. The reason that a battle arises at that time is because the **Internal man** is reformed by means of truths, and from these truths, he sees what is evil and false; yet these evils and falsities are still present in the **External** or natural man. Therefore, a disagreement first arises between the new will, which is above, and the old will, which is below. Because this conflict is between the two wills, it is also between the delights of each. For it is well known that *the flesh is against the spirit, and the spirit against the flesh* <note>original: "caro sit contra spiritum, & spiritus contra carnem"; a reference to Galatians 5:17</note>, and that the flesh with its lusts must be subdued before the spirit can act and the man can become new. After this disagreement of the wills, a battle breaks out, which is called <term>Spiritual Temptation</term> <note>In this context, "temptation" refers not just to a desire to sin, but to an intense internal struggle where one's spiritual life feels at risk</note>. However, this temptation or battle does not take place between "goods" and "evils," but between the <term>truths of good</term> and the <term>falsities of evil</term>. For "good" cannot fight by itself, but fights through "truths"; nor can "evil" fight by itself, but through its own "falsities." In the same way, the will cannot fight by itself but acts through the understanding, where its truths reside. A person does not feel that battle except as a pang of conscience within himself; yet it is the Lord and the devil (that is, hell) who are fighting in the man, struggling for dominion over him, or who shall possess him. The devil or hell attacks the man and calls out his evils, while the Lord protects him and calls out his goods. But even though that battle takes place in the spiritual world, it still happens in the man between the truths of good and the falsities of evil that are in him. Therefore, the man must fight exactly as if by his own power, for he has **free will** <note>original: "libero arbitrio"</note> to act for the Lord or to act for the devil. He acts for the Lord if he remains in truths from a place of good, and for the devil if he remains in falsities from a place of evil. From this it follows that whichever one wins—whether the internal man or the external—will rule over the other. It is exactly like two enemies fighting to see who will be the master of the other's kingdom; the one who wins takes the kingdom and brings everyone there under his obedience. Thus, if the Internal man wins, he commands and subdues all the evils of the external man, and then the process of regeneration continues; but if the external man wins, he commands and scatters all the goods of the internal man, and then regeneration perishes.

597. Today it is indeed known that "Temptations" exist, but hardly anyone knows where they come from, what they are like, and what good they produce. Where they come from and what they are like was shown just above, as well as what good they produce: namely, that when the Internal man wins, the External is subdued. Once the External is subdued, lusts are dispersed, and in their place, affections for good and truth are implanted. These are arranged so that the goods and truths which a person wills and thinks, he also actually performs and speaks from the heart. Beyond this, through victory over the external man, a person becomes spiritual and is then associated by the Lord with the Angels of Heaven, who are all spiritual. The reason why Temptations have not been understood until now—and why hardly anyone has known their source, nature, or benefit—is because the Church has not been in truths until now. No one is in truths unless they approach the Lord directly and reject the former faith and embrace the new. This is why no one has been admitted into any spiritual temptation for many ages—not since the age when the **Council of Nicaea** <note>The Council of Nicaea (325 AD) is criticized by the author for establishing the doctrine of the Trinity in a way that he believes divided God into three persons, leading to spiritual darkness</note> introduced the faith in three Gods. For if anyone had been admitted into it, they would have immediately succumbed, and thus would have plunged themselves deeper into hell. The "contrition" which is claimed to precede the modern Faith is not Temptation; I have asked many people about it, and they said it is a mere word and nothing more, unless perhaps it is some fearful thought about hellfire among the simple-minded.

598. After the Temptation is over, the person is in Heaven as far as the Internal man is concerned, and in the world by means of the External man. Therefore, through temptations in man, a conjunction is formed of Heaven...

...of Heaven and the World, and then the Lord rules his world from Heaven through him according to order. The opposite occurs if a man remains <term>natural</term> <note>that is, focused only on physical reality and self-interest</note>; then he desires to rule Heaven from the World. Such is the case with everyone who is in the love of ruling from self-love. If this person is examined inwardly, he does not believe in any God but in himself; and after death, he believes he is a god who prevails over others by power. Such insanity exists in hell, which has sunk so deep that some say they are God the Father, some the Son of God, and some the Holy Spirit; and among the Jews, some claim to be the Messiah. This makes it clear what a man becomes after death if the natural man is not <term>regenerated</term> <note>spiritually reborn</note>, and what he would become in his fantasies if a <term>New Church</term> were not established by the Lord, in which genuine truths are taught. This is what is meant by these words of the Lord: *“In the <term>consummation of the age</term> <note>original: "consummatione sæculi"; meaning the end of an era or the end of the current church's spiritual life</note>, that is, at the end of today's Church, there will be such affliction as has not been since the beginning of the World, nor ever shall be; therefore, unless those days were shortened, no flesh would be saved” (Matthew 24:21, 22).*

599. The Lord performs a <term>particular Redemption</term> <note>Redemption on the level of the individual person</note> during a person’s struggles or <term>temptations</term>, just as He performed a <term>total Redemption</term> while He was in the World. In the World, the Lord <term>glorified</term> His Human through battles and temptations—that is, He made it Divine. Similarly now, in the individual person who is in temptations, the Lord fights for them, overcomes the infernal spirits who infest them, and "glorifies" them after the temptation—that is, He makes them spiritual. After His universal Redemption, the Lord restored all things in Heaven and in Hell to order; He does the same for the person after temptation, namely, He restores all things of Heaven and the World within that person to order. After the Redemption, the Lord established a New Church; similarly, He also establishes the things of the Church within the individual and makes them into a "church in miniature." After the Redemption, the Lord gave peace to those who believed in Him, for He said, *“My peace I leave with you, my peace I give to you; not as the world gives, do I give to you” (John 14:27)*; similarly, He gives the person a sense of peace after temptation—that is, joy of mind and consolation. From this, it is clear that the Lord is a Redeemer for eternity.

600. An <term>internal man</term> who is regenerated while the <term>external man</term> is not simultaneously so can be compared to a bird flying in the air without a seat on dry land, but only in a swamp where it is infested by snakes and frogs, so it flies away and dies. He can also be compared to a swan swimming in the middle of the sea, unable to reach the shore to build a nest; therefore, the eggs she lays are submerged in the waters and devoured by fish. He can also be compared to a soldier on a wall that is undermined beneath his feet, who falls and dies in the ruins. He can also be compared to a beautiful tree moved to rotten soil, where a swarm of worms eats the root, so that it withers and dies. He can also be compared to a house without a foundation, or a column without a pedestal <note>original: "stylobata"</note>. Such is the internal man when he is only <term>reformed</term> <note>intellectually changed or corrected</note> and the external is not simultaneously so, for he has no fixed point of focus for doing good.

### *That a Regenerate Person has a New Will and a New Understanding.*

"From now on we know no one according to the flesh; therefore, if anyone is in Christ, *he is a new creature*” (2 Corinthians 5:16, 17). By a "new heart" in these passages is meant a <term>will</term>...

...new, and through a new spirit, a new understanding; for the **Heart** in the Word <note>original: "Verbo"; referring to the Sacred Scriptures</note> signifies the **will**, and **spirit**, when joined to the heart, signifies the **understanding**. From Reason, the reason a <term>regenerated</term> <note>spiritually reborn</note> man has a new will and a new understanding is because these two faculties make the man, and these are what are regenerated. Therefore, every man is such as he is in respect to these two: he is evil if his will is evil, and even more evil if his understanding favors it; and conversely, he is good if they are good. Religion alone renews and regenerates man; it holds the highest seat in the human mind, and sees beneath itself the civil matters belonging to the world. It also passes through these like pure sap through a tree even to its very peak, and from that height, it looks out upon natural things, just as someone from a tower or mountain looks out upon the plains below.

602. But it should be known that a man, in terms of his understanding, can rise almost into the light in which the Angels of Heaven dwell; but if he does not also rise in terms of his will, he is still the "old man" and not the "new." We have shown previously how the understanding lifts the will into the heights along with itself more and more; therefore, regeneration is primarily predicated of the will, and secondarily of the understanding. For the understanding in man is like light in the world, and the will is like the heat there. It is well known that light without heat does not give life or cause growth, but light joined to heat does. Furthermore, the understanding, in its lower region of the mind, is actually in the light of the world, but it is in the light of heaven in its higher region. Therefore, unless the will is raised from the lower region into the higher and joined to the intellect there, it remains in the world. In that case, the intellect flies up and down, but every night it returns to the will below and sleeps there; they join together like a man and a harlot, and produce two-headed offspring <note>original: "fœtus bicipites"; referring to monstrous or contradictory spiritual thoughts</note>. From this, it is also clear that unless a man has a new will and a new understanding, he is not regenerated.

603. The human mind is divided into three regions: the lowest is called **natural**, the middle is **spiritual**, and the highest is **celestial**. Through regeneration, a man is elevated from the lowest region, which is natural, into the higher region, which is spiritual, and through this into the celestial. That there are three regions of the mind will be demonstrated in the following Article. This is why a man who is not regenerated is called "natural," and a regenerated man is called "spiritual." From this, it is evident that the mind of a regenerated man is elevated into the spiritual region, and from that higher vantage point, he sees what is happening in the lower or natural mind. Anyone can see and acknowledge that there is a lower and higher region in the human mind by paying even slight attention to their own thoughts; for one sees what one is thinking. Thus, one says that they have thought or are thinking this or that. This would be impossible unless there were an interior thought called **perception**, which looks into the lower thought called **thinking**. A judge, when he has heard or read a long series of arguments presented by a lawyer, gathers them into a single view in the higher region of his mind—into a universal idea—and then sends his view down into the lower region of natural thought. There, he arranges his arguments in order and, according to the higher view, delivers his sentence and judges. Who does not know that a man can think and conclude in a moment or two what he cannot express through lower thought in an hour’s time? these examples are provided so it may be known that the human mind is divided into lower and higher regions.

604. As for the new Will, it resides above the old will in the spiritual region; likewise, the new Understanding is there, the latter with the former and the former with the latter. In that region, they join together and together look into the old or natural mind, arranging everything there so that it obeys. Who cannot see that if there were only one region in the human mind, where both evils and goods, and both falsities and truths, were mixed and committed together, a conflict would arise? It would be as if wolves and sheep, tigers and calves, and hawks and doves were put into a single cage together. What would happen then but a cruel slaughter, as the fierce beasts tore the tame ones apart? Therefore, it is provided that goods with their truths are gathered into the higher region so that they may subsist in safety and restrain the assaults [of evil], and also through chains and other...

to subjugate intermediate things, and afterwards to scatter evils along with their falsities. This, therefore, is what was stated in the previous article: that the Lord, through Heaven, governs those things of the World that are within a regenerated man. The higher or spiritual region of the human mind is also a Heaven in miniature, and the lower or natural region is a World in miniature; for this reason, man was called a <term>microcosm</term> <note>literally "small world"</note> by the ancients, and he can also be called a <term>microuranos</term> <note>literally "small heaven"</note>.

605. That a regenerated man—that is, one who is renewed in both will and intellect—exists in the heat of Heaven (which is its love) and simultaneously in the light of Heaven (which is its wisdom); and conversely, that a non-regenerated man exists in the heat of hell (which is its love) and simultaneously in the darkness of hell (which is its insanity), is a fact known today and yet unknown. The reason is that the Church as it exists today has made <term>regeneration</term> <note>spiritual rebirth</note> a mere appendix to its doctrine of faith, into which no reason is to be admitted; consequently, reason is excluded from anything belonging to that appendix, which, as stated, is regeneration and renewal. To those people, these things, along with faith itself, are like a house whose doors and windows are closed; therefore, no one knows what is inside that house—whether it is empty, or full of spirits from hell or angels from Heaven. Added to this is a confusion caused by a common fallacy: because a man can rise in his understanding almost into the light of Heaven, and from that intelligence think and speak about spiritual things regardless of the quality of his heart's love, the ignorance of this truth has caused everything concerning regeneration and renewal to remain unknown.

606. From these points, the following conclusions can be drawn: a non-regenerated man is like one who sees phantoms in the night and believes them to be men; later, when he is being regenerated, he is like that same person who, at the first break of dawn, sees that the things he saw in the night were mockeries; and finally, when he is regenerated and stands in the full light of day, he sees them as delusions. A non-regenerated man is like one who dreams, and a regenerated man is like one who is awake; in the Word <note>The Bible</note>, natural life is even likened to sleep, and spiritual life to wakefulness. The non-regenerated man is signified by the **foolish virgins** who had lamps but no oil, and the regenerated by the **wise virgins** who had lamps and oil together; by lamps are meant things of the understanding, and by oil, things of love. The regenerated are like the lamps of the golden lampstand in the Tabernacle; they are like the <term>showbread</term> <note>original: "Panes facierum"; literally "Bread of the Faces"</note> with incense upon them; and they are those who **shall shine as the brightness of the firmament, and like the stars for ever and ever**, according to Daniel, Chapter 12:3. A non-regenerated man is like one in the Garden of Eden who eats from the **Tree of Knowledge of good and evil**, and is therefore cast out of the garden—indeed, he is that very Tree; but the regenerated man is like one in that garden who eats from the **Tree of Life**. That it is granted to eat from it is clear from these words in the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation</note>: *To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of God* (Chapter 2:7). By the Garden of Eden is meant intelligence in spiritual things stemming from a love of truth (see <term>REVELATION REVEALED</term> <note>original: "APOCALYPSIS REVELATA"; one of Swedenborg's earlier works</note> no. 90). In a word, the non-regenerated man is a **Son of the evil one**, and the regenerated man is a **Son of the Kingdom** (Matthew 13:38); the "son of the evil one" there is a son of the devil, and the "son of the Kingdom" is a Son of the Lord.

607. The reason every person exists in communion—that is, in association—with the Angels of Heaven or with the spirits of hell, is because they are born to become spiritual; and this is not possible unless they are in some form of conjunction with those who are spiritual. which neither Man, nor Angel, nor Spirit knows, for the reason that man, as long as he lives in the World, is in a natural state, while an Angel and a Spirit are in a spiritual state; and because of the distinction between the natural and the spiritual, one does not appear to the other. This distinction, and its nature, is described in the book *<term>CONJUGIAL LOVE</term>* <note>The Latin title is "De Amore Conjugiali," a work by Swedenborg concerning the spiritual nature of marriage.</note> in the "Memorable Relation" found there at numbers 326 to 329. From this, it is clear that they are not joined in respect to their thoughts, but in respect to their affections. Scarcely anyone reflects upon these things, because affections are not in the light in which the intellect and its thought reside, but in the heat in which the will and its love's affection reside. The conjunction through the affections of love between men and between Angels and Spirits is so close that if it were severed, and they were thereby separated, men would instantly fall into a swoon, and if it were not restored and they were not rejoined, men would breathe their last. 

When it is said that a man becomes spiritual through regeneration, it is not meant that he becomes spiritual in the same way an Angel is in himself, but that he becomes <term>spiritual-natural</term>; that is, that there is something spiritual within his natural part, in the same way that thought exists within speech, or as the will exists within action—for if one ceases, the other ceases. In the same way, the Spirit of man is within every single thing that occurs in the body, and it is the Spirit that drives the natural part to do what it does. The natural, viewed in itself, is passive or a dead force, whereas the spiritual is active or a living force; the passive or dead force cannot act of itself, but must be acted upon by the active or living force. Since man lives continuously in community with the inhabitants of the spiritual World, therefore, when he departs from the natural World, he is immediately inserted among those similar to himself with whom he had been in the World. Hence it is that everyone after death seems to himself as if he were still living in the World, for he then comes into the company of those similar to himself regarding the affections of his will, whom he then recognizes, just as relatives and kinsmen recognize their own in the World; and this is what is meant in the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scripture or the Bible.</note> when it says of those who die that they are "gathered and collected to their own." From these things it can now be established that a regenerated man is in community with the Angels of Heaven, and a non-regenerated man is in community with the spirits of hell.

608. It must be known that there are three Heavens, and they are distinct from each other according to three degrees of love and wisdom, and that a man, according to his regeneration, is in community with Angels from those three heavens. Because this is so, the human Mind is also divided into three degrees or regions according to the heavens. But regarding these three heavens, and their distinction according to the three degrees of love and wisdom, see the book *<term>HEAVEN AND HELL</term>*, n. 29 and following; and also the short work *<term>THE INTERCOURSE BETWEEN THE SOUL AND THE BODY</term>*, n. 16, 17. Here it shall only be illustrated by a certain comparison what these three degrees are like, according to which those Heavens are distinct: they are as the head, the body, and the feet are in a man. The highest Heaven constitutes the Head, the middle constitutes the Body, and the Last constitutes the Feet; for the Universal Heaven is before the Lord like a single Man. That this is so was revealed to me by <term>personal observation</term> <note>original: "autopsiam." In this context, it refers to seeing with one's own eyes or first-hand experience in the spiritual world.</note>; for it was granted to me to see a single Society of Heaven, which consisted of myriads, as a single man at once—how much more then the universal Heaven before the Lord! Concerning this living Experience, see the book *<term>HEAVEN AND HELL</term>*, n. 59 and following. From this it is also clear how that well-known saying in the Christian World is to be understood: that the Church makes up the <term>Body of Christ</term> <note>original: "Corpus Christi"</note>, and that Christ is the life of that body. By this it can also be illustrated that the Lord is the all in all of Heaven, for He is the life in that body. Similarly, the Lord is the Church among those who acknowledge Him Alone as the God of Heaven and Earth, and believe in Him; that He Himself is the God of Heaven and Earth, He Himself teaches in Matthew 28:18, and that one must believe in Him, in John 3:15, 16, 36; Chapter 6:40; Chapter 11:25, 26.

Those three degrees are as Gold, Silver, and Copper are in relation to each other in nobility—with which metals a comparison is also made in the Statue of <term>Nebuchadnezzar</term>...

Daniel 2:31 and following. Those three <term>degrees</term> <note>In Swedenborg’s theology, "degrees" refer to distinct levels of reality (celestial, spiritual, and natural) that do not shade into one another but exist like end-to-end steps.</note> are also distinct among themselves, just as Ruby, Sapphire, and Agate are distinct from each other in purity and excellence; and also as the Olive, the Vine, and the Fig tree, and so on. Furthermore, Gold, Ruby, and Olive in the Word signify <term>celestial good</term>, which is the good of the highest heaven; Silver, Sapphire, and the Vine signify <term>spiritual good</term>, which is the good of the middle heaven; and Copper, Agate, and the Fig tree signify <term>natural good</term>, which is the good of the lowest heaven. It has been stated above that there are three degrees: celestial, spiritual, and natural.

610. To what has been said above, this shall be added: that the <term>Regeneration</term> <note>The process of being spiritually reborn or "made new" by God.</note> of man does not happen in a single moment, but successively from the beginning to the end of his life in the world, and that after this life it is continued and perfected. Because man is reformed through struggles and victories over the evils of his flesh, the Son of Man says to each of the seven Churches that he will give gifts to him who overcomes. As to the Church in Ephesus: *to him who overcomes, I will give to eat from the Tree of Life* (Revelation 2:7). To the Church of the Smyrneans: *He who overcomes shall not suffer harm in the second death* (Verse 11). To the Church in Pergamum: *To him who overcomes, I will give to eat of the hidden manna* (Verse 17). To the Church in Thyatira: *To him who overcomes, I will give power over the nations* (Verse 25). To the Church in Sardis: *He who overcomes will be clothed in white garments* (Chapter 3:5). To the Church in Philadelphia: *He who overcomes, I will make him a pillar in the Temple of God* (Verse 12). To the Church of the Laodiceans: *To him who overcomes, I will grant to sit with Me on My Throne* (Verse 21). Finally, this is added: that in the degree that a man is regenerated, or in the degree that regeneration is perfected in him, he should not attribute anything of good and truth—that is, of charity and faith—to himself, but to the Lord; for the truths which he successively absorbs clearly teach this.

## That as far as Man is regenerated, so far sins are removed, and that this removal is the Remission of sins.

611. The reason that sins are removed as far as a man is regenerated is that regeneration consists in restraining the flesh so that it does not dominate, and in taming the "old man" with his lusts so that he does not rise up and destroy the intellectual part. If the intellect is destroyed, man is no longer capable of being reformed. This reformation cannot take place unless the spirit of man, which is above the flesh, is instructed and perfected. Who, with an intellect still intact, cannot conclude from this that such things cannot happen in a single moment, but only successively—just as a man is conceived, carried in the womb, born, and educated, according to the principles shown above? 

For those things belonging to the flesh or the "old man" are inherent from birth and construct the first "house" of his mind, in which lusts dwell like wild beasts in their dens. They live first in the courtyards and enter by turns into the rooms of that house underground, and later rise up via stairs and form chambers for themselves. This happens successively as the infant grows, becomes a child, and then a youth, and then begins to think from his own intellect and act from his own will. Who does not see that this house built in the mind up to this point—in which lusts, like <term>doleful creatures</term>, <term>wild desert beasts</term>, and <term>satyrs</term> <note>original Latin: "ochim, ghoim & satyri." These are Hebrew terms from Isaiah 13:21 used to describe the desolation of a fallen state, inhabited by monstrous or wild inhabitants.</note> dance with joined hands—cannot be destroyed in a single moment and a new house built in its place? Must not the lusts holding hands and dancing thus first be removed, and new desires which are of good and truth be introduced in place of the cravings which are of evil and falsity? Every wise person can see that this cannot happen in a moment, for the sole reason that every evil is composed of countless lusts, and is like a fruit under the surface full of worms with white bodies and black heads. Furthermore, evils are numerous and joined together like a brood of spiders just hatched from the mother's belly; therefore, unless one evil is drawn out after another, until the bond is broken, man cannot become new.

These things have been brought forward for this reason: so that it may be known that to the extent that someone is regenerated, to that same extent their sins are removed.

612. Man from birth inclines toward evils of every kind, and from that inclination he lusts after them, and—so far as he is in freedom—he even commits them. For from birth he lusts to rule over others and to possess the goods of others; these two desires tear apart love toward one's neighbor. He then hates anyone who opposes him, and from that hatred he breathes vengeance, which inwardly fosters murder. This is also why he thinks nothing of adulteries, nothing of plunderings (which are secret thefts), and nothing of blasphemies (which are also false testimonies). He who thinks nothing of these things is also an atheist in his heart. Such is man from birth; from which it is clear that, by birth, man is <term>hell in a miniature image</term> <note>original: "infernum in minima effigie." Swedenborg views the individual human as a "microcosm" or small-scale version of the larger spiritual world.</note>. Now, because man, regarding the internal aspects of his mind, is born spiritual (unlike the beasts) and is consequently born for heaven—yet his natural or external man is, as was said, hell in a miniature image—it follows that heaven cannot be implanted in that hell unless the hell is removed.

613. Whoever knows how Heaven and Hell are situated in relation to each other, and how one is removed from the other, can know how a person is regenerated and what a regenerated person is like. So that this may be understood, it will be revealed in summary that all who are in Heaven face the Lord, and all who are in Hell turn their faces away from the Lord. Therefore, when hell is looked into from heaven, the inhabitants appear only by the back of the head and the back. Indeed, they even appear inverted like <term>antipodes</term> <note>A term for people on the opposite side of the globe; here used to mean they appear upside-down.</note>, with their feet upward and their heads downward; and this is so even though they walk on their feet and turn their faces around, for it is the opposite direction of their inner minds that produces that appearance. I report these wonders from <term>firsthand observation</term> <note>original: "autopsia." This refers to Swedenborg's claim of having direct, personal vision of the spiritual world.</note>. From these experiences, it was revealed to me how regeneration happens: it occurs exactly as Hell is removed and thus separated from Heaven. For, as said above, man regarding his first nature (which he draws from birth) is Hell in a miniature image, and regarding his second nature (which he draws from his second birth or regeneration), he is Heaven in a miniature image. It follows from this that evils in a person are removed and separated just as Hell and Heaven are separated on a large scale; and as evils are removed, they turn themselves away from the Lord and successively invert themselves, and this happens to the degree that Heaven is implanted—that is, as the person becomes new. For the sake of illustration, this shall be added: every evil in a person has a connection with those in hell who are in a similar evil; and conversely, every good in a person has a connection with those in Heaven who are in a similar good.

614. From what has been brought forward, it can be established that the <term>remission of sins</term> <note>Commonly understood as "forgiveness," Swedenborg argues it is actually the physical "moving away" of spiritual influences.</note> is not their total uprooting or wiping away, but rather their removal and thus their separation. Furthermore, every evil that a person has actually made their own remains. And because the remission of sins is their removal and separation, it follows that a person is held back from evil by the Lord and kept in good; and this is what is given to a person through regeneration. I once heard someone in the Lowest Heaven saying that he was free from sins because they had been "wiped away"—he added, "by the blood of Christ." But because he was within Heaven and yet in that error out of ignorance, he was let back into his own sins; as they returned, he acknowledged them. From this, he accepted a new faith, which was that every person, just like every Angel, is held back from evils and kept in goods by the Lord. From this it is clear what the Remission of sins is: that it is not instantaneous, but follows the progress of regeneration. The removal of sins, which is called their remission, can be compared to the casting out of filth from the camp of the children of Israel in the desert, which was all around them; for their Camp represented Heaven, and the Desert represented Hell. It can also be compared to the removal of the nations from the children of Israel in the land of Canaan, and the Jebusites from Jerusalem, who were not cast out but separated. It can be compared to Dagon, the god of the Philistines, who, when the Ark was brought in, first lay on his fa-

## That Regeneration is not possible without Free Will in spiritual matters.

615. Who but a stupid person cannot see that a human being cannot be <term>regenerated</term> <note>Spiritual rebirth or the process of being made new by God.</note> without <term>Free Will</term> <note>original: "Libero arbitrio." The capacity to choose or act from one's own volition.</note> in spiritual matters? For without it, can someone approach the Lord and acknowledge Him as Redeemer and Savior, and as the God of Heaven and Earth, as He Himself teaches in Matthew 28:18? Who, without that Free Will, can believe—that is, look upon and worship Him from faith—and apply themselves to receive the means and benefits of salvation from Him, and cooperate with Him in receiving them? Who, without free will, can do any good for their neighbor and practice charity? Or, among the many other things belonging to faith and charity, who can bring them into thought and will, and express them, and send them out into action? Otherwise, what is "Regeneration" but a mere word slipped from the mouth of the Lord (John 3)? It would either stop at the ear, or, having slipped from the mouth out of thought close to speech, it would become an articulated sound made of only eleven letters <note>original: "undecim literis." The Latin word "Regeneratio" contains eleven letters.</note>; a sound which cannot be raised by any meaning into any higher region of the mind, but falls into the air where it is dissipated.

616. Tell me, if you can, whether any stupidity could ever be more blind regarding Regeneration than that which exists among those who confirm themselves in the "faith of today." This doctrine holds that faith is infused into a person when they are like a **log or a stone**, and that justification—which includes the remission of sins, regeneration, and many other gifts—follows that infusion; and that human effort must be entirely excluded so that it does not infringe upon the merit of Christ. To establish this dogma even more firmly, they have snatched away from the human being all free will in spiritual matters by imposing a total lack of power in them. It is as if God alone worked on His part, and no power were given to the human to cooperate on theirs, and thus to join themselves to Him. 

What then is a human being in regard to regeneration, if not like someone bound hand and foot, similar to those bound in ships called **galleys**? If such prisoners were to free themselves from their manacles and shackles, they would be punished and condemned to death just like them—that is, if they were to do good to their neighbor from free will, and believe in God from themselves for the sake of salvation. What would a person be who is confirmed in such things, and yet has a pious desire for Heaven, but a specter standing in a vision? They would wonder whether that faith with its benefits has been infused, or if not, whether it will be infused; and therefore whether God the Father has had mercy, or whether His Son has interceded, or whether the Holy Spirit is busy elsewhere and not working. Finally, from total ignorance, such a person would give up on the matter and console themselves by thinking: "Perhaps that grace is present in the morality of my life, in which I remain as I was before; and thus that morality is holy in me, but profane in those who have not attained that faith." Therefore, so that holiness may remain in my morality, I will take care hereafter not to practice faith or charity from myself—along with many other such thoughts. Such a specter—or, if you prefer, such a statue—is anyone who thinks of Regeneration without Free Will in spiritual matters.

617. A person who believes that Regeneration is given without any free will in spiritual matters, and thus without cooperation, becomes as cold as ice toward all the truths of the Church...

Finally, they become like scaly serpents, whose deceits sound and shine just like their scales, and so on.

### That <term>Regeneration</term> is not possible without truths, through which Faith is formed, and with which Charity joins itself.

618. There are three things by which a human being is <term>regenerated</term> <note>The process of being spiritually reborn or "made new" by God.</note>: the Lord, Faith, and Charity. These three would lie hidden like the most exalted treasures buried in the earth, if Divine truths from the Word did not open them; indeed, they would remain hidden even to those who deny human cooperation, even if they read the Word a hundred or a thousand times, although they stand out there in clear light. As for the Lord: who, if confirmed in the faith of today, sees with an open eye what is written there—that He and the Father are one, that He is the God of Heaven and Earth, and that it is the Father's will that they should believe in the Son, besides countless similar things about the Lord in both Covenants? <note>The Old and New Testaments.</note> The reason is that they are not in truths, and therefore not in the light from which such things can be seen; and even if light were given, falsities would extinguish it, and then these passages would be passed over as if they were things deleted with ink, or like underground ditches that are stepped over and passed by. These things are said so that it may be known that without truths, this primary requirement of regeneration cannot be seen. 

As for <term>Faith</term>, that too cannot exist without truths; for faith and truth make one thing. The "good" of faith is like the soul, and truths make its body; therefore, to say that one believes or has faith without knowing any of its truths is like pulling the soul out of the body and speaking with something invisible. Furthermore, all the truths that make up the body of faith emit light from themselves, and they illustrate and present its face to be seen. 

It is the same with <term>Charity</term>; this emits heat from itself, with which the light of truth joins itself, just as heat does with light during springtime in the world. From the conjunction of these two, the animals and plants of the earth return to their fruitfulness. It is the same with spiritual Heat and Light; these similarly join together in a human being when he is in the truths of faith and simultaneously in the "goods" of charity. For as was said above in the chapter on Faith, from every single truth of faith flows light that illuminates, and from every single good of charity flows heat that kindles; furthermore, spiritual Light in its essence is <term>Intelligence</term>, and spiritual Heat in its essence is <term>Love</term>, and the Lord alone joins those two together in a person when He regenerates him. For the Lord said: *The words that I speak are spirit and life* <note>original: "Verba quæ Ego loquor, spiritus & vita sunt"</note>, <term>John 6:63.</term> *Believe in the Light, that you may be children of light... I have come as Light into the world* <note>original: "Credite in Lucem, ut filii lucis sitis, Ego Lux in Mundum veni"</note>, <term>John 12:36.</term> The Lord is the Sun in the spiritual world; from Him comes all spiritual light and heat. That light illuminates, and that heat kindles, and through the joining of both, He gives life to and regenerates the human being.

619. From these points it can be established that without truths there is no knowledge of the Lord, nor can there be Faith, and thus no <term>Charity</term> <note>Active love for one's neighbor</note>. Consequently, without truths there is no theology, and where there is no theology, there is no Church. Such is the state of the gatherings of people today who call themselves Christians and say they are in the light of the Gospel, when in reality they are in thick darkness itself. For truths lie hidden under falsities, just like gold, silver, and precious stones buried among bones in the **Valley of Hinnom** <note>original: "valle hinnomi"; a valley near Jerusalem historically associated with fire and destruction, used here as a metaphor for spiritual waste</note>. That this is the case became clearly evident to me from the **Spheres** <note>Spiritual atmospheres or "vibes" that radiate from the minds and beliefs of spirits</note> in the spiritual world which flow out and spread from modern Christianity.

One sphere is concerning the Lord; this exhales and pours forth from the **Southern Quarter** <note>In the spiritual world, the South is associated with the highest intelligence</note>, where the learned of the clergy and the well-read among the laity are found. Wherever this sphere goes, it creeps into people's ideas and, in many, it takes away their faith in the **Divinity of the Lord’s Human** <note>The teaching that the Lord's human nature is itself Divine</note>; in others it weakens it, and in others it makes it seem foolish. The cause is that it simultaneously brings in a faith in three Gods, and thus causes confusion.

Another sphere that brings "faith" is like a black cloud in winter time; it brings on darkness, turns rain into snow, strips the trees bare, freezes the waters, and takes away all pasture from the sheep. This sphere, joined with the previous one, instills a kind of lethargy regarding the one God, regarding **Regeneration** <note>The process of being spiritually reborn</note>, and regarding the means of salvation.

A third sphere concerns the conjunction of faith and charity. This is so powerful that it cannot be resisted, but today it is abominable. Like a plague, it infects anyone who breathes it in and tears apart every bond between those two means of salvation which were established from the creation of the world and restored by the Lord. This sphere even invades people in the natural world and extinguishes the **marriage torches** between truths and goods <note>The spiritual union of what is true in the mind with what is good in the heart</note>. I felt this sphere myself; when I thought about the conjunction of faith and charity, it interposed itself between them and violently tried to separate them. The angels complain about these spheres and pray to the Lord that they may be dissipated, but they received the answer that they cannot be dissipated as long as the **Dragon** is upon the earth, because those spheres originate from those who belong to the Dragon. For it is said of the Dragon that he was cast down to the earth, and then: *Therefore rejoice, O heavens... but woe to the inhabitants of the earth* (**Revelation 12**). These three spheres are like atmospheres driven by a storm, arising from the blowholes of dragons; because they are spiritual, they invade and drive men's minds. Spheres of spiritual truths are still few there, existing only in the **New Heaven** and among those under heaven who are separated from the Dragon’s followers. This is why those truths are so invisible to people in the world today, just as ships in the **Eastern Sea** are to captains and navigators sailing in the **Western Sea**.

620. Regeneration without truths is no more possible than the life of animals or the growth of trees without light from the sun; for if the sun did not give light at the same time it gives heat, the sun would become as described in the **Book of Revelation**, like **"sackcloth of hair"** <note>original: "saccus pilosus"</note> (**Chapter 6:12**) and **"blackened"** (**Joel 3:11**) and thus there would be mere darkness upon the earth (**Joel 4:15**). It would be similar for a person without truths, which emit light from themselves. For the Sun from which the lights of truths flow is the Lord in the spiritual world; unless spiritual light flowed from there into human minds, the Church would be in mere darkness, or in a shadow of a perpetual eclipse.

Regeneration, which happens through faith and charity, would—without truths that teach and lead—be like navigating a great ocean without a rudder, or without a compass and maps; it would be like riding through a dark forest at night. The internal sight of the mind in those who are not in truths but in falsities (believing them to be truths) can be compared to the sight of those whose optic nerves are obstructed, yet the eye still appears whole and capable of seeing, even though it sees nothing. To these things will be added these **MEMORABLE RELATIONS**. **FIRST**; I saw a Gathering of Spirits, all on their knees, praying to God that He would send Angels to them, with whom they might speak face to face <note>original: "ore ad os," literally "mouth to mouth"</note>, and to whom they might open the thoughts of their hearts; and when they rose up, three Angels in fine linen <note>original: "byssino"; fine white linen in the Bible often represents the "righteous acts of the saints" or pure truth</note> were seen standing in their sight, and they said: "The Lord Jesus Christ has heard your prayers, and therefore He has sent us to you; open to us the thoughts of your heart." Then the Angels answered: "Read the Word, and believe in the Lord, and you will see the Truths which should belong to your faith and your life; everyone in the Christian World draws their teachings from the Word as from the only Fountain; but two from the gathering said: "We have read, but we did not understand." And the Angels answered: "You did not approach the Lord, who is the Word, and you also first confirmed yourselves in falsities." The Angels further said: "What is faith without light? And what is thinking without understanding? This is not Human; even ravens and magpies can learn to speak without understanding. We can assert that every single person whose soul desires it can see the truths of the Word in light. There is no animal that does not know the food of its own life when it sees it; and man is a rational and spiritual Animal—he sees the food of his life, not so much for the body, but for the soul, which is the truth of faith, if he hungers for it and asks for it from the Lord. Whatever is not received by the understanding does not even stick in the memory as a reality <note>original: "quoad rem"</note>, but only as words. But if the Understanding is closed because of Religion, the way from Heaven is closed to it, and then a man sees no more in the Word than a blind man; we have seen many such fall into pits from which they did not rise.

And they said concerning **God**: Everyone who comes into Heaven is assigned a place there, and from that place, eternal joy according to their idea of God; for this idea reigns universally in all aspects of Worship. The idea of God as a Spirit—when "spirit" is believed to be like ether or wind—is an empty idea; but the idea of God as a **Man** is a just and right idea. For God is <term>Divine Love</term> and <term>Divine Wisdom</term> <note>These are the two fundamental essences of God in this theology</note>, with every quality belonging to them, and the Subject of these is Man, not ether or wind. The idea of God in Heaven is the idea of the Lord the Savior; He is the God of Heaven and Earth, as He himself taught. Let your idea of God be similar to ours, and we shall be associated. When they had said these things, their faces shone brightly.

**ON THE IMMORTALITY OF THE SOUL** they said: Man lives forever because he is able to be conjoined to God through love and faith. Every single person is capable of this; and that this "Power" <note>original: "Posse," referring to the human capacity or potentiality</note> constitutes the immortality of the soul, you can understand if you think a little more deeply about it.

**ON REGENERATION**: Who does not see that it is free for every man to think about God, or not to think about Him, provided he has been instructed that God exists? Thus, everyone has freedom in spiritual things just as much as in civil and natural things. The Lord gives this continuously to all; therefore, one becomes guilty if he does not think of Him. A man is a man because of this "power," but a beast is a beast because it lacks this power. Therefore, a man can reform and regenerate himself **as if by his own power**, provided that in his heart he acknowledges that it is from the Lord. Everyone who performs repentance and believes in the Lord is reformed and regenerated; man must do both **as if by himself**, but this **AS IF BY HIMSELF** <note>original: "SICUT A SE"; a central concept in this text meaning that while man must act using his own will and reason, he must recognize the power to do so actually flows from God</note> is from the Lord. It is true that man from himself can contribute nothing to this, not even a bit; nevertheless, you were not created as statues, but you were created as Men, so that you might do this from the Lord as if from yourselves. This is the unique reciprocal of love and faith which the Lord absolutely wills to be done to Him by man. In a word: act from yourselves, and believe it is from the Lord; thus you act as if from yourselves.

But then they asked whether "acting as if from oneself" was implanted in man from creation. The Angel answered, "It was not implanted, because acting from oneself belongs to God Alone; but it is given continuously—that is, it is joined to man continuously. And then, to the extent that a man does good and believes truth as if from himself, he is an Angel of Heaven; but to the extent that he does evil and believes what is false therefrom (which is also as if from himself), he is a **Spirit of Hell**. You may wonder that this latter is also 'as if from himself,' but you still see this when you pray to be guarded from the devil lest he seduce you, or lest he enter into you as he did into Judas, filling you with all iniquity and destroying both soul and body. But everyone becomes guilty who believes that he acts from himself, whether it be good or whether it be evil; but he does not become guilty who believes that he acts **as if from himself**. For if he believes that good is from himself, he claims for himself what is God's; and if he believes that evil is from himself, he attributes to himself what is the devil's."

**ON BAPTISM** they said: It is a spiritual Washing, which is Reformation and Regeneration; and that an Infant is reformed and regenerated when, having become an adult, he performs those things which the Godparents <note>original: "Patrini"; sponsors or sureties at a baptism</note> promised for him. These are two things: Repentance and Faith in God. For **FIRST**, they promise that he should renounce the devil and all his works; **SECOND**, that he should believe in God. All Infants in Heaven are initiated into those two things, but for them, the "devil" is hell, and "God" is the Lord. Furthermore, Baptism is a sign before the Angels that a person belongs to the Church. 

Having heard these things, those from the Gathering said, "We understand these things." But then a voice was heard from the side, crying out, "We do not understand!" and another voice, "We do not want to understand!" And it was investigated from whom those voices came, and it was discovered they were from those who had confirmed themselves in the falsities of faith, and who wished to be believed as oracles, and thus to be worshiped. The Angels said, "Do not wonder; there are very many such today. ## 622. THE SECOND MEMORABLE RELATION.

All who are prepared for Heaven—which takes place in the **World of Spirits**, which is intermediate between Heaven and Hell—after their time is completed, long for Heaven with a sigh. Soon their eyes are opened, and they see a way that leads to some Society in Heaven. They enter this way and ascend; and in the ascent there is a gate, and there a guard, who opens the gate, and so they enter. Then an Examiner meets them, who, on behalf of the Governor, tells them to enter further and inquire whether there are any houses which they recognize as their own; for for every new angel there is a new house. If they find one, they report this and remain there; but if they do not find one, they return and say they have not seen any. Then they are examined by a certain wise person there to see whether the Light that is in them agrees with the light that is in that society, and especially whether the Heat agrees. For the **Light of Heaven** in its essence is <term>Divine Truth</term>, and the **Heat of Heaven** in its essence is <term>Divine Good</term>, both proceeding from the Lord as the Sun there. If a different Light and a different Heat than the Light and Heat of that Society are within them—that is, if there is a different Truth and Good—they are not received. Therefore, they leave and go through ways opened between the Societies in Heaven, and this continues until they find a Society entirely agreeable to their affections, and there their habitation is established forever. For they are then among their own, as if among kin and friends whom they love from the heart because they are in a similar affection; and there they are in the sweetness of their life, and in the delight of their whole breast from the peace of the soul. For in the Heat and Light of Heaven there is an ineffable delight which is shared. Thus it happens with those who become angels.

But those who are in evils and falsities are allowed, by way of permission, to ascend into Heaven; yet when they enter, they begin to gasp for air and to breathe with a struggle. Soon their sight is darkened, their understanding grows dim, their thoughts cease, and a kind of deathly gloom <note>original: "lethas," likely referring to Lethe, the river of forgetfulness, or a lethal stupor</note> appears before their eyes, and so they stand like stumps. Then their heart begins to throb, their chest to tighten, and their mind to be seized with anguish and tortured more and more. In that state they writhe like serpents brought near a fire; therefore, they tumble away and cast themselves down a precipice, which then appears, nor do they rest until they are in Hell among their own kind, where they can draw breath and where their heart beats freely. Afterward, they hate Heaven, reject Truth, and in their hearts blaspheme the Lord, believing that their torture and torments in Heaven were caused by Him. From these few things it can be seen what the lot is of those who <term>disregard</term> <note>original: "floccipendunt," literally to weigh as a tuft of wool, meaning to value as nothing</note> the Truths of faith—which nevertheless make the light in which the angels of Heaven live—and who disregard the Goods of love and charity, which nevertheless make the heat of life in which the angels...

## 623. THE THIRD MEMORABLE RELATION.

Once it was granted to see three hundred of the Clergy and Laity together, all learned and erudite, because they knew how to confirm **Faith Alone** even unto <term>justification</term> <note>The theological concept of being declared righteous before God.</note>, and some even further. Because they held the faith that Heaven is merely admission by grace, they were given permission to ascend into one Society of Heaven—though it was not among the higher ones. When they ascended, they were seen from a distance as **Calves**, and when they entered Heaven, they were received civilly by the Angels; but when they spoke with one another, a trembling seized them, then horror, and finally a torture like that of death, and then they threw themselves down headlong. In their fall, they were seen as **dead Horses**. The reason they appeared as **Calves** during the ascent was because the natural affection for seeing and knowing, when exultant, appears through <term>correspondence</term> <note>The symbolic relationship between spiritual states and physical forms.</note> as a Calf; and that they appeared in their fall as **dead Horses** was because the Understanding of truth appears through correspondence as a **Horse**, but an understanding of no truth—which is what the Church's state was for them—appears as a **dead Horse**.

There were Boys below who saw them descending and appearing as dead horses in their descent. They then turned their faces away and said to their **Teacher**, who was with them: "What is this monstrosity? We saw men, and now in their place dead horses; because we could not bear to look at them, we turned our faces away. Teacher, let us not linger in this place, but let us depart." And they departed. Then the Teacher instructed them on the way regarding what a **dead horse** is, saying: "A Horse signifies the Understanding of truth from the Word. All the Horses you saw signified that. For when a man goes along meditating from the Word, his Meditation appears from a distance as a Horse—noble and lively if he meditates spiritually, but wretched and dead if he meditates materially." Then the boys asked what it means to meditate spiritually and materially from the Word. The Teacher replied, "I will illustrate this with examples. Who, while holily reading the Word, does not think inwardly within himself about God, about the Neighbor, and about Heaven? Everyone who thinks of God only from **Person** and not from **Essence** thinks materially. Also, he who thinks of the Neighbor only from external form and not from quality thinks materially. And he who thinks of Heaven only as a **place** and not from the love and wisdom from which Heaven is Heaven, he also thinks materially." But the boys said, "We have thought of God from Person, of the Neighbor from Form (that he is a man), and of Heaven as a Place that is above us; does this mean that when we read the Word, we appeared to someone then as dead horses?" The Teacher said, "No, you are still boys and cannot do otherwise. But I perceived in you an affection for knowing and understanding, which, because it is spiritual, meant you also thought spiritually; for some spiritual thought lies hidden within your material thought, which you do not yet realize. But I will return to what I said before: that he who thinks materially while reading the Word or meditating from the Word appears from a distance as a dead horse, but he who thinks spiritually appears as a living horse. He thinks materially of God who thinks only of **Person** and not of **Essence**. For there are many Attributes of the Divine Essence, such as **Omnipotence, Omniscience, Omnipresence, Eternity, Love, Wisdom, Mercy, and Grace**, and others. And there are Attributes proceeding from the Divine Essence, which are **Creation and Preservation, Redemption and Salvation, Enlightenment and Instruction**. Everyone who thinks of God from Person makes

That is, it places the obstacle right at the nose and fixes it in its cartilage, so that afterwards one cannot even "smell" spiritual things. From this, some have become such that when they perceive a "scent" from spiritual things, they fall into a faint; by "scent" I mean perception. These are they who make God into Three; they say indeed from Essence that God *is One*, but nonetheless while they pray according to their Faith—which is that God the Father should have mercy for the sake of the Son and send the Holy Spirit—they clearly make three Gods. They cannot do otherwise, for they pray to One so that He may have mercy for the sake of a Second and send a Third. And then their Master taught them concerning the Lord, that He is the One God, in Whom is the Divine Trinity.

## 624. THE FOURTH MEMORABLE RELATION.

Waking from sleep at midnight, I saw at a certain height toward the East an Angel holding a Paper in his right hand, which appeared in brilliant whiteness from the Sun; in its center was writing in golden letters, and I saw written: **THE MARRIAGE OF GOOD AND TRUTH.** <note>original: "CONJUGIUM BONI ET VERI"; a central concept in this theology, signifying the union of the heart's intentions (Good) and the mind's insights (Truth).</note> From the writing there flashed a splendor which went out into a wide circle around the Paper; that circle or border appeared like the dawn in springtime. After this, I saw the Angel descending with the Paper in his hand, and as he descended, the Paper appeared less and less bright, and that writing, which was **THE MARRIAGE OF GOOD AND TRUTH**, changed from a golden color to silver, then to copper, after that to iron, and finally to a rusty and corroded color. At last, the Angel was seen to enter a dark Cloud, and through the Cloud onto the Earth; and there that Paper, although it was still held in the Angel's hand, was not seen. This took place in the World of Spirits, in which all men first gather after death. Then the Angel spoke to me, saying: "Ask those who come here whether they see me, or anything in my hand." A multitude came, a crowd from the east, a crowd from the south, a crowd from the west, and a crowd from the north. I asked those arriving from the East and South—who were those who in the World had studied learning—whether they saw anyone here with me, or anything in his hand. They said—

# CHAPTER ELEVEN

### CONCERNING

## IMPUTATION.

->*That the Faith of the present-day Church, which is asserted to justify alone, and Imputation, make one.*<-

626. The reason that the Faith of the present-day Church (which is said to justify alone) and Imputation make one—or that faith and imputation in the present-day Church constitute a single thing—is because one belongs to the other; that is, one enters into the other mutually and reciprocally and causes it to be. For if "faith" is mentioned and "imputation" is not added, faith is merely a sound; and if "imputation" is mentioned and "faith" is not added, that too is merely a sound. But if these two are spoken of together, something articulate is formed, though it is still without meaning. Therefore, so that the understanding may perceive something, a third element must necessarily be added, which is the **merit of Christ**. From this, a sentence is formed that a person can express with some logic: for the faith of the present-day Church is that God the Father <term>imputes</term> <note>Attributing the qualities or actions of one person to another; in this context, treating a person as righteous because of Christ’s actions.</note> the justice of His Son and sends the Holy Spirit to work out its effects.

627. These three, therefore—Faith, Imputation, and the Merit of Christ—are one in the present-day Church and can be called a "triune" unit. If one of these three were taken away, today's Theology would become nothing, for it depends on those three perceived as one, just as a long chain depends on a **fixed hook**. If you were to remove either faith, or imputation, or the merit of Christ, everything said about **Justification**, the remission of sins, quickening, renewal, regeneration, sanctification, and about the Gospel, free will, charity, and good works—indeed, even about eternal life—would become like desolate cities or the ruins of a Temple. Faith itself, which stands as the leader, would become nothing, and thus the entire Church would be a desert and a desolation. From this it is clear upon what pillar the House of God is founded today; if it were pulled away, the house would collapse like the building in which the Lords of the Philistines and about three thousand people were entertained, whose two pillars **Samson** <note>original: "Schimson"; the biblical hero who destroyed the Philistine temple.</note> pulled down at once, at which time they were killed and slain (Judges 16:29). This is said because it has been shown in the preceding pages, and will be shown in the Appendix, that this Faith is not truly Christian because it disagrees with the Word, and that the imputation of that faith is vain because the merit of Christ cannot be <term>imputed</term>.

629. It is said that the Imputation of modern faith is twofold, but it is not "double" in the sense of God and His Mercy toward all, but rather like God and His Mercy toward only some. It is not like a parent and his love toward all his offspring, but like a parent and his love toward only one or another of his children. It is not like the Divine Law and its command to everyone, but like the Divine Law and its command to a few. Therefore, one kind of "doubleness" is expansive and unified, while the other is restricted and divided; the latter is a divided duality, while the former is a unity. For it is taught that the Imputation of Christ's merit is based on an arbitrary election, and that for these people there is an imputation of salvation—meaning some are adopted and the rest are rejected. This would be as if God lifted some into <term>Abraham's bosom</term> <note>A traditional term for the place of comfort in the afterlife.</note> and handed others over as morsels for the devil; yet the truth is that the Lord rejects and hands over no one, but the person hands himself over.

They do this so that nothing of the human being might enter into the imputation of Christ's merit. ### *That the Faith which consists of the imputation of the merit and justice of Christ the Redeemer first arose from the decrees of the Council of Nicaea concerning three Divine Persons from eternity; which Faith, from that time to the present, has been received by the entire Christian World.*

**632.** Regarding the Council of Nicaea itself: it was held by the Emperor Constantine the Great at the persuasion of Alexander, the Bishop of Alexandria. He called together all the bishops in Asia, Africa, and Europe to his palace in the city of Nicaea in Bithynia, so that they might use the Sacred Scripture to convict and condemn the heresy of Arius, a presbyter of Alexandria, who denied the Divinity of Jesus Christ. This took place in the year of Christ 318 <note>While the text says 318, the Council of Nicaea actually took place in 325 AD. 318 is often cited in older texts as the traditional number of bishops present.</note>. That those who were called together concluded that there were three Divine Persons—Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—from eternity, is especially evident from the two creeds called the Nicene and the Athanasian. In the Nicene Creed we read:
> "I believe in one God the Father, Almighty, Maker of heaven and earth; and in one Lord, Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son of God, born of the Father before all ages, God of God, <term>consubstantial</term> <note>Of the same substance or essence.</note> with the Father, who descended from the heavens, and was incarnate by the Holy Spirit from the Virgin Mary; and in the Holy Spirit, the Lord and Giver of Life, who proceeds from the Father and the Son, who with the Father and the Son together is worshiped and glorified."

In the Athanasian Creed are these words:
> "This is the Catholic Faith: that we worship one God in Trinity, and Trinity in Unity, neither confounding the Persons nor dividing the Substance. But because we are compelled by Christian truth to confess each Person individually to be God and Lord, so we are forbidden by the Catholic Religion to say there are three Gods or three Lords."

That is to say, it is permitted to *confess* three Gods and Lords, but not to *say* it; and this is so because religion forbids the latter, while truth dictates the former. This Athanasian Creed was written shortly after the Council of Nicaea was held, by one or more people who had been present at the Council, and it was also accepted as <term>ecumenical</term> or universal. From these things it is clear that it was then decreed that three Divine Persons from eternity are to be acknowledged, and although each Person individually by Himself was God, nevertheless they are not to be called three Gods and Lords, but One.

**633.** That the faith of three Divine Persons has been received from that time, and has been confirmed and preached by all Bishops, Hierarchs, Church leaders, and Priests up to the present time, is well known in the Christian world. And because a mental persuasion of three Gods emanated from this, no other Faith could be devised than...

## *That the Faith of the Imputed Merit of Christ was unknown in the Apostolic Church, which preceded [the Nicene]; and is nowhere understood in the Word.*

636. The Church that preceded the Council of Nicaea was called the Apostolic Church. That it was widespread and propagated into three parts of the world—Asia, Africa, and Europe—is evident not only from the Emperor Constantine the Great and his monarchy (which was later divided into many European kingdoms, but also reached the neighboring regions outside Europe), but also from the fact that he was a Christian and a zealot for religion. Therefore, as was said above, he summoned the bishops from Asia, Africa, and Europe to his palace in the city of Nicaea in Bithynia <note>A region in modern-day Turkey.</note>, so that he might cast the scandals of <term>Arius</term> <note>A priest whose teachings denied the full divinity of Christ, leading to the Council of Nicaea.</note> out of his empire. This was done by the Lord's Divine Providence; for if the Divinity of the Lord is denied, the Christian Church dies and becomes like a tomb adorned with this epitaph: *Here lies*. The Church that existed before this time was called Apostolic; and the distinguished writers of that Church were called the "Fathers," and true Christians were called "brothers" by their side. That this Church did not acknowledge three Divine Persons, and thus not a "Son of God from eternity" but only a "Son of God born in time," is clear from the Creed which was called "Apostolic" by their Church, where these words are read:

> I believe in God the Father Almighty, Creator of Heaven and Earth. And in Jesus Christ His only Son, our Lord, who was conceived by the Holy Spirit, born of the Virgin Mary. I believe in the Holy Spirit; the holy Catholic Church, the communion of saints.

From this it is plain that they acknowledged no other Son of God than the one conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of the Virgin Mary; and absolutely no "Son of God born from eternity." This Creed, like the other two, has been acknowledged as the authentic Catholic faith by the entire Christian Church to this very day.

it is the same with all things that persuasion and confirmation fix; these eventually appear like painted tapestries fastened with many nails to a wall glued together from worn-out pebbles.

## That the Imputation of the merit and righteousness of Christ is impossible.

640. So that it may be known that the <term>Imputation</term> <note>original: "Imputatio." In theology, this refers to the belief that God "credits" Christ’s holiness to a person’s account, legally covering their sins.</note> of the Merit and Righteousness of Jesus Christ is impossible, it is necessary to know what His Merit and Righteousness are. The Merit of our Lord the Savior is <term>Redemption</term>, the nature of which may be seen in its own chapter above (numbers 114 to 133); it is described there as the subjugation of the Hells and the ordering of the Heavens, and afterward the restoration of the Church. Thus, Redemption was a purely Divine work. It was also shown there that the Lord, through Redemption, put Himself in the power of regenerating and saving those who believe in Him and do His commandments, and that without that Redemption no mortal <note>original: "nulla Caro," literally "no flesh."</note> could have been saved. Since Redemption was a purely Divine work, belonging to the Lord alone, and that work constitutes His Merit, it follows that this is no more applicable, ascribable, or imputable to any human being than the Creation and Preservation of the Universe. Redemption was, in fact, a kind of new creation of the Angelic Heaven, and likewise of the Church. 

That the modern Church attributes that merit of the Lord the Redeemer to those who obtain "Faith" by grace is evident from their dogmas, among which this is the principal one. For it is said by the rulers of that Church and by their followers—both in the Roman Catholic Church and in the Churches of the Reformers—that by the <term>Imputation</term> of Christ’s Merit, those who have attained Faith are not only "accounted" just and holy, but actually *are* so. They claim that their sins are not sins in the sight of God because they have been forgiven, and the individuals have been <term>justified</term>—that is, reconciled, renewed, regenerated, sanctified, and enrolled in Heaven. That the entire Christian Church today teaches these same things is clearly evident from the <term>Council of Trent</term> <note>A 16th-century council that defined Catholic doctrine in response to the Reformation.</note>, the <term>Augustan and Augsburg Confessions</term> <note>Key documents defining Lutheran doctrine.</note>, and from the commentaries cited and accepted alongside them. What else flows from these statements—when translated into that system of faith—than that the possession of this faith is itself the merit and righteousness of the Lord? Consequently, it would mean the possessor of faith is Christ in another person; for it is said that Christ Himself is Righteousness, and that faith is righteousness, and that "imputation" (by which is also meant ascription and application) makes them not only accounted just and holy, but actually *be* so. Just add "Transfer" <note>original: "TRANSCRIPTIONEM."</note> to "imputation," "application," and "ascription," and you would be the Pope’s vicar.

641. Since, therefore, the Merit and Righteousness of the Lord are purely Divine, and purely Divine things are such that if they were applied or ascribed directly, a human being would die in an instant; they would be consumed like a log thrown into the naked sun, until hardly a spark of them remained. For this reason, the Lord with His Divine nature approaches angels and men through light tempered and moderated to the capacity and quality of each—thus through what is adequate and accommodated—and similarly through heat. 

In the spiritual world there is a Sun, in the middle of which is the Lord. From that Sun, He flows in through light and heat into the entire spiritual world and into everyone who is there; all light and all heat there originate from it. From that Sun, the Lord also flows with the same light and heat into the souls and minds of men. That heat in its essence is His Divine Love, and that light in its essence is His Divine Wisdom. The Lord adapts this light and heat to the capacity and quality of the receiving angel or human, which is done by means of spiritual "auras" or atmospheres that carry and transfer them. The Divine itself immediately surrounding the Lord creates that Sun. This Sun is as far distant from the angels as the Sun of the natural world is from men, for the reason that it might not touch them stripped and thus immediately; for if it did, they would be consumed, like a log thrown into the naked sun, as was said.
