From these things it can be established that the merit and righteousness of the Lord, because they are purely Divine, can by no means be brought into any angel or human through imputation; indeed, if even a single drop of it, not moderated as was mentioned before, were to touch them, they would instantly be tortured like those struggling with death, with their feet convulsing, their eyes rolling, and they would lose all life. This was made known in the <term>Israelite Church</term> <note>A term often used in this period to refer to the religious era of the Old Testament.</note> by the fact that no one could see God and live. The Sun of the spiritual world, as it is after Jehovah God took on the Human and added to it Redemption and a new Righteousness, is described in these words in Isaiah: *“The light of the Sun shall be sevenfold, like the light of seven days, in the day that Jehovah binds up the fracture of his people,”* Chapter 30:26; in which chapter, from beginning to end, the subject is the coming of the Lord. It is also described what would happen if the Lord were to descend and approach any wicked person, by these words in the <term>Apocalypse</term> <note>The Book of Revelation.</note>: *“They hid themselves in the caves and rocks of the mountains, and said to the mountains and rocks, hide us from the face of Him sitting upon the Throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb,”* Chapter 6:15, 16; it is called the "wrath of the Lamb" because the terror and torment appears that way to them when the Lord approaches. This can be clearly concluded from the fact that if any wicked person is let into Heaven, where charity and faith in the Lord reign, darkness seizes his eyes, dizziness and insanity seize his mind, and pain and torment seize his body, and he becomes as if lifeless; what then if the Lord Himself, with His Divine merit, which is Redemption, and with His Divine Righteousness, were to enter a man? The Apostle John himself could not endure the presence of the Lord, for it is read that *“when he saw the Son of Man in the midst of the seven lampstands, he fell at His feet as if dead,”* Revelation 1:17.

642. It is said in the Decrees of the Councils and in the Articles of the Confessions into which the <term>Reformed</term> <note>Refers to the Protestant churches following the tradition of Calvin or Luther.</note> swear, that God, through the infused merit of Christ, justifies the wicked; and yet, the good of even a single Angel cannot be communicated to, much less joined with, a wicked person without it being rejected and bouncing back like an elastic ball thrown against a wall, or being swallowed up like a diamond dropped into a swamp. Indeed, if any truly good thing were thrust in, it would be as if a pearl were tied to the snout of a pig. For who does not know that mercy cannot be cast into unmercifulness, innocence into revenge, love into hatred, or concord into discord—which would be like mixing Heaven and Hell? A man not <term>born again</term> <note>original: "renatus." Referring to the process of spiritual regeneration or rebirth.</note> is, as to his spirit, like a panther or an owl, and can be compared to a thorn or a nettle; but a man born again is like a sheep or a dove, and can be compared to an olive tree or a vine. Think, I pray, if you please: how can a man be turned into a "sheep-man," or an owl into a dove, or a thorn into an olive, or a nettle into a vine, through some "imputation," "assignment," or "application" of Divine righteousness? Such a thing would damn him rather than justify him. For a conversion to happen, must not the wild nature of the panther and owl, or the harmful nature of the thorn and nettle, first be taken away, and a truly human and innocent nature be implanted in its place? How this is done, the Lord also teaches in John, Chapter 15:1 to 7.

## That there is Imputation, but of good and evil, and at the same time of faith.

643. That there is an Imputation of good and evil—which is what is meant in the <term>Word</term> <note>The Bible or Sacred Scripture.</note> wherever it is named—is evident from countless passages there, some of which have been cited elsewhere; but so that everyone may be certain that no other kind of Imputation exists, some further passages from the Word will be brought forward here: *“The Son of man is to come, and then He will render to everyone according to his deeds,”* Matthew 16:27. *“Those who have done good shall come out to the resurrection of life, but those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment,”* John 5:29. *“A book was opened which is the book of life, and all were judged according to their works,”* Revelation 20:12, 13. *“Behold, I come quickly, and My reward is with Me, to give to everyone according to his work,”* Revelation 22:12. *“I will visit according to his ways, I will repay him for his works,”* Hosea 4:9, Zechariah 1:6, Jeremiah 25:14, Chapter 32:19. God, in the day of His wrath and just judgment, will render to

to each according to *his works*, Romans 2:5, 6.
> *We must all be made manifest before the Judgment Seat of Christ, so that each may receive the things done through the body according to what he has done, whether good or evil*, 2 Corinthians 5:10.

There was no other Law of imputation in the beginning of the Church, nor will there be any other at its end. That this was so at the beginning of the Church is clear from Adam and his Wife: because they did evil by eating from the Tree of the knowledge of good and evil, they were condemned (Genesis 2 and 3). That there will be no other law at the end of the Church is clear from these words of the Lord:
> *When the Son of Man comes in the glory of his Father, then He will sit upon the Throne of his glory, and will say to the Sheep on his right, "Come, you blessed, and possess as an inheritance the Kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the World; for I was hungry, and you gave Me to eat; I was thirsty, and you gave Me to drink; I was a stranger, and you took Me in; I was naked, and you clothed Me; I was sick, and you visited Me; I was in prison, and you came to Me." But to the Goats on the left, because they did not do good things, He said, "Depart from Me, you cursed, into the eternal Fire prepared for the devil and his angels,"* Matthew 25:31–46. <note>The author cites verse 33 onward, covering the separation of the sheep and goats based on their actions.</note>

From these passages, anyone with open eyes can see what the Imputation of good and evil actually is. The reason there is also an Imputation of Faith is that Charity (which belongs to what is good) and Faith (which belongs to what is true) are united in good Works; and unless they are united, the Works are not truly good (see above, numbers 373 to 377). Therefore James says:
> *Was not Abraham our Father justified by Works when he offered his Son upon the altar? Do you not see that Faith worked together with his Works, and from Works Faith was recognized as perfect? And the Scripture was fulfilled which says, "Abraham believed God, and it was imputed to him for righteousness,"* James 2:21, 22, 23.

644. The reason that the Leaders of the Christian Churches—and consequently their subordinates—have understood "imputation" in the Word to mean an imputation of Faith (upon which the Righteousness and Merit of Christ are inscribed and thus credited to a person) is that for fourteen centuries—that is, since the time of the <term>Synod of Nicaea</term> <note>Also known as the Council of Nicaea (325 AD), where the foundations of mainstream Christian dogma were formalized.</note>—they have not wanted to know about any other faith. Consequently, that faith alone has settled in their memory and thus in their minds, as if it were a fixed structure. Since that time, it has provided a false light, like the glow of a fire at night; by this light, that faith appeared to be the very core of theological truth. All other doctrines hang from it in a linked series, and they would all fall apart if that "head" or pillar were removed. Therefore, if they were to think of any Faith other than this "imputative" one while reading the Word, that light—along with their entire theological system—would be extinguished, and a darkness would arise from which the whole Christian Church would vanish. Therefore, it has been left, 
> *like the stump of roots in the earth, the tree having been cut down and destroyed, until seven times should pass over it*, Daniel 4:20. <note>A reference to King Nebuchadnezzar's dream, interpreted here as the survival of the core of the Church despite its spiritual decline.</note>

Which of the established leaders of the Church today, when this faith is challenged, does not stop up his ears as if with cotton to avoid hearing anything against it? But, my Reader, open your ears and read the Word, and you will clearly perceive a different faith and a different imputation than what you have been persuaded to believe until now.

645. It is amazing that although the Word from beginning to end is full of testimonies and proofs that to everyone is imputed his own good or evil, the dogmatic teachers of the Christian Religion have nonetheless stopped up their ears as if with wax, and anointed their eyes as if with salve, so that they have not heard or seen—nor do they now hear or see—any other Imputation than that of their own Faith mentioned above. And yet, that Faith can rightly be compared to a disease of the eye called <term>Gutta Serena</term> <note>Literally "clear drop"; an old medical term for amaurosis or total blindness where the eye looks perfectly healthy and clear despite the loss of sight.</note>. Indeed, it deserves that name, for it is an absolute blindness of the eye arising from an obstruction of the <term>Optic Nerve</term>, and yet the eye appears as though it sees perfectly. Similarly, those who are in this faith walk as if with open eyes, appearing to others as if they see everything, when in fact they see nothing. This is because a person knows nothing about that faith when it enters (for he is then like a lifeless log), nor does he later know if it is within him, or if there is anything in it at all. Yet afterward, they seem to see with clear eyes that this Faith gives birth to the noble offspring of <term>Justification</term>—namely, the <term>Remission of sins</term> <note>Forgiveness.</note>, <term>Vivification</term> <note>The process of being made spiritually alive.</note>, <term>Innovation</term> <note>Spiritual renewal.</note>, <term>Regeneration</term> <note>Being born again.</note>, and <term>Sanctification</term>—even though they have never seen, nor can they see, a single sign of any of these things.

646. That the good which is charity, and the evil which is iniquity, after death...

imputed; from all my experience regarding the fate of those who pass from this World into the other, it has been testified to me that everyone, after staying there for a few days, is examined as to what they are like—that is, what they were like in the former World regarding religion. Once this is done, the examiners report this to Heaven, and the person is then transferred to those like themselves, and thus to their own. This is how <term>Imputation</term> <note>original: "Imputatio"; the process of being spiritually assigned or credited with a certain character or destination</note> takes place. That the imputation of good happens to all who are in Heaven, and the imputation of evil to all in Hell, has been made clear to me from the arrangement of both by the Lord. The entire Heaven is organized into Societies according to all the varieties of the love of good, and the entire Hell according to all the varieties of the love of evil. The Church on earth is organized similarly by the Lord, for it corresponds to Heaven; its religion is goodness. Furthermore, ask anyone you like who is endowed with religion and reason, whether from this or from the other two parts of the World, whom they believe will go to Heaven and whom to Hell, and they will answer in agreement: those who do good go to Heaven, and those who do evil go to Hell. Moreover, who does not know that every true human being loves another person—as well as a community of many, a city, and a kingdom—based on their goodness? Indeed, they love not only humans but also animals, and even inanimate things like houses, possessions, fields, gardens, trees, forests, and lands; even metals and stones, for their goodness and use—goodness and use are one. Why would the Lord not love a human being and the Church based on their goodness?

### *That the Faith and Imputation of the New Church can by no means exist together with the faith and imputation of the previous Church; and if they are joined, such a collision and conflict results that everything of the Church in a person perishes.*

647. The reason the Faith and Imputation of the <term>New Church</term> <note>Swedenborg’s term for a new era of Christian understanding</note> cannot exist together with the faith and imputation of the previous (or still-persisting) Church is that they do not agree in one-third, nor even in one-tenth of their points. For the faith of the previous Church teaches that from eternity there existed three Divine Persons, each of whom was individually or by Himself God, and thus also three Creators. But the faith of the new Church is that there has been only one Divine Person, and thus one God from eternity, and that besides Him there is no other God. Therefore, the faith of the previous Church handed down a Divine <term>Trinity</term> divided into three Persons; but the faith of the new Church hands down a Divine Trinity united in one Person. The faith of the previous Church was in an invisible, inaccessible, and un-joinable God, of whom the idea was like that of a spirit, which is like ether or wind; but the faith of the new Church is in a visible, accessible, and joinable God, in whom—just as the soul is in the body—is the invisible, inaccessible, and un-joinable God. Of Him, one has the idea of a Man, because the one God, who was from eternity, was made man in time. The faith of the previous Church attributes all power to the invisible God and takes it away from the visible God; for it teaches that God the Father imputes faith and through it gives eternal life, and that the visible God [Jesus] only intercedes. It also teaches that both of them—or according to the Greek Church, God the Father—gives all the power of working the effects of that faith to the Holy Spirit, who is a third God in order by Himself. But the faith of the new Church attributes the omnipotence of imputing and also of working the effects of salvation to the visible God, in whom the invisible dwells. The faith of the previous Church is primarily in God as Creator, and not simultaneously in Him as Redeemer and Savior; but the faith of the new Church is in one God who is simultaneously Creator, Redeemer, and Savior. The faith of the previous Church is that Repentance, Remission of sins, Renewal, Regeneration, Sanctification, and Salvation follow by themselves from faith given and imputed, without any human effort being mixed in with them

...or be joined; but the faith of the New Church teaches repentance, reformation, regeneration, and thus the remission of sins, with the human being cooperating. The faith of the former Church hands down the <term>imputation of the merit of Christ</term> <note>The traditional doctrine that Christ's personal righteousness is legally credited to the believer's account.</note>, which the granted faith embraces; but the faith of the New Church teaches the imputation of good and evil, and at the same time of faith, and that this imputation is according to the Sacred Scripture, while the other is against it. The former Church teaches the gift of faith containing the merit of Christ, during which the human being is like a <term>stock and stone</term> <note>original: "truncus & lapis"; a phrase used in the 16th-century Formula of Concord to describe human passivity in the process of conversion.</note>, and it also teaches total impotence in spiritual things. The New Church, however, teaches an entirely different faith, which is not in the merit of Christ, but in Jesus Christ Himself—the God, Redeemer, and Savior—and <term>free will</term> <note>original: "liberum arbitrium"</note> both for applying oneself to receive and for cooperating. The former Church joins charity to its faith as an appendix, but not as something that saves, and in this way creates its religion; but the New Church joins faith in the Lord and charity toward the neighbor as two inseparable things, and thus creates a Religion; besides many other disagreements.

648. From that brief review of the disagreements or dissensions, it is clear that the faith and imputation of the New Church can by no means be one with the faith and imputation of the former or still-persisting Church. Because such discord and dissension exists between the faith and imputation of both Churches, there is a total <term>heterogeneity</term> <note>A state of being completely different in kind or nature.</note>; therefore, if both were present in a person’s mind, such a collision and conflict would occur that everything of the Church would perish, and the person would fall into either a delirium or a fainting fit in spiritual matters. Consequently, they would not know what the Church is, or if there even is a Church; nor would they then know anything of God, of faith, or of charity. The faith of the former Church, because it excludes all light from reason, can be compared to an **owl**; but the faith of the New Church can be compared to a **dove**, which flies by day and sees by the light of heaven. Therefore, joining them in one mind would be like the joining of an owl and a dove in one nest, where the owl would lay its eggs and the dove its own; and after incubation, the young would be hatched, and then the owl would tear the dove’s chicks to pieces and give them to its own young as food; for the owl is a voracious bird. Because the faith of the former Church is described in the **Apocalypse Chapter XII** as the **dragon**, and the faith of the New Church as the **woman clothed with the sun**, upon whose head is a crown of twelve stars, one can conclude by comparison what the state of a person’s mind would be if both were in one house together: namely, that the dragon would stand by the woman about to give birth with the intent of devouring her offspring, and that after she fled into the desert, he would pursue her and cast out water like a flood after her, so that she might be swallowed up.

649. A similar thing would happen if someone were to embrace the faith of the New Church and yet retain the faith of the former Church regarding the **Imputation of the merit and justice of the Lord**. For from this root, all the dogmas of the former Church have sprung up like branches. If this were to happen, the comparison would be as if someone escaped from five horns of the dragon only to involve themselves in the remaining five; or as if someone fled a wolf and fell upon a tiger; or like one leaving a pit where there is no water, only to fall into a pit where there is water and be submerged. For in this way, one would easily return to all the aspects of the former faith—the nature of which was explained above—and would then fall into this damnable state: that they would impute and apply to themselves the very Divine attributes of the Lord, which are Redemption and Justice. These can be worshipped, but they cannot be "applied" to oneself; for if a person were to impute and apply those things to themselves, they would be consumed like someone cast into the naked sun, even though it is by that sun's light and heat that the person sees and the body lives. It has been shown above that the Merit of the Lord is Redemption, and that His Redemption and His Justice are two Divine things which cannot be joined to a human being <note>In Swedenborg's view, humans can receive the *effects* of God's work, but cannot "own" or "be credited with" God's own infinite nature.</note>. Let everyone therefore beware of transferring the imputation of the former Church into the imputation of the new, for from this would arise tragic consequences that would stand in the way of their salvation.

# That the Lord imputes good to every person, and that Hell imputes evil to every person.

650. That the Lord <term>imputes</term> <note>original: "imputet"; in a theological sense, this means to credit or assign something to a person’s spiritual "account" or character.</note> good to a person and not any evil, and that the devil—by whom is meant <term>Hell</term>—imputes evil to a person and not any good, is a new idea in the Church. The reason it is considered new is that in many places in the **Word** <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures (the Bible).</note> it is read that God is angry, takes revenge, hates, damns, punishes, casts into hell, and tempts; all of which are of evil, and thus are evils. But it was shown in the chapter on the **Sacred Scripture** that the <term>literal sense</term> of the Word was written using such things as are called <term>appearances and correspondences</term> <note>The idea that spiritual truths are described in the Bible using earthly metaphors or "appearances" that human minds can grasp, even if the literal description (like God being angry) isn't the absolute spiritual reality.</note>. This was done so that there might be a conjunction of the External Church with its Internal, and thus of the World with Heaven. It was also shown there that when such things are read in the Word, these very "appearances of truth," while they pass from the human being to Heaven, are turned into genuine truths. These genuine truths are: that the Lord is never angry, never takes revenge, never hates, damns, punishes, casts into hell, or tempts; consequently, He does no evil to any person. I have frequently observed this change and turning in the Spiritual World.

651. Reason itself supports the fact that the Lord cannot do evil to any person, and therefore cannot impute it to them, for He is Love itself and Mercy itself—thus Goodness itself. These are of His <term>Divine Essence</term>; therefore, to attribute evil or anything of evil to the Lord would be contrary to His Divine Essence, and thus a contradiction. This would be as wicked as joining the Lord and the devil, or Heaven and Hell together, even though 
> *between these a great gulf is fixed, so that those who want to pass from here to there cannot, nor can those from there pass to us* 
<note>Luke 16:26</note>. Not even an Angel of Heaven can do evil to anyone, because the essence of good from the Lord is within them; and conversely, a spirit of hell cannot do anything but evil to another, because the nature of evil from the devil is within them. This essence or nature, which someone has made their own in the World, cannot be changed after death. Consider, I pray, what kind of being the Lord would be if He looked upon the evil out of anger and the good out of mercy. There are myriads of myriads of evil people, and myriads of myriads of good people; if He saved some out of grace and damned others out of vengeance, looking upon them with such different eyes—one gentle and the other harsh, one mild and the other cruel—what then would the Lord God be? Who, instructed by the preaching in the Temples, does not know that all good that is good in itself is from God, and conversely, all evil that is evil in itself is from the devil? If, therefore, any person were to receive both good and evil—good from the Lord and evil from the devil—both with their will, would they not become 
> *neither cold nor hot, but lukewarm, to be spat out* 
according to the Lord's words in the Apocalypse <note>Revelation 3:15, 16</note>.

652. That the Lord imputes good to every person and not evil to anyone, and consequently that He does not judge anyone to Hell, but elevates all to Heaven (as far as the person follows), is evident from these words of His: 
> *Jesus said, when I am lifted up from the earth, I will draw all to Myself* 
<note>John 12:32</note>.

<note>John 3:17, 18</note>.

<note>John 12:47, 48</note>. 
> *Jesus said, I judge no one* 
<note>John 8:15</note>. By "Judgment" here and elsewhere in the Word is meant judgment to Hell, which is damnation; but concerning Salvation, judgment is not predicated, but rather "resurrection to life" <note>John 5:24, 29; 3:18</note>. By the "Word" that will judge is meant the Truth, and truth...

The truth is that all evil is from Hell, and thus they are one; therefore, while a wicked person is being raised by the Lord toward Heaven, his own evil pulls him back, and because he loves evil, he follows it of his own accord. It is also a truth in the **Word** that Goodness is Heaven; therefore, while a Good person is being raised by the Lord toward Heaven, he ascends as if of his own accord and is introduced. These are said to be "written in the Book of Life," Daniel 12:1; Revelation 13:8, 17:8, 21:6. <note>The original text cites Revelation (Apoc.) chapters 12, 13, 17, and 21. Swedenborg often refers to the Book of Life as the record of a person's spiritual state.</note> There is actually a <term>sphere</term> <note>In Swedenborg’s theology, a "sphere" is a spiritual aura or radiation that emanates from every person and from the Divine, influencing those around them.</note> elevating everyone to Heaven, which continually proceeds from the Lord and fills the entire Spiritual World and the entire natural world; it is like a strong <term>current</term> <note>original: "vena"; literally "vein," but used here to describe a stream or current within the ocean.</note> in the Ocean which secretly draws a ship. All those who believe in the Lord and live according to His commandments enter that sphere or current and are elevated; but those who do not believe are unwilling to enter it, but move themselves to the sides, and there they are carried away by the stream that leads into Hell.

653. Who does not know that a Lamb cannot act otherwise than as a lamb, and a sheep not otherwise than as a sheep, and conversely, a wolf not otherwise than as a wolf, and a tiger as a tiger? If these beasts were mixed together, would not the wolf devour the lamb and the tiger the sheep? This is why they are under the guards of shepherds. Who does not know that a fountain of sweet water cannot produce bitter waters from its stream; and that a good tree cannot produce bad fruit; and that a vine cannot prick like a thorn, a lily flower burn like a briar, or a hyacinth sting like a thistle, and vice versa? Therefore, those evil shrubs are uprooted from the fields, vineyards, and gardens, and being gathered into heaps, are thrown into the fire. A similar thing happens with the wicked flowing into the Spiritual World, according to the Lord’s words, Matthew 13:30; John 15:6. The Lord also said to the Jews: *“Brood of vipers, how can you speak good things when you are evil? A good man out of the good treasure of his heart brings forth good things, and an evil man out of the evil treasure brings forth evil things,”* Matthew 12:34, 35.

->*That Faith, according to what it joins itself to, determines the sentence: if true faith joins itself with good, a sentence for eternal life is made; but if faith joins itself with evil, a sentence for eternal death is made.*<-

654. The works of charity performed by a Christian and those performed by a <term>heathen</term> <note>original: "Ethnico"; referring to non-Christians or those outside the revealed Word.</note> appear similar in external form, for one just like the other performs acts of civility and morality for his associate, which in part are similar to the goods of love toward the neighbor; indeed, he can give to the poor, help the needy, and listen to sermons in temples. But who can judge from this whether those external goods are similar in their **internal form**, or whether natural goods are also spiritual? This cannot be concluded except from faith, for faith qualifies them; for faith causes God to be in them and joins them with Himself in the <term>internal man</term> <note>The "internal man" is the soul or the higher part of the mind that is open to heaven.</note>; hence, natural goods become inwardly spiritual. That this is so can be seen more fully from the discussions in the Chapter on Faith, where the following points are demonstrated: *That faith does not live until it is joined to charity. That Charity becomes spiritual from faith, and faith from charity. That faith without charity, because it is not spiritual, is not faith; and that charity without faith, because it does not live, is not charity. That faith and charity apply themselves and join together mutually and reciprocally. That the Lord, Charity, and Faith make one, just as life, will, and intellect do; but if they are divided, each perishes, like a union crumbled into dust.*

655. From what has been brought forward, it can be seen that faith in the one and true God causes good to be good even in its internal form; and conversely, that faith in a false god causes good to be good only in its external form, which is not good in itself. Such was the faith of the gentiles of old in Jupiter, Juno, and Apollo; of the Philistines in Dagon; of others in Baal and Baal-peor; of Balaam the Magician in his god; and of the Egyptia- <note>The text cuts off here at the end of the page; the catchword "tio-" indicates the word continues as "Egyptians" on the next page.</note>

...[multiplication] of others into many. Faith in the Lord—who is the true God and Eternal Life, according to John in his first Epistle, 5:21, and in whom all the fullness of the Divinity dwells bodily, according to Paul in the Epistle to the Colossians 2:9—is completely different. What is faith in God but a looking toward Him, and from that, His presence, and at the same time a confidence that He helps? And what is true faith but that, and at the same time a confidence that all good is from Him, and that He makes His own good to be saving? Therefore, if this faith joins itself with what is good, the judgment is for eternal life; but it is entirely different if it does not join itself with what is good, and even more so if it joins with what is evil.

656. It has been shown above what the conjunction of <term>charity</term> <note>Charity, in this context, refers to the outward expression of love through good works and neighborly service.</note> and faith is like among those who believe in three Gods and yet say they believe in one. The reason is that charity joins itself with faith only in the external, natural man. This is because the mind is fixed on the idea of three Gods, while the lips are making a confession of one God; therefore, if the mind were to pour itself into the confession of the mouth at that moment, it would erase the declaration of one God, open the lips, and cast out its three Gods.

657. Everyone can see from reason that evil and faith in the one and true God cannot exist together. For evil is against God, and faith is for God; evil belongs to the will, and faith belongs to the thought. The will flows into the understanding and makes it think, but not the other way around; the understanding merely teaches what ought to be willed and done. Therefore, the good that such a person does is evil in itself. It is like a shiny bone whose marrow is rotten; it is like an actor on a stage playing a nobleman; it is like the beautiful face of an worn-out prostitute; it is like a butterfly flying with silver wings that lays its eggs on the leaves of a good tree, from which all its fruit perishes; it is like fragrant smoke from a poisonous herb; indeed, it is like a moral thief and a pious swindler. Therefore, his good, which is evil in itself, is hidden inside in the chamber, while his faith, walking and reasoning in the entrance hall, is a mere chimera, a mask, and a bubble. From these things, the truth of the proposition is clear: that faith determines the judgment concerning the good and evil that is joined to it.

## *That Thought is Imputed to No One, but rather the Will.*

658. Every learned person knows that there are two faculties or parts of the Mind: the **Will** and the **Understanding**. But few know how to distinguish them correctly, to examine their properties individually, and then to join them together. Those who cannot do this can only obtain the dimmest notion of the Mind. Therefore, unless the properties of each are first described individually, it cannot be understood that thought is <term>imputed</term> <note>In theology, "imputation" refers to the way God "credits" or "charges" a person with righteousness or sin. Swedenborg argues here that we are judged by our intentions (the Will) rather than just our fleeting thoughts.</note> to no one, but the will is. The properties of both, in summary, are these:

1. That love itself, and the things belonging to love, reside in the will; and that knowledge, intelligence, and wisdom reside in the understanding. The will inspires its love into these and brings about favor and assent; hence, as the love is, and the intelligence resulting from it, such is the person.

2. From this it also follows that all good and also all evil belong to the will; for whatever proceeds from love is called "good," even if it were actually evil, for the delight that makes up the life of love produces this feeling. Through this delight, the will enters the understanding and produces consent.

3. Therefore, the **Will** is the *being* <note>original: "esse"; the underlying essence or core reality of a thing.</note> or essence of a person's life, while the **Understanding** is the *existing* <note>original: "existere"; the outward manifestation or form that the essence takes.</note> or the resulting presence of that life. And because an essence is nothing unless it is in some form, so the will is nothing unless it is in the understanding; therefore, the will forms itself in the understanding and thus comes forth into the light.

4. Love in the **Will** is the "end" or purpose, and in the understanding, it seeks out and finds the "causes" through which it may promote itself to the "effect." And because the end is the purpose, and the person intends this, it is also the purpose of the will; through intention, it enters the understanding and moves it to turn over and weigh the means, and to conclude such things as tend toward the effect.

5. Everything belonging to a person's <term>proprium</term> <note>original: "proprium"; a technical term for the "selfhood" or the inherent nature of a person, which Swedenborg describes as being naturally inclined toward self-interest and evil.</note> resides in the will, and this is evil...

from the first birth, and good is produced from the second; the first birth is from one’s parents, but the second is from the Lord. From these few points, it can be seen that there is one property belonging to the **Will**, and another to the **Understanding**, and that by creation they are joined together like *essence* <note>original: "esse"</note> and *existence* <note>original: "existere"</note>; consequently, a person is a human being primarily from the will, and secondarily from the understanding. It is for this reason that the <term>will</term> <note>The faculty of the mind responsible for desires, intentions, and love.</note> is imputed to a person, but not the thought; and likewise evil and good, because these—as has been said—reside in the will, and from there in the thoughts of the understanding.

659. The reason why no evil is imputed to a person that they merely think about, is because a human being is so created that they are able to understand and thus think about both good and evil—good from the Lord, and evil from Hell. For a person is in the middle, and possesses the faculty of choosing one or the other from <term>free will</term> <note>The spiritual capacity to choose between good and evil, a central theme in this work.</note> in spiritual matters, which was treated in its own Chapter. And because one has the faculty of choosing from freedom, one can either will or not will; and whatever one wills is received by the will and becomes part of them <note>original: "appropriatur" - literally, "is appropriated."</note>, but whatever one does not will is not received, and thus does not become part of them. All the evils to which a person inclines by birth are inscribed on the will of their <term>natural man</term> <note>The part of the human psyche concerned with worldly and physical life, as opposed to the 'spiritual man.'</note>. Insofar as the person draws from these, they flow into the thoughts; similarly, goods with truths flow into the thoughts from above from the Lord. There, they are balanced like weights in the scales of a balance. If the person then adopts the evils, they are received by the old will and add themselves to it; but if they adopt goods with truths, a **new will** and a **new understanding** are formed by the Lord above the old ones, and there the Lord successively implants new goods by means of truths, and through these He subjugates the evils that are below, removes them, and arranges all things into order. From this it is also clear that Thought is the **purifier and the excretory** of the evils inherited from parents; therefore, if the evils which a person thinks were to be imputed, <term>reformation</term> and <term>regeneration</term> <note>The processes of spiritual growth and the creation of a 'new' person through divine influence.</note> could not take place.

660. Since good belongs to the will and truth belongs to the understanding, and many things in the World correspond to good—such as fruit and use—and <term>imputation</term> <note>The act of the Lord attributing or "crediting" a quality to a person's spiritual account.</note> itself corresponds to estimation and price, it follows that what has been said here about imputation can be compared with all created things. For as has been shown here and elsewhere before, all things in the universe relate to good and truth, and conversely to evil and falsity. A comparison can therefore be made with the **Church**: that it is valued by its charity and faith, and not by the rituals attached to it. A comparison can also be made with a **minister of the Church**: that he is esteemed for his will and love, and simultaneously for his understanding in spiritual matters, and not for his affability or his clothing. A comparison is also found in **worship** and the **temple** in which it occurs: worship itself exists in the will, and in the understanding as if in its own temple; and this is called "holy" not because of itself, but because of the Divine which is taught there. Also, a comparison is found in a **Government** where good reigns together with the truth that is loved, but not where there is truth without good. Who judges a **King** by his guards, horses, and carriages, and not by the Royalty which they know is in him? Royalty consists of the love and prudence of governing. Who in a **triumphal procession** does not look at the Victor, and from him the parade, rather than judging the Victor by the parade? Consequently, the formal comes from the essential, and not vice versa. The will is the *essential*, and the thought is the *formal*; and no one can impute anything to the formal except what it draws from the essential; thus to the latter and not the former.

These are inspired into them by the Lord from that Sun, and they are inspired according to reception, and reception is according to the love of becoming wise. After their times of instruction, those who have become Intelligent are sent out from there, and these are called the disciples of the Lord. They are first sent out to the West, and those who do not remain there, to the South, and some through the South to the East, and they are introduced into the Societies where their dwellings will be. 

Once, when I was meditating on Heaven and Hell, I began to desire a universal knowledge of the state of both, knowing that whoever knows universals can afterwards comprehend particulars, because the latter are within the former, just as parts are within a whole. In this desire, I looked toward that region in the northern quarter near the East, where the Places of Instruction were; and by a way then opened to me, I traveled there and entered into one College where there were young men. They did so and said: "The Universals of Hell are three, but the Universals of Hell are diametrically opposite to the Universals of Heaven. After these things were said, following a wish for peace, I departed and returned home. 

When I was at home, it was said to me from Heaven: "Examine those three Universals above and below, and afterwards we shall see them in your hand." It was said "in the hand" because all things that a person examines with the understanding appear to the Angels as if inscribed on the hands. This is why it is said in the <term>Apocalypse</term> <note>The Book of Revelation.</note> that they received a mark on their forehead and on their hand (Chapter 13:16, Chapter 14:9, Chapter 20:4).

After this, I examined the First universal Love of Hell, which was the Love of ruling from self-love, and afterwards the universal love of Heaven corresponding to it, which was the Love of ruling from the love of uses; for I was not permitted to examine one Love without the other, because the Understanding does not perceive one love without the other, as they are opposites. Therefore, so that both may be perceived, they must be set in opposition, one against the other; for a beautiful and handsome face shines forth from its opposite, an unbeautiful and deformed face. When I weighed the Love of ruling from self-love, it was given to me to perceive that this Love was most highly infernal, and thus was among those who are in the deepest Hell; and that the Love of ruling from the love of uses was most highly heavenly, and thus among those who are in the highest Heaven. 

The reason why the Love of ruling from self-love is most highly infernal is because to rule from self-love is to rule from the <term>proprium</term> <note>A technical term in this theology meaning 'what is one's own,' specifically the human ego or self-nature which, left to itself, is inclined toward evil.</note>, and the proprium of man from birth is evil itself, and evil itself is diametrically against the Lord. Wherefore, the further people progress into that evil, the more they deny God and the Holy things of the Church, and worship themselves and nature. Let those who are in that evil examine it in themselves, I pray, and they will see. This love is also such that as much as the reins are loosened for it—provided no impossibility stands in the way—it rushes from step to step, even to the highest; and it does not end there, but if no higher step is granted, it grieves and groans. Among Politicians, this Love ascends so far that they wish to be Kings and Emperors, and if possible, to rule over everything in the world, and to be called kings of kings and emperors of emperors. But the same Love among Churchmen <note>original: "Canonicos"</note> ascends so far that they wish to be gods, and as far as possible, to rule over everything of Heaven, and to be called gods. That both the former and the latter do not acknowledge any God in their hearts will be seen in what follows. But on the other hand, those who wish to rule from the love of uses do not wish to rule from themselves, but from the Lord, since the Love of uses is from the Lord and is the Lord Himself. ...while those who perform uses place these uses far above honors, the former <note>Those in Hell, or those governed by self-love.</note> place honors far above uses.

When I meditated on these things, I was told by an Angel from the Lord: "Very soon you will see and be confirmed by sight as to what that infernal Love is like." Then, suddenly, the earth opened to the left, and I saw a devil ascending from Hell. On his head was a square cap <note>A "pileus quadratus," similar to a mortarboard or a biretta, often associated with scholars or officials.</note> pressed down over his forehead all the way to his eyes. His face was full of pustules like those of a burning fever; his eyes were fierce, and his chest bulged out into a rhombus shape. From his mouth he belched smoke like a furnace. His loins were clearly on fire, and in place of feet he had bony ankles without flesh. From his body there exhaled a putrid and unclean heat. At the sight of him I was terrified and cried out to him, "Do not come near! Tell me, where are you from?" 

He answered hoarsely, "I am from the lower regions, and there I am in a society with two hundred others, which is the most eminent of all societies. There we are all emperors of emperors, kings of kings, dukes of dukes, and princes of princes. No one there is merely an emperor, nor merely a king, duke, or prince. We sit there upon thrones of thrones, and from there we send out mandates into the whole world, and beyond." 

Then I said to him, "Do you not see that you are insane from a fantasy <term>fantasy (phantasia): in this context, a spiritual delusion where one's internal desires create a false reality that seems completely real to the person</term> of superiority?" 

He replied, "How can you speak like that? To ourselves we appear exactly so, and we are also acknowledged as such by our companions." 

Hearing this, I did not want to say "you are insane" again, because he was indeed insane from fantasy. It was given to me to know that this devil, when he lived in the world, had been merely a steward <note>original: "curator," a manager or overseer</note> of some house; and that he was then so elated in spirit that he despised the entire human race in comparison to himself, and indulged in the fantasy that he was more worthy than a king, or even an emperor. Because of this pride, he had denied God and regarded all the holy things of the Church as nothing for himself, though perhaps something for the "stupid commoners." 

Finally, I asked him, "You two hundred there, how long do you boast like this among yourselves?" 

He said, "Forever. But those of us who torment others because our superiority is denied are cast down <note>original: "subsident," meaning to sink or be demoted</note>; for we are allowed to boast, but not to bring evil upon anyone." 

I asked again, "Do you know what the lot is for those who are cast down?" 

He said, "They sink down into a certain prison where they are called 'viler than the vile' or 'the vilest,' and they are made to work." Then I said to that devil, "Watch out, then, that you do not also sink down."

After this, the earth opened again, but to the right; and I saw another Devil rising up. Upon his head was something like a turban <note>original: "Cidaris," an ancient Persian or priestly headdress</note> wound round with coils like snakes, whose head stood out from the top. His face was leprous from forehead to chin, as were both of his hands. His loins were naked and black as soot, through which a dark fire glowed, and his ankles were like two vipers. 

When the first Devil saw this, he threw himself upon his knees and worshipped him. I asked, "Why do you do that?" 

He said, "He is the god of heaven and earth, and he is almighty." 

Then I asked this second one, "What do you say to this?" 

He answered, "What should I say? All power over Heaven and Hell is mine; the fate of all souls is in my hand." 

I asked again, "How can he, who is an 'emperor of emperors,' submit himself like this, and how can you receive worship?" 

He replied, "He is still my servant. What is an emperor before God? In my right hand is the lightning bolt of excommunication." 

Then I said to him, "How can you be so mad? In the world you were only a Canon <note>A "Canonicus" is a member of a cathedral chapter, a middle-ranking church official.</note>, and because you labored under the fantasy that you held the keys, and thus the power of binding and loosing <note>A reference to the biblical "Power of the Keys" (Matthew 16:19), often claimed as the basis for papal and clerical authority.</note>, you raised your spirit to this degree of madness that you now believe you are God himself." 

At this, he was indignant and swore that he was, and that the Lord has no power in Heaven because He has transferred it all to "us." "We have no need to do anything but command, and Heaven and Hell reverently obey. If we send someone to hell, the devils immediately receive him; likewise the Angels receive him whom we send to Heaven." 

I asked further, "How many are you in your society?" 

He said, "Three hundred, and we are all gods there, but I am the god of gods." 

After this, the earth opened under the feet of both, and they sank deep into their hells. It was given to me to see that beneath their Hells were workhouses into which those would fall who bring harm to others; for everyone in Hell is left to his own...

his own fantasy, and also his boasting in it, but it is not permitted to do evil to another. The reason they are like this there is because a person is then in their own spirit, and the spirit, after it has been separated from the body, comes into full freedom of acting according to its affections and the thoughts from them. Afterward it was granted me to look into their hells; and the Hell where the "emperors of emperors" and "kings of kings" were, was full of all uncleanness, and they appeared like various wild beasts with savage eyes. Similarly, in the other hell, where those who were "gods" and "the god of gods" were, there appeared dire birds of the night, which are called *ochim* and *ijim* <note>original: "ochim & Ijim"; these are Hebrew terms from Isaiah 13:21 referring to doleful creatures, desert owls, or jackals that inhabit ruins.</note>, flying around them; the images of their fantasy appeared to me in this way. From these things it was clear what political self-love is like, and what ecclesiastical self-love is like—the latter being a desire to be gods, while the former is a desire to be emperors—and that they desire and even attempt this as much as the reins on those loves are loosened.

After these sad and atrocious things were seen by me, I looked around and saw two Angels standing not far from me and talking together. One was dressed in a woolen robe shining with flaming purple, and a tunic of bright <term>fine linen (byssus): a high-quality, lustrous fabric used in ancient priestly or royal garments</term> under it; the other in similar clothing of scarlet with a <term>turban (cidaris): a ceremonial headdress or miter</term>, into which some <term>fire-stones (pyropi): a type of brilliant red gemstone or bronze-like alloy</term> were inserted on the right side. I approached them and greeted them with peace, and reverently asked, "Why are you here below?" They answered, "We have let ourselves down here from Heaven by the command of the Lord to speak with you about the blessed lot of those who wish to rule from the <term>love of uses (amor usuum): the desire to be useful to others for their own sake, rather than for self-glorification</term>. We are worshipers of the Lord; I am the Prince of a society, and the other is the High Priest there." And the Prince said that he was the servant of his society, because he served it by performing uses; and the other said that he was the minister of the Church there, because in serving them he ministered holy things for the uses of their souls. They said that both are in perpetual joys from the eternal happiness which is in them from the Lord, and that everything in 그 society is splendid and magnificent—splendid from gold and precious stones, and magnificent from palaces and gardens. "The reason is," they said, "that our love of ruling is not from self-love, but from the love of uses; and because the love of uses is from the Lord, therefore all good uses in the Heavens shine and glisten. And because we are all in this love in our society, the atmosphere there appears golden, from the light there which takes its color from the flaming quality of the Sun, and the flaming quality of the Sun corresponds to that love."

Having said these things, a similar sphere appeared even to me around them, and a fragrance was felt from it, which I also mentioned to them. I asked that they add something more to what they said about the love of use; and they continued, saying: "The dignities in which we are, we did indeed seek, but for no other end than that we might be able to perform uses more fully and extend them more widely. We are also surrounded with honor, and we accept it, not for our own sake, but for the good of the society; for our brothers and associates who are of the common people there hardly know any differently than that the honors of our dignities are in us, and therefore that the uses we perform are from us. But we feel differently; we feel that the honors of the dignities are outside of us, and that they are like the garments with which we are clothed; but that the uses we perform are from the love of them within us from the Lord, and this love receives its blessedness from communication with others through uses. And from experience we know that as much as we perform uses from the love of them, so much that love increases, and with the love, wisdom, from which the communication comes. But as much as we keep uses to ourselves and do not communicate them, so much does blessedness perish; and then the use becomes like food stored in the stomach, which, not being distributed to nourish the body and its parts, remains undigested, causing nausea. In a word, the whole of Heaven is nothing but a container of uses from first things to last: what is use but the actual love of the neighbor, and what holds the heavens together but this love?" 

Hearing these things, I asked, "How can anyone know whether they perform uses from self-love, or from the love of uses? Every person, whether good or evil, performs uses, and performs them from some love. Suppose that in the World there were a society composed of mere devils, and a society composed of mere angels; I think that the devils in their society, from the fire of their self-love and from the splendor of their own glory, would perform as many uses as the angels in theirs; who then can know from which Love, and from...

Two angels responded to these things: "Devils perform uses for the sake of themselves and for their reputation, so that they may be elevated to honors or gain wealth; but Angels do not perform uses for those reasons, but for the sake of the uses themselves out of a love for them. A human being cannot distinguish between these uses, but the Lord distinguishes them. Everyone who believes in the Lord and flees evils as sins performs uses from the Lord; but everyone who does not believe in the Lord, nor flees evils as sins, performs uses from themselves and for the sake of themselves. This is the distinction between uses performed by devils and uses performed by Angels." After these words were spoken, the two Angels departed, and from a distance they were seen carried in a fiery chariot like Elijah, and taken up into their Heaven.

**662. THE SECOND MEMORABLE RELATION.** After some time had passed, I entered a certain grove, and there I walked in meditation on those who are in <term>concupiscence (lust): an intense, driving desire for worldly things or selfish pleasures</term> and the resulting <term>fantasy: a state of delusional imagination where one believes their desires are actual reality</term> of possessing those things which belong to the world. Then, at some distance from me, I saw two Angels talking to each other and looking at me in turns. Therefore, I drew closer, and as I approached they spoke to me, saying: "We perceive within ourselves that you are meditating on what we are speaking about—or rather, that we are speaking about what you are meditating on—which arises from a reciprocal communication of affections." 

I therefore asked what they were speaking about. They said, "About Fantasy, about Concupiscence, and about Intelligence; and just now, about those who delight themselves in the vision and imagination of possessing everything in the world." 

I then asked them to express their thoughts on those three: Concupiscence, Fantasy, and Intelligence. Beginning their discourse, they said that everyone is in Concupiscence internally by birth, but in Intelligence externally by education; and that no one is in Intelligence—much less in wisdom—internally (that is, as to their spirit) except from the Lord. For everyone is held back from the concupiscence of evil and kept in intelligence according to their looking toward the Lord and their simultaneous conjunction with Him. Without this, a human being is nothing but concupiscence; yet in external matters, or as to the body, they remain in intelligence through education. 

For a person lusts after honors and wealth, or prominence and opulence; and these two are not attained unless one *appears* to be moral and spiritual—thus, intelligent and wise. So, one learns to appear this way from infancy. This is the reason why, as soon as a person comes among others or into a group, they invert their spirit and pull it away from concupiscence; they speak and act according to the decorum and honesty they learned from infancy and retain in the memory of the body. They take the greatest care that nothing of the madness of concupiscence, in which their spirit actually resides, should leak out. 

From this, every person who is not internally led by the Lord is a pretender, a sycophant, and a hypocrite; appearing to be a human being, and yet not being one. Of such a person it can be said that their shell (the body) is wise, while their kernel (the spirit) is insane; and that their external is human while their internal is bestial. Such people look upward with the back of their head <note>original: "occipitio"</note> and downward with their forehead <note>original: "frontispicio"</note>; thus they walk as if they were oppressed by a heaviness, with their head hanging and their face turned toward the ground. 

When these people leave the body and become spirits, and are then set free from external restraints, they become the madness of their own concupiscence. For those who are in the love of self desire to rule over the universe—indeed, to extend its limits even further to amplify their dominion—and they never see an end to it. Those who are in the love of the world desire to possess all its things, and they grieve and feel envy if any treasures lie hidden away with others. Therefore, so that such people do not become mere concupiscences (and thus not truly human), they are permitted in the spiritual world to think from the fear of losing their reputation—and thus honor and gain—as well as from the fear of the law and its punishment. They are also permitted to apply their minds to some study or work, through which they are held in external things and thus in a state of intelligence, however much they may wander and be insane internally. 

After this, I asked whether all those who are in concupiscence are also in its fantasy. They replied that those are in the fantasy of their concupiscence who think inwardly to themselves and indulge too much in their imagination by talking to themselves. These people almost separate their spirit from its connection with the body; they flood their understanding with their visions, and foolishly delight themselves as if they possessed the whole world. A person is cast into this delirium after death if they abstract their spirit from the body...

We stood in their midst and said, "Do you believe that you possess all the wealth of the Kingdom?" They answered, "We do." Then we asked, "Which of you?" They said, "Each one of us." They said, "Each of us knows that all his things are mine; no one is allowed to think, much less to say, 'mine are not yours,' but it is permitted to think and say, 'yours are mine.'" 

The coins on the tables appeared as if made of pure gold, even to us; but when we let in light from the east, they were actually tiny grains of gold, which they had so magnified through a common, shared fantasy. They said that anyone who enters must bring some gold with them, which they cut into small pieces, and these into grains, and by the power of a unanimous fantasy, they enlarge them into coins of a grander form. Then we said, "Were you not born as rational humans? Where did this visionary folly come from?" They said, "We know it is an imaginary vanity, but because it delights the inner parts of our minds, we enter here and take pleasure as if from the possession of everything. But we stay here only for a few hours, after which we go out, and as often as we do, a sound mind returns to us. Yet our visionary delight comes back to us at intervals and makes us re-enter and leave by turns; thus we are wise and insane by turns." <note>This highlights Swedenborg’s concept that people in the afterlife often choose their own delusions because they find them "delightful," even when they know they are not true.</note> We also know that a hard fate awaits those who craftily steal the goods of others. We asked what that fate was; they said, "They are swallowed up and thrust naked into some infernal prison, where they are kept to work for clothing and for food, and afterward for a few small coins <note>original: "obulos"</note> which they collect and in which they place the joy of their hearts; but if they do evil to their companions, they must give up part of their coins as a fine."

### 663. THE THIRD MEMORABLE RELATION.

Once I was in the midst of Angels, and I heard their conversation. Their talk was about Intelligence and Wisdom: that a human being does not feel or perceive otherwise than that both are in himself, and thus that whatever he wills and thinks is from himself, when nevertheless not a bit of them is from the human being, except for the faculty of receiving them. Among the many things they spoke of was also this: that the **Tree of Knowledge of good and evil** in the Garden of Eden signified the faith that Intelligence and Wisdom were from man, and that the **Tree of Life** signified that Intelligence and Wisdom were from God; and because Adam, by the persuasion of the serpent, ate from the former tree—believing that he was or would become like God—he was therefore expelled from the Garden and condemned. While the Angels were in this conversation, two Priests arrived, together with a man who in the world had been an Ambassador of a Kingdom, and I related to them what I had heard from the Angels...

I had heard about Intelligence and Wisdom; having heard these things, those three began to debate about both of them, and also about Prudence—whether they are from God, or whether they are from man. The debate was heated. Those three believed similarly that they were from man, because sensation itself and the perception following from it confirm this. But the Priests, who at that time were in a state of theological zeal, insisted that nothing of Intelligence and Wisdom, and thus nothing of prudence, are from man. They confirmed this from these passages in <term>the Word: Swedenborg's term for the Sacred Scriptures</term>: *A man can receive nothing unless it has been given him from heaven* <note>John 3:27</note>; and from these: Jesus said to the Disciples, *without Me you can do nothing* <note>John 15:5</note>. But then, because it was perceived by the Angels that even though the Priests spoke in this way, they still believed in their hearts the same as the Legate of the Kingdom, the Angels said to them: "Strip off your garments and put on the garments of political ministers, and believe that you are such." And they did so. Then they thought from their inner selves and spoke from the arguments they nurtured within, which were that all intelligence and wisdom reside in man and belong to him. They said, "Who has ever felt that these flowed in from God?" and they looked at one another and confirmed it. It is a peculiar thing in the spiritual world that a spirit thinks himself to be such as the garment upon him is; the reason is that the <term>Understanding: the faculty of thought</term> clothes everyone there. At that moment a Tree appeared beside them, and it was said to them, "It is the Tree of the knowledge of good and evil; watch yourselves, lest you eat from it." Yet, infatuated with their own Intelligence, they burned with a desire to eat from it, and said among themselves, "Why not? Is the fruit not good?" And they approached and ate. When the Legate of the Kingdom noticed this, they joined together and became friends of the heart; and holding hands, they went together along the way of their own intelligence, which leads toward Hell. But I still saw them brought back from there, because they were not yet prepared.

**664. THE FOURTH MEMORABLE RELATION.** Once I looked out into the spiritual world to the right, and I noticed some of the ELECT talking among themselves. I approached them and said, "I saw you from a distance, and around you was a sphere of heavenly light, from which I knew that you are among those who in the Word are called 'the Elect.' Therefore I approached for the sake of hearing what heavenly things you were discussing." They replied, "Why do you call us 'the Elect'?" I answered, "Because in the world where I am in the body, they do not know otherwise than that by 'the Elect' in the Word are meant those who are chosen and <term>predestined: the belief that God determines a person's eternal fate before they are born</term> for Heaven by God either before they are born or after they are born; and that to these alone is Faith given as a token of Election, while the rest are reprobated and left to themselves to go whatever way they wish to Hell. However, I know that no Election takes place before birth, nor after it, but that all are elected and predestined because all are called to Heaven. The Lord, after death, elects those who have lived well and believed rightly, and these only after they have been examined. That this is so, it has been given to me to know from much experience. And because I saw you encircled as to your heads by a sphere of heavenly light, I perceived that you are among the Elect who are being prepared for Heaven." To this they replied, "You report things never heard before. Who does not know that no man is born who is not called to Heaven? And that from those, after death, are elected those who have believed in the Lord and lived according to His commandments? To acknowledge any other 'Election' would be to accuse the Lord Himself not only of powerlessness to save but also of injustice."

**665.** After this, a voice was heard from Heaven from the Angels who were immediately above us, saying, "Ascend here, and we will question one of you who is still in the natural world as to his body, what they know there concerning CONSCIENCE." I replied, "If it pleases you, let us descend and we will call together a number of both Laymen and Clergy from those who are believed to be wise, and we will stand <term>in the perpendicular: directly beneath the angels, so they can hear</term> below you, and you will ask the questions, and thus hear with your own ears what they will answer." Then, after a short hour’s time, so many were present that they almost filled the space of a <term>stadium: an ancient measure of distance, here used to describe a large assembly ground</term>. But the Angels from above arranged them all into four Assemblies. One consisted of Politicians, the second of Scholars, the third of Physicians, and the fourth of Clergy. Once they were arranged, we said to them: "Forgive us for calling you together; the reason is that the Angels who are directly above us are burning to know what you thought about **Conscience** in the world where you previously lived, and what you still think about it now, since you still retain your former ideas on such matters. For it has been reported to the Angels that the knowledge of Conscience is among the lost arts in the world."

After this, we began, and first turned ourselves to the Assembly consisting of Politicians. We asked them to say from the heart, if they pleased, what they had thought, and what they still think now, regarding **CONSCIENCE**. To this they responded, one after another; their responses were collected into one: that they knew nothing other than that "Conscience" was "to know within oneself" <note>original: *se-cum scire*, a play on the Latin etymology of *conscientia*</note>—that is, to be conscious of what one intends, thinks, does, and says. 

But we said to them: "We did not ask about the etymology of the word 'Conscience,' but about Conscience itself." 

They replied: "What is Conscience other than the pain arising from a preconceived fear of losing honor or wealth, and also reputation on account of those two? But that pain is dispelled by feasts and cups of noble wine, and by conversations about the games of Venus and her boy <note>A reference to sexual lust and Cupid</note>." 

To this we said: "You are joking. Tell us, if you please, whether any of you has felt any anxiety from another source?" 

They responded: "What 'other source'? Is not the whole world like a Theater, upon which everyone acts out their own scene, just as actors do upon theirs? We elude and circumvent whoever we can by means of their own lusts—some by mockery, some by flattery, some by cunning, some by pretended friendship, some by feigned sincerity, and others by various political arts and deceptions. From this, we feel no mental pain, but on the contrary, a cheerfulness and gladness, which we breathe out silently and fully with an expanded chest. We have indeed heard from some in our company that anxiety and distress—as if of the heart and chest—came upon them at intervals, causing a contraction of the mind; but when they sought out the pharmacists regarding these things, they were instructed that these feelings arose from <term>melancholic humor: an imbalance of 'black bile' once thought to cause sadness</term> originating from undigested matter in the Stomach, or from a diseased state of the spleen. We have heard that some of these were restored to their former cheerfulness through medicines."

After we heard these things, we turned to the Assembly consisting of Scholars, among whom were also many skilled in the physical arts. Addressing them, we said: "You who have studied the Sciences, and are therefore believed to be Oracles of wisdom, say, if you please, what Conscience is." 

They responded: "What kind of proposition is this? We have heard, indeed, that among some there is a sadness, sorrow, and anxiety, infesting not only the gastric regions of the body but also the dwellings of the mind. For we believe that the two Brains are those dwellings; and because these consist of containing fibers, we believe there is some sharp fluid <note>original: *humor acris*</note> that twitches, bites, and gnaws the fibers there. This compresses the sphere of the mind's thoughts so that it cannot pour itself out into various delights. From this it happens that a person attends to only one thing, which destroys the sensitivity and elasticity of those fibers, making them stubborn and rigid. From these things arises the irregular movement of the <term>animal spirits: believed at the time to be the fluid or 'vapors' that carried nerve impulses</term>, which is called **Ataxia** <note>disorder or lack of coordination</note> by Physicians, and also a defect in their functions which is called **Lipothamia** <note>fainting or a swoon</note>. In a word, the Mind then sits as if besieged by hostile troops, nor can it turn itself here or there any more than a wheel fixed with a nail, or a ship stuck upon the Quicksands. Such distress of the Mind and thus of the Chest arises in those whose reigning Love suffers a loss; if this Love is attacked, the fibers of the Brain contract, and that contraction prevents the Mind from running out freely and capturing delights in various forms. According to their temperament, when people are in this crisis, they are invaded by different kinds of fantasies, insanities, and delusions—and some by 'brain-delusions' in religious matters, which they call 'stings of Conscience.'"

After this, we turned to the Third Assembly, which consisted of Physicians, among whom were also Surgeons and Pharmacists. We said: "You perhaps know what Conscience is—is it a hostile pain that seizes and..."

These physicians responded: "Conscience is nothing but a particular kind of pain. We know its origins better than others, for they are incidental diseases which infest the organs of the body and also the organs of the head, and consequently the Mind as well, since the mind sits in the organs of the brain like a spider in the center of the threads of its web, through which it runs out and back in a similar fashion. We call these diseases 'organic diseases,' and those which return in cycles we call 'chronic diseases.' But the kind of pain described to us by the sick as 'pain of Conscience' is nothing other than <term>Hypochondriacal disease: a condition formerly believed to be caused by vapors from the spleen or upper abdomen, resulting in melancholy or anxiety</term>, which primarily deprives the <term>Spleen</term>, and secondarily the <term>Pancreas</term> and <term>Mesentery</term>, of their natural functions. From this are derived stomach ailments, which lead to <term>Cachochymia: a disordered state of the bodily fluids or 'humors'</term>. For a compression occurs around the opening of the stomach which is called <term>Cardialgia: literally 'heart-pain,' though used here to mean severe heartburn or stomach distress</term>. From these are derived humors impregnated with black, yellow, or green bile, which block the smallest blood vessels, called <term>capillaries</term>. This results in <term>cachexia: wasting of the body</term>, <term>atrophy</term>, and <term>symphesis: a growing together of parts</term>, and also <term>spurious pneumonia</term> <note>original: "Peripneumonia notha"</note> arising from sluggish <term>pituita: phlegm</term>, and a corrosive, <term>ichorous: watery or thin</term> lymph throughout the entire mass of the blood. Similar things also flow from the escape of pus into the blood and its serum from ruptured <term>empyemas: collections of pus in a body cavity</term>, <term>abscesses</term>, and <term>apostemes: swellings or boils</term> in the body. When this blood rises through the <term>carotid arteries</term> into the head, it wears away, corrodes, and bites at the medullary, cortical, and meningeal layers of the Brain, and thus excites the pains which are called 'pains of Conscience'."

Having heard these things, we said to them: "You speak in the language of Hippocrates and Galen <note>Hippocrates and Galen were the foundational authorities of ancient medicine whose 'humoral' theories persisted into the 18th century</note>; that is all Greek to us <note>original: "illa nobis sunt græca," a common idiom meaning 'unintelligible'</note>, and we do not understand it. We did not ask about these diseases, but about Conscience, which belongs to the Mind alone." 

They replied: "The diseases of the mind and the diseases of the head are the same, and these ascend from the body; for they are connected like the two stories of a single house, between which there is a staircase for ascending and descending. Therefore, we know that the state of the mind depends inseparably on the state of the body. But those heavinesses or <term>Cephalalgias: headaches</term> which we gathered you understood to be 'consciences,' we have cured—some by plasters and blistering agents, some by infusions and emulsions, and some by seasonings and painkillers."

When we heard more of the same from them, we turned away and addressed the Clergy. We said, "You know what Conscience is; speak then, and instruct those present." 

They replied: "What Conscience is, we know and we do not know. We believed it to be **CONTRITION**, which precedes **Election** <note>Election refers to the theological concept of being chosen by God for salvation</note>—that is, the moment in which a person is gifted with faith, through which a new heart and a new spirit are made in them, and they are regenerated. But we have observed that such Contrition has happened to few; to some there is only a dread and an ensuing anxiety regarding hellfire, but hardly to anyone is there anxiety for their sins and the resulting just anger of God. But we confessors have healed those people through the Gospel: that Christ, through the Passion of the cross, took away damnation, and thus extinguished hellfire and opened Heaven to those who are blessed by the faith upon which the merit of the Son of God is inscribed by imputation. Furthermore, there are 'conscientious' people from various religions, both true and fanatical, who create scruples for themselves in matters of salvation—not only in essential things, but also in formal things, and even in <term>adiaphora: matters of religious indifference, neither commanded nor forbidden by God</term>. Therefore, as we said before, we know that Conscience exists, but what and of what nature a true Conscience is—which must be entirely spiritual—we do not know."

**666.** All these things, which were declared by the four Assemblies, were heard by the Angels who were above them. They said among themselves, "We perceive that no one in Christendom knows what Conscience is; therefore, we will send down one of our own to instruct them." And immediately there stood in their midst an Angel in a white garment, around whose head appeared a bright circlet in which there were tiny stars. Addressing the four Assemblies, he said: "We have heard in Heaven that you have offered your opinions on **CONSCIENCE** in order, and you have all supposed it to be some pain of the mind which infests the Head and then the Body, or the Body and then the Head. But Conscience, viewed in itself, is not a pain, but a spiritual **Willingness** to act according to those things which belong to Religion and Faith. It is for this reason that those who enjoy Conscience are in the tranquility of peace and in internal blessedness when they act according to their conscience..."

Having heard the definitions from the Politicians and Physicians on the previous page, the narrator now records the explanation given by an Angel, who distinguishes between true spiritual conscience and mere natural distress.</meta>
