-> # UNIVERSAL THEOLOGY # <-

...and in a state of unrest while they act against it. However, the pain of mind, which you believed to be *Conscience*, is not *Conscience*, but is *Temptation* <note>In this context, temptation refers to a spiritual struggle between one's higher ideals and lower impulses</note>, which is the battle of the spirit and the flesh; and when this is spiritual, it draws its lifeblood from conscience; but if it is merely natural, it takes its origin from diseases, which the Physicians recently listed. 

What *Conscience* is, however, can be illustrated by examples: A **Priest**, who has a spiritual will to teach truths for the *end* <note>original: "finem" — in Swedenborg's thought, the 'end' or purpose is the most vital part of an action</note> that his flock may be saved, has conscience; but he who does so for any other cause as an end, does not have conscience. A **Judge**, who looks uniquely to Justice, and carries this out with judgment, has conscience; but he who primarily looks to reward, friendship, and favor, does not have conscience. Furthermore, every man who has another's goods in his possession, without the other knowing, and thus without fear of the law or loss of honor and reputation, could gain them—if he nevertheless restores them to the other because they are not his, he has conscience, for he does what is just for the sake of what is just. 

Suppose also someone who could attain an office, but knows that another, who also seeks it, would be more useful to Society; if he yields the place to the other for the sake of the good of society, he has a good conscience; and similarly in other cases. All those who have conscience speak from the heart what they speak, and do from the heart what they do; for they have an **Undivided Mind**, since they speak and act according to that which they understand and believe to be true and good. 

From this it follows that a more perfect *Conscience* can exist among those who are in the truths of faith more than others, and who are in clear perception more than others, than among those who are less enlightened and in obscure perception. In true Conscience is the very spiritual **Life** of man, for there his **Faith** is joined to **Charity** <note>Charity here means "active love for the neighbor"</note>; wherefore to act from Conscience is, for them, to act from their spiritual Life, and to act against Conscience is, for them, to act against that Life of theirs. 

Besides, who does not know from common speech what Conscience is? When it is said of someone, "This man has a conscience," is it not also then understood, "This is a just man"? And conversely when it is said of someone, "This man has no conscience," is it not then also understood, "This man is unjust"? 

When the Angel had spoken these things, he was suddenly taken up into his Heaven, and the four groups gathered into one. After they had talked among themselves for a while about the Angel's sayings, behold, they were again divided into four groups, but different ones than before: 
* Into one where those were who understood the Angel's words and assented; 
* Into another where those were who did not understand but still favored them; 
* Into a third where those were who did not want to understand, saying, "What have we to do with Conscience?"; 
* And into a fourth where those were who mocked, saying, "What is Conscience but a puff of wind?" 

And I saw them withdrawing from each other, and then the first two groups going away to the right, and the two latter groups to the left; and the latter were descending, while the former were ascending.

# CHAPTER TWELVE

### ON

## B A P T I S M.

->*That without knowledge of the spiritual sense of the Word, no one can know what the two sacraments, Baptism and the Holy Supper, involve and effect.*<-

667. It was shown in the chapter on <term>Sacred Scripture</term> <note>original: "SCRIPTURA SACRA"</note> that there is a <term>spiritual sense</term> <note>original: "Sensus spiritualis" — a deeper, symbolic meaning within the Bible</note> in each and every part of the Word, and that this sense has been unknown until now, but is today disclosed for the sake of the New Church which is to be established by the Lord. What that sense is like can be seen not only there, but also in the chapter on the <term>Decalogue</term> <note>The Ten Commandments</note>, which was also explained according to that sense. Unless that sense were opened, who would think of those two sacraments, Baptism and the Holy Supper, as anything other than their natural sense (which is the sense of the letter)? And would they not say, or mutter to themselves, "What is Baptism but the pouring of water over the head of an infant, and what does this have to do with salvation?" and "What is the Holy Supper but the taking of bread and wine, and what does this have to do with salvation?" Furthermore, they might ask, where is the holiness in them, except for the fact that they have been received and commanded by the ecclesiastical order as divine and holy? In themselves, they would seem to be nothing more than ceremonies, of which the churches say that when the <term>Word of God</term> <note>original: "Verbum Dei"</note> is added to these elements, they become sacraments. I appeal to the laity, and also to the clergy, whether they have perceived anything else in their spirit and heart regarding these two sacraments, and whether they have revered them as divine for various other causes and reasons; yet these two sacraments, when viewed in the spiritual sense, are the most holy things of worship. That they are such will be established from what follows, where their uses will be handed down. But because the uses of these sacraments can by no means come into anyone’s mind unless the spiritual sense detects and unfolds them, it follows that without that sense, no one can know anything other than that they were ceremonies which are holy only because they were instituted by command.

668. That Baptism was commanded is clearly evident from the baptism of John in the Jordan, to which all Judea and Jerusalem went (Matthew 3:5, 6; Mark 1:4, 5). Furthermore, it is evident that the Lord our Savior Himself was baptized by John (Matthew 3:13 to 17), and moreover, that He commanded the disciples to baptize all nations (Matthew 28:19). Who does not see, if he wishes to see, that in that institution there is something divine which has hidden until now, because the spiritual sense of the Word was not previously revealed? And this sense is revealed today because the Christian Church, such as it is in itself, is now for the first time beginning; the former church was Christian in name only, but not in reality and essence.

669. The two sacraments, Baptism and the Holy Supper, are in the Christian Church like two <term>jewels</term> <note>original: "Clenodia" — precious insignia or crown jewels</note> in a King's scepter; if their uses are not known, they are merely like two forms made of ebony on a walking stick. These two sacraments in the Christian Church may also be compared with two rubies or carbuncles on the cloak of an Emperor <note>The text here ends mid-word: "Imperato-". The catchword "ris" completes the word "Imperatoris," meaning "of the Emperor."</note>

if their uses are unknown, they are like two carnelian stones or crystals on some robe. The uses of those two sacraments can be compared to a Temple which, due to its age, has sunk into the ground and lies surrounded by ruins up to its roof, over which young and old people walk, ride in carriages, and travel on horseback, not knowing that such a Temple is beneath their feet and hidden away—a temple in which there are Altars of gold, walls of silver inside, and decorations of precious stone. These cannot be dug up and brought to light except through the spiritual sense, which is disclosed today for the <term>New Church</term> <note>A reference to the "New Jerusalem" or the new era of Christianity Swedenborg believed he was inaugurating</note>, for the sake of its use in the Worship of the Lord. 

Those sacraments can also be compared to a double Temple, one of which is below and the other above. In the lower one, the Gospel is preached concerning the New Advent of the Lord, and also concerning <term>Regeneration</term> <note>original: "Regeneratione"; the process of being spiritually reborn</note> and the resulting salvation by Him. From this Temple, near the Altar, there is an ascent into the upper Temple where the <term>Holy Supper</term> <note>original: "Sancta Cœna"; the Eucharist or Communion</note> is celebrated; and from there is the passage into Heaven, where the Lord receives them. 

They can also be compared to the Tabernacle, in which, after entering, the Table appears upon which the <term>bread of the presence</term> <note>original: "panes facierum"; also known as showbread</note> is arranged in its order, and also the golden Altar for incense, and in the middle the Lampstand with lighted lamps, by which all those things come into view. And finally, for those who allow themselves to be enlightened, the Veil is opened to the <term>Holy of Holies</term> <note>The innermost chamber of the sanctuary</note>, where in place of the Ark in which the Decalogue had been, the <term>Word</term> <note>original: "Verbum"; the Sacred Scripture</note> is placed, over which is the <term>Mercy Seat</term> <note>original: "Propitiatorium"; the golden lid of the Ark</note> with Cherubim of Gold. These are the Representations of those two sacraments and their uses.

## *That by the Washing, which is called <term>Baptism</term>, is understood spiritual <term>Washing</term>, which is Purification from evils and falsities, and thus <term>Regeneration</term>.*

670. That Washings were commanded to the children of Israel is known from the Statutes brought through Moses: such as that Aaron should wash himself before he put on the garments of ministry (Leviticus 16:4, 24) and before he approached the Altar to minister (Exodus 30:18–21; Chapter 40:30, 31). Likewise the Levites (Numbers 8:6, 7), and also others who became unclean through sins. It is also said that they are sanctified through Washings (Exodus 24:9; Chapter 40:12; Leviticus 8:6). Therefore, so they might wash themselves, the <term>Bronze Sea</term> <note>original: "Mare æneum"; a large basin in the Temple</note> and several basins were placed near the Temple (1 Kings 7:23–39). Indeed, they washed vessels and utensils, such as tables, benches, beds, platters, and cups (Leviticus 11:32; Chapter 14:8, 9; Chapter 15:5–12; Chapter 17:15, 16; Matthew 23:25–27). 

But Washings and many similar things were enjoined and commanded to the children of Israel for this reason: because the Church established among them was a <term>Representative Church</term> <note>original: "Ecclesia repræsentativa"; a church where physical rituals symbolize spiritual realities</note>, and it was such that it prefigured the coming Christian Church. Therefore, when the Lord came into the world, He abolished the Representations, which were all external, and established a Church in which everything was to be internal. Thus the Lord dispelled the figures and revealed the actual images themselves, just as one removes a veil or opens a door and causes the interior things not only to be seen, but also to be entered. Out of all those rituals, the Lord retained only two, which would contain everything of the internal Church in one complex: these are <term>Baptism</term> in place of Washings, and the <term>Holy Supper</term> in place of the Lamb, which was sacrificed every day and fully at the <term>Feast of the Passover</term> <note>original: "Festo Paschatis"</note>.

671. That the Washings mentioned above prefigured and foreshadowed—that is, represented—spiritual Washings, which are purifications from evils and falsities, is clearly evident from these words: "When the Lord shall have washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion, and...

-># OF THE NEW HEAVEN AND THE NEW CHURCH<-

...washed away bloodstains <note>original: "sanguines"; a Latin plural often used to denote bloodguilt or stains of violence</note> in the spirit of judgment and the spirit of burning (Isaiah 4:4). *Though you wash yourself with lye and use much soap, yet the stain of your guilt remains before me* (Jeremiah 2:22; Job 9:30-31). *Wash me from my iniquity, and I shall be whiter than snow* (Psalm 51:2, 7). *O Jerusalem, wash your heart from wickedness, that you may be saved* (Jeremiah 4:14). *Wash yourselves, make yourselves clean; remove the evil of your deeds from my eyes; cease to do evil* (Isaiah 1:16). That the washing of a person's spirit was intended by the washing of their body, and that the <term>Internal</term> <note>The inner spiritual reality of a person, consisting of their will and understanding</note> things of the Church were represented by <term>External</term> <note>The outward rituals or physical actions performed in religious worship</note> things—such as those in the Israelite Church—is clearly evident from the Lord's words. When the Pharisees and Scribes saw that His disciples ate bread with unwashed hands, they found fault; for the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they wash their hands "with the fist" <note>original: "pugnotenus"; a specific ritual manner of washing up to the elbow or with a clenched fist</note>; besides many other things which they have received to hold, such as the washing of cups, pots, copper vessels, and couches. To them and to the crowd the Lord said: *Listen to Me, all of you, and understand: there is nothing outside a person that by going into him can defile him, but the things that come out of him are what defile him* (Mark 7:1–4, 14–15; Matthew 15:2, 11, 17–20). And elsewhere: *Woe to you, Scribes and Pharisees, for you clean the outside of the cup and the plate, but inside they are full of greed and self-indulgence. Blind Pharisee, first clean the inside of the cup and the plate, so that the outside also may be clean* (Matthew 23:25–26). From these passages it is evident that by "Washing," which is called Baptism, is meant spiritual washing, which is <term>Purification</term> <note>The process of being cleared of "evils" (bad intentions) and "falsities" (wrong beliefs)</note> from evils and falsities.

672. What person of sound reason cannot see that the washing of the face, hands, and feet, and all the limbs—indeed, of the whole body in a bath—effects nothing more than the removal of dirt, so that they appear clean in a human form before others? And who cannot understand that no mere washing enters into a person's spirit and makes it equally clean? For every scoundrel, plunderer, and thief <note>original: "furcifer, prædo & latro"</note> can wash himself until he shines; does that wipe away his villainy, his thievery, or his criminality? Does not the internal flow into the external and produce the effects of its own will and understanding? But the external does not flow into the internal; for this is against nature, because it is against order. The former, however, is according to nature, because it is according to order.

673. From this it follows that Washings, and also Baptisms—unless a person’s internal is purified from evils and falsities—accomplish no more than the cleaning of dishes and plates by the Jews, or, as follows in that same passage, like tombs which appear beautiful on the outside, but inside are full of dead men's bones and all uncleanness (Matthew 23:25–28). This is further evident from the fact that the Hells are full of "Satans" <note>In Swedenborg's terminology, "Satans" are those in hell who are centered in false beliefs, while "Devils" are those centered in evil desires</note> who were both baptized and unbaptized. What Baptism actually provides will be seen in what follows; therefore, without its uses and fruits, it contributes no more to salvation than the triple crown <note>original: "Cidaris triplicata"; the papal tiara</note> upon the Pope’s head or the sign of the cross upon his shoes contributes to his pontifical supremacy. It is no more than a purple robe around a Cardinal is to his dignity, or a pallium <note>A circular band of white wool worn by archbishops</note> around a Bishop is to the true function of his ministry; no more than a throne, crown, scepter, and robe are to a King's royal power; no more than a silken cap <note>original: "Pilus sericatus"; an academic cap worn by those with a doctorate</note> on the head of a laurel-crowned doctor is to his intelligence; or no more than banners before troops of cavalry are to their bravery in war. Indeed, it can further be said that it no more purifies a person than the washing of a sheep or a lamb before shearing; for the natural man separated from the spiritual man is merely animal—indeed, as shown before, he is more of a wild beast than a beast of the forest. Therefore, if you are washed with rainwater, with the water of dew, with the waters of the most excellent springs, or as the prophets say, if you are cleansed with lye, hyssop, or soap <note>original: "nitro, hyssopo, smegmate, seu sapone"</note> every day, you are still not purified from iniquities except through the means of <term>Regeneration</term> <note>The process of spiritual rebirth</note>, which have been discussed in the chapters on Repentance, and on Reformation and Regeneration.

## *That Baptism was instituted in place of Circumcision, because the circumcision of the heart was represented by the circumcision of the foreskin; this was for the purpose that the internal Church might succeed the external Church, which in each and every detail prefigured the Internal Church.*

674. In the Christian World, it is known that there is an Internal and an External man, and that the External is the same as the <term>Natural man</term> <note>The part of a person concerned with the physical world and self-interest</note>, and the Internal is the same as the <term>Spiritual man</term> <note>The part of a person where the spirit and heavenly influences reside</note>, because his spirit is within it. Since the Church consists of people, it follows that there is both an Internal and an External Church. If one examines the succession of Churches in their order from ancient times to the present, it will be seen that the prior Churches were external—that is, their worship consisted of external rituals which represented the internal things of the Christian Church, which was founded by the Lord when He was in the world, and is now for the first time being built up by Him. The primary thing that distinguished the Israelite Church from the rest in the <note>original: "Asiatico Orbe"; refers to the Ancient Near East</note> Asian World, and later from the Christian Church, was Circumcision. Because all the external features of the Israelite Church figured <note>original: "figurabant"; served as a symbolic preview or type</note> all the internal features of the Christian Church, the primary sign of that Church had an internal similarity to the sign of the Christian Church. For circumcision signified the rejection of the <term>concupiscences</term> <note>Strong, disordered desires or lusts, specifically those of the flesh</note> of the flesh, and thus purification from evils; Baptism signifies the same thing. From this it is clear that Baptism was commanded in place of Circumcision, both so that the Christian Church might be distinguished from the Jewish Church, and so that the internal Church might be more closely recognized; this is known from the Uses of Baptism, which follow.

675. That Circumcision was instituted as a sign that the men of the Israelite Church were from the posterity of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, is evident from these words: *"God said to Abraham, 'This is My covenant which you shall observe between Me and you, and your seed after you; every male among you shall be circumcised, and you shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin, that it may be a sign of the covenant between Me and you'"* (Genesis 17:10–11). This covenant, or its sign, was later confirmed through Moses (Leviticus 12:1–3). And because that Church was distinguished from others by that sign, before the children of Israel crossed the Jordan, they were commanded to be circumcised again (Joshua 5). The reason was that the Land of Canaan represented the Church, and the River Jordan represented the introduction into it. Furthermore, so that they might remember that sign in the land of Canaan itself, this was commanded: *"When you come into the land and plant any kind of tree for food, you shall count its fruit as uncircumcised <note>original: "praeputiabitis praeputium"; literally 'you shall foreskin its foreskin,' a Hebrew idiom for treating fruit as forbidden</note>; for three years it shall be uncircumcised to you, it shall not be eaten"* (Leviticus 19:23). That Circumcision represented and therefore signified the rejection of the lusts of the flesh, and thus purification from evils—the same as Baptism—is clear from those places in the Word where it is said that they should circumcise the Heart, as in these: *"Moses said, 'Circumcise the foreskin of your heart, and do not harden your neck anymore'"* (Deuteronomy 10:16). *"Jehovah your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your seed, that you may love Jehovah your God with all your heart and with all your soul, that you may live"* (Deuteronomy 30:6). And in Jeremiah: *"Circumcise yourselves to Jehovah, that He may remove the foreskins of your heart, you men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem, lest My wrath go forth like fire because of the evil of your doings"* (Chapter 4:4). And in Paul: *"In Jesus Christ neither circumcision nor uncircumcision counts for anything, but faith working through charity, and a new creature"* (Galatians 5:6, 6:15). From these things it is now clear that Baptism was instituted in place of circumcision, because through the circumcision of the flesh was represented the circumcision of the heart, which also signifies purifica-

purification from evils, for evils of every kind arise from the flesh, and the "foreskin" signifies the foul loves of the flesh. Because circumcision and the washing of baptism signify a similar thing, it is said in Jeremiah: "Circumcise yourselves to Jehovah, that he may remove the foreskins of your heart" (Chapter 4:4); and a little later, "Wash your heart from wickedness, O Jerusalem, that you may be saved" (Verse 14). What the "Circumcision" and "Washing of the heart" actually are, the Lord teaches in Matthew, Chapter 15:18–19 <note>In this passage, Jesus explains that what comes out of the heart—such as evil thoughts and intentions—is what truly defiles a person, rather than failing to wash one's hands.</note>.

676. There were many among the children of Israel, and today there are many among the Jews, who believe that they are chosen above all others simply because they are circumcised; and among Christians, there are those who believe the same because they are baptized. Yet both Circumcision and Baptism were given only as a **Sign** and a **Memorial**, intended to remind people that they must be purified from evils and thus become "chosen." What is the **External** without the **Internal** in a person? It is like a Temple without worship; it serves no use except perhaps as a stable. Furthermore, what is the External without the Internal but like a field of mere reeds and rushes without any grain? Or a vineyard of mere branches and leaves without any grapes? It is like the fig tree without fruit, which the Lord cursed (Matthew 21:19), or like the lamps in the hands of the foolish bridesmaids that had no oil (Matthew 25:3). Indeed, it is like living in a mausoleum <note>original: "Mausolæo"</note> where corpses lie beneath your feet, bones line the walls, and "night-specters" <note>original: "nocturnæ larvæ"; Swedenborg uses this to describe hellish or ghostly influences that haunt a mind devoid of spiritual life.</note> fly beneath the roof. Or it is like a chariot pulled by leopards, driven by a wolf, with a fool as the passenger. For the "external man" is not truly a human being, but only the *form* of a human; it is the **Internal**—which means being wise from God—that truly makes a person. This applies equally to the circumcised and the baptized: the rite is empty unless they also circumcise or wash their hearts.

### *That the first Use of Baptism is Introduction into the Christian Church, and at the same time insertion among Christians in the spiritual world.*

677. That Baptism is an introduction into the Christian Church is evident from many factors, such as these:
I. That Baptism was instituted in place of Circumcision. Just as Circumcision was the sign that one belonged to the Israelite Church, Baptism is the sign that one belongs to the Christian Church, as shown in the previous article. A sign's only purpose is recognition—much like different colored ribbons <note>original: "fasciæ"; literally bands or bandages used to identify infants</note> placed on the babies of two different mothers so they can be distinguished and not accidentally swapped.
II. That it is merely a sign of introduction is clearly seen from the baptism of infants. They possess no use of reason yet and are no more capable of receiving "faith" than the new shoots <note>original: "palmites"</note> on a tree.
III. Not only infants are baptized, but also all foreign converts <note>original: "proselytæ"</note> who turn to the Christian religion, whether young or old. This is done before they are even instructed, based simply on their confession that they wish to embrace Christianity, into which they are inaugurated through Baptism. The Apostles did the same, according to the Lord’s words to "make disciples of all nations, baptizing them" (Matthew 28:19).
IV. John the Baptist baptized all who came to him from Judea and Jerusalem in the Jordan (Matthew 3:6; Mark 1:9). The reason he used the Jordan was because that river was the entry point into the Land of Canaan. Since the "Land of Canaan" symbolized the Church (because the Church was established there), the Jordan symbolized the **Introduction** into it. (For more on the Land as the Church and the Jordan as Introduction, see *The Apocalypse Revealed*, no. 285).

All of this happens here on earth. In the Heavens, however, infants are introduced through Baptism into the "Christian Heaven," and the Lord assigns angels to them there to take care of them. Therefore, as soon as infants are baptized, angels are placed over them, who keep them in a state of being ready to receive <note>The text cuts off here, continuing on the next page.</note>

<summary>Swedenborg argues that baptism is an external sign of an internal spiritual washing, and its primary function is to serve as a marker of introduction into the Christian Church, both on earth and in the spiritual world.</summary>

faith in the Lord; but as they grow up and become their own masters and use their own reason, those guardian angels leave them, and they take to themselves such spirits as make one with their life and faith. From this, it is clear that Baptism is an insertion among Christians even in the Spiritual World.

678. That not only infants but also all people are inserted among Christians in the spiritual world through Baptism is because peoples and nations in that world are distinguished according to their religions. Christians are in the center, Muslims <note>original: "Mahumedani"</note> are around them, idolaters of various kinds are behind them, and Jews are at the sides. Furthermore, all who belong to the same religion are arranged into societies: in Heaven according to their affections of love for God and toward their neighbor; in Hell into congregations according to the affections opposite to those two loves, and thus according to the lusts of evil. In the spiritual world—by which we mean both Heaven and Hell—all things are most distinctly ordered in general and in every part, or in every genus and species; the preservation of the entire universe depends upon this distinct organization. This distinction is not possible unless everyone, after they are born, is known by some sign indicating which religious community they belong to. For without the Christian sign, which is Baptism, some Muslim spirit or some idolater could attach themselves to newly born Christian infants, or even to children, and breathe into them an inclination for their own religion, and thus distract their minds and alienate them from Christianity, which would be to distort and destroy spiritual order.

679. Anyone who traces effects back to their causes can know that the stability of all things depends on order, and that there are many kinds of order—general and particular—and that there is one Order which is the most Universal of all, upon which the general and particular orders depend in a continuous series. This Universal Order enters into all things just as essence enters into forms, so that they may act as one. It is this unity that preserves the whole, which would otherwise fall apart and not only slide back into primeval chaos, but into nothingness. What would happen to a human being if each and every thing in their body were not most distinctly ordered? If their collective functions did not depend upon one Heart and one pair of Lungs, what would the body be but a confused mass? Would the Stomach then perform its functions, or the Liver and Pancreas, the Mesentery and Mesocolon <note>These terms refer to the membranes that attach the intestines to the abdominal wall, which Swedenborg uses here to emphasize the intricate organization of the body.</note>, the Kidneys and the Intestines? It is because of the order within and between them that all these individual parts appear to the person as one. Without a distinct order in the Mind or Spirit of man, if its collective state did not depend on the Will and the Intellect, how confused and undigested it would be! Without that order, could a man think or will any more than a portrait of him on a canvas or a statue in a house? What would a man be without a most orderly influx from Heaven and the reception of it? And what would this influx be without the most Universal source upon which the government of the whole and all its parts depends—that is, unless it were from God, and unless all things existed, lived, and moved in Him and from Him? These things can be illustrated for the natural man by countless examples: what is an Empire or Kingdom without order but a gang of robbers, where a large group might kill thousands, only to be killed by a few in the end? What is a City without order, or even a House without order? And what is a kingdom, city, or house unless someone in each one acts as the head?

680. Furthermore, what is Order without distinction, and what is distinction without indicators, and what are indicators without signs by which qualities may be known? For without a knowledge of qualities, order is not recognized as order. The signs or "signatures" in Empires and Kingdoms are titles of dignity and the rights of administration attached to them; from these come the subordinations by which all are coordinated into one. In this way, a King exercises his royal power through an order distributed among many, which is what makes a Kingdom a Kingdom. It is the same in many other things, such as in Armies: what value would they have unless they were orderly distinguished into battalions <note>original: "phalanges"</note>, these into cohorts, and these into troops, with lower officers appointed over each and one supreme leader over all? And what...

What would those military arrangements be without signs, which are called standards <note>original: "Vexilla"</note>, which indicate in what position each person will be? Through such signs, everyone in battles acts as one, and without them, they would fall against the enemy no differently than a pack of dogs with open mouths, howling and in empty fury; and then everyone, lacking strength, would be slaughtered by an enemy organized into proper battle lines, for what are those who are divided against those who are united? By these things is illustrated this first use of baptism, which is a sign in the spiritual world that a person is among the Christians, where everyone is inserted into societies and congregations there according to the quality of the Christianity within him or outside of him.

## *That the second Use of Baptism is, that the Christian may know and acknowledge the Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer and Savior, and follow Him.*

**681.** This second use of Baptism, which is that one may know the Lord the Redeemer and Savior Jesus Christ, follows inseparably from the first, which is the introduction into the Christian Church and the insertion among Christians in the spiritual world. And what is that first use without this second following it, but a name alone? It is just like a subject who pledges himself to a King and yet rejects his laws or those of the country and pledges himself to a barbarian King and serves him; or like a servant who binds himself to some Master and receives his clothes as his insignia <note>distinguishing marks or livery</note>, and then runs away and serves another in those clothes; or like a standard-bearer who goes off with the banner and cuts it up, and either throws the pieces into the air or under the feet of the soldiers to be trampled. In a word, the name of being a Christian—that is, being Christ’s—and yet not acknowledging Him and following Him (which is to live according to His commandments) is as empty as a shadow, as smoke, or as a blackened painting; for the Lord says, *Why do you call Me Lord, Lord, and do not do what I say?* (Luke 6:46 and following). *Many will say to Me on that day, Lord, Lord, but then I will confess to them, I never knew you* (Matthew 7:22, 23).

**682.** By the Name of the Lord Jesus Christ, nothing else is meant in the Word <note>the Holy Scriptures</note> than the acknowledgment of Him and a life according to His precepts. That His name signifies these things, you may see the reason in the explanation of the Second Commandment in the Decalogue <note>the Ten Commandments</note>: *You shall not take the Name of God in vain*. Nothing else is meant by the Name of the Lord in these places: "Jesus said, you will be hated by all nations for My Name’s sake" (Matthew 10:22; 24:9, 10). "Where two or three are gathered in My Name, there I am in the midst of them" (Matthew 18:20). "As many as received Him, to them He gave power to be the sons of God, to those believing in His Name" (John 1:12). "Many believed in His Name" (John 2:23). "He who does not believe is judged already, because he has not believed in the Name of the only-begotten Son of God" (John 3:17, 18). "Those who believe will have life in His Name" (John 20:31). "For My Name’s sake you have labored and have not failed" (Revelation 2:3), and elsewhere. Who cannot see that by the Name of the Lord in those places is not meant the Name alone, but the acknowledgment of Him—that He is the Redeemer and Savior—and at the same time obedience, and finally faith in Him? For in Baptism, the infant receives the sign of the cross on the forehead and the breast, which is a sign of inauguration <term>inauguration: here meaning a formal initiation or dedication</term> into the acknowledgment and worship of the Lord. By "Name" is also meant the quality <note>the essential character or nature</note> of someone; the reason is that in the spiritual world everyone is named according to his quality. Therefore, by the name of being a Christian, his quality is meant: that he has faith in Christ and charity <note>spiritual love; original: "charitatem"</note> toward the neighbor from Christ. This is meant by "Name" in Revelation: "The Son of Man says, I have a few names in Sardis who have not defiled their garments, and they shall walk with Me in white, for they are worthy" (Chapter 3:4). By walking with the Son of Man in white is signified following the Lord and living according to the truths of His Word. Something similar is meant by "Name" in John: "Jesus said, the sheep..."

...they hear my voice, and I call my own sheep **by name** <note>original: "Nomine tenus"</note>, and I lead them out, and I walk before them, and the sheep follow Me, because they know my voice; but they do not follow a stranger, because they do not know the voice of strangers. Everyone receives this Name in Baptism, for it is contained within that sign.

**683.** What is a name without the reality it represents, but a vain thing? It is like a sound that bounces off the trees of a forest or the ceilings of a room, which is called an echo. It is like the almost lifeless sounds made by those who talk in their sleep, or like the sound of the wind, the sea, or a machine, which has no practical use. Indeed, what is a name like King, Duke, Consul, Bishop, Abbot, or Monk, without the function that belongs to that Name, but vanity? In the same way, what is the Name of "Christian" if a person lives like a barbarian and acts against the precepts of Christ? It is like looking at the sign of Satan instead of the sign of Christ, even though Christ’s name was woven into them with golden threads at baptism. 

What of those who, after they have received the mark of Christ, later mock His worship, snarl at His Name, and profess Him not as the Son of God, but as the son of Joseph? They are nothing but rebels and king-killers, and their voices are nothing but blasphemies against the Holy Spirit, which cannot be forgiven in this age or the next. These people, like dogs with open maws, bite at the Word and tear it with their teeth; among such people, in opposition to Christ and His worship, *all tables are full of the vomit of filthiness* (Isaiah 28:8; Jeremiah 48:26). Yet the Lord Jesus Christ is the Son of the Most High God (Luke 1:32, 35), the Only Begotten (John 1:18, 3:16), the True God, and Eternal Life (1 John 5:20, 21); in Whom all the fullness of the Divinity dwells bodily (Colossians 2:9). And He is not the son of Joseph (Matthew 1:25), besides a thousand other places in scripture.

## *That the Third use of Baptism, which is the final one, is that a person may be regenerated.*

**684.** This use is the very Purpose for which Baptism exists. It is called the "final" cause because a true Christian knows and acknowledges the Lord Jesus Christ as the Redeemer—and because He is the Redeemer, He is also the Regenerator <note>The "Regenerator" is the one who brings about spiritual rebirth.</note>. That Redemption and Regeneration make one may be seen in the chapter on Reformation and Regeneration (Article III). This is also because a Christian possesses the Word, in which the means of Regeneration are described; those means are Faith in the Lord and Charity <note>spiritual love or goodwill</note> toward the neighbor. 

This is the same as what is said of the Lord: *that He Himself baptizes with the Holy Spirit and with Fire* (Matthew 3:11; Mark 1:9–11; Luke 3:16; John 1:33). By the "Holy Spirit" is meant the Divine Truth of faith, and by "Fire" is meant the Divine Good of love or Charity, both of which proceed from the Lord. That the "Holy Spirit" means the Divine Truth of faith can be seen in the chapter on the HOLY SPIRIT; and that "Fire" means the Divine Good of love can be seen in the *REVEALED APOCALYPSE* (numbers 468, 395). Through these two, all Regeneration is performed by the Lord. The reason the Lord Himself was baptized by John (Matthew 3:13–17; Mark 1:9; Luke 3:21, 22) was not only to institute Baptism for the future and to lead by example, but also because He glorified His Human and made It Divine, just as He regenerates a person and makes them spiritual.

**685.** From what has been said before and now, it can be seen that the three uses of baptism hang together as one, just like a first cause, a middle (or efficient) cause, and an ultimate cause which is the effect—and the very end/goal for which the prior causes exist. For the first use is that one is named a Christian; the second, following from this, is that one knows and acknowledges the Lord as Redeemer, Regenerator, and Savior; and the third is that one is regenerated by Him. While this is happening, the person is redeemed and saved. Since these three uses follow...

...arranged in order, and in the end they join together, and from there they hold together as one in the minds <note>original: "idea"</note> of the Angels. Therefore, when Baptism is performed, and the Word is read and the ceremony named, the Angels who are present do not understand "baptism," but "Regeneration." Wherefore, through these words of the Lord, *Whoever believes and is baptized shall be saved, but whoever does not believe shall be condemned* (Mark 16:16), this is understood in Heaven by the Angels to mean that whoever acknowledges the Lord and is regenerated shall be saved. From this it also follows that Baptism is called by the Christian Churches on earth the WASHING OF REGENERATION <term>Washing of Regeneration: A traditional theological term for baptism, emphasizing it as a spiritual "cleansing" that begins a person's new life</term>. Let a Christian know, therefore, that whoever does not believe in the Lord cannot be regenerated, even if he has been baptized; and that baptizing without faith in the Lord accomplishes absolutely nothing (see above in this Chapter, Article II, no. 4). That Baptism involves purification from evils, and thus regeneration, can be very well known to every Christian; for while an infant is baptized, the priest signs the Cross on the forehead and upon the breast as a memorial of the Lord, and afterward turns to the godparents and asks whether they renounce the devil and all his works, and whether they receive the faith. To these questions, it is answered on behalf of the infant, "Yes, indeed." The renunciation of the Devil—*that is*, of the evils that are from hell—and faith in the Lord are what complete regeneration.

**686.** In the Word it is said that the Lord our God and Redeemer baptizes with the Holy Spirit and with fire; by this is meant that the Lord regenerates man through the Divine Truth of faith and through the Divine Good of love or charity (see above in this Article, no. 1). Those who have been regenerated by the Holy Spirit—that is, by the Divine Truth of faith—are distinguished in the Heavens from those who have been regenerated by Fire—that is, by the Divine Good of love. Those who are regenerated by the Divine Truth of faith walk in Heaven in garments of white fine linen, and are called **spiritual Angels**; but those who are regenerated by the Divine Good of love walk in garments of purple, and are called **celestial Angels** <note>Swedenborg describes heaven as divided into two "kingdoms": the Spiritual, focused on wisdom and truth, and the Celestial, focused on love and the heart.</note>. Those who walk clothed in white garments are meant by these passages: *They follow the Lamb clothed in fine linen, white and clean* (Revelation 19:14); *They shall walk with me in white* (Revelation 3:4); and also Chapter 7:14. The *Angels seen in the Lord’s sepulcher in white and shining garments* (Matthew 28:3; Luke 24:4) were of this kind; for "fine linen" signifies the righteousness of the saints (Revelation 19:8), where this is openly stated. That "Garments" in the Word signify truths, and "white garments" and "fine linen" signify Divine truths, may be seen in *The Apocalypse Revealed*, no. 379, where this is shown. The reason those who are also regenerated by the Divine Good of love are in purple garments is that purple is the color of love, which it derives from the fire of the Sun and its redness; by this, love is signified (see *THE APOCALYPSE REVEALED*, nos. 468, 725). Since garments signify truths, therefore the man who was found among the guests not clothed in a wedding garment was cast out and thrown into outer darkness (Matthew 22:11, 12, 13).

**687.** Furthermore, Baptism as Regeneration is represented by many things both in Heaven and in the World. In HEAVEN, as just stated, it is represented by white and purple garments; and also by the marriage of the Church with the Lord; and by the New Heaven and the New Earth, and the New Jerusalem descending from there, of which He who sat upon the Throne said, *Behold, I make all things new* (Revelation 21:1–5); and by the *river of the water of life coming out of the throne of God and the Lamb* (Revelation 22:1, 2). It is also represented by the five wise virgins who had lamps and oil, and entered with the Bridegroom to the wedding (Matthew 25:1, 2, 10). A baptized person—that is, a regenerated person—is meant by the "creature" (Mark 16:15; Romans 8:19, 20, 21) and by the *new creature* (2 Corinthians 5:17; Galatians 6:15); for "creature" is derived from "to be created," by which being regenerated is also signified (see *THE APOCALYPSE REVEALED*, no. 254). In the WORLD, Regeneration is represented by various things, such as the blossoming of all things on earth in the time of spring, and by their successive growth even to the stage of bearing fruit; similarly by the growth of every tree, shrub, and flower from the first month of heat to the last; it is also represented by the progressive ripening of all fruits from the first tender shoot to full maturity. ## *That the way was prepared through the Baptism of John, so that Jehovah the Lord could descend into the World and accomplish Redemption.*

688. In Malachi it is read: *Behold, I send my messenger <note>original: "Angelum"</note>, who shall prepare the way before Me; and the Lord, whom you seek, shall suddenly come to His temple, even the messenger of the covenant, whom you desire; but who may abide the day of His coming, and who shall stand when He appears?* Chapter 3:1. And again: *Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and terrible day of Jehovah, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse,* Chapter 3:23, 24 <note>in modern Bibles, these are Malachi 4:5-6</note>. And Zechariah the father, prophesying concerning his son John, said: *And you, child, shall be called the prophet of the Most High: for you shall go before the face of the Lord to prepare His ways,* Luke 1:76 <note>the text cites Luke 1:26, which describes the Annunciation; the quote actually comes from the end of the chapter</note>. And the Lord Himself said concerning that John: *This is he of whom it is written, behold, I send my messenger before my face, who shall prepare your way before You,* Luke 7:27. From these things it is evident that this John was a prophet sent to prepare the way of Jehovah God, who would descend into the world and accomplish Redemption, and that he prepared that way through Baptism and then the announcement of the Lord's Coming; and that without that preparation, everyone there would have been struck with a curse and perished.

689. The reason why the way was prepared through the Baptism of John was because through it—as was shown above—they were introduced into the future Church of the Lord and were inserted in Heaven among those who expected and desired the Messiah. Thus they were guarded by Angels so that the Devils from Hell might not break out and destroy them; wherefore it is said in Malachi: *Who shall abide the day of His coming, and lest Jehovah come and smite the earth with a curse,* 3:24. Similarly in Isaiah: *Behold, the day of Jehovah comes, cruel both with indignation and fierce anger and wrath... I will shake the heavens, and the earth shall tremble out of her place, in the day of His fierce anger,* 13:6, 9, 13, 22; Chapter 22:5, 11. Likewise in Jeremiah, that day is called a *day of wasting, vengeance, and destruction,* Chapter 4:9; Chapter 7:32; Chapter 46:10, 21; Chapter 47:4; Chapter 49:8, 26. In Ezekiel: *A day of wrath, of cloud and thick darkness,* Chapter 13:5; Chapter 30:2, 3, 9; Chapter 34:11, 12; Chapter 38:14, 16, 18, 19. Likewise in Amos, Chapter 5:13, 18, 20; Chapter 8:3, 9, 13. In Joel: *The day of Jehovah is great and very terrible; and who can abide it?* Chapter 2:1, 2, 11; Chapter 3:2, 4. And in Zechariah <note>The following quote is actually from Zephaniah 1:7-18, though the manuscript attributes it to Zechariah</note>: *In that day there shall be the noise of a cry... the great day of Jehovah is near... that day is a day of wrath, a day of trouble and distress, a day of wasting and desolation; the whole land shall be devoured by the fire of Jehovah's jealousy, for He shall make even a speedy riddance of all them that dwell in the land,* Chapter 1:7 to 18; besides other places. From these it is clear that unless the way had been prepared for Jehovah descending into the world by means of Baptism—the effect of which in Heaven was that the Hells were closed up and the Jews protected—[everyone would have perished].

...from total destruction: Jehovah also said to Moses, “*In one moment, if I were to ascend in your midst, I would consume the people*,” Exodus 33:5. That this is so is clearly evident from the words of John to the crowds going out to be baptized by him: “*You brood of vipers, who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?*” Matthew 3:7; Luke 3:7. That John also taught about Christ and His coming when he baptized may be seen in Luke 3:16; John 1:25, 26, 31, 32, 33; Chapter 3:26. From these passages it is clear how John prepared the way.

690. As far as John’s Baptism is concerned, it represented the cleansing of the **External man**, but the Baptism which exists among Christians today represents the cleansing of the **Internal man**, which is **Regeneration** <note>In Swedenborg’s theology, the "external man" refers to our outward actions and sensory life, while the "internal man" refers to our inner spirit and motivations.</note>; therefore it is read that John baptized with water, but that the Lord baptizes with the holy spirit and fire, and for that reason John's baptism is called the Baptism of repentance, Matthew 3:11; Mark 1:4 and following; Luke 3:3, 16; John 1:25, 26, 33; Acts 1:22; Chapter 10:37; Chapter 18:25. The Jews who were baptized were merely external men, and the external man without faith in Christ cannot become internal; that those who were baptized with the baptism of John became internal men when they received faith in Christ, and were then baptized in the Name of Jesus, may be seen in the Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 19:3 to 6.

691. Moses said to Jehovah, *Show me your glory, to whom Jehovah said, you cannot see my face, because man shall not see Me and live; and He said, behold the place where you shall stand upon the rock, and I will put you in a cleft of the rock, and I will cover you with my hand until I have passed by, and when I have removed my hand, you shall see my back <note>original: "posteriora mea"</note>, but my face shall not be seen*, Exodus 33:18 to 23. The reason that man cannot see God and live is because God is **Love Itself**, and Divine Love itself in the spiritual world appears before the Angels as a **Sun**, distant from them just as the Sun of our world is distant from men; therefore if God, who is in the midst of that Sun, were to draw near to the Angels, they would perish just as men would if the Sun of the world drew near to them, for it is equally burning. On this account, there are perpetual temperings which modify and moderate the heat of that love, so that it does not flow into Heaven exactly as it is in itself, for the Angels would be consumed by it. For this reason, when the Lord presents Himself more closely in heaven, the wicked who are below heaven begin to wail, to be tortured, and to lose consciousness; they flee into caves and into the clefts of the mountains, crying out, "fall upon us, and hide us from the face of Him who sits upon the Throne," Revelation 6:16; Isaiah 2:19, 21. The Lord Himself does not descend, but an Angel with a sphere of love from the Lord around him: I have sometimes seen the wicked terrified by that descent, as if they saw death itself before their eyes—some who threw themselves deeper and deeper into hell, and some driven into furies. This was why the children of Israel prepared themselves for three days before the descent of Jehovah upon Mount Sinai, and why the Mountain was fenced around, lest anyone approach and die, Exodus 19. It was similar with the Holiness of Jehovah the Lord in the **Decalogue** <note>The Ten Commandments</note> then promulgated, and the two Tables written by the finger of God and then placed in the **Ark**; over which the Mercy Seat was placed in the Tabernacle, and over this the Cherubim, lest anyone touch that Holiness directly with hand or eye. Even Aaron could not approach it except once a year, after he had purified himself through sacrifices and incense. This was why the Ekronites and Bethshemites died by the many thousands, simply because they saw the Ark with their eyes, 1 Samuel 5:11, 12; Chapter 6:19; and also Uzzah, because he touched it, 2 Samuel 6:6, 7. From these few points it is illustrated what sort of curse and slaughter the Jews would have been struck with, had they not been prepared by John’s Baptism to receive the Messiah, who was Jehovah God in Human form; and unless He had assumed the Human, and thus revealed Himself; and that they were prepared by this: that in Heaven they were enrolled and numbered among those who in their hearts expected and desired the Messiah, from which time Angels were sent and made their guardians.

<summary>This page explains that John the Baptist’s ritual of water baptism was a necessary "external" preparation to protect the Jewish people from the overwhelming spiritual power of God’s direct presence. Swedenborg uses the analogy of a spiritual sun to show that Divine Love is a consuming fire that requires tempering and mediation through a human form (the Messiah) to be safely received by humanity.</summary>

692. To these things I will add these **MEMORABLE RELATIONS**; the **FIRST**. While I was returning home from the School of Wisdom, I saw an Angel on the way dressed in a hyacinthine <note>A deep purplish-blue color, often associated in this context with heavenly intelligence</note> garment; he joined himself to my side and said, "I see that you have come from the School of Wisdom, and that you are gladdened by what you heard there. Because I perceive that you are not fully in this World, since you are simultaneously in the natural World, you therefore do not know of our Olympic Gymnasia <note>Spiritual meeting places named after the classical Greek sites, where ancient thinkers gather</note>, where the ancient Wise Men meet and learn from those newly arriving from your World what changes and successions of state Wisdom has undergone and is still undergoing. If you wish, I will lead you to the place where many of the ancient <term>Sophi (Wise Men)</term> and their sons—that is, their disciples—dwell." 

And he led me to the boundary between the North and the East. When I looked out from a high place, behold, a City was seen, and on one side of it were two Hills, the one closer to the city being lower than the other. He said to me, "That City is called the Athenæum, the lower Hill is called Parnassium, and the higher one Heliconeum. They are called this because the ancient wise men of Greece, such as Pythagoras, Socrates, Aristippus, and Xenophon, reside in and around the City with their disciples and young students." 

I asked about Plato and Aristotle; he said that they and their followers dwell in another region, because they taught rational things which belong to the intellect, while the others taught moral things which belong to life. He said that students are frequently sent from the City of Athenæum to the learned among the Christians to tell what they think today about God, about the Creation of the Universe, about the Immortality of the soul, about the State of man relative to the state of beasts, and about other matters of interior wisdom. 

He also said that a herald had today announced a meeting, a sign that the emissaries had encountered new Arrivals from Earth from whom they heard curious things. We saw many people coming out of the city and its vicinity, some having laurels upon their heads, some holding palms in their hands, some with books under their arms, and some with quills <note>original: "calamis," reed pens or quills</note> tucked into the hair at their left temples. We joined them and ascended together, and behold, upon the Hill was an octagonal Palace which they called the Palladium, and we entered. There were eight hexagonal niches, in each of which was a Library and also a Table, at which those crowned with laurel sat. In the Palladium itself, seats carved from stone were seen, upon which the rest sat down. 

Then a door was opened to the left, through which two Arrivals from earth were introduced. After they were greeted, one of the laurel-crowned men asked them, **WHAT NEWS FROM EARTH?** They said, "The news is that in the forests they have found men like beasts, or beasts like men, but who were recognized by their faces and bodies to have been born humans, but lost or abandoned in the forests in their second or third year of age." They said that these could not make any sound of thought, nor learn to articulate sound into any word; that they did not know the food suitable for them as beasts do, but would thrust forest items, both clean and unclean, into their mouths; besides many similar things. From these cases, some of the Learned among us have conjectured, and some have concluded, many things regarding the State of men relative to the state of beasts. 

Hearing this, some of the ancient Wise Men asked what they conjecture and conclude from those cases. The two Arrivals replied that there were many conclusions, but they could be reduced to these: 

1. That man by his nature, and also from birth, is more stupid and therefore viler than any beast; and that he remains so if he is not instructed. 

2. That he can be instructed because he has learned to make articulate sounds and thereby to speak, and that through this he began to express thoughts, and this successively more and more, until he could express the laws of Society, many of which are nevertheless impressed upon beasts from birth. 

3. That Rationality belongs to beasts just as much as to men. 

4. Therefore, if beasts could speak, they would reason as skillfully about every matter as men do; a sign of this is that they think from reason and prudence just as much as men. 

5. That the Intellect is only a modification of light from the Sun, with heat cooperating by means of the ether, so that it is merely an activity of interior nature; and that this can be exalted...

# OF THE NEW HEAVEN AND THE NEW CHURCH.

...to the point that it appears like wisdom. 6. That it is therefore vain to believe that man lives more than a beast after death, except perhaps that he might appear for a few days after death—from the exhalation of the body's life—like a mist in the form of a ghost <note>original Latin: *larva*</note>, before it is dissipated into nature; hardly different from how a shrub raised from its ashes appears in the likeness of its own form. <note>This refers to "palingenesis," a popular 17th-century chemical demonstration where the "shadow" or "ghost" of a plant was supposedly made to appear in a glass vial from its own salts or ashes.</note> 7. Consequently, that Religion, which teaches life after death, is an invention, so that the simple might be held inwardly in bond by its laws, just as they are held outwardly by the laws of the City <note>meaning the State or civil society</note>. They added to these things, that only the merely "ingenious" <note>those clever at reasoning from the senses</note> reason this way, but not the "Intelligent"; and when they asked what the Intelligent thought, they said they had not heard, but that this is what they suppose.

Hearing these things, all who sat at the Tables said, "Oh, what times these are now on the Earth! Alas, what changes Wisdom has undergone! It has turned into fatuous ingenuity. The Sun has set, and under the earth is diametrically opposite its noon. Who cannot know from evidence—from those left behind and found in the woods <note>referring to "wild children" or feral children, like Peter the Wild Boy, who were subjects of great scientific interest in Swedenborg's time</note>—that man is such if not instructed? Is he not as he is taught? Is he not born in ignorance beyond the beasts? Must he not learn to walk and speak? If he did not learn to walk, would he even stand up on his feet? And if he did not learn to speak, would he even mutter anything of thought? Is not every man just as he is instructed—maddened by falsities, or wise from truths? And one maddened by falsities in every fantasy believes himself wiser than the one who is wise from truths! Are there not fatuous and insane men, who are no more 'men' than those found in the woods? Are those devoid of memory not like them? We have concluded from these and those that man without instruction is neither man nor beast, but is a **form** which can receive into itself that which makes a man; and thus that he is not born a man, but *becomes* a man. And man is born as such a form so that he may be an **organ receiving life from God**, for the sake of the end that he may be a subject into which God might bring every good, and through union with Himself, bless him forever. We perceive from your speech that wisdom today is so far extinguished or infatuated that they know absolutely nothing about the state of man's life relative to the state of a beast's life; hence it is that they do not know the state of man's life after death. But those who *can* know this, but do *not want* to know, and therefore deny it—as many of your Christians do—we can liken to those found in the woods; not that they were made so stupid by a lack of instruction, but that through the fallacies of the senses, which are the darkness of truths, they have made themselves so stupid."

But then someone standing in the middle of the Palladium <note>The name for this spiritual gymnasium or place of learning</note>, holding a palm in his hand, said, "Unfold, I pray, this secret: how man, created as a **form of God**, could be changed into a **form of the devil**? I know that the Angels of Heaven are <term>forms of God</term> <note>original: *formæ Dei*</note>, and that the angels of hell are forms of the devil, and the two forms are opposite to each other—the latter of Insanity, the former of Wisdom. Tell us, therefore, how man, created as a form of God, could pass from such a day into such a night, so that he could deny God and eternal life?" To this, the <term>Teachers</term> <note>original: *Didascali*</note> responded in order: first the Pythagoreans, then the Socratics, and afterwards the rest. But among them was a certain Platonist; he spoke last, and his opinion prevailed, which was: that the men of the <term>Saturnian Age</term> <note>original: *Ævum Saturninum*, the mythical Golden Age of peace and plenty</note> or the <term>Golden Age</term> <note>original: *Sæculum aureum*</note>, knew and acknowledged that they were <term>forms receiving life from God</term> <note>original: *Formæ recipientes vitæ a Deo*</note>, and that therefore wisdom was inscribed on their souls and hearts; and hence, that from the light of truth they saw truth, and through truths perceived good from the delight of its love. But as the <term>human race</term> <note>original: *Humanum Genus*</note> in the following Ages receded from the acknowledgment that all the truth of wisdom and hence the good of love in them continually flowed in from God, they ceased to be habitations of God, and then also speech with God and association with Angels ceased. For the interiors of their minds were turned from their original direction—which had been raised upward to God by God—and were bent into an oblique direction more and more, outward into the World, and thus to God from God through the World, and finally inverted into the opposite direction, which is downward toward Self. And because God cannot be looked upon by a man who is internally inverted and thus turned away, men separated themselves from God, and were made forms of Hell, and thus of the devil. From these things it follows, that in the First...

A Platonist explains the "fall" as a gradual shift in human focus from God toward the world and self, turning the "form of God" into a "form of the devil."</summary>

In those Ages, they acknowledged with heart and soul that every good of love, and every truth of wisdom resulting from it, were theirs from God, and also that these things were God’s within them; thus, they were mere receptacles of life from God, and were therefore called Images of God, Sons of God, and Born of God. However, in succeeding Ages, they acknowledged this not with heart and soul, but with a kind of persuasive faith <note>original: "fide persuasiva"—a faith rooted in external pressure or intellectual convincing rather than internal sight</note>, then with a historical faith, and finally with the mouth alone. To acknowledge such a thing only with the mouth is not to acknowledge it at all—in fact, it is to deny it in the heart. From this, one can see what kind of wisdom exists today on earth among Christians, even though they can be inspired by God through the written Revelation; they do not even know the difference between a human and a beast. Consequently, many believe that if a human lives after death, a beast must also live; or because a beast does not live after death, neither will a human. Has not our spiritual light, which illuminates the sight of the mind, become thick darkness to them? And has not their natural light, which only illuminates the sight of the body, become their only splendor?

After these things, they all turned to the two Strangers and thanked them for their arrival and their account, praying that they would report what they had heard to their brothers. The strangers replied that they would confirm their own people in this truth: that to the extent they attribute every good of charity and truth of faith to the Lord, and not to themselves, to that extent they are human beings, and to that extent they become Angels of Heaven.

## 493. SECOND MEMORABLE RELATION.

After some weeks, I heard a voice from Heaven saying, "There is again a gathering on Parnassus; come, we will show the way." I approached, and when I was near, I saw someone upon Mount Helicon with a trumpet, with which he announced and proclaimed the Gathering. I saw people ascending from the City of the Athenaeum <note>A spiritual representation of a city of learning and wisdom</note> and its surrounding areas as before, and in their midst were three Newcomers from the World. These three were from among the Christians: one was a Priest, the second a Politician, and the third a Philosopher. Along the way, the others entertained them with various conversations, primarily about the Ancient Sages, whom they mentioned by name. The newcomers asked if they would see them; the guides said they would, and if they wished, they could greet them, for they are approachable. They asked about Demosthenes, Diogenes, and Epicurus. The guides said, "Demosthenes is not here, but is with Plato; Diogenes stays with his scholars at the foot of Helicon because he regards worldly things as nothing and only turns over heavenly things in his mind. Epicurus lives on the border to the west and does not enter among us, because we distinguish between good affections and evil affections, and we say that good affections are one with wisdom, while evil affections are against wisdom." 

When they climbed the hill of Parnassus, certain guards there brought water from the spring in crystal cups, saying, "This is water from the fountain of which the ancients told stories, saying it was broken open by the hoof of the horse Pegasus, and later consecrated to the nine Virgins." But by the winged horse Pegasus, they meant the <term>understanding of truth</term> <note>original: "Intellectum veri"</note> through which wisdom comes; by his hooves, they meant the experiences through which natural intelligence is formed; and by the nine Virgins, they meant knowledge and sciences of every kind. These are called Fables today, but they were <term>Correspondences</term> <note>Swedenborg's term for the symbolic relationship between spiritual realities and natural forms</note> from which the People of the Earliest Age spoke. The companions said to the three Strangers, "Do not be surprised; the guards have been instructed to speak this way. By 'drinking water from the fountain,' we understand being instructed about truths, and through truths about goods, and thus becoming wise."

After this, they entered the Palladium <note>A temple or hall of wisdom</note>, and with them the three Newcomers from the World: the Priest, the Politician, and the Philosopher. Then the "Laureates" <note>Those crowned with laurel as a sign of wisdom</note> who sat at the tables asked, **"WHAT IS NEW FROM THE EARTH?"** They replied, "This is new: that someone claims he speaks with Angels, and has his sight opened into the <term>spiritual world</term> just as he has it opened into the natural world; and he brings many new things from there, among which are these: that a human lives as a human after death, just as he lived before in the World; that he sees, hears, and speaks just as before in the World; that he is clothed and adorned just as before in the World; that he hungers and thirsts, eats and drinks, just as before in the World; that he enjoys marriage delight just as before in the World; that he sleeps and wakes just as before in the World; that there are lands and lakes, mountains and hills, plains and valleys...

[mountains], springs & rivers, gardens & groves; also that there are palaces & houses, as well as cities & villages, just as in the natural world; as also that there are writings & books, and that there are occupations & businesses, as well as precious stones, gold & silver; in a word, that there are all things there, even to the smallest detail, which are on earth, and those in the Heavens are infinitely more perfect, with only this difference: that all things in the spiritual world <term>Mundo spirituali</term> are from a spiritual origin, and thus are spiritual, because they are from the Sun there which is pure Love; and that all things in the natural world <term>Mundo naturali</term> are from a natural origin, and thus are natural & material, because they are from the Sun there which is pure fire; in a word, that a human after death is a perfect human, indeed a more perfect human than before in the World; for previously in the World he was in a material body, but in this he is in a spiritual body. 

Having said these things, the ancient Sages <term>Sapientes antiqui</term> asked what they think of these things on earth; those three visitors replied, "We know that they are true because we are here, and we have surveyed & explored everything; therefore we will say what has been spoken & reasoned about them on earth." 

And then the PRIEST <term>Sacerdos</term> said, that those of our order <note>referring to the clergy</note>, when they first heard these things, called them visions, then fabrications, later that they saw ghosts, and finally they hesitated and said, "Believe it if you wish." We have hitherto taught that a human will not be in a body after death until the day of the Last Judgment <term>Ultimum Judicium</term>. And the Sages asked, "Are there not some intelligent ones among them who can demonstrate & convince them of the truth that a human lives as a human after death?" 

The Priest said that there are some who demonstrate it, but they do not convince; those who demonstrate it say that it is against sound reason to believe that a human does not live as a human except on the day of the Last Judgment, and that in the meantime the Soul <term>Anima</term> is without a body. What is the Soul, and where is it in the meantime—is it a breath, or some wind flying in the air, or a being hidden in the middle of the earth? Where is its Seat <term>Sedes ejus</term>? Do the souls of Adam & Eve <term>Adami & Evæ</term>, and all those after them, now for six thousand years or sixty centuries still fly in the universe, or are they kept shut up in the center of the earth, awaiting the Last Judgment? What is more anxious & wretched than such an expectation? Is not their fate comparable to the fate of those bound with chains & fetters in prisons? If such a fate were for a human after death, would it not be better to be born a donkey than a human? Is it not also against reason to believe that the soul can be re-clothed with its body? Is not the body eaten by worms, mice, & fish? And should a bony skeleton scorched by the sun or crumbled into dust be brought to this new body? How will those cadaverous & rotten things be gathered together and united to souls? 

But to such things, when they hear them, they do not answer anything from reason, but stick to their faith, saying, "We bring reason into captivity under the obedience of faith" <note>original: "captamus rationem sub obedientia fidei" — a traditional theological stance where intellectual doubt is suppressed by religious dogma</note>. Regarding the gathering of all from the graves on the day of the Last Judgment, they say, "This is the work of Omnipotence." And when they name Omnipotence & Faith, reason is banished; and I can say that then sound reason becomes like nothing, and to some like a specter; indeed they can say to sound reason, "You are insane" <note>original: "insanis"</note>. 

Hearing these things, the Sages of Greece said, "Are not those paradoxes, as self-contradictory things, dissolved by themselves? And yet today in the World they cannot be dissolved by sound reason? What can be believed that is more paradoxical than what is told about the Last Judgment: that the Universe is then to perish, and that the Stars of heaven are then to fall upon the earth, which is smaller than the stars? And that the bodies of humans then—whether corpses, or mummies eaten by humans, or mere scraps—are to be joined with their souls? When we were in the World, we believed in the immortality of the souls of humans, from deductions which reason supplied to us, and we also designated places for the blessed, which we called the Elysian Fields <term>Campi Elysii</term> <note>the peaceful afterlife for the virtuous in Greek mythology</note>, and we believed them to be human images or appearances, but thin because they were spiritual." 

After these things were said, they turned to the other Stranger, who in the World had been a POLITICIAN <term>Politicus</term>; he confessed that he had not believed in life after death, and that he thought the news he had heard about it were fictions & inventions. "Meditating on it, I said: how can souls be bodies? Does not everything of a human lie dead in the grave? Is the eye there? How [can he see]..." <note>The sentence continues on the next page.</note>
