how is it possible to see? Is there an eye there? How can one hear? Where would a mouth come from to speak? If any part of a man lived after death, would it be anything other than a mere phantom <term>larvae</term> <note>original: "larvae"; in Roman mythology, these were the restless spirits of the dead, often depicted as frightening ghosts</note>? How can a phantom eat and drink, or enjoy conjugal delight? Where would his clothes, houses, food, and so forth come from? Phantoms, which are airy images, appear as if they exist, and yet they do not. I thought these and similar things about the life of men after death while in the World; but now, since I have seen everything and touched everything with my own hands, I am convinced by my very senses that I am a human just as I was in the World—so much so that I know no different, except that I live just as I lived, with the distinction that my reason is now sounder. At times, I have been ashamed of my former thoughts. The PHILOSOPHER told a similar story about himself; however, with this difference: that he had categorized those new things he had heard about life after death among the "opinions and hypotheses" which he had collected from both the Ancients and the Moderns. Upon hearing these things, the Sages <term>Sophi</term> <note>A term for wise men or practitioners of philosophy</note> were struck with amazement; and those who were of the Socratic School <term>Schola Socratica</term> said that from these newcomers from the earth, they perceive that the interiors of human minds have been successively closed off, and that now in the World, a faith in what is false shines like the truth, and a foolish cleverness shines like wisdom. They remarked that the light of wisdom in our times has lowered itself from the interior parts of the Brain down to the mouth under the nose, where it appears before the eyes like the "shimmer of the lips," and the speech of the mouth thereafter sounds like wisdom. Having heard this, one of the students <term>tyronibus</term> there said, "O, how stupid the minds of the earth-dwellers <term>terricolarum</term> are today! If only the disciples of Heraclitus and Democritus were present—who laugh at everything and weep at everything—we would hear great laughter and great weeping." <note>Heraclitus was known as the "weeping philosopher" for his melancholy view of the world, while Democritus was the "laughing philosopher" who mocked human folly.</note> After this assembly was concluded, they gave to the three novices from the earth the insignia of their jurisdiction, which were copper plates <term>lamellae cupreae</term> upon which certain Hieroglyphics were engraved, with which they departed.

694. **THE THIRD MEMORABLE ACCOUNT.** After some time, I looked toward the city of the Athenaeum <note>A spiritual representation of the ancient center of learning, Athens</note>, about which something was said in the previous Memorable Account, and I heard an unusual cry coming from there. There was something of laughter in it, something of indignation, and something of sadness; yet that cry was not discordant, but rather harmonious, because one emotion was not merely alongside the other, but one was within the other. In the spiritual world, the variety and mixture of affections are perceived distinctly in the sound. I asked from a distance what the matter was; and they said: "A messenger has come from the place where newcomers from the Christian World first appear, saying that he heard from three people there that in the World they came from, they believed (along with the rest of the people there) that for the blessed and happy after death, there would be every possible rest from labors. And because administrations, offices, and works are labors, they believed there would be rest from those as well." And because those three have now been brought here by our emissary and are standing before the gate and waiting, a Clamoring arose. By common consent, it was decided that they should be introduced not into the Palladium on Mount Parnassus <note>Parnassus was the mythological home of the Muses; the Palladium refers to a sacred site of wisdom</note> like the previous visitors, but into the great Auditorium there, so that they might reveal their "News" from the Christian World. Some men were sent to introduce them solemnly. Because I was in the spirit, and for spirits, distances are determined by the states of their affections—and because I then had an affection for seeing and hearing them—I seemed to myself to be present there. I saw them introduced and heard them speaking. The Elders or Wiser men <term>Seniores seu Sapientiores</term> sat at the sides of the Auditorium, and the rest in the middle; in front of these was a raised floor. Here the three Newcomers, with the messenger and a solemn company of younger men, were led through the middle of the Auditorium. After silence was established, they were greeted by a certain Elder <term>Majorennis</term> and asked, "WHAT IS NEW FROM THE EARTH?" They replied, "There are many new things, but please tell us regarding what matter?" The Elder replied, "WHAT IS NEW FROM THE EARTH CONCERNING OUR WORLD AND CONCERNING HEAVEN?" They answered, "When we first came into this world, we heard that here and in Heaven there are Administrations, Ministries, Functions, Businesses, the Study of all disciplines, and wonderful Works; and yet we believed that after our migration or translation from the natural World into this Spiritual one, we were going to enter into eternal rest from labors; and what are functions if not labors?" To this the Elder said, "Did you understand eternal rest from labors to mean eternal idleness <term>otium</term>, in which you would continually sit and lie down, drawing delights into your chest,"

Those three Newcomers, seeing so many books, were amazed and said: "Are there even Books in this World? From where come the parchment and paper, the pens and ink?" To this the Seniors said: "We perceive that you believed in the former World that this World was empty because it is spiritual; and that you believed this because you cherished an idea of the spiritual as something abstract from the material. And what is abstract from the material appeared to you like nothingness, or like a vacuum; when nevertheless here is the fullness of all things. All things here are **SUBSTANTIAL** and not material, and material things derive their origin from substantial things. We who are here are spiritual men because we are substantial and not material. Hence it is that all things exist here that are in the natural World, but in their perfection—even books and writings, and much more." 

The three Newcomers, when they heard the term **SUBSTANTIAL** mentioned, thought that it must be so, both because they saw the written Books and because they heard it said that matters originate from substances. To be further confirmed in these things, they were brought to the Dwellings of the scribes, who were transcribing copies written by the wise men of the city; and they inspected the writings and marveled that they were so neat and polished. 695. **FOURTH MEMORABLE RELATION.** Most people today who believe in life after death also believe that in Heaven their thoughts will be nothing other than Devotions, their Speech nothing but Prayers, and that these, together with the expressions of their faces and actions of their bodies, will be nothing but Glorifications of God; thus they imagine their Houses will be so many Houses of worship or sacred Buildings, and that all will be Priests of God. But I can assert that there, the Holy things of the Church do not occupy the Minds and Houses more than in the World where God is celebrated with worship—though they are more pure and interior—but that there, various things belonging to civil Prudence and various things belonging to rational Learning exist in their own excellence. 

One day I was raised up into Heaven and led into a Society where the <term>Sages</term> <note>original: "Sophi"; a term for the wise men or philosophers of antiquity.</note> were, who in ancient ages excelled in learning through study and meditation on such things as were of reason and simultaneously of use. They are now in Heaven because they believed in God, and now in the Lord, and loved their neighbor as themselves. I was then introduced into their Assembly and asked where I was from. I explained that I was in the natural World in Body, but in your Spiritual World in Spirit. Upon hearing this, those Angels were gladdened and inquired: "What do they know and understand in the World where you are bodily regarding **INFLUX**?" 

After I collected what I had gathered on that subject from the speeches and writings of celebrated men, I replied that they do not yet know of any Influx from the spiritual World into the natural World, but only of the Influx of Nature into things natural, such as the Influx of Heat and Light from the Sun into animated Bodies, and into Trees and shrubs—from which comes their vivification—and conversely the influx of cold into the same, from which comes their death. Furthermore, they know of the Influx of light into the Eyes from which comes sight, of the Influx of sound into the ears from which comes hearing, and of the Influx of odor into the nostrils from which comes smell, and so on. 

Besides these things, the Learned of this age reason in different ways about the Influx of the Soul into the Body and of the latter into the Soul; and regarding this they split into three parties: namely, whether the Influx is from the Soul into the Body, which they call **Occasional** <note>original: "Occasionalem"; referring to Occasionalism, the theory that God or the soul acts on the occasion of a bodily stimulus.</note>, based on the occasion of things falling upon the senses of the body; or whether it is the Influx of the body into the Soul, which they call **Physical** <note>original: "Physicum"; the theory that physical objects directly affect the soul.</note>, because objects fall upon the Senses and from these into the Soul; or whether it is a simultaneous and instantaneous Influx into the Body and the Soul at once, which they call **Pre-established Harmony** <note>original: "Harmoniam præstabilitam"; a theory famously proposed by Leibniz suggesting that soul and body are synchronized like two clocks, without direct interaction.</note>. Nevertheless, each person thinks of his own theory of Influx as occurring within Nature. Some believe the Soul to be a particle or drop of Ether; some believe it to be a small ball or spark of Heat and Light; some believe it to be some entity hiding in the Brain. But this or that which they call the Soul, they may indeed call "spiritual," but by "spiritual" they mean a purer "natural," for they know nothing of the spiritual World and its Influx into the natural World. Therefore they remain within the sphere of Nature; in it they ascend and descend, and they raise themselves into it like eagles into the air. And those who dwell only in Nature are like the natives of some Island in the sea who do not know that any Land exists outside of them, or like fish in a river who do not know there is air above their waters. When people are told of a world distinct from their own, where Angels and Spirits dwell, and that all <term>Influx</term> <note>original: "Influxus"; the theological and philosophical concept of life or influence flowing from a higher, spiritual level down into a lower, natural level.</note> into humans—and even the internal life of trees—originates from there, they stand amazed as if they were hearing ghost stories or astrological nonsense. Aside from the philosophers among us in the world where I am in the body, they think and speak of no other Influx than the influx of wine into cups, the influx of food and drink into the belly, and of taste onto the tongue; or perhaps they consider the influx of air into the lungs, and so on. But if these people hear anything regarding the Influx of the spiritual world into the natural world, they say, "Let it flow if it flows! What help or use is there in knowing this?" and they walk away. Later, when they speak about what they heard regarding that Influx, they toy with the idea as some play with pebbles between their fingers.

Afterward, I spoke with those Angels about the wonders that exist from the Influx of the spiritual world into the natural world; such as when caterpillars become butterflies, and also concerning bees and drones, the wonders of silkworms, and also of spiders. I noted that the inhabitants of the earth attribute these things to the light and heat of the Sun, and thus to Nature. What I have often marveled at is that they use these very things to confirm their belief in Nature, and such confirmations of Nature induce sleep and death upon their minds, and they become atheists. After this, I recounted the wonders of the plant kingdom: how everything proceeds from a seed all the way to new seeds in a precise order, just as if the earth knew how to lend and adapt its elements to the fertility of the seed, and from this to bring forth a sprout, to expand this into a stem, to send out branches from it, to clothe these with leaves, and later to distinguish them with flowers; and from the interiors of these to initiate and produce fruits, and through these—so that it may be born again—seeds like offspring. But because these things have become common, familiar, and ordinary through constant sight and perpetual recurrence, people do not look upon them as wonders, but as mere effects of nature. They believe this solely because they are ignorant that there is any spiritual world, and that this world operates from within and activates each and every thing that exists and is formed in the world of nature and upon its Earth. It operates just as the human Mind works upon the senses and movements of the Body; the individual things of nature are like tunics, sheaths, and garments that clothe spiritual things, and directly produce effects corresponding to the goal of God the Creator.

## 696. THE FIFTH MEMORABLE RELATION.

Once I prayed to the Lord that I might be allowed to speak with the disciples of **Aristotle**, and at the same time with the disciples of **Descartes**, and with the disciples of **Leibniz**, for the purpose of drawing out the opinions of their minds regarding the <term>Interaction of the Soul and Body</term> <note>original: "Commercio Animæ & Corporis"; a major 18th-century philosophical debate concerning how a spiritual soul can communicate with or move a physical body.</note>. After my prayer, nine men were present: three Aristotelians, three Cartesians, and three Leibnizians. They stood around me—the adorers of Aristotle on the left side, the followers of Descartes on the right, and the supporters of Leibniz behind me. From a distance, and at intervals between one another, they appeared like three men crowned with laurel. From the perception flowing in from Heaven, I knew they were the very leaders or chief teachers themselves. Behind Leibniz stood one man holding the hem of his garment; it was said that this was **Wolff** <note>Christian Wolff (1679–1754), a philosopher who popularized and expanded upon Leibniz’s ideas.</note>. When those nine men looked at one another, they first greeted and spoke to each other in a friendly voice. But soon after, a Spirit rose up from the lower regions with a torch in his right hand, and he waved it before their faces; because of this, they became enemies, three against three, and looked at one another with grim faces. For the lust for arguing and litigating seized them.

Then the Aristotelians began—who were also <term>Scholastics</term> <note>Refers to the school of philosophy dominant in medieval universities, heavily based on Aristotle's logic.</note>—saying, "Who does not see that objects flow through the senses into the soul, just as one enters a room through the doors, and that the soul thinks according to that Influx? When a lover sees a beautiful Virgin or a Bride, does not his eye sparkle and carry his love for her to the soul? When a miser sees bags in which there are coins, does he not burn for them with every sense, and from there bring this into the soul and excite the desire to possess them? When a proud man hears praises of himself from another, does he not prick up his ears, and do these not carry those praises to the soul? Are not the senses of the body like courtyards through which alone the entrance to the Soul is made? Who can conclude otherwise from these and countless similar examples than that Influx is from nature, or is 'Physical Influx'?"

When this was finished, the Spirit appeared again with the torch in his hand—but now in his left hand—and he waved it at the backs of their heads. For you, because you are in a state of confused ideas, do not see its truth; but the truth itself offered itself to the hand so that you might favor it."

### 697. THE SIXTH MEMORABLE AFFAIR.

Once, not far from me, I saw a <term>Meteor</term> <note>original: "Meteoron"; in this context, it refers to an atmospheric spiritual phenomenon or a symbolic vision in the sky, rather than a space rock.</note>. I saw a cloud divided into little clouds, some of which were blue and some dark. I saw them as if they were colliding with one another. Streaks of light flashed through them, which appeared now sharp like spear-points, now blunt like broken swords. Those streaks would now run out to meet each other, then pull back into themselves, exactly like boxers. So those diverse-colored little clouds appeared as if they were fighting amongst themselves, but they were actually playing. 

Because this vision was seen not far from me, I raised my eyes and focused my sight, and I saw boys, young men, and old men entering a House that was built of marble and founded upon porphyry. This phenomenon was happening above this House. I spoke to one of those entering and asked, "What is here?" He replied, "It is a <term>Gymnasium</term> <note>Gymnasium: a school or place of higher learning.</note> where young men are initiated into the various things of wisdom." Hearing this, I entered with them. I was in the spirit—that is, in a state similar to the inhabitants of the Spiritual World, who are called Spirits and Angels. 

And behold, in that <term>Gymnasium</term>, a <term>Chair</term> <note>original: "Cathedra"; a formal professor's chair.</note> was seen at the front, benches in the middle, seats all around the sides, and an <term>Orchestra</term> <note>Orchestra: here meaning a raised gallery or seating area for dignitaries.</note> above the entrance. The <term>Chair</term> was for the young men who were to respond to the problem proposed at that time; the benches were for the audience; the seats at the sides were for those who had previously responded wisely; and the <term>Orchestra</term> was for the Elders, who acted as umpires and judges. In the middle of the <term>Orchestra</term> was a <term>Pulpit</term> where a wise man sat, whom they called the <term>Headmaster</term> <note>original: "Archididascalus".</note>, who proposed the problems to which the young men from the <term>Chair</term> would respond. After they had gathered, the man rose from the pulpit and said, "Please respond now to..."

Some in the assembly, sitting upon the benches, exclaimed, "What man, from the Golden Age <note>original: "Saturnino ævo"; referring to a mythical era of peace and wisdom</note> even to our own, has been able by any rational thought to see and grasp what the soul is, and even less its nature? Then the young men chosen for that day rose to ascend the pulpit and respond to the problem. There were five of them, who had been examined by the elders and found to be powerful in sagacity. They were then sitting on cushions at the sides of the pulpit. Each, in the order in which they sat, ascended in turn. I saw the **First** one so dressed as he ascended, and he said: "What the soul is and what its nature is has been revealed to no one since the day of Creation; it is a secret in the treasuries of God alone. But it has been discovered that the soul resides in man like a Queen. Yet where her palace is, learned seers have only guessed. Some say it is in a small tubercle between the cerebrum and the cerebellum, which is called the **pineal gland** <note>original: "Glandula pinealis"; a small endocrine gland in the brain that René Descartes famously suggested was the seat of the soul</note>. In this they fixed the seat of the soul because the whole man is governed by those two brains, and that tubercle regulates them; therefore, that which regulates the brains at its will also regulates the whole man from head to foot." He said, "Because of this, it appeared as the truth, or at least a probability, to many in the world, but after a century it was rejected as a fiction." 

After he had said these things, he took off the gown, tunic, and cap, which the **Second** of the chosen ones put on and entered the pulpit. His statement regarding the soul was: "In the whole of heaven and the whole world it is unknown what the soul is and what its nature is. It is known that it exists, and that it is in man, but its location is only guessed at. It is certain that it is in the head, since the intellect thinks there and the will intends there, and at the front of the face of the head are man's five sense organs. To these and those, nothing gives life other than the soul, which resides within the head. But where its court is there, I would not dare to say. However, I have agreed with those who assigned it a seat in the three **ventricles of the brain** <note>original: "Ventriculis Cerebri"; the fluid-filled cavities in the brain</note>; sometimes with those who place it in the **striated bodies** <note>original: "Corporibus striatis"; parts of the basal ganglia involved in movement</note> there; sometimes with those in the **medullary substance** <note>original: "Substantia medullari"; the internal 'white matter' of the brain</note> of both brains; sometimes with those in the **cortical substance** <note>original: "Substantia corticali"; the 'gray matter' or outer layer of the brain</note>; and sometimes with those in the **dura mater** <note>original: "Dura matre"; the tough outermost membrane surrounding the brain</note>. For there have not been lacking white pebbles <note>original: "calculi sicti albi"; referring to ancient voting tokens used to indicate approval or a 'yes' vote</note> from confirmations for each of these seats. 

The 'votes' for the three ventricles in the brain were because they are the receptacles of the animal spirits and all the fluids of the brain. The 'votes' for the striated bodies were because these form the medulla through which the nerves go out, and through which both brains are continued into the spine, and from both of these emanate the fibers from which the whole body is woven. The 'votes' for the **medullary substance** of both brains were because that is the collection and mass of all the fibers which are the beginnings of the whole man. The 'votes' for the **cortical substance** were because the first and last ends are there, and from there are the beginnings of all fibers, and thus of senses and movements. The 'votes' for the **dura mater** were because it is the common covering of both brains, and from there, through a certain continuity, it extends itself over the heart and the viscera of the body. As for me, I do not judge one more than the other; I ask you to judge and choose which is preferable." 

Having said these things, he descended from the pulpit and handed the tunic, gown, and cap to the **Third**, who, climbing the pulpit, spoke as follows: "What have I, a youth, to do with such a sublime theorem? I appeal to the learned men sitting here at the sides, I appeal to you wise ones in the gallery—indeed, I appeal to the angels of the highest heaven—can anyone, from their own rational light, take for themselves any idea concerning the soul? But concerning its seat in man, I can guess as others do; and I guess that it is in the Heart, and from there in the Blood. And this is my guess, because the heart, by its blood, rules both the body and the head. For it sends out a great vessel called the **aorta** <note>original: "Aorta"</note> into the whole body, and it sends out vessels called **carotid arteries** <note>original: "vasa Carotides"</note> into the whole head. Hence there is a universal consensus

...that the Soul, from the Heart, through the blood, sustains, nourishes, and gives life to the entire organic system of both the Body and the Head. Hearing these things, some raised their voices, saying, "Learned, learned!" These were from the ranks of the Canons.

After this, the **Fourth** speaker, dressed in the same ceremonial robes, entered the Pulpit and said: "I also suspect that no one possesses a wit so subtle and polished that they can clearly perceive what the Soul is and what its nature is. Therefore, I think that for anyone who wishes to scrutinize it, their subtlety is wasted on a useless task. But from my childhood I have remained in the faith of the opinion held by the Ancients: that the soul of man is in his whole and in every part of him, and thus it is in the Head and every part of it, as well as in the Body and every part of it. It was a vain invention of the Moderns <term>Neoterici</term> <note>refers to "the newer ones," likely Enlightenment-era philosophers like Descartes or Willis who sought a specific localized "seat" for the soul</note> to designate a seat for it in one specific place rather than everywhere. Moreover, the Soul is a spiritual substance, of which neither extension nor place is predicated, but rather habitation and fulfillment. Who does not also understand 'life' when they name the 'soul'? And is not life in the whole and in every part?" After these words were spoken, many in the Audience favored him.

Next, the **Fifth** speaker stood up and, adorned with the same insignia, delivered this from the Pulpit: "I do not linger on where the Soul is—whether in some specific part or everywhere in the whole. Instead, from my own stores, I will open my mind on what the Soul is and its nature. The Soul is not thought of by anyone except as something pure, which can be likened to ether or air or wind, in which there is a vital quality due to the rationality that man possesses above the beasts. I have based this opinion on the fact that when a man expires, he is said to 'breathe out' or 'emit' his Soul or spirit. Thus also, the Soul living after death is believed to be such a breath, in which the thinking life exists, which is called the Soul. What else can the soul be?" 

But because I heard those in the Gallery <note>original: "Orchestra"; the seating area for the presiding elders</note> saying that the problem of the Soul—what it is and its nature—is not above the intellect, but within it and before it, I ask and pray that you yourselves might open this eternal Mystery." 

The Elders in the Gallery looked toward the **Headmaster** <term>Archididascalus</term>, who had proposed the problem. He understood from their nods that they wished for him to descend and teach. Immediately, he descended from the platform, passed through the Audience, and entered the Pulpit. Extending his hand, he said: "Listen, I pray. Who does not believe the Soul to be the innermost and most subtle Essence of man? But what is an Essence without a Form, other than a mere creature of reason <note>original: "ens rationis"; a conceptual entity that exists only in the mind</note>? Therefore, the Soul is a Form, and I shall tell you what kind of form it is. It is the form of all love and all wisdom. All things of love are called affections, and all things of wisdom are called perceptions. The latter, from the former and thus with them, make a single form in which there are innumerable things in such an order, series, and coherence that they can be called a 'one.' And they can be called a 'one' because nothing can be taken from it, nor can anything be added to it, for it to remain as it is. What is the human Soul but such a form? Are not all things of Love and all things of Wisdom the essentials of that form? And in man, these are in the Soul, and from the Soul they are in the Head and the body. 

"You are called Spirits and Angels, and you believed while in the World that Spirits and Angels were like winds or ethers, and thus merely Minds and Hearts. But now you see clearly that you are truly, really, and actually men, who lived and thought in a material body in the World. You knew that the material Body does not live and think, but rather the spiritual Substance within that body. This you called the Soul, though you did not know its form; and yet now you have seen it and do see it. You are all Souls, about whose immortality you have heard, thought, said, and written so much. And because you are Forms of love and wisdom from God, you cannot die forever. The Soul, therefore, is the human form, from which not a bit can be taken away, and to which not a bit can be added; and it is the innermost form of all the forms of the entire body. And because the forms which are on the outside receive from the innermost..."

# CHAPTER THIRTEEN

## CONCERNING

# THE HOLY SUPPER.

->*Without a knowledge of the correspondences between natural and spiritual things, no one can know the uses and benefits of the Holy Supper.*<-

698. This was partially explained in the chapter on **BAPTISM**, where it was shown that without an understanding of the spiritual sense of the Word, one cannot know what the two sacraments, Baptism and the Holy Supper, involve and effect; see numbers 667 to 669. It is said here that this is impossible without a knowledge of <term>correspondences</term> <note>Correspondences are the specific relationships between the natural world and the spiritual world, where every physical object reflects a spiritual reality.</note>, which amounts to the same thing, because the natural sense of the Word is turned into a spiritual sense through correspondences in Heaven. Consequently, these two senses correspond to each other; therefore, whoever knows correspondences can know the spiritual sense. What these correspondences are, and their nature, can be seen in the chapter on **SACRED SCRIPTURE** from beginning to end, as well as in the **EXPLANATION OF THE DECALOGUE** from the first commandment to the last, and particularly in **APOCALYPSE REVEALED**.

699. What true Christian does not acknowledge that these two sacraments are holy—indeed, that they are the holiest acts of worship in Christianity? But who knows where their holiness resides, or where it comes from? In the institution of the Holy Supper, based on the natural sense, nothing more is known than that the Flesh of Christ is given to be eaten and His Blood to be drunk, and that Bread and Wine stand in for them. Who, from that basis, can think otherwise than that it is holy solely because of the Lord's command? For this reason, the most learned of the Church have taught that when the Word is added to the element, it becomes a Sacrament. <note>original: "accedit Verbum ad Elementum fiat Sacramentum." This is a famous theological maxim by St. Augustine, often cited to explain how physical things like bread or water become holy.</note> However, because this origin of its holiness does not easily fit the intellect, nor does it appear in the physical elements or symbols themselves, but only in the memory, people approach it in different ways. Some do so from a confidence that sins are forgiven through it; some because they believe it sanctifies; some because it strengthens faith and thus promotes salvation. Those, however, who think lightly of it frequent it only out of a habit formed from childhood; and some, because they see no rational reason for it, omit it altogether. The impious, meanwhile, turn away from it, saying to themselves: "What is this but a ceremony onto which holiness has been impressed by the clergy? For what is there but bread and wine? And what is it but a fiction that the Body of Christ, which hung on the cross, and His Blood, which was then poured out, are distributed to the communicants along with the bread and wine?"—among other such things.

700. Such ideas about this most Holy Sacrament are fostered throughout all of Christianity today, solely because they coincide with the literal sense of the Word, while the spiritual sense has remained hidden until now. It is only today that this sense has been uncovered, in which alone the use and benefit of the Holy Supper can be seen in its true light. The reason this sense is only now being revealed is that previously Christianity existed only in name, and among some as a mere shadow. For until now, people have not approached and worshiped the Savior Himself directly as the only God in whom is the Divine Trinity; instead, they have approached Him only indirectly, which is not truly approaching or worshiping, but merely venerating Him as the cause for which man is...

# OF THE NEW HEAVEN AND THE NEW CHURCH.

...is salvation, which is not the essential cause but the means, which is below and outside of it. But truly, because Christianity itself is now first arising, and the New Church—which is understood by the <term>New Jerusalem</term> <note>A symbolic name for a new state of the Christian church as described in the Book of Revelation.</note> in the Book of Revelation—is now being established by the Lord, in which God the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are acknowledged as one because they are in one Person, it has pleased the Lord to reveal the spiritual sense of the Word. This is so that this Church may come into the actual use and benefit of the Sacraments, Baptism and the Holy Supper <note>original: "Sancta Cæna"</note>. This occurs when people see with the eyes of their spirit—that is, with their understanding—the Holiness that lies hidden within them, and apply this to themselves through the means the Lord has taught in His Word.

701. The Holiness of the Sacrament discussed here, without the spiritual sense of the Word being opened—or what is the same thing, without the <term>correspondences</term> <note>The relationship between physical objects and spiritual realities; for example, how bread relates to divine goodness.</note> of natural things with spiritual things being revealed—cannot be acknowledged inwardly any more than a treasure hidden in a field. Such a field is valued no more than a common field; but when it is discovered that there is a treasure in that field, the field is valued at a great price, and the buyer then claims that wealth for himself; and even more so when it is known that the treasure within it is more precious than any gold. Without the spiritual sense, that Sacrament is like a house that is locked up and full of heirlooms and treasure-chests, which is passed by like any other house on the street. But because it was built of marble by the Clergy as to its walls, and covered with plates of gold as to its roof, the sight of those passing by is drawn to look at it, praise it, and value it. It is different when that House is opened, and everyone is given the opportunity to enter, and the keeper supplies a loan to some from it, and a gift to others, to each according to their worth. It is called a gift from there because the precious things there are inexhaustible and are continually replenished. So it is with the Word regarding its spiritual contents, and with the Sacraments regarding their celestial contents.

The Sacrament discussed here, without its revealed holiness which lies hidden within, appears like river sand in which inconspicuous grains of gold are present in great abundance; but when revealed, it is like the gold collected from it and melted into a mass, and this fashioned into beautiful forms. This Sacrament, without its Holiness being detected and seen, is like a chest or case made of beech or poplar, in which diamonds, rubies, and many other precious stones lie arranged in order in their compartments. Who would not value that chest and case if they knew such things lay hidden inside, and even more when they see them, and also when they are distributed for free? That Sacrament, without its revealed correspondences with Heaven—and thus without the heavenly things to which it corresponds being seen—is like an Angel seen in the world in common clothing, who is honored only according to his clothes; it is altogether different when it is known that he is an Angel, and angelic words are heard from his mouth, and wonders are seen from his deeds. 

What Holiness is when it is merely preached, and what Holiness is when it is actually seen, can be illustrated by this example seen and heard in the spiritual world: A letter was read that was written by Paul <note>The Apostle Paul.</note> during the time he traveled in the world, but it had not been published, and no one knew it was by Paul. At first, it was held in low esteem by the listeners; but when it was discovered that it was one of Paul's Epistles, it was received with joy, and every single thing in it was adored. From this it was clear that the mere preaching of holiness regarding the Word and the Sacraments, when done by the leaders of the Clergy, does indeed impress a sense of holiness; but it is different when the holiness itself is uncovered and placed before the eyes to be seen, which happens through the revelation of the spiritual sense. By this, external Holiness becomes internal, and the preaching of it becomes the acknowledgment of it. It is the same with the holiness of the Sacrament of the Supper.

->UNIVERSAL THEOLOGY<-

### That through known Correspondences, it may be known what is understood by the Flesh and Blood of the Lord, and similarly by the Bread and Wine: namely, that by the Flesh of the Lord and by Bread is understood the Divine Good of His Love and also all the good of charity; and by the Blood of the Lord and by Wine, the Divine Truth of His Wisdom and also all the truth of Faith; and by Eating, appropriation. <note>In this context, "appropriation" refers to the process of making spiritual goodness and truth a permanent part of one's own life and character, much like the body absorbs nutrients from food.</note>

702. Since the spiritual sense of the Word has been revealed in our time, and along with it the knowledge of <term>Correspondences</term> <note>The systematic relationship between natural objects (like bread) and spiritual realities (like divine goodness).</note> because these serve as the link between worlds, only passages from the Word will be presented here. From these, it can clearly be seen what is understood by Flesh and Blood, and by Bread and Wine, in the **Holy Supper** <note>original: "Sancta Cæna"; also known as the Eucharist, Mass, or Communion.</note>. However, these will be preceded by the account of the Lord’s own institution of this Sacrament, and also by **His Doctrine concerning His Flesh and His Blood, and concerning Bread and Wine.**

703. **THE INSTITUTION OF THE HOLY SUPPER BY THE LORD.** Jesus celebrated the Passover with His disciples, and when evening came, he reclined with them; and while they were eating, Jesus took **BREAD**, and after blessing it, broke it and gave it to the disciples, and said, "Take, eat, this is **MY BODY**." And taking the **CUP**, and giving thanks, He gave it to them, saying, "Drink from it, all of you; this is **MY BLOOD**, that of the New Testament, which is poured out for many." **Matthew 26:26, 27, 28; Mark 14:22, 23, 24; Luke 22:19, 20.**

### THE DOCTRINE OF THE LORD CONCERNING HIS FLESH AND HIS BLOOD, AND CONCERNING BREAD AND WINE.

"Work for the food that does not perish, but the food that remains for eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you. Amen, amen, I say to you, Moses did not give you bread from heaven, but my Father gives you the true bread from heaven: for the bread of God is He who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world. I am the Bread of life; whoever comes to Me shall not hunger, and whoever believes in Me shall never thirst. I am the Bread that came down from heaven. Amen, amen, I say to you, whoever believes in Me has eternal life: I am the Bread of life. Your fathers ate manna in the wilderness and died: This is the Bread that comes down from heaven, so that anyone may eat of it and live and not die. I am the living Bread that came down from heaven; if anyone eats of this Bread, he will live forever; the Bread that I will give is my Flesh, which I will give for the life of the world. Amen, amen, I say to you, unless you eat the Flesh of the Son of Man and drink His Blood, you will not have life in you. He who eats my Flesh and drinks my Blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day: for my Flesh is food indeed, and my Blood is drink indeed. He who eats my Flesh and drinks my Blood remains in Me, and I in him." **John 6:27, 32, 33, 35, 41, 47, 48, 49, 50, 51, 53, 54, 55, 56.**

704. That flesh is not meant by "flesh" there, nor blood by "blood," anyone who is enlightened from heaven can perceive within themselves. Rather, in the **NATURAL SENSE**, both refer to the **Passion of the cross** <note>The suffering and crucifixion of Jesus.</note>, which they were to remember. This is why He said, when He instituted this supper of the Last Jewish Passover and the First Christian Passover, *"Do this in remembrance of Me,"* **Luke 22:19; 1 Corinthians 11:24, 25.** Similarly, bread is not meant by "Bread," nor wine by "Wine," but in the **NATURAL SENSE** they mean the same thing as Flesh and Blood—namely, the suffering of His cross—for it is written, *"Jesus broke the Bread and gave it to the disciples, and said, this is my Body; and taking the Cup, He gave it to them, saying, this is my Blood,"* **Matthew 26; Mark 14.**

705. That by those four—Flesh, Blood, Bread, and Wine—are understood the Spiritual and Celestial things which correspond to them, can be established from the places in the Word where they are named. That by FLESH in the Word is understood what is spiritual and celestial can be established from these passages: " *Come and gather yourselves to the SUPPER OF THE GREAT GOD* <note>original: "CÆNAM MAGNI DEI"</note>, *that you may eat the Flesh of kings, and the Flesh of commanders of thousands, and the Flesh of the mighty, and the Flesh of horses and of those who sit upon them, and the Flesh of all free men and servants, and of small and great*," Revelation 19:17, 18. And in Ezekiel: "*Gather yourselves from every side to MY SACRIFICE, which I sacrifice for you, a GREAT SACRIFICE upon the mountains of Israel, that you may eat Flesh and drink Blood: you shall eat the Flesh of the mighty, and drink the Blood of the princes of the earth; and you shall eat fat to satiety, and drink Blood even to drunkenness from my Sacrifice; and you shall be satisfied at my table, with horse and chariot, with the mighty and every man of war. Thus I will give my glory among the nations.*" Chapter 39:17 to 21. Who does not see that in those places by Flesh is not understood flesh, nor by Blood, blood, but the spiritual and celestial things which correspond to them? Otherwise, would these not be empty and strange expressions—that they should eat the flesh of kings, commanders, the mighty, horses, and those sitting on them, and that they should be satisfied at the table with horse, chariot, the mighty, and every man of war; and that they should drink the blood of the princes of the earth, and blood even to drunkenness? That these things are said concerning the Holy Supper of the Lord is clearly evident, for it is called the "Supper of the Great God" and also a "Great Sacrifice." Since all spiritual and celestial things refer solely to what is good and true, it follows that by Flesh is understood the Good of <term>charity</term> <note>Active love and goodwill toward others.</note>, and by Blood the truth of faith, and in the supreme sense the Lord regarding the Divine Good of love and the Divine Truth of wisdom. Spiritual good is also understood by Flesh in these words in Ezekiel: "*I will give them one Heart, and I will give a new spirit in the midst of you, and I will remove the Heart of stone, and I will give them a Heart of flesh*," Ezekiel 11:19, Chapter 36:26; by "Heart" in the Word is signified love, hence by a "Heart of flesh," the love of what is good. Furthermore, that by Flesh and Blood is understood good and truth, both spiritual, is further established from the significance of Bread and Wine in what follows, since the Lord says that His Flesh is Bread, and that His Blood is the Wine which was drunk from the Cup.

706. That by the Blood of the Lord is understood His Divine Truth and that of the Word, is because by His Flesh is spiritually understood the Divine Good of love; and these two are united in the Lord. It is known that the Lord is the Word, and there are two things to which everything in the Word refers: Divine Good and Divine Truth; therefore, if the Word is accepted in place of the Lord, it is clear that those two are understood by His Flesh and Blood. That by Blood is understood the Divine Truth of the Lord or the Word is evident from many places, such as that Blood was called the "Blood of the covenant," and a <term>covenant</term> <note>A sacred bond or conjunction between God and humanity.</note> is conjunction, and this is effected by the Lord through His Divine Truth; as in Zechariah, "*By the BLOOD OF thy COVENANT I will send forth the prisoners out of the pit*," 9:11. And in Moses: "*Moses, after he had read the Book of the law in the ears of the people, sprinkled half of the Blood upon the people, and said*, BEHOLD THE BLOOD OF THE COVENANT, *which Jehovah hath made with you concerning all these words*," Exodus 24:3 to 11. *And Jesus taking the cup, and gave it to them, saying, this is my Blood, that of the New Covenant* <note>original: "Novi Fæderis"; often translated as "New Testament."</note>, Matthew 26:27, 28; Mark 14:24; Luke 22:20. By the Blood of the New Covenant or Testament, nothing else is signified than the Word, which is called the Covenant and Testament, Old and New, and thus the Divine Truth therein. Since that is signified by Blood, therefore the Lord gave them Wine, saying, "*this is my Blood*," and Wine signifies Divine Truth; wherefore it is also called the *Blood of grapes*, Genesis 49:11, Deuteronomy 32:14. This is further evident from the Lord's words: "*Amen, amen I say to you, unless you eat the Flesh of the Son of man, and drink His Blood, you shall not have...*"

you will have life in you; for my Flesh is truly Food, and my Blood is truly Drink: *whoever eats my Flesh and drinks my Blood, remains in Me, and I in him*, John 6:50 to 58. It is clearly evident that by "Blood" here is meant the Divine Truth of the Word, because it is said that he who drinks it has life in himself and remains in the Lord and the Lord in him. It is well known in the Church that Divine Truth, and a life lived according to it, achieves this, and that the Holy Supper confirms it. Since Blood signified the Divine Truth of the Lord (which is also the Divine Truth of the Word, and this is the very Covenant and Testament, both Old and New), Blood was therefore the most holy <term>Representative</term> <note>A symbolic ritual or object that stands in for a spiritual reality in the physical world.</note> of the Church among the Children of Israel. In that Church, each and every thing was a <term>Correspondence</term> <note>The ancient science of how natural things mirror and connect to spiritual things.</note> of natural things with spiritual things. 

This is why they were to:
*   *Take the Paschal Blood and put it on the doorposts and lintels of the houses, so that the plague would not come upon them*, Exodus 12:7, 13, 22.
*   *The blood of the burnt offering was to be sprinkled upon the Altar, at its foundations, and upon Aaron, his sons, and their garments*, Exodus 29:12, 16, 20, 21; Leviticus 1:5, 11, 15; Chapter 3:2, 8, 13; Chapter 4:25, 30, 34; Chapter 8:15, 24; Chapter 17:6; Chapter 8:8; Deuteronomy 12:27.
*   *It was also sprinkled upon the Veil over the Ark, upon the Mercy Seat there, and upon the horns of the Altar of Incense*, Leviticus 4:6, 7, 17, 18; Chapter 16:12, 13, 14, 15.

A similar thing is signified by the "Blood of the Lamb" in the Revelation: *These have washed their robes and made them white in the Blood of the Lamb*, Chapter 7:14; and by these words there: *War broke out in heaven; Michael and his angels fought against the Dragon, and they overcame him through the Blood of the Lamb and through the Word of their testimony*, Chapter 12:7, 11. For it cannot be thought that Michael and his angels overcame the Dragon by anything other than the Lord’s Divine Truth in the Word. Angels in heaven cannot think of any material blood, nor do they think of the Lord's <term>Passion</term> <note>The suffering and death of Jesus on the cross.</note>, but of Divine Truth and of His Resurrection. Therefore, when a person thinks about the Blood of the Lord, the angels perceive the Divine Truth of His Word; and when a person thinks of the Lord’s Passion, they perceive His glorification, and then only the Resurrection. It has been granted to me to know that this is so through much experience.

That Blood signifies Divine Truth is also clear from these words in David: *God shall save the souls of the needy, precious shall their Blood be in His eyes, and they shall live, and He shall give them of the gold of Sheba*, Psalm 72:13, 14, 15, 16. "Precious blood in the eyes of God" stands for the Divine Truth present with them; the "Gold of Sheba" is the wisdom derived from it. And in Ezekiel: *Gather yourselves to the great Sacrifice upon the mountains of Israel, that you may eat Flesh and drink Blood; you shall drink the blood of the princes of the earth, and you shall drink blood even to drunkenness; thus I will set my glory among the nations*, 39:17 to 21. This refers to the Church which the Lord was about to establish among the nations. That "blood" here cannot mean literal blood, but the Truth from the Word among them, may be seen just above.

708. That by **WINE** the same thing is meant as by **Blood** is clearly evident from the Lord’s words: "*Jesus taking the CUP and saying, This is my Blood*," Matthew 26, Mark 14, Luke 22; and also from these: "*He washes his garment in WINE, and his cloak in the* BLOOD *of grapes*," Genesis 49:11; these words refer to the Lord. "*Jehovah of Hosts will make for all peoples a feast of fat things, a feast of lees, or of* SWEET WINE," Isaiah 25:6; this refers to the <term>Sacrament of the Holy Supper</term> to be instituted by the Lord. For this reason, the Church is called a **VINEYARD** in many places in the Word, as in Isaiah 5:1, 2, 4, Matthew 20:1 to 13; and the Lord calls Himself the **TRUE VINE**, and the people who are grafted into Him, the **BRANCHES** <note>original: *Palmites*.</note>, John 15:1, 5, besides many other places.

709. From these things it can now be established what is meant by the Lord’s Flesh and Blood, and by Bread and Wine, in a threefold sense: **Natural, Spiritual, and Celestial**. Every person who has been taught the Christian religion can know—and if they do not know, they can learn—that there is both <term>Natural Nourishment</term> and <term>Spiritual Nourishment</term>, and that natural nourishment is for the body, but spiritual nourishment is for the soul. For the Lord Jehovah says in Moses: "*Man does not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of Jehovah does man live*," Deuteronomy 8:2, 3. Now, because the body dies and the soul lives after death, it follows that spiritual nourishment is for eternal salvation. Who, then, does not see that these two types of nourishment are by no means to be confused? If anyone does confuse them, they cannot help but adopt natural and sensual ideas about the Lord’s Flesh and Blood and the Bread and Wine. These ideas, being material, bodily, and carnal, suffocate spiritual ideas concerning this most Holy Sacrament. However, if someone is so simple that they cannot think with their intellect about anything other than what they see with their eyes, I advise them that when they take the Bread and Wine in the Holy Supper and hear the Lord’s Flesh and Blood mentioned, they should think to themselves that it is the holiest act of worship. They should remember the <term>Passion of Christ</term> and His love for the salvation of humanity; for He says, "*Do this in remembrance of Me*," Luke 22:19; and also, "*The Son of Man came to give His life as a ransom for many*," Matthew 20:28, Mark 10:45. "*I lay down my life for the sheep*," John 10:15, 17, Chapter 15:13.

# That from these things understood, it can be comprehended that the **Holy Supper** <term>universally and singularly</term> <note>In this context, "universally" refers to the broad, governing principles, while "singularly" refers to every specific, individual detail. The author is arguing that the whole of spiritual reality is present in this one ritual.</note> contains all things of the Church and all things of Heaven.

711. In the preceding Article it was shown that the Lord Himself is present in the **Holy Supper**, and that the Flesh and Bread are Himself in regard to the **Divine Good of Love**, and that the Blood and Wine are Himself in regard to the **Divine Truth of Wisdom**. Therefore, there are three things which the **Holy Supper** involves: namely, the Lord, His Divine Good, and His Divine Truth. Since, therefore, the **Holy Supper** includes and contains these three, it follows that it also includes and contains the <term>Universals</term> <note>The primary or fundamental principles that govern everything else.</note> of Heaven and the Church. And because all <term>singulars</term> <note>The individual parts or specific instances.</note> depend on Universals, just as contents depend on the vessels that hold them, it also follows that the **Holy Supper** includes and contains all the specific details of Heaven and the Church. From this it is first evident that because the Lord’s Flesh and Blood (and likewise the Bread and Wine) mean Divine Good and Divine Truth—both from the Lord and being the Lord—the **Holy Supper** contains, in both a general and a specific sense, everything belonging to Heaven and the Church.

712. It is also known that the **Essentials of the Church** are three: namely, God, Charity, and Faith, and that everything within the Church refers back to those three as its primary principles. These are the same as what was mentioned above; for in the **Holy Supper**, "God" is the Lord, "Charity" is Divine Good, and "Faith" is Divine Truth. For what is charity but the good that a person does from the Lord? And what is faith but the truth that a person believes from the Lord? For this reason, there are three things in a human being regarding their internal self—namely, the **Soul** (or Mind), the **Will**, and the **Understanding**. These three are the <term>receptacles</term> <note>Containers or vessels designed to receive something.</note> of those three universals. The Soul or Mind itself is the receptacle of the Lord (for it lives from Him); the Will is the receptacle of love or good; and the Understanding is the receptacle of wisdom or truth. Therefore, every single thing in the Soul or Mind not only refers back to those three universals of Heaven and the Church but also proceeds from them. Consider anything that comes from a person: if the Mind, Will, and Understanding were not present in it, and if one of them were taken away, would the person be anything more than something inanimate? Similarly, there are three things in a person regarding their external self, to which every single thing refers and upon which they depend: namely, the **Body**, the **Heart**, and the **Lungs**. These three parts of the Body also <term>correspond</term> <note>The author uses "Correspondence" to describe a specific relationship where a physical thing acts as a functional mirror to a spiritual reality.</note> to the three parts of the Mind: the Heart to the Will, and the Lungs (or respiration) to the Understanding. That such a **Correspondence** exists has been fully shown in previous works. Thus, every single thing in a person, both in a general and specific sense, is formed as a receptacle for those three universals of Heaven and the Church. The reason is that man was created in the **image and likeness of God**, so that he might be in the Lord and the Lord in him.

713. Conversely, there are three things opposite to those Universals, which are the **Devil**, **Evil**, and **Falsity**. By "the Devil" is meant **Hell**, which stands in opposition to the Lord; Evil stands in opposition to Good; and Falsity against Truth. These three make a one, for where the devil is, there also is evil and the resulting falsity. These three also universally and singularly contain all things of Hell, and also all things of the World that are against Heaven and the Church. But because they are opposites, they are entirely separated; yet they are still held in connection through a wonderful subjection of all Hell under Heaven, of evil under good, and of falsity under truth, which subjection was discussed in the work *HEAVEN AND HELL*.

714. In order that specific things may be contained in their order and connection, it is necessary that they be Uni-

<term>Universals</term> <note>The primary principles or "big ideas" that govern everything else.</note> are the sources from which all things exist and in which they subsist. It is also necessary that <term>Singulars</term> <note>Specific, individual things.</note> reflect their Universals in a certain image; otherwise, the whole would perish along with its parts. This relationship ensures that all things of the universe are preserved in their integrity from the first day of Creation until now and beyond. It is well known that all things in the universe relate to good and truth; the reason for this is that all things were created by God from the **Divine Good of love** through the **Divine Truth of wisdom**. Take whatever you please, whether an animal, a shrub, or a stone: those three most universal things are inscribed upon them in a certain relationship.

715. Since Divine Good and Divine Truth are the most universal of all things of Heaven and the Church, for that reason **Melchizedek**, who represented the Lord, brought forth **Bread and Wine** to Abram and blessed him. Concerning Melchizedek it is read: *“Melchizedek, King of Salem, brought forth Bread and Wine; and he was the Priest to God Most High, and he blessed him,”* Genesis 14:18-19. That Melchizedek represented the Lord is evident from these words in David: *“You are a Priest forever after the manner of Melchizedek,”* Psalm 110:4. That these refer to the Lord may be seen in Hebrews 5:6, 8, 10; Chapter 6:20; Chapter 7:1, 10, 11, 15, 17, 21. The reason he brought forth Bread and Wine was that those two include all things of Heaven and the Church, and thus all things of Blessing, just like the Bread and Wine in the **Holy Supper**.

## That the whole Lord and His entire Redemption are in the Holy Supper.

716. That the whole Lord is in the **Holy Supper**, both as to His **glorified Human** and as to the **Divine** from which the Human came, is evident from His very own words. That His Human is present in the **Holy Supper** is clear from these: *“Jesus, taking Bread, broke it and gave it to the disciples, and said, ‘This is my Body’; and taking the Cup, He gave it to them, saying, ‘This is my Blood,’”* Matthew 26, Mark 14, Luke 22. Also in John: *“I am the Bread of life; if anyone eats of this Bread, he shall live forever; the Bread that I will give is my Flesh; truly, truly I say to you, he who eats my Flesh and drinks my Blood remains in Me, and I in him, and lives forever,”* John 6. From these it is clearly established that the Lord is in the **Holy Supper** as to His glorified Human. That the whole Lord as to His Divine also—from which the Human is—is present in the **Holy Supper**, is evident from these facts: That He Himself is the Bread that came down from Heaven (John 6); He came down from Heaven with the Divine, for it is said: *“The Word was with God, and the Word was God... all things were made by Him... and the Word was made Flesh,”* John 1:1, 3, 14. And further from this: *“the Father and He are one,”* John 10:30; *“all things of the Father are His,”* John 16:15; *“He is in the Father and the Father in Him,”* John 14:10-11, etc. Furthermore, His Divine can no more be separated from His Human than the Soul can be from the Body; therefore, when it is said that the whole Lord as to His Human is in the **Holy Supper**, it follows that His Divine, as the source, is also there at the same time. Now, since His Flesh signifies the Divine Good of His love, and the Blood the Divine Truth of His wisdom, it is clear that the whole Lord, both as to the Divine and the glorified Human, is Omnipresent in the **Holy Supper**; consequently, it is a <term>spiritual eating</term> <note>original: "manducatio spiritualis"; the idea that the soul consumes and incorporates spiritual nourishment.</note>.

717. That the Lord's whole **Redemption** is in the **Holy Supper** follows from what has just been said, for where the whole Lord is, there also is His whole Redemption. For He Himself as to the Human is the Redeemer, and therefore is Redemption itself; nothing of Redemption can be absent where He is entirely present. Therefore, all those who worthily approach the Holy Communion become His Redeemed; and because through Redemp-

He who receives is redeemed in the same degree to which he receives. From this, it is clear that the effects and fruits of the Lord's Redemption return to those who approach worthily.

718. In every healthy person, there is a capacity for receiving wisdom from the Lord—that is, the power to increase in **Truths** (from which wisdom is formed) forever. There is also a capacity for receiving love—that is, the power to bear the fruit of **Good** (from which love is formed), likewise forever. This perpetual fruiting of good and its resulting love, and that perpetual multiplication of truth and its resulting wisdom, is granted to the Angels, and also to those people who are becoming Angels. And because the Lord is Love itself and Wisdom itself, it follows that a person has the capacity for joining themselves to the Lord, and the Lord to themselves, forever. Yet, because a person is <term>finite</term> <note>Limited and bounded, unlike the infinite God.</note>, the Lord's very Divinity cannot be joined to them, but only <term>adjoined</term> <note>Attached or linked to the outside, rather than blending into one substance.</note>. For illustration: the light of the sun cannot be joined to the eye, nor the sound of the air to the ear; they can only be adjoined to them, and thus give the faculty of seeing and hearing. For a person is not **Life** in themselves—not even the Lord as to His Human <note>original: "quoad Humanum"</note> (John 5:26)—but is a receptacle of life. It is Life itself which is adjoined to a person, but not joined as one substance. These things are added so that it may be understood in what way the whole Lord and His entire Redemption are present in the Holy Supper.

## *That the Lord is present and opens Heaven to those who approach the Holy Supper worthily; and that He is also present with those who approach unworthily, but to these He does not open Heaven: consequently, just as Baptism is an introduction into the Church, so the Holy Supper is an introduction into Heaven.*

719. Who they are that approach the Holy Supper worthily will be discussed in the two following articles, along with those who approach unworthily; for when one side is affirmed, the other is known by its opposite. The reason the Lord is present with both the worthy and the unworthy is that He is <term>Omnipresent</term> <note>Present everywhere at once.</note>, in Heaven as well as in Hell, and also in the world; therefore, He is with the evil just as much as with the good. But with the good—that is, the <term>regenerate</term> <note>Those who have undergone a spiritual rebirth or "turning around" of their character.</note>—He is present <term>universally and singularly</term> <note>Present in the big picture and in every tiny detail of their lives.</note>. For the Lord is in them and they are in the Lord, and where the Lord is, there is Heaven. Heaven also makes up the Body of the Lord; therefore, to be in His Body is to be simultaneously in Heaven.

But the Lord's presence with those who approach unworthily is His universal presence, but not His singular presence (or, what is the same thing, it is an external presence, but not an internal one at the same time). His universal or external presence allows a person to live as a human being and to enjoy the capacity of knowing, understanding, and speaking rationally from that understanding. For a person is born for Heaven and is therefore spiritual—not merely natural like a beast. They also enjoy the capacity of willing and doing those things which the understanding can know and think about. But if the **Will** refuses those things that are truly rational (which are also inwardly spiritual), then the person becomes "External." Therefore, with those who only understand what is true and good, there is a universal or external presence of the Lord; but with those who also will and do what is true and good, there is a presence of the Lord that is both universal and singular, both internal and external. Those who only understand and speak truths and goods are, by comparison, the **foolish virgins** who had lamps but no oil; but those who not only understand and speak truths and goods but also will and do them, are the **wise virgins** who were let into the wedding, while the former stood outside and knocked, but were not let in— <note>The word cuts off here, continuing to the next page.</note>

From these things it is established that the Lord is present and opens Heaven to those who approach the Holy Supper worthily, and that He is also present with those who approach unworthily, but that for these latter He does not open Heaven.

620. <note>This paragraph number appears as 620 in the source, though logically it follows 719 in the sequence of this work.</note> Yet it must not be believed that the Lord closes Heaven to those who approach unworthily; He does not do this to any person until the very end of their life in the world. Rather, the person closes it to themselves. This is done through the rejection of faith and through an evil life. Nevertheless, a person is continually held in a state where repentance and conversion are possible; for the Lord is perpetually present and urges that He be received, for He says, *Behold, I stand at the door and knock; if anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in, and WILL SUP WITH HIM AND HE WITH ME*, Revelation 3:20. Therefore, the fault lies with the person themselves, who does not open the door. It is otherwise after death; then Heaven is closed and cannot be opened to those who, until the end of life, approached the Holy Table unworthily, for then the interiors of their minds are fixed and established.

721. That Baptism is the introduction into the Church was shown in the chapter on Baptism; however, that the Holy Supper is the introduction into Heaven is established from what has been said and perceived above. These two <term>Sacraments</term> <note>Holy rituals regarded as signs of spiritual grace.</note>, Baptism and the Holy Supper, are like two gates to eternal life. Every Christian person is let in and introduced through Baptism, which is the first gate, into those things which the Church teaches from the Word concerning the other life, all of which are means through which a person can be prepared and led to Heaven. The second gate is the Holy Supper; through it, every person who has allowed themselves to be prepared and led by the Lord is let in and introduced into Heaven: there are no other universal gates. These two can be compared with a Prince born to a kingdom: first, he is introduced into the knowledge required for governing; second is his coronation and the beginning of his rule. They can also be compared with a son born to a great inheritance, who must first learn and absorb those things pertaining to the proper management of possessions and wealth; second is the actual possession and administration. They can also be compared with the building of a house and with living in it; and also with the instruction of a person from infancy until the age when they are under their own right and judgment, and with their rational and spiritual life thereafter. One period must necessarily precede so that the other may be obtained, for the latter is not possible without the former. By these examples it is illustrated that Baptism and the Holy Supper are like two gates through which a person is introduced to eternal life, and that after the first gate there is a field which must be crossed, and the second is the goal where the <term>victory-prize</term> <note>original: "adorea"; a Roman term for a reward of grain given for military success, signifying glory.</note> is located toward which the course was directed. For the palm of victory is not given except after the skirmish, nor the reward except after the battle.

->*That those approach the Holy Supper worthily who are in faith in the Lord and in charity toward the neighbor, thus those who are regenerated.*<-

That God must be acknowledged so that one may have religion, and within it something of the Church, is dictated by Reason itself in which there is anything spiritual. Therefore, whoever approaches the Holy Supper and does not acknowledge God profanes it; for with the eye they see the bread and wine, and with the tongue they taste them, but the mind thinks: "What is this but an <term>indifferent thing</term> <note>original: "adiaphoron"; a Greek term used in theology for matters that are neither commanded nor forbidden, and thus of no spiritual consequence.</note>, and how do these differ from similar things on my own table? Yet I do this lest I be accused by the priesthood, and consequently by the common people, of the infamy of being an atheist." That Faith in the Lord is the *third means* of worthily enjoying the Holy Supper is because charity and faith make one, just as heat and light do in the time of spring, from which two joined together every tree is reborn; similarly, every person lives from spiritual heat, which is charity, and from spiritual light, which is the truth of faith. That faith in the Lord accomplishes this is established by these passages: *He who believes in Me shall never die, but shall live*, John 11:25, 26. *This is the will of the Father, that everyone who believes in the Son should have eternal life*, John 6:40. *God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son, that everyone who believes in Him should have eternal life*, John 3:15, 16. *He who believes in the Son has eternal life; but he who does not believe the Son shall not see life, but the anger of God remains upon him*, John 3:36. *We are in the truth, in the Son of God Jesus Christ; This is the true God and eternal life*, 1 John 5:20, 21.

723. That through these three—the Lord, Charity, and Faith—acting as one, a person is <term>regenerated</term> <note>the process of spiritual rebirth or being made new by God</note>, and that unless a person is regenerated, they cannot come into Heaven, has been shown in the chapter on REFORMATION AND REGENERATION. For this reason, the Lord cannot open Heaven to any others than the regenerated, and after natural death, no introduction into it is given to others. By the "Regenerated" who worthily approach, are meant those who are internally in those three Essentials of the Church and Heaven, and not those who are merely so externally; for these latter confess the Lord not with the soul but only with the tongue, and practice charity toward the neighbor not with the heart but only with the body. Such are all those who "work iniquity," according to these words of the Lord: *Then you will begin to say, Lord, we ate and drank in Your presence; but I will say to you, I do not know you or where you are from; depart from me, all you workers of iniquity*, Luke 13:26, 27 <note>The source text mistakenly cites Luke 23</note>.

It is similar with those who are called to the marriage of the Lord as the Bridegroom with the Church as the Bride; among these are the kinsmen, relatives, and friends who trace their lineage through regeneration <note>term: "regeneration" — the process of being spiritually reborn or made new by God</note> from the Lord. Furthermore, who in the world is initiated into the friendship of another except the one who trusts him with a sincere heart and does his will? Such a person, and no others, is numbered among his own, and to him he entrusts his goods.

## That those who worthily approach the *Holy Supper* are in the *Lord*, and the *Lord* is in them; consequently, that through the *Holy Supper*, a conjunction with the *Lord* is effected.

725. It has been demonstrated in several chapters above that those who approach the Holy Supper worthily are those who possess faith in the Lord and charity toward their neighbor; and that the truths of faith bring about the presence of the Lord, while the goods of charity, together with faith, bring about conjunction <note>term: "conjunction" — a vital, living connection or union between the human and the Divine</note>. From this it follows that those who worthily approach the Holy Supper are joined to the Lord, and those who are joined to the Lord are in Him and He in them. The Lord Himself declares that this happens to those who approach worthily in the Gospel of John, with these words: *He who eats my Flesh and drinks my Blood remains in Me and I in him* (John 6:56). That this is a conjunction with the Lord is also taught elsewhere in the same Gospel: *Abide in Me, and I in you... he who abides in Me and I in him, he bears much fruit* (John 15:4, 5; see also Revelation 3:20). What is conjunction with the Lord other than being among those who are in His Body? His Body is formed by those who believe in Him and do His will. His will is the exercise of charity according to the truths of faith.

726. The reason that eternal life and salvation cannot be given without conjunction with the Lord is that He is both. That He is ETERNAL LIFE is clearly established from passages in the Word, such as this in John: *Jesus Christ is the True God and Eternal Life* (1 John 5:21). That He is SALVATION is because salvation and eternal life are one. His name, *Jesus*, also signifies "Salvation," and for this reason, He is called the SAVIOR throughout the whole Christian world. Nevertheless, no others worthily approach the Holy Supper except those who are inwardly joined to the Lord; and those who are regenerated are inwardly joined to Him. Who the regenerated are was shown in the chapter on REFORMATION AND REGENERATION. Furthermore, there are many who confess the Lord and do good to their neighbor, but if they do not do this out of love for the neighbor and faith in the Lord, they are not regenerated. This is because they do good to the neighbor only for reasons regarding the world and themselves, and not for the sake of the neighbor as the neighbor. The works of such people are merely natural, hiding nothing spiritual within them; for these people confess the Lord only with their mouth and lips, from which their heart is far removed. True love for the neighbor and true faith are from the Lord alone, and both are given to a person while he, from his own free will, naturally does good to the neighbor, rationally believes truths, and looks to the Lord. When these three occur because of the commands in the Word, then the Lord implants charity and faith in the person's center and makes them both spiritual. Thus the Lord joins the man to Himself, and the man joins himself to the Lord; for...
