A connection, unless it is made reciprocally, does not exist. But these things have been fully shown in the chapters on **CHARITY** & **FAITH**, on **FREE WILL**, and on **REGENERATION**.

727. It is well known that through invitations to tables and through banquets, connections and associations are made in the world; for by these means, the host intends something that contributes to some end, looking toward agreement or friendship. Much more is this true of invitations that have spiritual things as their end. The feasts in the Ancient Churches were feasts of charity <note>original: "convivia charitatis"; also known as "Agape" or "love-feasts" in the early Christian tradition, where members shared a meal to strengthen their community bonds</note>; similarly in the primitive Christian Church, in which people strengthened one another so that they might remain in the worship of the Lord from a sincere heart. The sacrificial meals of the children of Israel near the Tabernacle signified nothing other than unanimity in the worship of Jehovah; for this reason the meat that was eaten was called "Holy" (Jeremiah 11:15; Haggai 2:12, and many times elsewhere), because it came from the sacrifice. How much more so the Bread and Wine, and the Paschal Meat <note>the "Paschal Meat" refers to the lamb eaten during the Passover</note> at the Lord’s Supper, who offered Himself as a sacrifice for the sins of the whole world. Furthermore, the connection with the Lord through the Holy Supper can be illustrated by the connection of family members from one head of the family <note>term: "Patrefamilias" — the father or master of a household who acts as the root of a family line</note>. From him descend blood relations, and in order, those related by marriage and distant kin; and all of these draw something from the first lineage. But they do not actually draw flesh and blood in a physical sense, but rather they draw from that flesh and blood the soul, and from that, an inclination toward similar things by which they are connected. This connection even appears commonly in their faces and also in their manners, and for this reason they are called "one flesh," as in Genesis 29:14; 37:27; 2 Samuel 5:1; 19:12, 13, and elsewhere. It is similar with the Lord, who is the Father of all the faithful and the blessed. The connection with Him is made through love and faith, through which two they are called "one flesh." This is why He said: *He who eats my Flesh and drinks my Blood remains in Me and I in him.* Who does not see that the Bread and Wine do not do this themselves, but rather the good of love (which is understood by the Bread) and the truth of faith (which is understood by the Wine)? These are the Lord's own, and they proceed and are communicated from Him alone. Indeed, every connection is made through love, and love is not love without trust. Those who believe that the Bread is literal flesh and the Wine is literal blood, and are unable to raise their thoughts any higher, may remain in that belief; but let it be only with the understanding that the most holy thing which connects them with the Lord is that which is attributed and assigned to a person as their own, even though it constantly remains the Lord's.

## That the Holy Supper is, for those who approach worthily, like a signing and a seal that they are the children of God.

728. The reason the Holy Supper is, for those who approach worthily, like a signing and a seal that they are the children of God, is because (as said above) the Lord is then present. He introduces into Heaven those who are born of Him, that is, the regenerated. The Holy Supper does this because the Lord is then present even as to His Human; for it was shown above that in the Holy Supper the whole Lord is present, along with His entire work of Redemption. For He says of the Bread, "This is my Body," and of the Wine, "This is my Blood." Consequently, He admits them at that time into His Body; and the Church and Heaven make up His Body. When a person is being regenerated, the Lord is indeed present, and through His Divine operation, He prepares the person for Heaven; but so that the person may actually enter, they must actually present themselves to the Lord. And because the Lord actually presents Himself to the person, the person must actually receive Him—not as He hung on the cross, but as He is in His glorified Human. In this Human He is present, and its "Body" is Divine Good, and its "Blood" is Divine Truth. These are given to the person, and through these the person is regenerated and is in the Lord and the Lord in them; for, as shown above, the eating that is performed in the Holy Supper is a spiritual eating. Once these things are rightly understood, it is clear that the Holy Supper is like a signing and a seal, providing evidence that those who approach it worthily are the children of God.

729. Those, however, who depart this life in infancy or childhood, and thus do not reach an age where they can worthily approach the Holy Supper, are introduced by the Lord through Baptism. For, as was shown in the chapter on Baptism, that rite is an introduction into the Christian Church, and at the same time an insertion among Christians in the spiritual world. In that world, the Church and Heaven are one; therefore, for those children, introduction into the Church is also introduction into Heaven. Because they are educated under the Lord’s own guidance, they are regenerated more and more and become His children, for they know no other Father. Furthermore, infants and children born outside the Christian Church <note>referring to those in non-Christian cultures or religions</note> are introduced into the heaven designated for their own religion by a means other than Baptism, after they have received faith in the Lord; however, they are not mixed with those who are in the Christian heaven. Indeed, there is no nation in the entire world that cannot be saved if it acknowledges God and lives a good life; for the Lord has redeemed all these people, and every human being is born spiritual <note>meaning they possess the inherent capacity for spiritual life</note>, which gives them the ability to receive the gift of redemption. Those who receive the Lord—that is, those who have faith in Him and do not live in the evils of life—are called **CHILDREN OF GOD, and BORN of GOD** (John 1:12, 13; Chapter 11:52); they are also called **CHILDREN OF THE KINGDOM** (Matthew 13:38) and **HEIRS** (Matthew 19:29; Chapter 25:34). The **DISCIPLES OF THE LORD** are also called **CHILDREN** (Matthew 13:33), as are **ALL THE ANGELS** (Job 1:6; Chapter 2:1).

730. The Holy Supper is similar to a Covenant <note>term: "Fædus" — a formal treaty or pact between two parties, here describing the legal and spiritual agreement between God and humanity</note> which is struck after the terms have been agreed upon, and is finally ratified with a seal. The Lord *Himself* teaches that His Blood is a covenant; for He said, when He took the cup and gave it, *“Drink of it, all of you; this is my Blood, that of the New Testament”* (Matthew 26:28; Mark 14:24; Luke 22:20). The New Testament is the New Covenant; this is why the Word written by the Prophets before the Lord’s coming is called the Old Testament or Covenant, and the Word written by the Evangelists and Apostles after His coming is the New Testament or Covenant. (That the Divine Truth of the Word is meant by "Blood," and likewise by "Wine" in the Holy Supper, may be seen above in Article II, numbers 7 and 10.) The Word is the very Covenant that the Lord has struck with man, and man with the Lord, for the Lord descended as the Word—that is, as the Divine Truth. Because this is His Blood, therefore blood in the Israelite Church (which was a representative of the Christian Church) was called the **BLOOD OF THE COVENANT** (Exodus 24:7, 8; Zechariah 9:11), and the Lord was called the **COVENANT OF THE PEOPLE** (Isaiah 42:6; Chapter 49:8; Jeremiah 31:31 to 34; Psalm 111:9).

That there must be a complete signing so that there may be some certainty, and that this follows after deliberate acts, is also according to the order of the world. What is an embassy or a will without a signature? What is a legal judgment without a signed sentence to make the judgment valid? What is a high office in a kingdom without a commission? What is a promotion to any position without confirmation? What is the possession of a house without a purchase or an agreement with the owner? What is progress toward a goal, or running toward a finish line for a prize, if there is no finish line or goal where the prize is to be claimed, and unless the judge has established his pledge in some way? These last examples are added only for the sake of illustration, so that even a simple person may perceive that the Holy Supper is like a signing, a seal, a token <note>original: "tessera" — a small tablet or ticket used as a sign of identity or membership</note>, and a certification of an embassy even before the angels, showing that they are children of God; and moreover, it is like a key to the house in Heaven where they will live forever.

He flew face down and lowered himself slowly toward the earth, which appeared to me as a continent. As he touched the ground, he stood upright and walked here and there on his feet. Then, seeing me, he directed his steps toward me. I was <note>original: "in spiritu"</note> in the spirit, and in this state I was standing on a hill in the southern region. When he was close, I spoke to him and asked, "What is happening now? I heard the blast of your trumpet and saw your descent through the air."

The Angel answered: "I have been sent to call together those most celebrated for their learning, most keen in intellect, and most eminent in the reputation for wisdom, who are from the kingdoms of the Christian world upon this continental land. They are to gather on this hill where you are staying, and from their hearts express their minds on what they had thought, understood, and tasted as wisdom while in the world regarding **HEAVENLY JOY** and **ETERNAL HAPPINESS**. The reason for my mission is this: some newcomers from the world, having been admitted into our heavenly society which is in the East, reported that not even one person in the entire Christian world knows what heavenly joy and eternal happiness are, or even what Heaven is. My brothers and companions were greatly astonished at this, and they said to me: 'Go down, call out, and summon the wisest in the <term>world of spirits<note>the intermediate realm where all people first gather after the death of the physical body</note></term>, where all mortals are first collected after their departure from the natural world, so that we may be made certain from the mouths of many whether it is the truth that such darkness, or shadowy ignorance, exists among Christians concerning the future life.'" 

He then said, "Wait a little while, and you will see the groups of wise men flowing toward this place; the Lord will prepare a meeting house for them." I waited, and behold, after half an hour I saw two companies from the North, two from the West, and two from the South. As they arrived, they were introduced by the Angel of the trumpet into the prepared house, and there they took the seats assigned to them according to their home regions. There were six companies or cohorts; a seventh was from the East, which was not seen by the others because of its brilliant light. 

After the gathering, the Angel opened the reason for the summons and asked that the cohorts, in order, express their wisdom concerning **HEAVENLY JOY** and **ETERNAL HAPPINESS**. Then each cohort formed themselves into a circle, faces turned toward faces, so that they might recall that matter from the ideas they had formed in the former world, and now examine them, and after consultation, express what they had scrutinized.

732. After the consultation, the **FIRST COHORT**, which was from the North, said that Heavenly Joy and Eternal Happiness are one and the same as the life of Heaven itself. Therefore, anyone who enters Heaven enters into its festivities as far as their life is concerned, no differently than one who enters a wedding enters into its festivities. Is not Heaven before our sight above us, and thus in a specific place? And are there not there, and nowhere else, joys upon joys and pleasures upon pleasures? A person is brought into these regarding every perception of the mind and every sensation of the body, out of the fullness of the joys of that place, when they enter Heaven. Therefore, heavenly happiness, which is also eternal, is nothing other than admission into Heaven, and admission through Divine Grace. 

When these things were said, the **SECOND COHORT** from the North, out of its wisdom, expressed this prediction: "Heavenly Joy and Eternal Happiness are nothing other than the most cheerful company with Angels and the sweetest conversations with them. By these, faces are kept continually expanded in joy, and the mouths of the whole company are kept in pleasant laughter from charming talk and jokes. And what are heavenly joys but variations of such things forever?"

The **THIRD COHORT**, which was the first of the wise from the western region, produced this from the thoughts of their affections: "What is Heavenly Joy and Eternal Happiness but feasting with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob? At their tables there will be delicate and sumptuous foods, and generous and noble wines. After the feasts, there will be games and dances of virgins and youths dancing to the measures of symphonies and flutes, interspersed with the sweetest singing of odes. Finally, in the evening, there will be stage plays; and after these, feasting again, and so on every day forever."

**THE FIFTH COHORT**, which was the first of the ingenious groups from the Southern quarter, spoke thus: "Heavenly joys and eternal Happiness are nothing else than supreme lordships, most opulent treasures, and from these, a magnificence greater than royalty and a most illustrious splendor. That the joys of Heaven and their continual enjoyment, which is eternal happiness, consist of these things, we have perceived from those in the former world who possessed them; and furthermore, from the fact that the happy in Heaven are to reign with the Lord, and will be kings and princes, because they are His children, He who is the **King of kings and Lord of lords**. We have seen that they shall sit upon thrones, and that Angels shall minister to them. We have perceived the magnificence of Heaven from this: that the **New Jerusalem** <note>A reference to the vision in the Book of Revelation 21</note>, by which the glory of Heaven is described, is to have gates, each of which will be a single pearl, and streets of pure gold, and a wall founded upon precious stones. Consequently, everyone received into Heaven has his own palace gleaming with gold and precious things, and a lordship which shall succeed in order from one to another. And because we know that joys are innate in such things, and happiness is inherent in them, and that these are the irrefragable <note>unbreakable or undeniable</note> promises of God, we could not deduce the most happy state of heavenly life from anywhere else."

After this, **THE SIXTH COHORT**, which was the second from the Southern quarter, raised its voice and said, "The joy of Heaven and its Eternal happiness is nothing else than the perpetual Glorification of God, a festival lasting forever, and a most blessed worship with songs and shouts of joy; and thus a constant elevation of the heart to God, with full confidence of the acceptance of prayers and praises because of the Divine generosity of their blessedness." Some from this Cohort added that this Glorification would be accompanied by magnificent lights, and with the most fragrant incense, and with processions of great pomp, with a **High Priest** <note>original: "Pontifice maximo"</note> going before with a great Trumpet, followed by the Primates and Key-bearers <note>likely a reference to high-ranking church officials or "Clavigeris," those holding the keys of office</note>, both great and small, and after these, men with palms, and women with golden images in their hands.

733. **THE SEVENTH COHORT**, which because of its light was not seen by the rest, was from the East of Heaven; they were Angels from the same society as the Angel of the trumpet. When they heard in Heaven that not even one person in the Christian World knew what heavenly joy and eternal happiness were, they said among themselves, "This can by no means be the truth; such darkness and such stupor of mind cannot exist among Christians. Let us also descend and hear whether it be true, for if it is true, it is surely a prodigy <note>a marvel or a strange omen</note>." Then those Angels said to the Angel of the trumpet, "You know that every person who has desired Heaven, and has thought something certain about the joys there, is introduced after death into the joys of his own imagination; and that after they have experienced what those joys are like—that they are according to the vain ideas of the mind and the deliriums of their fantasy—they are led out of them and instructed. This happens to most in the **World of Spirits** <note>In Swedenborg's theology, the *Mundus Spirituum* is an intermediate state where people arrive immediately after death before being prepared for Heaven or Hell</note> who in their former life meditated on Heaven and reached some conclusion about the joys there, even to the point of desiring them." Having heard these things, the Angel of the trumpet said to the six Cohorts called together from the wise of the Christian World, "Follow me, and I will introduce you into your joys, and thus into Heaven."

After these things were said, the Angel led the way, and first he was accompanied by the **Cohort** <note>original: "Cohors"; here referring to a specific group of spirits sharing a common belief</note> of those who had persuaded themselves that **Heavenly Joys** were nothing but the most joyful company and the sweetest conversations. The Angel led this group to assemblies in the **Northern Region**, for whom the Joys of Heaven in the former world had been nothing else. There was a spacious House there in which such people were gathered; in the House were more than fifty rooms, divided according to various kinds of conversations. In these rooms they spoke of such things as they had seen and heard in the marketplace and in the streets; in others they spoke various pleasantries about the beautiful sex <note>a historical reference to women</note>, interspersed with jokes, increased until the faces of everyone in the company expanded into the laughter of merriment. In other rooms they spoke news of the Courts, of the Ministries, of the political State, and of various things which had emanated from secret Councils, together with reasonings and conjectures about future events; in others they spoke of Trade; in others of literary matters; in others of such things as belong to civil Prudence and moral Life; in others of Ecclesiastical matters and Sects, and so forth. It was granted to me to look into that House, and I saw people running from room to room, seeking out the company of their own affection and the joy resulting from it. And in these companies I saw three types: some as if panting to speak, some eager to inquire, and some greedy to listen.

There were four gates to the House, one on each side, and I observed that many were breaking away from their companies and hurrying to leave. I followed some to the Eastern gate and saw some sitting near it with sad faces; I approached and asked why they sat so sadly. They replied, "The gates of this house are kept closed for those wishing to exit, and it is now the third day since we entered. We have spent the life of our desire in company and conversation, and we are so exhausted by the continuous talking that we can hardly bear to hear the noisy murmur of it. Therefore, out of weariness, we have brought ourselves to this gate and knocked, but we were answered that the gates of this house are not opened to those exiting, but to those entering. 'Stay,' they say, 'and enjoy the joys of Heaven.' From these responses, we concluded that we are to remain here forever; thus sadness has invaded our minds, and now our chests begin to tighten and anxiety arises."

Then the Angel addressed them and said: "This state is the death of your joys, which you believed to be uniquely heavenly, when yet they are nothing but **accessories** to Heavenly things." And they asked the Angel, "What then is Heavenly Joy?" And the Angel replied with these few words: "It is the **delight of doing something that is of use** to oneself and others; and the delight of use <note>original: "jucundum usus"; a central concept in the author's theology, suggesting that true happiness comes from being productive and helpful</note> draws its essence from **Love** and its existence from **Wisdom**. The delight of use arising from Love through Wisdom is the soul and life of all Heavenly joys. There are indeed the most joyful social gatherings in the heavens, which exhilarate the minds of the Angels, delight their spirits, gladden their hearts, and recreate their bodies; but these come to them after they have performed uses in their functions and in their works. From these uses is the soul and life in all their joys and delights; but if you take away 그 soul or life, the accessory joys gradually cease to be joys—first they become indifferent, then worthless, and finally sad and anxious." When these things were said, the gate was opened, and those sitting there leaped out; they fled home, each to his own function and to his own work, and were refreshed.

After a short delay, all the tables appeared full of dishes, and the small spaces between them were decorated with little pyramids containing preserves. Those about to feast stood around them, waiting to see the heads of the tables; after waiting a little while, they were seen entering in a procession from Abraham down to the last of the Apostles. Soon, each one approached his own table and reclined on a couch at its head; then they said to those standing around, "Recline also with us." And the men sat down with those **Fathers** <note>original: "Patribus"; referring to the biblical patriarchs and apostles</note>, and the women with their wives, and they ate and drank with joy and with reverence. After dinner, those Fathers went out; and then games were organized, dances of young women and men, and after these, spectacles. When these were finished, they were invited again to the Feasts, but with a fixed rule: on the first day they would eat with Abraham, on the second with Isaac, on the third with Jacob, on the fourth with Peter, on the fifth with James, on the sixth with John, on the seventh with Paul, and with the rest in order until the fifteenth day, from which they would renew the banquets in a similar order by changing seats, and so on forever.

After this, the Angel called the men of the group together and said to them: "All these whom you saw at the tables were once in a similar imaginary thought about the **Joys of Heaven** and the resulting **Eternal Happiness** as you were. For the purpose that they themselves might see the emptiness of their own ideas and be led away from them, such feasting scenes were established and permitted by the **Lord**. Those leading figures whom you saw at the heads of the tables were actors playing old men, most of them from a rural class, who, being bearded and somewhat arrogant due to a certain wealth, had the fantasy induced upon them that they were those ancient Fathers. But follow me into the exit paths from this arena." 

They followed, and they saw fifty here and fifty there who had stuffed their bellies with food to the point of nausea, and they longed to return to the familiarity of their homes—some to their duties, some to their businesses, and some to their manual labor. But many were held back by the guards of the grove and asked about their days of feasting, and whether they had yet eaten at the tables with Peter and Paul; they were told that if they left early, it would be a cause of shame for them because it is unseemly. But most answered: "We have filled up on our joys; the food has become tasteless to us, our taste is parched, our stomachs loathe it, we cannot bear to taste it. We have dragged through several days and nights in that luxury; we urgently beg to be let out." Having been dismissed, they fled home with gasping breath and a hurried pace.

After this, the Angel called the men of the group and on the way taught them these things about Heaven: "In Heaven, just as in the world, there are Foods and Drinks, there are Banquets and Feasts. Among the Leaders there, there are Tables upon which are rich dishes, delicacies, and elegancies, by which their spirits are cheered and refreshed. There are also Games and Spectacles, and there are Musical performances and Songs; and all these are in the highest perfection. Such things are also for their joy, but not for their happiness. Happiness must be *within* the joys, and thus *from* the joys. Happiness within joys makes them to be truly joys; it enriches them and sustains them so they do not become cheap or disgusting. And this happiness comes to everyone from the <term>use</term> <note>original: "usus"; a central concept in Swedenborg's thought, meaning the useful function or service a person performs for others</note> in their own function. There is a certain vein latent in the affection of the will of every Angel which draws the mind toward doing something; through this, the mind calms and satisfies itself. This satisfaction and that tranquility make the state of the mind receptive to the **love of use** from the Lord. From the reception of this comes **Heavenly Happiness**, which is the life of those joys mentioned before. Heavenly Food in its essence is nothing other than love, wisdom, and use together—that is, use through wisdom from love. Therefore, food for the body is given to everyone in Heaven according to the use they perform: magnificent to those who are in eminent use, modest but of exquisite flavor to those in middle-degree use, and cheap to those in low use, but none to the lazy."

Stay a little while and prepare yourselves, because the older among you will be Kings, and the younger will be Princes." After these words, a Throne appeared next to every Column, and on the throne a silk robe, and on the robe a sceptre and a crown. And next to every Pyramid appeared a seat raised three cubits from the ground, and on the seat a chain made of gold links and sashes of the equestrian order, fastened at the ends with diamond-encrusted rings. Then it was shouted: "Go now, clothe yourselves, sit and wait!" Immediately the older ones ran to the thrones, and the younger ones to the seats, and they clothed themselves and sat down. 

But then there appeared something like a mist <note>original: "nimbus"</note> ascending from below, and when this was inhaled, those sitting on the thrones and seats began to swell in the face, to be puffed up in the chest, and to be filled with confidence that they were now kings and princes. That mist was the aura of fantasy with which they were inspired. Suddenly, young men flew down as if from Heaven and stood—two behind every throne and one behind every seat—to serve them. Then, in turns, a herald cried out, "You kings and princes, wait yet a little longer; your halls are now being prepared in Heaven; the courtiers with their guards will arrive any moment to lead you in." They waited and waited, until their spirits panted and they were worn out with longing.

After three hours, the Heaven above their heads was opened, and Angels descended. Pitying them, they said, "Why do you sit here so foolishly, acting like stage players? They have played tricks on you and turned you from men into idols, because you let it into your hearts that you were to reign with Christ like kings and princes, and that Angels would then serve you. Have you forgotten the Lord’s words, that in Heaven, he who wishes to be great must become a servant? Learn, therefore, what is meant by 'kings' and 'princes,' and what it means to 'reign with Christ': it is to be wise and to perform **uses** <note>original: "usus"; a technical term in this theology referring to useful services or productive actions performed for the sake of the neighbor and society</note>. For the Kingdom of Christ, which is Heaven, is a Kingdom of Uses. For the Lord loves everyone, and from that love He wills good for everyone; and 'good' is 'use.' 

Because the Lord performs good things or uses through the mediation of angels, and in the World through men, He therefore gives the love of use and its reward—which is internal blessedness and eternal happiness—to those who faithfully perform uses. There are, in the Heavens just as on earth, supreme Dominions and very wealthy Treasuries; there are governments and forms of government, and therefore there are greater and lesser powers and dignities. Those who are in the highest positions have Palaces and Courts which exceed the palaces and courts of Emperors and Kings on earth in magnificence and splendor; and from the number of courtiers, ministers, and guards, and from their magnificent garments, honor and glory surround them. But those Supreme ones are chosen from those whose heart is in the public welfare, and who only perceive the grandeur of magnificence through their physical senses for the sake of obedience. And because it belongs to the public welfare that everyone should be of some use in society, as in a common body, and because every use is from the Lord and is done through angels and men as if by them, it is clear that this is what it means to reign with the Lord." Having heard these things from Heaven, those masked kings and princes descended from their thrones and seats, and threw away their sceptres, crowns, and robes; and the mist, in which the aura of fantasy had been, receded from them, and a white cloud enveloped them, in which was the aura of wisdom, from which health returned to their minds.

To these he said, "Follow me, and I will lead you into Paradise, your Heaven, so that you may begin the blessedness of your eternal happiness."

After they entered, he led them through winding paths from one region to another. At the first entrance to Heaven, there was actually a Paradise, into which those people are admitted who believed while in the world that the entire Heaven is a single Paradise because it is called "Paradise." These were people who had impressed upon themselves the idea that after death there is a total rest from labors, and that this rest is nothing other than drawing in breaths of delight, walking upon roses, being gladdened by the most delicate juices <note>original: "mustis"; young wine or unfermented juice</note> of grapes, and celebrating festive receptions; they believed this life is only given in a Heavenly Paradise.

Led by the Angel, they saw a huge multitude of both old and young, as well as children, and also women and girls. They were sitting in groups of three and groups of ten <note>original: "triades & triades, ac decades & decades"</note> upon rose-beds, weaving garlands to decorate the heads of the old men, the arms of the young men, and the chests of the children in bundles. Others were squeezing juice from grapes, cherries, and berries into cups and drinking convivially. Others were inhaling the fragrances exhaled and scattered around from flowers, fruits, and scented leaves. Others were singing sweet songs that soothed the ears of those present. Others sat at fountains, directing the water from the gushing springs into various shapes. Others were walking, chatting, and sharing witty jokes. Still others were entering little garden houses to lie down on couches—among many other paradise-like joys.

After these things were seen, the Angel led his companions through various circuits here and there, and finally to those sitting in a most beautiful rose-grove surrounded by olive, orange, and lemon trees. These people were shaking their heads and holding their hands against their cheeks, mourning and weeping. The Angel's companions spoke to them and asked, "Why do you sit like this?"

And they replied, "It is now the seventh day since we came into this Paradise. When we entered, our minds seemed as if they were elevated into Heaven and admitted into its innermost auspicious joys. But after three days, those joys began to grow dull and to be erased from our minds; they became imperceptible and thus vanished. Since our imaginary joys have expired in this way, we feared the loss of all the sweetness of our lives, and we became uncertain whether any eternal happiness even exists. Afterward, we wandered through the streets and open spaces seeking the gate through which we entered. But we wandered in circles and circles, and we asked those we met; some of them said that the gate cannot be found, because this Paradise-garden is a spacious Labyrinth of such a nature that anyone who wishes to go out actually goes deeper in. Therefore, you cannot help but stay here forever; you are in the middle of it, where all delights are at their center."

They said further to the Angel's companions, "We have now sat here for a day and a half, and because we are without hope of finding an exit, we have rested ourselves upon this rose-bed and we look around us at the abundance of olives, grapes, oranges, and lemons. But the more we look at them, the more the sight is exhausted by seeing, the smell by smelling, and the taste by tasting. This is the cause of the sadness, mourning, and weeping in which you see us."

Hearing this, the Angel of the group said to them, "This Paradise-Labyrinth is truly the entrance to Heaven; I know the way out, and I will lead you forth." After he said this, those who were sitting rose up and embraced the Angel, following him along with his group. On the way, the Angel taught them what Heavenly Joy and the resulting Eternal Happiness actually are: they are not external paradise-delights unless internal paradise-delights are within them at the same time. External paradise-delights are merely delights of the bodily senses, but internal paradise-delights are delights of the soul’s affections. Unless the latter are within the former, there is no heavenly life, because there is no soul in them. Every delight without its corresponding soul fades and grows numb from continued use, and it exhausts the mind more than labor does. There are Paradise gardens everywhere in the Heavens, and from these the Angels also have joys; and to the extent that the delight of the soul is within them, those joys are truly joys to them.

Hearing this, they all asked: "What is the delight of the soul, and where does it come from?" The Angel replied, "The delight of the soul comes from love and wisdom from the Lord; and because love is the efficient cause <note>the fundamental force that produces an effect</note>, and it acts through wisdom, therefore it belongs to both..."

**738.** After this, the leading Angel returned to the House to those who had firmly persuaded themselves that heavenly joy and eternal happiness consist in the *perpetual glorification of God* and a festival continuing forever. This was because they had believed while in the world that they would then see God, and because the life of heaven is called a "perpetual Sabbath" due to the worship of God. To these, the Angel said, "Follow me, and I will lead you into your joy." 

He led them into a small city, in the middle of which was a Temple, and all the houses were called "sacred buildings." In that city, they saw a great many people from every corner of the surrounding land, and among them a number of Priests who received the newcomers, greeted them, and taking them by the hand, led them to the gates of the Temple. From there, they were led into buildings around the Temple and initiated into the perpetual worship of God. The Priests told them that this city was the courtyard to Heaven, and that the Temple of this city was the entrance to the magnificent and most spacious Temple in Heaven, where God is glorified by Angels with prayers and praises forever. 

The rules established here and there were that they must first enter the Temple and remain there for three days and three nights, and after this initiation, they were to enter the houses of this city—which are just as many sanctified buildings for us—and move from house to house, and in communion with those gathered there, they were to pray, cry out, and recite sermons <note>original: "concionata"; refers to preached material or formal sermons.</note>. They were warned: "Be entirely careful that you think of nothing else within yourselves, and speak with your associates of nothing other than holy, pious, and religious things."

After this, the Angel led his company into the Temple, which was full and packed with many who had held great dignity in the world, as well as many from the common people. Guards <note>original: "præsidia"</note> were placed at the gates so that no one was allowed to leave before the three-day stay was completed. The Angel said, "Today is the second day since these people entered; observe them, and you will see their 'glorification of God.'" 

And they observed them, and saw many sleeping; and those who were awake were yawning and yawning. Some—because of the continual lifting of their thoughts to God without any return of those thoughts to the body—appeared to have faces detached from their bodies (for so they appeared to themselves, and thus to others). Others had a wild look in their eyes <note>original: "deliros oculis"</note> from the perpetual withdrawal of their sight. In a word, all felt a tightness in the chest and were weary in spirit from boredom; they turned away from the pulpit and cried out: "Our ears are stunned! End the sermons! The voice is heard no longer, and the sound begins to be loathsome!" 

And then they rose up and ran in a mass to the gates, broke them open, pressed against the guards, and drove them away. Seeing this, the Priests followed them, staying by their sides, teaching and teaching, praying, and sighing, saying: "Celebrate the Festival! Glorify God! Sanctify yourselves! In this courtyard of Heaven, we will inaugurate you into the eternal Glorification of God in the magnificent and most spacious Temple in Heaven, and thus to the enjoyment of eternal happiness!" 

But these words were not understood and barely heard by the people because of the mental dullness caused by two days of mental suspension and being kept away from domestic and public affairs. When they tried to pull themselves away from the Priests, the priests grabbed their arms and their clothes, urging them toward the buildings where sermons were being recited—but in vain. The people cried out, "Leave us alone! We feel in our bodies as if we are fainting!" 

As they said this, behold, four Men appeared in white robes and miters <note>A miter is a type of tall, peaked hat worn by high-ranking church officials.</note>. One of them had been an Archbishop in the world, and the three others had been Bishops, and they had now become Angels. These called the Priests together and, addressing them, said: "We have seen you from Heaven with these sheep; how you pasture them! You pasture them until they go insane! You do not know what is meant by the 'Glorification of God.' It means to bear the fruit of love—that is, to faithfully, sincerely, and diligently do the work of one’s function <note>original: "functionis opus"; the specific duty or job one has in society.</note>..."

> *In this MY FATHER IS GLORIFIED, that you bear much fruit, and become my disciples*, John 15:8.
You Priests can be engaged in the glorification of worship, because this is your office, and from it you receive honor, glory, and remuneration; but nonetheless, you cannot be in that glorification more than others unless honor, glory, and remuneration are joined with your duty. After these words were spoken, the Bishops commanded the gatekeepers to let everyone in and let everyone out; for there is a great multitude who could think of no other heavenly joy than the perpetual worship of God, because they knew nothing of the actual state of Heaven.

**739.** After this, the Angel with his companions returned to the place of assembly, from which the groups of Wise Men had not yet departed. There he called to himself those who believed that heavenly joy and eternal happiness consist merely in being let into Heaven, and that this admission is by Divine grace alone; and that once inside, joy would come to them just as it does in the world to those who enter the courts of Kings on festival days or are invited to weddings. To these the Angel said, "Stay here for a little while, and I will sound the trumpet, and there will come here men famous for their reputation of wisdom in the spiritual matters of the Church." After a few hours, nine men were present, each marked with laurel, the honor of their fame. The Angel led these into the Assembly House where all those previously called were present. In their presence, the Angel spoke to the nine laurel-crowned men, saying, "I know that according to your wish and your idea, it was granted to you to ascend into Heaven, and that you have returned to this lower or sub-heavenly earth with full knowledge of the state of Heaven. Tell us, therefore, how Heaven appeared to you."

And they answered in order. The **FIRST** said: "My idea of Heaven from my earliest childhood until the end of my life in the world was that it was a place of all blessedness, favors, delights, charms, and pleasures; and that if I were let in, I would be surrounded by an atmosphere of such happiness and would breathe it in with a full chest, just like a bridegroom when he celebrates his nuptials and enters the bedchamber with his bride. In this idea I ascended into Heaven, and I passed the first guards and also the second; but when I came to the third, the captain of the guards spoke to me and said, 'Who are you, friend?' and I answered, 'Is this not Heaven? I have ascended here according to my heart’s desire; let me in, I pray.' And he let me in. And I saw Angels in white garments, and they surrounded me and inspected me, and they murmured this: 'Look at this new guest, not clothed in the garment of Heaven.' I heard this and thought, 'This seems to me like the man of whom the Lord says that he entered into the wedding without a wedding garment' <note>A reference to the parable in Matthew 22:11–13, where a guest is cast out for not wearing the proper spiritual "attire."</note>. And I said, 'Give me such garments'; but they laughed. And then someone ran from the Court with a command: 'Strip him naked, cast him out, and throw his clothes after him.' And so I was cast out."

The **SECOND** in order said: "I believed as he did, that if I were only let into the Heaven that is above my head, joys would flow around me and I would breathe them forever. I even obtained my wish; but the Angels, seeing me, fled away and said among themselves, 'What is this monster? How did this *night bird* <note>original: "Avis noctis." In this context, it implies an owl or a creature that cannot stand the light of spiritual truth.</note> get here?' And I actually felt a change from being a human, even though I was not changed; this happened to me from the attraction of the heavenly atmosphere. But soon someone ran from the Court with a command that two servants should lead me out and conduct me back by the way I ascended, all the way to my house; and when I was at home, I appeared to others and to myself as a man again."

The **THIRD** said: "My idea of Heaven was always based on a place and not on love; therefore when I came into this world, I longed for Heaven with a great desire. I saw people ascending and I followed them, and I was admitted, but not beyond a few paces. But when I wanted to gladden my soul from the idea of the joys and blessedness there, from the light of Heaven (which was white as snow, the essence of which is said to be wisdom), a stupor seized my mind, and from that a darkness came over my eyes, and I began to lose my wits. And soon, from the heat of Heaven (which corresponded to the brightness of that light)...

At this he laughed and ascended, believing, like others, that everyone in the entire world was capable of receiving the joys there in their fullness. "But truly," he said, "when I was inside, I was almost deprived of life; and from the pain and resulting torture in my head and body, I prostrated myself on the ground and writhed like a snake moved near a fire, and I crawled even to the edge of a precipice and threw myself off. Afterward, I was picked up by those standing below and carried to an inn, where my health returned to me." **THE REMAINING FIVE** also told wonders about their ascents into Heaven; they compared the changes in the states of their life to the state of fish when they are lifted from the waters into the air, and to the state of birds in the <term>ether</term><note>Here referring to the highest, thinnest part of the atmosphere where life cannot be sustained.</note>. They said that after those hard misfortunes, they no longer desired Heaven, but only a life in company with their own kind, wherever they might be; and that they now know that in the World of Spirits, where we are, all are first prepared—the good for Heaven and the evil for Hell—and that when they are prepared, they see ways opened for them to the <term>Societies</term><note>The various communities or groups of angels or spirits who share similar affections and beliefs.</note> of those like themselves, with whom they are to remain forever; and that they then enter these ways with delight, because these are the ways of their own love. All those from the first assembly, hearing these things, also confessed that they had no other idea of Heaven than as a place where, with open mouths, they would swallow down surrounding joys forever.

After this, the Angel of the trumpet said to them: "You see now that the joys of Heaven and eternal happiness are not matters of place, but are <term>states of life</term><note>A central theme in this theology: that one's environment in the afterlife is an outward reflection of their internal spiritual condition.</note> of the human being. The state of heavenly life is from love and wisdom; and because <term>use</term><note>The performance of useful functions or service to others.</note> is the container of those two, the state of heavenly life is from their conjunction in use. It is the same if we say Charity, Faith, and Good Works; for Charity is Love, Faith is Truth from which comes Wisdom, and Good Work is Use. Furthermore, in our Spiritual World there are places just as in the natural world, otherwise there would be no habitations and distinct dwellings; yet there, place is not place, but is the appearance of place according to the state of love and wisdom, or charity and faith. Everyone who becomes an angel carries his own heaven within himself, because he carries the love of his own Heaven; for man from creation is a miniature <term>effigy</term><note>A representation or image.</note>, image, and type of the Great Heaven; the human form is nothing else. Therefore, everyone comes into that society of Heaven whose form he is in his own individual image; for this reason, when he enters into 그 society, he enters into a form corresponding to himself, so that he enters as if from himself into it, and as if from it into the heaven within himself, and he draws its life as his own, and his own as its. Every society is like a Common Whole, and the Angels there are like similar parts from which the Common Whole exists together. From these things it now follows, that those who are in evils and the resulting falsities have formed within themselves an image of Hell, and this image is tortured in Heaven by the influx and the violence of the activity of one opposite against another; for infernal love is opposite to heavenly love, and therefore the delights of those two loves collide with each other like enemies, and kill each other when they meet."

Ten were chosen and followed the Angel. Go with my escort, and tell them that their arrival is welcome to me, and lead them into my antechamber, and assign to each his own room with its bedchamber; and from my courtiers choose some, and from the servants some who may wait upon them, and who may serve them at their beck and call; and it was done so. When they were brought to the Palace, they first saw it from the outside; it was vast, built of <term>porphyry</term><note>A hard, reddish-purple igneous rock, historically associated with royalty and imperial dignity.</note>, and the foundation was of jasper, and before the gate were six tall columns of lapis lazuli, the roof was of plates of gold, the windows high and of the clearest crystal, their posts also of gold. After this, they were led inside the Palace, and taken from room to room, and they saw ornaments of ineffable beauty, and under the ceilings, decorative carvings of inimitable skill; near the walls were placed tables of silver fused with gold, upon which were various utensils made of precious stones, and of entire gems in celestial forms; and more things, such as no eye on earth had ever seen, and therefore no one could have brought himself to believe that such things exist in Heaven. While they were in a state of wonder at these magnificent sights, the Angel said, "Do not marvel; these things which you see were not made or manufactured by any angelic hand, but were created by the <term>Artisan of the Universe</term><note>original: "Opifice Universi"; a term for God as the supreme architect and creator.</note>, and given as a gift to our Prince; therefore, here is the art of architecture in its very essence, and from this are derived all the rules of this art in the World." Furthermore, the Angel said, "You might imagine that such things would fascinate our eyes and infatuate them, even to the point that we believe them to be the joys of our Heaven; but because our hearts are not in them, they are merely accessories to the joys of our hearts; therefore, as much as we contemplate them as accessories, and as the handiwork of God, so much do we contemplate the Divine Omnipotence and Mercy in them."

741. After this the Angel said to them, "It is not yet Noon of the day; come with me into our Prince’s Garden, which is adjacent to this Palace." This is not a Garden; we see only one Tree, and on its branches and at its top there are fruits as if of gold, and leaves as if of silver, and their edges adorned with emeralds; and under that Tree are infants with their tutors." To this the Angel, with an inspired voice, said, "This Tree is in the middle of the Garden, and is called by us the Tree of our Heaven, and by some the <term>Tree of Life</term>. But go on, and draw near, and your eyes will be opened, and you will see the Garden." And they did so, and their eyes were opened, and they saw trees most productive with flavorful fruits, entwined with leafy vines, whose tops with their fruits nodded toward the Tree of Life in the center. The beginning of the circulation was separated from the Tree in the center by a significant interval, and that interval sparkled with a beam of light, from which the trees of the spiral shone with a successive and continuous splendor from the first to the last. The first trees were the most excellent of all, luxuriant with rich fruits, called <term>Paradise trees</term><note>original: "Paradisiacæ"; trees specifically of a heavenly or Edenic nature.</note>, never seen because they are not given nor capable of being given in the lands of the natural World; after these followed oil trees <note>olive trees</note>; after these, wine trees <note>vines</note>; after these, fragrance trees; and lastly, trees of wood useful for building. Here and there in this arboreal Spiral or in this circle were seats formed from the drawn-together and intertwined branches of the trees from behind, and enriched and adorned with their fruits. In that perpetual arboreal Circle were gates which opened into flower-beds, and from these into lawns, divided into plots and borders. When the Angel's companions saw these things, they exclaimed, "Behold, Heaven in form! Wherever we turn the sight of our eyes, something of Hea—"

After they were half-satisfied with the meal, the Prince addressed the ten guests and said: "I have heard that in the world beneath this Heaven, you were called together to reveal your thoughts concerning the **Joys of Heaven** and the **Eternal Happiness** resulting from them, and that you expressed these in various ways, each according to the delights of his own bodily senses. But what are the delights of the bodily senses without the delights of the soul? It is the soul that makes those things delightful. The delights of the soul in themselves are imperceptible blessings, but they become more and more perceptible as they descend into the thoughts of the mind, and from these into the sensations of the body. In the thoughts of the mind, they are perceived as happiness; in the sensations of the body, as delights; and in the body itself, as pleasures. From all of these together comes **Eternal Happiness**. But from the latter alone, that happiness is not eternal but temporary, which ends and passes away, and sometimes turns into unhappiness. You have now seen that all your joys are also the joys of heaven, even more excellent than you could ever have imagined; yet even these do not affect our minds from the inside. There are three things which flow as one from the Lord into our souls; these three as one, or this <term>trinity</term><note>Latin: "trinum." In this theological context, it refers to a three-fold unity of attributes.</note>, are **love, wisdom, and use**. However, love and wisdom do not exist except ideally, because they exist only in the affection and thought of the mind; but in **use** they exist really, because they are simultaneously in the act and work of the body. Where they exist really, there they also subsist. And because love and wisdom exist and subsist in use, it is use that affects us; and <term>use</term><note>A technical term in this work meaning the practical application of one's talents and duties for the benefit of others or society.</note> is to faithfully, sincerely, and diligently perform the works of one's own office. The love of use, and the resulting devotion to use, keeps the mind from drifting and wandering about, and from drinking in all the lusts which flow in from the body and the world through the senses with their allurements, by which true Religion and true Morality, with their goods, are scattered to the four winds. But the devotion of the mind to use contains and collects these, and disposes the mind into a form receptive of wisdom from those truths; and then it banishes the mockeries and trifles of both falsehoods and vanities to the sidelines. But you shall hear more on these matters from the wise men of our Society, whom I shall send to you this afternoon." Having said these things, the Prince rose, and with him his guests; he spoke a word of peace and commanded the Angel who was their leader to lead them back to their rooms and show them all the honors of courtesy; and also to call men of refinement and affability to entertain them with conversation about the various joys of this Society.

745\. When they had returned, it was done as commanded, and those called from the city to entertain them with conversation about the various joys of the Society arrived. After greetings, they spoke of elegant matters as they walked together. But the Angel, their leader, said: "These ten men have been invited into this Heaven to see its Joys and thereby receive a new idea of Eternal Happiness; tell them, therefore, something of its joys that affect the senses of the body; later, the Wise Men are coming, who will mention the things that make those joys blessed and happy." Hearing this, those called from the city related the following: "There are days of festivity appointed here by the Prince, so that minds may be relaxed from the exhaustion which the desire of competition had brought upon some. On these days, there are musical harmonies and songs in the public squares, and outside the city, there are games and spectacles. In the squares, there are then elevated orchestras surrounded by railings entwined with vines, from which clusters of grapes hang; within these, on three levels, sit the Musicians with stringed instruments and wind instruments, of high voice and low voice, of strong voice and soft voice; and at the sides are male and female singers, who delight the citizens with the most pleasant shouts of joy and songs, both in chorus and solo, varied in kind at intervals. These activities continue there on those festive days from morning until noon, and from then until evening. 2. Furthermore, every morning, from the houses around the squares, the sweetest songs of virgins and girls are heard, with which the whole city rings. It is a certain affection of spiritual love which is sung every morning—that is, it is sounded through the modifications of a musical voice or melodies—and that affection is perceived in the song as if it were the affection itself; it flows into the souls of the listeners and stirs them to a corresponding state. Such is heavenly song. 3. At noon, the doors are opened, and after noon sometimes the windows as well, and one can see the games of boys and girls in the streets, with their tutors and masters moderating them while sitting in the porches of the houses. 

4. At the edges of the city in its outskirts, there are various games for boys and youths; there are running games, and ball games; there are games with struck ball-clubs called **rachets** <note>original: "rachets." This refers to an early form of rackets or tennis.</note>; there are wrestling matches among the boys to see who is more energetic and who is slower in speaking, acting, and perceiving; and for those who are more energetic, some laurel leaves are given as a prize; besides many other things which excite the abilities lying hidden in the boys. 

5. Furthermore, outside the city are the **Theatrical Spectacles** of comedians upon stages, representing various honors and virtues of the moral life. Among them are also actors included for the sake of **relatives** <note>In this philosophical context, "relatives" refers to things defined by their relationship to their opposites or variations in degree.</note>; and one of the ten visitors asked what was meant by "for the sake of relatives," and they replied: "No virtue, with its honors and graces, can be presented to the life except through relatives, from the greatest of them to the least. The actors represent the smallest degrees of these until they become nothing; but it is sanctioned by law that they may not exhibit anything of the opposite—which is called dishonorable and unbecoming—except figuratively and as if from a distance." The reason this is sanctioned is because no honor or good of any virtue passes through successive steps into what is dishonorable and evil; rather, it passes to its own minimum until it perishes, and only when it perishes does the opposite begin. Therefore **Heaven**, where all things are honorable and good, has nothing in common with **hell**, where all things are dishonorable and evil.

746. While they were talking, a servant ran up and announced that eight **Sages** <note>Wise men or scholars.</note> were present by the Prince’s command and wished to enter. Hearing this, the Angel went out, received them, and led them in. Soon the Sages, after the solemnities and courtesies of social meeting, spoke first with them about the beginnings and increases of wisdom, mixing in various things about its progress, and how wisdom among angels never reaches an end or ceases, but grows and increases forever. Hearing this, the Angel of the group said to them: "Our Prince at the table spoke with these guests about the **seat of wisdom**, saying that it is in **use** <note>In Swedenborgian theology, "use" refers to performing helpful service or functions for the sake of others and the Lord.</note>; speak, if you please, with them about that as well." 

And they said: "Man, when first created, was imbued with wisdom and the love of it, not for his own sake, but for the sake of communicating it with others. From this, it is inscribed in the wisdom of the wise that no one should be wise or live for himself alone, but for others at the same time. From this comes **Society**, which otherwise would not exist. To live for others is to perform **uses**. Uses are its bonds, which are as many as there are good uses, and uses are infinite in number. 
* There are **spiritual uses**, which belong to love for God and love toward the neighbor; 
* there are **moral and civil uses**, which belong to the love of the society and the state in which a person is, and of the companions and citizens with whom he lives; 
* there are **natural uses**, which belong to the love of the world and its necessities; 
* and there are **corporeal uses**, which belong to the love of self-preservation for the sake of higher uses. 

All these uses are inscribed on man, and follow in order, one after another, and when they exist together, one is within the other. Those who are in the first uses, which are spiritual, are also in those that follow, and these are the truly wise. However, those who are not in the first, yet are in the second and the following, are not so wise, but only appear so from external morality and civility. Those who are not in the first and second, but are in the third and fourth, are anything but wise, for they are <term>satans</term><note>In this system, "satans" are those who love the world and false reasoning, whereas "devils" are those who love themselves above all.</note>, for they love only the world, and themselves for the sake of the world. But those who are only in the fourth are the least wise of all, for they are **devils**, because they live for themselves alone, and if they do anything for others, it is solely for their own sake. Furthermore, every love has its own delight, for love lives through this; and the delight of the love of uses is a **heavenly delight**, which enters the following delights in order, and according to the order of succession, exalts them and makes them eternal." After this, they enumerated the **Heavenly Delights** proceeding from the love of use...

But around evening, a messenger clothed in linen came to the ten visitor companions of the Angel and invited them to the Wedding to be celebrated the following day; and the visitors were greatly delighted that they were also to see a wedding in Heaven. After this, they were led to a certain Counselor at the side and dined with him; after dinner, they returned and retired from each other, each to his own bedroom, and slept until morning. When they awakened, they heard the Singing of virgins and girls from the houses around the Market mentioned above; at that time, the affection of conjugial love <term>conjugial love</term><note>A central term in Swedenborg’s theology, referring to the spiritual, eternal union of a husband and wife that continues in the afterlife.</note> was being sung. By the sweetness of the song, they were deeply affected and stirred, perceiving a blessed pleasantness inherent in their joys, which elevated and renewed them. When it was time, the Angel said, "Gird yourselves, and put on the garments of Heaven which our Prince has sent to you." They put them on, and behold, the garments shone as if from a flaming light; they asked the Angel why this was, and he replied, "Because you are going to a wedding; among us, garments then shine and become wedding-garments."

747. After this, the Angel led them to the House of the wedding, and the doorkeeper opened the doors. Soon, having been received within the threshold and greeted by an Angel sent by the Bridegroom, they were introduced and led to the seats designated for them. Soon they were invited into the Antechamber <term>antithalamus</term><note>The room preceding the bridal chamber; a foyer for the ceremony.</note>, where they saw in the middle a Table upon which was placed a magnificent Lampstand equipped with seven branches and bowls of gold; on the walls hung silver lamps. Once these were lit, the atmosphere appeared like gold. They saw at the sides of the Lampstand two Tables upon which Bread was placed in a triple row, and at the four corners were Tables upon which stood crystal Cups. While they were examining these, behold, the door from the room next to the bridal chamber was opened, and they saw six Virgins coming out, and after them the Bridegroom and Bride, holding each other by the hands. They led each other to the Throne, which was placed opposite the Lampstand, upon which they seated themselves—the Bridegroom on the left and the Bride on his right—and the six virgins took their places at the side of the throne next to the Bride. The Bridegroom was clothed in a Mantle of glowing purple and a Tunic of shining fine linen, with an Ephod <note>A ceremonial vestment, originally worn by ancient Hebrew priests.</note> upon which was a golden plate surrounded by diamonds; on the plate was engraved a Young eagle, the wedding emblem of this heavenly society. A miter <note>original: "cidaris," a form of turban or priestly headdress.</note> covered the Bridegroom's head. The Bride, however, was clothed in a scarlet cloak, and under it an embroidered gown, continuous from the neck to the feet; under the breast was a golden sash, and on her head a crown of gold set with rubies. When they were thus seated, the Bridegroom turned to the Bride and placed a golden ring on her finger; he then took out bracelets and a necklace of pearls, fastening the bracelets on her wrists <note>original: "poplites manuum," literally 'the knees of the hands,' referring to the joints of the wrists.</note> and the necklace around her neck, and said, "Receive these pledges." While she received them, he kissed her and said, "Now you are mine," and called her his wife. This being done, those invited shouted, "May there be a Blessing!" Each shouted this by himself, and then all together. One sent by the Prince in his stead also acclaimed it; at that moment, the Antechamber was filled with that aromatic smoke which was a sign of blessing from heaven. Then the attendants took the Bread from the two tables next to the Lampstand, and from the tables in the corners the Cups, now filled with wine, and gave to each guest his own bread and his own cup, and they ate and drank. After this, the Husband and his Wife rose up, with the six virgins following with silver lamps now lit in their hands, even to the threshold; the Couple entered the Bridal Chamber, and the door was closed.

748. Afterward, the Angel guide spoke with the guests about his ten companions, saying that by command he had introduced them and shown them the magnificent things of the Prince’s Palace and the wonders there, and that they had feasted at the table with him; and that afterward they had spoken with our Wise Men. He asked that they might also be allowed to join in some conversation with you; and they approached and conversed. One wise man from among the men...

[he] spoke of the wedding, [asking] "Do you understand what those things you have seen signify?" They said, "Only a little." Then they asked him why the Groom, now the Husband, was in such attire. He responded that the Groom, now the Husband, represented the Lord, and the Bride, now the Wife, represented the Church, because Weddings in Heaven represent the Marriage of the Lord with the Church. This is why a Mitre <note>original: "Cidaris," a ceremonial headdress</note> was upon his head, and he was clothed in a cloak, a tunic, and an ephod <term>ephod</term><note>An ornate vestment worn by the high priest in ancient Israel.</note>, just like Aaron; and why upon the head of the Bride, now the Wife, was a Crown, and she was clothed in a Robe <note>original: "Chlamyde," a Greek-style mantle</note> like a Queen. "But tomorrow," he added, "they will be dressed differently, because this Representation lasts only for today." They asked again, since He represented the Lord and She represented the Church, why She sat at His right hand. The wise man responded, "Because there are two things that make the Marriage of the Lord and the Church: Love and Wisdom. The Lord is Love, and the Church is Wisdom, and Wisdom is at the right hand of love; for the person of the Church is wise as if of themselves, and as they become wise, they receive love from the Lord. The right hand also signifies power, and love has its power through wisdom. But as was said, after the wedding the representation is changed, for then the Husband represents Wisdom, and the wife represents the Love of his wisdom. Truly, this Love is not the prior love, but is a secondary love, which is from the Lord to the wife through the wisdom of the husband. The love of the Lord, which is the prior love, is the love of being wise within the husband; therefore after the wedding, both together, the husband and his wife, represent the Church." They asked once more, "Why did you men not stand at the side of the Groom, now the Husband, just as the six Virgins stood at the side of the Bride, now the Wife?" The wise man responded, "The reason is that today we are numbered among the virgins, and the number six signifies all and completeness." But they said, "What does this mean?" He replied, "Virgins signify the Church, and the Church consists of both sexes; therefore even we, as far as the Church is concerned, are Virgins. That this is so is evident from these words in the Revelation: '*These are they who have not been defiled with women, for they are VIRGINS, and they follow the Lamb wherever He goes*' (Chapter 14:4). And because Virgins signify the Church, the Lord *likened it to ten VIRGINS invited to a wedding* (Matthew Chapter 25:1 <note>The text incorrectly cites Chapter 24.</note>). And because the Church is signified by Israel, Zion, and Jerusalem, it is so often called in the Word the VIRGIN and DAUGHTER OF ISRAEL, OF ZION, and OF JERUSALEM. The Lord also describes His Marriage with the Church with these words in David: 'THE QUEEN AT YOUR RIGHT HAND IN THE BEST GOLD OF OPHIR, *in her clothing of interwoven gold, she shall be brought to the King* IN EMBROIDERY; THE VIRGINS HER COMPANIONS WHO FOLLOW HER *shall come into the King’s palace*' (Psalm 45:10 to 16)." Afterward they said, "Is it not appropriate that some Priest be present and minister in these things?" The wise man responded, "This is appropriate on earth, but not in the heavens, because of the representation of the Lord Himself and the Church. This they do not know on earth. Yet among us, a Priest still administers the Betrothals, and hears, receives, confirms, and consecrates the Consent. Consent is the essential of marriage, and the other things that follow are its formalities."

749. After this, the guiding Angel approached the six Virgins and told them about his companions, asking that they might deign to join their company. They approached, but when they were near, they suddenly withdrew and entered the women's apartment <note>original: "gynæceum," the inner room of a house reserved for women</note> where their virgin friends also were. Seeing this, the guiding Angel followed them and asked why they had withdrawn so suddenly without speaking to them. They responded, "We could not draw near." He asked, "Why is this?" and they replied, "We do not know, but we perceived something that repelled and drove us back; may they forgive us." The Angel returned to his companions and told them the answer, adding, "I suspect that you do not have a chaste love of the sex. In Heaven we love virgins for their beauty and elegance of manners, and we love them intensely, but chastely." At this his companions laughed and said, "You suspect rightly! Who is able to see such beauties close by and not desire something?"

750. After this festive gathering, all those invited to the wedding departed, and also those ten Men with their Angel. It was late Evening, and they went to bed. At dawn—

-># OF THE NEW HEAVEN AND THE NEW CHURCH<-

Early in the morning they heard the proclamation, **TODAY IS THE SABBATH** <note>original: "HODIE SABBATHUM"</note>, and they arose and asked the Angel what that meant. He replied that it was for the Worship of God, which returns at stated times and is proclaimed by the Priests; it is performed in our Temples and lasts about two hours. "Therefore," he said, "if it pleases you, come with me, and I will lead you in." They prepared themselves and accompanied the Angel, and entered. And behold, the Temple was large, capable of holding about three thousand people, semi-circular in shape, with continuous benches or seats following the circular figure of the Temple. The Pulpit was placed in front of them, slightly back from the center; the door was behind the pulpit to the left. The ten visiting men entered with the Angel as their leader, and the Angel assigned them places where they should sit, telling them, "Everyone who enters the Temple knows his own place; he knows this by an innate sense and cannot sit elsewhere. If he sits elsewhere, he hears nothing and perceives nothing, and he also disturbs the order; if that order is disturbed, the Priest is not inspired."

**751.** After the congregation had gathered, the Priest ascended the pulpit and preached a sermon full of the spirit of wisdom. The sermon was about the holiness of the **Sacred Scripture** and the conjunction of the Lord with both Worlds, the Spiritual and the Natural, through it. In the state of enlightenment in which he was, he fully demonstrated that this Holy Book was dictated by **JEHOVAH** the Lord, and that consequently He Himself is in it, so much so that He is the Wisdom there. However, he explained that the Wisdom which is Himself therein lies hidden beneath the sense of the letter, and is not opened except to those who are in the truths of doctrine and at the same time in the goods of life, and thus are in the Lord and the Lord in them. To the sermon, he added a prayer of devotion, and then descended. As the listeners were leaving, the Angel asked the Priest to speak a few words of peace with his ten companions; so he approached them, and they talked for half an hour. He spoke of the Divine Trinity, explaining that it is in Jesus Christ, in whom all the Fullness of the Divinity dwells bodily, according to the decree of the Apostle Paul <note>A reference to Colossians 2:9</note>; and afterward he spoke of the Union of Charity and Faith, though he said "the Union of Charity and Truth," because Faith is Truth.

**752.** After the giving of thanks, they went home; and there the Angel said to them, "Today is the third day since your ascent into this society of Heaven, and you have been prepared by the Lord for these three days to remain here; therefore, it is time for us to part. Take off, then, the garments sent by the Prince, and put on your own." As soon as they were in their own clothes, they were inspired with a desire to depart; so they left and descended, the Angel accompanying them as far as the place of assembly. There they gave thanks to the Lord that He had deigned to bless them with knowledge and, from that, with understanding regarding Heavenly Joys and eternal Happiness.

# CHAPTER FOURTEENTH

### ABOUT

## THE CONSUMMATION OF THE AGE: THE COMING
## OF THE LORD: AND THE NEW HEAVEN
## AND NEW CHURCH.

->*That the Consummation of the Age is the final time or end of the Church.*<-
<note>The "consummation of the age" is a phrase from the Gospels often translated as "the end of the world," but the author interprets it specifically as the end of a particular religious era or "church."</note>

**753.** On this Earth there have been several Churches, and all in the course of time were consummated, and after their consummation new ones existed, and so on until the present time; the consummation of the Church occurs when no Divine truth remains except what is falsified or rejected. While there is no genuine truth, no genuine good can be given, because every quality of good is formed through truths. For good is the essence of truth, and truth is the form of good, and without a form, no quality exists. Good and truth can no more be separated than the will and the understanding, or what is the same thing, than the affection of love and the thought arising from it. Therefore, when truth is consummated in a Church, good is also consummated there; and when this happens, the Church has its end—that is, its consummation.

**754.** A Church is consummated by various things, especially by those that make what is false appear as if it were true; and when that appears to be Truth, then Good (which is good in itself and is called spiritual good) is no longer given. The good that is then believed to be good is merely natural good, which a moral life produces. The causes why truth and good are consummated together are primarily two Natural Loves, which are diametrically opposite to the two spiritual loves; these are called **Love of self** and **Love of the world**. When the love of self is ruling, it is opposite to love for God; and when the love of the world is ruling, it is opposite to love toward the neighbor. Love of self is to wish well to oneself alone, and to no other except for the sake of oneself; the love of the world is similar. And these loves, when they have been baited <note>The Latin 'inescati' suggests being lured or hooked like a fish.</note>, spread themselves like dead flesh <note>original: "caro morticina"</note> through the body and successively consume all its parts. That such love has invaded the Churches is clearly evident from **Babylonia** <note>Swedenborg uses "Babylonia" to refer to a state of religious corruption where the desire for power and wealth replaces spiritual worship.</note> and its description in Genesis 11:1–9; Isaiah 13, 14, 47; Jeremiah 50; and in Daniel 2:31–47; 3:1–7 and following; chapter 5; chapter 6:8 to the end; chapter 7:1–14; and in the Revelation chapters 17 and 18, both from beginning to end. This [Babylonia] finally exalted itself to such an extent that it not only transferred the Divine Power of the Lord to itself, but also strives with the greatest zeal to gather to itself all the treasures of the World. That similar loves would break out from many Leaders of the Churches outside of Babylonia, were it not that their power is limited and thus restrained, can be concluded from signs and appearances that are not at all vain. What else then follows, than that such a man regards himself as God and the World as Heaven, and perverts every truth of the Church? For truth itself, which is truth in its own nature, cannot be known or acknowledged by a merely natural man, nor can it be given to him by God, because it falls into an inverted state and becomes false. Besides these two loves, there are still many...
