[...the primary] causes of the consummation of truth and good, and thus the consummation of the Church; however, these causes are secondary and subordinate to those two primary ones.

**755.** That the **Consummation of the Age** <note>original: *Consummatio Sæculi*. Often translated as "the end of the world," but the author defines it as the end of a specific religious era.</note> is the final time of the Church is evident from various places in the Word where it is named, such as: *I have heard from **Jehovah** a **consummation and a decree** over the whole earth* (Isaiah 28:22). *The consummation is determined, overflowing with justice; for the Lord Jehovih of Hosts is making a **consummation and a decree** in all the earth* (Isaiah 10:22–23). *In the fire of Jehovah's zeal the whole earth shall be consumed, because He shall make a speedy **consummation** with all the inhabitants of the earth* (Zephaniah 1:18). By "the Earth" in these passages is signified the Church, because the land of Canaan is understood, where the Church was located. That the Church is signified by "the Earth" may be seen confirmed from many passages from the Word in *The Apocalypse Revealed* <note>One of the author's previous works, published in 1766.</note>, numbers 285 and 902. *At length upon the bird of abominations shall be **desolation**, and even until the **consummation and decree**, it shall drop upon the **devastation*** (Daniel 9:27). That these things were said by Daniel concerning the end of the present Christian Church may be seen in Matthew 24:15. *The whole earth shall be a **waste**, yet I will not make a **consummation*** (Jeremiah 4:27). *The iniquity of the Amorites is not yet **consummated*** (Genesis 15:16 <note>The OCR lists Gen X:22-23, but the text refers to the common citation of Gen 15:16 regarding the "full measure" of iniquity.</note>). *Jehovah said, I will go down and see whether they have made a **consummation** according to the cry that has come to Me* (Genesis 18:21, concerning Sodom). The final time of the present Christian Church is also understood by the Lord as the "Consummation of the Age" in these passages: *The disciples asked Jesus, what shall be the sign of Your coming and of the **consummation of the age**?* (Matthew 24:3). *At the time of harvest I will say to the reapers, gather first the tares to be burned; gather the wheat into the barns; so shall it be in the **consummation of the age*** (Matthew 13:30, 40). *In the **consummation of the age** the angels shall go forth and separate the wicked from the midst of the just* (Matthew 13:49). *Jesus said to the disciples, behold, I am with you even until the **consummation of the age*** (Matthew 28:20). It should be known that <term>Vastation</term>, <term>Desolation</term>, and <term>Decree</term> signify the same thing as <term>Consummation</term>; however, *Desolation* signifies the consummation of truth, *Vastation* the consummation of good, and *Decree* <note>original: *Decisio*. Sometimes translated as "decision" or "determination."</note> the full consummation of both; and that the "Fullness of Time," in which the Lord came into the world and in which He is to come again, is also the Consummation.

**756.** The Consummation of the Age can be illustrated by various things in the natural world, for here everything on the Earth grows old and is consumed, but through alternating phases called the <term>Cycles of things</term>. These cycles run through time both in general and in part. **In general**, the year passes from spring to summer, and through that into autumn, ending in winter, from which it returns to spring; but this is the cycle of heat. **In part**, the day passes from morning to noon, and through that into evening, ending in night, from which it returns to morning; but this is the cycle of light. Every human being also runs through a cycle of nature: beginning life from infancy, proceeding to adolescence and youth, and from there to old age, and finally dies. Likewise every bird of the air and every beast of the earth. Every tree also begins from a bud, proceeds to full height, and successively withers until it falls. The same happens with every bush and shrub, and even every leaf and flower; and also with the soil itself, which in time becomes sterile; and with all stagnant water, which gradually putrefies. All these are alternating Consummations, which are natural and temporary, yet periodic; for when one thing has passed from its origin to its end, another similar thing arises. Thus everything is born, decays, and is born again, so that the purpose of creation might be continued. That the same happens with the Church is because the human being *is* the Church, and collectively they constitute it; one generation follows another, and there is a variety of all minds. Iniquity, once rooted as an inclination, is passed down to posterity, and it is not uprooted except through <term>regeneration</term>, which is performed by the Lord alone.

## *That today is the final time of the Christian Church, which was predicted and described by the Lord in the Gospels and in Revelation.*

**757.** That the **Consummation of the Age** <note>original: *Consummatio saeculi*. This phrase is often translated in Bibles as "the end of the world," but the author argues it specifically refers to the end of a particular religious dispensation or "Church."</note> signifies the final time of the Church was shown in the preceding Article. From this, it is clear what is meant by the **Consummation of the Age** about which the Lord spoke in the Gospels: Matthew 24, Mark 13, and Luke 21. For we read, *As Jesus sat upon the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to Him privately, saying, "What shall be the sign of Your Coming and of the **Consummation of the Age**?"* (Matthew 24:3). Then the Lord began to predict and describe the Consummation—how it would occur successively until His Coming, and that He would then come in the clouds of Heaven with power and glory, and gather His elect, among many other details (verses 30–31), which in no way occurred at the destruction of Jerusalem. The Lord described these things there in prophetic language, in which every single word carries its own weight. What each specific word involves has been explained in *Heavenly Secrets* <note>original: *Arcana Caelestia*, the author's multi-volume commentary on Genesis and Exodus, published 1749–1756.</note>, numbers 3353 to 3356, 3486 to 3489, 3650 to 3655, 3751 to 3757, 3898 to 3901, 4057 to 4060, 4229 to 4231, 4332 to 4335, and 4422 to 4424.

**758.** That all those things the Lord spoke with His disciples were said concerning the final time of the Christian Church is clearly evident from **Revelation**, where similar things are predicted regarding the **Consummation of the Age** and His Coming. These are all explained individually in *The Apocalypse Revealed* <note>original: *Apocalypsi Revelata*, published by the author in 1766.</note>. Now, because the things the Lord said before His disciples concerning the Consummation and His Coming coincide with what He later revealed through John in Revelation concerning the same subjects, it is clearly evident that He meant no other Consummation than that of today’s Christian Church. Furthermore, the end of this Church was also prophesied in Daniel; therefore the Lord says, *When you see the **abomination of desolation**, predicted by the prophet Daniel, standing in the holy place, let him who reads note it well* (Matthew 24:15; Daniel 9:27). The same is also found in the other Prophets. 

That such an **Abomination of Desolation** <term>Abomination of Desolation: A theological state where the essential truths and goods of the church have been so distorted or ignored that the church effectively ceases to be a spiritual path.</term> exists in the Christian Church today will be further demonstrated in the Appendix. There, it will be seen that not a single genuine truth remains in the Church, and also that unless a **New Church** is raised up in place of the current one, *no flesh could be saved*, according to the Lord’s words in Matthew 24:22. The fact that the Christian Church, as it is today, is consummated and devastated to such an extent cannot be seen by those on earth who have confirmed themselves in its falsities. The reason is that the confirmation of a falsity is the negation of truth; therefore, it places a kind of veil over the intellect and thereby guards it, lest anything else should enter to pull up the ropes and stakes by which it has built and shaped its system like a sturdy tent. Added to this is the fact that the **natural rational mind** <note>The author distinguishes between "natural reason," which can justify any belief regardless of its truth, and "spiritual reason," which sees from a love of truth.</note> can confirm whatever it pleases, whether false or true. When a thing is confirmed, both appear in a similar light, and it is not recognized whether it is a **false light** <note>original: *lux fatua*. Literally a "foolish light," like a will-o'-the-wisp or a mirage.</note>, such as occurs in a dream, or whether it is a true light, such as exists in the day. But the **spiritual rational mind** is altogether different; in this mind are those who look to the Lord, and who are in the love of truth from Him.

**759.** It is because of this that every Church, established by "Seers" through their confirmations, appears to them as if it alone were in the light, and that all others who disagree are in darkness. For those who see through confirmations are not unlike owls, which see light in the shadows of night, but see the sun and its rays during the day as thick darkness. Such was, and still is, every Church that is in falsities, once it has been established by its leaders—who seem to themselves to be as keen-sighted as lynxes—who have made a morning light for themselves out of their own...

<note>The text begins mid-sentence, continuing from the previous page's discussion of different types of intellectual light.</note> ...one's own intelligence, and the evening light derived from the Word. Did not the Jewish Church, when it was utterly devastated—which was the state it was in when our Lord came into the world—cry out loudly through its Scribes and Lawyers <note>original: *Legisperitis*, those skilled in the Mosaic Law</note> that because it possessed the Word, it alone was in celestial light? And yet, they crucified the Messiah or Christ, who was the Word itself and the "all in all" of everything within it. What else does that Church cry out, which is understood as **Babylon** in the Prophets and in the Revelation <note>Babylon is used by the author to symbolize the Roman Catholic Church of his day, which he viewed as prioritizing its own power over scripture.</note>, than that she is the Queen and Mother of all Churches, and that the rest, which withdraw from her, are spurious offspring who are to be excommunicated? And this she does even though she has thrust the Lord Savior from His Throne and Altar and placed herself above them. 

Does not every Church, even the most heretical, once it has been accepted, fill regions and cities with the cry that it alone is Orthodox and Universal <note>original: *Oecumenica*</note>, and that with it is the Gospel which the Angel flying in the midst of heaven announced (Revelation 14:6)? And who does not hear the echo of their voice from the common people, saying that it is so? Did not the entire **Synod of Dort** <note>A national assembly held in 1618–1619 to settle a divisive controversy in the Dutch Reformed Church regarding predestination.</note> see Predestination in no other way than as a Star falling from Heaven upon their heads? They kissed that dogma just as the Philistines did the idol **Dagon** in the temple of **Eben-Ezer** at Ashdod, and as the Greeks did the **Palladium** <note>A sacred statue of the goddess Pallas Athena believed to protect the city of Troy; here used to mean a core, cherished belief.</note> in the temple of Minerva. For they called it the "Palladium of religion," not knowing that a falling star is a meteor of false light <note>original: *luce fatua*, a reference to *ignis fatuus* or "will-o'-the-wisp."</note>. When such a light falls into the brain, it can confirm every falsehood through fallacies, until it is believed to be true light; it is then decreed to be a fixed star, and finally men swear that it is the "star of stars." 

Who speaks more persuasively about the certainty of his own fantasy than an atheist Naturalist? Does he not laugh with his whole heart at the Divine things of God, the Celestial things of Heaven, and the Spiritual things of the Church? What lunatic does not believe his own folly to be wisdom, and wisdom to be folly? Who can distinguish by sight alone the false light of rotten wood from the light of the moon? Who, being naturally averse to balsamic scents—as those affected by "uterine disease" <note>An 18th-century medical term for hysteria or similar conditions believed to involve sensitivity to smells.</note>—does not repel them from their nostrils and prefer foul smells instead? And so it goes. 

These examples are brought forward for the sake of illustration, to show that by natural light alone it cannot be recognized that a Church is "consummated"—that is, that it is in mere falsehoods—until truth from Heaven shines in its own light. This is because falsehood cannot see truth, but truth can see falsehood. Every human being is such that they can see and comprehend truth when they hear it; however, a person confirmed in falsehoods cannot bring that truth into their understanding so that it remains, because it finds no place there. If by chance it does enter, the troop of falsehoods gathered there casts it out as something alien <note>original: *heterogeneum*</note>.

## *That this Last Time of the Christian Church is the very Night into which the former Churches have ended.*

**760.** That there have been four Churches in general on this Earth since its creation, one of which succeeded the other, can be established from the Word, both Historical and Prophetical. This is seen especially in the book of Daniel, where those four Churches are described by the **Statue seen by Nebuchadnezzar** in a dream (Chapter 2), and afterwards by the **four Beasts** ascending from the sea (Chapter 7). 

1. The **First Church**, which is to be called the **Most Ancient**, existed before the flood; its Consummation or end is described by the Flood. 
2. The **Second Church**, which is to be called the **Ancient**, was in Asia and partly in Africa; it was consummated and perished through idolatries. 
3. The **Third Church** was the **Israelitish**, begun from the proclamation of the Decalogue upon Mount Sinai, continued through the Word written by Moses and the Prophets, and consummated or finished by the profanation of the Word. The fullness of this profanation was at the time the Lord came into the World; therefore, they crucified Him, who was the Word. 
4. The **Fourth Church** is the **Christian**, established by the Lord through the Evangelists and Apostles. There have been two distinct epochs of this Church: one from the time of the Lord until the **Council of Nicaea** <note>The first ecumenical council in 325 AD, which the author argues introduced the idea of three divine persons and thus began the Church's spiritual decline.</note>, and the second from that Council...

761. That the final time of the Christian Church is the **Night** itself, into which the previous ones have ended, is evident from the Lord’s Prediction concerning it in the Gospels and in Daniel. In the Gospels, from these words: *“That they shall see the Abomination of desolation,”* and *“that there shall be great affliction, such as has not been from the beginning of the World until now, nor shall be: and that unless those days were shortened, no flesh could be saved: and finally, the Sun will be darkened, the Moon will not give its light, and the Stars will fall from Heaven,”* Matthew 24:15, 21, 22, 29. That time is also called **Night** elsewhere in the Gospels, as in Luke: *“In 그 Night there shall be two in one bed; one shall be accepted, but the other shall be left,”* 17:34; and in John: *“I must work the works of Him who sent Me; the Night comes, when no one can work,”* 9:4. Since all Light departs at midnight, and the Lord is the true Light (John 1:4 sq. <note>original: *sequens*, meaning "and following"</note>, Chapter 8:12, Chapter 12:35, 36, 46); therefore, He said to the Disciples when He ascended into Heaven: *I am with you even to the Consummation of the age* <note>original: *Consummationem saeculi*, often translated as "end of the world," but here meaning the end of a religious era</note>, Matthew 28:20, and then He departs from them to a **New Church**. 

That this final time of the Church is the Night itself, into which the former Churches have ended, is also evident in Daniel from these words: *“At last upon the bird of abominations shall be Desolation, and even to the Consummation and the Decree it shall drop upon the Devastation,”* Chapter 9:27. That this was predicted concerning the end of the Christian Church is clearly apparent from the Lord’s words in Matthew 24:15 <note>The author cites verse 18 in the text, but refers to the context of the Abomination mentioned in verse 15.</note>; also from those in Daniel concerning the fourth Kingdom or the fourth Church represented by Nebuchadnezzar's statue: *“Whereas you saw iron mixed with miry clay, they shall mingle themselves by the seed of man, but they shall not cohere one with another, just as iron does not mix with clay,”* Chapter 2:43; the **seed of man** is the truth of the Word. And also from these things concerning the fourth Church represented by the fourth Beast ascending from the sea: *“I was seeing in the visions of the night, and behold, a fourth Beast, terrible and formidable, it shall devour the whole earth, and shall tread it down, and break it in pieces,”* Chapter 7:7, 23. By this, it is understood that it will consume every truth of the Church; and then it will be Night, because the truth of the Church is light. Similar things are predicted about this Church many times in the Revelation, especially in Chapter 16, where it treats of the vials of the wrath of God poured out upon the earth, by which are signified the falsehoods <note>original: *falsitates*</note> that will then inundate and destroy the Church. Similarly in many places in the Prophets, as in these: *“Shall not the day of Jehovah be darkness and not light, even very dark and no brightness in it?”* Amos 5:18, 20; Zephaniah 1:15. Also: *“In that day Jehovah shall look down upon the earth, and behold darkness, and the light is darkened in its ruins,”* Isaiah 5:30, Chapter 8:22; the **day of Jehovah** is the day of the Lord’s coming.

762. That four Churches have existed on this Earth since the Creation of the World is according to Divine order, which is that there is a beginning and its end before a new beginning arises. Hence it is that every day begins from morning, progresses, and ends in night, and after this begins anew; also that every year starts from spring, progresses through summer to autumn, and ends in winter, and after this starts again. For these to happen, the Sun rises in the East, and from there progresses through the south to the West, and ends in the north, from which it rises again. It is similar with the Churches: the First of them, which was the **Most Ancient**, was like morning, spring, and the east; the Second, or the **Ancient**, was like day, summer, and the south; the Third <note>The Israelite/Jewish Church</note> was like evening, autumn, and the west; and the Fourth <note>The Christian Church</note> was like night, winter, and the north. From these progressions according to order, the wise men of Antiquity concluded there were four **Ages of the World**, the first of which they called *golden*, the second *silver*, the third *copper* <note>original: *cupream*, often translated as the Bronze Age</note>, and the fourth *iron*, with which metals the Churches themselves were also represented by Nebuchadnezzar's statue. -># OF THE NEW HEAVEN AND THE NEW CHURCH.<-

The Church before the Lord appears as one man, and this <term>Greatest Man</term> <note>original: *Maximus Homo*. A central concept in this theology where the entire human race or the Church is seen as a single collective human form before God.</note> passes through its ages just like an individual man: namely, from infancy to adolescence, and through this to youth, and finally into old age; and then when it dies, it shall rise again. The Lord says, *“Unless a grain of wheat falling into the earth dies, it remains [alone]; but if it dies, it bears much fruit,”* John 12:24.

763. That which occurs according to order—moving first toward its ultimate end in both the General and the Specific—exists so that a variety of all things may arise, and through these varieties, every quality. For "quality" is perfected through relative differences between opposites, from more to less. Who cannot see that Truth receives its specific quality by the existence of Falsity, and likewise Good by the existence of Evil, just as light exists by the existence of darkness, and heat by the existence of cold? What would color be if only white existed and not black? The quality of intermediate colors would be nothing but imperfect. What is Sensation without relation? And what is relation except to opposites? Is not the sight of the eye dimmed by pure white alone, and enlivened by a color that draws something from black within itself, such as the color green? Is not the Ear deafened by one tone continuously straining its organs, and excited by a melody that is varied through relationships? What is the beautiful without relation to the unbeautiful? Therefore, so that the beauty of a maiden may be presented vividly, in certain paintings a deformed image is placed at the side. What is pleasant and favorable without relation to the unpleasant and unfavorable? Who does not lose their mind from one constant idea, unless variety from things tending toward their opposites provides an interval? It is the same in the spiritual things of the Church, whose opposites relate to evil and falsity; these, however, are not from the Lord, but from man, who possesses free will that he can bend to a good use or an evil use. Comparatively, it is like darkness and cold; these are not from the Sun, but from the Earth, which by its successive revolutions withdraws and turns itself away. And yet, without this turning and withdrawal, there would be neither day nor year, and therefore nothing and no one upon the earth. I have heard that the Churches, which are in different goods and truths (provided their goods relate to love to the Lord, and their truths to faith in the Lord), are like so many <term>Jewels</term> <note>original: *Clenodia*, meaning treasures or precious gems.</note> in a King’s Crown.

## That after this Night follows Morning, and that the Advent of the Lord is that Morning.

764. Since the successive States of the Church, in general and in particular, are described in the Word through the four seasons of the Year—which are spring, summer, autumn, and winter—and through the four times of the Day—which are morning, noon, evening, and night—and because the current Church in Christendom is Night, it follows that the Morning is now at hand, that is, the Beginning of a new Church. That the successive states of the Church are described in the Word by the four states of the light of day is evident from these passages: *“Until the* EVENING *and the* MORNING, *two thousand three hundred [days]; then shall the Sanctuary be justified; the vision of the* EVENING *and the* MORNING *is truth,”* Daniel 8:14, 26. *“One calling to Me from Seir: Watchman, what of the* NIGHT? *The watchman said, The* MORNING *comes, and also the* NIGHT,” Isaiah 21:11, 12. *“The end is come, the* MORNING *is come upon thee, O inhabitant of the Earth; behold the* DAY *is come, the* MORNING *has gone forth,”* Ezekiel 7:6, 7, 10. *“Jehovah in the* MORNING, *in the* MORNING *He will bring His judgment to light, nor shall it be wanting,”* Zephaniah 3:5. *“God is in the midst of her, God shall help her when she looks toward the* MORNING,” Psalm 46:6. *“I have waited for Jehovah, my soul waits for the Lord, more than those who watch for the* MORNING, *those who watch for the* MORNING, *for with Him is plenteous Redemption, and He shall redeem Israel,”* Psalm 130:5 to 8. In these passages, by Evening and Night is understood the final time of the Church, and by Morning its first time. The Lord Himself is even called "the Morning" in these places: *“The God of Israel said, to me spoke...*

766. The Lord is present with every person, and He urges and presses to be received; and when a person receives Him—which happens when they acknowledge Him as their God, Creator, Redeemer, and Savior—it is His first coming, which is called the *Dawn* <note>original: *Diluculum*. The very first glimmer of light before the morning starts.</note>. From this time, the person begins to be enlightened in their understanding of spiritual matters and to progress into more and more interior wisdom; and as they receive that wisdom from the Lord, so they progress through the morning into the Day, and this day lasts with them into old age until death; and after death, they come into Heaven to the Lord Himself. There, even if they died an old man, they are restored to the morning of their life, and the beginnings of wisdom implanted in the natural world are continued for eternity.

767. A person who is in faith in the Lord and in charity toward their neighbor is a *Church* in particular; the *Church* in general is composed of such individuals. This is a wonderful thing: that every Angel looks at the Lord—who is the <term>Sun of the Angelic Heaven</term> <note>original: *Sol Cæli Angelici*. In this theology, the Lord does not appear as a person to all angels at once, but as a spiritual Sun that provides all heat (love) and light (wisdom).</note>—before them, regardless of which way their body or face is turned. He is the one who appears before their eyes while they are in spiritual meditation. Something similar happens to a person in the world in whom the *Church* resides, as far as the sight of their spirit is concerned; but because this is veiled by natural sight (which is flattered by the other senses focused on the body and the world), this *State* of their spirit is unknown. This looking toward the Lord in every turning takes its origin from the fact that every truth (from which come wisdom and faith) and every good (through which come love and charity) are from the Lord—and indeed are the Lord's within the person. Thus, every single truth of wisdom is like a mirror in which the Lord is seen, and every good of love is an image of the Lord. This is the reason for this wonder. An evil spirit, however, perpetually turns away from the Lord and continually looks toward his own love, and this also in every turning—

That something of this kind is even implanted in nature can be concluded from certain sprouts among the grasses that surround them; they strive to rise above them toward the heights so that they may look upon the sun; also, some turn themselves from the east to the west during the day so that they may ripen under the sun's guidance. This can also be compared to a bride, who constantly carries something of the image of the bridegroom in the sight of her spirit, and sees him in his gifts as if in mirrors, and longs for his arrival, and receives him with joy when he comes, in which the love of her heart exults.

### *That the Coming of the Lord is not His Coming to destroy the visible Heaven and the habitable Earth, and to create a New Heaven and a New Earth, as many have until now supposed from a lack of understanding the Spiritual sense of the Word.*

768. The opinion prevailing today in the churches is that the Lord, when He comes for the last judgment, will appear in the clouds of Heaven with the Angels and the sound of trumpets, and will gather all who live upon the Earth, along with those who have died, and will separate the wicked from the good, as a shepherd separates goats from sheep. It is believed that He will then cast the wicked, or goats, into hell, and raise the good, or sheep, into Heaven; and that He will then simultaneously create a New visible Heaven and a New habitable Earth; and upon this Earth He will send down a City, which will be called the New Jerusalem, the structure of which will be according to the description in Revelation Chapter 21—namely, made of jasper and gold, with foundations of its walls made of every precious stone, and its height, width, and length being equal, each 12,000 stadia <note>A "stadium" was a Greek unit of distance; 12,000 stadia is roughly 1,400 miles.</note>. It is believed that into this City all the elect would be gathered, both those who are living and those who have died since the beginning of the world; and that these would then return into their bodies and enjoy eternal joy in that magnificent City, as in their Heaven. This opinion concerning the coming of the Lord and the Last Judgment is what reigns today in Christian churches.

769. Regarding the state of souls after death, these things are generally and specifically believed today: that human souls after death are *Spirits* <note>original: *Pneumata*. Here, Swedenborg is referring to the common conception of souls as "breaths" or "ghosts."</note>, of which people foster an idea as if they were a breath of wind; and that because they are such, they are reserved until the day of the last judgment either in the middle of the earth, where their Purgatory is, or in the *Limbo of the Fathers* <note>original: *Limbo patrum*. In traditional theology, this was a temporary state for the souls of the righteous who died before Christ’s resurrection.</note>. However, people disagree on these points: some suppose that they are ethereal or airy forms, and thus are like phantoms or specters, and that some of these live in the air, some in the woods, and some in the waters. Others suppose that the souls of the deceased are transferred to the planets or to the stars, and given dwellings there; and some believe that after thousands of years they return into bodies. Most, however, believe that they are reserved for a time until the entire Firmament, together with the World of Earth and Water, is to perish, which will happen by fire—either breaking out from the center of the earth or cast down from Heaven like a universal lightning bolt. Then the graves will be opened, and the reserved souls will be clothed again in their bodies and transferred into that Holy City Jerusalem, and thus upon the earth al-

770. When the Clergy and the Laity are asked whether they firmly believe all those things—such as that the people before the Flood together with Adam and Eve, and those after the Flood together with Noah and his sons, as well as Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob with all the Prophets and Apostles, along with the souls of all other humans, are still reserved in the very center of the earth, or are flying about in the ether or the air; and also whether they believe that souls are to put on their bodies again and be united with them, even though these are corpses eaten away by worms, mice, and fish, or Egyptian mummies eaten by men <note>Mummy powder was historically used in Europe as a medicinal ingredient</note>, or certain wretched remains burnt by the sun and fallen into dust; and also whether they believe that the stars of Heaven will then fall upon the earth, even though the earth is smaller than even one of them—are these not paradoxes which reason itself dissipates, just as it usually does with contradictions? But to these things some answer nothing; some say that these are matters of faith, under whose obedience we "keep our understanding captive" <note>original: "captamus intellectum"; a reference to the theological idea that reason must be subservient to dogma</note>; some say that not only these, but many things above the rational, belong to Divine Omnipotence. And when they name Faith and Omnipotence, reason is exiled, and then sound reason either disappears and becomes as nothing, or becomes like a specter and is called insanity. They add: "Are these things not according to the Word? Who would not think and speak from that?"

771. It has been shown in the chapter on Sacred Scripture that the Word in its literal sense was written through Appearances and Correspondences <term>Correspondences</term> <note>The relationship between the natural world and the spiritual world where every natural object represents a spiritual reality</note>, and that therefore there is a spiritual sense in every part of it, in which the truth is in its own light, while the sense of the letter is in the shade. Lest, therefore, the person of the New Church <note>Swedenborg's term for a new era of Christianity based on internal, spiritual understanding</note> wander in the shade in which the literal sense of the Word is—as the person of the old church has done—concerning especially Heaven and Hell, and his own life after death, and here concerning the Coming of the Lord, it has pleased the Lord to open the sight of my spirit. He has thus introduced me into the spiritual world and granted me not only to speak with spirits and angels, and with relatives and friends, even indeed with kings and princes who have met their fates in the natural world, but also to see the wonders of Heaven and the miseries of Hell. Thus I have seen that man does not dwell in some point <note>original: "Pu", likely "Puncto"</note> of the earth, nor fly about blind and mute in the air or in a vacuum, but that man lives in a substantial body <term>substantial body</term> <note>A body made of spiritual substance that looks and feels solid to the spirit, as opposed to a material body</note>, in a much more perfect state—if he comes among the blessed—than he lived in before when in a material body. Lest, therefore, man should plunge himself deeper into the opinion concerning the destruction of the visible Heaven and the habitable Earth, and thus into ignorance concerning the spiritual world—from which ignorance come naturalism and simultaneously atheism, which today has begun to take root in the interior rational mind among the learned—and lest it spread further like gangrene <note>original: "morticinum in carne"; literally "dead flesh in the body"</note> into his external mind from which he speaks, I have been enjoined by the Lord to publish various things from what I have seen and heard, both concerning HEAVEN AND HELL and concerning the LAST JUDGMENT; and also to explain the Apocalypse, where the Coming of the Lord, the former heaven, the new heaven, and the Holy Jerusalem are treated. From reading and understanding these things, anyone can see what is meant there by the Coming of the Lord, by the New Heaven, and by the New Jerusalem.

### *That this coming of the Lord, which is the Second, exists for the purpose that the evil may be separated from the good, and that those who have believed and do believe in Him may be saved, and that from these a New Angelic Heaven and a New Church on earth may be formed, and that without this, no Flesh could be saved, Matthew 24:22.*

772. That this Second Coming of the Lord does not exist for the purpose of destroying the visible Heaven and the habitable Earth was shown in the preceding Article. That it is not for the purpose of destroying anything, but for building up—and therefore not for condemning, but for saving those who have believed in Him since His first Coming, and those who will believe hereafter—is evident from these words of the Lord: "*God did not send His Son into the World to judge the World, but that the World might be saved through Him; he who believes in Him is not judged, but he who does not believe is already judged, because he has not believed in the Name of the only-begotten Son of God,* John 3:17." And elsewhere: "*If anyone hears my words, yet does not believe, I do not judge him; for I did not come to judge the World, but to save the World; he who rejects Me and does not receive my words has that which judges him; the Word which I have spoken, that will judge him,* Chapter 12:47, 48." That the Last Judgment took place in the spiritual world in the Year 1757 <note>Swedenborg famously claimed to have witnessed the "Last Judgment" not as a physical end of the world, but as a reorganization of the spiritual realm that occurred in 1757.</note> was made known in the small work **The Last Judgment**, published in London in the Year 1758, and further in the **Continuation** regarding it, published in Amsterdam in 1763; to which I testify, because I saw it with my own eyes in full wakefulness.

773. The reason the Coming of the Lord is for the purpose of forming a new Heaven from those who have believed in Him, and for establishing a new Church from those who hereafter believe in Him, is because these two are the ends <term>ends: the ultimate goals or purposes</term> of His Coming. The very end of the creation of the Universe was no other than that an Angelic Heaven might be formed from human beings, in which all who believe in God will live in eternal happiness; for Divine Love, which is in God and is essentially God, can intend nothing else, and Divine Wisdom, which is also in God and is God, can produce nothing else. Since the Creation of the universe had as its end an Angelic Heaven from the Human Race, and at the same time a Church on earth—for through the Church a person passes into Heaven—and since the Salvation of men (which involves people yet to be born in the World) is thus a continuation of creation, therefore everywhere in the Word <note>original: "Verbo"; Swedenborg uses "the Word" to refer specifically to the Sacred Scriptures.</note> the term "to Create" is used, and by it is meant to form for Heaven. This is seen in these places: "*Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a steadfast Spirit within me,* Psalm 51:10 <note>original: "Psalm LI: 12"; Swedenborg follows the numbering of the Latin Vulgate.</note>. *You open your hand, they are filled with good; you send forth your Spirit, they are created,* Psalm 104:28, 30. *The people who shall be created will praise Jah,* Psalm 102:18. *Thus said Jehovah your Creator, O Jacob, your Former, O Israel: I have redeemed you, I have called you by my name... everyone called by my Name, I have created him for my glory,* Isaiah 43:1, 7. *In the day that you were created they were prepared; you were perfect in your ways on the day you were created, until perversity was found in you,* Ezekiel 28:13, 15"—this is said of the King of Tyre. "*That they may see, know, attend, and understand that the hand of Jehovah has done this, and the Holy One of Israel has created this,* Isaiah 41:19, 20." From these it can be established what is meant by "to Create" in these following passages: "*Jehovah creating the Heavens, stretching out the Earth, giving breath to the people upon it, and Spirit to those walking in it,* Isaiah 42:5, Chapter 45:12, 18. *Behold, I am creating a new Heaven and a new Earth; rejoice forever in what I am creating: behold, I am about to create Jerusalem an exultation,* Isaiah 65:17, 18."

774. The presence of the Lord is perpetual with every person, both the evil and the good, for without His presence no person lives; but the Coming...

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the nature of the Second Coming. While the previous page established that the Coming is for salvation rather than destruction, this page explains how the Lord is present in the human mind and introduces the core idea that the Second Coming happens through the Word (the Bible) rather than a physical appearance.</meta>

<page-num>470</page-num>
->UNIVERSAL THEOLOGY<-

His presence belongs only to those who receive Him, who are those who believe in Him and follow His commandments. The Lord’s perpetual presence makes it possible for a person to become rational and, eventually, spiritual. This is achieved by the **Light** proceeding from the Lord as the **Sun** in the spiritual world, which a person receives through their understanding. That Light is truth, and it is through truth that a person possesses rationality. However, the **Coming** <note>original: *Adventus*</note> of the Lord occurs for the person who joins **heat** to that light—that is, love to truth. For the heat proceeding from that same Sun is love toward God and toward the neighbor. The mere presence of the Lord, and the resulting enlightenment of the understanding, can be compared to the presence of solar light in the world; unless it is joined with heat, everything on earth is desolated. But the Lord's coming can be compared to the coming of heat in the springtime. Because heat then joins itself to light, the earth softens, seeds sprout, and they bring forth fruit. Such is the parallel between spiritual things, in which a person’s spirit exists, and natural things, in which their body exists.

775. It is the same with the Church as a collective or whole as it is with an individual person. The Church in its collective form consists of many people, while the Church in an individual form is the Church within each of those many people. It is according to Divine order that there be **Generals** <note>In this context, "Generals" refers to universal or overarching structures that contain specific details.</note> and **Particulars**, and that both exist together in every single thing; otherwise, particulars could not exist or endure. Just as nothing particular exists within a human being unless there are "generals" to surround them: the particulars in a person are the internal organs <note>original: *viscera*</note> and their parts, while the "generals" are the membranes or coverings <note>original: *involucra*</note> which are not only around the whole person but also around each individual organ and each part within them. It is the same in every beast, bird, and worm; the same in every tree, shrub, and seed. Nor can a sound be produced by strings or wind unless there is a most general medium from which the specific notes of the melody draw their common foundation to exist. It is the same with every sense of the body, such as sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch; and it is also the same with every internal sense belonging to the mind. These examples are brought forward for the sake of illustration, so it may be known that in the Church, too, there are Generals and Particulars, and even **Most General** principles. This is why four Churches have preceded in order <note>Swedenborg taught that human history progressed through four "churches" or spiritual eras: the Most Ancient (Adam), the Ancient (Noah), the Israelite, and the Christian.</note>, and from this progression arose the most general foundation of the Church, and successively the general and particular aspects of each. In a person, there are also two "Most Generals" from which all common and individual parts derive their existence: in the body, these are the **Heart** and the **Lungs**; in the spirit, they are the **Will** and the **Understanding**. Upon these, all things of life depend, both generally and particularly; without them, they would fall apart and die. The same would be true of the entire Angelic Heaven, the whole Human Race, and indeed the entire Created World, if they did not all depend—generally and particularly—upon God, His Love, and His Wisdom.

### ***That this Second Coming of the Lord is not in Person, but is in the Word, which is from Him, and is Himself.***

776. We read in many places that the Lord is to come in the clouds of heaven, such as in <term>Matthew</term> 17:5, 24:30, 26:64; <term>Mark</term> 14:61-62; <term>Luke</term> 9:34-35, 21:27; <term>Revelation</term> 1:7, 14:14; and <term>Daniel</term> 7:13. But until now, no one has known what is meant by the **Clouds of Heaven**. People have believed that He would appear in them in Person. However, that the "Clouds of Heaven" mean the **Word in its literal sense**, and that the "Glory and Power" in which He is then to come (<term>Matthew</term> 24:30) mean the **spiritual sense of the Word**, has remained hidden until now. This is because, up to this point, no one has even guessed that there is a spiritual sense...

## OF THE NEW HEAVEN AND THE NEW CHURCH.

...is in itself, may be in the Word. Now, because the spiritual sense of the Word has been opened to me by the Lord, and it has been granted to me to be together with angels and spirits in their world as one of them, it has been revealed that by the **Cloud of Heaven** is meant the Word in its natural sense, and by **Glory** is meant the Word in its spiritual sense, and by **Power** is meant the Lord’s power through the Word. That the "cloud of heaven" signifies this can be seen from these passages in the Word: *There is none like the God of Jeshurun, riding in the heaven, and in His magnificence upon the* CLOUDS, Deuteronomy 33:26–27. *Sing to God, praise His name, extol Him who rideth upon the* CLOUDS, Psalm 68:4. *Jehovah riding upon a* LIGHT CLOUD, Isaiah 19:1. "To ride" signifies to instruct in Divine truths from the Word, for a **horse** <note>In Swedenborg’s system of symbolism, a horse represents the human understanding of the Bible.</note> signifies the understanding of the Word; see *Apocalypse Revealed*, no. 298. Anyone can see that God does not literally ride upon clouds. Furthermore, God rode upon *Cherubim*, and *He placed His tent* in the CLOUDS OF THE HEAVENS, Psalm 18:10–12; "Cherubim" also signify the Word; see *Apocalypse Revealed*, nos. 239, 672. *Jehovah binds the waters in His clouds, and spreads His* CLOUD *over the throne*, Job 26:8–9. *Ascribe strength to Jehovah, His strength is in the* CLOUDS, Psalm 68:34. *Jehovah created over every dwelling of Zion a* CLOUD *by day, for over all the glory shall be a covering*, Isaiah 4:5. The Word in the **sense of the letter** <note>The literal, surface-level meaning of the Bible.</note> was also represented by the CLOUD in which Jehovah descended upon Mount Sinai when He promulgated the Law; those parts of the Law which were then promulgated were the first-fruits of the Word. As further confirmation, this must be added: in the spiritual world, there are clouds just as in the natural world, but from a different origin. In the spiritual world, there are sometimes bright clouds above the angelic heavens, but dark clouds over the hells. The bright clouds over the angelic heavens signify obscurity there arising from the literal sense of the Word; but when those clouds are dissipated, it signifies that they are in the light of its spiritual sense. But the dark clouds over the hells signify the falsification and profanation of the Word. The reason that clouds in the spiritual world signify such things is because the Light that proceeds from the Lord as a Sun there signifies **Divine Truth**; for this reason, He is called LIGHT, John 1:9, 12:35. It is for this reason that the Word itself, which is kept in the inner sanctuaries of the temples there, appears surrounded by a bright white light; and its obscurity is induced by clouds.

777. That the Lord is the Word is clearly evident from these words in John: *In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God, and the Word was made Flesh*, Chapter 1:1, 14. The reason "the Word" there means **Divine Truth** is because Divine Truth for Christians comes from nowhere else than from the Word, which is the fountain from which all the Churches named after Christ draw living waters in their fullness—even if it is as if in a cloud, in which its natural sense exists, yet in glory and power, in which its spiritual and celestial senses exist. That there are three senses in the Word—the **Natural**, the **Spiritual**, and the **Celestial**, one more interior than the other—has been shown in the chapter on SACRED SCRIPTURE and in the chapter on the DECALOGUE OR CATECHISM. From this it is clear that by "the Word" in John is meant Divine Truth. John himself testifies to this again in his First Epistle: *We know that the Son of God has come, and has given us* UNDERSTANDING, *that we may know the* TRUTH, *and be in the* TRUTH, *in His Son Jesus Christ*, Chapter 5:20. And therefore the Lord so often said AMEN <note>original: *AMEN dico vobis* (Amen I say to you)</note> to you; and "Amen" in the Hebrew language means **Truth**. That He Himself is the AMEN, see Revelation 3:14, and the TRUTH, John 14:6. When the learned of this century are consulted as to what they understand by "the Word" in John 1:1, they say it means the Word in its pre-eminence; and what else is the "Word in its pre-eminence" than Divine Truth? From these things it is clear that the Lord is also now going to appear in the Word. The reason He will not appear in Person is because, after His ascension into heaven, He is in a **Glorified Human** <term>original: *Humano glorificato*; the resurrected, Divine body of the Lord which transcends physical limitations.</term>, and in this He cannot appear to any man unless He first opens the eyes of that person's spirit; and these cannot be opened in anyone who is in evils and the resulting falsities—thus, not in any of the "goats" whom He places on the left. Therefore, when He manifested Himself to the disciples, He first opened their eyes, for it is written: *And their eyes were opened, and they knew Him, but He became invisible to* <note>The text ends mid-sentence; the catchword "iis" (them) indicates the sentence continues: "...to them." This refers to the story of the disciples on the road to Emmaus in Luke 24:31.</note>

...them, Luke 24:31. A similar thing happened with the women at the Tomb after the resurrection; this is why they then saw Angels sitting in the tomb and speaking with them, whom no man can see with the material eye. That not even the Apostles, before the Lord’s resurrection, saw the Lord in His glorified Humanity with bodily eyes, but in the spirit—which appears after waking as if in a dream—is evident from His transformation <note>original: "transformatione"; this refers to the Transfiguration on the mount.</note> before Peter, James, and John, in that they were then "heavy with sleep," Luke 9:32. Therefore it is vain to believe that the Lord is to appear in the cloud of Heaven in Person; rather, He appears in the Word, which is from Him, and thus is Himself.

778. Every man is his own love and his own intelligence, and whatever proceeds from him draws its essence from those two essentials or properties of his life; for this reason, Angels know a man for what he essentially is from a brief interaction with him—from the *Sound* they know his love, and from his *Speech* they know his intelligence. The cause is that the two universals of every man's life are the will and the understanding; the Will is the receptacle and dwelling-place of his love, and the Understanding is the receptacle and dwelling-place of his intelligence. Therefore, all things that proceed from a man, whether action or speech, constitute the man and are the man himself. In a similar way, but in a super-eminent degree, the Lord is Divine Love and Divine Wisdom, or what is the same, Divine Good and Divine Truth; for His Will is of Divine love, and Divine Love is of His Will, and His Intellect is Divine Wisdom, and Divine Wisdom is His Intellect. The human Form is the container of these. From these things it can be understood how the Lord is the Word <note>The "Word" here refers to the *Logos* or the Holy Scripture as the embodiment of Divine Truth.</note>. On the contrary, however, he who is against the Word—that is, against the Divine Truth therein, and consequently against the Lord and His Church—is his own evil and his own falsity, both as to his mind and as to the effects resulting from his body, which relate to his actions and speech.

->**That this Second Coming of the Lord is effected through a man, before whom He manifested Himself in Person, and whom He filled with His spirit, to teach the Doctrines of the New Church through the Word from Him.**<-

779. Since the Lord cannot manifest Himself in Person, as has been shown just above, and yet He predicted that He would Come and establish a new Church, which is the New Jerusalem, it follows that He would do this through a man who is able not only to receive the Doctrines of this Church in his understanding but also to publish them in print <note>original: "typis evulgare"; literally to make known by types/printing.</note>. That the Lord manifested Himself before Me, His servant, and sent me to this office, and that after this He opened the sight of my Spirit and thus introduced me into the spiritual World, and granted me to see the Heavens and the Hells, and also to speak with angels and spirits—and this now continually for many years—I testify in truth. Likewise, I testify that from the first day of that calling, I have not received anything regarding the Doctrines of that Church from any Angel, but from the Lord Alone, while I read the Word.

780. To the end that the Lord might be constantly present, He revealed to me the spiritual Sense <term>spiritual Sense: the hidden, inner meaning of the Bible that Swedenborg claimed to uncover</term> of His Word, in which Divine Truth is in its own light, and in this light He is continually present. For His presence in the Word comes from no other source than through the spiritual Sense; through the light of this sense He passes into the shadow in which the Sense of the letter <note>The "Sense of the letter" refers to the literal, historical, or physical text of the Bible.</note> exists, much like what happens with the light of the Sun during the day when a cloud intervenes. That the Sense of the letter of the Word is like a cloud, and the spiritual Sense is glory, and the Lord Himself is the Sun from which the Light comes—and that thus the Lord is the Word—has been demonstrated above. That the "Glory" in which He is to come (Matthew 24:30) signifies Divine Truth in its own light,

## *That by the New Heaven and the New Earth, and the New Jerusalem descending from there in the Revelation, this is understood.*

781. It is read in the <term>Revelation</term>, *"I saw a <term>New Heaven</term> and a <term>New Earth</term>, for the former heaven and the former earth had passed away. And I, John, saw the <term>Holy City, New Jerusalem</term>, descending from God out of Heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her Husband,"* Chapter 21:1, 2. Something similar is also read in <term>Isaiah</term>: *"Behold, I create a new heaven and a new earth; the former things shall not be remembered; rejoice and exult forever, for behold, I am about to create <term>Jerusalem</term> as an exultation, and her people as a joy,"* 65:17, 18. It has been revealed earlier in this chapter that a <term>New Heaven</term> is being formed by the Lord today from those Christians who acknowledged in the world, and were able to acknowledge after their departure from the world, that the Lord is the God of Heaven and Earth, according to His own words in Matthew, Chapter 28:18.

782. The reason the <term>New Church</term> is understood by the <term>New Jerusalem</term> descending from God out of Heaven (Revelation 21) is because <term>Jerusalem</term> was the metropolis in the land of Canaan; there was the Temple and the Altar, and there the sacrifices were performed—thus, it was the site of Divine Worship itself, to which every male of the whole land was commanded to come three times a year. Furthermore, it is because the Lord was in <term>Jerusalem</term>, taught in His Temple, and afterwards glorified His Humanity there; from this, it follows that <term>Jerusalem</term> signifies the Church. That the Church is understood by <term>Jerusalem</term> is clearly evident from the Prophetic books in the Old Testament concerning the <term>New Church</term> to be established by the Lord, in that she is called <term>Jerusalem</term> there. The passages themselves will be cited, from which anyone endowed with interior reason can see that the Church is what is meant. Let these be the passages: *"Behold, I create a <term>NEW HEAVEN AND A NEW EARTH</term>, the former things shall not be remembered; behold, I am <term>ABOUT TO CREATE JERUSALEM</term> as an exultation, and her people as a joy, that I may exult over <term>JERUSALEM</term> and rejoice over my people. ...they shall call them, *The Holy People, The Redeemed of <term>Jehovah</term> <note>The personal name of God in the Hebrew Bible, often translated as "LORD." Jehovah has comforted His people, He has redeemed* JERUSALEM, Isaiah 52:1, 2, 6, 9. *Sing, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of* JERUSALEM; *be glad with all your heart; the King of Israel is in your midst; you shall not fear evil anymore; He will rejoice over you with joy; He will rest in His love; He will joy over you with singing; I will make you a name and a praise among all the people of the earth,* Zephaniah 3:14–17, 20. Thus said <term>Jehovah</term> your Redeemer, saying to JERUSALEM, *You shall be inhabited,* Isaiah 44:24, 26. Thus said <term>Jehovah</term>, *I will return to Zion, and will dwell in the midst of* JERUSALEM; *whence* JERUSALEM *shall be called the City of Truth, and the Mountain of <term>Jehovah of Hosts</term> <note>original: "Jehovæ Zebaoth"</note>, the Mountain of Holiness,* Zechariah 8:3, 20–23. *Then you shall know that I am Jehovah your God, dwelling in Zion My holy mountain; and* JERUSALEM *shall be holiness: and it shall come to pass in that day, the mountains shall drop down new wine, and the hills shall flow with milk; and* JERUSALEM *shall remain from generation to generation,* Joel 3:17–21. *In that day the branch of Jehovah shall be for beauty and glory; and it shall come to pass, that he who is left in Zion, and he who remains in Jerusalem, shall be called Holy, everyone written for life in* JERUSALEM, Isaiah 4:2, 3. *In the last days the mountain of the house of Jehovah shall be established as the head of the mountains, for out of Zion shall go forth the law <note>original: "Doctrina"</note>, and the word of Jehovah from* JERUSALEM, Micah 4:1, 2, 8. *At that time they shall call* JERUSALEM *the Throne of Jehovah; and all nations shall be gathered to the Name of Jehovah, to* JERUSALEM; *neither shall they walk anymore after the stubbornness of their evil heart,* Jeremiah 3:17. *Look upon Zion, the city of our appointed feasts; your eyes shall see* JERUSALEM, *a quiet habitation, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down; its stakes shall never be removed, nor shall any of its cords be broken,* Isaiah 33:20. See also elsewhere, as in Isaiah 24:3; Chapter 37:32; Chapter 66:10–14; Zechariah 12:3, 6–10; Chapter 14:8, 11, 12, 21; Malachi 3:2, 4; Psalm 122:1–7; Psalm 130:4, 5, 6.

That by "Jerusalem" in these passages is understood the Church to be established by the Lord, and not the Jerusalem inhabited by the Jews, is evident from every detail of its description in the places cited. For instance, it says that <term>Jehovah God</term> will create a New Heaven and a New Earth, and also then a New Jerusalem; and that this city will be a crown of beauty and a royal diadem; that it is to be called Holiness, the City of Truth, the Throne of <term>Jehovah</term>, a quiet habitation, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down; that there the wolf and the lamb shall feed together; and it is said that there the mountains shall drop down new wine, and the hills flow with milk, and that it shall remain from generation to generation; besides many other things, such as that the people there are Holy, everyone written for life, and shall be called the Redeemed of <term>Jehovah</term>. Furthermore, in all these places, the subject is the <term>Advent of the Lord</term> <note>The coming or arrival of God into the world.</note>, especially His **Second Advent**, when Jerusalem will become such as is there described; for previously she was not married, that is, made the <term>Bride and Wife of the Lamb</term>, as is said of the **New Jerusalem** in the Revelation.

The former church, or the church of today, is what is understood by "Jerusalem" in Daniel, and its beginning is described there by these words: *"Know and perceive, from the going forth of the word to restore and to build* JERUSALEM *unto Messiah the Prince, shall be seven weeks; afterward, in sixty-two weeks, the street and the trench shall be restored and built, but in troublesome times,"* Chapter 9:25. But its end is described there by these words: *"At last, upon the wing of abominations shall be desolation, and even until the <term>consummation</term> <note>The "consummation of the age" refers to the end of a specific spiritual era or church, preceding the start of a new one.</note> and that which is determined shall be poured out upon the devastation,"* verse 27. These last words are those understood by the Lord’s words in Matthew: *"When you see the abomination of desolation predicted by Daniel the prophet, standing in the holy place, let him who reads note it well,"* Chapter 24:15. That "Jerusalem" in the places cited above did not mean the Jerusalem inhabited by the Jews can be seen from the places in the Word where it is said of the latter that it was utterly lost and to be destroyed, as in Jeremiah 5:1.

783. That the Church is the Lord's, and that from the Spiritual Marriage (which is the marriage of Good and Truth), the Lord is called the Bridegroom and Husband, and the Church is called the Bride and Wife, is known to Christians from the Word, especially from these passages: "John said of the Lord, *He who has the* <term>BRIDE</term> *is the* <term>BRIDEGROOM</term>, *but the friend of the* <term>BRIDEGROOM</term> *is he who stands and hears Him, and rejoices because of the* <term>BRIDEGROOM’S</term> *voice,* John III: 29. 784. That a New Heaven is formed before a New Church on earth is according to Divine Order; for the Church is both Internal and External, and the Internal Church makes one with the Church in Heaven (and thus with Heaven itself). The Internal must be formed before the External, and afterwards the External through the Internal; that this is so is a matter known among the Clergy in the world. In the same measure as this New Heaven—which constitutes the Internal of the Church in man—grows, the New Jerusalem (that is, the New Church) descends from that Heaven. Therefore, this cannot happen in a single moment, but takes place as the falsities of the previous Church are removed. For anything new cannot enter where falsities have previously been implanted, unless those falsities are uprooted. This will happen first among the Clergy, and so among the Laity; for the Lord said, *No one puts new wine into old wineskins, otherwise the wineskins burst and the wine is spilled; but they put new wine into new wineskins, and both are preserved together*, Matthew IX: 17, Mark II: 22, Luke V: 37, 38. That these things do not happen until the <term>Consummation of the Age</term> <note>original: "Consummatio sæculi." This refers to the end-time of a specific church era or "dispensation," rather than the physical destruction of the world.</note> (by which is meant the end of the Church), is evident from these words of the Lord: *Jesus said, the Kingdom of the Heavens is like a man sowing good seed in his field; but while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares, and went away; when the blade sprang up, then the tares appeared also; the servants came and said to him, do you want us to go and gather the tares? But he said, No, lest while gathering the tares you uproot the wheat with them; let both grow together until the harvest, and at the time of harvest I will say to the reapers, gather the tares first and bind them in bundles to be burned, but gather the wheat into my barn. The harvest is the Consummation of the Age; just as the tares are gathered and burned in the fire, so shall it be in the Consummation of the Age*, Matthew XIII: 24 to 30, 39, 40. By the "wheat" there is meant the truths and goods of the New Church, and by the "tares" the falsities and evils of the previous one. That the "Consummation of the Age" means the end of the Church, may be seen in the first article of this treatise.

785. That there is an Internal and an External in every thing, and that the external depends on the internal just as the body depends on its soul, is evident from every single thing in the world when properly examined. In man this is manifest: his entire body comes from his mind, and thus in every single thing that proceeds from a man, there is an internal and an external. In his every action is the Will of the mind, and in his every speech is the Understanding of the mind; likewise in his every Sensation. In every bird and beast—even in every insect and worm—there is an internal and an external. So too in every tree, plant, and sprout; yes, even in every stone... <note>The text cuts off here at the catchword "lapide" (stone).</note>

...and the dust of the ground; to illustrate this, a few examples concerning the silkworm, the bee, and dust are sufficient. The internal of the silkworm is that from which its external is driven to prepare silk, and afterward to fly forth as a butterfly. The internal of the bee is that from which its external is driven to suck honey from flowers and to build cells into wonderful forms. The internal of the dust of the ground <note>Swedenborg uses the term "pulvisculus" (fine dust) here to refer to the pollen of plants, which was a developing concept in 18th-century botany.</note>, from which its external is driven, is its impulse to fertilize the female; it exhales from its small womb something that introduces itself into the innermost parts of the female, and this produces fruit, and that internal follows its growth until the new seed is formed. The same occurs in opposite things, in which there is also an internal and an external, such as in the spider: its internal, from which its external is driven, is the faculty and the resulting inclination to build an ingenious web, from the center of which it may lay snares for flies that fly into it, which it then eats. It is similar in every other harmful worm, as well as in every serpent, and also in every wild beast of the forest; and likewise in every impious, cunning, and deceitful man.

## *That this New Church is the Crown of all the Churches which have existed until now in the world.*

786. That there have been four Churches in general on this Earth since the beginning—one before the Flood, the second after the Flood, the third the Israelitish Church, and the fourth named the Christian Church—has been shown above. And because all Churches depend on the knowledge and acknowledgment of One God, with whom the person of the Church can be joined, and since all four Churches were not in that truth, it follows that one Church is to succeed those four, which will know and acknowledge one God. The Divine Love of God had no other end in view when He created the world than to join man to Himself and Himself to man, and thus to dwell with man. The reason the prior Churches were not in the truth is that the <term>Most Ancient Church</term> <note>The era before the Great Flood.</note>, which was before the flood, worshiped an invisible God, with whom no conjunction is possible. The <term>Ancient Church</term> <note>The era following the Flood.</note>, which was after the flood, did likewise. The Israelitish Church worshiped Jehovah, who in Himself is the Invisible God (Exodus 33:18 to 23), but under a human form which Jehovah God put on through an Angel, in which He was seen by Moses, Abraham, Sarah, Hagar, Gideon, Joshua, and sometimes by the Prophets. This Human form was a representation of the Lord who was to come, and because this was representative, therefore everything in their Church was made representative. It is well known that the Sacrifices and the rest of their worship represented the Lord who was to come, and that these were set aside when He came. But the fourth Church, which is called the Christian Church, acknowledged one God indeed with the lips, but in three persons, each of whom individually or by himself was God; thus they acknowledged a divided Trinity, and not one united in one Person. From this, an idea of three Gods remained in the mind, even though the words "one God" were on the lips. Furthermore, the teachers of the Church, from the very doctrine they composed after the Council of Nicaea <note>The council held in 325 AD which established the orthodox definition of the Trinity.</note>, teach that one must believe in God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Spirit, all invisible, because they existed in a similar Divine Essence before the world began; and yet with an invisible God, as was said above, no conjunction is possible. They do not yet know that the one God, who is invisible, came into the world and assumed the Human, not only to redeem men, but also to become visible, and thus capable of being joined to them. For it is written: <term>THE WORD WAS WITH GOD, AND GOD WAS THE WORD, AND THE WORD WAS MADE FLESH</term> <note>original: "VERBUM ERAT APUD DEUM, & DEUS ERAT VERBUM, & VERBUM CARO FACTUM EST"</note> (John 1:1, 14); and in Isaiah: <term>A child is born to us, and a son is given to us, whose Name is GOD, HERO, FATHER OF ETERNITY</term> <note>original: "Puer natus est nobis, & Filius datus est nobis, cujus Nomen, DEUS, Heros; PATER ÆTERNITATIS"</note> (Chapter 9:5/6). And in the Prophets many times it is said that Jehovah Himself would come into the world and would be the Redeemer, which He also became in the Human which He assumed.

# THE NEW HEAVENS AND THE NEW CHURCH

787. The reason why this New Church is the **Crown of all the Churches** that have existed in the world until now is because it will worship one visible God, in whom is the invisible God, just as the soul is in the body. The reason a conjunction <note>original: "conjunctio"; here referring to a spiritual connection or union</note> of God with man is possible in this way and no other is because man is a natural being, and therefore thinks in a natural way. This connection must exist within his thought and thus within the affection of his love, and this occurs when a person thinks of God as a Man. Connection with an invisible God is like the connection of the eye's vision with the vastness of the universe, the end of which it cannot see; or like sight in the middle of the ocean, which falls upon the air and the sea and is lost. But a connection with a visible God is like seeing a man in the air or sea who stretches out his hands and invites one into his arms. For all connection of God with man must also be reciprocal—of man with God—and this second, reciprocal part is not possible except with a visible God. That God was not visible before He assumed the <term>Human</term> <note>original: "Humanum"; Swedenborg uses this term to refer to the body and soul the Lord took on in the world, which became Divine.</note> is taught by the Lord Himself in John: *You have never heard the Father's voice, nor seen His form* (Chapter 5:37); and in Moses: *That no one can see God and live* (Exodus 33:20). However, that He is seen through His Human is stated in John: *No one has ever seen God; the only-begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, He has revealed Him* (Chapter 1:18); and in the same: *Jesus said, I am the way, the truth, and the life; no one comes to the Father except through Me; he who knows Me knows the Father, and he who sees Me, sees the Father* (Chapter 14:6, 7, 9). That there is a connection with the invisible God through the visible One—that is, through the Lord—He Himself teaches in these passages: *Jesus said, abide in Me, and I in you; he who abides in Me, and I in him, bears much fruit* (John 15:4, 5). *In that day you will know that I am in the Father, and you in Me, and I in you* (John 14:20). *The glory which You gave Me, I have given them, that they may be one even as we are one, I in them and You in Me... that the love with which You loved Me may be in them, and I in them* (John 17:21, 22, 23, 26; also Chapter 6:56). Furthermore, He teaches that the Father and He are one, and that one must believe in Him to have eternal life. It has been shown many times above that salvation depends on this connection with God.

788. That this Church is to succeed the Churches that have existed since the beginning of the world, and that it will endure for ages of ages, and will be the Crown of all previous Churches, was prophesied by Daniel. First, when he recounted and explained to Nebuchadnezzar his dream of the four kingdoms (by which are understood the four Churches represented by the statue he saw), saying: *In the days of these, the God of the heavens shall cause a kingdom to arise which shall not perish for ages... and it shall consume all those kingdoms, but it shall stand for ages* (Chapter 2:44); and that this would happen through *a Stone made into a great Rock filling the whole Earth* (Verse 35). By a "Rock" in the <term>Word</term> <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures.</note> is understood the Lord in terms of Divine Truth. The same prophet says elsewhere: *I was watching in the visions of the night, and behold, with the clouds of the heavens, one like the Son of Man; and to Him was given dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, and all peoples, nations, and languages shall worship Him; His dominion is an everlasting dominion which shall not pass away, and His kingdom one that shall not perish* (Chapter 7:13, 14). He said this after seeing four great beasts ascending from the sea (Verse 3), by which the four previous Churches were also represented. That these things were prophesied by Daniel concerning this present time is clear from his words in Chapter 12:4, as well as from the Lord's words in Matthew 24:15, 30. Similar things are said in the <term>Apocalypse</term> <note>The Book of Revelation.</note>: *The seventh angel sounded, then there were great voices from heaven, saying, the kingdoms of our Lord and of His Christ have been made, and He shall reign for ages of ages* (Chapter 11:15).

789. Furthermore, the rest of the prophets have predicted in many places what this Church would be like, from which these few examples will be brought forward. In Zechariah: *There shall be one day, known to Jehovah, not day nor night, for around the time of evening there shall be light: in that day living waters shall go out from Jerusalem... and Jehovah shall be King over all the earth; in that day Jehovah shall be one, and His name one* (14:7, 8, 9). 790. What this future Church is to be like is described at length in the Revelation, which deals with the end of the former Church and the rise of the New.
