## OF THE NEW HEAVEN AND THE NEW CHURCH

<insert>That those who come to the marriage supper of the Lamb (*Revelation* 19:9), this was done in the Month of June, on the 19th Day, in the Year 1770. This was understood by these words of the Lord: "He shall send His Angels, and they shall gather together His elect from the ends of the heavens even to the ends of them" (*Matthew* 24:31).</insert>

792. The Spiritual World was discussed in a specific work entitled *HEAVEN and HELL*, in which many things of that world were described; and since every person enters that world after death, the state of people there was also described. Who does not know, or cannot know, that a person lives after death, because he was born human, created in the image of God, and because the Lord teaches this in His Word? But what kind of life he will have in the future has been unknown until now. It was believed that he would then be a Soul, of which people held no other idea than as if it were ether or air, so that it is a *breath* <note>original Latin: *Pneuma*</note> such as a person breathes out from the mouth when he dies, in which, however, his life-force resides; but they thought it would be without sight like that of the eye, without hearing like that of the ear, and without speech like that of the mouth. Yet, a person after death is just as much a human being, and such a human being that he does not know otherwise than that he is still in the former world. He sees, hears, and speaks as in the former world; he walks, runs, and sits as in the former world; he lies down, sleeps, and wakes as in the former world; he eats and drinks as in the former world; he enjoys conjugial delight <note>Swedenborg uses the term "conjugial" to refer specifically to spiritual, eternal marriage love, distinguishing it from merely physical "conjugal" union</note> as in the former world; in a word, he is a human being in each and every respect. From this it is clear that death is not extinction, but a continuation of life, and that it is merely a transition.

793. That a person is equally a human being after death, although he does not then appear before the eyes of the material body, can be established from the Angels seen by Abraham, Hagar, Gideon, Daniel, and certain Prophets; from the Angels seen in the Lord’s Tomb, and afterwards many times by John, concerning whom we read in the REVELATION; and especially from the Lord Himself, who showed that He was a Man by touch and by eating, and yet He became invisible before their eyes. Who can be so delirious as not to acknowledge that, even though invisible, He was equally a Man? The reason they saw Him was because the eyes of their Spirit were then opened; and when these are opened, the things that are in the spiritual world appear just as clearly as those that are in the natural world. The difference between a person in the natural world and a person in the spiritual world is that the latter is clothed in a substantial Body, while the former is in a material Body, within which is his substantial body; and the substantial person sees the substantial person just as clearly as the material person sees the material person. But the substantial person cannot see the material person, nor the material person the substantial person, because of the difference between the material and the substantial, the nature of which can be described, but not in a few words.

794. From the things seen over so many years, I can report the following: that in the spiritual world there are lands just as in the natural world, and that there are plains and valleys, as well as mountains and hills, and also springs and rivers; that there are paradises, gardens, groves, and forests; that there are cities, and in them palaces and houses; also that there are writings and books; that there are employments and trades; and that there are gold, silver, and precious stones; in a word, that there are each and every thing that exists in the natural world, but those in Heaven are infinitely more perfect. But the difference is that all things seen in the spiritual world are created in a moment by the Lord—such as houses, paradises, food, and the rest—and that they are created according to their correspondence <note><term>correspondence</term>: the spiritual law where outward environments perfectly reflect the inner states (affections and thoughts) of the inhabitants</note> with the interiors of the Angels and Spirits, which are their affections and the thoughts from them; whereas all things seen in the natural world arise and grow from seed.

795. Since this is the case, and I have spoken there daily with the nations and peoples of this world—not only with those in Europe, but also with those in Asia and Africa, and thus with those of various religions—I will add, as a <term>Coronis</term> <note>original: "Coronidis loco"; a Greek term meaning a finishing touch or an appendix to a work</note> to this work, a brief description of the state of some of them. It must be held that the state of every nation and people in general, as well as of individuals in particular, in the spiritual world is according to their acknowledgment and worship of God. All who acknowledge God in their heart, and from this time forward those who acknowledge the Lord Jesus Christ as God the Redeemer and Savior, are in heaven; those who do not acknowledge Him are beneath heaven, where they are instructed. Those who receive Him are raised into heaven, and those who do not receive Him are cast down into hell. Among these latter are those who, like the <term>Socinians</term> <note>Followers of Fausto Sozzini who denied the divinity of Christ, viewing him only as an exemplary man.</note>, have approached only God the Father, and those who, like the <term>Arians</term> <note>Followers of Arius who believed Jesus was a created being, subordinate to God the Father.</note>, have denied the Divinity of the Lord’s Humanity. For the Lord said, **I AM THE WAY, THE TRUTH, AND THE LIFE; NO ONE COMES TO THE FATHER EXCEPT THROUGH ME**; and to Philip, who wished to see the Father, He said **THAT HE WHO SEES AND KNOWS ME, SEES AND KNOWS THE FATHER** (John 14:6 and following).

## CONCERNING LUTHER, MELANCHTHON, AND CALVIN IN THE SPIRITUAL WORLD.

796. I have frequently spoken with these three leaders, who were the reformers of the Christian Church, and have thereby been instructed as to what the state of their lives has been from the beginning until today. As for LUTHER, from the first moment he entered the spiritual world, he was a most bitter propagator and defender of his own dogmas, and as the multitude of those from Earth who agreed with and favored him grew, his zeal for them increased. A house was given to him there, similar to the one he had in his physical life in Eisleben <note>The town in modern-day Germany where Martin Luther was born and died.</note>. In the middle of it, he erected a slightly elevated throne on which he sat, and through an open door, he admitted listeners. He arranged these people into ranks: he took those most favorable to him into the closest circle, and placed those less favorable behind them. He spoke continuously, and occasionally permitted questions, so that he might take up the thread of a finished speech again from a new starting point. From this general favor, he finally became imbued with a POWER OF PERSUASION, which in the spiritual world has such efficacy that it cannot be resisted by anyone, nor can anyone speak against what is said. But because this was a type of spell <note>original: "incantationis"</note> used by the ancients, he was later strictly forbidden from speaking further from that Persuasion; afterwards, he taught as before, from memory and understanding at the same time. Such Persuasion, which is a species of spell, flows from self-love, from which it finally becomes such that when anyone contradicts, the person not only attacks the matter in question but also the person themselves. This was the state of his life until the Last Judgment, which took place in the spiritual world in the year 1757. But a year after that, he was moved from his first house to another, and at the same time into another state. Since he heard here that I, who am in the natural world, was speaking with those in the spiritual world, he came to me among several others. After some questions and answers, he perceived that today is the end of the former Church and the beginning of the New Church, of which Daniel prophesied and the Lord Himself foretold in the Gospels, and that this New Church is understood by the New Jerusalem in the Apocalypse, and by the eternal Gospel which the Angel flying in the midst of heaven preached to those dwelling upon the earth (Revelation 14:6). Hearing this, he became very indignant and scolded me. But as he perceived that a New Heaven was being formed by those who acknowledge the Lord alone as the God of Heaven and Earth, according to His words in Matthew 28:18, and as he noticed the groups gathered daily around him were diminishing, his scolding ceased. He then drew closer to me and began to speak more familiarly; and after he was convinced that...

At last, after being convinced, he began to favor these truths, and then more and more to confirm himself in the truths upon which the New Church is established. I heard him saying, "Do not wonder that I seized upon faith alone as justifying, and excluded charity from its spiritual essence, and also took away all free will in spiritual things from men, besides many other things which depend on faith alone once accepted, like links in a chain; for my purpose was to be severed from the Roman Catholics, and I could not otherwise reach and obtain that goal. Therefore, I do not wonder that I went astray, but I do wonder that one person who was out of his mind could have produced so many others just as delirious." He looked sideways at some dogmatic writers of his time, famous in their day and faithful followers of his doctrine, noting that they did not see the contradictions in Holy Scripture, even though they are standing right there. It was told to me by examining angels that this leader, more than many others who confirmed themselves in justification by faith alone, is in a state of conversion, because in his childhood, before he entered upon the Reformation, he was imbued with the dogma of the pre-eminence of charity; for this reason, he taught so excellently about charity both in his writings and in his sermons. From this it follows that the faith of justification was implanted in his external natural man, but was not rooted in his internal spiritual man. It happens differently, however, with those who in their childhood confirm themselves against the spirituality of charity, which also happens of itself when justification by faith alone is established through confirmations. I spoke with the Prince of Saxony <note>This likely refers to Frederick III, "the Wise," or John, "the Steadfast," Electors of Saxony and patrons of Luther.</note> with whom Luther had been in the world; he told me that he had often chided Luther, especially for separating charity from faith and declaring the latter to be saving and not the former, when yet Holy Scripture not only joins those two universal means of salvation, but Paul even prefers charity to faith, saying that there are three—faith, hope, and charity—and that the greatest of these is charity (*1 Corinthians 13:13*); but Luther as often replied that he could not do otherwise because of the Roman Catholics. This Prince is among the happy.

797. The reason I could not speak with him as often or as closely was that he could not approach in the same way, because he had devoted his study only to justification by faith alone, and not to charity; and I was surrounded by angelic spirits who are in charity, and these blocked his access to me. I heard that as soon as he entered the spiritual world, a house was prepared for him similar to the house in which he lived in the world. This happens to most newcomers, so that they do not know but that they are still in the natural world, and that the time elapsed since death was merely like a sleep. In his room, everything was also similar—a similar table, a similar desk with drawers, and also a library. Therefore, as soon as he arrived there, just as if he had awakened from a sleep, he sat down at the table and continued writing, specifically about justification by faith alone, and continued this for several days, saying nothing at all about charity. When the angels perceived this, he was asked through messengers why he did not also write about charity. He replied that there was nothing of the Church in charity, for if charity were received as an essential attribute of the Church, man would also claim for himself the merit of justification and thus of salvation, and so would also deprive faith of its spiritual essence. From this time he was translated interiorly toward the South-West, and so into another House, from which he spoke with me, saying that now his *Writing* concerning Charity does not vanish as before, but appears obscurely on the following day. I wondered at this: that when he walks, his steps are heard as a thumping, like those who walk in iron shoes upon a stone floor. 

To these things must be added that when some newcomers from the World entered his Chamber for the sake of speaking with him and seeing him, he would call one of the magical spirits, who by means of fantasies could induce various beautiful appearances, and who then adorned his Chamber with decorations and rose-colored tapestries, and also with the appearance of a Library in the middle. But indeed, as soon as they left, those appearances vanished, and the former lime-plastering and emptiness returned—but this was while he was in his former State.

He was a natural man, believing nothing except what he could gather from the objects of the bodily senses; from this it happened that he concluded all the dogmas of his faith from his own intelligence and not from the Word. If he cited the Word, he did so for the sake of the common people, so that they might favor him with their assent. II. After this first period, having been left by the angels, he wandered about and inquired where those were who from ancient times believed in <term>PREDESTINATION</term> <note>The doctrine that God has foreordained the eternal destiny of every soul</note>. It was told to him that they were far from here, shut away and covered over, and that there was no way to reach them except from the back side under the earth. However, the disciples of <term>Gottschalk</term> <note>original: "Godoskalchi"; refers to Gottschalk of Orbais, a 9th-century monk who taught a strict form of predestination</note> still wander about freely and sometimes gather in a place called <term>Pyris</term> in the spiritual language. Because he desired their company, he was led to the assembly where some of them were standing; and when he came among them, he was in the delight of his heart and formed an interior friendship with them. III. But after the followers of Gottschalk were led away to their brothers in the cavern, he became weary; therefore he sought a refuge here and there, and finally was received into a certain society where there were only simple people, and among them also religious ones. When he noticed that they knew nothing and could grasp nothing regarding <term>Predestination</term>, he betook himself to a corner of that society and hid there for a long time, nor did he open his mouth about any matter of the Church. This was provided so that he might recede from his error concerning Predestination, and so that the ranks of those might be filled who, after the <term>Synod of Dort</term> <note>original: "Dodrectanam Synodum"; a 1617–1619 gathering of the Reformed Church that solidified the "five points of Calvinism"</note>, adhered to that detestable heresy, all of whom were successively banished to the cavern to join their companions. IV. Finally, when he was sought by modern Predestinarians to find where <term>Calvin</term> was, after a search he was found on the outskirts of a certain society consisting of mere simpletons. For this reason, he was called away to a certain <term>Magistrate</term> <note>original: "Prætorem"</note> who was enticed by similar dregs [of doctrine]; this man therefore received him into his house and guarded him, and this continued until the <term>New Heaven</term> <note>original: "Novum Cælum"; in Swedenborg’s theology, a spiritual reorganization preceding a new era of the Church</note> began to be established by the Lord. At that time, because the Magistrate who was his guardian was cast out along with his crowd, Calvin betook himself to a certain house of ill repute and stayed there for some time. V. And because he then enjoyed the freedom of wandering about and also of approaching the dwelling where I was, it was granted to me to speak with him—firstly about the New Heaven which is being built today by those who acknowledge the Lord alone as the God of heaven and earth, according to His own words in Matthew Chapter 28:18; and that these believe that He and the Father are one (John 10:30); and that He is in the Father and the Father in Him; and that he who sees and knows Him, sees and knows the Father (John 14:6 to 11); and that thus there is one God in the Church as in heaven. To these things said by me, he at first remained silent as he was accustomed to do, but after half an hour he broke the silence and said: "Was not Christ a man, the son of Mary who was married to Joseph? How can a man be worshiped as God?" And I said, "Is not Jesus Christ our Redeemer and Savior, God and Man?" To which he replied, "He is God and Man, yet the Divinity is not His, but is the Father's." And I asked, "Where then is Christ?" He said, "He is in the lowest parts of heaven," which he confirmed by citing His humiliation before the Father and that He allowed Himself to be crucified. To this he added taunts against the worship of Him, which then broke into his memory from the world, the sum of which was that His worship is nothing other than <term>Idolatry</term> <note>The worship of an idol or physical image as God</note>. He wished to add unspeakable things about that worship, but the angels who were with me closed his lips. I, however, out of a zeal for converting him, said that the Lord our Savior is not only God and Man, but also that in Him God is Man and Man is God. And I confirmed this from Paul: *That in Him all the fullness of the Divinity dwells bodily* (Colossians 2:9); and from John: *That He is the true God and eternal life* (1 John 5:20, 21); then from these words of the Lord Himself: *That it is the will of the Father that everyone who believes in the Son should have eternal life, and that he who does not believe shall not see life, but the anger of God remains upon him* (John 3:36; Chapter 6:40); and moreover, that the symbolic Faith called <term>Athanasian</term> <note>The Athanasian Creed, which defines the Trinity and the Incarnation</note> dictates that in Christ, God and Man are not two, but one, and are in one Person, just as the soul and body are in one man. Faith, through which justification and salvation are achieved, has its inner sanctuary and shrine there. Does any man have Free Will in spiritual matters? Are not all things of salvation free gifts? Therefore, I hear and perceive arguments against these things—and thus against Predestination—as nothing other than belches from the stomach and as <term>stomach rumblings</term> <note>original: 'boribogmos'; a Greek-derived term for the rumbling of the bowels</note>. But I will give my own Confession, which is this: 'There is a God, and He is Almighty, and there is no salvation for any others than those who have been chosen and predestined by God the Father; everyone else is assigned to his own lot, that is, to his fate.'"

Upon hearing these things, I replied in a heat of indignation: "You speak unspeakable things; go away, evil spirit! Do you not know that you are in the spiritual world? Do you not know that there is a Heaven and there is a Hell, and that Predestination involves the idea that some are signed over to Heaven and some to Hell? That God created the greatest part of humanity for eternal damnation, and does not will that the greatest part be converted and live. I spoke afterward with some of those imprisoned in that cavern and asked about their lot; they said they were forced to work for their food, and that they were all enemies to one another, and that each one seeks a reason for doing evil to the other, which they do whenever they detect even a slight opening, and that this is the delight of their life. Furthermore, concerning Predestination and the Predestinarians, see what was written above in numbers 485 to 488.

## CONCERNING THE DUTCH IN THE SPIRITUAL WORLD

800. In the work **HEAVEN AND HELL**, it was recorded that Christians—among whom the Word is read and there is knowledge and acknowledgment of the Lord as Redeemer and Savior—occupy the center of the nations and peoples of the entire spiritual world. This is because the greatest spiritual light exists among them, and from that center, Light is propagated to all the surrounding areas, even to the furthest edges, according to the principles shown in the treatise on **SACRED SCRIPTURE** (above, numbers 267 to 272). Within this Christian center, the Reformed <note>Protestant groups such as the Lutherans and Calvinists</note> have been assigned places according to their reception of spiritual light from the Lord. Because the Dutch <note>original: 'Hollandi'</note> possess that light more deeply and fully joined to their natural light, and are thus more capable than others of receiving things belonging to reason, they have gained dwellings in that Christian <term>heartland</term> <note>original: 'Meditullio'; the central or innermost part</note> in the East and the South. They are in the East because of their capacity to receive spiritual Heat <note>symbolizing Love</note>, and in the South because of their capacity to receive spiritual Light <note>symbolizing Wisdom</note>. That the <term>Quarters</term> <note>original: 'Plagæ'; the four cardinal directions</note> in the spiritual world are not like those in the natural world, and that dwellings are assigned according to the reception of Faith and Love—with those excelling in Love in the East and those excelling in Intelligence in the South—may be seen in the work **HEAVEN AND HELL**, numbers 141 to 153.

801. The reason the Dutch are in those quarters of the Christian heartland is also because Commerce <note>original: 'Negotiatio'</note> is their <term>final love</term> <note>The primary purpose or goal that drives a person's life</note>, and money is a mediating love serving that end; such a love is spiritual. However, where money is the final love and commerce is the mediating love serving it—as is the case among the Jews—that love is merely natural and stems from avarice. The reason the love of trading is spiritual when it is the final goal is due to its use: it serves the common good, with which one's own good is indeed connected (and though the private good may seem more prominent because man thinks from his natural self, the end goal remains the service of trade). Everyone in heaven is regarded according to their final love; for the final love is like the Lord of a Kingdom or the master of a house, and all other loves are like its subjects and servants. Furthermore, the final love resides in the highest and innermost parts of the mind, while mediating loves are below and outside it, serving it at its command. The Dutch possess this spiritual love more than others. In contrast, the Jews possess an inverted love, which is why their love of trading is purely natural, containing nothing of the common good within it, but only private gain.

802. The Dutch cling more firmly to the principles of their religion than others and are not easily moved from them. Even if they are convinced that this or that point is not in agreement, they still do not concede, but turn away and remain unmoved; thus, they also distance themselves from the inner intuition of truth, for they keep their rational mind closed under obedience <note>Meaning they prioritize traditional religious loyalty over new logical insights</note>. Because they are like this, when they enter the spiritual world after death, they are prepared in a unique way to receive the spiritual things of heaven, which are Divine Truths. They are not simply "taught," because they do not easily receive instruction; instead, Heaven is described to them as it is, and then they are allowed to ascend there and see it. Then, whatever agrees with their <term>disposition</term> <note>original: 'genio'; their inherent character or spirit</note> is infused into them. Having been sent down again, they return to their own people with a full desire for Heaven. If they then do not receive this Truth—that God is one in Person and Essence, and that this God is the Lord the Redeemer and Savior, and that the Divine Trinity is in Him—and also this Truth, that Faith and Charity achieve nothing through mere knowledge and talk without a life according to them, and that these are given by the Lord when people perform repentance after self-examination; if they turn away from these things when taught, and persist in thinking of God as three persons and of religion as a mere matter of fact, they are reduced to misery. Their commerce is taken away until they see themselves reduced to <term>extremity</term> <note>original: 'ad incitas'; a gambling or chess metaphor meaning a state where no further moves are possible, or utter ruin</note>. They are then led to those who, because they possess Divine Truths, live in abundance.

It also details how they are uniquely prepared for heaven through observation rather than direct instruction due to their firm adherence to traditional religious principles.</summary>

->UNIVERSA THEOLOGIA<-

# UNIVERSA THEOLOGIA

among everyone, and among those with whom trade flourishes, a thought is instilled into them from Heaven regarding the source of their condition. At the same time, there is a reflection upon their Faith and upon their Life—that they should turn away from evils as sins. They also inquire and perceive, though only slightly, the harmony [of these thoughts] with their own thinking and reflection; this happens by turns. At last, they think to themselves that in order to escape from miseries, they must believe and live in the same way. Then, as they receive that Faith and live that life of Charity, they are granted wealth and a prosperity of life. In this way, those who led some life of Charity in the world are corrected by their own efforts and prepared for Heaven. These later become more steadfast than others, so much so that they could be called "Constancy" itself; nor do they allow themselves to be led away by any reasoning, fallacy, or obscurity introduced by sophistry, or from a distorted vision based only on confirmations. For they become more clear-sighted than they were before.

803. The **Teaching Doctors** in their academies study most intensely the mysteries of the current faith, especially those there who are called **Cocceians** <note>Followers of Johannes Cocceius (1603–1669), a Dutch theologian who emphasized the "Covenant of Grace" and a more mystical, biblical interpretation of theology.</note>. Because the dogma of **Predestination** inevitably grows out of those mysteries—and this was further established by the **Synod of Dordrecht** <note>An international church assembly held in 1618–1619 to settle a divisive controversy in the Dutch Reformed Church regarding Arminianism and Calvinist predestination.</note>—it is sown and implanted like a seed taken from the fruit of any tree and placed in a field. From this, it follows that the **Laity** talk much among themselves about Predestination, but in different ways: some embrace it with both hands, some with only one hand and with a smile, and some cast it away like a lizard-snake. For they are ignorant of the mysteries of faith from which that "viper" was hatched. The reason they are ignorant of these things is that they are intent upon their business; the mysteries of that faith may touch their intellect, but they do not penetrate it. Therefore, the dogma of Predestination among the laity, and also among the clergy, is like a statue in human form placed upon a rock in the sea, holding a large seashell in its hand that shines like gold. At this sight, some captains sailing past lower their sails out of honor and veneration; some merely wink at it and offer a greeting; and some hiss at it as if at a joke. It is also like an unknown bird from India perched upon a high tower: some swear it is a turtledove, some guess it is a rooster, and some swear and cry out that it is certainly an owl.

804. The **Dutch** are easily distinguished from others in the spiritual world because they appear in similar clothes to those they wore in the natural world—with the difference that those who have received Faith and Spiritual Life appear in brighter ones. The reason they appear in similar clothes is that they remain constant in the principles of their Religion, and everyone in the spiritual world is clothed according to those principles. Therefore, white garments made of **fine linen** <note>original: 'bysso'; fine white linen often symbolizes the "righteous acts of the saints" in biblical and Swedenborgian symbolism.</note> belong to those there who are in Divine Truths.

805. The cities in which the Dutch live are guarded in a unique way. All the streets in them are covered, and there are gates in the streets, for the purpose of preventing them from being looked at from the rocks and hills around them. This is done because of their inherent prudence in hiding their plans and not revealing their intentions; for in the spiritual world, such things are dragged out through "inspections" <note>In the spiritual world, seeing someone or looking into their home can reveal their internal state or secrets.</note>. When someone comes with the intention of exploring their state, he is led, when he is about to leave, to closed street gates, and thus he is led back and guided through many others—even to the point of extreme annoyance—and then he is let out. This is done so that he does not return. **WIVES** who affect command over their husbands live on one side of the city and do not meet with their husbands more often than they are invited, which is done in a civil manner. Then the husbands also lead them to houses where spouses live without one ruling over the other, showing them how decorated and clean their houses are, and how pleasant life is for them, and that these things come to them from mutual and **conjugial love** <term>conjugial love</term> <note>original: 'Amor conjugalis'; Swedenborg’s specific term for the spiritual and eternal love between a husband and wife, distinct from mere natural or physical attraction.</note>. Those wives who pay attention to these things and are affected by them desist from dominion and live together [with their husbands]. They then obtain a dwelling closer to the center and are called **Angels**. The reason is that truly conjugial Love is Heavenly Love, which is without dominion.

->NEW HEAVENS AND THE NEW CHURCH<-

## ON THE ENGLISH IN THE SPIRITUAL WORLD.

806. There are two states of thought in man, the External and the Internal; a man in the External state is in the natural world, and in the Internal state, he is in the spiritual world. These states make a single whole among the good, but they do not make a single whole among the wicked. What a man is like regarding his Internal is rarely apparent in the world, since from infancy he has learned to be moral and rational, and he loves to appear so; but in the spiritual world, it clearly appears what he is like, for a man is then a spirit, and the spirit is the Internal man. Now, because it has been granted to me to be in that world and to see there what the Internal men from one kingdom and another are like, I ought to reveal it, as it is of importance.

807. Regarding the English nation: the better among them are in the center of all Christians. The reason is that they possess an interior intellectual light. This does not appear to anyone in the natural world, but it appears conspicuously in the spiritual world. They derive this light from their freedom of speaking and writing, and through that, of thinking. Among others who are not in such freedom, that light—because it has no outlet—is clouded over. Truly, that light is not active of itself, but is made active by others, especially by men of reputation and authority; as soon as something is said by these leaders, that light shines forth. For this reason, <term>Governors</term> are set over them in the spiritual world, and priests of great reputation and distinguished talent are given to them, in whose judgments they acquiesce because of their natural disposition.

808. There is a similarity of minds among them, because of which they form familiarities with friends who are from their own country, and rarely with others; they also bring mutual help to one another and love sincerity. They are lovers of their country and zealots for its glory; they look upon foreigners much like a man on the roof of his palace looks through a <term>telescope</term> <note>original: *tubum opticum*</note> at those inhabiting and wandering outside the city. The politics of their kingdom occupy their minds and possess their hearts, sometimes to such an extent that they withdraw their spirits from the studies of higher judgment, through which superior intelligence is acquired. To be sure, those who attend such studies in <term>Lyceums</term> <note>Refers to universities or places of higher learning.</note> in their youth do imbibe these things; but they pass away like temporary phenomena. Yet, because of these studies, their rationality becomes alive and sparkles with light, from which they form beautiful images—just as a crystal prism turned toward the sun forms rainbows and tints a flat object with golden colors.

809. There are two great cities similar to London, into which most of the English come after death; I was permitted to see the first city and also to walk through it. The center of that city is where the meeting place of merchants is in London, called the <term>Exchange</term> <note>The Royal Exchange, the historic center of commerce in the City of London.</note>; the Governors dwell there. Above that center is the East; below it is the West; on the right side is the South, and on the left side is the North. In the Eastern quarter dwell those who, more than others, have led a life of charity; there are magnificent palaces there. In the Southern quarter dwell the wise, among whom are many splendid things. In the Northern quarter dwell those who, more than others, have loved freedom of speaking and writing. In the Western quarter dwell those who boast of <term>Justification by Faith Alone</term> <note>The theological doctrine that salvation is achieved through belief rather than through good works.</note>. To the right in this quarter is the entrance into this city, and also the exit from it; those who live evilly are sent out there. The priests who are in the West and teach that "Faith Alone" do not dare to enter the city through the great streets, but through the narrower alleys, because no other inhabitants are tolerated in the city itself except those who are in the <term>Faith of Charity</term>. I heard them complaining about the preachers from the West, that they construct their sermons with such art and eloquence, and involve that "Justification by Faith" (which is unknown to the listeners) in such a way that the people do not know whether good ought to be done or not. They preach faith as an intrinsic good and separate it from the good of charity, which they call "meritorious" and thus not acceptable to God. But when those who [dwell in the...]

They live in the Eastern and Southern quarters of the City, hear such sermons, and then leave the Temples; and the Preachers are afterwards deprived of their priesthood.

810. I later heard many reasons why those Preachers are deprived of their priesthood. They said that the primary reason is that they do not fashion their sermons from the Word and thus from the Spirit of God, but from their own rational light and thus from their own spirit. They do indeed take their beginnings, like preludes, from the Word, but they only touch these with their lips, and because these are not savory to them, they set them aside. They soon choose something "tasty" from their own intelligence, which they roll around in their mouths and turn over on their tongues like delicacies, and in this way they teach. They said that, as a result, there is no more spiritual content in their sermons than there is in the songs of <term>songbirds</term> <note>original: "oscinum" — birds whose songs or cries were used for divination, like ravens or crows</note>; and that they are decorated with allegories like "hairpieces beautifully curled" or "barley flour whitened over a bald head." 

The mystical parts of their sermons regarding **Justification through faith alone** they compared to the Quails cast from the sea over the camp of the sons of Israel, from which many thousands died (Numbers 11); but theological matters concerning **Charity and Faith together** they compared to Manna from Heaven. Once I heard their Priests speaking among themselves about "faith alone"; and I saw a certain Image formed by them which represented their "faith alone." In their own light—which was a light of fantasy—this appeared like a great Giant; but when light from Heaven was let in, it appeared above like a monster and below like a serpent. Upon seeing this, they drew back, and the image was thrown into a pond by those standing by.

811. Another large City, also called London, is not in the Christian center, but is situated far from it toward the north: into this city come those who are inwardly evil after death. In its center there is open communication with Hell, by which they are also absorbed from time to time.

812. From those of the English nation who are in the spiritual world, it has been perceived that they have a double Theology: one from the Doctrine of their faith, and the other from the Doctrine of Charity. The Doctrine of faith is held by those who are initiated into the priesthood; the Doctrine of Charity is held by many of the laity, especially those who live in Scotland and its borders. With these latter, the <term>Solifidians</term> <note>Those who believe in "faith alone" (from the Latin *sola fide*).</note> are afraid to start arguments, because the Scots fight them using both the Word and Reason. This Doctrine of Charity is found in the Prayer read every Sabbath day in the Temples before those who approach the **Sacrament of the Supper**, in which it is openly stated that if they are not in Charity, and do not shun evils as sins, they cast themselves into eternal damnation; and that otherwise, if they should approach Holy Communion, the Devil would enter into them as he did into Judas.

## ON THE GERMANS IN THE SPIRITUAL WORLD.

813. It is well known that the inhabitants of any Kingdom divided into many Provinces do not have a similar "genius" or character, and that they differ from one another in particular ways, just as the inhabitants of different climates across the globe differ generally. However, a common Character still reigns among those who are under one King and thus under one established Law. 

As for Germany, compared to the Kingdoms around it, it is divided into many Sovereignties. There is an Empire there, under whose general auspices everyone remains, but nonetheless, the Prince of each territory enjoys <term>despotic right</term> <note>In this context, Swedenborg refers to the absolute legal authority a Prince held over his specific territory within the Holy Roman Empire.</note> in his particular area; for there are larger and smaller Duchies, and each is like a Monarch in his own domain. Furthermore, Religion there is divided: in some Duchies are those called "Evangelicals" <note>Lutherans</note>, in some are the "Reformed" <note>Calvinists</note>, and in some are the "Pontificals" <note>Catholics</note>. Since there is such a diversity of authorities and religions at the same time, the Germans—in terms of their minds, inclinations, and lives—can be described from what is seen in the spiritual world with more difficulty than the nations and peoples elsewhere. But because a common Character still reigns everywhere among people of the same Language, that character can be seen and described to some extent from ideas gathered into one.

814. Since the Germans are under a despotic Government in each particular Duchy,

...they are, for that reason they do not exist in the **Freedom of speaking and writing** as the Dutch and British do; and when the freedom of speaking and writing is restrained, the **freedom of thinking**—that is, of perceiving things in their full breadth—is also held in restraint. For it is like the cistern of a fountain surrounded by a wall, where the water is raised up to the mouth of the spring, so that the spring itself no longer bubbles up. Thought is like the spring, and speech is the cistern; in a word, influx adapts itself to efflux. Similarly, the Intellect from above adapts itself to the measure of the freedom of speaking and acting out one’s thoughts. For this reason, that noble nation <note>The Germans.</note> pays little attention to matters of judgment, but rather to matters of memory. This is the reason why they are primarily devoted to **Literary History** <note>original: "Historiæ Literariæ" — a term then used for the history of learning, bibliography, and scholarship</note>, and in their books they trust in men of fame and erudition among them, quoting their judgments in abundance and subscribing to one or another. This state of theirs is represented in the spiritual world by a man who carries books under his arms; when someone argues about some matter of judgment, he says, "I will give you an answer," and immediately pulls out a book from under his arm and reads from it.

815. Many things proceed from this state of theirs, including this: that they keep the spiritual matters of the Church inscribed in the memory, and rarely elevate them into the higher Intellect, but only let them into the lower Intellect, from which they reason about them. This is entirely different from the free nations. The latter, regarding the spiritual matters of the Church which are called **Theology**, are like **Eagles** that raise themselves to any height; but the nations that are not free are like **Swans** in a river. Furthermore, the free nations are like great **Stags** with high horns, which run through fields, groves, and forests in full liberty; but the nations that are not free are like stags kept in enclosures <note>original: "Viuariis" — game parks or preserves</note> to serve a Prince. Furthermore, the peoples in freedom are like the flying horses called **Pegasi** by the ancients, which fly not only over the seas, but also over the hills called **Parnassian**, and also over the seats of learning <note>original: "Musæa"</note> below them; but the peoples who have not been emancipated are like noble horses beautifully decorated with trappings in the King's stables. Similar to these are the differences of judgment in the mystical matters of Theology. The clergy there, while they are students, write down the dictates from the mouths of their teachers in the academies <note>original: "Lyceis"</note>, and keep these as the credentials of their learning; and when they are inaugurated into the priesthood, or appointed as lecturers in the schools, the latter from their chairs and the former from their pulpits draw their canonical speeches mostly from those dictates I just mentioned. Their priests who do not teach from orthodoxy commonly preach the **Holy Spirit** and its wonderful operations and stirrings of holiness in hearts; but those who teach about **Faith** from modern orthodoxy appear to the angels as if they were distinguished by a laurel wreath tied from oak leaves. But those who teach from the **Word** concerning **Charity** and its works appear to the angels as if they were adorned with a laurel wreath woven from fragrant laurel leaves. The **Evangelicals** <note>The Lutherans.</note> there, in their contentions with the **Reformed** <note>The Calvinists.</note> about truths, appear as if they are tearing their clothes, for the reason that clothes signify truths.

816. I asked where the people of **Hamburg** are found in the spiritual world, and it was said that they nowhere appear gathered into one society, and much less into any city, but that they are scattered and mixed among the Germans in various quarters. When the cause was investigated, it was said to be this: because of the continual inspections and, as it were, travels of their minds outside their own city, and very little within it; for such as the state of a man's mind is in the natural world, such is his state in the spiritual world. For the mind of man is his spirit, or the posthumous man living after his departure from the material body.

...they send out emissaries to unknown paths to seduce others, but they are tracked down, and after they are punished, they are either sent back to their own people or cast down.

818. After the **Last Judgment**, which took place in the spiritual world in the year 1757, the state of all people—and thus also of these—was so changed that they are no longer permitted to gather into large crowds as they did before. Instead, for every Love, whether good or evil, specific paths have been arranged. Those who arrive from the world enter these paths immediately and travel to the Societies that correspond to their inner loves. Thus, the evil are carried to Societies located in **Hell**, and the good to Societies located in **Heaven**. This precaution ensures that they do not form "artificial heavens" for themselves as they did previously. In the world of spirits <note>In Swedenborg's theology, the "world of spirits" is an intermediate realm where everyone first arrives after death before being prepared for their final destination in heaven or hell.</note>, these Societies are numerous; there are as many of them as there are genera and species of the affections of love, both good and evil. In the meantime, before they are either raised into Heaven or cast down into Hell, they are in a spiritual conjunction with people in our world, because humans also stand in the middle between Heaven and Hell.

819. The Catholics have a certain **Synod** <note>original: "Synedrium" — a governing council or assembly</note> in the Southern quarter toward the East. Their leaders meet there and consult on various matters regarding their religion, primarily how the common people are to be kept in blind obedience and how their own dominion might be expanded. However, no one who was a Pope in the natural world is admitted into that council, because their minds are occupied by a sense of "Divine Authority," resulting from having claimed the Lord’s power for themselves while on Earth. Nor is any Cardinal permitted to enter that Synod, due to their sense of superiority. These Cardinals instead gather in a large chamber beneath the leaders, but after staying for a few days they are taken away, though it has not been granted to me to know where. 
There is also another assembly in the Southern quarter toward the West. Its business is to usher the "credulous commoners" into Heaven. They arrange many societies around themselves that focus on various **external delights**: in some there are dances, in some musical harmonies, in some processions, and in some theaters and stage plays. In some societies there are those who use "fantasies" <note>In this context, fantasies are sensory illusions in the spirit world that appear real but lack spiritual substance.</note> to create various types of magnificence; in some they simply tell fortunes and joke; in some they speak together in a friendly way—here about religious matters, there about civil matters, and elsewhere even about lewd topics. They send the credulous into one of these societies according to each person's pleasure, calling it "Heaven." But after a day or two of being there, everyone is overcome with boredom and leaves, because those delights are merely external and not internal. In this way, many are led away from their trivial beliefs regarding the power of the church to admit people into Heaven. As for their specific worship, it is almost identical to their worship in the world; it similarly consists of **Masses**, which are conducted not in the common language of spirits, but in a language made up of high-sounding words that inspire a sense of external holiness and trembling, even though the spirits do not understand them at all.

820. Everyone who comes from the Earth into the spiritual world is initially held in the confession of their faith and the religion of their homeland; this is also true for the Catholics. Therefore, they always have a "representative Pope" placed over them, whom they worship with the same rituals as in the world. It is rare that someone who was actually a Pope in the world is placed over them after their passing; however, one who served in the Papal office thirty or forty years ago <note>Likely referring to Pope Benedict XIV (r. 1740–1758), whom Swedenborg elsewhere described as having a secret respect for the Word of God.</note> was placed over them because he cherished in his heart the idea that the **Word** was more holy than is generally believed, and that the Lord ought to be worshipped. I was permitted to speak with him, and he said that he worships the Lord alone, because He is God, who has all power in heaven and on earth, according to His own words in Matthew 28:18 <note>original: "All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth."</note>; and he said that the invocation of saints is a mockery. He added that while in the world he intended to restore that Church, but was unable to do so for reasons he explained. I saw him during the day of the **Last Judgment**, when the great northern city inhabited by both Catholics and Reformers was being destroyed; he was carried out on a litter and moved to a safe place. At the sides of the large Society where he acts as Pope, there are established...

...there are **Schools** <term>Gymnasia: in Swedenborg's writings, these are places of spiritual instruction and intellectual debate</term>, where those who are in a state of uncertainty regarding Religion go. There, converted **Monks** are present, who teach them about God the Savior Christ, and also about the holiness of the Word. These monks leave it to the judgment of the newcomers to turn their minds away from the sanctifications introduced into the Roman Catholic Church. Those who receive these teachings are introduced into a spacious Society, where those who have withdrawn from the Worship of the Pope and the Saints reside. When they arrive there, they are like those who have awakened from a heavy sleep into full wakefulness; and like those who come from the unpleasantness of winter into the loveliness of early Spring; and like a Sailor when he touches the harbor. They are then invited to feasts by those who are already there, and noble Wine is given to them to drink from crystal cups. I have also heard that Angels from Heaven lower a platter to the guest, upon which there is **Manna** in a similar form and with a similar taste to that which was lowered upon the Camps of the children of Israel in the desert; this platter is carried around to the Guests, and everyone is given the freedom to taste it.

821. All those from the Catholic Religion who, when they realize they live after death, and who in the former World thought more about God than about the Papacy, and performed works of Charity from a simple heart, are easily led away from the superstitions of that Religion once they are instructed that the Lord Himself, the Savior of the World, reigns here. For these, the transition from **Papism** <note>original: "Papismo" — a term used by the author to describe the Roman Catholic system of governance</note> to **Christianity** is as easy as entering a Temple through open doors; or as it is to pass the Guards <note>original: "Satellitia"</note> in the courtyards to enter the Hall at the King's command; or as it is to lift one's face and look up to Heaven when voices are heard from there. But conversely, it is just as difficult to lead away from the superstitions of that Religion those who, in the course of their life in the World, rarely if ever thought about God, and loved that Worship only for the sake of its festivities. For them, it is like entering a Temple through closed doors; or like passing through the Guards in the courtyards to enter the Hall when the King forbids it; or like a snake in the grass trying to lift its eyes to Heaven. It is a remarkable thing that all those who flow from that Catholic Religious system into the spiritual World do not see Heaven where the Angels are; it appears to them like a dark Cloud above them, which limits their sight. But indeed, as soon as anyone who has been converted comes to those who are also converted, Heaven is opened, and they sometimes see Angels there in white Garments, to whom they are also elevated after their time of preparation is complete.

## CONCERNING THE SAINTS OF THE PAPISTS IN THE SPIRITUAL WORLD.

822. It is well known that evil is implanted or hereditary in man from his Parents, but it is known to few in what that evil dwells in its fullness: it dwells in the love of possessing the goods of all others, and in the **love of ruling**. For this latter love is of such a nature that, as far as the reins are loosened for it, it bursts forth until it burns with a desire to rule over all, and finally until it wishes to be invoked and worshipped as a God. This Love is the **Serpent** who deceived **Eve** <note>original: "Chaivam" — a Latinization of the Hebrew name for Eve, Chavah</note> and **Adam**; for he said to the Woman, *God knows that in the day you eat of the fruit of that Tree, your eyes will be opened*, AND THEN YOU WILL BE AS GOD (Genesis 3:4, 5). Therefore, as much as a man rushes into this Love with the reins loosened, so much does he turn away from God and turn toward himself, becoming a worshipper of himself. Then he may invoke God with a warm mouth out of self-love, but with a cold heart out of contempt for God. At such a time, the Divine things of the Church can serve as means, but because the end is dominion, the means are no more to his heart than they serve that purpose. Such a man, if he is raised to the highest honors, is in his own image like **Atlas** <note>A Titan from Greek mythology who carried the sky on his shoulders</note> carrying the terrestrial Globe on his shoulders; or like **Phoebus** <note>The Greek/Roman sun god</note> carrying the sun with his horses around the world.

823. Since man is such by heredity, therefore all those who have been "sanctified" through **Papal Bulls** <note>Official decrees or charters issued by the Pope, in this case referring to the canonization of saints</note> are removed from the eyes of others in the spiritual World and are hidden away; all communication with their worshippers is taken away from them. 824. Many from the Catholic people, especially Monks, when they arrive in the spiritual world, look for the Saints—especially the Saint of their own Order. They are surprised when they do not find them, but they are later instructed that these saints are intermingled either among those in Heaven or those in the **Lower Earth** <term>Infera Terra: in Swedenborg's theology, a region in the spiritual world where people undergo preparation or vastation before moving to heaven or hell</term>. In both places, they know nothing of the worship and invocation directed at them. Those who do know and wish to be invoked fall into delusions and speak foolishly. The worship of Saints is such an abomination in Heaven that as soon as the angels hear of it, they shudder; for to the extent that worship is attributed to any human, it is taken away from the Lord. In this way, He cannot be worshiped alone; and if the Lord is not worshiped alone, a division is made which destroys communion and the happiness of life flowing from it. To let me know what the Catholic Saints are like, so that I might make it known, about a hundred were brought up from the Lower Earth who knew of their own "Sanctification." They ascended from behind, and some before my face. I spoke with one of them, whom they said was **Xavier** <note>Saint Francis Xavier, a co-founder of the Jesuits</note>. While he spoke with me, he was like a foolish person; yet he was able to tell me that in his own place, where he is shut up with others, he is not foolish, but he becomes foolish whenever he thinks he is a Saint and wants to be invoked. I heard a similar murmur from those who were behind me. It is different with those called Saints who are actually in Heaven; they know absolutely nothing of what happens on earth, nor is it permitted for them to speak with any of the Catholic people who are in that superstition, lest any idea of that matter should enter into them.

825. From this state of theirs, anyone can conclude that their Invocations are merely mockeries. Furthermore, I can assert that they hear the invocations made to them on Earth no more than their statues by the roadside, nor more than the walls of a temple, nor more than the birds nesting in the towers. It is said by their servants in the world that the Saints reign in Heaven together with the Lord Jesus Christ, but this is a fiction and a fabrication; for they no more reign with the Lord than a stable-boy with a King, a doorman with a Nobleman, or a messenger with a Primate. For John the Baptist said of the Lord, *that he was not worthy to untie the strap of His shoe* <note>original Latin: "non dignus sit solvere corrigiam calcei Ipsius"</note> (Mark 1:7; John 1:27). What then are people like these?

826. There occasionally appears to the Parisians who are in a Society in the spiritual world, a certain Woman at a middle height, in splendid clothing and with a face like a saint, and she says she is **GENEVIEVE**. But when some begin to worship her, her face and clothing are immediately changed, and she becomes like an ordinary woman. She rebukes them for wanting to worship a woman who, among her companions, is held in no more esteem than a servant-maid, marvelling that people of the world are captured by such trifles.

827. To this I will add something most worthy of note: Once, **MARY THE MOTHER OF THE LORD** passed by, appearing above my head in white clothing. Stopping for a moment, she said that she had been the Mother of the Lord, and that He was indeed born of her, but that having become God, He put off everything human from her <note>Swedenborg taught that Jesus gradually shed the "maternal humanity" inherited from Mary to become fully Divine</note>. Therefore, she now worships Him as her God and does not want anyone to acknowledge Him as her Son, because everything in Him is Divine.

829. Since religion resides in the highest parts of a person, and from those highest parts the lower things live and shine, and because **Mohammed** is present in their minds alongside their religion, someone representing Mohammed is always placed in their sight. So that they may turn their faces toward the East, above which is the Lord, he is placed below the **Christian Center** <term>Meditullium: a central or middle region in Swedenborg's spiritual geography</term>. This is not the actual Mohammed who wrote the **Quran** <note>original: "Alcoranum"</note>, but another person who performs his office; nor is it always the same person, but he is changed. Once it was a man from **Saxony** who, having been captured by the **Algerians**, became a Muslim. Because he had also been a Christian, he was occasionally moved to speak with them about the Lord, saying that He was not the son of Joseph but the Son of God Himself. Other men succeeded this Mohammed later on. In the place where that representative Mohammed has his seat, a fire appears like torches so that he may be recognized; but that fire is not visible to anyone other than the Muslims.

830. The actual Mohammed who wrote the Quran does not come into view today. I was told that in the earliest times he presided over them, but because he wished to rule over everything of their religion like a God, he was ejected from his seat—which he held under the Papists—and sent down to the right side near the south. Once, a certain society of Muslims was incited by malicious spirits to acknowledge Mohammed as God. To settle the sedition, Mohammed was brought up from the **lower earth** <term>Infera Terra: a region of the spiritual world for preparation or vastation</term> and shown to them, and I saw him then as well. He appeared similar to **corporeal spirits** <note>spirits focused only on the physical or external senses</note> who have no interior perception; his face verged toward black. I heard him speak these words: *I am your Mohammed*; and soon he seemed to sink back down.

831. Muslims are hostile to Christians primarily because of the belief in three Divine Persons, and the resulting worship of three Gods and three Creators. They are hostile to **Roman Catholics** in addition because of their kneeling before images; hence they call the latter **Idolaters** and the former **fanatics**. They say that Christians make a **three-headed God** <note>original: "Tricipitem"</note>, and that they say "one" but whisper "three"; consequently, they say Christians tear apart Omnipotence and make three out of the one and only. They say Christians are like **Fauns** <note>mythological half-human, half-goat creatures</note> with three horns, one for each God, and yet three for one; and that they pray this way, sing this way, and sound this way from their pulpits.

832. Like all nations that acknowledge one God, love what is just, and do good based on religion, Muslims have their own Heaven, but it is outside the Christian one. However, the Muslim Heaven is divided into two: in the lower one, they live honestly with multiple wives, but no one is elevated from there into the higher Heaven except those who give up their concubines and acknowledge the Lord as our Savior, and at the same time acknowledge His dominion over Heaven and Hell. I heard that it is impossible for them to think that God the Father and our Lord are one, but that it is possible for them to believe He rules over the Heavens and the Hells because He is the Son of God the Father. This is the faith among them through which the Lord grants them ascent into the higher Heaven.

833. The fact that the Muslim religion has been received by more kingdoms than the Christian religion can be a scandal to those who think about **Divine Providence** and simultaneously believe that no one can be saved except a person born a Christian. But the Muslim religion is not a scandal to those who believe that all things are of Divine Providence; these people search for the reason why it is so, and they find it. It is in this: that the Muslim religion acknowledges the Lord as the Greatest Prophet, the wisest of all, and also as the Son of God. But because they have made the Quran the book of their religion, and consequently Mohammed (who wrote it) resides in their thoughts and they follow him with a certain worship, they think little about our Lord. So that it may be fully known that this religion was raised up by the Lord's Divine Providence to destroy the idolatries of many nations, it will be described in some order; but first, concerning the origin of idolatries. # UNIVERSAL THEOLOGY

[...the public] <note>The text begins mid-word with "cus," likely completing "publicus" from the previous page.</note> spread into very many kingdoms of the world, was because all the Churches before the Advent of the Lord were **representative** churches <note>A "representative" church is one where external rituals and objects symbolize internal, spiritual realities.</note>. Such was the **Israelite Church**: there, the Tabernacle, the garments of Aaron, the sacrifices, everything in the Temple of Jerusalem, and even the statutes, were representative. Among the ancients, there was the **Science of Correspondences** <term>Correspondences: the spiritual philosophy that every natural object reflects a specific spiritual truth</term>, which is also the science of representations. This was the "Science of sciences," especially cultivated by the **Egyptians**, and was the origin of their **hieroglyphics**. 

From this science, they knew what animals of every kind signified, as well as trees of every kind, mountains, hills, rivers, and springs; they also knew the meaning of the sun, moon, and stars. Through that science, they also had knowledge of spiritual things, because the things represented—which are the kinds of things belonging to the spiritual wisdom of the angels in heaven—were their origins. 

Now, because all their worship was representative, consisting of mere correspondences, they held their worship on mountains and hills, and also in groves and gardens. For this reason, they consecrated springs and, moreover, made sculpted horses, oxen, calves, lambs, and even birds, fish, and serpents. These they placed near their temples, in their courtyards, and also in their homes, arranged according to the spiritual things of the church to which they corresponded, or which they represented and thus signified. 

After some time, when the Science of Correspondences was lost to memory, their descendants began to worship the sculptures themselves as holy in their own right, not knowing that their ancient parents saw nothing holy in them, but only that they represented holy things according to correspondences. From this arose the **idolatries** that filled so many kingdoms of the world. 

To uproot these idolatries, it was brought about by the **Divine Providence** of the Lord that a new religion, adapted to the **temperament of the Orientals** <note>The author uses "genius" (temperament) to describe the cultural and psychological character of Eastern peoples.</note>, should be inaugurated. In this religion, there would be something from both Testaments of the **Word**, and it would teach that the Lord came into the world, and that He was the greatest Prophet, the wisest of all, and the **Son of God**. This was achieved through **Mohammed**, after whom that religion is named. 

From this, it is clear that this religion was raised up by the Divine Providence of the Lord and adapted to the temperament of the Orientals, as was said, for the purpose of destroying the idolatries of so many nations and providing some knowledge of the Lord before they entered the spiritual world (which occurs after death). This religion would not have been received by so many kingdoms, nor could it have uprooted idolatries there, unless it had been made compatible with their ideas and thoughts—especially unless **polygamy** <note>The practice of having more than one wife.</note> had been permitted. This was also because Orientals, without that permission, would have burned with foul adulteries more than Europeans and would have perished.

834. Once I was granted to perceive the nature of the **heat of their polygamous love**. I spoke with one who acted in the place of Mohammed <note>The author previously explained that "representatives" of Mohammed are used in the spiritual world to lead the Muslim communities.</note>. After some conversation at a distance, this substitute sent me an ebony spoon and other items, which were signs that they came from him. At the same time, communication was opened from various places regarding the heat of their polygamous love. 

In some places, it was felt like the heat in **baths** after washing; in others, like the heat in **kitchens** where meat is being boiled; in others, like the heat in **eating-houses** where foul-smelling food is on sale; in others, like in the cellars of **apothecaries** <note>original: "Pharmacopolas"</note> where emulsions and similar things are prepared; in others, like the heat in **brothels and dens of vice**; and in some, like in **shops** where skins, leather, and shoes are sold. In this heat, there was also something rancid, harsh, and burning, arising from **jealousy**. 

However, the heat in the **Christian heavens**, when the delight of their love is perceived as an odor, is fragrant like gardens and vineyards, like rose-beds, and in some places like spice shops, and in others like wine-presses and wine cellars. That the delights of loves in the spiritual world are often perceived as odors has been shown throughout my **Memorable Relations** <note>original: "MEMORIALIBUS"</note> following the chapters.

## CONCERNING THE AFRICANS IN THE SPIRITUAL WORLD; AND ALSO SOMETHING CONCERNING THE GENTILES.

835. The **Gentiles** <note>original: "Gentes"; referring to non-Christian nations or people who were not part of the Church.</note>, who know nothing of the Lord, appear in the spiritual world outside of those who do know Him; so much so, that the furthest boundaries are formed by none other than those who were complete idolaters and worshipped the Sun and Moon in their former world. However, those who acknowledge One God and make the precepts—such as those in the **Decalogue** <term>Decalogue: The Ten Commandments</term>—a matter of religion and thus of their life, communicate more directly with the Christians in the center <note>The "center" refers to the spiritual arrangement where Christians occupy the middle of the spiritual world because they have the Word (the Bible).</note>; for in this way, communication is not intercepted by the **Muslims** <note>original: "Mahumedanis"</note> and the **Catholics** <note>original: "Pontificiis," literally those under the Pontiff or Pope.</note>. The nations are also distinguished according to their character and their ability to receive light through the Heavens from the Lord: for among them there are those who are "Internal" and those who are "External," which they derive partly from the climate, partly from the stock from which they come, partly from their education, and partly from their religion. The **Africans** are more internal than the rest.

836. All who acknowledge and worship one God, the Creator of the Universe, cherish a human idea concerning God <note>That is, they conceive of God as being in the form of a Man.</note>; they say that no one can have any other idea of God. When they hear that many cherish an idea of God as being like **ether** or a cloud, they ask where such people are; and when they are told that they are among the Christians, they deny that such a thing is possible. But it is answered that they have such an idea because God is called a "Spirit" in the Word, and they think of spirit in no other way than as the substance of ether or as some form of a cloud, not knowing that every Spirit and every Angel is a **Man**. Yet it was tested whether their spiritual idea was similar to their natural idea, and it was found not to be similar among those who inwardly acknowledge the Lord the Savior as the God of Heaven and Earth. I heard a certain priest saying that no one could have an idea of a **Divine Human** <note>original: "Divini Humani"; a central concept in this theology that God is the Infinite Man.</note>, and I saw him transferred to various nations, to those more and more internal, and also to their Heavens, and finally to the Christian Heaven; and everywhere a communication of their interior perception concerning God was given, and he noticed that they had no other idea of God than the idea of a **Divine Man**, and that man—who is an image and likeness—could not have been created by anyone else.

837. Since the **Africans** excel the rest in interior judgment, I have had conversation with them on matters of deeper inquiry, and recently concerning God; concerning the Lord the Redeemer; and concerning the **Internal and External man** <note>The "internal man" refers to the soul or spiritual mind, while the "external man" refers to the natural mind and body.</note>. Because they were delighted with that conversation, I will mention some things which they perceived from their interior sight concerning those three subjects: **CONCERNING GOD**, they said that He certainly descended and offered Himself to be seen by men, because He is their Creator, Protector, and Leader, and because the human race is His own; and that He sees, examines, and provides for all things and every single thing in the Heavens and on Earth—their good things as being in Himself, and Himself in them. The reason is that He is the **Sun of the Angelic Heaven**, which is seen as high above the spiritual world as the sun of the earth is seen above the natural world. He who is the Sun sees, examines, and provides for all and every single thing that is below. And because His **Divine Love** is what appears as the Sun, it follows that He provides for the greatest and smallest things such matters as belong to life; and for men, such things as belong to love and wisdom—those of Love through the heat from that Sun, and those of wisdom through the light from it. If, therefore, you form for yourselves an idea of God as the Sun of the Universe, you will certainly see and acknowledge His **Omnipresence**, **Omniscience**, and **Omnipotence** from that idea.

838. **FURTHER CONVERSATION WAS HELD WITH THEM CONCERNING THE LORD THE SAVIOR**; and it was said that God in His essence is Divine Love, and that Divine Love is like the purest Fire. And because Love, viewed in itself, intends nothing else than to become one with another whom it loves—and Divine Love intends nothing else than to unite itself to man and man to itself, even so that He is in him and he in Him—and because Divine Love is like the purest Fire, it is clear that God, being such, could not possibly be in man, and...

Therefore, He descended and took on the **Human** <term>Human: In this context, the "Human" (Latin: *Humanum*) refers to the physical and mental nature of a human being which God assumed to interact with the world.</term> according to the Order established by Him from the creation of the world. This order was that He should be conceived by a Power propagated from Himself, be carried in the womb, be born, and then grow in wisdom and love, and thus approach a union with His Divine Origin. In this way, God became Man, and Man became God. That this is so, the Scripture concerning Him—which Christians possess and which is called the **Word**—clearly teaches and testifies. God Himself, who in His Human is called **Jesus Christ**, says that the Father is in Him and He is in the Father, and that whoever sees Him sees the Father, besides many other statements to the same effect. 

Reason also sees that God, whose Love is like the purest Fire, could not otherwise unite Himself to man and man to Himself. Can the fire of the sun, as it is in itself, touch a man—much less enter into him—unless it veils its rays with atmospheres and presents itself through a tempered heat? Can the pure ether surround a man, much less flow into the bronchial tubes of his lungs, unless it is packed with air and thus adapts itself? A fish cannot even draw life from the air, but must live in the element of life applied to it <note>meaning the water</note>. Indeed, not even a King on earth can administer every single thing in his kingdom in his own person or immediately, except through higher and lower officials who together constitute his "royal body." Nor can the soul of a man present itself to be seen by another, enter into companionship with him, or communicate proofs of its love, except through the body. How then could God do so, except through the Human which is His own? Having heard these things, the Africans, because they are more internally rational than others, perceived them clearly; and each favored the teaching according to his own perception.

839. Finally, a conversation was shared concerning the **INTERNAL AND EXTERNAL MAN**. It was said that men who perceive things interiorly are in the light of truth, which is the light of Heaven; but men who perceive things only exteriorly are in no light of truth, because they are only in the light of the world. Thus, "Internal" men are in intelligence and wisdom, while "External" men are in madness and a distorted vision. Internal men are spiritual because they think from the spirit elevated above the body, and therefore see truths in the light; but External men are natural and sensual because they think from the fallacies of the bodily senses, and therefore see truths as if in a cloud, and when they turn them over in their minds, they see falsehoods as truths. 

Internal men are like those standing upon a Mountain in a field, or upon a Tower in a city, or upon a Watchtower at sea; but External men are like those standing in a valley beneath the mountain, or in a crypt beneath the tower, or in a small boat beneath the watchtower, who see nothing but what is closest to them. Furthermore, Internal men are like those who live in the second or third story of a House or Palace, whose walls contain windows of crystal glass, who look out over the city in its wide extent and recognize every small building there; but External men are like those who live in the lowest floor, whose windows are made of glued paper <note>A common historical substitute for expensive glass windows</note>, who cannot see even a single street outside the house, but only what is inside, and even that only by candlelight or the fireplace. Internal men are also like Eagles flying on high, seeing everything beneath them far and wide; conversely, External men are like Roosters who stand on a post and crow loudly to the hens walking on the ground. Moreover, Internal men perceive that what they know, compared to what they do not know, is like the water in a jug compared to the water in a lake; but External men perceive things no differently than if they knew everything. Upon hearing these things, the Africans rejoiced, because from the interior sight in which they excel, they recognized that it is so.

840. Because the Africans are of such a character, a **Revelation** is taking place among them today, which, having begun, is spreading from their region round about, though not yet as far as the seas. They despise newcomers from Europe who believe that man is saved by faith alone, and thus by thinking alone, and...
