I heard the joy of the Angels over that Revelation, because through it a communication is opened to them with the human **Rational** <term>Rational: In Swedenborg's theology, the "Rational" (Latin: *Rationali*) is the intermediate faculty of the mind that connects spiritual light with natural thought.</term>, which until now had been closed off by the Universal Dogma—that the Intellect [must be kept] under obedience to the faith of Churchmen.

# ON THE JEWS IN THE SPIRITUAL WORLD.

**841.** The Jews, before the **Last Judgment** <term>Last Judgment: Swedenborg claimed to have witnessed a spiritual Last Judgment in the year 1757, which reorganized the spiritual world.</term> which took place in the Year 1757, appeared in a Valley on the left side of the Christian center; after that, they were moved to the North, and commerce with Christians was forbidden to them, except with wanderers outside the Cities. There are in that Quarter two large Cities into which the Jews are moved after death, which before the Judgment they called **Jerusalem**, but after it by another name, because after the Judgment by "Jerusalem" is understood the Church regarding Doctrine, in which the Lord alone is worshiped. Converted Jews are placed over them in their Cities, who warn them not to speak abusively of Christ; and they punish those who still do so. The streets of their Cities are filled with mud up to the ankles, and the Houses with filth, from which they also smell, so that they cannot be approached. Afterward I noticed that many from that Nation had also obtained a place of residence in the Southern Quarter; and when I asked who they were, I was told they are those who thought little of the Rituals of the others, and wavered in their minds as to whether the Messiah would ever come, and also those who thought about various things in the World from reason and lived according to it. The greatest part of these are composed of the Jews who are called **Portuguese** <note>original: "Portugisi"; referring primarily to the Sephardic Jews of Western Europe, often perceived in the 18th century as more integrated and secularized.</note>.

**842.** An Angel sometimes appears to the Jews above at a middle height with a Staff in his hand, and gives them to believe that he is <term>MOSES</term>. He exhorts them to desist from the madness of expecting the Messiah even there, because the Messiah is Christ, who rules them and everyone; he tells them that he [Moses] knows this, and also knew of Him while he was in the World. Having heard this, they withdraw; the greatest part forget it, but a few retain it. Those who retain it are sent to Synagogues composed of the Converted, where they are instructed; and to those who have been instructed, new Clothes are given in place of their torn ones, and the Word is given to them, neatly written, as well as a dwelling in a City that is not unseemly. But those who do not receive these things are cast down, many into Forests and Deserts, where they practice robbery among themselves.

**843.** The Jews trade in that World just as in the former one, dealing in various things, especially in precious Stones, which they obtain for themselves through unknown ways from Heaven, where precious Stones exist in abundance. The reason their trade is in precious Stones is that they read the Word in its original Language and hold the Sense of its letter to be Holy; and precious Stones correspond to the Sense of the letter. (That the spiritual origin of these Stones is the Sense of the letter of the Word, and that their correspondence comes from there, may be seen above in the Chapter on **SACRED SCRIPTURE**, nos. 217, 218). They can also by artifice prepare similar ones and induce a fantasy that they are genuine; but these individuals are severely fined by their Governors.

**844.** The Jews, more than others, do not know that they are in the spiritual world, but believe they are still in the natural world. The reason is that they are entirely external men and do not think anything regarding Religion from an interior perspective. Therefore, they also speak about the Messiah just as they did before, and some say that He will come with David, and wearing a shining diadem...

...going before them and leading them into the Land of Canaan, and on the way drying up the rivers they will cross by the raising of his Staff. They believe that Christians (whom they also call "Gentiles" among themselves) will then seize the hems of their garments, humbly praying to be allowed to accompany them, and that they [the Jews] will receive Wealth according to their abundance, and that these Christians will also serve them. They confirm these things for themselves through what is read in Zechariah Chapter 8:23 and in Isaiah Chapter 66:20. They also believe that David will come and be their King and Shepherd, based on Jeremiah Chapter 30:9, and from Ezekiel Chapter 34:23 to 25 and Chapter 37:23 to 26. They are utterly unwilling to hear that by "David" there is meant our Lord Jesus Christ, and that by "Jews" there are meant those who will be of His Church.

**845.** When they are asked whether they firmly believe that everyone will come into the Land of Canaan, they say that everyone will, and that then the deceased Jews will rise again and enter that Land from their graves. When it is pointed out that they cannot possibly leave their graves because they already live after death, they respond that they will then descend and enter their bodies, and so live. When told that the Land cannot be large enough to hold everyone, they respond that it will then be enlarged. When it is suggested that the Kingdom of the Messiah, because he is the Son of God, will not be upon Earth but in Heaven, they respond that the Land of Canaan will then be Heaven. When it is said that they do not know where Bethlehem Ephrathah is, where the Messiah is to be born according to the prediction in Micah Chapter 5:1 and in David <note>original: "apud Davidem"; referring to the Psalms</note> Psalm 132:6, they respond that the Mother of the Messiah will nonetheless give birth there; and some say that wherever she gives birth, that place is Bethlehem. When it is asked how the Messiah can dwell with such wicked people, and this is confirmed by many passages from Jeremiah—and especially from the Song of Moses in Deuteronomy 32—showing that they are the worst of people, they respond that among the Jews there are both good and bad, and that it is the bad who are meant there. When it is said that their origin is from a Canaanite woman and from the harlotry of Judah with his daughter-in-law (Genesis 38), they respond that it was not harlotry. But when it is countered that Judah nonetheless commanded that she be brought out and burned for harlotry, they go away to deliberate; after consultation, they say that it was simply a **Levirate marriage** <term>Levirate marriage: An ancient custom where a man was required to marry his brother's widow to provide an heir for the deceased.</term>, which neither his second son Onan nor his third son Shelah provided. To this they add that very many of them are from the Tribe of Levi, which held the priesthood; they say "it is enough that we are all from the loins of Abraham." When they are told that there is a spiritual sense deeper within the Word which deals much with Christ or the Messiah, they respond that this is not so; but some of them say that deep within the Word, or at its bottom, there is nothing but gold. These and other similar things they say.

**846.** Since, as to my Spirit, I have been raised into the Angelic Heaven and into one Society there, some of the Wise ones there then approached me and said, **"WHAT IS NEW FROM THE EARTH?"** I said to them, "This is the News: that the Lord has revealed **Secrets** <term>Secrets: Swedenborg uses the Latin "Arcana," referring to hidden spiritual truths not previously known to the church.</term> which in excellence exceed the Secrets revealed from the beginning of the Church until now." They asked, "What are they?" I said that they were these:

The Angels asked whether the inhabitants of the World knew about Correspondences before this. # GENERAL TABLE OF CONTENTS

## THE FAITH OF THE NEW HEAVEN AND THE NEW CHURCH IN UNIVERSAL AND PARTICULAR FORM, numbers 1 to 3.

# CHAPTER I: ON GOD THE CREATOR.

->ON<-
->THE UNITY OF GOD.<-

1. That the whole of Sacred Scripture, and consequently all the Doctrines of the Churches in the Christian World, teach that God exists, and that He is One, n: 5 to 7.
2. That there is a universal Influx <term>Influx: A central concept in Swedenborg’s thought, referring to the constant flow of life, heat, and light from God into the spiritual and natural worlds.</term> from God into the souls of men, [conveying] that God exists, and that He is One, n: 8.
3. Hence it is that in the whole World there is no Nation, possessing Religion and sound Reason, that does not acknowledge a God, and that God is one, n: 9, 10.
4. That regarding what that one God is like, Nations and Peoples have differed and still differ, for several reasons, n: 11.
5. That human Reason, from many things in the World, can perceive and conclude if it is willing, that God exists, and that He is one, n: 12 to 13.
6. That unless there were One God, the Universe could not have been created and preserved, n: 13.
7. That the man who does not acknowledge God is excommunicated from the Church and condemned, n: 14.
8. That among men who acknowledge not One God, but several, nothing of the Church holds together, n: 15.

->ON THE DIVINE BEING, WHICH IS JEHOVAH.<-

1. That this One God is called Jehovah from His Being <note>original: "Esse"; a philosophical term for the underlying essence or "to be-ness" of a thing.</note>, thus because He Alone Is and Will Be, and because He is the First and the Last, the Beginning and the End, the Alpha and Omega <note>original: "Alphah & Omegah"; the first and last letters of the Greek alphabet, signifying the totality and eternity of God.</note>, n: 19.
2. That this One God is Substance itself and Form itself, and that Angels and Men are substances and forms from Him; and that so far as these are in Him and He in them, so far they are Images and Likenesses of Him, n: 20.
3. That the Divine Being <note>original: "Esse"</note> is Being in Itself, and at the same time Manifestation <note>original: "Existere"; in this context, it refers to the outward expression or existence of the inner essence.</note> in Itself, n: 21, 22.
4. That the Divine Being and Manifesting in Itself cannot produce another Divine that is Being and Manifesting in Itself; consequently, another God of the same Essence is not possible, n: 23.
5. That the plurality of Gods in ancient Ages, and also today, arose from nothing else than not understanding the Divine Being, n: 24.

# GENERAL INDEX

## ON THE INFINITY OF GOD, OR HIS IMMENSITY AND ETERNITY.

1. That God, because He Is and Exists in Himself, and all things in the Universe are and exist from Him, is Infinite, n: 28.
2. That God, because He was before the World, and thus before Times and Spaces arose, is Infinite, n: 29.
3. That God, after the World was made, is in Space without space, and in Time without time, n: 30. <note>This highlights the author's view that God is not limited by the physical dimensions of the universe He created.</note>
4. That the Infinity of God in relation to Spaces is called Immensity, and in relation to Times is called Eternity; and that although these relations exist, there is still nothing of space in His Immensity, and nothing of time in His Eternity, n: 31.
5. That enlightened Reason can see the Infinity of God from very many things in the World, n: 32.
6. That every Created thing is Finite, and that the Infinite is in finite things as in Receptacles <term>Receptacles: Beings or objects designed to receive and contain the life and heat flowing from the Divine.</term>, and in Men as in His own images, n: 33. 34.

## ON THE ESSENCE OF GOD, WHICH IS DIVINE LOVE AND DIVINE WISDOM.

1. That God is Love itself and Wisdom itself, and that these two make up His Essence, n: 37.
2. That God is Good itself and Truth itself, because Good belongs to Love, and Truth belongs to Wisdom, n: 38.
3. That God, because He is Love itself and Wisdom itself, is Life itself in Himself, n: 39. 40.
4. That Love and Wisdom in God make one <note>original: "unum faciant"; they form a perfect, inseparable unity.</note>, n: 41. 42.
5. That the Essence of love is to love others outside of oneself, to want to be one with them, and to make them blessed from oneself, n: 43. 44. 46.
6. That these [traits] of Divine Love were the cause of the Creation of the Universe, and that they are the cause of its Preservation, n: 46. 47.

## ON THE OMNIPOTENCE, OMNISCIENCE, AND OMNIPRESENCE OF GOD.

1. That Omnipotence, Omniscience, and Omnipresence belong to Divine Wisdom from Divine Love, n: 50. 51.
2. That God's Omnipotence, Omniscience, and Omnipresence cannot be known unless it is known what Order is, and unless these things are known: that God is Order, and that together with Creation He introduced Order both into the Universe and into each and every part of it, n: 52 to 55. <term>Order: The divine laws and structure that govern the spiritual and natural worlds.</term>
3. That the Omnipotence of God, both in the Universe and in each and every part of it, proceeds and operates according to the Laws of His own order, n: 56. 57. 58.
4. That God is Omniscient; that is, He perceives, sees, and knows each and every thing, even to the most minute, which happens according to Order; and from those, also what happens contrary to Order, n: 59 to 62.
5. That God is Omnipresent from the Firsts to the Lasts of His Order, n: 63. 64. <note>original: "a Primis ad Ultima"; from the highest spiritual beginnings to the lowest physical ends.</note>
6. That Man was created as a form of Divine Order, n: 65. 66. 67.
7. That a Man has power against evil and falsity from Divine Omnipotence, and has wisdom regarding Good and Truth from Divine Omniscience, and is in God from Divine Omnipresence, only in so far as he lives according to Divine Order, n: 68. 69. 70.

## ON THE CREATION OF THE UNIVERSE.

That no one can acquire any correct idea of the Creation of the Universe, unless some universal concepts are first provided to bring the Understanding into a state of perception; concerning which, see number 75.
The Creation of the Universe is described through five **MEMORABLE RELATIONS** <term>Memorable Relations: Vivid narrative accounts of experiences the author claims to have had in the spiritual world, used to illustrate spiritual truths.</term>, numbers 76, 77, 78, 79, 80.

## CHAPTER II, ON THE LORD THE REDEEMER.

1. That Jehovah God descended and assumed the Human <term>the Human: The physical body and human nature taken on by God in the person of Jesus Christ.</term>, so that He might redeem and save mankind, numbers 82, 83, 84.
2. That Jehovah God descended as Divine Truth, which is the Word, and yet that He did not separate the Divine Good, numbers 85 to 88.
3. That God assumed the Human according to His own Divine Order, numbers 89, 90, 91.
4. That the Human, through which God sent Himself into the World, is the Son of God, numbers 92, 93, 94.
5. That the Lord, through acts of Redemption, made Himself Justice <note>original: "Justitiam"; in this context, it refers to the restoration of divine order and righteousness.</note>, numbers 95, 96.
6. That the Lord, through those same acts, united Himself to the Father and the Father to Himself, numbers 97 to 100.
7. That in this way God became Man, and Man became God, in one Person, numbers 101, 102, 103.
8. That the progression toward union was His state of Emptying <note>original: "Exinanitionis"; the process of laying aside the limitations of the merely human nature inherited from the mother.</note>, and the Union itself is His state of Glorification, numbers 104, 105, 106.
9. That from this time forward, no one from the Christian world comes into Heaven unless they believe in the Lord God the Savior, numbers 107, 108.
10. Corollary: On the State of the Church before the Lord’s Coming, and its State after it, number 109.

## ON REDEMPTION.

1. That Redemption itself was a subjugation of the Hells <note>original: "Infernorum"</note>, and an ordering of the Heavens, and through these, a preparation for a New spiritual Church, numbers 115, 116, 117.
2. That without that Redemption, no human could have been saved, nor could the Angels have remained in a state of integrity, numbers 118, 119, 120.
3. That the Lord thus redeemed not only men, but also Angels, numbers 121, 122.
4. That Redemption was a purely Divine Work, number 123.
5. That this Redemption itself could not have been accomplished except through God incarnate, numbers 124, 125.
6. That the Passion of the cross was the final Temptation, which the Lord sustained as the Greatest Prophet, and that it was the means for the Glorification of His Human, but was not Redemption itself, numbers 126 to 131.
7. That the belief that the Passion of the cross was Redemption itself is a fundamental error of the Church; and that this error, together with the error concerning three Divine Persons from eternity, has perverted the whole Church to such an extent that nothing spiritual remains within it, numbers 132, 133.

# CHAPTER III, ON THE HOLY SPIRIT AND ON DIVINE OPERATION.

1. That the Holy Spirit is the Divine Truth, and also the Divine Power and Operation proceeding from the One God, in whom is the Divine Trinity—thus from the Lord God the Savior, numbers 139, 140, 141.
2. That the Divine Power and Operation, which is understood by the "Holy Spirit," are in general **Reformation** and **Regeneration**; and according to these, Renewal, Quickening, Sanctification, and Justification; and according to these, Purification from evils, and the Remission of sins, and finally Salvation, numbers 142 to 145.
3. That this Divine Power and Operation, which is understood by the "sending of the Holy Spirit," is specifically Enlightenment <note>original: "Illustratio"</note> and Instruction among the Clergy <term>Clergy: Those specifically called to church ministry, whom the author believes receive a particular spiritual influence for teaching.</term>, numbers 146, 147, 148.
4. That the Lord works these Powers in those who believe in Him, numbers 149, 150, 151.
5. That the Lord operates from Himself from the Father, and not vice versa <note>original: "non vicissim"</note>, numbers 153, 154, 155.
6. That the spirit of a man is his Mind, and whatever proceeds from it, numbers 156, 157.
**Corollary**, that nowhere in the Old Testament is it said that the Prophets spoke from the Holy Spirit, but from Jehovah God; but it is otherwise in the New Testament, number 158.

## ON THE DIVINE TRINITY.

1. That there is a Divine Trinity, which is the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, numbers 164, 165.
2. That these Three—Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—are the three Essentials of one God, which make a one, just as Soul, Body, and Operation do in a human being, numbers 166 to 169.
3. That before the World was created this Trinity did not exist, but that it was provided and made after the World was created, when God became incarnate, and then it existed in the Lord God the Redeemer and Savior Jesus Christ, numbers 170, 171.
4. That a "Trinity of Divine Persons from eternity," and thus before the World was created, is a "Trinity of Gods" in the ideas of thought, and that this cannot be abolished by the oral confession of one God, numbers 172, 173.
5. That a Trinity of Persons was unknown in the Apostolic Church, but that it arose from the Council of Nicea <term>Council of Nicea: A gathering of Christian bishops in 325 AD that defined the nature of the Son of God in relation to the Father.</term>, and was introduced from there into the Roman Catholic Church, and from that into the Churches that separated from it, numbers 174 to 176.
6. That from the Nicene and Athanasian Trinities <term>Athanasian Creed: An early Christian statement of faith that focuses on the Trinity and the nature of Christ.</term> together, there arose a Faith in three Gods, which has perverted the whole Christian Church, numbers 177, 178.
7. That from this comes that "Abomination of desolation," and "Affliction such as has not been," which the Lord had foretold in Daniel, the Evangelists, and in the Revelation, numbers 179, 180, 181.
8. Furthermore, that unless a New Heaven and a New Church are established by the Lord, no flesh would be saved, number 182.
9. That from a Trinity of Persons, each of whom is singly God according to the Athanasian Creed, many absurd and inconsistent ideas about God have arisen, which are phantasies and abortions, numbers 183, 184.

# CHAPTER IV, ON THE SACRED SCRIPTURE, OR THE WORD OF THE LORD.

1. That the Sacred Scripture, or the Word, is Divine Truth itself, numbers 189 to 192.

--- That the Spiritual Sense is in each and every part of the Word, demonstrated, numbers 196, 197, 198.
--- That when the Lord was in the World, He spoke through **Correspondences**, thus spiritually while speaking naturally, number 199. <term>Correspondences: The systematic relationship between natural objects or words and the spiritual realities they represent.</term>

### CHAPTER V, THE CATECHISM OR DECALOGUE EXPLAINED AS TO ITS EXTERNAL AND INTERNAL SENSE.

1. That the Decalogue was Holiness itself in the Israelite Church; here concerning the holiness of the Ark in which the Law [was kept], numbers 283 to 286.
2. That the Decalogue in the **Sense of the letter** contains the common precepts of faith and life, but in the **spiritual and celestial Sense**, it contains universally all things, numbers 287 to 290.
3. THE FIRST COMMANDMENT: There shall be no other God before my faces, numbers 291 to 296. <note>original: "coram faciebus meis." This reflects the literal Hebrew idiom for "in my presence."</note>
4. THE SECOND COMMANDMENT: You shall not take the Name of your God in vain, for Jehovah will not hold him guiltless who takes His Name in vain, numbers 297 to 300.
5. THE THIRD COMMANDMENT: Remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy: six days you shall labor and do all your work, but the seventh Day is the Sabbath to Jehovah your God, numbers 301 to 304.
6. THE FOURTH COMMANDMENT: Honor your Father and your Mother, that your days may be prolonged, and that it may be well with you upon the earth, numbers 305 to 308.
7. THE FIFTH COMMANDMENT: You shall not Kill, numbers 309 to 312.
8. THE SIXTH COMMANDMENT: You shall not Commit Adultery, numbers 313 to 316.
9. THE SEVENTH COMMANDMENT: You shall not Steal, numbers 317 to 320.
10. THE EIGHTH COMMANDMENT: You shall not answer as a false witness against your neighbor, numbers 321 to 324.
11. THE NINTH AND TENTH COMMANDMENTS: You shall not covet your neighbor’s House, you shall not covet your neighbor’s Wife, nor his Servant, nor his Maidservant, nor his Ox, nor his Donkey, nor anything that is your Neighbor’s, numbers 325 to 328.
12. That the Ten Commandments of the Decalogue contain all things that belong to love to God, and all things that belong to love toward the neighbor, numbers 329 to 331.

PREFACE; That Faith is first in time, but that Charity is first in end, number 336. <note>This means that while we learn the facts of faith first, the ultimate purpose or "end" of those facts is to lead us to a life of love and service (charity).</note>

—— *Because He is the visible God, in whom is the invisible [God], number 339.*
2. That Faith in sum is, that whoever lives well and believes rightly, is saved by the Lord, numbers 340 to 342.

## CHAPTER VII: CONCERNING CHARITY, OR LOVE TOWARD THE NEIGHBOR: AND CONCERNING GOOD WORKS.

1. That there are three universal Loves: the Love of Heaven, the Love of the World, and the Love of self, numbers 394, 395, 396.
    —— Concerning the <term>Will and Understanding</term> <note>In the author's psychology, the Will is the seat of love and intention, while the Understanding is the seat of thought and faith.</note>, number 397.
    —— Concerning Good and Truth, number 398.
    —— Concerning Love in general, number 399.
    —— Concerning the Love of self, and concerning the Love of the World in particular, number 400.
    —— Concerning the External and Internal man, number 401.
    —— Concerning the merely <term>Natural and Sensual man</term> <note>These terms describe people who live only for physical or material concerns without spiritual insight.</note>, number 402.
2. That those three Loves, when they are rightly subordinated, perfect the man; but when they are not rightly subordinated, they pervert and invert him, numbers 403, 404, 405.
3. That every man individually is the <term>Neighbor</term> <note>Latin: "Proximus." The author expands the definition of "neighbor" from a person to include societies, the country, and the church.</note> who is to be loved, but according to the quality of his good, numbers 406 to 411.
4. That Man in the plural, which is a Society smaller or larger, and that Man in the composite of these, which is the Fatherland, is the Neighbor who is to be loved, numbers 412, 413, 414.
5. That the Church is the Neighbor, who is to be loved in a higher degree; and the Lord’s Kingdom in the highest degree, numbers 415, 416.
6. That to love the Neighbor viewed in himself is not to love the Person, but the Good that is in the Person, number 417, 418, 419.
7. That Charity and good Works are two distinct things, just like willing well and doing well, numbers 420, 421.
8. That Charity itself is to act justly and faithfully in the Office, Business, and Work in which each person is engaged, and with those with whom they have any dealing, numbers 422, 423, 424.

9. That

## CHAPTER VIII, ON FREE WILL. <note>original: "LIBERO ARBITRIO." This refers to the human capacity to choose between good and evil, particularly in spiritual matters.</note>

1. The Precepts and Dogmas of the Church today concerning Free Will, numbers 463, 464, 465.
2. That two Trees were placed in the Garden of Eden, one of Life and the other of the Knowledge of good and evil, signifies that Free Will in spiritual things has been given to man, numbers 466 to 469.
3. That man is not Life, but a Receptacle of life from God, numbers 470 to 474.
4. That man, as long as he lives in the World, is held in the middle between Heaven and Hell, and there in a spiritual Equilibrium, which is Free Will, numbers 475 to 478.
5. That from the Permission of evil, in which every person’s Internal man is, it clearly appears that man has Free Will in spiritual things, numbers 478 to 482.
6. That without Free Will in spiritual things, the Word <note>The Holy Scripture</note> would not be of any use; consequently, the Church would not be anything, numbers 483, 484, 485.
7. That without Free Will in spiritual things, there would be nothing in man by which he might reciprocally join himself to the Lord; and therefore, there would be no <term>Imputation</term> <note>The legal or theological assignment of responsibility or credit for one's actions.</note>, but mere Predestination, which is detestable, number 485.

10. That the Will and Understanding of man are in this Free Will; but that doing evil, in both Worlds, the Spiritual and the Natural, is restrained by laws, because otherwise Society on both sides would perish, numbers 497, 498, 499.
11. That if men did not have Free Will in spiritual things, everyone in the whole world could have been led to believe in the Lord within one day; but the reason this cannot be done is that what is not received from Free Will does not remain, numbers 500, 501, 502.

## CHAPTER IX. ON REPENTANCE.

1. That <term>Repentance</term> <note>original: "Pænitentia"</note> is the first thing of the Church within man, numbers 510, 511.
2. That <term>Contrition</term> <note>A state of grief or remorse for sin.</note>, of which it is said today that it precedes Faith and is followed by the consolation of the Gospel, is not Repentance, numbers 512 to 515.
3. That oral Confession alone—stating that one is a Sinner—is not Repentance, numbers 516 to 519.
4. That man is born into every kind of evil, and that unless he removes them in part through Repentance, he remains in them; and he who remains in them cannot be saved, numbers 520 to 524.
---
-> — What the fulfillment of the Law is, numbers 523, 524. <-
5. That the knowledge of sin, and the examination of something within oneself, begins repentance, numbers 525, 526, 527.
6. That actual Repentance consists in examining oneself, knowing and acknowledging one's sins, praying to the Lord, and beginning a New life, numbers 528 to 531.
7. That true Repentance consists in not only examining the acts of one's life, but also the intentions of one's <term>will</term>, numbers 532, 533, 534.
8. That those also perform Repentance who do not examine themselves, yet nevertheless desist from evils because they are sins; and that this Repentance is performed by those who do Works of Charity out of religion, numbers 535, 536, 537.
9. That Confession ought to be made before the Lord God the Savior, followed by prayer for help and the power to resist evils, numbers 538, 539, 540.
10. That actual Repentance is easy for those who have performed it several times, but resistant to those who have not performed it, numbers 561, 562, 563.
11. That he who has never performed Repentance, or looked into and searched himself, eventually does not know what damnable evil is and what saving good is, numbers 564, 565, 566.

## CHAPTER X. ON REFORMATION AND REGENERATION.

1. That unless a man is <term>regenerated</term> <note>Literally "born again"; the process of spiritual rebirth.</note> anew, and created as if fresh, he cannot enter the Kingdom of God, numbers 572 to 575.
2. That the New Generation or Creation is performed by the Lord alone through Charity and Faith as the two Means, with man cooperating, numbers 576, 577, 578.
3. That all can be regenerated, because all have been redeemed, each according to his own state, numbers 579 to 582.
4. That Regeneration occurs in a manner similar to how a person is conceived, carried in the womb, born, and educated, numbers 583 to 586.
5. That the first act of the new generation is called <term>Reformation</term>, which belongs to the Understanding, and the second act is called <term>Regeneration</term>, which belongs to the Will and from there to the Understanding, numbers 587 to 590.
6. That the Internal man must first be reformed, and through this the External man, and that man is regenerated in this way, numbers 591 to 595.
7. That while this is happening, a conflict arises between the Internal and External man, and then the one who conquers rules over the other, numbers 596 to 600.
8. That the regenerated Man has a new Will and a new Understanding, numbers 601 to 606.
9. That the regenerated Man is in communion with the Angels of Heaven, and the unregenerated man is in communion with the spirits of Hell, numbers 607 to 610.

## CHAPTER XI. ON IMPUTATION.

1. That the Faith of the present-day Church, which is said to justify alone, and <term>Imputation</term> <note>The theological concept of "charging" or "crediting" someone with the merit or guilt of another.</note>, make one, numbers 626, 627.
2. That the Imputation belonging to the present-day Faith is twofold: one of the Merit of Christ, and the other of the Salvation resulting from it, numbers 628 to 631.
3. That the Faith which imputes the merit and righteousness of Christ the Redeemer first arose from the decrees of the <term>Nicene Synod</term> <note>The Council of Nicaea (325 AD), where the foundational doctrines of the Trinity were established.</note> concerning three Divine Persons from eternity; which Faith has been received by the entire Christian world from that time to the present, numbers 632 to 635.
4. That the Faith imputing the merit of Christ was not known in the preceding Apostolic Church, and is nowhere understood in <term>the Word</term> <note>Referring to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note>, numbers 636 to 639.
5. That the Imputation of the merit and righteousness of Christ is impossible, numbers 640, 641, 642.
6. That there is an Imputation, but of good and evil, numbers 643 to 646.
7. That the Faith and Imputation of the <term>New Church</term> <note>The author's term for a new spiritual era or dispensation of Christianity.</note> cannot exist together with the Faith and Imputation of the former Church; and if they are together, such a collision and conflict occurs that everything of the Church in man perishes, numbers 647, 648, 649.
8. That the Lord imputes good to every man, and that Hell imputes evil to every man, numbers 650 to 653.
9. That Faith, along with that which it joins itself to, determines the sentence; if true Faith joins itself with good, a sentence for Eternal Life is made, but if Faith joins itself with evil, a sentence for Eternal Death is made, numbers 654 to 657.
10. That Thought is imputed to no one, but <term>Will</term> is, numbers 658, 659, 660.

## CHAPTER XII. ON BAPTISM.

1. That without knowledge of the spiritual sense of the Word, no one can know what the two Sacraments, <term>Baptism</term> and the <term>Holy Supper</term> <note>Communion or the Eucharist.</note>, involve and effect, numbers 667, 668, 669.
2. That by the washing called Baptism is meant spiritual washing, which is purification from evils, and thus regeneration, numbers 670 to 673.
3. That Baptism was instituted in place of <term>Circumcision</term>, because by the circumcision of the foreskin was represented the circumcision of the heart, for the purpose that the Internal Church might succeed the External Church, which in each and every thing prefigured the Internal Church, numbers 674, 675, 676.
4. That the first use of Baptism is introduction into the Christian Church, and at the same time, insertion among Christians in the <term>spiritual world</term> <note>The realm of souls and spirits that the author claims to have visited.</note>, numbers 677 to 680.
5. That the second use is that the Christian may know and acknowledge the Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer and Savior, and follow Him, numbers 681, 682, 683.
6. That the third use of Baptism, which is the final use, is that man may be regenerated, numbers 684 to 687.

# INDEX OF MEMORABLE RELATIONS.

I. I heard certain newcomers talking among themselves about the three Divine Persons from eternity; and then a certain man, who had been a <term>Primate</term> <note>A high-ranking church official, such as an archbishop.</note> in the world, opened the ideas of his thought concerning that mystery. He said that his mind's view was, and still is, that Three sit in Heaven upon high thrones: God the Father upon a throne of fine gold <note original: "obryzo auro">A term for pure, refined gold often used in biblical contexts.</note> with a scepter in His hand; God the Son at His right hand upon a throne of the purest silver, with a crown upon His head; and God the Holy Spirit upon a throne of shining crystal, holding a dove in His hand, in which form He appeared when Christ was baptized. He said that all around them, hanging lamps made of precious stones glittered in a triple order; and that from a distance, in a circus, stood innumerable angels adoring and glorifying. Furthermore, he spoke about the Holy Spirit—how He brings faith, purifies, and justifies. He said that many of his Order favored these ideas of his, believing that I too, because I am a layman, would have faith in them. But then, having been given the opportunity to speak, I replied that from my childhood I have fostered the idea that God is one. Therefore, I explained in his presence what the Trinity involves, and what is signified by the Throne, Scepter, and Crown where those things are preached concerning God in <term>the Word</term> <note>The Holy Scriptures.</note>. To these I added that all who believe in three Divine Persons from eternity cannot do otherwise than believe in three Gods; and furthermore, that the Divine Essence is not divisible: number 16.

II. The conversation of angels concerning God: that *His Divine is Divine Being <note original: "Esse">A technical term referring to the fundamental core of existence, or "to be" in its purest form.</note> in itself, and not from itself; and that it is the One, the Same, the Very Thing, and Indivisible:* also that God is not in a place, but is present with those who are in a place: and that His Divine Love appears to the angels as a Sun, and that the Heat from it is, in its essence, Love, and the Light from it is, in its essence, Wisdom: number 25.
— That the proceeding Divine Attributes, which are Creation, Redemption, and Regeneration, belong to one God, and not to Three: number 26.

III. Since I perceived that a huge multitude of men are of the persuasion that all things belong to Nature, and thus that Nature is the Creator of the universe, I spoke with a certain clever man in a certain <term>Gymnasium</term> <note>In this context, a place of learning or spiritual assembly for discussion.</note> where such people were, concerning these three things: 1. Whether Nature belongs to life, or whether Life belongs to nature. 2. Whether the Center belongs to the expanse, or whether the Expanse belongs to the center. 3. Concerning the Center and the Expanse of Nature and of Life; and that the Center of nature is the Sun of the natural world, and its Expanse is the world itself; and that the Center of life is the Sun of the spiritual world, and its Expanse is that world itself. These subjects were discussed from both sides, and finally the truth was shown: number 35.

IV. That I was led into a certain theater of wisdom, where angelic spirits were gathered from the four quarters, who had been enjoined from Heaven to discuss three Secrets: 1. What the *Image of God* is and what the *Likeness of God* is. 2. Why a man is not born into the knowledge of any love, when nevertheless beasts and birds are born into the knowledge of all their loves. 3. What is signified by the *Tree of Life*, and the *Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil*; and furthermore, that they should join those three into one opinion, and report this to the angels of heaven. When these things were done, the Opinion was reported and accepted by the angels: number 48.

V. That from the evil spirits just above Hell, something like the roar of the sea was heard, which was a tumult that broke out among them because they heard above them that God Almighty has bound Himself to order. Some of them ascended from there and spoke to me sharply regarding that matter, saying that God, because He is Almighty, is not bo- <note>The text ends mid-word, likely continuing on the next page to say God is not "bound" by laws.</note>

<meta>This page continues the "Index of Memorable Relations" from page 516. It summarizes short narrative accounts (Memorable Relations) found in the main body of the work, focusing here on the nature of Divine Order, Omnipotence, and the creation of the universe.</meta>

<page-num>517</page-num>
->INDEX OF MEMORABLE RELATIONS.<-

V. Whether I was bound to any particular <term>Order</term> <note>In this context, "Order" refers both to a religious or social organization and the philosophical concept of cosmic structure.</note>; and being questioned about Order, I said: 1. That God is Order itself. 2. That He created man from Order, in Order, and for Order. 3. That He created man’s rational mind according to the order of the spiritual world, and his body according to the order of the natural world. 4. That consequently, it is a Law of Order that man, from his own "little spiritual heaven" <note original: "microurano">From the Greek for "small heaven."</note> or <term>microcosm</term>, should rule his "little natural world," just as God, from His "great heaven" <note original: "Macrourano">From the Greek for "great heaven."</note> or spiritual world, rules His <term>macrocosm</term> or natural world. 5. That many more Laws of Order flow from this, some of which are added here. What happened afterward to those spirits is described in number 71.

VI. Concerning the reasoning of certain spirits from <term>Holland</term> <note original: "Batavia">The Latin name for the region of the Netherlands.</note> and Britain in the spiritual world regarding <term>Imputation</term> <note>The theological concept of "charging" or "crediting" someone with the merits of Christ.</note> and <term>Predestination</term>: on one side, they asked why God, because He is Omnipotent, does not simply credit the Justice of His Son to everyone and thus make them all redeemed? Since He is Omnipotent, He could make all the Satans of Hell into Angels of Heaven; indeed, if it pleased Him, He could make <term>Lucifer</term>, the Dragon, and all the "goats" <note>A biblical reference to those not chosen for salvation.</note> into archangels, needing nothing but a single little word to do so. On the other side, it was argued that God is Order itself, and that He can do nothing against the Laws of His own Order, because that would be to act against Himself; besides many other points they playfully debated among themselves on this matter, number 72.

VII. That I afterward spoke with others who held a belief in Predestination, which they deduced from God’s absolute power or Omnipotence; they claimed that otherwise, there would be less power in God than in a monarch on Earth, who can turn the laws of justice like the palms of his hands and act absolutely, just as <term>Augustus Caesar</term> <note original: "Octavius Augustus">The first Roman Emperor, known for his vast power.</note> and also <term>Nero</term> acted. To this, it was answered that God created the world and everything in it from Himself as Order, and thus implanted Order into them; and that the Laws of His Order are as numerous as the Truths in <term>the Word</term> <note>The Holy Scriptures.</note>. Then, some Laws of Order were recounted, both what they are on God’s part and what they are on man’s part; and that these cannot be changed because God is Order itself, and man was created in the image of His order, number 73.

VIII. That I spoke with a gathering of Clergy and Laity about Divine Omnipotence; they said that Omnipotence is unlimited, and that "limited Omnipotence" is a contradiction. To this, it was answered that it is not a contradiction to act omnipotently according to the laws of Justice with Judgment; it is even said in <term>David</term> <note>Referring to the Book of Psalms, traditionally attributed to King David.</note> that *Justice and Judgment are the support of God's Throne* (Psalm 89:14). It was added that it is not a contradiction to act omnipotently according to the laws of Love from Wisdom, but it *is* a contradiction to suggest that God could act against the laws of Justice and Love, for that would be to act without Judgment and Wisdom. Furthermore, the current faith of the Church involves such a contradiction—the idea that God can make the unjust man just, or distinguish the wicked with all the gifts of salvation and rewards of life; along with more about this Faith and Omnipotence, number 74.

IX. Once, while I was meditating on the Creation of the Universe by God, I was led away in spirit to certain wise ones. They first complained about the ideas they had picked up in the world, which were about the Creation of the universe out of <term>Chaos</term> and Creation out of nothing; for these ideas obscure, ruin, and pervert any meditation on the Creation of the universe by God. Therefore, when asked what my mind thought, I expressed this: that it is useless to conclude anything other than a fantasy about the Creation of the Universe unless it is known that there are two worlds, the Spiritual and the Natural, and that in each there is a Sun. The Sun of the spiritual world is pure Love, in the midst of which is God, and from it come all spiritual things, which are in themselves **substantial**. The Sun of the natural world is pure Fire, and from it come all natural things, which are in themselves **material**. From this knowledge, one can conclude that the Creation of the Universe is from God, and understand how; this is briefly outlined in number 76.

<summary>This index page summarizes Swedenborg's arguments that God's power is not arbitrary but operates strictly through "Divine Order," and introduces his cosmological theory of two suns—one spiritual and one material.</summary>

X. That some <term>Satans</term> <note>In Swedenborg's writings, "Satans" specifically refers to hellish spirits who are centered on false intellectual reasoning, whereas "Devils" are those centered on evil of the will.</note> of Hell desired to speak with the Angels of Heaven, for the purpose of convincing them that all things are from Nature, and that God is merely a word unless it is understood to mean nature; and they were permitted to ascend. Then certain Angels from Heaven descended into the <term>World of Spirits</term> <note>A transitional realm between Heaven and Hell where souls go immediately after death.</note> to hear them. When the Satans saw them, they ran up furiously, saying: "You are called Angels because you believe that there is a God, and that Nature is nothing by comparison; and yet you believe these things even though it is against all the senses. Which of your five senses perceives anything other than Nature?" After these and many other bitter things were said, the Angels reminded them that they were now living after death, even though they had not previously believed this. Then the Angels caused them to see the beautiful and splendid things of Heaven, and said that these things exist there because everyone there believes in God; afterwards, they caused them to see the foul and filthy things of Hell, saying that these things are there because the inhabitants believe in Nature. Upon seeing these things, the Satans were at first convinced that there is a God and that He created Nature; but as they descended, their love of evil returned and closed off their intellect from the higher light. With that light closed off, they believed as before: that all things belong to Nature, and nothing to God. (Number 77).

XI. A living model of the **Creation of the Universe** was shown to me by Angels. I was led into Heaven, and it was granted to me to see all things belonging to the animal kingdom, the vegetable kingdom, and the mineral kingdom. These were exactly similar to the objects of those three kingdoms in the natural world. Then the Angels said that all those things in Heaven are created by God in a moment, and they continue to exist as long as the Angels are in a state of love and faith regarding their thought; and that this instantaneous creation clearly testifies to the creation of similar things—indeed, a similar process—in the natural world, with the only difference being that natural things "clothe" spiritual ones. This "clothing" was provided by God for the sake of generations (one thing from another), through which creation is perpetuated. Consequently, the creation of the universe was achieved in the same way as it happens every moment in Heaven. However, all things in the three kingdoms of nature that are harmful and foul (which are listed here) were not created by God, but arose together with Hell. (Number 78).

XII. A conversation with certain individuals who were **famous for their learning** in the world concerning the Creation of the Universe. Speaking from the same ideas they had previously entertained, they said: One, that Nature created itself; another, that Nature gathered its elements into <term>vortices</term> <note>A reference to the Cartesian theory that the universe is composed of spinning whirlpools of matter.</note> and that the Earth was formed from their collision; and a third, that it arose from a **Chaos** which in size equaled a large part of the universe, and that the purest elements first erupted from it to form the Sun and Stars, followed by less pure elements for the atmospheres, and finally the thick matter for the terraqueous Globe. To the question of where human souls come from, they said that the ether had collected into small, distinct spheres, and that these infuse themselves into those about to be born to create souls, and after death they fly back to their former troop in the ether, and from there return into others, according to the ancient <term>metempsychosis</term> <note original: "Mathempychoſin">The transmigration of souls, or the belief that a soul moves into a new body after death.</note>. After this, a certain Priest, using solid reasons for the Creation of the Universe by God, reduced everything they said to a tasteless jumble and put them to shame; yet they still retained their former delusions. (Number 79).

XIII. With a certain **Satan** concerning God, the Angelic Heaven, and Religion. Because he did not know any better than that he was still in his former world, he said that God is the Universe, that the Angelic Heaven is the atmospheric firmament, and that Religion is a spell used to fascinate the common people, along with many other foolish things. But when it was brought back to his memory that he was now living after death, and that he had not previously believed in such a life, at that moment he confessed that he had been insane; however, as soon as he turned around and moved away, he was just as insane as before. (Number 80).

XIV. That in the night I saw a <term>Will-o'-the-wisp</term> <note original: "Ignis fatuus">Literally "foolish fire"; a natural phosphorescence or atmospheric light often associated in folklore with spirits or delusions.</note> falling to the earth, which by many...

XIV. One who is called the Dragon <note>In Swedenborg’s interpretation of the Book of Revelation, "the Dragon" represents those who separate faith from charity and believe in three persons of the Trinity.</note>; I observed the place where he fell, and the ground there was sulfurous mixed with iron dust. When I looked there in the morning, I saw two Tents; and then soon a Spirit glided down from Heaven, whom I approached and asked why he had descended. He replied that he was cast down by Michael’s Angels <note>Referring to the war in heaven described in Revelation 12:7.</note> because he had said that God the Father and His Son are two and not one. He said that the entire Angelic Heaven believes that God the Father and His Son are one, just as the soul and body are one, and that they confirm this by many things from the **Word** <note>Swedenborg uses "the Word" to refer to the Sacred Scriptures.</note>, and furthermore from reason: that the soul of a son is from nothing but the Father, and that it is in the body in the likeness of the father. He added that he had indeed confessed in Heaven, as he had previously on earth, that God is one; but because the confession of his mouth and the thought of his mind disagreed on this point, they said he did not believe in any God, because one cancels out the other. He said this was the cause of his being cast down. Returning to the same place a day later, I saw two Statues made of similar dust (which was a mixture of sulfur and iron) in place of the two tents; one represented the Faith of the modern Church and the other its Charity, both beautifully clothed, but the garments were brought on by fantasies. However, because they were made of that dust, when rain was sent down from Heaven, both began to bubble and burn up. n. 110.

XV. That in the spiritual world, no one is allowed to speak differently than they think, otherwise a hypocritical sound is clearly heard; and for this reason, no one in Hell can name **JESUS**, because *Jesus* signifies *Salvation*. Through this, it was tested how many in the Christian world today believe that Christ is God even as to His Human; therefore, where many of the Clergy and Laity were gathered, it was proposed to them that they say aloud <term>DIVINE HUMAN</term> <note>original: "DIVINUM HUMANUM." This is a central concept in Swedenborgian theology, asserting that Christ’s human nature was made divine and is the only way to approach the Father.</note>. Yet hardly any were able to pull these two words together out of their thought and thus pronounce them. It was confirmed before them by many passages from the Word that the Lord even as to His Human was God, such as those in Matthew 28:18; John 1:1, 2, 14; Chapter 17:2; Colossians 2:9; 1 John 5:21, and elsewhere; but still they could not speak the words *Divine Human*. What was surprising was that neither could the Lutherans <note>original: "Evangelici," often used for Protestants, specifically Lutherans in this context.</note>, although their orthodoxy teaches that in Christ God is Man and Man is God; and even more so that neither could the Monks, who nevertheless most holily adore the Body of Christ in the Eucharist. From these things it was discovered that the greater part of Christians today are internally either <term>Arians</term> or <term>Socinians</term> <note>Arians denied the full divinity of Christ; Socinians denied His pre-existence and saw Him as a mere man. Both were considered heresies by the established church.</note>, and that if these people worship Christ as God, they are hypocrites. n. 111.

XVI. An altercation concerning a small book, *A Brief Exposition of the Doctrine of the New Church* <note>original: "Summaria Expositio Doctrinæ Novæ Ecclesiæ," a work published by Swedenborg in Amsterdam in 1769.</note>, published by me in Amsterdam; and especially regarding the point that not God the Father, but the Lord God the Redeemer is to be approached and worshipped. Those arguing against this said that it is nevertheless stated in the Lord’s Prayer, *Our Father who art in Heavens, hallowed be thy Name, thy Kingdom come*, and consequently that God the Father is to be approached. To settle this dispute, I was summoned, and I then demonstrated that God the Father in His Divine nature cannot be approached, but only in His Human nature; and because the Divine and the Human in Him are one Person, the Lord is that Father. This was also confirmed from the Word—both from the Old Testament, where the Son of God is called the Father of Eternity, and in many places <term>Jehovah the Redeemer</term>, <term>Jehovah our Righteousness</term>, and the God of Israel—as well as from the New Testament many times. Thus, when the Lord God the Redeemer is approached, the Father is approached, and then His Name is hallowed and His Kingdom comes, besides many other points. n. 112.

XVII. That I saw an Army upon red and black horses, all of them in it turned with their faces toward the horses’ tails, and their backs toward the horses’ heads, shouting for battle against those riding upon white horses. This ludicrious Army broke out from the place called **Armageddon** (Revelation 16:16), and it consisted of those who in their youth were imbued with the dogmas of <term>Justification by faith alone</term>, and who afterwards, when they were promoted to eminent offices, rejected those things which... <note>The text ends mid-sentence.</note>

XVII. That those things which belong to faith and religion pass from the internal parts of their minds to the external parts of the body, where they finally vanish. A description of how they appeared in **Armageddon**, and it was heard from there that they wished to engage in battle with the angels of Michael. This was granted, but at some distance from there; and here a battle was fought among them concerning the understanding of the words in the **Lord’s Prayer**: *Our Father who art in the Heavens, hallowed be thy Name, thy Kingdom come* <note>original: "Pater noster qui es in Cælis, sanctificetur Nomen tuum, adveniat Regnum tuum"</note>. Then it was said by the angels of Michael that the Lord the Redeemer and Savior is the Father to all in the Heavens, since He Himself taught: That the Father and He are one; That the Father is in Him and He is in the Father; That he who sees Him, sees the Father; That all things of the Father are in Him; also that it is the will of the Father that they believe in the Son, and that those who do not believe in the Son shall not see life, but that the anger of God shall remain upon them; also that to Him belongs all power in Heaven and on Earth; and that He has power over all flesh; and furthermore that no one has seen nor can see God the Father, but only the Son who is in the bosom of the Father, besides many other things. After this battle at Armageddon, those who were convicted were partly cast into the **Abyss** <note>A reference to the bottomless pit described in Revelation chapter 9.</note>, concerning which see Revelation Chapter IX, and partly sent away into the desert, n. 113.

XVIII. That I was in a Temple where there were no windows, but a large opening in the roof, and those gathered there spoke together concerning **REDEMPTION**, saying unanimously that Redemption was accomplished through the **Passion of the cross**; but while they were in that conversation, a black Cloud covered the opening in the roof, whence darkness was created in the Temple. However, shortly after, that Cloud was dispersed by Angels who descended from Heaven, who then sent down One from among themselves into the Temple to instruct them concerning Redemption. He said that the Passion of the cross was not Redemption, but rather the subjugation of the Hells, the ordering of the Heavens, and thus the restoration of all things which had collapsed both in the spiritual World and in the natural World, and that without this, no Flesh could have been saved. Concerning the Passion of the cross, he said that through it the most intimate union with the Father was completed; and that when it is accepted as Redemption itself, many things unworthy of God—indeed, even wicked things—follow, such as that He concluded damnation upon the entire Human Race, and that the Son took that upon Himself, and that He thus appeased the Father, and through intercession brought Him back into His Divine Essence, which is Love and Mercy, besides other things which are scandalous to attribute to God; n. 134.

XIX. That the Sun of the spiritual World was seen, in which Jehovah God is in His Human; and then this was heard from Heaven: **THAT GOD IS ONE**; but when this fell down into the spiritual World, it was changed according to the forms of the minds there, and finally into three Gods. One there, reasoning, confirmed this by these points: that there is One who created all things, Another who redeemed all, and a Third who works all things; also that there is One who imputes, Another who mediates, and a Third who inscribes these things upon man, and thus imparts faith, through which He justifies him. But because the Faith in three Gods had perverted the entire Christian Church, from a given perception I uncovered for them what is understood by **Mediation, Intercession, Propitiation, and Expiation** <term>These four terms represent the traditional process of atonement in Christianity, which Swedenborg reinterprets as functions of God's humanity.</term> in the presence of the one God. Namely, that those four are attributes of the Human of Jehovah God: because Jehovah God without the Human cannot approach man, nor be approached by man. **Mediation** signifies that the Human is the intermediary; **Intercession** signifies that He mediates perpetually; **Propitiation** signifies that there is a kind/gracious access for every man to God; and **Expiation** signifies that this access is also for sinners; and all these things are through the Human, n. 135.

XX. That I entered into a **Gymnasium** <note>Swedenborg uses this term to describe halls of learning or debate in the spiritual world.</note>, where it was being debated how one should understand what is said of the Son of God, that He **SITS AT THE RIGHT HAND OF THE FATHER**. Concerning this there were various opinions, yet all held that the Son actually sits in such a way; but they debated why this was so. Then some believed that it was done for the sake of Redemption, some that it was out of love, some that He might be a Counselor, some that He might have honor from...

To the angels, some said it was because it was granted to Him to reign in the place of the Father; others said it was so that He might be heard by the right ear for those for whom He intercedes. Furthermore, they debated whether the Son of God has sat thus from eternity, or whether it was the Son of God born in the world. Having heard these things, I raised my hand <note>original: "sustuli palmam," a gesture requesting permission to speak</note>, asking to be allowed to say something, and to explain what is understood by **sitting at the right hand of God**. I said that it signifies the **Omnipotence of God** through the **Human** which He assumed. For by this He achieved **Redemption**—that is, He subjugated the Hells, created a **New Angelic Heaven**, and restored a **New Church**. I confirmed from the Word that this is what is understood by sitting at the right hand, for by the "Right Hand" power is signified; and afterward, this was confirmed from Heaven by the appearance of a **Right Hand** over them, from whose power and resulting terror almost all were deprived of life, n. 136.

XXI. That in the spiritual world I was led into a certain **Sanhedrin** <note>A formal assembly or council, named after the ancient Jewish high court.</note> in which were gathered famous men who lived before the **Council of Nicaea**—who are called the **Apostolic Fathers**—and also distinguished men who lived after that Council. I saw that some of the latter appeared with smooth-shaven chins and in wigs fashioned from women's hair, but all the former had bearded chins and their own natural hair. Before them stood a man acting as judge and arbiter of the writings of this century, who began with a lamentation, saying: "A man from the **Laity** has arisen who has dragged our Faith out of its sanctuary—that faith which is a star shining day and night before us. But he has done this because he is blind <note>original: "cœcutit"</note> to the mysteries of that faith, and has not seen the justice of Christ within it, nor the wonders of His Justification. Yet that Faith is in **three Divine Persons**, and thus in the whole God; and because he has transferred his faith into the **Second Person**, and not even into Him but into His **Human**, it cannot be otherwise than that **Naturalism** <note>The belief that only nature exists, excluding the divine or supernatural.</note> flows from it." 

Those who lived after the Council of Nicaea favored this statement, saying it was impossible for faith to be anything else or from anywhere else. But the **Apostolic Fathers**, who lived before that century, were indignant and recounted many things said in Heaven about the **Nicene** and **Athanasian Faith**, which may be seen there. But because the leader of the Sanhedrin was associated in spirit with that writer in **Leipzig**, I spoke to him and demonstrated from the Word that Christ is God even as to His **Human**; I also showed from the Lutheran book of dogma called the ***Formula of Concord*** that in Christ God is Man and Man is God, and that the ***Augsburg Confession*** highly approves of the worship of Him, besides many other things, at which he fell silent and turned away. Afterward, I spoke with a certain spirit who was associated with an eminent man in **Gothenburg** <note>Refers to Bishop Erik Lamberg of Gothenburg, an opponent of Swedenborg.</note>, who had defiled the worship of the Lord with even greater insults; but at last, those two insults were declared to be lies invented by craft to turn away wills and deter people from the holy worship of the Lord, n. 137.

XXII. That **Smoke** appeared ascending from the lower earth, and it was said that smokes are nothing other than **falsities** in a mass. Then a desire came upon certain angels to explore what those falsities were that smoked so, and they descended and came upon four troops of spirits: two were of the **Clergy** (learned and unlearned), and two were of the **Laity** (educated and uneducated). They were all confirming among themselves that an **invisible God** must be worshiped, and that holiness and a hearing are then granted to the worshipers, whereas it would be different if a **visible God** were worshiped. They confirmed this holiness and hearing from an invisible God by various arguments, and said that they therefore acknowledge **three Gods from eternity** who are invisible. 

But it was shown that the worship of an invisible God—and especially of three invisible ones—is no worship at all. To confirm this, **Socinus** and **Arius** <note>Faustus Socinus (1539–1604) and Arius (c. 256–336), historical figures who denied the full divinity of Jesus Christ.</note> were brought up from the lower regions with some of their followers, all of whom had worshiped an invisible divinity. When they spoke from their natural or external mind, they said that God exists, even if invisible. But when their external mind was closed and their internal mind opened, and they were compelled by this to give their true confession about God, they said: "What is God? We have not seen His appearance, nor heard His voice. What then is God but a creature of reason <note>original: "ens rationis"</note>, or nature?" But they were instructed that it pleased God to descend—

XXIII. First, concerning the Stars in the natural world, that they are perhaps similar in number to the angelic societies in Heaven, since every society there sometimes shines like a star. Afterward, I spoke with angels about a certain path which appears crowded with countless spirits; it is the path through which all who depart from the natural world pass into the spiritual world. I approached this path in the company of angels, and we called out twelve men from that path and asked them what they believe concerning Heaven and Hell, and the life after death. Because they were recent arrivals from the world and did not know otherwise than that they were still in the natural world, they answered from the ideas they had brought with them: 

**FIRST**, That those who live morally come into Heaven, and that no one goes to Hell, because everyone lives morally. 

**SECOND**, That God rules Heaven and the devil rules Hell, and because they are opposites, one calls "good" what the other calls "evil"; thus a man, if he is a hypocrite, because he stands on the side of both, can live equally under the dominion of one or the other. 

**THIRD**, That there is no Heaven nor Hell; for who has come from there and told us? 

**FOURTH**, That no one has been able to return from there and tell us, because a human, when he dies, is either a ghost or the wind. 

**FIFTH**, That we must wait for the day of the Last Judgment, and that then they will tell you and you will know everything; but when he said this, he laughed in his heart. 

**SIXTH**, How can the soul of a man, which is only wind, re-enter its body eaten by worms, and be reclothed in a skeleton that is either burnt or fallen into dust? 

**SEVENTH**, That humans cannot live any longer after death than beasts and birds; are they not equally rational? 

**EIGHTH**, I believe in Heaven, but I do not believe in Hell, because God is Almighty and is able to save everyone. 

**NINTH**, That God, because He is gracious, cannot send anyone into eternal fire. 

**TENTH**, That no one can come into Hell, because God sent His Son, who expiated all people and took away the sins of everyone; what can the devil do against that? 

**ELEVENTH**, who was a Priest, said that those alone are saved who have attained faith, and that Election <note>The theological doctrine that God chooses certain individuals for salvation before they are even born.</note> is at the disposal of the Almighty. 

**TWELFTH**, who was a Politician, said: I say nothing about Heaven and Hell, but let the priests continue to preach about them, so that the minds of the common people may be held bound by an invisible bond to laws and leaders. 

Upon hearing these things, the angels were stunned, but they woke them up by instructing them that they were now living after death; they then introduced them into Heaven, but they did not stay there long, because it was found that they were merely natural, and that consequently the backs of their heads <note>original: "occipitia." In Swedenborg's spiritual anatomy, the back of the head is associated with the will and the indwelling of spiritual life; a "hollowed" back of the head suggests a lack of genuine spiritual substance.</note> were hollowed out; concerning this hollowing and its cause, something is said at the end, n. 160.

XXIV. That a sound was heard like a mill, and following the sound, I saw a house full of cracks, where an entrance opened underground. In it was a man collecting many things from the Word <note>The Bible</note> and from books concerning **JUSTIFICATION BY FAITH ALONE** <term>Justification: The theological concept of how a person is made right or "just" before God.</term>, and scribes at his side were writing his collections onto paper. When asked what he was now collecting, he said this: that God the Father fell out of grace with the human race, and therefore sent His Son to expiate and propitiate. To this I replied that this is against Scripture and against reason; for if God could fall out of grace, He would also have fallen out of His own essence, and thus He would not be God. When I demonstrated this to the point of conviction, he grew inflamed with anger and ordered his scribes to throw me out; but as I left of my own accord, he threw a book after me which his hand happened to grab, and that book was the Word, n. 161.

XXV. A dispute arose among the spirits as to whether anyone can see any genuine Truth in the Word unless they approach the Lord immediately <note>Without a mediator or through direct spiritual focus on Jesus Christ as God.</note>, who is the Word itself; but because there were those who contradicted this, an experiment was made. Then, those who approached God the Father did not see any truth, but all who approached the Lord saw it. While this dispute was persisting, some spirits ascended from the Abyss <note>In this context, the "Abyss" refers to a lower spiritual region inhabited by those who have confirmed themselves in false doctrines.</note>, concerning...

which <note>This sentence continues from the previous page's description of a vision.</note> **Revelation IX** mentions, where they discuss the secrets of **justification by faith alone**, saying that they themselves approach **God the Father** and see His secrets in **clear light**; but the answer was given that they see those things in a **fatuous light** <note>original: "luce fatua," a deceptive, illusory light like a swamp-fire</note>, and that they do not possess even a single **Truth**. That this was so was proved by their being led into a house where there was a **Table**, upon which **Light from Heaven** flowed directly. They were told to write those truths which they brought from the **Word** upon a **Sheet of Paper**, and to place it upon that table. When this was done, that **Paper** on which the truths were written shone like a **Star**; but truly, when they approached and fixed their gaze upon it, the **Paper** appeared blackened as if by soot. Afterward, they were led to another similar **Table**, upon which lay the **Word** encircled by a **rainbow**; when a certain **standard-bearer** <note>original: "Ante-signanus," a leader or primary advocate of a doctrine.</note> of the doctrine of **faith alone** touched it with his hand, there was an explosion like that from a **musket**, and he was thrown into a corner of the **Room**, where he lay as if dead for **half an hour**. By these things they were convinced that all the truths they had from the **Word** were true in themselves, but falsified in them, n. 162.

XXVI. That in the **Spiritual World** there are **Climates** just as in the **Natural World**; and that from this there are also **Northern Zones**, where there are snows and ice. Once, having been led there in spirit, I entered a **Temple** then covered with snow and illuminated inside by lamps, where behind the Altar was seen a **Tablet** upon which was written this: **THE DIVINE TRINITY: FATHER, SON, AND HOLY SPIRIT, WHO ARE ESSENTIALLY ONE, BUT PERSONALLY THREE**; and I heard a **Priest** preaching about the four **Mysteries of faith**, concerning which the intellect must be kept in check under the **obedience of faith** <note>original: "obedientia fidei," a theological concept where reason is surrendered to dogma.</note>, as they appear. After the **Sermon**, the **Listeners** gave thanks to the **Priest** for his discourse so rich in wisdom; but when I asked them if they understood anything, they replied, "We caught everything with eager ears; why do you ask if we understood? Does the intellect not stand amazed in such matters?" To these things the **Priest**, being present, added: "Because you have heard and not understood, you are blessed, for from that comes your salvation," besides many other things, n. 185.

XXVII. That the **Human Mind** is divided into three **Regions**, just as **Heaven** is in which the **Angels** dwell; and that **Theological matters** reside in the highest region of the Mind among those who love truths because they are truths; and that beneath them, in the middle region, are moral matters, and under these, or in the last region, are political matters, while the various sciences form the door. But among those who do not love truths, **Theological matters** sit in the lowest region, and there they mix themselves with a person's own impulses <note>original: "propriis hominis," referring to the self-centered nature or 'proprium'.</note>, and thus with the fallacies of the senses. And it is for this reason that some are unable to perceive anything of **Theological matters**, n. 186.

XXVIII. That I was led to a place where those meant by the **FALSE PROPHET** in **Revelation** were located; and I was invited by them there to see their **Shrine**, and I followed and saw it. In it was the image of a **Woman** dressed in a scarlet garment, holding a gold coin in her right hand and a chain of pearls in her left; but these things were induced by fantasy. But when the interiors of the mind were opened by the Lord, in place of the Shrine, a house full of cracks was seen, and in place of the woman, a **beast** was seen, such as is described in **Revelation Chapter XIII: 2**; and beneath the floor there was a swamp, in which the **Word** lay deeply hidden. But soon, as an East Wind blew, the Shrine was taken away, the swamp was dried up, and the **Word** was revealed. And then, through light from Heaven, there appeared a **TABERNACLE** like the one **Abraham** had when the three **Angels** came and announced the birth of **Isaac**. And afterward, as light was sent forth from the second Heaven, in place of the Tabernacle there appeared a **TEMPLE** like the one that had been at Jerusalem. After these things, Light from the third Heaven shone upon it, and then the Temple disappeared, and **THE LORD ALONE** was seen standing upon the **Foundation Stone**, where the **Word** was. But because an exceeding holiness then filled the minds, this light was withdrawn, and in its place was sent...

XXIX. That a magnificent Palace was seen, in which there was a Temple, and in this, seats <note>original: "folia," likely a misprint for "solia" meaning thrones or seats</note> were placed in a triple Order: into this a Council was summoned by the Lord, in which they were to deliberate concerning the Lord the Savior, and concerning the Holy Spirit; and when as many of the Clergy were present as there were seats, they entered into the Council; and because it was about the Lord, the first Proposition was, **WHO ASSUMED THE HUMAN IN THE VIRGIN MARY;** and then an Angel standing at the Table read before them what the Angel Gabriel said to Mary, **THE HOLY SPIRIT SHALL COME UPON THEE, AND THE POWER OF THE MOST HIGH SHALL OVERSHADOW THEE, AND THE HOLY THING WHICH SHALL BE BORN OF THEE SHALL BE CALLED THE SON OF GOD, Luke 1:35;** and also from Matthew Chapter 1:20, 25; and moreover many things from the Prophets, that Jehovah himself would come into the World, and also that Jehovah himself is called Savior, Redeemer, and Righteousness; from which it was concluded that Jehovah himself assumed the Human. The second deliberation concerning the Lord was, **WHETHER THE FATHER AND THE LORD JESUS CHRIST ARE ONE IN THIS WAY, AS THE SOUL AND BODY ARE ONE,** and this was confirmed from many places in the Word, and also from the symbolic Faith <note>Referring to the Athanasian Creed, often called the "symbolic faith" in this period.</note> of the Church today; from which it was concluded that the Soul of the Lord was from God the Father, and therefore that His Human is Divine, and that this must be approached so that the Father may be approached, since Jehovah God through it sent Himself into the World, and made Himself visible to the eyes of men, and thus also accessible. There followed a Third deliberation, which was concerning the **HOLY SPIRIT**, and then first the idea of three Divine Persons from eternity was discussed, and it was established from the Word that the Divine Holy, which is called the Holy Spirit, proceeds from the Lord from the Father. Finally, from the deliberations in this Council, this Conclusion was made: That in the Lord the Savior there is a Divine Trinity, which is the Divine from which <note>The "Divine from which" refers to the Father as the essential soul or source.</note> which is called the Father, the Divine Human which is called the Son, and the Divine Proceeding which is called the Holy Spirit, and that thus there is one God in the Church. After the Council was finished, splendid Garments were given to those who participated; and they were led into the New Heaven, no. 188.

XXX. XXXI. That the same Word is still preserved among the peoples in <term>GREAT TARTARY</term> <note>A historical name for the vast region of North and Central Asia, including parts of modern Russia, Mongolia, and China.
