XXXIII. That those who are in the spiritual World cannot appear to those in the Natural world, nor vice versa—thus neither Spirits and Angels to men, nor men to them—on account of the <term>DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE SPIRITUAL AND THE NATURAL</term> <note>original: "discrimen inter spirituale et naturale"</note>, or what is the same thing, between the substantial and the material: it is from this origin that spirits and angels have an entirely different Language, a different Writing, and also different Thought than those which men have. That this is so was revealed through living experience, which took place as they entered into their own circles and returned to me, and thus compared them. From this it was discovered that not even one word of the spiritual Language is similar to any word of a natural Language; and that their Writing consists of syllables, each one of which involves the sense of some thing; and that the Ideas of their thought do not fall into the ideas of natural thought. The cause of these differences is that spirits and angels are in primary principles, but men are in derived things; or that the former are in prior things, which act as causes for posterior things, and men are in the posterior things derived from them. It was said that a similar difference exists between the languages, writings, and thoughts of the Angels of the third Heaven and those of the Angels of the second, no. 280.

XXXIV: Concerning the <term>STATE OF MEN AFTER DEATH</term> <note>original: "statu hominum post mortem"</note> in general; and concerning the state of those who have confirmed themselves in the falsities of Doctrine in particular: concerning both, these things were observed:
1. That men for the most part are resuscitated on the third day after death, and that they then do not know otherwise than that they are still living in the former World. 
2. That all flow into the World that is intermediate between Heaven and Hell, which is called the World of Spirits. 
3. That there they are transferred into various Societies, and thus are explored as to what they are like. 
4. That there the good and faithful are prepared for Heaven, while the evil and unfaithful are prepared for Hell. 
5. Afterward, Hell is described as it is; and that there those are called **Satans** who are in falsities from confirmation, and **Devils** who are in the evils of life, no. 281.

XXXV. That from the lower Earth, which is directly above Hell, I heard outcries: **OH HOW JUST, OH HOW LEARNED, OH HOW WISE.** And because I wondered that "Just, Learned, and Wise" ones were also found there, I descended, and first approached that place where they were crying out, **OH HOW JUST.** And I saw there something like a Tribunal, and in it Judges of injustice, who could skillfully pervert the laws and turn judgments to anyone’s favor; and that thus their judgments were merely based on their own will. And when the sentences were carried out to the clients, then these people would cry out all along the way, "Oh how Just!" Regarding these, the Angels afterward said that such people cannot see even a tiny bit of what is just. After a time, those Judges were cast into Hell, and their law books were turned into playing cards; and in place of judging, they were given the task of preparing makeup <note>original: "fucos" — rouge or paint used for deception or beautification.</note> with which they might smear the faces of harlots, and thus turn them into beauties, no. 332.

Swedenborg often uses this to describe those who have no spiritual life within their intellect.</note>; and that afterward they are sent out into deserts, where they prattle among themselves and speak only vanities, no. 333.

XXXVII. I then approached a third assembly, from where I heard a shout, **OH HOW WISE**, and I found that those gathered there were people who cannot see whether truth is truth, but still make whatever they want appear as truth, and for this reason they are called **CONFIRMERS**; that they were such, I noticed even from various responses to propositions, such as making it true that *Faith is everything of the Church*, and afterward that *Charity is everything of the Church*, and also that *faith and charity together are everything of the Church*; and because they confirmed each of these and adorned them with appearances so that they shone like truths, therefore those standing by shouted, **OH HOW WISE**. Afterward, some playful things were also proposed to them, so that they might make them true, for they say that no truth exists except that which man makes true; these were the playful things: *that light is darkness and darkness light*; then also *that a crow is white and not black*, which two things they made to appear exactly as truths—their confirmations may be seen there. Concerning them, it was told to me by Angels that such people possess not even a grain of understanding; since everything that is above the rational in them is closed, and everything below the rational is open, and this can confirm whatever one pleases, but cannot see any truth to be truth; therefore this is the mark of one who lacks understanding, for to be able to see that truth is truth and falsity is falsity, and to confirm that, is the mark of one who is intelligent. no. 334.

XXXVIII. I spoke with Spirits who were famous for the reputation of their learning in the natural World, who were then disputing among themselves about **INNATE IDEAS**, whether any were in humans as they are in beasts; and then a certain angelic Spirit thrust himself in and said, "You are disputing about <term>goat's wool</term> <note>original Latin idiom: "lana caprina"—referring to a useless or trivial argument over something that doesn't exist.</note>; there are no innate ideas in humans, nor are there any innate in beasts." At these words they all grew angry, but after being given the opportunity to speak, he first spoke about beasts, that no ideas are innate to them. The reason is that they do not think, but only act from instinct, which for them comes from their natural love; this creates an <term>analogue of will</term> in them, which flows immediately into their bodily senses and excites what accords with and favors their love—and yet Ideas are predicated of thought alone. That beasts have only sensation and no thought, he confirmed by various things, especially by the wonders known about spiders, bees, and silkworms, saying: "Does the Spider think in its tiny head, while it forms its web, that it must be connected in this way for these or those uses? Does the Bee think in its tiny head, 'I will suck honey from these flowers, and wax from these; from this I will build cells in a continuous series, and in these I will place honey in abundance so that it also suffices for winter,' besides many other things? Does the Silkworm in its tiny head think, 'Now I will betake myself to spinning silk, and when I have spun it, then I will fly out and play with companions and look out for my prosperity'?" He mentioned similar things among Beasts and Birds. Concerning humans, he said that every mother and nurse, and also father knows, that to newly born infants absolutely no ideas are innate, and that there are none until they have learned to think; then ideas arise and are formed according to the quality of thought which they had drawn from instruction. This happens because nothing else is born with man than the faculty for knowing, understanding, and being wise, and an inclination to love not only oneself and the world, but also the neighbor and God. XXXIX. Once an angelic Spirit illustrated **WHAT FAITH AND CHARITY ARE**, and what their conjunction achieves; he illustrated this through a comparison with Light and Heat, which meet in a third thing, because Light in Heaven is in its essence the Truth of faith, and Heat there in its essence is the Good of charity. Therefore, just as Light without heat—such as exists during winter in the World—strips the trees of their leaves and fruits, so does faith without charity; but just as Light joined to heat—as it is in the springtime—gives life to all things, so does faith joined to charity, no. 385.

XL. Two Angels descended, one from the Eastern Heaven where they are in love, and the other from the Southern Heaven where they are in wisdom. They spoke about whether the essence of the Heavens was Love or Wisdom, and they agreed that it is Love and, from that, Wisdom; therefore, the Heavens were created by God from Love through Wisdom, no. 386.

XLI. After that, I entered a certain Garden where I was led around by a certain Spirit, and finally to a Palace called the **TEMPLE OF WISDOM**. It was quadrangular, the walls were made of crystal, the roof of jasper, and the floor of various precious stones. He said that no one could enter it unless they believed that what they know, understand, and are wise in—compared to what they do *not* know, understand, and are wise in—is respectively so little that it is hardly anything. Because I believed this, I was granted entry, and it was seen that the whole structure was built according to the form of light. In that Temple, I recounted what I had recently heard from the two Angels concerning Love and Wisdom; they asked whether they had also spoken of the Third thing, which is **USE**. They said that Love and Wisdom without Use are merely ideal entities, but in Use they become real; it is the same with Charity, Faith, and Good Works, no. 387. <note>"Use" is a technical term in Swedenborg’s philosophy, referring to the practical application of love and wisdom in service to others.</note>

XLII. One of the Dragon-spirits <note>In Swedenborg's works, "the Dragon" represents those who believe in "faith alone" without the need for a good life.</note> invited me to see the delights of his love and led me to something like an **AMPHITHEATER**. On its benches sat Satyrs and Harlots, and then he said, "Now you shall see our Game." He opened a gate and let in young bulls, rams, goats, and lambs; then, through another gate, he let in lions, panthers, tigers, and wolves, which rushed upon the flock and tore them apart and slaughtered them. But all those things that were seen had been brought about through fantasies. Having seen this, I said to the Dragon, "After a time you will see this theater turned into a Lake of fire and sulfur." When the game was finished, the dragon went out accompanied by his satyrs and harlots and saw a flock of sheep. From this, he understood that one of the Cities of the New Jerusalemites was nearby. Seeing it, he was seized with a desire to capture it and cast out the inhabitants; but because it was surrounded by a wall, he intended to take it by trickery. He then sent one skilled in <term>incantation</term> <note>original: "incantationis"—here implying spiritual manipulation or deceptive persuasion.</note> who, having been let in, spoke craftily with the Citizens about Faith and Charity—specifically which of them is primary, and whether Charity contributes anything to salvation. But the dragon, angry at the response, left the city and gathered many from his crowd and began to besiege the City. Yet, while he was in the middle of his attempt to capture and invade it, fire from Heaven consumed them, according to what was predicted in **REVELATION** <note>original: "Apocalypsi"</note> Chapter 20: 8, 9; no. 388.

After a day, some ascended from there and told what kind of fate they had undergone there, and how they had gone to the Bishops and rebuked them because of their persuasion, and that they had spoken many things with them...

XLIV. That I approached a certain house, where those gathered were debating among themselves whether the good that a man does in the state of justification through faith is a "good of religion" or not. The consensus was that by "good of religion" is meant good that contributes to salvation; but the opinion of those who said that every good a man does does not contribute anything to salvation prevailed, because no voluntary good of man can be joined with what is free <note>meaning "free grace"</note>, since salvation is given freely; nor can any good from man be joined with the Merit of Christ, through which alone salvation is given; nor can the operation of man be joined with the Operation of the Holy Spirit, who does everything without the help of man. From these points it was concluded that good works, even in the state of justification through faith, contribute nothing to salvation, but faith alone. On hearing this, two Gentiles <note>non-Christians, often used by Swedenborg to represent those who live naturally good lives without specific dogma</note> standing in the doorway said to each other: "These people have no religion; who does not know that doing good to the neighbor for God's sake—thus from God and with God—is religion?" no. 390.

XLV. I heard Angels lamenting that there is such **SPIRITUAL POVERTY** today in the Church that they know nothing more than that there are three Divine Persons, and that faith alone saves, and only historical facts about the Lord, and that they are deeply ignorant of what is mentioned in the Word concerning the Lord, His Unity with the Father, His Divinity and Power. And they said that a certain Angel was sent down by them to investigate whether such poverty existed among Christians today, and that he asked a certain man what his religion was; he replied that it was Faith. He then asked him about Redemption, Regeneration, and Salvation; he replied that all those are matters of Faith; and also about Charity, that it is within faith, and "who can do good from himself?" To whom the Angel afterwards said: "You have answered like someone playing a single note on a flute; I hear nothing but faith. But if you know nothing besides that, you know nothing." Then he led him to his companions in a desert, where there was not even a blade of grass; besides more, no. 391.

XLVI. That I saw five gymnasia <note>ancient Greek or Roman places for physical and intellectual exercise, here used as spiritual schools or debating halls</note> surrounded by various lights, and that I entered the First with many others, which appeared as if in a flaming light. Many were gathered there; and the President proposed that they offer their opinions on **CHARITY**. After they began, the **FIRST** said his opinion was that Charity was Morality inspired by faith. The **SECOND**, that it was Piety inspired by pity. The **THIRD**, that it was doing good to everyone, both the upright and the wicked. The **FOURTH**, that it was serving relatives and friends in every way. The **FIFTH**, that it was giving alms to the poor and helping the needy. The **SIXTH**, that it was building Hospitals, Infirmaries, and Orphanages. The **SEVENTH**, that it was enriching Temples and doing good to their Ministers. The **EIGHTH**, that it was the old Christian Brotherhood. The **NINTH**, that it was forgiving everyone their offenses. Each of them confirmed his opinion at length, which, because they are many, cannot be transferred here; therefore let them be seen in the **MEMORABLE RELATION** itself. ...that all those things which were said above by the nine celebrated men concerning Charity are excellent examples of Charity, provided they are done out of justice with judgment; and because Justice and Judgment come from no other source than from the Lord the Savior, so that they are done by a man from Him: this was approved by most in their **Internal Man**, but not yet in their **External Man**, no. 459. <note>In Swedenborg’s thought, the "Internal Man" is the higher part of the mind open to heaven, while the "External Man" is the part interacting with the world. Often, one can understand a truth spiritually but not yet act on it in the physical world.</note>

XLVII. That from a distance a sound was heard like the gnashing of teeth <note>original: "stridor dentium"</note>, and mixed with it a kind of beating noise; I approached the sounds and saw a small hut built of plastered reeds. Instead of the gnashing of teeth and the beating sound, I heard arguments inside the hut about **Faith** and **Charity**: which of them was the essential of the Church. Those who were for Faith brought forth their arguments, saying that Faith is spiritual because it is from God, but Charity is natural because it is from man; in turn, those who were for Charity said that Charity is spiritual and Faith is natural, unless it is joined to Charity. To these a certain **Syncretist** <note>One who attempts to reconcile or merge different, often opposing, beliefs</note>, wishing to settle the dispute, added his confirmation that Faith is spiritual and Charity is only natural. But it was stated that moral life is twofold—spiritual and natural—and that in a man who lives from the Lord, it becomes spiritual-moral, but in a man who does not live from the Lord, it becomes natural-moral, such as is found among the wicked and sometimes among spirits in Hell, no. 460.

XLVIII. That I was led in spirit into a certain Garden in the southern quarter, and there I saw people sitting under a laurel eating figs. I asked them how they understood that a man can do good from God, and yet still do it as if from himself. They replied that God works good within a man, but if the man does it from his own will and understanding, he defiles it so that it is no longer good. But I said to them that man is only an organ of life; and that if he believes in the Lord, he does good from himself from the Lord, but if he does not believe in the Lord (and even more if he does not believe in any God), he does good from himself from Hell. Furthermore, I said that the Lord gave man **Free Will** <note>original: "Liberum Arbitrium"</note> to act from one or the other. That the Lord gave this Freedom was confirmed from the Word <note>The Bible</note>, because He commanded man to love God and his neighbor, to produce the good works of charity as a tree produces fruit, and to keep His commandments to be saved, and that everyone would be judged according to his deeds. None of these would have been commanded if man could not do good from himself from the Lord. After these things were said, I gave them shoots from a certain vine, and the shoots in their hands put forth grapes; among other things, no. 461.

XLIX. That I saw a **MAGNIFICENT SHIPYARD**, and in it large and small vessels, and on the benches were boys and girls who were waiting for **TURTLES** to rise out of the sea. When they emerged, I saw that they had **Two Heads**: one which they withdrew at will into the shells of their bodies, and another which appeared in a form like a man; from this human head they spoke with the boys and girls, who stroked them on account of their elegant speeches and also gave them gifts. After seeing these things, it was explained by an Angel what they signified: namely, that there are men in the world (and consequently as many spirits after death) who say that God does not see anything that those who have attained Faith think or do, but only looks at the faith which He has hidden in the interiors of their minds. These same people, before congregations in temples, bring forth holy things from the Word just like others, but they do this from the "larger head" appearing like a man, into which they then insert the small one, or withdraw it into the body. These same people were later seen in the air in a vessel flying with seven sails, and they were there in laurels and purple garments, shouting that they were the "Heads of the Wise" from all the **Clergy**; but those sights were images of pride flowing from the ideas of their minds. When they were on the earth, I spoke with them first from Reason, and afterward from Holy Scripture, no. 462.

<insert>Continued from previous page:</insert> ...sacred, and I demonstrated through many examples that their doctrine was insane and, because it was against the Sacred Scripture, was from Hell. However, the arguments by which I demonstrated these things cannot be transferred here on account of their length; therefore, they may be seen in the **Memorable Relation** <note>original: "Memorabili"; Swedenborg used these "Memorable Relations" to recount his interactions with spirits between chapters of theological exposition</note> itself. Furthermore, it was noted that they were later seen in a sandy place wearing clothes made of scraps and girded with nets, almost like fishing nets, around their waists, through which their nakedness appeared; and finally, they were sent down into a society which is on the border of the Machiavellians <note>original: "Machiavellistas"; referring to those who prioritize political cunning and deceit over morality</note>, no. 462.

L. That an assembly <note>original: "Comitium"</note> was called together, which sat in a round Temple, in which there were Altars at the sides, near which the members of the assembly sat; but there was no Primate <note>A presiding bishop or leader</note> there, so each person broke out into the middle on their own and shouted the feelings of their mind. A conversation was begun concerning **Free Choice in Spiritual Matters** <note>original: "Libero Arbitrio in Spiritualibus"; the ability of a person to choose spiritual good or evil</note>. The **First** to break out cried out that there was no more Free Choice in such matters for a man than there was for Lot’s wife when she was turned into a pillar of salt. The **Second** said no more than for a beast or a dog. The **Third** said no more than for a mole or an owl in the light of day. The **Fourth** said that if a man had Free Choice in spiritual matters, he would become a maniac and believe himself to be like God, able to regenerate and save himself. The **Sixth** read from the book of the Evangelicals <note>Referring here to the Lutheran church</note> called the **Formula of Concord** <note>original: "Formula Concordiæ"; a key Lutheran doctrinal statement from 1577</note>, stating that a man has no more Free Choice in spiritual matters than a tree trunk or a stone, and that he cannot understand, think, or will even a tiny bit concerning them, and certainly cannot apply or adapt himself to receive anything spiritual—among many other points mentioned above in no. 464. After these things were said, I was also given the opportunity to speak; and speaking, I said: "What is a man without Free Choice in spiritual matters other than a brute? And for what purpose do all theological matters serve without it?" But to this they responded, "Read our theology, and you will not find anything spiritual in it; it is so hidden away inside that not even a shadow of it appears. Therefore, read what our theology teaches about Justification <note>The process of being made righteous before God</note>—that is, about the remission of sins, regeneration, sanctification, and salvation—and you will not see anything spiritual there, because these flow in through faith without any consciousness on the man's part." They also removed charity far from what is spiritual, and likewise removed repentance from any contact with it. Furthermore, regarding Redemption, their theology attributes purely natural human properties to God—such as that He shut up the human race under universal damnation, that the Son took that damnation upon Himself, and that He thus appeased <note>original: "propitiaverit"</note> the Father. And what else is intercession and mediation with the Father? From these things, it is clear that in our entire theology there is nothing spiritual, and not even anything rational, but merely things natural and below those. But then suddenly lightning from Heaven was heard, and the members of the assembly, terrified by it, broke out and everyone fled to his own home, no. 503.

LI. That I spoke with two spirits, one of whom loved good and truth, and the other who loved evil and falsity; and I discovered that both enjoyed a similar faculty for thinking rationally. But when the one who loved evil and falsity was left to himself, I saw as if smoke ascended from hell and extinguished the light that was above his memory. However, when the one who loved good and truth was left to himself, I saw that something like a gentle flame descended from Heaven and illuminated the region of his mind above his memory, and from there also those things which were below it. Afterward, I spoke with the one who loved evil and falsity about **Free Choice in Spiritual Matters**, and at the mere mention of it, he became incensed and cried out that no one can move a foot or hand to do any spiritual good, nor a tongue or mouth to speak any spiritual truth, and thus that one cannot even apply or adapt oneself to receive any such thing. "Is not man dead and merely passive in such matters? How can a dead and merely passive thing do good and speak truth from itself? Does not our Church also speak this way?" The other, however, who loved good and Truth, spoke thus concerning Free Choice in spiritual matters: "What would the whole Word <note>The Bible</note> be without it, and what..."

LI. The Church: what *Religion* is, what the *Worship of God* is, and likewise what the *Ministry* is without it; and from the light of my understanding, I know that a human being without that spiritual *Free Choice* <note>original: "Libero"; referring to the capacity to choose spiritual good or evil</note> would not be a human, but a beast, for it is from that *Freedom* that a human is a human and not a beast; and furthermore, that without *Free Will* <note>original: "Libero arbitrio"</note> in spiritual matters, a person would have no life after death, and thus no eternal life, because there would be no conjunction with God; therefore, to deny this belongs only to those who are insane in spiritual matters. Afterward, something like a fiery serpent <note>original: "præster"; likely a reference to the 'fiery serpents' of the Bible, symbolizing sensual and deceptive reasoning</note> was seen in a tree, which offered fruit from there to the one who denied *Free Will* in spiritual things; after it was eaten, smoke appeared ascending from hell, which extinguished the light in the upper part of his rational mind, no. 504.

LII. A grinding sound was heard like two millstones <note>original: "lapidum molarium"; millstones often symbolize the grinding out of doctrines or arguments</note> colliding with one another, and I went toward the source of the sound and saw a house containing many small cells. In these sat the "Learned" of this age, confirming **JUSTIFICATION BY FAITH ALONE**. Approaching one, I asked what he was working on; he replied it was the **ACT OF JUSTIFICATION**, which is the head of all doctrine in our Orthodoxy. I asked whether he knew of any sign when justifying faith enters and when it has entered; he said that this happens passively and not actively. To this I replied that if you take away the "active" in it, you also take away the "receptive," and thus that "act" would be merely an ideal state—what is called a "thing of reason" <note>original: "ens rationis"; a philosophical term for something that exists only in the mind</note>. It would be nothing but the tinkling statue of Lot's wife <note>A biblical reference to being turned into a pillar of salt (Genesis 19:26)</note>, made of pure salt, or like the stroke of a scribe's pen or a fingernail. The man, becoming enraged, took a lampstand to throw it at me, but the lamp being extinguished, he threw it at his companion instead, no. 505.

LIII. Two flocks were seen, one of goats and the other of sheep; but when viewed up close, they were seen as men instead of goats and sheep. It was perceived that the flock of goats consisted of those who make Faith alone the means of salvation, and the flock of sheep of those who make Charity and Faith together the means. When asked why they were there, those who appeared as goats said they were holding a council, because it had been revealed to them that Paul's saying—*That a man is justified by faith without the works of the law* (Romans 3:28)—has not been rightly understood. They argued that "Faith" there does not mean modern faith, but faith in the Lord the Savior; and by "Works of the Law" are meant not the works of the Decalogue <note>The Ten Commandments</note>, but the works of the Mosaic law, which were ritualistic. This was also demonstrated; and they said they had concluded that Faith produces good works just as a tree produces fruit. Those who made up the flock of sheep favored this; but then an Angel, standing between the two flocks, cried out to the flock of sheep: "Do not listen, for they have not receded from their former Faith!" He divided the flock of sheep into two and said to those on the left: "Join yourselves to the goats, but I foretell to you that a wolf is coming who will snatch them away, and you with them." Then an inquiry was made into how they understood that "Faith produces good works like a tree produces fruit," and it was found that their perception of the conjunction of faith and charity was entirely different from that comparison, and thus it was a deceptive way of speaking. Once this was understood, the flocks of sheep reunited into one as before, and some of the goats joined them, confessing that charity is the essence of faith, and that faith separated from it is merely "natural," but when joined to it, it becomes "spiritual," no. 506.

LIV. A conversation with Angels about the three Loves, which are universal and thus present in every human being: **LOVE OF THE NEIGHBOR OR THE LOVE OF USES**, which in itself is spiritual; **LOVE OF THE WORLD OR THE LOVE OF POSSESSING WEALTH**, which in itself is **MATERIAL**; and **LOVE OF SELF OR THE LOVE OF RULING OVER OTHERS**, which in itself is corporeal <note>fleshly or physical</note>. When those three loves are rightly subordinated in a person, the person becomes truly human; they are rightly subordinated when the love of the neighbor forms the head, the love of the world the body, and the love of self the feet. It is entirely different when they sit in a person contrary to this order. It was shown what a person is like when the love of the world forms— <note>text cuts off, likely continuing on the next page</note>

...the head, and the nature of self-love; that when it dominates, the human being is inverted, appearing wild in the inner parts of his mind, but appearing as a stage-actor <note>original: "histrio"; an actor or one who puts on a false front</note> in his outer parts and thus in his body. After this, a certain devil was seen ascending from the lower regions with a gloomy face and a white circle around his head. He claimed to be Lucifer, though he was not, and stated that in his inner self he is a devil, but in his outer self he is an Angel of Light. He related that while in his outer state, he is moral among the moral, rational among the rational, and even spiritual among the spiritual. When he lived in the world, he preached and spoke out against evildoers of every kind, and was therefore called a "son of the Morning" <note>original: "filius Aurorae"; a traditional title for Lucifer</note>. He expressed wonder that while he was in the pulpit, he perceived things no differently than as he spoke; yet it was quite different when he was outside the Temple. He explained the cause: in the Temple he was in his *Externals* and only in his *Understanding*, but outside the Temple he was in his *Internals* and in his *Will*. Thus, the Understanding lifted him up toward Heaven, but the Will dragged him down toward hell; and the Will prevails over the Understanding because the Will directs the latter to its own favor and whim. After this, the devil who was lying about being Lucifer sank down into Hell, no. 507.

**LV.** A round Temple was seen, whose roof was like a Crown, its walls were continuous windows made of crystal, and the gate was made of a pearly substance. Inside was a pulpit upon which lay the Word <note>referring to the Holy Scriptures</note> surrounded by a sphere of light. In the center of the Temple was the Sanctuary <note>original: "Adytum"; the innermost, most sacred part of a temple</note> before which hung a Veil, but it was now pulled aside; within stood a Cherub with a flashing sword in hand. After these sights, the meaning of each thing was explained to me. Above the gate was this writing: **NOW IT IS PERMITTED** <note>original: "**NUNC LICET**"</note>, which signified that it is now permitted to enter intellectually into the Mysteries of faith. It was given to me to perceive that it was very dangerous to enter into the dogmas of faith through the intellect when those dogmas are born of one's own intelligence and are thus based on falsehoods—and even more dangerous to try to confirm them using the Word. For this reason, by Divine Providence, the Word was taken away from Roman Catholics, and among Protestants it was closed off by their own dogma that the Understanding must be held captive under obedience to their faith. But because the Dogmas of the New Church <note>referring to the "New Jerusalem" or the new spiritual era the author describes</note> are all from the Word, it is permitted to enter into them with the Intellect, because they are continuous Truths from the Word which shine clearly before the intellect. This is what is meant by the writing over the gate, **NOW IT IS PERMITTED**, and by the fact that the Veil of the Sanctuary was pulled aside. Afterward, a paper was brought to me by an infant who was an Angel in the third heaven, on which was written:

> **ENTER HENCEFORTH INTO THE MYSTERIES OF THE WORD HITHERTO CLOSED, FOR ITS INDIVIDUAL TRUTHS ARE SO MANY MIRRORS OF THE LORD**, no. 508.

**LVI.** That I was seized by a severe illness from the smoke flowing in from "Jerusalem," which in Revelation 11:8 is called Sodom and Egypt. I was seen by those in that City as if I were dead; they said among themselves that I was not worthy of burial, just as is said of the two Witnesses in that same chapter of Revelation. Meanwhile, I heard many blasphemies from the townspeople because I had preached repentance and faith in the Lord Jesus Christ. But because judgment was looming over them, I saw that the whole City fell and was flooded with waters; afterward, they ran about among heaps of stones, lamenting their fate, even though they believed that through the faith of their Church they were reborn and thus righteous. But they were told they were nothing of the sort, since they had never practiced any repentance, and therefore did not know a single damnable evil within themselves. Afterward, it was told to them from Heaven that faith in the Lord and repentance are the two Means of regeneration and salvation, and that this is very well known from the Word, and moreover from the Decalogue, Baptism, and the Holy Supper, concerning which see the **MEMORABLE RELATION**, no. 567.

LVII. That all who come into the spiritual world after death are held, in the first stage, in *Externals* <note>The "external man" refers to the outward personality, social manners, and public behavior one used while living in the world.</note>, in which they were in the natural world. Because most people live morally, attend church, and pray to God while in these Externals, they believe they will certainly come into Heaven. However, they are taught that every person after death successively strips off the External man, and the Internal man is opened. Then it becomes known what the person is like in themselves, since a human being is a human being based on their Will and Understanding, and not solely from Action and Speech. From this, it follows that a person can appear in *Externals* like a *Sheep*, even though in *Internals* they are like a *Wolf*; and such is the person in their Internal man unless they explore the evils of their will and their intention therefrom, and perform repentance for them; plus more, n. 568.

LVIII. That every Love breathes out a delight, but that the DELIGHTS OF LOVES <note>original: "jucunda amorum"; the pleasant sensations or joys that arise from what a person loves.</note> are felt only slightly in the natural world, but clearly in the spiritual world. There, they are sometimes turned into odors, and it is then perceived what kind the delights are and to which love they belong. The delights of good love, such as those in the *Heavens*, are perceived like fragrances in gardens and flower beds; conversely, the delights of evil love, such as those in the *Hells*, are perceived like stenches and foul smells from stagnant pools and latrines. Because they are so opposite, devils are tortured when they sense any sweet-smelling odor of heaven, and likewise, angels are tortured when they sense any foul-smelling odor of Hell. That this is so was confirmed by two examples. For this reason, the Anointing Oil was prepared from aromatics, and it is said of Jehovah that He smelled a "pleasing odor" from burnt offerings; and conversely, it was commanded to the children of Israel that they should carry unclean things outside the camp and bury their excrement; for their camp represented Heaven, and the desert outside represented Hell, n. 569.

LIX. That a certain new spirit, who in the world meditated much on Heaven and Hell, desired to know what both were like. He was told from Heaven: INQUIRE WHAT IS DELIGHTFUL AND YOU WILL KNOW <note>original: "Inquire quid jucundum et cognosces"</note>. Therefore, going away, he inquired, but among purely natural spirits he did so in vain. But he was led to three Assemblies in order: to one where they explored Ends <note>The ultimate purposes or motivations behind actions.</note>, and were therefore called *Wisdoms*; to another where they searched into Causes, and were therefore called *Intelligences*; and to a third where they examined Effects, and were therefore called *Sciences*. From all of these, he was instructed that life for every angel, spirit, and person comes from the Delight of their love, and that the will and thought cannot move a single step except from the delight of some love, and this delight is what everyone calls "Good." Furthermore, the Delight of Heaven is the delight of doing good, and the delight of Hell is the delight of doing evil. So that he might be further instructed, a devil unexpectedly ascended and described the delights of Hell in his presence—that they consisted of revenging, committing adultery, plundering, and blaspheming—and that when these are sensed there as odors, they are sensed as balsams, which is why he called them the "delights of his nostrils," n. 570.

LX. That an Assembly of spirits was seen praying to God to send Angels who might instruct them on various matters of faith, because they were hesitant on most points, since the Churches differ so much among themselves, and all their ministers say: BELIEVE US, WE ARE MINISTRI OF GOD, AND WE KNOW. Angels appeared, whom they questioned about *Charity* and *Faith*, about *Repentance*, about *Regeneration*, about *God*, about the *Immortality of the soul*, and about *Baptism* and the *Holy Supper*. To each of these the Angels responded in such a way that it fell into their understanding <note>The angels provided rational explanations rather than demanding blind faith.</note>, saying further that everything which does not fall into the understanding is like seed sown in sand, which, however much it is watered by rain, still withers away. Also, that an Understanding closed by religion no longer sees anything in the *Word* <note>The Bible or Sacred Scripture.</note> from the light that is within it from the Lord; indeed, if one reads it, they become more and more blind in matters of faith and salvation, n. 621.

LXI. How a person, once they are prepared for Heaven, enters it: specifically, that after preparation they see the path leading to the Society in Heaven where they are to live forever; and that near the society there is a gate which is opened; and that after entry, it is examined whether there is in them a similar light and similar heat—that is, a similar truth and good—as is found among the Angels of that society. When this is discovered, they walk about and inquire where their own home is, for there is a new home for every novice Angel; once it is found, they are received and counted as one among them. But for those in whom there is no light and heat—that is, the truth and good of Heaven—there is a harsh fate: when they enter, they are miserably tortured, and because of the agony, they cast themselves headlong downward. This happens to them because of the sphere of Heaven’s light and heat, which is the opposite of what they are. Afterward, these people no longer desire Heaven but are associated with their own kind in Hell. From this, it is clear how vain it is to think that Heaven is merely admission by grace, and that those admitted enjoy joys there just like those in the World who enter a wedding house, n. 622.

LXII. That many who believed Heaven was merely admission by grace, and that after admission there would be eternal joy, ascended into Heaven by permission; but because they could not endure the light and heat—that is, the faith and love there—they threw themselves down headlong. At that time, to those standing below who saw them, they appeared like **dead Horses**. Among those standing below who saw them this way were some boys with their teacher; he instructed them on what the appearance of **dead Horses** signified, and who they are who appear that way from a distance. He said they are those who, when they read the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scripture or the Bible.</note>, think materially and not spiritually about God, the Neighbor, and Heaven. Those think materially of God who think of His Essence based on His Person; of the Neighbor based on his face and speech rather than his quality; and of Heaven as a place rather than a state of love. But those think spiritually who think of God based on His Essence and from that His Person; of the Neighbor based on his quality and from that his face and speech; and of Heaven based on the state of love there and from that the place. Afterward, he taught them that a **Horse** signifies the understanding of the Word; and because the Word is a "living Letter" to those who think spiritually while reading it, they appear from a distance like **living Horses**; conversely, because the Word is a "dead Letter" to those who think materially, they appear from a distance like **dead Horses**, n. 623.

LXIII. That an Angel was seen with a Paper in his hand, upon which was written <term>THE MARRIAGE OF GOOD AND TRUTH</term> <note>original: "Conjugium boni et veri"; the fundamental union of the heart’s intentions (good) and the mind’s thoughts (truth).</note>, descending from Heaven into the World. It was seen that the Paper shone in Heaven, but in its descent, it shone gradually less and less until neither the Paper nor the Angel appeared, except to some unlearned people who were simple of heart. To these, the Angel explained what the "Marriage of Good and Truth" involves—namely, that each and every thing in the whole Heaven and the whole World contains both together, because good and truth make one in the Lord God the Creator. Therefore, there is nowhere anything that is only good, nor anything that is only truth; consequently, in each and every thing, there is a Marriage of good and truth, and in the Church, a Marriage of Charity and Faith, since Charity belongs to good and Faith belongs to truth, n. 624.

...possessing the goods of the world from the love of performing uses <term>uses: meaningful work or service to others that contributes to the common good</term>, and truly conjugial <note>original: "conjugialis," referring to the spiritual and physical union of marriage</note> love; and that the universal principles of hell are three loves opposite to those three, which are: the love of ruling from self-love, the love of possessing the goods of others from the love of the world, and scortatory <term>scortatory: relating to casual or illicit sexual encounters</term> love. It is described afterward what the first **INFERNAL LOVE IS, WHICH IS THE LOVE OF RULING FROM SELF-LOVE**, showing that among laypeople it is such that when the reins are loosened, they wish to rule over everything in the world, and among the clergy, they wish to rule over everything in heaven. That such a fantasy <note>original: "phantasia," here meaning a delusive or hallucinatory mental state</note> exists among those who are in that love was confirmed by similar people in hell, where such people are together in a certain valley, who delight their spirits through fantasies that they are "emperors of emperors" or "kings of kings"; and elsewhere, that they are Gods; and it was seen that at the sight of these, the former ones—who were of such lofty spirit—fell upon their knees and worshipped them. That afterward I spoke with two others, one of whom was a Prince of a certain society in heaven, and the other who was a High Priest there, who said that among them in that society things are magnificent and splendid because their love is not from self-love but from the love of uses, and that they are surrounded by honors, and that they accept them not for their own sake, but for the sake of the good of obedience. I then asked them how anyone can know whether they perform a use from the love of self or the world, or from the love of uses, since all three perform uses; suppose there were a society composed of sheer satans, and a society composed of sheer angels, I could guess that the satans would perform just as many uses in their society from the love of self and the world as the angels do in theirs. Who, then, can know from which love the uses come? To this the Prince and Priest replied that satans perform uses for the sake of reputation, so they may be raised to honors and gain wealth, but angels perform uses for the sake of the use itself; however, the former are distinguished from the latter primarily by this: that everyone who believes in the Lord and shuns evils as sins performs uses from the Lord, and thus from the love of uses, but everyone who does not believe, nor shuns evils as sins, performs uses from themselves and for themselves, and thus from the love of self or the world, n. 661.

<margin>LXVI.</margin> That I entered a certain grove and saw two angels talking together; I approached, and they were speaking about the **LUST OF POSSESSING ALL THINGS OF THE WORLD**, and that many who appear moral in their actions and rational in their speech are in the insanity of that lust, and that this lust turns into fantasies among those who indulge their ideas regarding it; and because everyone is allowed to delight in their own fantasy in the spiritual world as long as they do no evil to another, there are also congregations of such people in the lower earth <note>the "lower earth" refers to a region in the spiritual world between heaven and hell</note>; and because it became known where they were, we descended and entered among them, and saw that they were sitting at tables on which was a huge amount of gold coins, saying that those were the riches of all kingdoms, but it was only an imaginary vision called a fantasy, through which they created that appearance: but when it was said to them that they were insane, they turned from the tables and confessed it was so, but because that vision delighted them so much, they could not help but enter by turns and favor the charms of their senses: they added to this that if anyone steals from another or does other evil, they fall into a certain prison beneath them, and are kept there to work for food, clothing, and a few small coins <note>original: "obulis," a small unit of currency</note>, and if they do evil even there, they are deprived of those things and punished, n. 662.

The Ambassador began to confirm with many arguments that all Intelligence and also Prudence <term>Prudence: here meaning practical wisdom or the ability to govern one's actions rightly</term> is from God. Afterward, the Priests were also asked to take off their own garments and put on the garments of political ministers. When this was done, the Priests spoke from their interior selves, saying that all Intelligence and Prudence is from man. The reason they spoke this way was that a Spirit thinks himself to be such as the clothing upon him suggests. After this, those three became "heart-friends," and while talking together, they walked along a way that stretched downward; but later I saw them returning. (number 663).

LXVIII. The discussion first concerns those who in the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note> are called the **ELECT** <note>original: "Electi"</note>, and that these are those who, after death, are found to have lived a life of Charity and Faith. They are separated from those who did not live such a life, and thus they are the ones who are then **CHOSEN** and prepared for Heaven. Therefore, to believe that only some are chosen and predestined for Heaven before or after birth—and not all, since all are called—would be to accuse God of an inability to save, and also of injustice. (number 664).

LXIX. It was stated by a certain newcomer in Heaven that no one in the Christian world knows what **CONSCIENCE** <note>original: "Conscientia"</note> is. Because the Angels did not believe this, they told a certain Spirit to summon the "Intelligent ones" with a trumpet to ask whether they knew what Conscience is. This was done, and they arrived; among them were Politicians, Scholars, Doctors, and Priests. First, the **POLITICIANS** were asked what Conscience is. They replied that it is a pain arising from a preconceived or later-conceived fear of losing honor or wealth, or that it arises from a "melancholy humor" <note>An old medical theory suggesting that an imbalance of bodily fluids caused sadness or anxiety.</note> originating from indigestion in the stomach, among other things. Afterward, they asked the **SCHOLARS** <note>original: "Eruditos"</note> what they knew of Conscience. They replied that it is a grief and anxiety infesting the body and then the head, or the head and then the body, from various causes—especially when the mind is fixed on only one thing, which happens primarily when one's "reigning love" <term>reigning love: the primary motivation or obsession that governs a person's life</term> suffers. From this, fantasies, delusions, and in some, religious manias occur, which are called the "bites of conscience." After these, the **DOCTORS** were asked what Conscience is, and they said it is merely a pain arising from various diseases (which they listed in great number) and that they had cured many such people through medicines. The diseases from which these pains—called Conscience—are derived may be seen listed in the **MEMORABLE RELATION**. Finally, the **PRIESTS** were asked what Conscience is. They said it is the same as Contrition <note>original: "Contritio"; the feeling of remorse for sins.</note>, which precedes Faith, and that they cured it through the Gospel. Furthermore, they said there are "conscientious" people in every religion, both true and fanatical, who create scruples for themselves in matters of salvation, even in indifferent matters <note>original: "adiaphoris"; things that are religiously neutral or not essential to salvation.</note>. After hearing these things, the Angels perceived the truth: that no one knew what Conscience is. Therefore, they sent an Angel from among them to teach. Standing in their midst, he said that Conscience is not a "pain," as you all have supposed, but is a life lived according to Religion. That life is found primarily among those who are in the faith of Charity; those who have conscience speak what they speak from the heart and do what they do from the heart. He illustrated this with examples. Therefore, when it is said of someone that they "have a Conscience," it is understood that they are a just person, and vice versa. Having said this, those who had been summoned divided themselves into four groups: into the first went those who understood the Angel's words and favored them; into the second, those who did not understand but still favored them; into the third, those who did not want to understand, saying to one another, "What do we have to do with Conscience?"; and into the fourth, those who mocked, saying, "What is Conscience but a puff of wind?" After this, the two latter groups were seen to withdraw to the left, and the two former to the right. (number 665).

...inquiring into something regarding wisdom, such as it is today on earth; and then two Christians were found and brought forward, who were immediately asked, **WHAT IS NEW FROM THE EARTH** <note>original: "QUID NOVI E TERRA"</note>; and they replied that this is the News there: that men have found in the forests people who were perhaps left there in early childhood, and that these appear as humans in their faces, but nevertheless were not truly human; and that from these cases, people in the World have concluded that a man is nothing more than a beast, except that he is able to articulate sound and thus speak, and that a beast could similarly be wise if it were trained to sound articulately, along with several other points. The Sages <term>Sages: Translated from "Sophi," referring here to the wise men of the ancient world who lived according to spiritual principles</term>, having heard these things, drew several conclusions about Wisdom and the changes it had undergone since their times. They were especially struck by the fact that people no longer know the distinction between the state of a human and the state of a beast, nor even that a human is only born into the *form* of a human, and that he becomes a human through instruction—becoming the kind of human that corresponds to the instruction he receives. He becomes wise from truths, insane from falsehoods, and inwardly a wild beast from evils. They noted that only the *capacity* for knowing, understanding, and being wise is born in a person, for the purpose that he might be a subject into whom God can inspire wisdom from its first degree to its highest. They said further that they understood from the Newcomers that the wisdom which in their time was in the East is today in the West. Afterward, they instructed the Newcomers on how it is that a human, created in the image of God, could be turned into the form of a devil: but concerning these things and others, see the **MEMORABLE RELATION** <note>original: "MEMORABILE"</note>, number 692.

<margin>LXXI.</margin> <note>71</note> An Assembly was again called in the place where the ancient Sages were, because they had heard from messengers that they had encountered three new Newcomers from the earth: one who was a Priest, another who was a Politician, and the third who was a Philosopher. When they were brought in, they were immediately asked, **WHAT IS NEW FROM THE EARTH**, and they replied: this is the News, that they have heard that a certain man claims to speak with Angels and Spirits, and that he recounts many things about their state. Among these, he claims that a person is just as much a human after death, with the only difference being that he is then clothed in a spiritual body, whereas before he was in a material body. Having heard these things, they asked the **PRIEST** what he had thought of those claims while on Earth. He replied that because he had believed that a person would not live as a human again until the day of the Last Judgment <note>The "Last Judgment" refers to the traditional theological belief that souls wait in an intermediate state until the end of the world to be reunited with their physical bodies</note>, he and others of his Order thought the man's reports were visions, and later mere inventions, and that finally he had been at a loss. 

To the question of whether the inhabitants of the earth could not see through Reason that a human lives as a human after death, and thus dispel those paradoxes about the state of souls in the meantime—which claim that souls meanwhile flutter like winds in the Universe and continually await the Last Judgment to be joined with their bodies (a fate that would be worse than that of any beast)—the Priest replied that people might say so but are not convinced. He added that they attribute the joining or reunion of souls with their corpses and skeletons in the grave to the Omnipotence of God, and when they name Omnipotence and also Faith, all reason is exiled. Afterward, the **POLITICIAN** was asked about what he had heard; he replied that in the World he could not believe that a human would live as a human after death, since everything belonging to the human lies dead in the grave, and thus he thought that man had seen Phantoms and believed them to be angels and spirits. But he said that now, for the first time, he was convinced by his very senses that a human lives just as before, and that he was therefore ashamed of his former thoughts. The **PHILOSOPHER** related almost similar things about himself and some from his School; and furthermore, that he had filed away those things he had heard about what was seen and heard by that man among the "Opinions and Hypotheses" which he had collected from both Ancient and Modern sources. 

The Sages, having heard these things, were' struck with' amazement—especially that Christians, who are in light above others due to Revelation <note>The "Revelation" refers to the written Word or Bible</note>, should be in such darkness concerning their life after death, when "we and the wise men of our time knew and believed in that life." They said further that they noticed that the Light of wisdom from that age has lowered itself from the interior parts of the Brain...

**LXXII.** That new Visitors from the World were found and led to the City under Mount Parnassus <note>In Greek mythology, Parnassus was the home of the Muses and the seat of poetry and learning; here it represents a place of wisdom in the spiritual world.</note>, and they were asked, **WHAT IS NEW FROM THE EARTH** <note>Original: "QUID NOVI E TERRA"</note>. They replied that in the World they had believed that after death there would be a total Rest from labors. However, they heard when they came here that there are Administrations, Offices, and Works just as in the former World, and thus that there is no Rest. To this, the Sages there replied: "You believed this because you thought you would now live in mere idleness; yet from idleness comes a sluggishness, numbness, stupidity, and sleepiness of the Mind and thus of the whole Body, which are Death and not Life." Then they were led around the City to see the Administrators and Workers. Having seen these, they wondered that such things existed, since they had also believed in a certain "empty void" <note>Original: "inane," referring to a common philosophical or theological idea that the soul exists as a formless vapor after death.</note> in which souls would live before a New Heaven and a New Earth came into being. They were instructed that everything appearing here before their eyes is **substantial** (called "spiritual"), while everything in the former World is **material** (called "natural"). This difference exists because they have different origins: specifically, everything in this World exists and subsists from the Sun which is pure Love, while everything in that World exists from the Sun which is pure Fire. Furthermore, they were instructed that not only are there Administrations in this World, but also Studies of every kind, as well as Writings and Books. The Visitors were gladdened by these instructions, and as they were leaving, certain Virgins came with embroidery and spinning—the works of their own hands—and gave these to them. Before them, they sang an Ode which expressed the affection for useful works along with its pleasures in an angelic melody. (See section number 694).

**LXXIII.** That I was introduced into an Assembly where some of the ancient Philosophers were present, and I was asked what people in my World know about **INFLUX** <term>Influx: The spiritual process by which life and influence flow from the soul into the body, or from the spiritual world into the natural world.</term>. To this I replied that they know of no other than the Influx of the light and heat of their own Sun into the things of nature—both those that are animate and those that are inanimate. I told them that people know absolutely nothing of the Influx of the spiritual World into the Natural, even though all the wonders seen in the animal and vegetable kingdoms (which are partially listed here) result from that Influx. Because they do not know of this Influx, they confirm themselves in favor of Nature and become Naturalists, and eventually Atheists. (See section number 695).

**LXXIV.** That I spoke with the followers of Aristotle, Descartes, and Leibniz concerning **PHYSICAL INFLUX**, **OCCASIONAL INFLUX**, and **PRE-ESTABLISHED HARMONY** <note>These represent three major historical theories on how the mind and body interact. Physical Influx (Aristotle) suggests the body affects the soul; Occasional Influx (Descartes/Malebranche) suggests God intervenes at every moment; Pre-established Harmony (Leibniz) suggests they are like two clocks synchronized by God at creation.</note>, and I heard how each man confirmed his own hypothesis. Since they could not look into the matter with an understanding above these arguments, but only from within them, they settled the dispute by drawing lots. The lot came out in favor of **Spiritual Influx**, which in some respects coincides with Occasional Influx. (See section number 696).

**LXXV.** That I was led into a certain Gymnasium (a place of learning) in which Youths were being initiated into various matters of wisdom. The subject of the debate then was: **WHAT IS THE SOUL, AND WHAT IS ITS NATURE?** There was a Podium which those about to answer would ascend. Soon one man ascended, saying that no one since the creation of the world has been able to discover what the soul is or what its nature is. But because they knew the Soul was in man, it was asked exactly where it resided. There was one who thought that in man it resides in a certain Gland called the **Pineal Gland**, which sits between the two...

That an Angel was seen with a trumpet, through which he called together those celebrated for their learning among Christians, so that they might bring forward what they had previously believed in the World regarding **the Joy of Heaven, and Eternal Happiness**. This was done because it was said in Heaven that no one in the Christian World knows anything about these things. After a short hour, six groups of learned Christians were seen to be present, who, when asked what they knew about the Joys of Heaven and eternal Happiness, spoke as follows: The **First Group** said they believed it would simply be an Admission into Heaven, and then into its festive Joys, just as someone is admitted into a wedding house and its festivities. The **Second Group** said they believed it to be the most joyful Company and most pleasant Conversations with Angels. The **Third Group** said they believed it to be Feasting with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. The **Fourth Group** said they believed it to be Paradisiacal Delights. The **Fifth Group** said it was supreme Dominions, the most opulent Treasures, and more-than-royal Magnificence. The **Sixth Group** said it was the Glorification of God, and a Festival lasting forever. Therefore, so that those learned men might know whether the things they believed were the joys of heaven, it was granted to them to enter into those joys of theirs, and to each group by itself, for the reason that they might learn through living experience whether those joys were imaginary or real; this happens with most who flow from the natural World into the spiritual one, sections 731, 732, 733.

And then soon that Group, which had thought Heavenly Joys were the most joyful Company and pleasant Conversations with Angels, was let into the joys of their imagination; but because they were external joys and not internal, after a few days they were affected by weariness and withdrew, section 734.

***

Afterwards those who had believed that Heavenly Joys were Feasting with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, were let into similar things; but because they perceived that those Joys were only external and not internal, they became weary and departed, section 735.

— A similar experience occurred with those who believed that **Heavenly Joys and eternal Happiness** consist in high-ranking positions of power, the wealthiest treasures, and royal magnificence, n: 736. <note>The author uses these stories to illustrate that spiritual happiness is not the same as worldly status or wealth.</note>

— Similarly, afterwards, with those who believed that **Heavenly Joys and eternal Happiness** consist in the perpetual glorification of God and a festival lasting forever; these were finally instructed on what is understood in the **Word** <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note> by the "Glorification of God," n: 738.
— Finally, the same occurred with those who believed they would enter into **Heavenly Joys** and Happiness simply by being admitted into **Heaven**, thinking that joys would be for them just as they are for those who enter a wedding house and join in the festivities; but because it was shown to them through living experience that there are no joys in **Heaven** except for those who have lived the life of heaven—that is, a life of charity and faith—and that, conversely, **Heaven** becomes a place of torment for those who have led a contrary life, they withdrew and joined themselves with those like them, n: 739.
Because it was perceived by the Angels that no one in the natural world yet knew the nature of **Heavenly Joys**, and thus the nature of eternal happiness, a trumpet-angel was commanded to choose ten men from those assembled and introduce them into a **Society of Heaven**, so that they might see with their own eyes and perceive with their minds what **Heaven** is and what kind of joys are there; and so it was done. After their admission, they were first permitted to see the magnificent Palace of the Prince there, n: 740. Then the Paradise nearby, n: 741. Afterwards, the Prince himself and his Nobles in splendid garments, n: 742. Then, invited to the Prince’s Table, they saw preparations such as no eye on earth had ever seen; and at the Table they heard the Prince instructing them regarding **Heavenly Joys and eternal Happiness**, explaining that they essentially consist in **internal Bliss**, and from this in **external Delights**, and that internal bliss derives its essence from the <term>affection for use</term> <note>Original: "affectione usus." This refers to the love of being helpful or performing productive service for others, which the author argues is the core of heavenly happiness.</note>, n: 743. After the meal, by the Prince’s command, certain wise men of that Society were summoned, who fully instructed them on what internal bliss is and where it comes from—which is Eternal Happiness—and how this bliss makes external delights become true Joys, along with many other things concerning these matters, n: 745 to 746. After this, they were permitted to see a Wedding in that **Heaven**, regarding which see n: 747 to 749. And finally, they listened to a Sermon, n: 750. 751. Having seen and heard all these things, full of knowledge about **Heaven** and glad in heart, they descended, n: 752.

**LXXVII.** This section treats of <term>REVELATION</term>; that it has pleased the Lord to manifest Himself to me, and to open the interiors of my Mind, and thus to allow me to see the things that are in **Heaven and Hell**, and that He has thus uncovered Secrets which in excellence and dignity exceed the Secrets revealed until now, which are:
I. That in each and every part of the **Word** there is a <term>SPIRITUAL SENSE</term>, which does not appear in the sense of the letter: and that therefore the **Word** was written through <term>Correspondences</term> <note>The author's theory that every natural object or word in the Bible has a specific, matching spiritual reality.</note> of spiritual things with natural things.
II. That the <term>CORRESPONDENCES</term> themselves, and their nature, have been made manifest.
III. Also regarding the <term>LIFE OF MEN AFTER DEATH</term>.
IV. Regarding **HEAVEN AND HELL**, the nature of the one and the nature of the other; and also regarding **BAPTISM AND THE HOLY SUPPER**.
V. Regarding the **SUN in the Spiritual World**, that it is pure Love from the Lord, who is in the midst of it; the Light proceeding from it is wisdom, and the Heat proceeding from it is Love; and thus that Faith and Charity come from there, and that all things proceeding from it are Spiritual, and thus living; whereas the Sun of the natural world is pure fire, and therefore all things from that Sun are natural, and thus dead.
VI. That there are three <term>Degrees</term> <note>A technical term in the author's philosophy referring to levels of existence or consciousness (e.g., natural, spiritual, celestial).</note>, hitherto unknown.
VII. And furthermore, regarding the <term>LAST JUDGMENT</term>; That the <term>LORD THE SAVIOR IS THE GOD OF HEAVEN AND EARTH</term>; regarding the <term>NEW CHURCH</term> and its Doctrine; regarding the <term>INHABITANTS OF THE PLANETS</term>; and

### A THEOREM PROPOSED BY A CERTAIN PRINCE-ELECTOR IN GERMANY, WHO ALSO HELD THE HIGHEST ECCLESIASTICAL DIGNITY.

Once in the spiritual world, I saw a certain <term>PRINCE-ELECTOR</term> <note>original: "Dux Elector"; one of the high-ranking princes of the Holy Roman Empire who had the right to elect the Emperor</note> in Germany, who had also held the highest dignity in church affairs, and next to him two Bishops, and also two Ministers, and from a distance I heard what they were saying among themselves. The Prince-Elector asked the four standing by him whether they knew what constitutes the Head of Religion in Christianity. The Bishops replied: the head of Religion in Christianity is **FAITH ALONE JUSTIFYING AND SAVING**. He asked again: "Do you know what lies hidden deep inside that Faith? Open it up, look inside, and tell me." They replied that nothing else lies hidden inside it than the **MERIT AND JUSTICE OF THE LORD THE SAVIOR**. To this, the Prince-Elector said: "Does the Lord the Savior then lie hidden within it in His Human, in which He is called **JESUS CHRISTUS**, because He alone in His Human was Justice?" To this they said: "This follows certainly and indivisibly." The Prince-Elector pressed them, saying: "Open that Faith and look inside still further, and investigate well whether anything else is in there." And the Ministers said: "**THE GRACE OF GOD THE FATHER** also lies hidden in there." To which the Prince-Elector said: "Conceive and perceive this rightly, and you will see **THAT IT IS THE GRACE OF THE SON WITH THE FATHER**, for He petitions and intercedes. Therefore, I say to you, since you confess, venerate, and kiss that 'Faith Alone' of yours, you must altogether confess, venerate, and kiss the Lord the Savior in His Human alone; for, as was said above, He in His Human was and is **JUSTICE**." That He is also **JEHOVAH** and **GOD** in this Human, I have seen in the Sacred Scriptures, from these passages: "*Behold, the days are coming, when I will raise up for David a righteous Branch, who shall reign as King, and shall prosper... and this is the Name which they shall call Him, **JEHOVAH OUR JUSTICE***" <note>original: "Jehovah Justitia Nostra"</note>, Jeremiah chapter 33:15, 16. In Paul: "*In Jesus Christ all the **FULLNESS OF DIVINITY** dwells bodily*" <note>original: "Plenitudo Divinitatis"</note>, Colossians 2:9. And in John: "*Jesus Christ is the **TRUE GOD**, and Eternal Life*" <note>original: "Verus Deus"</note>, 1st Epistle 5:20, 21. For which reason He is also *called the **GOD OF FAITH***, Philippians 3:9.
